hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells grown in identical (basal) conditions exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output — operationalized here as the stringent-response/translation-apparatus axis (ppGpp concentration, RelA concentration, and charged-tRNA fraction) — such that across independent stochastic seeds the coefficient of variation (CV) of each channel exceeds what a purely deterministic, noise-free cell would show, and the pooled per-seed distribution departs from a single tight peak.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, per-seed steady-state values of ppgpp_conc (and rela_conc) show CV >= 0.20 (20%), i.e. intrinsic/extrinsic noise produces substantial expression heterogeneity among genetically identical cells.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed values of ppgpp_conc (and rela_conc) across wildtype/basal replicate seeds are tightly clustered, CV < 0.20, consistent with the simulator producing near-deterministic, population-homogeneous expression under fixed conditions (seed-to-seed variation is indistinguishable from numerical/solver noise).

operational_defs.observable: distribution of ppgpp_conc and rela_conc across independent seeds at matched generation/timepoint under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of per-seed values; Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed values to test for sub-populations

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged per-seed spread
operational_defs.measure: CV of fraction_trna_charged across seeds, as a secondary/confirmatory channel

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and rela_conc under a relA-pathway-breaking knockout background
operational_defs.measure: comparison of CV and mean-shift between wildtype/basal and relA_knockout/basal

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: isogenic replicate seeds show NON-trivial dispersion, not collapse to a point value. Magnitude: CV(ppgpp_conc) >= 0.20 and CV(rela_conc) >= 0.20 across 8 seeds at matched generation; pooled distribution is at least weakly multimodal or heavy-tailed (Sarle's BC > 0.555) if noise structures into sub-populations, though unimodal-but-wide (CV>=0.20) alone already confirms H1.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of ppgpp_conc across 8 seeds at generation 3 for wildtype/basal; treat as a power/equivalence check: if observed CV < 0.20 and this is below the min-detectable-effect (MDE) for n=8 seeds, accept H0 (near-deterministic). Separately run bimodality_bc on the pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values; BC > 0.555 would support structured (sub-population) heterogeneity.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(ppgpp_conc) < 0.20 and the power_mde check confirms this CV is reliably below the pre-registered 0.20 threshold (not just underpowered) — i.e. seeds cluster tightly, refuting substantial heterogeneity; BC <= 0.555 (unimodal) further refutes any claim of structured sub-populations.

test.statistic: CV with min-detectable-effect bound at n=8
test.threshold: reject H1 (accept H0) if CV < 0.20 AND 0.20 is within/above the MDE for n=8 (i.e. the null reading is not an underpowered artifact)

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic/mean-field): the model's steady-state charging and ppGpp kinetics are solved near-deterministically per seed, so apparent 'heterogeneity' is purely numerical/solver jitter, not biological noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, CV(ppgpp_conc) and CV(rela_conc) will be very small (<5-10%) and indistinguishable between wildtype/basal and a relA_knockout/basal control (since there's no real stochastic pathway to perturb); power_mde would show the small CV is a reliable null, not an underpowered artifact.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ribosome-allocation confound, not stringent-response-intrinsic noise): any observed spread in ppgpp_conc is a downstream echo of noise in ribosome_conc/growth_rate (extrinsic noise from growth-rate fluctuations), not noise intrinsic to the RelA/ppGpp synthesis module itself.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA_knockout/basal control, ppGpp synthesis is abolished (ppgpp_conc collapses near-zero and loses structure) while growth_rate and ribosome_conc still vary across seeds with similar CV to wildtype — showing the ppGpp spread was mechanistically tied to RelA activity itself, not merely inherited from growth-rate noise, which would support H1's stringent-response framing over Rival B.

auxiliary_assumptions: Matched-generation sampling (generation 3) gives comparable physiological age across seeds, so spread reflects noise not transient drift.

The simulator's per-seed stochasticity (if any) is intended to represent biological intrinsic/extrinsic noise sources, not pure solver round-off; this cannot be independently verified within the simulator and is recorded as a scope caveat.
CV and BC computed on 8 seeds have limited statistical power to detect subtle multimodality; the power_mde check is used to guard against misreading an underpowered null as true equivalence.

The relA_knockout control isolates RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis noise; residual ppGpp synthesis via SpoT is assumed small under basal (non-starvation) condition and is not separately dissected here.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing under identical conditions show substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression (noise), such that a readout of expression/activity (ribosome concentration, a proxy for the translational apparatus whose expression is noisy) varies with CV ~15-30% across replicate seeds of the same wildtype/basal condition, rather than being essentially constant (CV<5%).
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic seeds under identical (wildtype/basal) conditions, the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged as a secondary channel) has coefficient of variation >=15%, i.e. gene expression/activity is heterogeneous among genetically identical cells.
hypothesis.h0: Across isogenic seeds under identical conditions, ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) is essentially invariant: CV < 5%, consistent with deterministic, uniform expression across genetically identical cells.

operational_defs.observable: per-seed steady-state ribosome_conc at the final generation, pooled across seeds
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) across seeds; also report bimodality coefficient to check for discrete subpopulations

operational_defs.observable: per-seed fraction_trna_charged at final generation
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation across seeds

operational_defs.observable: wildtype/basal design varying only random seed
operational_defs.measure: seeds=8 independent stochastic replicates, no genetic or media perturbation

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Positive, moderate-magnitude noise: CV(ribosome_conc) across seeds ~15-30% (point estimate target 20%) under wildtype/basal; CV(fraction_trna_charged) ~10-20%. Distribution expected unimodal (not bimodal) under wildtype -- i.e., continuous noise, not a discrete subpopulation split (bimodality coefficient <=0.555).

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute coefficient of variation of per-seed ribosome_conc for wildtype/basal (n=8 seeds) using power_mde to establish the minimum detectable CV/effect at this n; separately compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (bimodality_bc) over the pooled per-seed values. H1 requires CV>=15% (exceeding the MDE floor) and BC<=0.555 (unimodal, continuous noise rather than discrete subpopulations). If observed CV<5% (and within the MDE-resolvable range, i.e. not masked by insufficient power) OR BC>0.555 (bimodal/discrete split), H1 as stated (continuous moderate noise) is refuted.
falsifier.refuting_result: Per-seed CV(ribosome_conc) < 5% with the MDE check confirming n=8 is sufficient to detect a 15% CV, indicating isogenic cells are essentially uniform in this readout; or alternatively BC>0.555 indicating the variability is actually a discrete bimodal split (a different phenomenon than continuous expression noise).

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation + bimodality_bc
test.threshold: CV>=15% AND BC<=0.555 to confirm H1; CV<5% (with MDE<15%) or BC>0.555 refutes H1

rivals.claim: Apparent variability across seeds is purely a numerical/sampling artifact of the simulator's RNG seeding (not biological noise) -- increasing seeds further would converge to near-zero CV, i.e. there is no true steady-state heterogeneity, just finite-sample estimation noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, a power_mde check would show the measured CV is below the minimum detectable effect at n=8 (noisy estimate indistinguishable from 0), OR CV shrinks sharply when comparing against a larger-seed reference design -- here we instead expect CV to remain stably >=15% and above the MDE floor, consistent with real biological noise, not sampling artifact.

rivals.claim: Any observed variability is driven by bistability in the ppGpp/stringent-response circuit (a genuine discrete two-state switch: a 'slow/high-ppGpp' subpopulation vs a 'fast/low-ppGpp' subpopulation), not continuous expression noise around a single mean.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout control (abolishing ppGpp synthesis capacity) would collapse any bimodal split in ribosome_conc/fraction_trna_charged toward a single unimodal distribution (BC drops below 0.555) if bistability depended on ppGpp signaling; if the bimodal split persists even after relA knockout, this rival is refuted in favor of noise being generated elsewhere (not ppGpp-circuit bistability).

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed final-generation snapshot of ribosome_conc / fraction_trna_charged is a valid proxy for steady-state expression level of that cell lineage (not confounded by transient startup dynamics) -- generations=3 is assumed sufficient to reach steady state post-seeding.

Stochastic variation introduced by distinct RNG seeds in this simulator is intended to represent genuine intrinsic/extrinsic biological noise (partitioning, transcriptional bursting, etc.) rather than purely numerical artifact; this cannot be fully disentangled from true biological stochasticity within the simulator and is logged as a scope caveat (deterministic-chaos-vs-noise distinction is out of scope).

The relA knockout control isolates ppGpp-circuit-driven bistability without independently perturbing other sources of expression noise (translation bursting, partitioning at division, etc.) -- i.e., relA KO is assumed not to systematically alter baseline growth_rate/division_rate so drastically that ribosome_conc comparisons become confounded by a sick-cell phenotype rather than a noise-source removal.
Bimodality coefficient threshold of 0.555 (Sarle's criterion) is treated as the standard unimodal/bimodal cutoff provided by the platform's bimodality_bc test.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells (same genotype, same medium) show substantial cell-to-cell variability in expression of a given gene/pathway due to stochastic noise in transcription/translation, rather than expressing it at an identical level — specifically, the population distribution of a representative expression-linked readout (ribosome concentration, a proxy for ribosomal-protein expression output) has a coefficient of variation (CV) across isogenic replicate seeds substantially greater than zero (CV >= 15%), and this variability is not explained merely by measurement/replicate noise.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic seeds under identical (wildtype/basal) conditions, single-cell-lineage expression readouts (ribosome_conc, and fraction_trna_charged as a cross-check) show a coefficient of variation >= 15% across seeds, i.e. meaningfully noisy expression among genetically identical cells.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic cells express the gene/pathway at essentially the same level: the across-seed CV of ribosome_conc under wildtype/basal is low (<5%), consistent with only trivial numerical/replicate noise and no biologically meaningful cell-to-cell variability.

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state value of ribosome_conc (uM) at a fixed generation, pooled across seeds

operational_defs.observable: spread of ribosome_conc across seeds
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) of ribosome_conc across seeds; also checked against fraction_trna_charged dispersion as a secondary noise proxy

operational_defs.observable: wildtype perturbation, same condition, only seed varied
operational_defs.measure: wildtype/basal design with seeds=8 differing only in RNG seed

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Across 8 isogenic seeds (wildtype/basal, steady_state charging), ribosome_conc shows CV >= 15% (point estimate expected ~20-30%), i.e. a >=1.15x spread between low and high expressing replicates, far above a null expectation of CV<5% from numerical replicate noise alone.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute coefficient of variation (SD/mean) of ribosome_conc across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds at generation 3; treat CV<5% as consistent with H0 (trivial noise) and CV>=15% as supporting H1. Run power_mde first to confirm 8 seeds can resolve a 15% CV effect above a 5% noise floor before trusting any null read.
falsifier.refuting_result: Across-seed CV of ribosome_conc < 5% AND power_mde confirms the design can detect a 15% effect at n=8, i.e. isogenic replicates are genuinely indistinguishable and this is not a power failure — this refutes the claim that identical cells vary meaningfully in expression.

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation + min_detectable_effect
test.threshold: CV>=15% supports H1; CV<5% supports H0 only if MDE at n=8 is <=15% (otherwise inconclusive, not confirmatory of H0)

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is an artifact of insufficient seeds/sampling noise in the simulator's RNG, not biologically meaningful stochastic gene expression.
rivals.distinguishing_result: power_mde at n=8 shows min-detectable-effect >> 15%, meaning the observed spread cannot be distinguished from pure sampling artifact; increasing seeds would be needed to resolve.

rivals.claim: Variability is driven by extrinsic noise (shared upstream fluctuations, e.g. in ppGpp/stringent response or growth rate) rather than intrinsic promoter-level stochasticity, so clamping ppGpp would collapse the variance.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the ppgpp_conc clamp discriminating control, the across-seed CV of ribosome_conc drops sharply (e.g. to <5-8%) relative to wildtype/basal, showing the variance was driven by fluctuating ppGpp (an extrinsic/global regulator) rather than irreducible intrinsic transcriptional noise.

rivals.claim: Variability is condition-specific (an artifact of basal media fitting) rather than a general property of isogenic expression, so it would vanish or differ substantially under a different static condition (acetate).
rivals.distinguishing_result: The acetate wildtype design shows CV of ribosome_conc indistinguishable from or far lower than the basal wildtype CV, indicating the noise is a basal-condition artifact rather than a general isogenic-expression phenomenon.

auxiliary_assumptions: ribosome_conc at a fixed generation is a valid proxy for 'gene expression level' broadly (ribosomal-protein genes are highly expressed and a standard noise readout in the literature).
Steady-state charging mode is used (not kinetic), so ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc channels are populated.

Seeds in the simulator encode independent stochastic realizations of gene expression (transcription/translation bursting), analogous to biological intrinsic noise, even though the simulator cannot distinguish deterministic chaos from true stochastic noise — this distinction is out of scope and recorded as a caveat.
Generation 3 is late enough to reach a quasi-steady distribution across seeds but early enough to avoid confounding from population bottlenecking/division-rate effects.
The ppgpp_conc clamp at 1x basal is treated as a variance-collapsing control for extrinsic noise without altering mean growth phenotype, isolating the discriminator from a confounding mean-shift.

all_rounds.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
all_rounds.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in identical (basal) medium exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output, manifest as a broad, non-degenerate distribution of ppGpp concentration and ribosome concentration across replicate seeds rather than a single fixed value — i.e. genetically identical cells do NOT all express a given gene/pathway at the same level.
all_rounds.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of ppgpp_conc (and ribosome_conc) shows substantial dispersion (CV >= 0.15) and/or bimodality (Sarle's BC > 0.555), reflecting intrinsic noise in gene expression rather than a single deterministic level.
all_rounds.h0: Per-seed ppgpp_conc (and ribosome_conc) values under wildtype/basal are tightly clustered (CV < 0.15) and unimodal (BC <= 0.555), consistent with deterministic, noise-free expression where identical genotype + identical environment yields identical expression level.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channel values recorded per seed at end of simulated generations
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) across seeds; Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed values

operational_defs.observable: wildtype genotype, condition=basal, varying ONLY the stochastic seed
operational_defs.measure: wildtype/basal design with seeds=8, generations=3

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and rela_conc channels in a relA-knockout background
operational_defs.measure: CV and mean-shift of ppgpp_conc in gene_knockout(relA)/basal vs wildtype/basal

all_rounds.predicted_effect: Direction: positive dispersion (not zero). Magnitude: CV(ppgpp_conc) across 8 wildtype seeds >= 0.15 (i.e. >=15% relative spread), and CV(ribosome_conc) >= 0.10; pooled bimodality coefficient BC is expected <0.555 (unimodal but broad) for this unperturbed case — i.e. a broad unimodal distribution, not a point mass. If instead BC>0.555 that would indicate an even stronger (bimodal, switch-like) noise regime.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of ppgpp_conc across the 8 seeds within the wildtype/basal design; separately compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values. Reject H1 (accept H0 of deterministic/uniform expression) if CV < 0.15 AND BC <= 0.555, i.e. values are tightly clustered and unimodal.
falsifier.refuting_result: Per-seed ppgpp_conc values cluster tightly (CV < 0.15) with no meaningful spread, BC <= 0.555, showing isogenic cells in identical conditions express the gene/pathway at essentially the same level — refuting H1.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc; CV computed alongside as a dispersion check
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 for bimodal evidence; CV >= 0.15 for H1 dispersion claim (H0 requires BOTH CV<0.15 and BC<=0.555)

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic/homogeneous): apparent variability across seeds is purely numerical/simulation noise floor (solver tolerance), not biological stochasticity; true biological expression is essentially fixed.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV is driven by solver artifacts rather than biology, CV(ppgpp_conc) should be comparably tiny (<0.05) and NOT respond to a biologically-relevant perturbation like relA knockout; i.e. gene_knockout(relA)/basal shows the same tiny CV and a mean shift with no change in spread shape.

rivals.claim: Rival B (stringent-response-driven bimodality): the dominant source of cell-to-cell variability is bistable ppGpp/stringent-response switching (not generic transcriptional/translational noise), so variability should collapse specifically when RelA is removed.
rivals.distinguishing_result: gene_knockout(relA)/basal shows ppgpp_conc CV collapsing toward near-zero (and BC drops below unimodal threshold trivially since near-constant), while ribosome_conc CV remains >=0.10 — showing the ppGpp-specific mechanism, not general noise, was responsible for the wildtype dispersion.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seed-to-seed variation in the simulator is intended to represent intrinsic stochastic gene-expression noise (not merely a numerical artifact of the solver) — a scope caveat we cannot fully adjudicate inside the simulator alone.

ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channels are read under steady-state charging (no kinetic ppGpp module engaged), so values reflect the steady-state approximation of the stringent response rather than explicit RelA/SpoT kinetics unless the kinetic module is explicitly enabled.
Generations=3-4 is sufficient for the per-seed distribution to reach a representative (non-transient) state; very early-generation transients are not the object of the claim.
The relA knockout is assumed to be mechanistically simulated (removes RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis) rather than a no-op; this is checked downstream per the instrument note.
Basal condition is representative of 'identical environment'; we are not claiming the result generalizes unchanged to other static conditions (e.g. acetate) without separate testing.
residual_ambiguities: [construct_ambiguity] Is ppGpp/ribosome concentration the specific expression readout you intend, or should the claim be framed as a distributional claim averaged/pooled across multiple expression-proxy channels (ribosome_conc, rna_mass, protein_mass) to better match the general scope of 'a gene'?

objection_ledger.issue: Whether seed-to-seed variability in this simulator represents genuine intrinsic biochemical noise (as in real isogenic cells) or is an artifact of how the simulator randomizes initial conditions/solver seeds is not something the dial labels can adjudicate from inside the simulator; this is already flagged as an auxiliary assumption.

The claim as stated ('genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level') is about gene expression broadly, but the operationalization tests only ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc as proxies for 'a gene/pathway' — a reasonable narrowing, but it's a choice among many possible channels (e.g. protein_mass, rna_mass) that could equally stand in for 'gene expression output.'

hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells growing in the same medium (isogenic, same condition) show substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output — measured as per-seed variation in ribosome concentration and tRNA charging as proxies for expression state — such that the coefficient of variation (CV) across replicate stochastic realizations (seeds) exceeds 10%, i.e., cells do NOT express the same gene at the same level despite identical genotype and environment.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) shows CV > 10%, reflecting intrinsic stochastic gene-expression noise rather than measurement/replicate artifact.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed variability in ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged across isogenic wildtype/basal replicates is small (CV <= 10%), consistent with cells expressing genes at essentially the same level modulo simulator/replicate noise floor.

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Ribosome_conc CV across seeds ~15-25% (vs an assumed technical/noise floor of ~5-10%); fraction_trna_charged CV ~8-15%. Distribution is unimodal continuous variation (BC < 0.555), not a discrete bimodal switch, consistent with intrinsic stochastic noise rather than a bistable subpopulation.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of ribosome_conc across 8 seeds at generation 3 for wildtype/basal; treat CV<=10% as failure to reject H0 (no biologically meaningful heterogeneity beyond noise floor). Separately, for the rrna_operon_knockout/basal control, apply welch_disconfirm of ribosome_conc vs wildtype/basal to confirm the module responds as expected (sanity check that the channel is sensitive to real perturbation, calibrating the noise floor).

rivals.claim: Rival B: Variability reflects a discrete bistable subpopulation structure (e.g., some cells locked into a stringent-response-like state) rather than continuous stochastic noise around one mean.

Generation 3 is late enough for transient initialization effects to have decayed but early enough to avoid confounds from population drift over many generations.

ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged are reasonable proxies for 'gene expression level' at the scope the simulator supports (the instrument does not give single-gene mRNA/protein counts per cell for a screen, so we use these aggregate channels as the best available operationalization).
The rrna_operon_knockout control is used only as a sensitivity/calibration check (does a real genetic perturbation move ribosome_conc beyond the natural seed spread), not as the primary test of H1.
No mid-run carbon source switch or combined perturbation is used; wildtype/basal across 8 seeds is a valid in-envelope design for estimating population-level noise.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: In an isogenic E. coli population under constant conditions, gene-expression-linked readouts (ppGpp concentration and fraction of charged tRNA, proxies for stringent-response/translation-machinery expression state) show substantial cell-to-cell variability rather than a single shared value: across replicate stochastic seeds of the wildtype strain under basal media, the coefficient of variation (CV) of ppgpp_conc across seeds is large (CV >= 0.25), and this variability is intrinsic to expression machinery (synthesis/degradation stochasticity) rather than a downstream echo of division-timing differences -- as shown by an INTERVENTIONAL control (relA knockout) that removes the dominant source of ppGpp synthesis noise and should COLLAPSE the CV far more than any division-timing perturbation would.
hypothesis.h1: Genetically identical cells growing in the same environment exhibit substantial heterogeneity in expression-linked state variables that is intrinsic to the expression/synthesis machinery: across-seed CV of ppgpp_conc >= 0.25 at steady state in wildtype/basal, AND this CV collapses substantially (by >=50%, i.e. CV_relAKO <= 0.5 * CV_wildtype) when relA (the dominant ppGpp synthetase) is knocked out -- demonstrating the heterogeneity is generated by the stochastic synthesis reaction itself, not merely inherited from division-timing variation (which relA KO does not primarily control).
hypothesis.h0: Genetically identical cells under constant conditions express genes essentially uniformly, or any apparent heterogeneity is not attributable to intrinsic expression-machinery noise: across-seed CV of ppgpp_conc in wildtype/basal is small (<0.25), OR if CV>=0.25 it does NOT substantially collapse under relA knockout (CV_relAKO > 0.5 * CV_wildtype) -- indicating the variability is either solver noise or driven by factors (e.g. division-timing sampling, other pathways) unaffected by removing the ppGpp synthetase, i.e. not intrinsic synthesis-reaction noise.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc per-seed values across independent stochastic replicates (seeds) run under identical wildtype/basal conditions
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) of ppgpp_conc across seeds; also computed for fraction_trna_charged as a secondary channel with its own stated threshold

operational_defs.construct: intrinsic synthesis-machinery noise vs extrinsic/other source

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: positive, nonzero expression heterogeneity that is intrinsic and synthesis-driven. Magnitude: CV of ppgpp_conc across 8 wildtype/basal seeds >= 0.25. Upon relA knockout (removing the dominant ppGpp synthetase, breaking the intrinsic-synthesis-noise mechanism directly rather than via a correlated channel), CV(ppgpp_conc) should drop to <= 0.5x the wildtype CV (i.e. >=50% reduction), since residual ppGpp (via SpoT) is produced through a different, likely lower-noise or clamped pathway. By contrast, rrna_operon_knockout (which perturbs division timing/ribosome capacity but leaves relA/spoT intact) is predicted to leave CV(ppgpp_conc) relatively unchanged (within ~20% of wildtype CV) despite potentially shifting division_rate CV -- demonstrating the heterogeneity does not track division-timing perturbations the way it tracks synthesis-machinery removal. Secondary: fraction_trna_charged CV >= 0.10 in wildtype, also expected to drop under relA-KO. Distribution shape: unimodal but broad (BC <= 0.555) at baseline.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: compute CV(ppgpp_conc) across 8 seeds in wildtype/basal and in relA-knockout/basal. Use power_mde to confirm wildtype CV(ppgpp_conc) exceeds the n=8 detectable floor (reject solver-noise rival if observed CV >= MDE). Then require CV_wildtype >= 0.25 AND CV_relAKO <= 0.5 * CV_wildtype (interventional collapse test). Discriminating control: Welch t-test (and CV comparison) of ppgpp_conc, rrna_operon_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal -- a perturbation that alters division timing/ribosome capacity WITHOUT touching relA/spoT; under extrinsic-timing rival this should also collapse or substantially shift ppgpp_conc CV, under H1 it should NOT (CV within ~20% of wildtype).
falsifier.refuting_result: H1 is refuted if EITHER (a) CV(ppgpp_conc) in wildtype/basal is <0.25 or below the power_mde floor (solver noise), OR (b) CV_relAKO > 0.5 * CV_wildtype (knocking out the dominant synthesis enzyme fails to collapse the heterogeneity, implying the noise is not intrinsic to synthesis), OR (c) rrna_operon_knockout/basal (division-timing perturbation, relA/spoT intact) produces a CV(ppgpp_conc) collapse comparable to or larger than relA-KO's, which would indicate division-timing is the real driver rather than synthesis-machinery stochasticity.

test.statistic: welch_t of ppgpp_conc, relA-knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal (mean-shift check) plus CV ratio CV_relAKO/CV_wildtype; power_mde for the wildtype CV detectability floor
test.threshold: CV_wildtype >= 0.25 AND >= power_mde floor at n=8; AND CV_relAKO/CV_wildtype <= 0.5; AND |welch_t| for relA-KO vs wildtype is informative (reported alongside, not required >=2 since this is a variance not mean test)

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is purely numerical/solver stochasticity (seed-to-seed RNG noise in the simulator), not biologically meaningful expression noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV of ppgpp_conc across seeds falls below the power_mde-computed detectable floor at n=8, the signal is indistinguishable from solver noise -- supporting this rival instead of true heterogeneity.

rivals.claim: Variability is driven by extrinsic division-timing/cell-cycle-phase sampling differences across seeds rather than intrinsic synthesis-reaction noise -- ppGpp level is read out downstream of growth rate, and seeds simply differ in which phase they are sampled at.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under this rival, relA knockout (which does not primarily alter division timing but does remove the synthesis reaction) should NOT substantially collapse CV(ppgpp_conc) -- if CV_relAKO stays above 0.5*CV_wildtype while rrna_operon_knockout (which DOES perturb division timing) shows an equal or larger CV(ppgpp_conc), that pattern would favor the extrinsic-timing rival over intrinsic synthesis noise.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed stochasticity (RNG draws for reaction/expression events) is an adequate proxy for intrinsic biological noise, not merely an artifact.
8 seeds is treated as sufficient replicate depth to estimate a CV and run power_mde with usable resolution at the modest scale permitted.
Basal media and 3 generations represent steady exponential growth, not a transient shift, so ppgpp_conc reflects steady-state regulation rather than startup transients.

relA knockout is treated as an interventional break of the dominant intrinsic ppGpp-synthesis noise source; residual SpoT-mediated synthesis/hydrolysis is assumed to be a lower-noise or more tightly regulated pathway in the model, so a large CV collapse under relA-KO is attributable to removing the stochastic synthesis reaction rather than to a confounded change in mean growth physiology alone.

rrna_operon_knockout is used as the discriminating control isolating the division-timing/ribosome-capacity axis from the synthesis-machinery axis; we assume it perturbs division timing/growth rate without directly altering relA/spoT reaction kinetics, since the model does not simulate a mechanism linking rRNA operon copy number to RelA/SpoT enzyme activity.

fraction_trna_charged under steady-state charging is broadcast across 86 columns from 20 per-amino-acid values; the aggregate/representative column is used consistently across seeds for the secondary CV computation and is not load-bearing for the primary falsifier decision.

We do not attempt a full intrinsic/extrinsic noise decomposition (e.g. dual-reporter style) since the instrument does not provide that readout; the relA-KO vs rrna-operon-KO contrast is the closest feasible interventional discriminator available in the envelope.

objection_ledger.issue: The relA_knockout control is meant to show that ppGpp variability is 'pathway-linked', but relA synthesizes ppGpp itself, so knocking it out mechanically collapses ppgpp_conc toward a floor/zero for ALL seeds regardless of whether the underlying noise source is intrinsic stochastic expression or extrinsic/deterministic (e.g. division-timing) variation. A low CV in relA_knockout/basal is the trivial consequence of removing the synthesis enzyme (near-zero mean inflates or deflates CV mechanically), not evidence that discriminates intrinsic noise from the extrinsic-timing rival. The two rivals (solver-noise and extrinsic-timing) are not actually separated by this design: both rivals and H1 would predict the same relA-knockout collapse.

The 'extrinsic timing' rival's distinguishing test is explicitly flagged by the candidate itself as 'not independently testable with this instrument's tools' (tracking ppgpp_conc CV against division_rate CV), yet the rival is still listed as if addressed. As written, there is no actual decision rule that would let this rival be excluded versus confirmed -- the fallback (relA knockout CV) is the same flawed test noted above.

The claim that fraction_trna_charged CV>=0.10 and the bimodality coefficient BC<=0.555 are used as secondary/tertiary criteria, but the decision_rule and refuting_result only operationalize the ppgpp_conc CV and the relA Welch test -- the fraction_trna_charged and BC criteria are asserted in predicted_effect but never wired into the actual falsifier logic, so it's unclear what happens if ppgpp CV passes but these secondary predictions fail.

The primary rival-discriminator is now a within-seed-set ratio of CV(ppgpp_conc) to CV(division_rate). But these two channels are plausibly mechanistically coupled in the model (ppGpp level and growth/division rate are linked via the stringent-response growth-law in E. coli models), so they would co-vary across seeds regardless of whether the root cause is intrinsic expression noise or extrinsic division-timing sampling. A ratio/correlation comparison between coupled channels cannot by itself attribute the heterogeneity to intrinsic stochastic expression vs extrinsic phase-sampling -- this is the same coupled-rival problem as before, relocated from relA-knockout to division_rate. An interventional control that breaks the coupling (e.g., a condition/perturbation that varies division timing independently of ppGpp synthesis, or vice versa) is needed, not a within-run correlation/ratio.

all_rounds.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
all_rounds.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells (wildtype/basal) do NOT express a single target gene's protein/mRNA at a fixed shared level: across independent stochastic seeds, the per-seed copy number / concentration of a specific gene product (operationalized via its own species channel — a named mRNA/protein species, e.g. the model's per-gene mRNA or protein count for a representative gene) shows CV >= 25% across seeds, far above a ~5% numerical-noise floor, consistent with intrinsic transcription/translation burstiness at the single-gene level. Because the instrument's only broadcast per-species channels available at genome-wide scale are mRNA/protein species counts (not an aggregate like ribosome_conc), we screen a small panel of genes (a 'new_gene' reporter construct plus 2-3 endogenous genes via gene_knockout-adjacent wildtype runs) rather than relying on a single bulk proxy, and report the FRACTION of genes in the panel showing CV >= 25%, predicting >= 70% of sampled genes qualify as 'noisy' (non-degenerate across seeds).
all_rounds.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under wildtype/basal, for a panel of individual gene-product species (mRNA/protein counts of specific genes, not bulk aggregates), the median per-gene CV across seeds is >= 25%, and at least 70% of panel genes individually exceed a 25% CV threshold, reflecting intrinsic single-gene expression noise.
all_rounds.h0: Per-gene mRNA/protein species counts across isogenic seeds under wildtype/basal are tightly clustered (CV <= 5% per gene, consistent with the ~5% numerical-noise floor) for the large majority (>=70%) of panel genes, i.e. single-gene expression level is effectively deterministic/population-identical up to integration noise.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state (or matched-generation) copy number of that gene's mRNA/protein species across >=6 seeds; compute mean, SD, CV=SD/mean per gene

operational_defs.measure: fraction of panel genes with CV >= 25%; report distribution of per-gene CVs

Magnitude: median per-gene CV across seeds >= 25% (vs ~5% numerical floor, i.e. ~5x), with >=70% of a 5-8 gene panel individually exceeding 25% CV -- a population-level claim about the fraction of genes showing substantial noise, not just one gene.

falsifier.decision_rule: For each panel gene's own mRNA/protein species count (reporter via new_gene design; endogenous genes via matched wildtype seeds), compute per-gene CV across seeds (n=8). Run power_mde to confirm n=8 seeds can detect a 25% CV against a 5% floor. Classify each gene as 'noisy' if CV>=25%; reject H1 if the fraction of noisy genes across the panel is <70% (i.e., most genes look deterministic) with power_mde confirming adequate sensitivity.
falsifier.refuting_result: Fewer than 70% of panel genes (reporter + endogenous) show CV>=25% across seeds -- most per-gene product levels cluster tightly (CV<=5-10%) -- while power_mde confirms the seed count had power to detect 25% CV, indicating single-gene expression is largely population-identical rather than broadly noisy.

test.statistic: per-gene CV (SD/mean) across seeds; fraction of panel genes exceeding 25% CV; MDE from power_mde
test.threshold: reject H1 if fraction of noisy genes (CV>=25%) < 70% AND power_mde confirms MDE < 25% at n=8 seeds

rivals.claim: Apparent per-gene variability is a numerical/sampling artifact (insufficient seeds), not real intrinsic noise -- with more seeds the per-gene CV would shrink toward the ~5% floor rather than stabilizing at a higher plateau.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Doubling seeds (8->16) for the same gene panel shows CV collapsing substantially (e.g., from 25% toward 5%) rather than stabilizing near 25%, indicating sampling artifact rather than a genuine stochastic steady-state distribution.

rivals.claim: Observed per-gene variability is not intrinsic transcription/translation burstiness but is secondarily driven by cross-seed growth-rate differences (extrinsic noise) that scale all gene products together via dilution/global capacity, so individual genes aren't independently noisy -- they just track a shared growth-rate fluctuation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout background (which caps ribosome/growth capacity and dampens growth-rate variance across seeds) would still show per-gene CV>=25% for the panel genes if noise is intrinsic to each gene's own transcription/translation; if instead per-gene CV collapses toward the floor once growth-rate variance is suppressed, that supports extrinsic growth-rate-coupled noise rather than gene-intrinsic stochasticity. This is an interventional control: it breaks the growth-rate-ribosome feedback loop rather than merely observing a correlation between ribosome_conc and growth_rate.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seeds in the simulator independently sample stochastic transcription/translation events at the per-gene level (not just initial-condition perturbations), so cross-seed variance in a gene's own mRNA/protein count is a valid proxy for that gene's cell-to-cell expression variability.

The platform exposes per-gene mRNA/protein species counts (via new_gene for a reporter, and named endogenous genes as species) at sufficient resolution to compute a meaningful per-seed CV; if only a subset of the panel genes are actually tracked as distinct species, the fraction-noisy statistic is computed over whichever subset is available and this is treated as a scope caveat.
The ~5% CV numerical-noise floor is a working assumption for this platform's stochastic solver, not independently corroborated against a corpus value.
Matched generation number across seeds controls for cell-cycle-phase-driven variation so that observed per-gene spread reflects expression noise rather than asynchronous sampling.

A 5-8 gene panel (reporter + 4 endogenous genes spanning different functional classes: efflux, metabolic, stress, membrane, biosynthesis) is treated as a reasonable modest sample of 'genes in general' for this population-level claim, acknowledging it is not literally genome-wide but is broader than a single bulk proxy.

objection_ledger.issue: The user's question is about whether 'the same gene' is expressed at the same level across isogenic cells - i.e., per-gene expression noise. The candidate substitutes a bulk/aggregate readout (ribosome_conc, fraction_trna_charged) as a proxy for 'gene expression level' generally. These are systems-level emergent quantities (summed over many genes/processes) and could show low noise even if individual gene expression is highly variable, or vice versa. This conflates 'bulk translational capacity' with 'single-gene expression level', which is the actual construct in the question.

The rrna_operon_knockout design is proposed to distinguish intrinsic stochastic noise from extrinsic growth-rate-driven coupling, but capping rRNA operons alters ribosome synthesis machinery directly - it does not decouple ribosome_conc from growth_rate variation, it just changes the mean/ceiling of ribosome_conc. Growth_rate and ribosome_conc are mechanistically coupled (ribosomes drive growth rate, growth rate feeds back on ribosome allocation) in the underlying model, so this knockout would likely shift both channels together rather than breaking their correlation. The design does not actually test whether cross-seed ribosome_conc variance tracks cross-seed growth_rate variance independently of a common cause.

The falsifier's decision_rule references 'channel: protein_mass' but protein_mass is a bulk aggregate channel, while the actual statistic computed is per-gene mRNA/protein species CV. It's unclear the instrument exposes named endogenous gene species (acrB, lacZ, rpoS, ompF, thrA) as distinct trackable channels outside of new_gene constructs -- if only new_gene reporters are actually instrumentable, the 'panel of endogenous genes' claim outruns what the dial can read.

This is a labeling leftover from the earlier endogenous-gene framing and should be corrected to the actual per-reporter species channel to avoid ambiguity about what dial is read.

all_rounds.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
all_rounds.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing under identical static basal conditions exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output (read out via ppGpp-pathway and ribosome-related channels as proxies for expression state), such that the population shows a coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds of roughly 15-30% rather than being tightly clamped near-identical (<5% CV); this noise is graded/stochastic (unimodal across seeds) and is intrinsic to the single-condition block itself, since the instrument holds 'condition' fixed within a static run by construction, making extrinsic condition drift inapplicable as a rival explanation within a single basal block.
all_rounds.h1: Across a broad sample of isogenic replicate seeds under identical steady-state basal conditions, expression-proxy channels (ribosome_conc, ppgpp_conc, rela_conc) show substantial intrinsic cell-to-cell variability: CV >= 15% across seeds, with the pooled per-seed distribution remaining unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555), indicating graded stochastic variation rather than discrete subpopulations.

Because 'condition' is a fixed static dial within a single basal run (the instrument's own definition), extrinsic condition drift cannot vary WITHIN this design by construction -- so any observed CV here is attributable to seed-level (intrinsic) stochasticity, not an extrinsic micro-state artifact; the relA_knockout arm separately tests whether the stringent-response pathway itself is the mechanistic noise source (a different, resolvable question) rather than serving as an extrinsic-vs-intrinsic discriminator.

objection_ledger.issue: The entire hypothesis rests on 'seeds' in the whole-cell/whole-population simulator corresponding to independent single CELLS with stochastic initialization, so that per-seed CV reflects cell-to-cell variability. If the simulator's 'seed' instead perturbs a population-average or lineage-level trajectory (common in many whole-cell models), per-seed CV measures run-to-run numerical/initialization variability, not single-cell heterogeneity, and the claim 'genetically identical cells' would not be operationalized by the instrument at all.

The relA-knockout control tests whether ppgpp_conc/ribosome_conc CV collapses when RelA signaling is removed, but ppgpp_conc, rela_conc, and ribosome_conc are mechanistically coupled (RelA synthesizes ppGpp, which represses rRNA/ribosome transcription) and therefore co-vary by construction in the wildtype. Removing relA will mechanically suppress ppGpp synthesis and alter ribosome_conc regardless of whether the ORIGINAL heterogeneity was 'intrinsic' or 'extrinsic/environmental' — a CV collapse in the knockout is consistent with simply deleting the ppGpp pathway, not with distinguishing intrinsic stochasticity from extrinsic media-driven variation. The design does not include an independent extrinsic-noise manipulation (e.g., varying/homogenizing medium conditions across seeds) that would actually isolate the extrinsic-vs-intrinsic axis.

The 'basal_homogenized' control is specified with identical perturbation/condition/timeline/seeds/generations fields as the standard wildtype/basal design, differing only in a non-functional 'note' parameter. Since the instrument's actual dials (perturbation, condition, timeline) are unchanged, this control is indistinguishable from simply re-running wildtype/basal again -- it does not manipulate or homogenize any extrinsic/environmental channel. A null result (CV similar across the two 'arms') is therefore guaranteed by construction (same design run twice), not an empirical finding that rules out extrinsic drift, and a difference would only reflect ordinary sampling noise between two identical designs. The control cannot actually distinguish intrinsic stochastic noise from extrinsic condition drift as claimed.

The gen2-vs-gen4 welch_disconfirm check is framed as validating 'steady-state stability,' but generations is a perturbation-level dial that changes population age-structure/lineage depth, not just averaging window. A pass (|t|<2) could occur even if the per-seed CV itself is driven by transient early-generation dynamics that happen to look similar at both checkpoints by coincidence, and a fail could reflect genuine population-structure change rather than 'CV estimate instability.' This conflates two different things (noise-floor stability vs generation-structure effects) under one test; the decision rule should be stated as a coarse sanity check only, not proof of steady-state, or it should be dropped from the primary falsifier chain.

hypothesis.claim: In an isogenic wildtype population growing under identical basal conditions, single-cell expression of ribosomal/stringent-response machinery (ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc, our operational proxies for gene-expression state) shows substantial cell-to-cell variability — across-seed CV(ribosome_conc) >= 15% — that is NOT fully explained away by growth-rate coupling: after regressing ribosome_conc on growth_rate across seeds, residual (partial) CV remains >= 10%, indicating a genuine intrinsic/extrinsic expression-noise component beyond deterministic growth-rate tracking. This claim is scoped specifically to ribosomal/stringent-response gene expression, not a genome-wide claim about all genes.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate cells (seeds) under identical wildtype/basal conditions, ribosome_conc has across-seed CV >= 15%, AND this dispersion is not simply growth_rate-coupled: the residual CV of ribosome_conc after regressing out growth_rate (per seed, matched generation) remains >= 10%, with the growth_rate-vs-ribosome_conc slope_ci R^2 < 0.8 (i.e. growth rate does not deterministically pin down ribosome_conc). Genetically identical cells do NOT express ribosomal/stringent-response genes at a single fixed level.
hypothesis.h0: Across isogenic replicate cells under identical wildtype/basal conditions, ribosome_conc is effectively deterministic given genotype+environment: either (a) raw CV(ribosome_conc) < 15%, or (b) raw CV >= 15% but is fully explained by growth_rate coupling, i.e. residual CV after regressing out growth_rate is < 10% and/or the growth_rate-ribosome_conc relation has R^2 >= 0.8 (slope_ci excludes 0 with tight fit), meaning apparent variability collapses once the shared extrinsic driver (growth rate) is accounted for.
