hypothesis.claim: In an isogenic E. coli population growing in identical (basal) media, cell-to-cell stochastic variation in gene expression produces substantial heterogeneity in steady-state gene-product levels even though all cells share the same genotype and environment — i.e. expression noise is intrinsic, not just seed-to-seed simulation artifact, and the distribution of a representative expression-linked channel across replicate cells (seeds) shows a coefficient of variation (CV) well above the numerical/sampling noise floor, with no bimodal subpopulation structure (a single unimodal but broad distribution) under unperturbed conditions.
hypothesis.h1: Across replicate isogenic seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and corroborating fraction_trna_charged) shows a CV >= 15%, consistent with substantial intrinsic expression noise, and is unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555).
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed variation in ribosome_conc across wildtype/basal replicates is indistinguishable from the simulator's numerical/sampling noise floor (CV < 15%) OR the distribution is not simply unimodal (BC > 0.555, suggesting the apparent heterogeneity actually reflects discrete subpopulations rather than continuous noise).

operational_defs.construct: cell-to-cell expression heterogeneity among genetically identical cells
operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel value at a fixed generation, sampled across independent stochastic seeds under the same wildtype/basal condition
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) of ribosome_conc across seeds; corroborated by CV of fraction_trna_charged across seeds

operational_defs.construct: distribution shape (continuous noise vs. discrete subpopulations)
operational_defs.observable: pooled per-seed ribosome_conc values
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over the pooled seed values

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc variability under a design expected to minimize biological stochasticity contribution (same wildtype/basal design, used as the reference distribution against which CV is judged non-trivial)
operational_defs.measure: welch_t and effect_pct from disconfirm(target, reference, channel) plus z_vs_corpus_spread as descriptive positioning

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) will show nontrivial dispersion across isogenic seeds, not a point value. Magnitude: CV >= 15% across 8 seeds at generation 3 under wildtype/basal, i.e. at least ~3x the typical numerical seed-noise floor (assumed ~5% CV for a well-behaved channel), and the pooled distribution will remain unimodal (BC <= 0.555, i.e. below the 2-cluster-split threshold), consistent with continuous stochastic noise rather than two discrete subpopulations.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (dispersion): compute CV of ribosome_conc across 8 seeds at generation 3 for wildtype/basal; treat CV>=15% as evidence of substantial heterogeneity (power_mde check: with n=8 seeds, confirm 15% CV is above the minimum detectable effect at this n before concluding presence of noise). Step 2 (shape): compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled 8-seed values; unimodal continuous noise requires BC<=0.555.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV < 15% (heterogeneity statistically indistinguishable from the sampling/numerical noise floor established by power_mde) OR BC > 0.555 (distribution is bimodal/multimodal, implying discrete subpopulations rather than continuous intrinsic noise) — either result refutes H1 as stated.

test.statistic: CV with min-detectable-effect check at n=8, followed by bimodality_bc as a secondary shape test
test.threshold: CV >= 15% must exceed MDE at n=8; BC <= 0.555 for unimodality

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is purely a numerical/simulation artifact (seed-to-seed solver noise) with no biological noise-generation mechanism, so CV should collapse toward the floor once compared against a condition expected to have minimal biological stochastic drivers (e.g. a ppGpp-clamped background that removes a major regulatory noise source).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, ppgpp_conc-clamped/basal (interventional control) would show CV of ribosome_conc statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal (Welch t < 2, effect_pct small), indicating the noise floor itself (not a biological ppGpp-driven noise mechanism) explains the dispersion seen in wildtype.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity reflects discrete bistable subpopulations (e.g. a stringent-response ON/OFF switch) rather than smooth intrinsic noise, so the population is actually a mixture of two physiological states.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Bimodality coefficient BC > 0.555 on pooled wildtype/basal ribosome_conc values, revealing a clean 2-cluster split (e.g. high-ribosome/low-ppGpp vs low-ribosome/high-ppGpp clusters) rather than one broad unimodal distribution.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seeds in the simulator represent independent draws of intrinsic stochastic processes (transcription/translation bursting, partitioning at division) and are a valid proxy for cell-to-cell variation in a real isogenic population.

ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged are adequate proxies for 'gene expression level' at the scope of this question (we are not screening every individual gene's mRNA/protein channel, but using a representative, broadly-influenced expression readout as the question is population/genome-general in framing).

Generation 3 is late enough for steady-state-like behavior to have developed from seed-specific stochastic trajectories, but early enough to avoid confounding from division-rate anomalies or culture drift.

The simulator's numerical/sampling noise floor is reasonably approximated via the power_mde check at n=8 seeds rather than requiring a separate deterministic (zero-noise) reference run, since no such reference design exists in the envelope.

Differences in CV or BC between wildtype/basal and ppgpp_conc-clamped/basal are attributable to the clamp's effect on a specific regulatory noise source (ppGpp-driven stringent response) rather than secondary growth-rate confounds; growth_rate and division_rate will be checked as auxiliary channels to confirm the clamp doesn't crash viability.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells growing in the same medium exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output (here operationalized via ribosome concentration and ppGpp concentration as proxies for expression-machinery levels), such that the population shows a coefficient of variation (CV) across isogenic replicate seeds that is well above the noise floor expected from measurement/sampling alone — i.e., intrinsic stochastic gene expression produces a broad, non-degenerate distribution of expression levels rather than a single sharp value.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic seeds under identical (wildtype/basal) conditions, the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and correspondingly ppgpp_conc) shows CV >= 15% and is consistent with a broad/bimodal-leaning spread (Sarle's BC > 0.555) rather than a tight unimodal point distribution, reflecting genuine cell-to-cell expression heterogeneity.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds under identical conditions produce effectively the same expression level: the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc is tight and unimodal (CV < 15%, BC <= 0.555), consistent with deterministic/averaged expression dominating over stochastic noise.

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: steady-state active ribosome concentration (uM) recorded per seed per generation

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: ppGpp concentration (uM) per seed, as a second expression-correlated readout

operational_defs.observable: distribution of per-seed channel values at a matched generation/timepoint
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) across seeds; Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed values

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Isogenic population shows CV(ribosome_conc) >= 15% across seeds (vs an assumed technical/sampling noise floor of ~5%), and pooled per-seed values give BC > 0.555, i.e. a markedly non-degenerate, possibly multimodal-leaning spread rather than a single sharp point value. Fraction of seeds falling outside +/-10% of the population mean expected to exceed 40%.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed ribosome_conc values at a matched late generation across 8 seeds; separately compute CV = sd/mean across those seeds. Reject H1 (fail to find heterogeneity beyond noise) if CV < 15% AND BC <= 0.555, indicating a tight unimodal distribution consistent with H0.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(ribosome_conc) < 15% and BC <= 0.555 across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds, i.e. isogenic cells converge on essentially the same expression level with no meaningful heterogeneity beyond measurement noise.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed ribosome_conc; CV computed alongside as secondary descriptive
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 (reject unimodal/H0); CV >= 15% as corroborating magnitude criterion

rivals.claim: Rival A (homeostatic buffering): Any apparent variance in ribosome_conc/ppgpp_conc across seeds is just simulator/sampling noise around a single homeostatic set point maintained by tight feedback (e.g., ppGpp-ribosome coupling), not genuine biological heterogeneity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, CV stays below ~15% and BC stays <=0.555 even across 8 independent seeds at matched generations — the wildtype/basal target design itself would show a tight unimodal cluster, directly matching the H0 refuting_result.

rivals.claim: Rival B (growth-rate-driven determinism): Apparent cell-to-cell variability in ribosome_conc is not intrinsic expression noise but is fully explained by seed-to-seed differences in growth_rate (faster growers simply have proportionally more ribosomes), i.e., a deterministic growth-law relationship rather than stochastic expression noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An OLS slope_ci fit of ribosome_conc on growth_rate across the 8 seeds would show a tight linear relationship with R^2 near 1 and residual CV (after regressing out growth_rate) collapsing below 15%, meaning the 'noise' is actually explained variance from growth rate, not stochastic gene expression.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's intrinsic stochasticity (seed-to-seed variation under identical parameters) is an adequate proxy for 'genetically identical cells expressing noise', since no explicit transcriptional bursting model is separately exposed.

Ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc are valid proxies for general 'gene expression level' given the platform does not expose a generic single-gene mRNA/protein noise channel at genome scale for this screen; results generalize qualitatively to the broader expression-noise question but are not a literal genome-wide promoter screen.
Matched generation/timepoint across seeds is required for a fair CV/BC comparison (avoid conflating cell-cycle-phase variance with expression noise).

The rrna_operon_knockout and relA knockout controls are assumed to perturb ribosome capacity and ppGpp synthesis respectively without introducing lethality before the matched generation, so that seeds remain comparable (division_rate will be checked to confirm viability).
residual_ambiguities: [construct_ambiguity] Should seed-to-seed variability in this simulator be interpreted as modeling genuine intrinsic biological expression noise (e.g., stochastic transcription/translation events), or merely as numerical/sampling variation in the simulation engine that happens to be a convenient stand-in for biological noise?

objection_ledger.issue: Rival A ('homeostatic buffering produces only noise-floor variance') is not actually a distinct rival — its distinguishing_result is identical to the H0 refuting_result of the main falsifier. A rival must be excluded by a result pattern the main test does NOT already cover; here Rival A and H0 collapse into the same test, so no extra work is done to exclude it.

The candidate_designs list includes rrna_operon_knockout and relA gene_knockout perturbations as 'controls' but the falsifier/decision_rule only references the wildtype/basal target and never specifies how results from the knockout arms feed into confirming/refuting H1 or excluding Rival B. Without a stated decision rule tying the relA knockout result to the growth-rate rival, these arms are decorative rather than load-bearing.

The claim says 'genetically identical cells' but the instrument only ever runs seeds of a whole-cell/population simulator parameterized identically — it's unclear whether 'seed-to-seed variation' in this simulator is meant to represent intrinsic stochastic gene expression (bursting, molecule-count noise) versus simply numerical/integration randomness unrelated to biology. Which does the user intend the seed variability to model?

Rival C's distinguishing_result is a double-bind: a sharp CV/BC drop confirms Rival C, but a 'partial' reduction 'proportional to the capacity cut' is claimed to support H1 instead. No threshold is given for what counts as 'proportional' vs 'collapsed', so essentially any intermediate result (the most likely outcome) can be post-hoc assigned to either side. This makes the rrna_operon_knockout arm's decision rule for excluding Rival C non-binding.

The seed-matching requirement ('matched generation/timepoint') assumes seeds reach the matched generation at comparable wall-clock/division counts despite growth-rate variability being part of what's measured; if growth rate itself varies across seeds, 'matched generation' and 'matched timepoint' are not the same alignment and the choice could materially affect CV/BC estimates. This is a minor but unaddressed auxiliary choice.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in the same medium show substantial cell-to-cell variation in gene expression (measured here via downstream proteome/physiology channels tied to expression state), not identical levels: specifically, wildtype replicate seeds under basal condition will show appreciable coefficient of variation (CV) in ribosome_conc and protein_mass across seeds/cells, with a non-trivial fraction of extreme outlier seeds, rather than a tight, near-deterministic single value.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds (same genotype, same basal medium), per-seed steady-state ribosome_conc (and protein_mass) values show substantial intrinsic variability: CV >= 15% across seeds, with the pooled distribution showing a non-negligible heavy-tailed/bimodal-leaning spread (Sarle's BC > 0.555 in at least one of the two channels) rather than collapsing to a single tight value.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds under identical basal conditions show only replicate/measurement noise: CV < 15% and the pooled distribution is unimodal (BC <= 0.555) in both ribosome_conc and protein_mass, i.e., expression level is effectively deterministic given genotype+environment.

operational_defs.construct: gene expression level in an isogenic population
operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc and protein_mass per seed at matched generation
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state values pooled across seeds; compute CV (sd/mean) and Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled values

operational_defs.observable: spread of per-seed channel values around the population mean
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds; BC for distribution shape

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: wildtype replicate seeds will show CV >= 15% in ribosome_conc and protein_mass (versus a naive near-zero/measurement-noise-only CV ~3-5% expected under strict determinism), and at least one channel will have BC > 0.555, consistent with a heavy-tailed or bimodal-leaning distribution rather than a single sharp value.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV (sd/mean) of ribosome_conc pooled across seeds for wildtype/basal (n=8 seeds, gen 3); also compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the same pooled values. Reject H1 (treat as H0/deterministic) if CV < 15% AND BC <= 0.555.
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled per-seed ribosome_conc CV < 15% and BC <= 0.555, i.e., isogenic seeds converge tightly to one value with no heavy-tail/bimodal structure, consistent with deterministic expression given genotype+environment.

test.statistic: bimodality_coefficient (BC) and CV
test.threshold: BC>0.555 OR CV>=15% required to support H1; refute if BC<=0.555 AND CV<15%

rivals.claim: Rival A: Apparent heterogeneity is purely a numerical/discretization artifact of the stochastic solver (extrinsic simulator noise), not biologically meaningful intrinsic noise; a rrna_operon_knockout (reducing ribosome capacity, hence buffering stochastic bursts) should SHRINK the CV if the heterogeneity were mechanistically tied to ribosome-synthesis bursting rather than solver artifact.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, rrna_operon_knockout/basal shows CV and BC statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal (no change in heterogeneity despite altered ribosome synthesis dynamics), implying the variance is solver noise unrelated to ribosome biogenesis stochasticity.

rivals.claim: Rival B: The variability reflects slow extrinsic physiological drift (e.g., growth-rate differences between seeds) rather than intrinsic transcription/translation noise at a fixed growth rate; i.e., growth_rate itself varies across seeds and ribosome_conc/protein_mass track growth_rate deterministically (a coupled, not independent, noise source).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival B is true, a slope_ci regression of ribosome_conc on growth_rate across seeds shows a tight linear relationship (slope CI excludes 0, high R^2), meaning ribosome_conc heterogeneity is fully explained by growth_rate heterogeneity rather than being an independent expression-noise phenomenon.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed stochastic variation in this simulator is intended to approximate biological intrinsic+extrinsic noise sources (transcription bursting, partitioning at division, metabolic fluctuation), not merely numerical integration error; we cannot fully disentangle solver artifact from biological noise within this simulator, so this is recorded as a scope caveat rather than chased further.

Seeds are treated as independent isogenic 'cells' sampled from the same genotype/environment distribution; cross-seed comparison at matched generation number is treated as a valid proxy for a population snapshot.

ribosome_conc and protein_mass are treated as adequate proxies for 'gene expression level' at the whole-proteome/physiology scale, since the instrument does not expose single-mRNA-species copy-number distributions directly in this configuration.

Growth conditions (basal media, generation count) are held fixed across seeds so that any observed spread is attributable to stochastic/intrinsic variability rather than deliberate environmental differences.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells growing in the same medium do NOT express a given gene at the same level: single-cell (seed-to-seed) protein output is substantially noisy (CV>=0.25), and part of that noise is 'extrinsic' -- i.e., it co-varies WITHIN matched seeds with shared physiological channels (ribosome_conc, growth_rate) rather than being an independent, gene-private fluctuation. Knocking out relA (removing stringent-response/ppGpp coupling to the growth machinery) should attenuate this within-seed covariation (and/or the shared-channel CV) relative to wildtype, because relA is a candidate conduit linking ribosome/growth state to expression noise, while leaving pure intrinsic birth-death noise on the target gene largely intact. Given n=8 seeds, the Pearson r estimate is noisy, so the decision rule now REQUIRES a bootstrap confidence interval on r (resampling seeds) rather than a bare point estimate, so that an |r| classification is only trusted if its 95% CI does not straddle the 0.3/0.5 decision boundary.
hypothesis.h1: Across 8 isogenic wildtype/basal seeds: (i) target-gene protein CV >= 0.25; (ii) ribosome_conc and growth_rate CV >= 0.10 across the SAME seeds; and (iii) the per-seed Pearson correlation r between target-gene protein level and ribosome_conc (paired by seed index) satisfies point estimate |r| >= 0.5 AND its bootstrap 95% CI (seed-resampling, >=1000 resamples) lower bound stays >= 0.3, evidencing genuine within-seed covariation (extrinsic sharing) that survives small-n sampling uncertainty. Additionally, in the relA knockout (same seeds/condition), the |r| point estimate drops below 0.3 with its bootstrap 95% CI upper bound staying < 0.5, and/or ribosome_conc CV drops by >=30% relative to wildtype (via welch_disconfirm |t|>=2), while target-gene CV remains >=0.20 (intrinsic noise persists), confirming relA's causal role in shared (extrinsic) noise generation at a resolution n=8 can actually support.
hypothesis.h0: Either (a) target-gene CV < 0.25 (near-deterministic expression); OR (b) target-gene CV is high but the wildtype |r| bootstrap 95% CI includes values < 0.3 (i.e., the apparent correlation is not distinguishable from chance given n=8, so sharing is not established); OR (c) relA knockout leaves |r| and ribosome_conc CV statistically unchanged from wildtype -- welch_disconfirm |t|<2 on ribosome_conc AND the relA-arm |r| bootstrap CI overlaps the wildtype CI -- meaning no causal stringent-response contribution to the shared-noise signature is detectable at this sample size.

operational_defs.construct: cell-to-cell expression variability (noise) of a gene
operational_defs.observable: per-seed protein copy number/concentration for target gene acrB under wildtype/basal, pooled across 8 seeds
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = std/mean) across seeds; per-seed spread from disconfirm

operational_defs.construct: extrinsic (shared, physiology-wide) noise, operationalized as within-seed covariation
operational_defs.observable: paired per-seed values of target-gene protein level and ribosome_conc (and growth_rate) from the SAME 8 seeds, matched by seed index
operational_defs.measure: Pearson r (via fit_relation) between the paired per-seed vectors, PLUS a bootstrap 95% CI on r obtained by resampling the 8 seed-pairs with replacement (>=1000 resamples); |r|>=0.5 with CI lower bound >=0.3 counts as reliably shared/extrinsic signal

operational_defs.construct: causal contribution of stringent response (RelA/ppGpp) to extrinsic noise sharing
operational_defs.observable: same paired per-seed measurements (target-gene protein, ribosome_conc) under gene_knockout/relA, basal, 8 seeds
operational_defs.measure: change in |r| (point estimate and bootstrap CI) and in ribosome_conc CV relative to wildtype; a causal role is supported if relA-arm |r| CI upper bound <0.5 while wildtype CI lower bound >=0.3 (non-overlapping classification), or ribosome_conc welch_disconfirm |t|>=2 with >=30% CV drop, while gene CV stays >=0.20

operational_defs.observable: wildtype or gene_knockout perturbation, identical params/condition, only seed index varied
operational_defs.measure: design labels wildtype/basal and gene_knockout/basal (relA), seeds=8 each

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: positive, nonzero and PARTIALLY SHARED cell-to-cell variability. Magnitude: wildtype target-gene protein CV ~0.25-0.40 across 8 seeds; ribosome_conc/growth_rate CV ~0.10-0.20; within-seed Pearson r(gene, ribosome_conc) ~0.5-0.7 with bootstrap 95% CI roughly [0.3, 0.85] (lower bound clears the 0.3 floor, supporting a reliably-shared, not merely coincidental, component). In the relA knockout: |r| point estimate drops to <0.3 with bootstrap CI upper bound <0.5 (non-overlapping with wildtype's CI), and/or ribosome_conc CV falls by >=30% (welch_disconfirm |t|>=2) relative to wildtype, while gene CV remains >=0.20, isolating the intrinsic component and demonstrating relA's causal contribution to the extrinsic/shared signature at a resolution n=8 seeds can actually discriminate.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1: on wildtype/basal (8 seeds), compute target-gene CV, ribosome_conc CV, growth_rate CV, Pearson r (fit_relation) between paired per-seed target-gene protein and ribosome_conc values, and a bootstrap 95% CI on that r via seed-resampling (>=1000 resamples). Reject H1's noise claim if gene CV<0.25 or if both ribosome_conc/growth_rate CV<0.10. Reject H1's SHARING claim if the |r| point estimate <0.5 OR the bootstrap CI lower bound <0.3 (i.e., CI straddles the decision boundary, so n=8 cannot support the classification). Step 2: welch_disconfirm comparing ribosome_conc, gene_knockout/basal (relA) vs wildtype/basal, across the same 8 seeds; also compute relA-arm |r| and its bootstrap CI. Reject the causal/relA part of H1 if |t|<2 AND the relA-arm CI overlaps the wildtype CI (no non-overlap, i.e. no detectable attenuation).
falsifier.refuting_result: Either target-gene CV<0.25 (near-deterministic), or wildtype |r| bootstrap CI lower bound <0.3 (sharing claim not supported above sampling noise), or the relA knockout shows |t|<2 vs wildtype on ribosome_conc AND its |r| CI overlaps wildtype's CI (no causal attenuation of sharing detectable) -- any of these disconfirms H1.

test.statistic: Welch t on ribosome_conc channel, gene_knockout/basal (relA) vs wildtype/basal across 8 matched seeds; paired Pearson r (fit_relation) plus bootstrap 95% CI (seed-resampling, >=1000 resamples) on target-gene protein vs ribosome_conc within each design
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for relA vs wildtype shift; wildtype |r|>=0.5 with bootstrap CI lower bound >=0.3; relA-arm |r| CI upper bound <0.5 (non-overlapping with wildtype CI) to confirm causal attenuation; wildtype gene CV>=0.25 and ribosome_conc/growth_rate CV>=0.10 required as baseline noise/sharing evidence

rivals.claim: Rival A (pure intrinsic noise / no extrinsic sharing): target-gene variability arises purely from local stochastic birth-death events; growth_rate/ribosome_conc stay tightly constant (CV<0.05) across seeds, or if they do vary, they are UNCORRELATED (bootstrap CI for |r| includes values near 0) with the target gene's per-seed values even though both show nonzero marginal CV.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Wildtype shows high gene CV (>=0.25) but the |r| bootstrap CI with ribosome_conc includes 0 or its lower bound stays below 0.3, across the matched 8 seeds -- marginal CVs may both be elevated by chance but show no reliably detectable within-seed covariation, disconfirming shared/extrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Rival B (deterministic/negligible noise -- underpowered seeding artifact): the simulator's steady-state kinetics make per-seed outcomes essentially identical regardless of gene; all channels (target gene, ribosome_conc, growth_rate) show CV<0.05 across the 8 seeds, and power_mde confirms n=8 is sufficient to detect even a 0.10 CV effect, so the near-zero observed CV is a true null, not underpowering.
rivals.distinguishing_result: All three channels show CV<0.05 and power_mde flags n=8 as adequate to detect CV>=0.10, confirming near-determinism rather than a measurement/power artifact.

rivals.claim: Rival C (ribosome/growth coupling exists but is NOT stringent-response/relA-dependent -- e.g., driven purely by cell-cycle/mass partitioning noise): wildtype shows high |r| (with CI lower bound >=0.3) between gene and ribosome_conc, but the relA knockout shows NO attenuation -- |t|<2 on ribosome_conc AND the relA-arm |r| CI overlaps the wildtype CI -- implying the shared extrinsic signal is generated by a relA-independent mechanism (e.g. stochastic partitioning at division) rather than the stringent response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA knockout arm reproduces wildtype's |r|>=0.5 (CI overlapping wildtype) and ribosome_conc CV within 10% of wildtype despite |t|<2, showing the extrinsic coupling persists independent of RelA/ppGpp, refuting the causal stringent-response mechanism while leaving the general extrinsic-noise claim (H1 parts i-ii) intact.

objection_ledger.issue: The relA knockout is listed as a 'candidate_design' but is never wired into a decision rule or predicted differential result. The falsifier and predicted_effect only reference wildtype/basal seeds; there is no stated comparison (e.g., relA-KO CV vs wildtype CV) that would let the relA arm actually discriminate extrinsic-noise-via-stringent-response from other sources. As written, the relA design is decorative -- it doesn't do interventional work in the decision rule.

The single-seed CV test (comparing target-gene CV to ribosome_conc/growth_rate CV within the SAME wildtype condition) cannot distinguish genuine extrinsic noise (a causal physiological driver of gene expression variability) from two independently noisy but uncoupled channels that happen to both exceed threshold by chance across only 8 seeds. The coupled-rival logic applies in reverse here: co-occurring CVs are being used as evidence of 'sharing' but no pairing/correlation across the SAME seeds (not just both having high marginal CV) is computed.

With only 8 seeds, the Pearson r estimate for |r|>=0.5 vs <0.3 thresholds has wide sampling variance; no power/CI justification (e.g., bootstrap CI on r or power_mde check) is given to show n=8 can reliably discriminate these r thresholds, risking a false accept/reject purely from small-sample noise.

all_rounds.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
all_rounds.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells simulated under identical media conditions (wildtype/basal) show substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity in growth rate and ppGpp concentration purely from intrinsic stochastic noise (gene expression, partitioning, timing), with growth_rate CV >= 15% and ppgpp_conc CV >= 20% across independent seeds — i.e., genetic identity and environmental identity do NOT imply phenotypic identity.
all_rounds.h1: Across independent stochastic seeds of the SAME genotype and SAME static condition (wildtype/basal), the per-seed distribution of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc has substantial dispersion (growth_rate CV >= 15%; ppgpp_conc CV >= 20%), reflecting genuine intrinsic noise rather than seed-to-seed numerical artifact.
all_rounds.h0: Per-seed variation in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc under wildtype/basal is negligible (CV < 5%), i.e. the simulator's stochastic seeds produce effectively identical phenotypes and any apparent spread is noise-floor/numerical.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel, per-seed endpoint value at final generation
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) across seeds; also per-seed spread from disconfirm output

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc channel, per-seed endpoint value
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) across seeds

operational_defs.observable: comparison of wildtype/basal seed spread vs a tighter-bound rrna_operon_knockout/basal condition (discriminating control) which perturbs ribosome capacity deterministically rather than stochastically
operational_defs.measure: welch_t and effect_pct between conditions; distinguishes intrinsic noise from a confound of unmodeled deterministic drift

all_rounds.predicted_effect: Direction: positive, nonzero dispersion. Magnitude: growth_rate CV approx 0.15-0.25 (15-25%) across 8 seeds at generation 3; ppgpp_conc CV approx 0.20-0.35 (20-35%) across the same seeds. Distribution shape: unimodal (not bimodal) around the population mean, consistent with continuous intrinsic noise rather than a discrete bistable switch.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed growth_rate at generation 3 across 8 seeds (same design, used as its own distribution since H1 is about within-condition spread, not a between-condition mean difference); compute CV = sd/mean. Separately, run power_mde to confirm 8 seeds can detect a CV of 0.15 given observed per-seed spread. Reject H1 (support H0) if growth_rate CV < 0.05 AND ppgpp_conc CV < 0.05, i.e. the min detectable effect is well below 0.15 yet observed CV sits in the noise floor.
falsifier.refuting_result: growth_rate CV < 0.05 and ppgpp_conc CV < 0.05 across 8 seeds at generation 3, with power_mde confirming the design had sufficient power to detect CV=0.15 (MDE < 0.15), indicating isogenic cells in identical conditions are effectively phenotypically identical modulo numerical noise.

all_rounds.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
all_rounds.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in identical (basal) medium exhibit substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity due to intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression/metabolism, such that the across-seed coefficient of variation (CV) of growth_rate is large (CV ≈ 10-20%) and the distribution of a noise-sensitive channel (fraction_trna_charged) departs from unimodality in a non-trivial fraction of seeds.
all_rounds.h1: Genetically identical cells (same genotype, same wildtype/basal condition, differing only in random seed) show growth_rate variability across seeds with CV >= 10%, substantially exceeding the technical/numerical noise floor, and pooled per-seed fraction_trna_charged values show detectable bimodality (Sarle's BC > 0.555) in at least one tested condition.
all_rounds.h0: Across-seed variability in growth_rate among isogenic wildtype/basal replicates is small (CV < 10%, consistent with numerical/sampling noise only) and fraction_trna_charged is unimodal (BC <= 0.555) across seeds; i.e., genetically identical cells behave essentially the same under identical conditions.

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged pooled across seeds
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed on pooled per-seed values

operational_defs.construct: stochastic vs mechanistic origin of heterogeneity
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc under a background knockout that dampens stochastic feedback (relA knockout removing ppGpp burst dynamics)

all_rounds.predicted_effect: Direction: isogenic replicates diverge measurably despite identical genotype/environment. Magnitude: growth_rate CV across 8 seeds ≈ 12-18% (vs an assumed numerical noise floor of <5% CV from a trivial duplicate-seed check), and pooled fraction_trna_charged across seeds shows BC > 0.555 in >=1 of 2 tested conditions (basal, acetate), indicating a non-trivial (>=20%) fraction of seed-distributions departing from unimodality.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: compute CV of growth_rate across 8 seeds for wildtype/basal; treat CV<10% as failing to show heterogeneity beyond noise floor. Secondary: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed fraction_trna_charged values across wildtype/basal and wildtype/acetate; reject H1's bimodality claim if BC<=0.555 in both conditions. Tertiary interventional check: Welch t of growth_rate CV (computed per-seed-bootstrap) between wildtype/basal and relA_knockout/basal; if CV is NOT reduced in the knockout (|t|<2), this undercuts a stringent-response-driven-noise mechanism but does not by itself refute heterogeneity existing.
falsifier.refuting_result: growth_rate CV across seeds < 10% (cells are effectively deterministic clones) AND fraction_trna_charged BC <= 0.555 in both basal and acetate conditions -> H1 refuted, isogenic cells behave essentially identically under matched conditions.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed fraction_trna_charged; CV computed directly on growth_rate across seeds
test.threshold: BC>0.555 in >=1 condition AND growth_rate CV>=10% jointly required to confirm H1; refute if CV<10% AND BC<=0.555 in all tested conditions

rivals.claim: Rival A (pure numerical/sampling noise): apparent cell-to-cell variability is an artifact of stochastic solver/integration noise, not biological heterogeneity, and would vanish or shrink with better-sampled aggregate channels unrelated to gene expression stochasticity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If variability is purely numerical, a non-expression channel like dry_mass (a slowly-integrating, heavily averaged readout) would show comparably large CV as growth_rate/fraction_trna_charged; the relA knockout (which does not touch the integrator) would show the SAME CV as wildtype. Finding dry_mass CV << growth_rate CV, or finding a growth_rate CV difference between wildtype and relA-knockout, argues against pure numerical artifact.

rivals.claim: Rival B (deterministic environmental micro-heterogeneity, not intrinsic stochasticity): apparent heterogeneity actually reflects deterministic sensitivity to slightly different initial conditions per seed (chaos-like divergence) rather than ongoing intrinsic molecular noise, and would be abolished by a background change that stabilizes the regulatory network (e.g., relA knockout damping ppGpp burst feedback) even though both are 'stochastic seeds' in the simulator.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival B is correct, the relA_knockout/basal design would show growth_rate CV collapse toward the <10% floor (because the destabilizing feedback loop, not general stochasticity, drove divergence), whereas if intrinsic noise is distributed across many independent reactions, relA knockout only modestly reduces CV, leaving it still >=10%.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed random number stream represents intrinsic biochemical/stochastic noise sources (reaction firing, partitioning at division) rather than purely numerical artifacts; we cannot fully disentangle deterministic chaos from genuine stochastic noise within this simulator, so this distinction is treated as an explicit scope caveat, not resolved experimentally here.
growth_rate and fraction_trna_charged are recorded at matched generation indices across seeds so that comparisons are not confounded by different absolute simulated time.

8 seeds provide sufficient power to estimate CV and detect a >=10% CV at the expected noise floor (~5%); this is a modest/exploratory n and may be underpowered for subtle (<10%) effects, which is acceptable given the scope of this screening-level claim.

relA knockout is viable under basal/acetate conditions for the generations simulated (does not crash before generation 3), allowing a valid CV comparison; division_rate will be checked to confirm viability was not confounded by lethality.
residual_ambiguities: [construct_ambiguity] Should growth_rate and fraction_trna_charged be sampled as a single instantaneous value at generation 3, or averaged over generations 1-3, for computing per-seed CV?

objection_ledger.issue: The 'numerical noise floor of <5% CV' used to justify the CV>=10% threshold is asserted but never actually measured in the design. No candidate_design computes CV from a trivial duplicate/identical-seed run (e.g., re-running the same seed twice) to establish what the floor actually is in this instrument; the 10% cutoff is simply assumed rather than calibrated.

Rival A's distinguishing test relies on comparing CV of growth_rate/fraction_trna_charged against CV of dry_mass as 'proxy for pure numerical noise.' But dry_mass, growth_rate, and fraction_trna_charged are all mechanistically coupled outputs of the same integrated cellular state in this model (mass accumulation depends on charged tRNA fraction and vice versa via ribosome allocation). A difference in their CVs could reflect differential sensitivity/amplification along the coupled network rather than true distinction between 'numerical artifact' and 'biological noise' channels. This comparison does not interventionally break the coupling between the channels being contrasted.

The decision rule includes a fallback ('if CV_floor cannot be driven near zero... fall back to absolute 10% threshold') that reintroduces an uncalibrated arbitrary cutoff if the primary calibration doesn't behave as expected. This is a reasonable contingency but slightly softens falsifiability; stating explicitly in advance which outcome triggers which branch (rather than post hoc) would tighten it.

It is unclear whether 'matched generation/timepoint' sampling for growth_rate and fraction_trna_charged means a single snapshot per seed or an average over the trajectory; this affects CV estimation but is a minor measurement detail the user could clarify.

all_rounds.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
all_rounds.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in the same medium (wildtype/basal) exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in growth rate and ppGpp concentration purely from intrinsic stochastic noise — i.e., across independent seeds (same genotype, same condition), growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show coefficient of variation (CV) comparable to or exceeding that seen between some mild genetic/environmental perturbations, rather than collapsing to a single deterministic value or to a phase-asynchrony artifact.
all_rounds.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) has CV >= 0.15 (i.e. >=15% relative spread) at BOTH generation 1 and generation 4 (not shrinking toward zero with more generations), demonstrating that genetically identical cells behave differently due to persistent intrinsic/extrinsic stochasticity rather than measurement artifact or transient phase asynchrony.
all_rounds.h0: Per-seed variability in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc under wildtype/basal is negligible (CV < 0.15) at the final generation, OR the CV observed at generation 1 collapses markedly (e.g. by >=50% relative) by generation 4, consistent with cells being near-deterministic / only transiently phase-asynchronous given fixed genotype and environment.

all_rounds.predicted_effect: Direction: positive, nonzero, persistent spread. Magnitude: CV(growth_rate) across seeds >= 0.15 at both gen1 and gen4 with CV_gen4/CV_gen1 ratio >= 0.8 (not collapsing), CV(ppgpp_conc) >= 0.20 at gen4, pooled distribution unimodal (BC <= 0.555), and |Pearson r| between per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc < 0.3 in magnitude is NOT required for H1 (coupling is plausible) but r effectively 0 combined with CV shrinking toward 0 as seeds increase would indicate artifact.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Compute CV of growth_rate across the 8 seeds at generation 4; reject H1 if CV < 0.15. Phase-asynchrony exclusion: compute CV of growth_rate across the same 8 seeds at generation 1 and at generation 4 (per-generation snapshots within the single 8-seed/4-generation run); reject H1 (favor phase-asynchrony rival) if CV_gen4/CV_gen1 <= 0.5 (i.e. spread collapses by half or more as generations proceed). Power check: run disconfirm(wildtype/basal_8seed vs wildtype/basal_4seed) via power_mde to confirm MDE at n=8 is below 0.15 so a null reading is not just underpowered. Bimodality check: BC over pooled gen4 growth_rate values; reject unimodal-noise framing if BC>0.555 (favors bistable rival).
falsifier.refuting_result: Either (a) CV(growth_rate) at generation 4 < 0.15 (near-homogeneous), or (b) CV_gen4/CV_gen1 <= 0.5 (variability is transient phase asynchrony, not persistent intrinsic noise), or (c) BC>0.555 (bimodal subpopulations, not continuous noise) -- any of these refutes the H1 as stated.

test.statistic: CV (sd/mean) of per-seed growth_rate at gen1 and gen4; ratio CV_gen4/CV_gen1; min detectable effect at n=8 seeds
test.threshold: CV_gen4 >= 0.15 AND CV_gen4/CV_gen1 >= 0.8 required to claim persistent real heterogeneity; reject H1 if CV_gen4 < 0.15, or ratio <= 0.5, or MDE at n=8 exceeds 0.15 (underpowered)

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is a numerical/sampling artifact of the simulator's stochastic solver rather than genuine biological noise (e.g. finite integration step, pseudo-random seed propagation creating trivial jitter with no biological correlate).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If artifact-only, growth_rate CV across seeds at gen4 would be <5%, AND the 4-seed vs 8-seed power_mde comparison would show CV shrinking toward zero as n increases rather than stabilizing at a biological plateau >=0.15; additionally |Pearson r| between per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc would be near 0 with no co-variation across seeds.

rivals.claim: Variability exists but is driven entirely by division-timing/cell-cycle phase asynchrony (extrinsic, deterministic-given-phase) rather than true intrinsic molecular noise -- i.e. cells are deterministic but seeds just sample different points in a deterministic oscillation, which washes out with more generations.
rivals.distinguishing_result: CV_gen4/CV_gen1 <= 0.5 within the same 8 seeds, i.e. growth_rate CV measured at generation 1 is markedly higher than at generation 4, showing convergence/averaging-out rather than a stable biological plateau of heterogeneity.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: In a genetically identical (isogenic) E. coli population growing in the same static medium, intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism produces substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic variability: across independent seeds (each seed = one isogenic lineage trajectory), instantaneous growth_rate and ppgpp_conc will show coefficient of variation (CV) on the order of 15-30%, not the <5% expected from deterministic, purely parameter-driven dynamics.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical fixed conditions (wildtype/basal), the per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) has CV >= 15%, reflecting genuine intrinsic noise rather than numerical/seed artifact.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) variability across isogenic wildtype/basal seeds is small (CV < 5%), consistent with near-deterministic trajectories where seed-to-seed differences are negligible noise floor, not biologically meaningful heterogeneity.

Under rrna_operon_knockout/basal, CV of growth_rate is predicted to rise further, by roughly 1.5-2x relative to wildtype/basal (e.g. ~30-40%), consistent with reduced ribosome copy number amplifying partitioning noise.

falsifier.refuting_result: Observed per-seed CV of growth_rate across seeds <5% (indistinguishable from a near-deterministic trajectory given the MDE at n=8), showing seed variation is numerical noise, not biological heterogeneity

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is a numerical/sampling artifact of stochastic solver seeding rather than biologically meaningful noise (no real intrinsic noise mechanism is simulated).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If artifact, CV of growth_rate should NOT scale with known noise-generating perturbations (e.g. rrna_operon_knockout, which reduces ribosome pool and should amplify partitioning noise) — i.e., welch_disconfirm of growth_rate CV between wildtype/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal shows |t|<2 (flat CV) rather than a significant increase.

rivals.claim: Variability is driven predominantly by a bistable/bimodal stringent-response switch (ppGpp) rather than continuous intrinsic noise — i.e., cells fall into two discrete growth states rather than a unimodal noisy distribution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc test on pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values yields BC > 0.555, indicating two subpopulations rather than a single noisy distribution.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed mechanism is intended to model genuine intrinsic biochemical noise (partitioning at division, transcriptional bursting) rather than purely numerical pseudo-randomness; this cannot be independently verified from outside the simulator and is taken as a scope caveat.
Matched-generation comparison (e.g. generation 3) across seeds is a valid snapshot for computing CV; transient early-generation effects are assumed to have relaxed by generation 3.

rrna_operon_knockout is assumed to reduce steady-state ribosome concentration without abolishing growth outright over 3 generations (division_rate not collapsing to 0), so that a CV comparison remains meaningful.

CV computed from 8 seeds is assumed sufficiently powered per power_mde to distinguish a 15%+ true CV from a <5% noise floor; if MDE at n=8 exceeds 15%, the test is underpowered and the result would be reported as inconclusive rather than a refutation.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: In a genetically identical (isogenic) E. coli population grown under constant conditions, intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression produces substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity: across independent stochastic replicates (seeds) of the wildtype/basal design, single-cell growth rate and ppGpp concentration show coefficient of variation (CV) well above pure measurement/model noise (CV >= 15%), and a non-trivial minority (~10-20%) of cells occupy a distinguishably slow-growing/high-ppGpp sub-state consistent with bimodal or heavy-tailed behavior rather than a single tight point value.
hypothesis.h1: Isogenic cells simulated with identical parameters but different stochastic seeds (wildtype/basal) show substantial heterogeneity in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds (CV >= 15%), and the pooled per-seed distribution is non-unimodal (bimodality coefficient > 0.555) or shows a heavy tail consistent with a distinguishable slow/high-stress subpopulation of roughly 10-20%.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic wildtype/basal replicates differ only by sampling noise: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc CV across seeds is low (<15%, comparable to numerical/measurement noise) and the pooled distribution is unimodal (bimodality coefficient <= 0.555), i.e. no distinguishable subpopulation structure.

operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) across seeds; bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed values

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values from wildtype/basal (n=8 seeds, 3 generations); reject H0 (unimodal/low-noise) if BC>0.555 OR if CV across seeds >=15%. As a complementary magnitude check, run power_mde to confirm n=8 seeds has adequate power to detect a 15% CV against the technical-noise floor established by wildtype/basal_control_small_n; if power is inadequate, treat any non-significant CV result as inconclusive rather than confirmatory of H0.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555 AND CV<15% for growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc), indicating the pooled distribution is unimodal and tight, i.e. seed-to-seed variation is within numerical-noise bounds and no distinguishable subpopulation exists.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) values
test.threshold: BC>0.555 to reject unimodality; also CV>=15% as a complementary magnitude check

rivals.claim: Apparent heterogeneity is an artifact of insufficient sampling / numerical integration noise, not biological stochasticity (the simulator's intrinsic noise model is too weak or the population is effectively deterministic given a seed).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, CV across seeds stays below ~5% (matching the technical-replicate-only control design wildtype/basal_control_small_n) and BC stays near 0.5 (unimodal), i.e. refuting_result is observed.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity exists but is driven by a single slow deterministic process (e.g. cell-cycle phase / division timing) rather than genuine stochastic gene-expression noise, so it would vanish or collapse to a narrow unimodal spread if ribosome/RNA synthesis noise were suppressed while cell-cycle timing noise remained.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout (reducing ribosome capacity/noise source) control still shows BC>0.555 and high CV driven purely by cell-cycle-linked timing, meaning the bimodal structure is NOT attributable to the stringent-response/translation noise pathway but to an orthogonal deterministic driver.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seed-to-seed variation in the simulator is intended to represent intrinsic biochemical stochasticity (reaction-event noise), not merely pseudo-random-number artifacts unrelated to biology.
3 generations is sufficient for growth_rate and ppgpp_conc to reach a quasi-steady distributional shape per seed; longer runs would only sharpen, not qualitatively change, the CV/bimodality signal.

The 'technical_replicate_only' wildtype/basal control approximates a numerical-noise floor (same seed/initial conditions re-run) to calibrate what CV is attributable to non-biological noise versus genuine stochastic divergence.

Division_rate differences across seeds are not confounding growth_rate comparisons (i.e., we are not conflating cells that fail to divide with slow-growing-but-viable cells); this will be checked as a secondary channel but is not the primary test.

n=8 seeds is assumed, pending a power_mde check, to be sufficient to detect a 15% CV against the technical-noise floor; if power_mde indicates otherwise, the null cannot be confidently accepted on a non-significant result.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells (isogenic, same medium) show substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity driven by intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism, even with zero genetic or environmental variation: across replicate seeds of the wildtype/basal design, growth_rate and ppgpp_conc will show high relative dispersion (CV) across seeds, not a tight point value.
hypothesis.h1: In an isogenic population simulated under identical media (wildtype/basal, varying only RNG seed), the across-seed coefficient of variation (CV) of growth_rate is >=15% and of ppgpp_conc is >=25%, i.e. intrinsic noise produces a broad, non-degenerate distribution of phenotypes rather than a single deterministic value.
hypothesis.h0: Across-seed CV of growth_rate is <5% and ppgpp_conc CV is <10% (i.e. the isogenic population is effectively homogeneous within replicate/numerical noise; apparent spread is simulation-numerical artifact, not biologically meaningful heterogeneity).

falsifier.decision_rule: power_mde check: compute per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across n=8 independent stochastic replicates of wildtype/basal; compute CV for each channel and the minimum detectable effect (MDE) at n=8 given per-seed spread. Reject H1 (treat as equivalence to H0) if observed CV(growth_rate) < 5% AND CV(ppgpp_conc) < 10%, i.e. if the observed spread falls below the MDE floor for meaningful heterogeneity at this sample size.
falsifier.refuting_result: Across-seed CV(growth_rate) < 5% and CV(ppgpp_conc) < 10%, with per-seed spread indistinguishable from a single tight cluster (observed spread below MDE for n=8), indicating the isogenic population is phenotypically homogeneous and the simulator's intrinsic noise is negligible at this scale.

test.threshold: CV(growth_rate)>=15% AND CV(ppgpp_conc)>=25% at n=8 seeds to reject H0; if observed CV falls below MDE floor (CV<5%/10%) treat as confirmed null

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic/numerical-floor hypothesis): any observed spread across seeds is purely numerical integration noise (solver tolerance, floating-point RNG seeding of initial conditions) with no biological meaning — the 'true' isogenic population is essentially a point mass.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, CV(growth_rate) and CV(ppgpp_conc) would sit at or below the numerical floor (<5%/<10%) even as generations increase from 1 to 4, and increasing generations would NOT increase spread (noise would not compound).

rivals.claim: Rival B (extrinsic/environmental confound hypothesis): any observed cell-to-cell spread is driven by extrinsic fluctuations in the shared medium/condition parameterization rather than intrinsic stochastic gene expression — i.e. it is condition-dependent, not an isogenic noise property.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, switching condition from basal to a different static medium (e.g. acetate) while holding genetics fixed would change the CV substantially (e.g. acetate CV very different from basal CV), showing spread tracks media parameterization rather than being an intrinsic, condition-independent property of the stochastic simulation engine.

rivals.claim: Rival C (ribosome-allocation/ppGpp coupling confound): apparent growth_rate heterogeneity is not independent intrinsic noise but a deterministic downstream consequence of noise in a single upstream regulatory node (ppGpp/RelA), which would be eliminated if that node's dynamics were removed.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, clamping ppgpp_conc to a fixed multiple of basal (ppgpp_conc perturbation, removing RelA/SpoT-driven fluctuation) should collapse growth_rate CV toward the numerical floor; growth_rate heterogeneity persisting at a similar CV even with ppGpp clamped would refute this rival and support broader intrinsic multi-node noise (H1).

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed RNG stream genuinely models intrinsic biochemical stochasticity (reaction timing, partitioning noise) rather than being a fixed deterministic trajectory re-labeled by seed.
8 seeds is sufficient replicate depth to estimate a CV with usable precision for a power_mde check; if power is insufficient the test will be read as inconclusive rather than confirming H0.
generations=3 is long enough for stochastic fluctuations to propagate into growth_rate/ppgpp_conc divergence but short enough to avoid confounding with population-level selection/outgrowth effects.

Numerical integration tolerance in the solver does not itself scale with seed count in a way that would spuriously inflate CV (i.e. the <5%/<10% floor is a reasonable estimate of pure numerical noise for this platform).
Clamping ppgpp_conc (Rival C control) does not itself introduce an independent large noise source that would confound interpretation of leftover growth_rate CV.

Basal media and 2-4 generations is long enough to reach a biologically meaningful (not merely numerical-transient) steady state for growth_rate and ppgpp_conc.
