hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells growing in the same static medium exhibit substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity driven by intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism — specifically, isogenic replicate seeds under wildtype/basal conditions will show a coefficient of variation (CV) in growth_rate across seeds of at least ~15%, and this variability will NOT collapse to near-zero even though all seeds share identical genotype and media.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic seeds (same genotype, same static condition), single-cell/single-run readouts of growth_rate (and correspondingly ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged) show substantial dispersion (CV >= 15%) that is reproducibly larger than the technical/numerical noise floor, i.e. genetically identical cells behave differently due to intrinsic stochasticity rather than genetic or environmental differences.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic seeds under the same condition show negligible dispersion in growth_rate (CV < 5%), consistent with the simulator producing near-deterministic, genotype-and-environment-determined trajectories with only trivial numerical noise; i.e. identical cells behave identically up to rounding-level noise.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel, per-seed values at a fixed generation under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = std/mean) of growth_rate across seeds; also computed for ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged as secondary channels

operational_defs.observable: dispersion that persists when genotype and condition are held fixed and only the stochastic seed varies
operational_defs.measure: per-seed spread statistic from the instrument plus welch_t comparing wildtype/basal seed-group mean growth_rate against a mechanistically-dampened control (rrna_operon_knockout/basal or ppgpp_conc clamp, which alters ribosome allocation/stringent-response switching)

operational_defs.observable: magnitude of CV relative to an a priori 5% numerical-noise threshold
operational_defs.measure: CV point estimate and its distance from the H0 threshold, with power_mde confirming the n=8-seed design has power to discriminate CV=15% from CV=5%

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Isogenic seeds under wildtype/basal will show growth_rate CV approximately 15-25% across 8 seeds at generation 3-4, i.e. a clearly non-trivial dispersion (at least 3x the 5% H0 noise floor), with correlated dispersion in ppgpp_conc (CV ~10-20%) and fraction_trna_charged (CV ~5-15%) reflecting shared stochastic translation/metabolic fluctuations rather than a flat, near-zero spread.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary test: welch_disconfirm comparing per-seed growth_rate of wildtype/basal (n=8) against rrna_operon_knockout/basal (n=8) at generation 3-4; the CV of wildtype/basal is computed directly from its own 8 seeds (no separate 'lownoise' design needed). Reject H0 (accept non-trivial heterogeneity) only if wildtype/basal CV>=15% AND power_mde confirms n=8 can discriminate CV=15% from CV=5% (MDE <= 10 percentage points). Reject H1 (support H0) if wildtype/basal CV<5%, or if power_mde shows n=8 is underpowered to tell 15% from 5% CV, in which case no claim can be made.
falsifier.refuting_result: Growth_rate CV across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds comes out <5% (e.g. 1-3%), indistinguishable from pure numerical rounding noise, showing isogenic cells behave essentially identically under fixed genotype/condition; equivalently power_mde shows the 8-seed design cannot distinguish 15% from 5% CV, so the predicted non-trivial heterogeneity cannot be substantiated.

test.statistic: CV (std/mean) of growth_rate across seeds; min detectable effect (MDE) at n=8 for the 15%-vs-5% CV contrast
test.threshold: reject H1 if CV<5% OR MDE at n=8 exceeds 10 percentage points (i.e., underpowered to separate the predicted 15% from the null 5%)

rivals.claim: Apparent heterogeneity is an artifact of insufficient replicate sampling / simulator RNG seeding rather than genuine biological noise amplification through the expression-ribosome-metabolism network.
rivals.distinguishing_result: power_mde shows the 8-seed design is well-powered (MDE well below 10 percentage points) yet observed CV still comes out <5%, meaning the low dispersion is real and not a sampling-power artifact.

rivals.claim: Observed variability is dominated by ppGpp/stringent-response bistability (a discrete alarmone-driven switch) rather than generic intrinsic expression noise, so clamping ppGpp should abolish most of the growth_rate spread.
rivals.distinguishing_result: ppgpp_conc/basal clamp (ppGpp held at 1x basal, damping stringent-response switching) shows growth_rate CV across seeds drops sharply (e.g. to <5%) relative to wildtype/basal's ~15-25%, implicating ppGpp bistability as the dominant noise source rather than distributed intrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is mainly a ribosome-capacity/allocation effect (extrinsic noise from varying ribosome numbers per cell) rather than intrinsic transcriptional/translational stochasticity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal (reduced ribosome capacity, less room for allocation variance) shows growth_rate CV collapses toward the H0 band (<5-8%) relative to wildtype, while fraction_trna_charged CV remains similar to wildtype, implicating ribosome-capacity variance rather than generic stochastic noise; this is the welch_disconfirm comparison used as the primary falsifier.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed stochastic RNG stream is the operational stand-in for 'intrinsic noise' in genetically identical cells; we cannot separate true biological stochasticity from numerical/discretization artifacts within the sim, so CV>=15% is interpreted as 'non-trivial heterogeneity' regardless of its deeper microphysical origin (explicit scope caveat).
Generation 3-4 is late enough for transient initial-condition effects to wash out but early enough to avoid confounding with population-level selection/extinction dynamics.

growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, and fraction_trna_charged are each computed consistently across the 8 seeds under steady-state charging (no kinetic-module toggling) so channel semantics stay fixed across conditions.

The rrna_operon_knockout and ppgpp_conc clamp controls are assumed to only perturb their targeted mechanism (ribosome capacity / alarmone level) without introducing confounded viability-crash dynamics that would dominate growth_rate variance for mechanistic reasons unrelated to noise (checked via division_rate as a secondary viability gate).

objection_ledger.issue: The decision_rule's PRIMARY test (CV>=15% vs <5%, verified by power_mde) determines H1/H0 using ONLY the wildtype/basal arm's own seed dispersion. The rrna_operon_knockout and ppgpp_conc clamp arms are introduced only in 'rivals' with their own informal distinguishing_result, but no pre-registered quantitative threshold (e.g., 'reject ribosome-capacity rival only if knockout CV drops below X and wildtype stays above Y') is given for those comparisons analogous to the primary falsifier. Without a pre-specified rule, a post hoc 'CV collapses' call risks being unfalsifiable in practice for the specific mechanistic attribution (intrinsic noise vs ribosome-allocation extrinsic noise vs ppGpp bistability).

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells simulated with identical genetic parameters but independent stochastic seeds (same wildtype/basal condition) exhibit substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc vary across seeds with a coefficient of variation (CV) of roughly 10-20%, reflecting intrinsic noise in gene expression/metabolism rather than any genetic or environmental difference.
hypothesis.h1: Across independent stochastic seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) has CV >= 10%, i.e. isogenic cells show measurable phenotypic heterogeneity attributable to intrinsic stochastic noise.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) values under wildtype/basal are effectively homogeneous: CV < 10%, consistent with seeds merely resampling numerical/integration noise rather than reflecting biologically meaningful heterogeneity.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel values recorded per seed at the end of each generation, pooled across seeds
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of growth_rate across seeds; secondary CV of ppgpp_conc across seeds

operational_defs.observable: spread of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds holding perturbation, condition, and generations fixed
operational_defs.measure: per-seed spread reported by disconfirm(), compared across wildtype/basal vs rrna_operon_knockout/basal vs gene_knockout(relA)/basal

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Wildtype/basal across 8 seeds: growth_rate CV ~ 12-18% (mean ~1.0 1/h, SD ~0.12-0.18), and ppgpp_conc CV ~ 15-25%, both well above a single crisp pass/fail cutoff of 10%. No systematic shift in the mean (seeds are isogenic), only increased spread relative to a near-zero numerical-noise floor. Under rrna_operon_knockout (ribosome capacity cut roughly in half), the artifact-rival specifically predicts growth_rate CV should COLLAPSE toward the numerical floor (CV drop by >=50% relative to wildtype, e.g. to <6%) because the regime that supposedly generates spurious variability is removed; H1 instead predicts CV stays within ~70-130% of the wildtype value (i.e. noise persists, since it is generic expression/partitioning noise, not a ribosome-capacity artifact).

falsifier.decision_rule: Single crisp cutoff: compute CV of growth_rate across 8 seeds for wildtype/basal via disconfirm(); H1 requires CV>=10% (reject H0 if so, accept H0/refute H1 if CV<10%, no dead zone). Separately, compare wildtype/basal CV to rrna_operon_knockout/basal CV using welch_disconfirm on growth_rate (|welch_t|>=2 for a significant difference in the underlying per-seed means/variance structure) AND require the rrna_operon_knockout CV to drop by >=50% relative to wildtype CV to count as support for the ribosome-capacity-artifact rival instead of H1.
falsifier.refuting_result: Observed wildtype/basal growth_rate CV is <10% (seeds behave as near-numerically-identical), OR the rrna_operon_knockout CV collapses to <50% of the wildtype CV (supporting the artifact rival that heterogeneity is a ribosome-capacity-regime effect, not generic intrinsic noise).

test.statistic: CV (SD/mean) of growth_rate across seeds for wildtype/basal vs rrna_operon_knockout/basal; Welch t on per-seed growth_rate values between the two designs
test.threshold: Pass H1 only if (a) wildtype CV>=10% (single cutoff, no dead zone) and (b) rrna_operon_knockout CV >= 50% of wildtype CV (i.e. does NOT collapse) -- |welch_t|>=2 used to confirm the two designs' per-seed growth_rate distributions are statistically distinguishable when checking (b)

rivals.claim: Apparent heterogeneity is an artifact of a specific ribosome-capacity parameter regime, not genuine generic stochastic noise -- removing ribosome-allocation slack (rrna_operon_knockout) should collapse the spread toward the numerical floor if the rival is true.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under rrna_operon_knockout/basal, growth_rate CV drops to <50% of the wildtype/basal CV (e.g. from ~15% to <7.5%), consistent with heterogeneity being a regime-specific artifact of excess ribosome capacity rather than generic intrinsic noise; H1 is refuted in this branch.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is driven mainly by ppGpp/stringent-response pathway stochasticity specifically (a single dominant noise source funneling through RelA), not generic whole-proteome stochastic expression noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under gene_knockout(relA)/basal, if growth_rate CV collapses substantially (e.g. to <50% of wildtype CV) while in wildtype ppgpp_conc CV is much larger (>2x) than growth_rate CV and tracks per-seed growth_rate rank order, that supports ppGpp-specific stochasticity as the dominant driver; if growth_rate CV in the relA knockout remains >=70% of the wildtype value, generic intrinsic noise (not ppGpp-specific) is supported instead.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed stochasticity (random number stream per seed) is intended to represent biologically meaningful intrinsic noise (expression bursting, partitioning at division, etc.), not purely numerical integration artifacts -- this cannot be fully disentangled within the simulator and is recorded as a scope caveat.

8 seeds x 3 generations gives adequate replicate power to estimate a CV in the 10-20% range and to detect a >=50% CV reduction between wildtype and rrna_operon_knockout; if the empirical per-seed spread reported by disconfirm() is noisier than expected, generations/seeds may need to be scaled up in a follow-up.

growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are read under steady-state charging (ribosome_conc and rela_conc also available) for wildtype and rrna_operon_knockout; the relA knockout control relies on ppgpp_conc/rela_conc still being recorded appropriately for a gene_knockout perturbation.

Division_rate is assumed to remain at or near 1.0 for wildtype/basal and the two controls over 3 generations (no lethality), so growth_rate heterogeneity is not confounded by differential viability; this should be checked post hoc via the division_rate channel.

A single crisp 10% CV cutoff (replacing the prior 5-10% dead zone) is treated as the pre-registered decision boundary; no additional tie-breaking rule is needed because every observed CV value now maps unambiguously to accept or reject H1.

objection_ledger.issue: The rrna_operon_knockout control for rival 1 (ribosome-capacity artifact) is not actually decisive: rrna_operon_knockout changes the mean ribosome allocation regime but doesn't cleanly isolate 'is noise generic vs regime-specific' -- both H1 and the rival predict 'CV changes somehow' under a different parameter regime, since almost any claim about noise could be rationalized post hoc whether CV goes up, down, or stays the same under a knockout that itself shifts the operating point. The design needs a stated, specific directional prediction under rrna_operon_knockout that the artifact-rival would make differently from H1, otherwise any outcome is consistent with 'heterogeneity is noise.'

The decision_rule creates a gap between 5% and 10%: if observed CV lands at, say, 7%, neither 'reject H1' (CV<5%) nor the stated pass threshold (CV>=10%) formally fires, leaving an unadjudicated zone. This should be tightened to a single crisp cutoff (or pre-registered monotonic rule) so every possible outcome maps to accept/reject.

The relA-knockout rival test (ppGpp-specific stochasticity vs generic noise) only uses a CORRELATIONAL signature within wildtype (ppgpp_conc CV >2x growth_rate CV and tracking per-seed rank order) plus an interventional relA knockout threshold. The rank-order tracking criterion is still a co-movement/correlation check between two mechanistically coupled channels (ppgpp_conc and growth_rate both respond to ribosome/charging state), so that piece of the distinguishing_result doesn't itself exclude the rival -- only the relA knockout CV-collapse criterion does the real interventional work. This is minor since the knockout arm is present, but the correlational tie-breaker should be dropped or explicitly deprioritized relative to the interventional relA result.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells simulated with identical genotype and media (wildtype/basal) display substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity driven by intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism, such that growth_rate and ppgpp_conc vary across seeds with coefficient of variation (CV) on the order of 10-20%, well above the near-zero variation expected if the network behaved deterministically.
hypothesis.h1: Across many isogenic replicate seeds (same genotype, same static media), single-cell-level readouts (growth_rate, ppgpp_conc) show substantial dispersion (CV >= 10%) that is NOT explained by condition/media differences, reflecting genuine intrinsic noise in the stochastic simulation.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds under identical condition show negligible dispersion (CV < 5%) in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc, i.e. the simulator's stochastic kinetics produce effectively deterministic, reproducible trajectories indistinguishable from seed-to-seed numerical jitter.

operational_defs.construct: phenotypic heterogeneity among genetically identical cells
operational_defs.observable: per-seed endpoint values of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc under wildtype/basal across many seeds
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of each channel pooled across seeds; also per-seed spread reported by disconfirm

operational_defs.observable: dispersion of growth_rate/ppgpp_conc across seeds that are identical in genotype, condition, and generations
operational_defs.measure: CV magnitude and bimodality_bc shape of the pooled distribution

operational_defs.construct: whether heterogeneity is ribosome-allocation/ppGpp-mechanism-dependent vs generic numerical noise
operational_defs.observable: comparison of CV in a relA-knockout background (stringent response abolished) vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of ppgpp_conc and growth_rate CV/mean between relA_knockout/basal and wildtype/basal

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Pooled across >=8 seeds, growth_rate and ppgpp_conc each show CV in the 10-20% range under wildtype/basal (vs <5% expected under H0 numerical-jitter-only); the pooled per-seed distribution is approximately unimodal (bimodality_bc <= 0.555) at this single condition, consistent with continuous intrinsic noise rather than discrete subpopulations.

falsifier.decision_rule: power_check: run wildtype/basal with 8 seeds; compute CV of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds. Also run bimodality_bc on the pooled per-seed growth_rate values. Reject H1 (heterogeneity claim) if CV < 5% for both channels (i.e. effect is at or below the min detectable effect at n=8, so dispersion is indistinguishable from numerical jitter).
falsifier.refuting_result: CV < 5% for growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across the 8 seeds, with per-seed spread reported by disconfirm showing no seeds deviating beyond ~1-2% of the mean -- indicating the simulator produces near-deterministic trajectories under identical genotype/condition.

test.statistic: CV (SD/mean) of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds; min detectable effect at n=8
test.threshold: CV < 5% => H0 not rejected (refutes H1); CV >= 10% => H1 supported

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is driven by the stringent response / ppGpp feedback loop amplifying small fluctuations in charged-tRNA into large growth-rate swings, not generic intrinsic noise throughout the whole network.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In relA_knockout/basal (stringent response abolished), CV of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc collapses toward the H0 range (<5%) relative to wildtype/basal, showing the ppGpp loop was the main noise amplifier rather than noise being uniformly distributed across all pathways.

rivals.claim: Observed cell-to-cell differences are an artifact of transient relaxation from initial conditions (deterministic chaos / unconverged transients) rather than persistent intrinsic stochastic noise, so dispersion should shrink with more generations as cells converge to the same attractor.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Running wildtype/basal for 4 generations vs 1 generation shows CV decreasing substantially (e.g. from ~15% to <5%) with generation number, indicating transient convergence rather than sustained stochastic heterogeneity.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed random number stream constitutes the intended source of 'intrinsic noise' (distinct from numerical integration error), and seeds are treated as independent isogenic replicates.
growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are read at matched simulated time/generation across seeds so comparisons are not confounded by cell-cycle phase differences.
CV is computed on endpoint (or matched-generation) values pooled across the 8 seeds; no additional smoothing or outlier removal is applied.

The relA_knockout control isolates the stringent-response contribution without being confounded by basal growth defects large enough to change division_rate (checked via division_rate channel as a viability sanity check).

Whether deterministic chaos vs genuine stochastic noise underlies any residual dispersion at 4 generations is not resolvable by this simulator; this is recorded as a scope caveat rather than pursued further.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: In a genetically identical (isogenic) E. coli population grown under constant conditions, intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism produces substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity: across isogenic replicate seeds, single-cell growth rate and ppGpp concentration show a coefficient of variation (CV) that is large relative to measurement/model noise (growth_rate CV ~15-25%, ppgpp_conc CV ~20-30%), and this spread is not an artifact of batch/condition differences but emerges purely from stochastic seed-to-seed variation under one fixed condition.
hypothesis.h1: Under a single fixed condition (wildtype/basal), isogenic replicate seeds exhibit growth_rate and ppgpp_conc distributions with CV >= 15%, i.e. meaningfully dispersed beyond what a tight deterministic model would predict (CV < 5%).
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds under wildtype/basal show growth_rate and ppgpp_conc CV < 5% (effectively deterministic, noise-free behavior); any larger spread reflects only numerical/sampling noise, not biologically meaningful heterogeneity.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed instantaneous growth_rate (1/h) at a fixed generation, pooled across seeds; compute mean, SD, CV = SD/mean

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed ppgpp_conc (uM) at a fixed generation, pooled across seeds; compute CV

operational_defs.construct: whether spread is noise vs batch artifact
operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: fraction of seeds that complete division by final generation, used to confirm seeds are viable/comparable so spread isn't driven by partial lethality

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Isogenic seed-to-seed distributions of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are unimodal but broad: growth_rate CV ~15-25% and ppgpp_conc CV ~20-30% across >=8 seeds under wildtype/basal, i.e. roughly 3-5x larger than a null CV of <5% expected from a near-deterministic model.

falsifier.decision_rule: power_check: compute per-seed CV of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds; treat H0 (CV<5%, near-deterministic) as supported only if the observed CV is below the minimum detectable effect (MDE) floor for n=8; if observed CV >=15% and exceeds MDE, reject H0 (near-determinism) in favor of H1 (substantial intrinsic heterogeneity)
falsifier.refuting_result: Observed CV for growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across the 8 seeds is <5% (or indistinguishable from the MDE floor), indicating isogenic cells behave near-identically and heterogeneity is negligible

test.statistic: CV (SD/mean) per channel across seeds; MDE at n=8
test.threshold: reject H0 if observed CV >= 15% AND CV exceeds MDE for n=8

rivals.claim: Apparent heterogeneity is just numerical/simulation noise (RNG artifacts), not biologically grounded stochasticity in gene expression/metabolism.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV is driven by RNG artifacts rather than biology, increasing seeds should not change the shape of the distribution in a biologically structured way, and a bimodality test would show no structured substructure -- bimodality_bc would be near 1/3 (unimodal, unstructured), consistent with pure noise either way; this rival is hard to fully separate from H1 since both predict unimodal spread, so it is treated as an auxiliary caveat rather than a cleanly falsifiable rival.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is bimodal (two subpopulations, e.g. growth-arrested vs growing), not a single broad unimodal distribution -- i.e. cells fall into discrete phenotypic states rather than continuous noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed growth_rate values exceeds 0.555, indicating two distinct clusters rather than one noisy unimodal population; this would refute the 'continuous noise, unimodal' framing of H1 even if overall CV is still elevated.

rivals.claim: Any observed spread is driven by division/viability differences (some seeds fail to divide or divide late), not by continuous intrinsic noise in growing cells.
rivals.distinguishing_result: division_rate differs substantially across seeds (e.g. some seeds <1.0 while others =1.0), showing the CV is confounded by partial lethality/division defects rather than reflecting homogeneous-population noise.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed channel values are sampled at a matched generation/timepoint across seeds so differences reflect seed-to-seed (intrinsic) variability, not developmental-stage mismatch.

The simulator's seed-to-seed variation is intended to represent genuine stochastic/intrinsic noise (molecular-count fluctuations), not merely numerical integration error; this cannot be fully disentangled within the simulator and is treated as a scope caveat.
8 seeds is accepted as a modest but adequate replicate count to estimate CV and run a power_mde check; larger n would tighten the MDE but is deferred to a follow-up scale-up.

division_rate near 1.0 across seeds is required to confirm the population is not confounded by partial lethality; if division_rate varies sharply, CV estimates are reinterpreted cautiously per rival 3.

params.note: power_check reference uses same design; power_mde computed on this same dataset to establish MDE for n=8

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells simulated under identical media conditions exhibit substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity that exceeds the simulator's baseline numerical-noise floor: across stochastic replicate seeds of the wildtype/basal condition, growth rate and ppGpp concentration show coefficient-of-variation (CV) >= 15%, at least 3x the CV of a mass-balanced reference channel (dry_mass). This claim is deliberately agnostic between intrinsic gene-expression stochasticity and extrinsic per-seed initialization differences as the ultimate SOURCE of that excess variance -- the instrument cannot adjudicate that split -- but asserts the excess dispersion itself is a reproducible, mechanism-linked (RelA/ppGpp-pathway-modulated) feature of the simulation, not a channel-agnostic solver artifact.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic seeds (same genotype, same condition), the per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) has CV >= 15%, exceeding the dry_mass noise floor by >=3x, AND this excess variance is partially attributable to the RelA/ppGpp pathway specifically (not merely a generic per-seed initialization effect that would equally inflate an unrelated channel): relA knockout should measurably shift CV(ppgpp_conc) toward the floor while leaving dry_mass CV unchanged in both conditions, demonstrating the excess is channel-specific and mechanism-linked rather than a uniform extrinsic inflation applied to all channels alike.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic seeds under identical condition show negligible dispersion (CV < 15%, or CV within 3x of the dry_mass floor) for growth_rate/ppgpp_conc, OR the excess dispersion (if present) is uniform extrinsic/initialization noise that also inflates dry_mass variance proportionally and is unaffected by relA knockout -- i.e., a channel-agnostic noise source rather than a RelA/ppGpp-pathway-linked one.

operational_defs.observable: wildtype/basal perturbation replicated across independent stochastic seeds, no genetic or media perturbation
operational_defs.measure: per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc time series, summarized as end-of-run (or steady-state window) values

operational_defs.observable: spread of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds within the same design
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) across seeds; also Sarle's bimodality coefficient to check for discrete subpopulations

operational_defs.observable: CV of dry_mass across wildtype/basal seeds, a near-conserved mass-balanced channel not specifically coupled to the stringent-response pathway, used as a shared proxy for whatever generic (numerical OR extrinsic-initialization) noise affects all channels
operational_defs.measure: CV(dry_mass) across the same 8 seeds, under BOTH wildtype and relA-knockout, as the empirical MDE floor that CV(growth_rate)/CV(ppgpp_conc) must exceed to count as a positive result

operational_defs.construct: channel-specificity / mechanistic (vs uniform extrinsic) origin of excess variance
operational_defs.observable: comparison of dry_mass CV (should stay ~constant across wildtype vs relA-knockout if extrinsic/initialization noise is uniform and channel-agnostic) against ppgpp_conc CV (should collapse toward the floor under relA-knockout if the excess is pathway-specific)
operational_defs.measure: CV(dry_mass, wildtype) vs CV(dry_mass, relA-knockout) [expect no meaningful shift -- rules out a global extrinsic-noise-amplification confound from the KO itself] jointly with CV(ppgpp_conc, wildtype) vs CV(ppgpp_conc, relA-knockout) [expect collapse toward floor]

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Isogenic wildtype seeds under basal condition show CV(growth_rate) >= 15% and CV(ppgpp_conc) >= 15% across 8 seeds, each >=3x the CV(dry_mass) floor (expected CV(dry_mass) <5% and essentially unchanged, within ~20% relative, between wildtype and relA-knockout, ruling out a KO-induced global extrinsic inflation). Under relA-knockout, CV(ppgpp_conc) is predicted to drop by >=50% toward the dry_mass floor (demonstrating channel-specific, pathway-linked excess variance) while CV(dry_mass) itself stays flat across the two conditions. The pooled distribution is NOT strongly bimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555) at this scale. This is a within-design dispersion claim about the EXISTENCE and partial mechanistic basis of excess variance, not a claim about intrinsic-vs-extrinsic ultimate origin (out of scope per r2.1).

falsifier.decision_rule: power_check: compute CV(growth_rate) and CV(ppgpp_conc) across the 8 wildtype seeds at steady state; compute CV(dry_mass) on the same seeds as the floor. Heterogeneity is supported only if CV(growth_rate) >= 15% AND CV(growth_rate) >= 3x CV(dry_mass). Separately compute CV(dry_mass) under relA-knockout/basal: if CV(dry_mass, relA-KO) differs from CV(dry_mass, wildtype) by >50% relative, treat the floor comparator as confounded (inconclusive) rather than refuted. Also run bimodality_bc on pooled per-seed growth_rate values (reject bimodal if BC<=0.555).
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(growth_rate) < 15%, or CV(growth_rate) is within 3x of CV(dry_mass) (indistinguishable from the floor) -- heterogeneity claim refuted or deemed an artifact of generic (numerical or uniform extrinsic) noise rather than a detectable, channel-differentiated phenomenon

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation_ratio_to_noise_floor
test.threshold: CV(growth_rate) >= 15% AND CV(growth_rate)/CV(dry_mass) >= 3; else inconclusive/refuted

rivals.claim: Apparent spread across seeds is purely generic (numerical OR uniform extrinsic-initialization) noise affecting all channels roughly equally, not a channel-differentiated or mechanism-linked phenomenon -- i.e., CV(growth_rate)/CV(ppgpp_conc) should be of the same order as CV(dry_mass), AND this ratio should be insensitive to relA knockout.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(growth_rate)/CV(ppgpp_conc) are NOT meaningfully larger than CV(dry_mass) (ratio <3x), OR if CV(dry_mass) itself shifts substantially between wildtype and relA-KO (indicating the KO perturbs the shared noise floor rather than a specific pathway), the generic-noise rival is supported and H1 is refuted.

rivals.claim: Observed variance in ppgpp_conc/growth_rate is driven specifically by stochastic firing of the RelA/SpoT stringent-response machinery, not extrinsic per-seed initialization differences acting through a mass-insensitive channel -- so removing relA should collapse ppgpp_conc variance toward the dry_mass floor while dry_mass CV itself stays flat.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under relA-knockout/basal, if CV(ppgpp_conc) collapses toward the dry_mass floor while CV(dry_mass) is unchanged from wildtype, this supports a RelA-specific, mechanism-linked noise source for ppGpp; if CV(ppgpp_conc) does NOT collapse (stays >=15% and >=3x the floor) despite relA removal, that implicates an extrinsic or RelA-independent source and only the weaker 'excess-variance-exists' claim survives, not the mechanism-linked part of H1.

auxiliary_assumptions: dry_mass is a reasonable shared proxy for generic (numerical or extrinsic-initialization) noise because it is a near-conserved, mass-balanced quantity; checking its CV stability across wildtype vs relA-knockout partially (not fully) tests whether it is immune to confounding by the specific intervention used, though it cannot rule out ALL possible mass-insensitive extrinsic channels.
8 seeds is sufficient to estimate CV and run Sarle's BC descriptively at this exploratory scale; a human will scale seeds up before drawing strong population-level conclusions.
The steady-state (or end-of-run) window used for summarizing growth_rate/ppgpp_conc is comparable across seeds (no systematic phase-of-cycle confound at generation 3).

relA gene_knockout is assumed to be mechanistically simulated (removes RelA-driven ppGpp synthesis) by the platform; if the KO is not mechanistically implemented, the relA control is treated as inconclusive rather than falsifying, per the simulator's known scope limits.

Whether the residual variance (if any) reflects deterministic chaos vs genuine intrinsic stochastic noise vs extrinsic per-seed initialization differences is NOT resolvable by this instrument and is explicitly out of scope for this test; the hypothesis claims only that excess variance exists and is at least partially channel-specific/mechanism-linked, not that it is purely intrinsic gene-expression noise.

objection_ledger.issue: The rrna_operon_knockout control is meant to distinguish 'genuine biological noise' from 'numerical/solver artifact', but the predicted direction (reduced ribosome capacity should AMPLIFY noise if biological, and the rival predicts flat/shrink) is not independently justified -- a biological noise-buffering mechanism (e.g., feedback control stabilizing growth rate) could equally predict flat or reduced CV under rrna knockout, which would be misread as supporting the solver-artifact rival. The test does not actually isolate 'numerical artifact' from 'biological noise that happens to be buffered'.

The second rival (hidden extrinsic/environmental heterogeneity) is distinguished only by comparing CV magnitudes across ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged, and growth_rate -- but these channels are mechanistically coupled via the stringent-response/charging feedback loop and will co-vary regardless of whether the root cause is intrinsic expression noise or extrinsic per-seed initialization differences. This is a coupled-rival comparison, not an interventional control; it cannot attribute the variance to intrinsic gene-expression stochasticity versus extrinsic seed-level media/initialization differences.

The CV>=15% threshold is stated as exceeding 'the MDE floor for n=8 replicates' but no actual MDE calculation, baseline noise estimate, or power analysis is shown -- making it unclear whether 15% is a principled detection threshold or an arbitrary number that could trivially pass or fail depending on solver seed variance unrelated to the hypothesis.

The relA-knockout control tests whether ppGpp-specific variance depends on RelA, but it does not establish that dry_mass is actually immune to the SAME extrinsic/initialization noise sources (e.g. per-seed differences in initial metabolite pools) that could inflate growth_rate/ppgpp_conc CV. If dry_mass is buffered by mass-conservation constraints in the solver regardless of biological vs numerical origin, a low CV(dry_mass) does not prove growth_rate's extra variance is biological rather than extrinsic-but-channel-specific noise (e.g. noise entering through translation/charging state initialization that happens not to perturb total mass). The floor comparison addresses solver-artifact vs biological noise reasonably, but does not fully exclude 'extrinsic per-seed heterogeneity acting through a mass-insensitive channel' as a rival to 'intrinsic gene-expression stochasticity'.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells growing in the same fixed medium do NOT express a given gene/protein at the same level: isogenic wildtype seeds show substantial cell-to-cell variability in a representative protein's mass/abundance (operationalized here as protein_mass, the closest available whole-cell proxy for single-gene product abundance since no per-gene reporter channel is exposed), and a majority of this variability is 'extrinsic' — i.e., driven by shared, cell-level physiological state (ribosome capacity, growth rate) rather than being gene-intrinsic birth-death jitter uncorrelated with those state variables. Because protein_mass and ribosome_conc are mechanistically coupled by construction (ribosomes are protein; more ribosome mechanically yields more translation flux), the diagnostic evidence for 'extrinsic' noise is NOT the raw protein_mass~ribosome_conc slope (which would be positive under almost any growth model) but whether a perturbation that decouples stochastic ribosome-number fluctuations from the rest of cell physiology (rrna_operon_knockout, which caps ribosome supply and should compress cell-to-cell ribosome/growth-rate variance) correspondingly COMPRESSES protein_mass CV — evidence that protein variability rides on shared physiological fluctuations rather than being a fixed gene-intrinsic floor.
hypothesis.h1: In wildtype/basal, per-seed protein_mass (sampled at a fixed generation across >=6 isogenic seeds) has CV >= 0.20, i.e., cells are measurably non-identical in protein content despite shared genotype/medium. Furthermore, this variability is substantially extrinsic/shared-physiology-driven: capping ribosome supply via rrna_operon_knockout should compress BOTH ribosome_conc/growth_rate variance AND protein_mass CV by at least ~40% relative to wildtype/basal (not leave protein_mass CV unchanged), because a true gene-intrinsic-dominated noise source would be insensitive to this background perturbation.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic wildtype seeds show tightly clustered protein_mass (CV < 0.10), OR — if CV >= 0.10 is observed in wildtype — that variability is gene-intrinsic/fixed and does NOT respond to the rrna_operon_knockout manipulation: protein_mass CV under rrna_operon_knockout is statistically indistinguishable from (or not meaningfully lower than) wildtype/basal CV, i.e., Welch t comparing the two conditions on protein_mass is not significant, consistent with the observed spread being sampling/equilibration noise or a fixed intrinsic floor rather than shared extrinsic physiological covariation.

operational_defs.construct: cell-to-cell expression variability (total noise) for 'a given gene'
operational_defs.observable: per-seed value of protein_mass sampled at a fixed generation across wildtype seeds (best available whole-cell proxy for single-gene product abundance; no per-gene reporter channel is exposed by the instrument, so the claim is explicitly scoped to this proxy, noted as an auxiliary assumption)
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) of per-seed protein_mass, via the instrument's per-seed spread statistic

operational_defs.construct: extrinsic noise / shared physiological driver of variability
operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc and growth_rate channels per seed, and how protein_mass CV changes when ribosome supply is perturbed at the population level via rrna_operon_knockout
operational_defs.measure: welch_t comparison of protein_mass CV (and underlying per-seed values) between wildtype/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal; a significant REDUCTION in protein_mass spread under the ribosome-capping perturbation is the diagnostic signature of extrinsic-noise dependence, avoiding the definitional-coupling problem of a raw protein_mass~ribosome_conc slope

operational_defs.observable: residual protein_mass variability that persists even after ribosome supply is capped (i.e., the portion of CV NOT eliminated by rrna_operon_knockout)
operational_defs.measure: protein_mass CV under rrna_operon_knockout/basal, reported descriptively as the intrinsic floor once extrinsic ribosome-driven variance is suppressed

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Wildtype/basal protein_mass CV across 8 seeds >= 0.20 (vs null <0.10). Under rrna_operon_knockout/basal, protein_mass CV drops by >=40% relative to wildtype (e.g., from ~0.25 to <=0.15), and this difference is detected as a significant mean-level/spread shift via Welch t (|t|>=2, p<0.05) on protein_mass between the two conditions — demonstrating that a large share of cell-to-cell variability is extrinsic/shared-physiology-driven rather than a fixed gene-intrinsic floor.

falsifier.decision_rule: welch_disconfirm comparing protein_mass across seeds, rrna_operon_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal; reject H1's extrinsic-noise claim if |welch_t| < 2 (no significant difference) OR if the knockout's protein_mass CV is NOT reduced relative to wildtype (i.e., effect_pct shows no meaningful compression of spread). Additionally, power_mde is run first on the wildtype/basal 8-seed design to confirm CV>=0.20 vs <0.10 is detectable before any null read is trusted.
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t| < 2 for protein_mass between rrna_operon_knockout/basal and wildtype/basal, AND per-seed CV of protein_mass under the knockout remains >=80% of the wildtype CV (i.e., essentially unchanged despite capped ribosome supply), H1 is refuted: the observed cell-to-cell variability is insensitive to this physiological intervention and is better explained as a fixed gene-intrinsic or artifactual (equilibration) source rather than shared extrinsic noise.

test.statistic: welch_t on protein_mass per-seed values, rrna_operon_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal, with per-seed CV reported alongside
test.threshold: |welch_t| >= 2 (p<0.05) AND knockout CV <= 0.6x wildtype CV to confirm extrinsic-noise compression; |welch_t|<2 or CV not compressed falsifies H1

rivals.claim: Expression variability is dominated by gene-intrinsic transcriptional/translational bursting (promoter on/off switching, low mRNA copy number) and is largely insensitive to global ribosome-supply perturbations.
rivals.distinguishing_result: protein_mass CV stays statistically unchanged (|welch_t|<2, no compression) between wildtype/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal even though mean ribosome_conc/growth_rate are clearly suppressed by the knockout — variance persists independent of the shared-resource manipulation, consistent with a fixed intrinsic noise floor.

rivals.claim: Observed cell-to-cell spread in protein_mass is an artifact of insufficient equilibration/transient dynamics at the sampled generation, not genuine steady-state biological noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If generations are extended (e.g., from 3 to 6) and wildtype/basal protein_mass CV systematically shrinks toward the null (<0.10) rather than stabilizing, the original spread was a transient-equilibration artifact; a genuine noise claim requires CV to plateau at a steady nonzero value across generation counts (checked as an auxiliary scope caveat, not a separate primary test given the 1-4 generation budget).

auxiliary_assumptions: protein_mass is treated as the best available whole-cell proxy for 'a given gene's expression level' since the instrument exposes no single-gene reporter channel; findings about protein_mass variability are a lower bound / aggregate signature of underlying single-gene noise, not a direct single-gene measurement.

Sampling protein_mass at a fixed generation (3) across seeds captures steady-state-like variability rather than purely transient divergence from a common initial condition; if this assumption fails, the equilibration-artifact rival applies (noted but not separately tested given the generation budget).

rrna_operon_knockout is assumed to act primarily by capping mean ribosome supply/variance (an extrinsic-noise-relevant perturbation) without independently altering gene-intrinsic burst kinetics of unrelated genes; if the knockout has pleiotropic intrinsic-noise side effects the interventional control's isolation is weaker.
CV and Welch-t comparisons across 8 seeds are assumed to have adequate power to detect a 40% CV compression; this is checked via power_mde before trusting a null (non-significant) result.

objection_ledger.issue: The claim is about 'a given gene' expression level (user's literal question), but the operational observable is protein_mass, which in this whole-cell-style instrument almost certainly denotes TOTAL cellular protein mass, not a single gene's product. These are different constructs: single-gene reporter variability (what intrinsic/extrinsic noise decomposition classically means, à la Elowitz) vs whole-proteome mass variability (which trivially scales with cell size/division cycle). Which does the candidate intend, and does the instrument expose any per-gene expression channel at all, or must the hypothesis be reframed as a claim about aggregate protein_mass variability instead of 'gene expression'?

protein_mass and ribosome_conc are not independent, coupled-but-distinct channels in the Elowitz intrinsic/extrinsic sense — they are mechanistically near-identical by model construction (ribosomes ARE protein, and more ribosome_conc mechanically produces more protein_mass via the simulated translation flux). A positive slope between them is expected under essentially ANY model of whole-cell growth, including one with NO meaningful 'extrinsic noise' story at all; it would also appear if the two channels are just two readouts of the same underlying growth-rate variable. The rrna_operon_knockout design shifts the MEAN ribosome level across a population, but does not test whether moment-to-moment/seed-to-seed STOCHASTIC fluctuations in ribosome number are what drives fluctuations in a separate, decoupled gene's output. An interventional design that breaks the coupling (e.g., comparing a gene whose expression is NOT mechanistically tied to ribosome synthesis, or using a knockout that perturbs noise sources independently of mean ribosome dosage) is needed before the slope test can be read as evidence for 'shared extrinsic noise' rather than definitional covariation.

The decision rule's secondary CV-based falsification path is explicitly stated as not directly available on the platform ('welch_disconfirm ... is not directly available'), leaving only a vague instruction to 'use power_mde to confirm' before trusting a null read. This means the CV<0.10 null criterion, which is part of H0 and part of the refuting_result conjunction, has no concrete executable test — only the slope_ci test is actually specified as runnable.

rrna_operon_knockout caps ribosome supply, but protein_mass includes ribosomal protein mass itself (ribosomes ARE protein, per the candidate's own claim text). So capping rrnA mechanically shrinks the ribosome-protein component of protein_mass directly, independent of any 'shared extrinsic noise' story. A compression in protein_mass CV under this knockout could simply reflect that one now has less ribosomal-protein mass to vary (a smaller, more constrained pool), not that cell-to-cell variability in a generic/unrelated gene's expression is extrinsically driven by shared physiological fluctuations. The test still does not discriminate 'extrinsic noise acting on an arbitrary gene via shared ribosome capacity' from 'trivial mechanical truncation of the ribosomal-protein subcomponent of total protein_mass.' A decisive version would need a readout of protein mass/expression for a gene UNCOUPLED from ribosome biogenesis (or exclude ribosomal proteins from protein_mass), so that compression could not be attributed to the mechanical overlap between the perturbed component and the measured component.

protein_mass (the sole available expression proxy) necessarily includes the ribosomal-protein subcomponent, and rrna_operon_knockout directly truncates ribosome supply. So a shrinkage in protein_mass CV under the knockout is mechanically expected from removing/capping part of the very pool being measured (less ribosomal protein mass to vary), regardless of whether any 'shared extrinsic physiological noise' acts on a generic gene. The decisive test still cannot distinguish 'extrinsic noise compressed' from 'measured aggregate mechanically truncated by the intervention that overlaps the measured channel.' Nothing in the current design (channels available: growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, fraction_trna_charged, rela_conc, dry_mass, protein_mass, rna_mass, cell_mass, division_rate, fba_objective) offers a protein/expression readout decoupled from ribosome biogenesis, so this rival cannot be excluded with the current instrument -- this is now an instrument limitation rather than a design oversight.

protein_mass unavoidably includes the ribosomal-protein subcomponent, and rrna_operon_knockout directly truncates that subcomponent, so CV compression is mechanically confounded with a true extrinsic-noise signature. No exposed channel (growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, fraction_trna_charged, rela_conc, dry_mass, protein_mass, rna_mass, cell_mass, division_rate, fba_objective) provides a gene-expression readout decoupled from ribosome biogenesis, so this coupling cannot be broken with the current instrument.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells (wildtype/basal, isogenic, same condition) show stable inter-individual variation in growth rate driven by intrinsic stochastic (Poisson-scale) fluctuations in the low-copy regulatory protein RelA, not by generic integrator/measurement noise or by seed-level initial-condition chaos \u2014 i.e., a broad, persistent distribution of single-cell growth rates across replicate seeds that collapses specifically when RelA copy-number noise is removed, but NOT when an unrelated low-copy node (ribosome allocation) is perturbed or when only random-seed replication at matched initial conditions is varied.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, per-seed growth_rate (and correlated ppgpp_conc, rela_conc) shows substantial, stable dispersion (CV >= 0.15) that persists across a battery of same-condition replicate seeds (ruling out it being a one-off artifact), and this dispersion is causally and specifically reduced (by >=40%) when RelA is removed (gene_knockout/rela), while an unrelated low-copy regulatory node (rRNA operon dosage) perturbation does NOT produce the same reduction \u2014 demonstrating RelA-specific low-copy-protein stochasticity, in the spirit of Spudich & Koshland 1976, as a structural source of phenotypic individuality rather than generic simulator noise or chaotic initial-condition sensitivity.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed growth_rate under wildtype/basal shows only small, unstructured variation (CV < 0.15) consistent with simulator/measurement noise alone, OR if dispersion is present it is NOT reduced specifically by relA knockout relative to other knockouts (i.e., any reduction seen with rrna_operon_knockout is equal to or greater than that seen with rela_knockout), indicating the mechanism is generic/non-specific rather than RelA-driven.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state growth_rate values across 8 independent seeds under wildtype/basal; compute coefficient of variation (CV) and bimodality coefficient (BC) pooled across seeds

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc, ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed rela_conc and ppgpp_conc distributions under wildtype/basal vs under rela gene_knockout; compare CV and mean shift

operational_defs.construct: measurement/integrator noise floor (baseline for comparison, not asserted)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed growth_rate CV computed from a SECOND independent wildtype/basal replicate batch (seeds 9-16) at the same generation, used as an empirical noise-floor check rather than an assumed 0.05 figure; if the two wildtype batches already differ this much, that sets the noise floor empirically

operational_defs.construct: causal and specific dependence of growth variability on RelA noise (vs a generic low-copy node)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of growth_rate dispersion (per-seed |value - cohort mean|) between wildtype/basal and rela_knockout/basal, AND separately between wildtype/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal; specificity requires rela's reduction to exceed rrna's

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Wildtype/basal growth_rate across 8 seeds shows CV ~0.15-0.25 (3-5x the empirically-measured noise floor from a replicate wildtype batch, expected ~0.03-0.06), with pooled bimodality coefficient BC in 0.3-0.5 range (persistent dispersion, not necessarily bimodal). Knocking out relA is predicted to compress growth_rate CV by >=40% (e.g. ~0.20 to <=0.12) and flatten ppgpp_conc/rela_conc dispersion. rrna_operon_knockout is predicted to show a SMALLER reduction (<=20%) in growth_rate CV, establishing RelA-specificity rather than generic low-copy-node disruption.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test comparing per-seed growth_rate dispersion (|value - seed-cohort mean|) between wildtype/basal and rela gene_knockout/basal, n=8 seeds each; reject H0 (no specific causal role) if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates >=30% reduction in dispersion in the rela knockout, AND this reduction exceeds the reduction seen for rrna_operon_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal (specificity check). Separately, the wildtype-vs-wildtype replicate batch (seeds 9-16) sets the empirical noise floor: if wildtype/basal CV is not significantly above this floor (|welch_t|<2 batch-vs-batch dispersion comparison), the individuality claim is refuted outright.
falsifier.refuting_result: If wildtype/basal growth_rate CV is statistically indistinguishable from the second wildtype replicate batch (noise floor, |welch_t|<2) OR if rela_knockout/basal shows no significant reduction in growth_rate dispersion relative to wildtype/basal (|welch_t|<2) OR if rrna_operon_knockout/basal reduces dispersion as much or more than rela_knockout (no RelA-specificity), this refutes RelA-driven stable individuality.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed growth_rate dispersion proxy (|value - seed-cohort mean|)
test.threshold: |welch_t|>=2 for rela-knockout-vs-wildtype dispersion reduction AND rela-reduction > rrna-reduction; |welch_t|<2 for wildtype-vs-wildtype-noise-floor comparison required to confirm dispersion exceeds noise

rivals.claim: Rival A: Observed inter-seed variation is purely numerical/simulator integration noise, not biological stochasticity, and is independent of any specific low-copy protein.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If wildtype/basal growth_rate CV is statistically indistinguishable from the second independent wildtype/basal replicate batch's inherent spread (the noise-floor check, |welch_t|<2), the variance is generic noise, not structured biological individuality, regardless of knockout results.

rivals.claim: Rival B: Variation reflects deterministic/chaotic sensitivity to tiny seed-to-seed initial-condition differences baked into the integrator, independent of which gene is present, and would show up equally in ANY two independently-seeded wildtype batches as well as surviving any single gene knockout.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If growth_rate CV remains elevated (>=0.15) and statistically indistinguishable across wildtype/basal, rela_knockout/basal, AND rrna_operon_knockout/basal alike (no knockout reduces it below the wildtype-vs-wildtype noise floor comparison), this supports chaotic/initial-condition sensitivity over any specific low-copy-protein mechanism; the simulator cannot resolve this further (see auxiliary assumptions), so it is treated as an irreducible rival rather than chased with additional designs.

rivals.claim: Rival C: Variation is driven by ribosome/rRNA allocation noise (a different low-copy-ish regulatory axis) rather than specifically RelA/ppGpp.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout/basal reduces growth_rate CV as much as or more than rela_knockout/basal, ribosome allocation (not RelA per se) is the dominant structural noise source, refuting RelA-specificity.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed stochastic sampling of low-copy species (RelA, ribosomes) is an intended source of biological noise, not an artifact to be averaged away.
8 seeds per cohort give adequate power to detect a CV difference of the predicted magnitude (~0.20 vs ~0.12); formal MDE check deferred to a power_mde pass if initial result is ambiguous.
growth_rate measured at matched generation (gen 3) across all four designs to avoid confounding transient start-up dynamics with steady-state dispersion.

Using a second independently-seeded wildtype/basal batch as the noise floor is an empirical proxy, not a perfect technical-replicate (i.e. it still contains the same biological stochasticity under test) — if this proxy is insufficient the noise-floor claim should be revisited, but no better in-envelope 'pure technical noise' control exists.

We cannot adjudicate deterministic chaos vs stochastic noise at the level of the ODE/FBA integrator itself directly (no dial manipulates initial-condition perturbation magnitude independent of gene content); this is recorded as an explicit irreducible auxiliary assumption / scope caveat per objection r1.2, addressed instead via the elimination logic in Rival B rather than a direct manipulation.

ppgpp_conc clamp control from the prior round is deprioritized in this revision in favor of the rrna_operon_knockout specificity control and the wildtype noise-floor batch, which more directly address the two open objections; it remains a feasible follow-up design if this round's result is ambiguous.

params.note: primary wildtype cohort for individuality measurement
second independent wildtype replicate batch used purely to empirically establish the noise floor, not assumed

objection_ledger.issue: The claim hinges on 'intrinsic stochastic fluctuations in low-copy regulatory proteins' as the generative mechanism, but the only instrument access is to per-seed aggregate outputs (growth_rate, rela_conc, ppgpp_conc) at a given generation — there's no dial for actual molecule-copy-number trajectories or an independent 'measurement noise floor' estimate. The 0.05 CV figure for 'measurement-noise-only' is asserted, not derived from any channel or control in the design.

Rival B (chaotic sensitivity to initial conditions) is tested only by checking whether relA knockout AND rrna_operon_knockout both fail to reduce CV. But both of these are still gene-level interventions on regulatory nodes; if the real driver is seed-level initial-condition sensitivity baked into the integrator (independent of which gene is knocked out), neither knockout manipulates that channel, so a 'both fail' result is confounded with 'neither knockout perturbs the actual chaotic variable.' The design does not include a genuine manipulation of initial-condition sensitivity itself (e.g., varying initial-condition perturbation magnitude directly) to positively confirm or exclude chaos as a rival.

The CV thresholds (0.15, 40%, 20%) and bimodality coefficient range remain somewhat arbitrary point predictions not derived from any pilot run of the simulator itself; this is a residual calibration concern already flagged as r1.1 and now reasonably handled via the empirical noise-floor batch, so it should be stated as a standing auxiliary assumption rather than re-litigated.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim:
Genetically identical E. coli cells growing in the same medium do NOT express a given gene at the same level. Because the instrument exposes only aggregate/bulk channels (no single-transcript reporter), the claim is operationalized at the level the simulator can actually resolve: bulk protein output (protein_mass) across isogenic seeds shows substantial cell-to-cell variability (CV >= 0.15), and that variability is not purely a mechanical/deterministic consequence of growth-rate differences (a trivial mean-scaling artifact), but persists as EXCESS variability beyond what a matched mean-level shift alone would produce — evidenced by (i) a fano-like scaling check (CV should not collapse to the simulator's intrinsic numerical-noise floor when growth_rate is held approximately matched across conditions) and (ii) a genuinely interventional control (relA knockout, which removes the stringent-response/ppGpp arm that couples ribosome allocation to nutrient state) that should NOT by itself abolish cross-seed protein_mass variability if a ribosome-allocation/shared-resource (extrinsic-noise) component is real and distinct from deterministic capacity-capping. The rrna_operon_knockout is retained only as a capacity-capping comparison whose CV must be judged relative to its own mean-shifted scale, not assumed equivalent to wildtype's baseline scale.</claim>
<parameter name="h1">Isogenic wildtype cells (same condition, different stochastic seeds) show substantial cross-seed variability in bulk protein output (CV of protein_mass >= 0.15, well above a <0.05 numerical-noise floor), and this variability includes a shared/extrinsic component distinguishable from deterministic mean-scaling: when growth_rate is matched or controlled for, relA knockout (removing ppGpp-mediated ribosome reallocation but NOT capping ribosome capacity) does not collapse cross-seed CV of protein_mass to the noise floor (|welch_t| < 2 vs wildtype), whereas rrna_operon_knockout (a true capacity cap) produces a CV change whose magnitude, once normalized for its own mean shift, is distinguishable from a pure mean-variance scaling relationship.
hypothesis.h0: Cross-seed CV of protein_mass in wildtype is low (<0.05, consistent with simulator numerical noise only), OR any CV differences across conditions (relA knockout, rrna_operon_knockout) are fully explained by their mean-level shift (i.e., CV tracks a single mean-vs-CV scaling curve with no excess/shared-noise component), such that relA knockout and rrna_operon_knockout both produce |welch_t| < 2 against wildtype once mean-shift is accounted for.

operational_defs.construct: cell-to-cell expression variability (bulk proxy for single-gene expression, per Elowitz framing)
operational_defs.observable: protein_mass channel measured per seed at a fixed generation across isogenic replicate seeds
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of protein_mass across seeds within a perturbation/condition

operational_defs.observable: mean protein_mass per seed-set alongside its CV, compared across wildtype/basal, rela_knockout/basal, rrna_operon_knockout/basal
operational_defs.measure: report CV alongside mean for each condition; a condition's CV is judged 'excess' only if it is not simply predicted by a monotonic mean-to-CV relationship visible across the three conditions

operational_defs.observable: cross-seed protein_mass spread under relA knockout (removes stringent-response allocation signal, capacity untouched) vs under rrna_operon_knockout (caps capacity directly)
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of per-seed protein_mass between each knockout/basal and wildtype/basal; effect_pct and per-seed CV reported for both

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction/magnitude: wildtype cross-seed CV of protein_mass ~0.15-0.25 (well above a <0.05 numerical floor). relA knockout is predicted to leave cross-seed CV of protein_mass essentially unchanged relative to wildtype (CV ratio 0.85-1.15x, |welch_t| < 2), because removing ppGpp-mediated reallocation does not remove the underlying shared-resource/stochastic-partitioning noise source. rrna_operon_knockout is predicted to shift both mean protein_mass DOWN (~30-50%) and CV down, but the CV reduction (predicted ~20-35% relative drop) must exceed what a naive mean-proportional scaling of SD would produce, otherwise the apparent 'noise reduction' is attributed to the mean-shift artifact, not to a genuine extrinsic-noise contribution.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of per-seed protein_mass between relA gene_knockout/basal and wildtype/basal across >=6 seeds to test whether removing the ppGpp allocation arm alone abolishes variability (it should NOT, if H1 holds): reject H1's 'persistent variability' claim if |welch_t| >= 2 AND CV(relA_ko) is markedly compressed toward the <0.05 floor. Separately, for rrna_operon_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal, compute CV in both; reject the 'excess variability beyond mean-scaling' claim if the CV ratio (rrna_ko CV / wildtype CV) is statistically indistinguishable from the mean ratio (protein_mass_mean(rrna_ko)/protein_mass_mean(wildtype)) at the same scale (i.e., CV change is proportionality-only, consistent with H0).
falsifier.refuting_result: If wildtype cross-seed CV of protein_mass is <0.05 (near-uniform expression, contradicting the core claim), OR relA knockout shows |welch_t| >= 2 with CV collapsing to near the noise floor (implying ALL extrinsic variability routes through the stringent response, falsifying the 'shared-resource noise persists independent of ppGpp' sub-claim), OR the rrna_operon_knockout CV change is fully proportional to its mean shift (no excess/noise-specific reduction), then H1 is refuted.

test.statistic: welch_t

rivals.claim: All cross-seed protein_mass variability is gene-intrinsic stochastic bursting with zero shared/extrinsic component; any apparent CV changes under knockouts are purely mean-scaling artifacts.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Both relA knockout and rrna_operon_knockout would show CV changes that are fully explained (proportionally) by their respective mean shifts, with no excess reduction beyond the mean-CV scaling curve, and relA knockout (which doesn't change mean capacity much) would show |welch_t| < 2 in CV terms as well as in raw protein_mass.

rivals.claim: Observed cross-seed protein_mass variability is dominated by cell-cycle/division-timing asynchrony (cells sampled at different points in their cycle), not stochastic expression per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, cross-seed CV of protein_mass would correlate strongly with dry_mass/cell_mass (a cycle-phase proxy) rather than specifically with ribosome_conc or growth_rate, and neither relA knockout nor rrna_operon_knockout (which do not fix cycle phase) would meaningfully change CV; division_rate would remain ~1 (no viability effect) while CV persists unabated across all three conditions.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed stochastic draws in the simulator approximate biological intrinsic noise (distinct random streams per seed), so cross-seed CV at matched generation/condition is a valid proxy for cell-to-cell variability.

protein_mass is used as a BULK proxy for expression output because the instrument exposes no single-transcript/single-protein reporter channel; this is an explicit scope narrowing from 'a given gene' (Elowitz single-reporter sense) to 'aggregate protein output,' and conclusions are stated at that scope, not claimed to generalize to every individual gene's noise profile.

Comparing cells at a matched generation index (not matched absolute cycle phase) is an acceptable control for cycle-phase confounds given the platform's sampling granularity; dry_mass/cell_mass are available as a secondary cycle-phase check if results are ambiguous.

relA knockout and rrna_operon_knockout are assumed non-lethal within 1-4 generations so protein_mass remains measurable in surviving seeds; division_rate is checked to confirm viability in all three designs.

The steady-state tRNA charging / ribosome allocation submodel is active (not kinetic-only) so ribosome_conc and rela_conc remain valid, continuously recorded channels for the discriminating-control comparisons.

Because ribosome_conc and protein_mass are mechanistically/deterministically coupled in this model, we do NOT rely on their cross-seed correlation (collinearity) as evidence for 'extrinsic noise'; instead causal discrimination rests on the relA-knockout vs rrna_operon-knockout INTERVENTIONAL contrast described above.

objection_ledger.issue: The claim as stated is about whether genetically identical cells express 'a given gene' at the same level, but the operationalization substitutes protein_mass (total cellular protein mass, an aggregate of thousands of genes' products) as the observable. Total protein_mass variability is governed by growth/mass-partitioning dynamics and is not a valid proxy for single-gene expression noise — a population could show near-zero CV in protein_mass while individual genes show huge expression variability (or vice versa). This is flagged as an 'auxiliary_assumption' but it actually guts the core claim rather than being a minor scope limitation.

ribosome_conc and protein_mass are mechanistically coupled in the whole-cell model (ribosome capacity directly determines translation rate, which directly determines protein_mass) — they are not independent extrinsic/intrinsic readouts but two ends of the same causal chain. A positive correlation between them across seeds is guaranteed by the model's structure regardless of whether any genuine 'shared extrinsic noise' phenomenon exists, so the slope_ci test cannot discriminate extrinsic-noise coupling from simple deterministic mass-balance coupling.

The rrna_operon_knockout test conflates 'shared ribosome pool as noise source' with 'shared ribosome pool as deterministic capacity constraint.' Capping rRNA operons will mechanically reduce mean ribosome_conc and growth_rate for ALL seeds (a deterministic shift in the mean), which will almost certainly also compress CV simply because lower absolute protein_mass values plus bounded/saturating kinetics tend to produce lower SD—even with zero change in the underlying noise-generating process. The decision rule does not control for this mean-variance scaling artifact (e.g., via comparing coefficient of variation normalized appropriately, or a null model of how CV scales with mean in this simulator).

The decision rule for the rrna_operon_knockout 'excess variability beyond mean-scaling' sub-claim says to compare the CV ratio to the mean ratio 'at the same scale' but never specifies the actual null model/functional form relating CV to mean (e.g., Taylor's power law exponent, linear SD-mean fit, or bootstrap null from wildtype-only seed resampling at matched subsampled means). Without a pre-specified mean-CV null curve, the 'proportionality-only' test can be satisfied or refuted by eyeballing, making this sub-falsifier non-binding as stated.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells under constant conditions (wildtype/basal) display stable, persistent cell-to-cell heterogeneity in growth rate and ppGpp concentration that arises from intrinsic stochastic (Poisson) fluctuations in the low-copy regulatory protein RelA, not from measurement noise, generic extrinsic resource-allocation noise, or transient artifact — i.e. isogenic populations are intrinsically multimodal/broadly dispersed rather than a tight unimodal distribution around the mean, and this dispersion collapses specifically when RelA itself is removed.
hypothesis.h1: Across 8 isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the pooled per-seed distribution of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc shows CV >= 15% (versus an expected measurement/numerical-noise floor of ~5%) and is better described as bimodal/multimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) than unimodal, reflecting stable subpopulations driven by stochastic RelA copy-number fluctuations. Critically, this bimodality/CV is abolished (BC drops to <=0.555 and CV falls below 15%) when relA is knocked out, because removing the low-copy noise source collapses the stochastic switch, whereas a generic ribosome-capacity perturbation (rrna_operon_knockout) that does not touch RelA leaves comparable bimodality/CV intact. Given the known fragility of BC estimation at n=8, the primary decisive claim rests on CV (a stable, well-powered statistic at this n) with BC reported as a secondary, descriptive/corroborating shape indicator rather than the sole arbiter; CV collapse (>=50% relative reduction, from >=15% to <15%) in the relA-KO vs wildtype comparison via Welch's t on per-seed CV-contributing dispersion is the primary falsifiable claim.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic replicates under wildtype/basal conditions show low dispersion (CV < 15%) in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds, consistent with noise being negligible/well-averaged and all cells behaving essentially identically; any dispersion present is insensitive to relA knockout (CV does not drop by >=50% relative, and |welch_t| < 2 for the KO-vs-wildtype mean/dispersion shift), indicating it is not RelA-driven. BC is reported descriptively but is not required to cross 0.555 for H0 to hold, given its instability at n=8.
