hypothesis.predicted_effect: Pooled across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal, growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show CV >= 15% (vs ~5% measurement floor), sustained from generations 1-2 through 3-4 (not decaying below 15%); BC is reported descriptively and expected >0.555 as corroborating (not decisive) evidence of multimodality (~20-40% of seeds in a distinct low-growth/high-ppGpp mode). Under relA gene_knockout/basal, CV falls below 15% (>=50% relative reduction vs wildtype) with |welch_t|>=2 on the dispersion-sensitive comparison, and BC (descriptively) drops toward <=0.555. Under rrna_operon_knockout/basal (a non-RelA noise source), CV remains >=15%, comparable to wildtype (|welch_t|<2 vs wildtype).

falsifier.decision_rule: PRIMARY test: Welch's t-test of pooled per-seed growth_rate dispersion (8 seeds, gens 1-4) comparing relA gene_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal; H1's RelA-causal claim is supported only if |welch_t| >= 2 AND the relA-KO CV is reduced by >=50% relative to wildtype CV (from >=15% to <15%). BC (bimodality_bc) on pooled wildtype values and on relA-KO values is computed and reported as a SECONDARY descriptive corroborator only, given its known instability at n=8 seeds — a BC result that disagrees with the CV-based conclusion is flagged as an auxiliary caveat, not treated as refuting evidence on its own.
falsifier.refuting_result: relA gene_knockout/basal shows CV >= 15% (not reduced by >=50% relative to wildtype) and |welch_t| < 2 vs wildtype, indicating the heterogeneity is not RelA-specific and is instead generic/extrinsic or simulator artifact.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t| >= 2 for KO vs wildtype growth_rate dispersion shift, combined with >=50% relative CV reduction in KO vs wildtype

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is driven by generic extrinsic noise in global resource allocation (ribosome/metabolite pools) rather than RelA-specific low-copy fluctuations.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal (removing ribosome capacity, a non-RelA noise source) shows CV>=15% comparable to wildtype (|welch_t|<2 vs wildtype), while relA gene_knockout/basal shows the CV collapse (>=50% relative reduction, |welch_t|>=2) — this pattern (KO of the OTHER node doesn't help, KO of RelA does) confirms RelA-specificity rather than generic extrinsic noise; conversely if BOTH knockouts collapse CV equally, that favors the generic-extrinsic-noise rival.

rivals.claim: Observed variability is a simulator/sampling artifact (numerical or solver-level noise) with no biological persistence across generations, not stable intrinsic individuality.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV computed over generations 1-2 decays below 15% by generations 3-4 within wildtype/basal seeds (i.e., the dispersion washes out rather than persisting), this favors the artifact/transient-noise rival over persistent intrinsic individuality; persistence (CV>=15% sustained in both windows) favors H1.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's intrinsic stochastic module (seed-to-seed variation) is intended to model genuine biological noise (e.g. low-copy molecule Poisson fluctuations) rather than pure numerical artifact; we cannot fully distinguish deterministic-chaos vs stochastic-noise origins within the simulator and treat this as out of scope.

relA gene_knockout is assumed to be mechanistically simulated (i.e. actually removes RelA synthesis activity and its downstream Poisson-noise contribution) rather than being a no-op in this model; if relA KO has no mechanistic effect on ppgpp_conc at all (checked via basic viability/division_rate), the discriminating control is uninformative and this will be flagged rather than over-interpreted as support for a rival.

Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc sampled at fixed generation windows (1-2 vs 3-4) are representative of per-seed steady behavior and not dominated purely by initial-condition transients from cell initialization.

Sarle's BC is known to be a biased/unstable estimator at n=8 seeds; it is therefore used only as a descriptive secondary indicator of distribution shape, never as the primary pass/fail criterion — the decisive claim is carried entirely by the CV + Welch's t comparison, which is adequately powered at n=8 for the predicted >=50% relative effect size (to be confirmed via power_mde in a follow-up if the observed effect is borderline).

objection_ledger.issue: The RelA-specific-noise rival vs the generic-extrinsic-noise rival is to be distinguished by a 'ppgpp_conc clamp' at 1.0x basal — but clamping ppgpp_conc to its basal value does not intervene on RelA itself; ppGpp and RelA are mechanistically coupled (RelA synthesizes ppGpp), so observing that this clamp 'does not reduce bimodality' cannot attribute the cause to RelA specifically versus any other node in the same regulatory loop. An interventional control is needed that actually knocks out or titrates relA (e.g. a gene_knockout or graded_gene_knockout on relA) to break the coupling, not a clamp on its downstream product.

The second rival (simulator/sampling artifact, no persistence across generations) is described only in prose ('autocorrelation across the 1-4 generation window') with no concrete statistic, threshold, or candidate_design wired to a decision_rule. As written there is no specified test that could actually fail to support this rival-exclusion.

With only 8 seeds, estimating Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) reliably to compare against a fixed 0.555 threshold is statistically fragile (BC estimators are known to be unstable/biased at small n); the candidate's own auxiliary_assumptions flag this as a possible underpowering issue but defer it to a 'follow-up round' rather than resolving it now.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells, grown in the same static basal medium, display stable, non-transient cell-to-cell heterogeneity (isogenic phenotypic individuality) in growth rate and ppGpp/ribosome output, arising from intrinsic stochastic (Poisson-scale) fluctuations in the low-copy regulatory protein RelA rather than from measurement noise or general ribosome-economy fluctuation. This heterogeneity manifests as a wide, possibly bimodal, distribution of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across isogenic replicate seeds, with a sizeable fraction (~20-30%) of seeds lying outside +/-1 CV of the population mean, persisting across generations, and is causally dependent on RelA such that deleting relA collapses the ppGpp/growth-rate spread substantially (>=40% CV reduction) while a general-noise/ribosome-economy mechanism would not.
hypothesis.h1: Across >=8 isogenic replicate seeds of wildtype/basal: (1) growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) pooled per-seed means (generations 2-4) show CV>=15% and Sarle's bimodality coefficient BC>0.555, persisting across generations 1-4 (inter-seed CV ratio gen4/gen1 >=0.8); AND (2) this spread is RelA-dependent: relA gene_knockout reduces ppgpp_conc CV across seeds by >=40% relative to wildtype/basal, consistent with low-copy Poisson-scale RelA fluctuation driving the heterogeneity rather than general ribosome-economy noise.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds of wildtype/basal show a narrow, unimodal distribution of growth_rate (CV<15%, BC<=0.555) consistent with only measurement/replicate noise and no stable individuality; OR, if spread exists, relA knockout fails to reduce ppgpp_conc CV by >=40% (i.e., CV reduction <40% or an increase), indicating the heterogeneity is not RelA-specific.

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Pooled across 8 isogenic seeds of wildtype/basal: growth_rate CV>=15% (vs ~5-8% measurement-noise floor) and BC>0.555 (non-unimodal, e.g. ~25% slow-growing subpopulation), persisting across generations (CV ratio gen4/gen1 >=0.8). rela_conc CV should exceed protein_mass CV by >=2-fold. Critically, relA knockout should reduce ppgpp_conc CV across seeds by >=40% relative to wildtype/basal (e.g. from ~20% CV down to <=12% CV), demonstrating causal dependence on low-copy RelA fluctuation rather than generic ribosome-economy/flux noise.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed mean growth_rate values (generations 2-4) across 8 seeds; reject H0 (no individuality) if BC>0.555, and separately require CV>=15%. Secondary (mechanism): compute ppgpp_conc CV across 8 seeds in relA_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal using welch_disconfirm on per-seed ppgpp_conc values; require the percent CV reduction >=40% (and/or welch_t|>=2| on the underlying per-seed values indicating a significant shift toward a narrower/lower distribution) to confirm RelA-specific causality.
falsifier.refuting_result: Either (a) BC<=0.555 AND growth_rate CV<15% (no individuality signal at all), OR (b) individuality exists but relA knockout reduces ppgpp_conc CV by <40% relative to wildtype (welch_t<2, i.e. CV not significantly collapsed), indicating the spread is not RelA-specific and is better explained by the general ribosome-economy rival.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate means; CV; welch_t on ppgpp_conc CV between wildtype and relA KO
test.threshold: BC>0.555 and CV>=15% for individuality; ppgpp_conc CV reduction >=40% (welch_t>=2 on relA KO vs wildtype per-seed ppgpp_conc) for RelA-specific causality

rivals.claim: Apparent heterogeneity is purely numerical/measurement noise from finite-seed sampling, not biological individuality (Null rival).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, BC<=0.555 and growth_rate CV<15%, and CV stays flat near the noise floor across generations rather than showing a persistent bimodal split.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity exists but is driven by global ribosome/ppGpp allocation dynamics (a ribosome-economy rival) or general metabolic flux noise, not specifically by low-copy RelA Poisson fluctuation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, relA knockout would NOT substantially reduce ppgpp_conc CV (reduction <40%, welch_t<2) because heterogeneity persists via ribosome_conc/flux noise independent of RelA copy number.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is transient (cells re-randomize each division, no persistence), i.e. fluctuations average out and are not stable individuality.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the inter-seed CV would significantly decline from generation 1 to generation 4 (CV ratio <0.8, slope CI excludes zero and negative), i.e. spread collapses toward the mean rather than persisting.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's intrinsic stochastic seed-to-seed variation is an adequate proxy for true biological cell-to-cell noise (the model's RNG is assumed to recapitulate Poisson-scale low-copy-number fluctuation, not merely add uniform jitter to a deterministic trajectory); this is irreducible within the simulator and not further pressed.
Per-seed mean over generations 2-4 (excluding generation 1 startup transient) is a fair summary of 'steady' phenotype; we are not modeling lineage/mother-daughter correlation explicitly.
rela_conc and ppgpp_conc are read under whichever charging mode (steady-state or kinetic) the run uses consistently across all seeds/conditions compared, so CV comparisons are apples-to-apples.

8 seeds is treated as adequate replicate power for BC, CV, and welch_t estimation at this screening scale; a larger-seed follow-up would be needed to pin down the exact subpopulation fraction or a smaller/larger CV-reduction effect.
division_rate is assumed ~1 (no lethality) in wildtype/basal and relA KO at this generation count, so growth_rate/ppgpp_conc differences reflect graded phenotype rather than survivorship bias.

relA knockout is assumed mechanistically simulated (i.e., removing RelA measurably perturbs ppGpp synthesis in this model) rather than a no-op; if downstream testing reveals relA KO has no mechanistic effect on ppgpp_conc at all, this specific rival-exclusion test would be uninformative and would need a different intervention (e.g. ppgpp_conc clamp) as a fallback.

params.label: single_seed_baseline for noise-floor reference, used descriptively not as primary null

objection_ledger.issue: The core claim hinges on 'seeds' in the simulator representing genuinely independent stochastic cell lineages comparable to isogenic single-cell replicates, but nothing establishes that varying the RNG seed in this envelope actually instantiates cell-to-cell biological noise (vs. e.g. just different random initial conditions in a deterministic ODE solved once per seed, which would trivially not show division-level stochasticity at all). This is listed as an auxiliary assumption already, so I will not press it further as substantive, but flag it once as it bears directly on falsifiability of the headline claim.

The relA knockout control is a good interventional step, but the decision rule for that rival test is not specified with the same rigor as the main falsifier: the candidate says CV 'would remain similarly high' in the rival case but gives no numeric threshold (e.g., a specific fold-reduction cutoff) for when the relA KO result counts as confirming vs. refuting the low-copy-Poisson mechanism. Without a quantitative decision rule, the rival-exclusion test cannot actually fail in a predefined way.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Expression noise is set largely by a gene's regulatory architecture and abundance regime: low-abundance, bursty regulatory-pathway products (RelA/ppGpp stringent-response components, and ribosome capacity under rRNA-operon stress) show higher cell-to-cell variability (CV across seeds) than high-abundance, continuously-synthesized bulk/constitutive products (protein_mass, dry_mass), because the ribosome/charged-tRNA supply driving translation bursts is itself a limiting, noisy resource. Removing the bursty regulatory node (relA knockout) should reduce noise in its own pathway's proxies, while compressing ribosome capacity (rRNA operon knockout) should further amplify ribosome_conc noise beyond what reduced mean abundance alone predicts.
hypothesis.h1: Across a panel of backgrounds, CV (across seeds, fixed generation) of channels proxying low-abundance/regulatory products (rela_conc, ppgpp_conc in wildtype; ribosome_conc under rrna_operon_knockout) is >=1.5x the CV of channels proxying high-abundance constitutive products (protein_mass, dry_mass) in matched wildtype/basal; relA knockout reduces CV of ppgpp_conc/rela-pathway proxies relative to wildtype (architecture removal lowers noise), and rrna_operon_knockout raises ribosome_conc CV by >=1.3x its wildtype value (capacity limitation amplifies noise beyond mean-abundance effects).
hypothesis.h0: CV of regulatory/low-abundance-proxy channels (rela_conc, ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc) is statistically indistinguishable from (or lower than) CV of high-abundance constitutive-proxy channels (protein_mass, dry_mass) across seeds in wildtype/basal, AND relA knockout and rrna_operon_knockout produce no detectable shift (|welch_t|<2) in their respective target-channel CV relative to wildtype — i.e., architecture/capacity class does not predict noise level or its manipulability.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed CV of protein_mass and dry_mass across 8 seeds in wildtype/basal

operational_defs.construct: causal dependence of noise on the stringent-response architecture
operational_defs.observable: rela_conc and ppgpp_conc under relA knockout vs wildtype

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction + magnitude: in wildtype/basal, CV(rela_conc) and CV(ppgpp_conc) >= 1.5x CV(protein_mass) and CV(dry_mass) (e.g., CV_rela ~0.25-0.40 vs CV_protein_mass ~0.10-0.15). Under rrna_operon_knockout, CV(ribosome_conc) rises to >=1.3x its wildtype value. Under relA knockout, CV(rela_conc)/CV(ppgpp_conc) drops toward wildtype's bulk-proxy baseline (CV ratio target/reference < 1, i.e. noise reduced by architecture removal), with a mean-level welch_t>=2 confirming relA knockout changes the channel distribution (not just its spread).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test on per-seed ribosome_conc values, rrna_operon_knockout vs wildtype/basal, across 8 seeds at generation 3; reject H0 if |welch_t| >= 2 AND effect_pct indicates CV(ribosome_conc) under knockout is >=1.3x CV under wildtype (capacity limitation amplifies noise beyond the mean-shift alone)
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t| < 2, or if the CV ratio (knockout/wildtype) for ribosome_conc is <1.3x despite a mean-level shift (i.e., ribosome_conc simply shifts mean without increased relative spread), H1 is refuted: capacity limitation does not amplify noise beyond simple abundance reduction, undermining the architecture-driven noise claim.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed ribosome_conc, target vs reference; CV ratio computed from per-seed spread
test.threshold: |welch_t| >= 2 and CV ratio >= 1.3

rivals.claim: Noise is driven mainly by mRNA/protein copy number alone (simple Poisson/molecular-counting noise), independent of regulatory architecture (ppGpp/stringent pathway specifics) — any low-copy channel is noisy regardless of its regulatory wiring.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV scales purely with abundance level (low mean concentration predicts high CV generically) with no extra elevation specifically in rela_conc/ppgpp_conc relative to other similarly-low-mean channels, and rrna_operon_knockout's ribosome_conc CV increase is fully explained by its mean shift (CV ratio ~ (mean ratio)^-0.5, the Poisson expectation) rather than exceeding it, this rival is supported over the architecture-specific claim.

rivals.claim: Noise is dominated by growth-rate fluctuations (extrinsic/global noise) rather than gene-specific architecture — all channels co-vary with growth_rate noise, so apparent CV differences just reflect differential sensitivity to a shared global noise source, not intrinsic bursty synthesis.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV differences between rela_conc/ppgpp_conc/ribosome_conc and protein_mass/dry_mass track growth_rate's own CV ratio across wildtype vs rrna_operon_knockout (i.e., the CV gap scales with the growth_rate CV gap rather than being specific to the targeted channel), this rival is supported; relA knockout's effect on ppgpp_conc/rela_conc CV would then be explainable by its effect on growth_rate variability rather than removal of a bursty synthesis node per se.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed CV at a fixed generation (generation 3) is a valid proxy for intrinsic expression noise, assuming seeds are independent stochastic replicates and generation-to-generation drift within a seed is not the dominant noise source.

rela_conc and ppgpp_conc are acceptable proxies for 'regulatory/low-abundance gene' noise class; protein_mass and dry_mass are acceptable bulk proxies for 'constitutive high-abundance' class, even though they aggregate many genes rather than isolating a single gene's mRNA/protein count.

The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation reflects biologically meaningful intrinsic+extrinsic noise rather than pure numerical/solver artifact; this is a scope caveat the simulator cannot fully resolve and is accepted as a modeling limitation.

relA knockout is assumed to meaningfully perturb the stringent-response/ppGpp synthesis architecture in the simulated gene regulatory network (downstream confirmation needed since mechanistic fidelity of each KO is not knowable a priori).

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales with regulatory/translational architecture rather than mean expression level alone: genes whose protein output depends on low-copy-number upstream regulators or small burst numbers (e.g. genes controlled via stringent-response/ppGpp-linked regulation, operationalized here as ribosomal-protein/RelA-linked genes whose synthesis is gated by ppGpp/charged-tRNA state) show substantially higher cell-to-cell noise (CV across seeds) than constitutively expressed, high-copy 'housekeeping' genes, because fewer discrete synthesis/regulatory events per cell cycle amplify stochastic fluctuations (classic low-copy-number noise amplification), and this excess noise is NOT explained away by mean-expression scaling alone.
hypothesis.h1: The CV of single-cell output for the stringent-response-coupled, low-abundance regulatory gene class (proxied by ribosome_conc and rela_conc) is at least 2x higher than the CV for a constitutively-expressed high-abundance reference class (proxied by rna_mass and protein_mass), measured across isogenic replicate seeds under identical media, and this excess persists beyond what a single log(CV)~log(mean) power-law fit across both classes would predict (i.e. the regulatory class sits measurably ABOVE the fitted line, not merely further along it).
hypothesis.h0: The CV of output across seeds does not differ (within Welch-t replicate noise) between the low-abundance regulatory class and the constitutively-expressed high-abundance class, and/or any apparent CV difference is fully accounted for by a single mean-CV power law (regulatory-class points fall ON the fitted line, no systematic residual offset).

all_rounds.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
all_rounds.claim: Across genes/pathway-level readouts, expression noise (cell-to-cell CV across isogenic seeds) scales inversely with mean abundance: a low-abundance, stringent-regulated channel (rela_conc) shows substantially higher relative noise than a high-abundance, growth-coupled channel (ribosome_conc), and this difference is NOT simply inherited from growth-rate fluctuations — i.e. it survives an intervention (relA knockout) that removes stringent-pathway-specific stochasticity while leaving growth-rate variability intact.
all_rounds.h1: The ratio CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc), computed across seeds at matched final generation in wildtype/basal, is >=1.5 (point estimate ~3-5), and this ratio's 95% bootstrap CI excludes 1.5 on the high side, while in relA_knockout/basal (where rela_conc is suppressed near zero and thus its noise reflects only residual/leak expression, not stringent-pathway bursting) the gap in CV(ribosome_conc) alone does not change by more than 1.3x relative to wildtype, showing ribosome_conc noise is not just riding on the same growth-rate fluctuations that would be perturbed by removing RelA.
all_rounds.h0: The ratio CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc) across seeds in wildtype/basal is <1.5 (bootstrap CI includes or is below 1.5) — i.e. abundance/regulatory class does not predict a meaningfully larger relative noise for the low-abundance stringent-linked channel versus the high-abundance channel in this simulator.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV(rela_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc) across the 8 seeds in wildtype/basal; bootstrap (resample seeds with replacement, 1000 iters) the ratio CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc) to get a 95% CI. falsifier.decision_rule: Welch's t-test comparing per-seed CV of rela_conc vs per-seed CV of ribosome_conc (both from the 8 wildtype/basal seeds, generation-3 snapshot); reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 and CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc) >= 3. falsifier.refuting_result: Either (a) CV(rela_conc) or CV(ppgpp_conc) is not significantly different from, or less than 3-fold, CV(ribosome_conc) in wildtype (|welch_t|<2 or ratio<3), or (b) the relA-knockout CV of ppgpp_conc collapses to near-ribosome-like low CV (ratio <1.5-fold vs wildtype ribosome_conc CV), indicating feedback architecture, not raw abundance, is the primary noise determinant.

test.threshold: |t|>=2 and CV ratio>=3 for the abundance comparisons; |t|<2 for the knockout-persistence check

hypothesis.claim: Expression noise scales inversely with mean molecular abundance: across a small panel of regulatory vs. housekeeping channels, the across-seed coefficient of variation (CV) is systematically higher for low-abundance regulatory species (rela_conc, ppgpp_conc) than for a high-abundance housekeeping species (ribosome_conc), and this abundance-noise relationship -- not feedback architecture -- is the dominant driver, as shown by an interventional control (relA knockout) that removes the stringent-response feedback loop without equalizing abundance.

hypothesis.h0: Per-seed CV of the low-abundance channels (rela_conc, ppgpp_conc) is statistically indistinguishable from CV of the high-abundance channel (ribosome_conc) (|welch_t|<2 or ratio <3-fold), OR the CV gap disappears/collapses upon relA knockout, indicating the noise difference is driven by feedback architecture and/or extrinsic growth fluctuations rather than abundance per se.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales inversely with a gene's expression/regulatory 'load': genes whose products are low-abundance and transcriptionally/translationally bottlenecked (here operationalized via genes that sit downstream of limiting translational capacity, i.e. ribosomal-protein genes under rRNA-operon depletion) show higher relative noise in their protein output than genes with high, unconstrained expression (housekeeping genes under wildtype conditions). Concretely, reducing ribosome biogenesis capacity (rrna_operon_knockout) increases the coefficient of variation of ribosome/ribosomal-protein concentration across isogenic replicates far more than it affects a high-abundance, unconstrained channel like protein_mass, because low-copy-number, supply-limited gene products are more susceptible to stochastic partitioning and bursty synthesis.
hypothesis.h1: Limiting a gene's synthesis capacity (rRNA operon dosage, hence ribosome supply) increases the cross-seed coefficient of variation (CV) of its downstream product concentration (ribosome_conc) by at least 2-fold relative to wildtype, while leaving a high-abundance, non-limiting channel (protein_mass) CV nearly unchanged (<20% relative change).
hypothesis.h0: rRNA operon knockout does not increase the cross-seed CV of ribosome_conc relative to wildtype (CV ratio within [0.8, 1.2]x of wildtype), i.e. noise is independent of synthesis-capacity limitation.

operational_defs.observable: cross-seed variability of its concentration channel at matched timepoint/generation
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) of ribosome_conc (proxy for ribosomal-protein output) computed across seeds, compared to CV of protein_mass as a high-abundance reference channel

operational_defs.observable: rRNA operon copy number available for ribosome assembly
operational_defs.measure: rrna_operon_knockout perturbation (reduced rRNA operon dosage) vs wildtype/basal

operational_defs.observable: overall growth rate and division success
operational_defs.measure: growth_rate and division_rate channels, checked to ensure CV increase isn't simply a byproduct of near-lethal growth arrest

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: rrna_operon_knockout raises ribosome_conc CV across seeds by >=2-fold (e.g. from ~0.08 CV in wildtype to >=0.16 CV in the knockout), while protein_mass CV changes by <20% relative (e.g. 0.05 to <0.06). This is a differential-noise claim, not a mean-shift claim (mean ribosome_conc may also drop, but the focus is variance structure).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test comparing per-seed ribosome_conc values (target vs reference), computed on log-transformed values to approximate CV-sensitive variance comparison; additionally compute CV ratio = CV(target)/CV(reference) directly from per-seed spread. Reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 AND CV ratio >= 1.5. Also require protein_mass CV ratio (same comparison) < 1.2 to rule out a global noise inflation confound.
falsifier.refuting_result: If ribosome_conc CV ratio target/reference < 1.5 (noise not meaningfully amplified) or protein_mass CV also inflates by >=1.5x (indicating a nonspecific global noise effect rather than a capacity-specific one), H1 is refuted.

test.statistic: welch_t on log(ribosome_conc) per-seed values; CV ratio computed from per-seed spread output
test.threshold: |welch_t|>=2 and CV_ratio>=1.5 for ribosome_conc; CV_ratio<1.2 for protein_mass control

rivals.claim: Noise differences are driven by overall growth-rate slowdown/stress (a general stringent response), not by the specific capacity bottleneck in ribosome synthesis — i.e. any sufficiently harsh perturbation would inflate noise similarly, with ppGpp elevation as the common causal driver upstream of both growth slowdown and noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Since ppGpp rise is mechanistically coupled to rRNA depletion (stringent response triggers on uncharged tRNA accumulation), an observational comparison of ppgpp_conc vs ribosome_conc CV would be confounded. Instead, use relA gene_knockout (the enzyme producing ppGpp) crossed onto the rrna_operon_knockout background's closest feasible single-perturbation proxy: run relA gene_knockout alone under basal — if relA knockout alone (removing ppGpp synthesis capacity, independent of rRNA dosage) shows NO ribosome_conc CV inflation while rrna_operon_knockout does, this supports capacity-specificity over a ppGpp-driven generic stress mechanism. If relA knockout ALSO shows CV inflation similar to rrna_operon_knockout, the rival (ppGpp-driven generic noise) is supported instead.

rivals.claim: Any gene knockout perturbs seed-to-seed variability nonspecifically via simulation/solver noise (an artifact of FBA/stochastic integration under stress), not a biological noise-amplification mechanism specific to capacity bottlenecks.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a knockout of an unrelated, non-ribosomal gene (e.g. a metabolic enzyme not linked to translation capacity, acrB) also produces >=1.5x CV inflation in ribosome_conc, this rival is supported; absence of such inflation in the control knockout supports specificity to the ribosome-capacity bottleneck.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed stochastic variation under isogenic wildtype conditions is a faithful proxy for intrinsic gene-expression noise as classically defined (Elowitz-style), even though the simulator's noise source (solver/integration stochasticity + partitioning) may not map 1:1 onto biological transcriptional bursting.

ribosome_conc is an adequate proxy for ribosomal-protein gene product abundance even though it aggregates many ribosomal protein species into one active-ribosome channel; we cannot decompose per-ribosomal-protein-gene noise in this instrument.

Matched generation/timepoint sampling across seeds is valid for CV comparison (i.e. cells are compared at equivalent physiological age, not conflating cell-cycle phase variation with intrinsic noise).

division_rate and growth_rate are monitored only as confound checks, not as the primary readout; a knockout that is near-lethal (division_rate << 1) would need separate acknowledgment since near-death noise is a distinct phenomenon from steady-state expression noise.

relA gene_knockout is an adequate (if imperfect) interventional proxy for 'abolish ppGpp induction'; residual SpoT-mediated ppGpp synthesis may remain, so a null result from this control is interpreted as evidence against a STRONG ppGpp-driven generic-noise account, not as fully ruling out any ppGpp contribution.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales with the regulatory architecture and copy-number of the controlling machinery: genes whose product is itself a low-abundance, rate-limiting regulatory protein (e.g. RelA, a stringent-response synthetase) show higher relative noise (CV) in their own expression/activity readout than high-abundance 'housekeeping-like' structural components (e.g. ribosomal protein pool reflected in ribosome_conc), because low molecule-count species are more susceptible to stochastic birth-death fluctuations (intrinsic noise scales ~1/sqrt(N)).
hypothesis.h1: Across an isogenic population of seeds, the per-seed coefficient of variation (CV) of a low-copy regulatory channel (rela_conc) is substantially larger (>=2x) than the CV of a high-copy structural/translation-capacity channel (ribosome_conc), under matched wildtype/basal conditions.
hypothesis.h0: The per-seed CV of rela_conc is statistically indistinguishable from (within 2x of, and not significantly different by Welch t) the per-seed CV of ribosome_conc under wildtype/basal, i.e. noise does not differ systematically by abundance/regulatory class.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed CV = std/mean of rela_conc across seeds; compare to ribosome_conc CV

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc channel, steady-state charging mode
operational_defs.measure: mean and SD across 6-8 seeds, same generation, same condition

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel
operational_defs.measure: mean and SD across same seeds/condition

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: CV(rela_conc) > CV(ribosome_conc). Magnitude: CV(rela_conc) ~0.25-0.4 (25-40%) vs CV(ribosome_conc) ~0.05-0.10 (5-10%), i.e. at least a 2-4x ratio in CV between the low-abundance regulator and the high-abundance structural pool.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed CV of rela_conc and of ribosome_conc from the SAME wildtype/basal design (n=8 seeds, gen 3). Treat the ribosome_conc CV distribution as the comparator: test H1 via Welch t on per-seed values of a derived noise proxy (absolute deviation from the per-seed mean, which approximates CV-scale variance) for rela_conc vs ribosome_conc; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 with rela_conc deviations larger, AND the raw CV ratio (CV_rela/CV_ribo) >= 2.
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t| < 2 for the deviation comparison, or CV_rela/CV_ribo < 2 (or even reversed), H1 is refuted: abundance/regulatory-class does not predict noise in this sim.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and CV ratio>=2

rivals.claim: Noise is driven mainly by promoter/transcriptional burst kinetics (burst size/frequency), not by steady-state copy number per se — a low-copy but constitutively, smoothly-made regulator could still be low-noise, while a bursty high-copy gene could be noisy.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If an rrna_operon_knockout (which lowers ribosome capacity/copy number without touching RelA's promoter) raises ribosome_conc CV to match or exceed rela_conc CV, that shows copy-number depletion alone (independent of promoter identity) can produce high noise, undermining the claim that it's RelA's specific regulatory/promoter architecture rather than generic low-copy stochasticity.

rivals.claim: Growth-rate coupling (extrinsic noise) dominates: both rela_conc and ribosome_conc noise are driven by shared fluctuations in growth_rate across seeds, not by intrinsic molecule-count effects.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If per-seed rela_conc and ribosome_conc both correlate tightly with per-seed growth_rate (and their CVs track growth_rate CV proportionally), then the noise difference reflects extrinsic coupling to growth state, not intrinsic low-copy stochasticity specific to RelA.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variability at steady-state charging mode captures a meaningful proxy for intrinsic molecular noise (birth-death fluctuations), even though it is not a single-cell trajectory noise decomposition (intrinsic vs extrinsic unresolved).
rela_conc and ribosome_conc are measured in the same steady-state charging regime (no kinetic ppGpp module needed) so both channels are valid and comparable.
Per-seed CV at a fixed generation (gen 3) is a stable, comparable snapshot across designs, not confounded by differing growth trajectories between seeds.

The rrna_operon_knockout control is assumed to reduce ribosome_conc copy number substantially without crashing viability by generation 3 (division_rate checked as feasibility gate, not primary readout here).

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales inversely with the gene product's abundance/synthesis rate: low-copy-number regulatory genes (e.g., relA, a RelA-class synthetase expressed at low copy) show much higher relative noise in their downstream readout than high-copy, highly-expressed genes (e.g., ribosomal-protein-linked ribosome_conc), because noise in a birth-death/synthesis process is dominated by small-number Poisson-like fluctuations that average out at high copy number.
hypothesis.h1: The coefficient of variation (CV, across isogenic seeds) of a gene's expression-linked channel is a decreasing function of that gene's mean abundance/synthesis rate: low-abundance genes (rela_conc) show CV at least 2x higher than high-abundance genes (ribosome_conc) under matched wildtype conditions.
hypothesis.h0: CV of expression-linked channels is independent of mean abundance across genes; low-abundance (rela_conc) and high-abundance (ribosome_conc) channels show statistically indistinguishable CV across seeds (within replicate noise).

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Inverse relationship between mean abundance and noise: CV(rela_conc) / CV(ribosome_conc) >= 2.0 (e.g. CV_rela ~0.35-0.5 vs CV_ribosome ~0.1-0.15), consistent with Poisson-like 1/sqrt(N) scaling of low-copy synthetase vs high-copy ribosome pool.

Treat the claim as supported only if observed CV ratio >=2.0 and the minimum detectable effect at n=6-8 is below the observed ratio.

test.threshold: CV ratio >= 2.0 AND MDE at n<=8 seeds is <= 2.0 (i.e. the design is powered to detect the predicted effect)

rivals.claim: Noise is driven by regulatory architecture (burst size/frequency of transcription), not raw abundance -- a gene under stringent/feedback control (ppGpp-linked) is intrinsically bursty regardless of copy number.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Clamping ppGpp via ppgpp_conc (removing RelA/SpoT feedback dynamics) would collapse rela_conc-associated noise toward the ribosome-like low-CV regime even though rela's mean abundance is unchanged, showing noise tracks regulatory feedback not copy number alone.

rivals.claim: Noise differences are an artifact of differential mRNA/protein degradation and dilution rates (lifetime), not synthesis copy number -- short-lived regulators are noisier because fluctuations don't have time to average out, independent of abundance per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a high-abundance but short-lived species (not directly testable by name here, so scope-limited) showed CV comparable to rela_conc despite high mean, abundance alone would not explain the CV gap; within our two channels, this rival is hard to separate without a half-life control -- noted as an auxiliary limitation.

auxiliary_assumptions: rela_conc and ribosome_conc are both recorded under steady-state charging (no kinetic-charging requirement needed since the ppGpp module is on by default per channel note), so both channels are comparably sampled.
CV computed across 6-8 seeds at a matched generation is a valid proxy for intrinsic expression noise (isogenic stochastic replicates), not measurement artifact.
Differences in CV reflect intrinsic stochastic kinetics rather than deterministic seed-to-seed drift in initial conditions (assumed negligible given matched wildtype/basal setup).

The ppgpp_conc clamp and relA knockout are treated as the closest in-envelope interventional controls for isolating regulatory-feedback effects from raw-abundance effects; neither perfectly matches mean abundance to rela_conc's baseline, which is a known limitation.
mRNA/protein half-life controls are outside the current envelope's directly nameable channels; this gap is recorded as a scope caveat rather than chased further.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales inversely with the gene's expression level/regulatory robustness: low-abundance, tightly stringent-response-coupled genes (here operationalized via ribosome-synthesis machinery under ppGpp control) show higher cell-to-cell variability than high-abundance, constitutively expressed housekeeping-like machinery, because low copy number amplifies stochastic birth-death fluctuations and because genes whose transcription is gated by a single upstream regulator (RelA/ppGpp) inherit that regulator's own noise, whereas genes buffered by large constitutive pools do not.
hypothesis.h1: The coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds of a low-abundance, regulator-gated channel (rela_conc) is substantially higher (>=2x) than the CV of a high-abundance, less tightly single-regulator-gated channel (ribosome_conc) under matched wildtype growth conditions, and this gap shrinks when the regulatory coupling is removed (relA knockout background).
hypothesis.h0: The per-seed CV of rela_conc and ribosome_conc are statistically indistinguishable (within replicate noise) under wildtype/basal, i.e. expression-level/regulatory-architecture differences do not produce a detectable noise gap.

rivals.claim: Noise is driven mainly by growth-rate/division-cycle dilution dynamics (extrinsic noise from cell size/growth fluctuations) rather than by regulatory architecture or abundance per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV of rela_conc and ribosome_conc both track growth_rate CV closely (high correlation) and the CV gap disappears once growth_rate is matched, growth-rate-driven extrinsic noise -- not gene-specific regulatory coupling -- would be the better explanation.

rivals.claim: Noise differences are purely a function of mean copy number (Poisson/birth-death scaling, CV ~ 1/sqrt(N)) regardless of regulatory architecture -- i.e., any low-abundance gene would be noisy, with no special role for ppGpp/RelA coupling.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If, after clamping ppgpp_conc (removing the RelA feedback loop) in the ppgpp_conc perturbation design, rela_conc CV does NOT drop (stays >=2x ribosome_conc CV), that shows abundance alone -- not regulatory coupling -- explains the gap, refuting the regulatory-architecture mechanism.

all_rounds.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
all_rounds.claim: Across gene classes spanning a range of mean expression level, per-seed (replicate) CV of expression-proxy channels scales inversely with mean abundance: low-abundance gene products (relA, a regulatory synthetase present at very low copy number) show substantially higher across-seed relative variability than high-abundance housekeeping gene products (ribosomal proteins/rRNA machinery). Because relA sits on the ppGpp/ribosome regulatory axis, the test adds an abundance-matched-but-pathway-independent control gene (a metabolic/housekeeping enzyme whose activity is read via fba_objective-linked flux, not through growth_rate/ppGpp) to rule out the rival explanation that any observed divergence is just shared growth-rate-driven extrinsic noise rather than true copy-number-dependent intrinsic noise.
all_rounds.h1: log(CV) of a gene-class proxy channel decreases with log(mean abundance of that proxy) across >=4 distinct gene-class designs (wildtype, relA KO, rRNA-operon KO, and an off-axis metabolic-gene KO), with OLS slope significantly negative (slope CI excludes 0, point estimate roughly -0.4 to -0.6, consistent with CV^2~1/N scaling), and this negative relationship persists even for the off-axis gene that does not share the ppGpp/ribosome regulatory coupling.
all_rounds.h0: Per-seed CV of the proxy channels does not vary systematically with mean abundance across the gene-class designs; the log(CV)-log(mean) slope 95% CI includes 0, or the divergence between low- and high-abundance classes is indistinguishable from replicate noise (|welch_t| < 2).

Secondary/consistency check: Welch t of per-seed CV(rela_conc) vs per-seed CV(ribosome_conc) across seeds; supports H1 if |welch_t|>=2 in the predicted direction. The slope_ci test alone is sufficient to reject or fail to reject H1; the Welch t is reported as a consistency check, not required for rejection.

rivals.claim: Noise differences are driven by regulatory architecture (e.g. ppGpp-mediated feedback) rather than raw abundance per se -- relA is subject to tight stringent-response feedback that could suppress or amplify its noise independent of copy number.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under a ppgpp_conc clamp (fixing ppGpp at 1x basal, removing the natural RelA-ppGpp feedback loop), CV of rela_conc-linked downstream readouts (ribosome_conc) drops toward the high-abundance-gene baseline even though relA's own mean abundance is unchanged -- showing feedback, not abundance, sets the noise level. If instead CV stays elevated for the low-abundance gene class under the clamp, feedback is excluded as the dominant driver.

rivals.claim: Observed variability reflects extrinsic/global noise (shared fluctuations in ribosome allocation, RNAP, or growth rate affecting all genes proportionally) rather than intrinsic per-gene stochasticity tied to copy number.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If extrinsic noise dominates, CV(rela_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc) would co-vary tightly with CV(growth_rate) across seeds, and -- critically -- the off-axis metabolic-gene KO (not coupled to ppGpp/ribosome physiology) would show LOW noise despite low abundance, breaking the abundance-CV trend line; this would falsify the intrinsic-noise/abundance-scaling claim in favor of a shared global driver.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's seed-to-seed variation is treated as a PROXY for intrinsic single-cell expression noise, not a direct simulation of per-molecule stochastic birth-death kinetics; r1.1 is acknowledged as an irreducible scope limitation of the instrument, not resolved by this design.

rela_conc, ribosome_conc, and fba_objective are adequate proxies for underlying gene copy-number/expression-level differences across the three gene classes (low-abundance regulatory, high-abundance housekeeping, off-axis metabolic).

pykA (or an equivalent non-essential central-metabolism gene) knockout is mechanistically simulated with a stable low-abundance activity readout via fba_objective across >=6 surviving seeds over 3 generations; if the KO is lethal or fba_objective is degenerate (near-zero/undefined) for this gene, a different off-axis metabolic gene will be substituted without changing the test logic.

Partial rRNA operon knockout (operon_fraction_removed=0.3) is used instead of full knockout to keep the perturbation survivable across 3 generations, allowing CV to be computed from surviving seeds; this is a deliberate dose choice, not a confound.
Seed-to-seed CV computed over 6-8 seeds is treated as a usable (if noisy) relative-ranking estimate of expression noise across gene classes, not as a precise single-cell distribution estimate.

The 4-point condition-level slope regression (each point averaged over >=6 seeds) is acknowledged as having limited degrees of freedom; it is reported as the primary decisive test per r1.3 resolution, but a strict confirmatory follow-up would add more gene-class designs if the CI is borderline.

objection_ledger.issue: The core claim is about intrinsic stochastic noise from low molecule copy number (birth-death fluctuations), but the simulator's 'seeds' almost certainly encode coarse-grained parametric/initial-condition variation across whole-cell simulations, not per-molecule stochastic birth-death kinetics of individual genes. Seed-to-seed CV of a bulk concentration channel (rela_conc, ribosome_conc) conflates simulator-level stochasticity (numerical/parameter noise) with the biological intrinsic-noise mechanism (CV^2 ~ 1/N) the hypothesis is actually about.

The extrinsic-noise rival's distinguishing result is framed as 'CV(rela_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc) highly correlated across seeds' vs 'abundance-dependent divergence' -- but relA and ribosomal proteins are both coupled via growth_rate/ppGpp physiology (relA governs ppGpp which governs ribosome synthesis), so these two channels are mechanistically coupled, not independent. A correlation/divergence contest between two coupled channels cannot cleanly attribute the result to abundance-scaling vs shared global driver; you need an intervention that decouples them (e.g., compare CV scaling using a gene unrelated to the ppGpp/ribosome regulon, or hold growth_rate fixed via condition while varying only gene identity) to exclude the extrinsic/global-noise rival.

The falsifier's decision rule has two conjunctive/disjunctive conditions (Welch t on CV comparison AND/OR a 3-point log-log slope regression) but with only 3 x-values (wildtype, gene_knockout, rrna_operon_knockout) the 'slope CI' is fit on essentially 3 condition-level means (even with 6-8 seeds each, the independent x-points for the regression are only 3), making a stable, well-powered slope CI estimate questionable. It's unclear whether the slope test is meant to be decisive on its own or merely supplementary to the pairwise CV comparison.

The ppGpp-feedback rival (relA's own regulatory loop suppressing/amplifying its noise independent of abundance) is described with a clamp design (ppgpp_conc perturbation, row 5), but that design and its distinguishing_result are never incorporated into the actual decision_rule/falsifier -- only the extrinsic-noise rival's off-axis control (pykA) is wired into the primary slope_ci test. As written, the feedback rival is asserted to be excluded by argument but has no corresponding statistic in the falsifier.

The primary slope_ci test regresses log(CV) on log(mean) with only n=4 condition-level points (one per design), which gives very low statistical power to get a CI that excludes zero even if the true relationship is negative -- making 'fail to exclude zero' a weak/ambiguous falsifier rather than a crisp one.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Expression noise in this whole-cell instrument is best measured not at single-gene resolution (unavailable) but at the resolution of ribosome-capacity perturbations that titrate a gene class's effective mean output: knocking out increasing numbers of rRNA operons progressively lowers ribosome_conc and, through reduced active-ribosome number, increases the seed-to-seed CV of ribosome_conc and protein_mass -- consistent with intrinsic birth-death (Poisson-like, CV ~ 1/sqrt(N)) scaling of the limiting ribosome pool. We explicitly treat the rRNA-operon dose series as a stand-in exemplar for the general mean-vs-noise relationship (NOT a direct gene-A-vs-gene-B comparison, which this instrument cannot resolve at single-gene level), and we strengthen statistical power by using per-seed (not per-condition-mean) data points in the slope fit, giving n=32 (8 seeds x 4 doses) rather than n=4.
hypothesis.h1: Across a dose series of rRNA-operon knockouts (0/1/2/3 operons removed, all else matched), fitting per-seed log(ribosome_conc) against a per-seed local-window CV estimate pooled across all 32 seed-condition observations, log(CV of ribosome_conc) is negatively related to log(mean ribosome_conc): OLS slope approx -0.5, 95% CI excluding 0, R^2>=0.3; CV rises from ~3-6% (wildtype, high ribosome number) to ~15-25% at 3-operon knockout (low ribosome number), a 3-5 fold increase in CV as mean ribosome_conc falls. This single-gene-class titration stands in for the general principle that lower mean expression level (smaller molecule-number pool) predicts higher relative noise, a relationship the instrument can only resolve where one gene/class dominates a measured channel.
hypothesis.h0: CV of ribosome_conc is uncorrelated with mean ribosome_conc across the operon-dose series (slope not different from 0); any noise increase under rRNA knockout is better explained by a level-independent mechanism (e.g. stress/ppGpp induction uniformly destabilizing expression, or division_rate/viability confounds) rather than by the shrinking size of the fluctuating ribosome pool itself.

objection_ledger.issue: The channels available (protein_mass, rna_mass, etc.) are whole-cell aggregate quantities, not per-gene expression levels. The claim is about 'a gene's expression noise' but the operationalization uses bulk protein_mass/rna_mass as a proxy for a single targeted gene's output, assuming the knockout's effect is cleanly resolvable as a distinguishable shift in an aggregate channel. For a single non-essential regulator (rpoS) at 25-75% residual activity, its contribution to total protein_mass is likely negligible/undetectable against whole-proteome mass, so the CV measured is essentially whole-cell protein mass noise, not gene-specific expression noise.

The hypothesis conflates 'mean expression level' with 'gene identity/class' (low_expr_regulator vs rRNA operon vs high_expr control). These differ in many ways besides mean copy number (regulatory architecture, essentiality, operon structure, feedback), so observing a negative log(CV)-log(mean) slope across only 2-3 distinct gene targets cannot isolate mean-level scaling from these other gene-specific confounds -- the panel is too small and too heterogeneous to support a general '1/mean' scaling claim.

The tf_activity clamp and ppgpp_conc rival tests use the same whole-cell aggregate channels (protein_mass) as the main test, so if rpoS's contribution is too small to move whole-cell protein_mass in the main test, the rival-discriminating tests will suffer the identical sensitivity problem and cannot actually detect a 'collapse toward a floor' or a 'shared extrinsic drop' -- both rival and main test ride on the same potentially under-powered channel.

The user's question is about 'one gene's expression noise vs another's' broadly, but the final hypothesis only ever tests one gene class (rRNA operons) at varying dose, never actually comparing it to a genuinely different gene/class to establish relative noisiness. This is an acknowledged scope narrowing, appropriate given instrument limits, but should be explicitly flagged as an auxiliary assumption that the rRNA/ribosome case is used as a stand-in exemplar for the general mean-noise relationship, not a direct gene-vs-gene comparison.

The decision rule pools all 4 dose conditions into a single OLS fit with presumably only 4 mean/CV points (one per dose, each itself an average over 8 seeds), giving an OLS slope estimated from n=4 data points. A 95% CI on a slope from 4 points is a very low-power test; the rubric's R^2>=0.3 and CI-excludes-0 thresholds may be easy to satisfy or fail somewhat arbitrarily with so few degrees of freedom. This is a minor power/design concern, not a falsifiability flaw, since the test can still fail its own stated threshold.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales with the regulatory/structural burden placed on the gene's own synthesis machinery: genes whose protein products are low-abundance and whose synthesis depends heavily on a scarce, tightly-controlled resource (ribosome allocation under stringent control) show higher cell-to-cell noise than high-abundance, constitutively-expressed genes. Operationally, we test this via a genome-adjacent proxy: knocking out ribosome capacity (rRNA operons) or clamping ppGpp (which reallocates ribosomes toward stress genes and away from growth genes) should disproportionately increase the relative noise (CV) of a low-abundance, growth-coupled readout (ribosome-associated protein mass fraction, read via protein_mass and rna_mass) compared to a reference high-abundance bulk readout, because low-copy genes are more sensitive to stochastic partitioning of a limited translational resource.
hypothesis.h1: Perturbing ribosome capacity or ppGpp level (stringent response) increases the per-seed coefficient of variation (CV) of protein_mass (as a proxy for low-abundance, ribosome-limited gene products) by at least 1.5-fold relative to wildtype/basal, while a high-abundance bulk channel (dry_mass) shows negligible CV change (<10%).
hypothesis.h0: Ribosome-capacity or ppGpp perturbations do not change the CV of protein_mass relative to wildtype/basal beyond replicate noise (CV fold-change not significantly different from 1, and no significant mean shift via Welch t).

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Expression noise differences measurable at this whole-cell model's resolution are dominated by a single shared extrinsic/global resource-allocation noise floor, and this floor's proximate driver is ppGpp/stringent-response signaling rather than raw ribosome-operon capacity per se. Concretely: (1) bulk proteome-wide noise (CV^2 of protein_mass across seeds) correlates with growth-rate noise (CV^2 of growth_rate across seeds) across conditions, consistent with a shared extrinsic floor; and (2) clamping ppGpp (ppgpp_conc) collapses this correlation and/or changes the floor's magnitude MORE than deleting rRNA operons does, because ppgpp_conc directly perturbs the signaling node while rrna_operon_knockout only indirectly perturbs it through reduced ribosome output. This directly tests (and separates) the two mechanisms proposed in round 2 rather than pooling them, resolving r2.1 (rival not excluded) while keeping the proven bulk-noise operationalization from round 2.
hypothesis.h1: Pooling wildtype/basal, rrna_operon_knockout/basal, and ppgpp_conc/basal (6 seeds each), protein_mass CV^2 correlates with growth_rate CV^2 across conditions (Pearson r>=0.6). Critically, the two interventions act via DIFFERENT strength on this shared floor: ppgpp_conc clamp shifts mean protein_mass CV^2 by >=50% relative to wildtype/basal AND this shift is itself significantly different (|Welch t|>=2) from the shift produced by rrna_operon_knockout, demonstrating that ppGpp signaling -- not raw ribosome capacity -- is the proximate lever on the shared extrinsic noise floor.
hypothesis.h0: Either (a) protein_mass CV^2 is not significantly correlated with growth_rate CV^2 across conditions (correlation CI includes 0), indicating no detectable shared extrinsic floor, OR (b) the protein_mass CV^2 shift produced by ppgpp_conc clamp is NOT significantly different from the shift produced by rrna_operon_knockout (|Welch t|<2 comparing the two interventions' per-seed CV^2 distributions), indicating ppGpp signaling and ribosome capacity are indistinguishable/confounded drivers of the floor at this resolution.

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Positive correlation between protein_mass CV^2 and growth_rate CV^2 pooled across the 3 conditions (Pearson r>=0.6, R^2>=0.36), consistent with a shared floor ~0.1-0.2 CV^2 units (matching the classical Taniguchi/Ozbudak extrinsic-floor magnitude of ~0.1). ppgpp_conc clamp shifts mean protein_mass CV^2 by >=50% relative to wildtype/basal; rrna_operon_knockout shifts it by a smaller or differently-signed amount, and the two interventions' shifts differ from each other by a Welch |t|>=2, indicating ppGpp signaling is the proximate (not merely correlated) driver of the shared extrinsic noise floor.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of per-seed protein_mass CV^2 between ppgpp_conc/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal; reject H0(b) if |welch_t|>=2, indicating the two interventions produce distinguishable noise-floor shifts (ppGpp signaling is the dominant lever, not raw capacity). Separately, confirm the shared floor itself via slope_ci of protein_mass CV^2 on growth_rate CV^2 pooled across wildtype/basal, rrna_operon_knockout/basal, and ppgpp_conc/basal (3 conditions x 6 seeds); reject H0(a) if the 95% CI on the slope/correlation excludes 0 and r>=0.6.
falsifier.refuting_result: Welch t between ppgpp_conc/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal protein_mass CV^2 has |t|<2 (the two interventions are indistinguishable, so ppGpp signaling cannot be claimed as the proximate driver over raw capacity), OR the slope/correlation CI for protein_mass CV^2 vs growth_rate CV^2 pooled across conditions includes 0 (no shared extrinsic floor detectable at all).

rivals.claim: Gene-specific translational burst size (Ozbudak/Taniguchi: noise = a/mean + b, extrinsic floor ~0.1) is the true dominant mechanism of genome-wide expression noise, and any extrinsic-floor signature we observe in bulk protein_mass merely reflects that the floor swamps an underlying intrinsic per-gene effect this instrument cannot resolve.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Untestable directly here -- no per-gene protein-count channel exists. Recorded as an irreducible scope limitation (auxiliary assumption); our claim is restricted to what the extrinsic-floor observable can show at this resolution, not a refutation of the classical intrinsic-noise result.

rivals.claim: Ribosome capacity (not ppGpp signaling) is the proximate driver: rrna_operon_knockout and ppgpp_conc clamp should shift protein_mass CV^2 by similar magnitudes because ppGpp's main effect on noise is mediated entirely through its downstream effect on ribosome synthesis/availability, i.e. capacity and signaling are mechanistically inseparable at this resolution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If the Welch t comparing ppgpp_conc/basal vs rrna_operon_knockout/basal protein_mass CV^2 has |t|<2 (shifts statistically indistinguishable), this rival is supported: capacity and signaling are confounded/equivalent drivers, and no proximate-mechanism claim can be made beyond 'translation-capacity-adjacent perturbations shift the floor.'

auxiliary_assumptions: No per-species/per-gene stochastic protein-count channel exists in this instrument; single-gene burst-size noise (Ozbudak/Taniguchi mechanism) is therefore explicitly out of scope for direct falsification here and is retained only as a rival whose distinguishing result is 'untestable at this resolution' rather than confirmed/refuted.

protein_mass CV^2 across seeds is treated as a whole-proteome aggregate noise measure, not a single-gene measure; any single highly-expressed or highly-variable gene's contribution is assumed to be a small fraction of total protein_mass variance.

growth_rate CV^2 is assumed to be a reasonable proxy for shared global resource-allocation/extrinsic noise, given its mechanistic coupling to translation, ribosome allocation, and ppGpp in this model.

rrna_operon_knockout and ppgpp_conc clamp are assumed to be separable (non-confounded) interventions in the envelope; we do not combine them (combined perturbation is out of envelope), so the comparison between their individual effects on protein_mass CV^2 is the best available proxy for separating signaling from capacity mechanisms.
Deterministic-chaos vs. true stochastic noise sources remain indistinguishable in this simulator and are out of scope, as previously noted.

params.rationale: reduce genome-wide ribosome/translation capacity without directly forcing ppGpp level, to isolate the capacity-driven contribution to the noise floor

discriminating interventional control: directly clamp ppGpp signaling, independent of ribosome-operon deletion, to isolate the signaling-driven contribution to the shared noise floor and compare its magnitude against rrna_operon_knockout

residual_ambiguities: reached round cap without full convergence

objection_ledger.issue: The core observable — CV^2 of a single gene's protein copy number across isogenic seeds — requires a per-species stochastic protein count channel. The only listed channels are bulk aggregates (protein_mass, rna_mass, ribosome_conc). The candidate's workaround ('protein_mass tagged to gene_knockout target_genes param') assumes the simulator exposes per-gene protein trajectories under a gene_knockout perturbation used as a mere label — but gene_knockout in the perturbation list presumably knocks the gene OUT (removes its expression), which is incompatible with 'reading out its baseline noise.' If no per-gene protein channel exists, the entire panel design cannot be run as described.

Using protein_mass (bulk, whole-cell) fluctuations as a proxy for single-gene noise silently assumes that whole-cell protein_mass CV^2 is dominated by/tracks the focal gene's own stochastic fluctuations rather than being swamped by cell-size/extrinsic variation shared across thousands of co-expressed proteins. Given protein_mass aggregates the entire proteome, a single low-abundance gene's intrinsic noise would be utterly undetectable in that signal; the proxy cannot discriminate intrinsic burst-size noise from extrinsic cell-to-cell mass variation, which is exactly the rival (extrinsic noise floor) the hypothesis is trying to rule out.

Rival 2 (extrinsic/global physiological fluctuations dominate) is tested only by correlating each gene's CV^2 with growth_rate CV^2 — but growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, and protein_mass are mechanistically coupled in this whole-cell model (all driven by the same global resource-allocation/translation machinery). A tight correlation between gene CV^2 and growth_rate CV^2 would not distinguish 'burst size causes noise' from 'global coupling causes both to co-vary.' An interventional control is needed (e.g., ppgpp_conc clamp or relA-equivalent knockout that decouples ppGpp/growth fluctuations from translation-capacity fluctuations) rather than a correlational comparison.

The rivals section proposes that ppgpp_conc clamp vs rrna_operon_knockout should have DIFFERENT effects on the growth_rate–protein_mass CV^2 correlation (signaling vs capacity mechanism), but the actual falsifier/decision_rule never tests this differential pattern — it only runs a Welch t for rrna_operon_knockout vs wildtype and a single pooled correlation across all three conditions. As written, the decisive test cannot distinguish 'ribosome capacity drives the floor' from 'ppGpp signaling drives the floor', despite the design including both perturbations specifically to make that distinction.

H1 requires BOTH r>=0.6 AND each intervention shifting CV^2 by >=50%, but H0/refuting_result only specifies failure of ONE of these (Welch t OR correlation CI). This creates an asymmetric decision space: a result could satisfy neither full H1 nor the stated H0 (e.g., Welch t passes but ppgpp_conc clamp shift is only 30%), leaving the outcome unclassified under the stated decision rule.

ppgpp_conc is clamped at 3x basal while rrna_operon_knockout removes 3 operons -- these are not matched in 'perturbation strength' on any common scale, so a finding that the two shifts differ (|t|>=2) could simply reflect that one intervention is mechanistically more severe/further from wildtype than the other, not that ppGpp signaling is proximate versus ribosome capacity. The claim 'ppGpp signaling is the proximate driver, not raw capacity' requires the two perturbations to be calibrated to equivalent severity (e.g., matched effect on mean growth_rate or mean ppgpp_conc itself), otherwise the differential-t result is confounded by dose mismatch rather than mechanism.

The decision rule still leaves one gap: if the Welch t comparing ppgpp_conc vs rrna_operon_knockout is >=2 (interventions differ) but the pooled correlation CI in the shared-floor test excludes 0 only weakly or r<0.6, it's ambiguous whether H1 is confirmed (since H1 requires r>=0.6 AND the differential t AND each intervention's >=50% shift from wildtype) or whether this falls under H0(a). Suggest explicitly stating that H1 requires ALL three numeric conditions jointly and any single failure maps to the corresponding H0 clause, to close the residual seam between the two H0 disjuncts and the triple-condition H1.

all_rounds.question: How does a cell decide how many ribosomes to make in a given medium?
all_rounds.claim: E. coli sets ribosome concentration via a ppGpp-mediated growth-rate control circuit: in richer media (higher achievable growth rate) ppGpp falls, de-repressing rRNA/r-protein synthesis so that steady-state ribosome_conc rises approximately linearly with growth_rate, and this relationship is causally dependent on ppGpp signaling (synthesized by RelA) rather than being a passive byproduct of translation flux.
all_rounds.h1: Across media conditions, steady-state ribosome_conc scales positively and approximately linearly with growth_rate (slope significantly >0, consistent with the classical ribosome-growth-rate law), and this coupling requires ppGpp/RelA signaling: (a) clamping ppGpp to a fixed low value across conditions collapses the growth-rate/ribosome_conc slope (refit slope statistically indistinguishable from 0, or reduced by >=70% vs wildtype), and (b) deleting relA (removing ppGpp synthesis capacity) produces the same qualitative collapse/flattening, confirming RelA is the proximate causal lever rather than an independent confound.
all_rounds.h0: ribosome_conc does not vary systematically with growth_rate across conditions (wildtype slope 95% CI includes 0), OR neither the ppgpp_conc clamp nor the relA knockout changes the growth_rate-ribosome_conc slope relative to wildtype (clamped/knockout slopes statistically indistinguishable from wildtype slope across conditions).

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: steady-state ribosome_conc (uM) averaged over last generation per seed, per condition

operational_defs.construct: growth rate achievable in a medium
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: instantaneous specific growth rate (1/h) averaged over last generation per seed, per condition

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: steady-state ppGpp concentration (uM) averaged per seed, per condition; clamped via ppgpp_conc perturbation in one causal-test arm

operational_defs.construct: RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis capacity (proximate signaling lever)
operational_defs.observable: rela_conc and ppgpp_conc under relA gene_knockout
operational_defs.measure: rela_conc (uM, confirms knockout removes RelA protein) and ppgpp_conc (uM) logged alongside ribosome_conc/growth_rate per seed, per condition, in the relA-knockout arm

all_rounds.predicted_effect: OLS fit of ribosome_conc (uM) on growth_rate (1/h) across >=4 media conditions (basal, acetate, succinate, amino_acid timeline) in wildtype: positive slope with R^2>=0.6, slope magnitude ~5-15 uM per (1/h), i.e. ribosome_conc roughly doubles from slowest to fastest condition (~2-fold range). Under ppgpp_conc clamp (1x basal, refit across basal+acetate conditions): slope collapses to <30% of wildtype slope magnitude. Under relA gene_knockout (refit across basal+acetate conditions): ppgpp_conc drops toward baseline/low plateau and ribosome_conc-vs-growth_rate slope also collapses to <30% of wildtype slope, qualitatively matching the ppGpp clamp's effect (both arms raise ribosome_conc at low-growth conditions by >=20% relative to wildtype matched condition).

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: OLS slope of ribosome_conc on growth_rate across the 4 wildtype conditions; reject H0 (no scaling) if slope 95% CI excludes 0 and R^2>=0.6. Causal test 1 (ppGpp): refit OLS slope of ribosome_conc on growth_rate across ppgpp_conc-clamped basal+acetate arms; compare to wildtype slope (across matched basal+acetate subset) via slope CI non-overlap or reduction >=70%. Causal test 2 (RelA): Welch t of ribosome_conc, relA gene_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal across seeds; reject H0 of no RelA-dependence if |t|>=2 AND ppgpp_conc is confirmed reduced (Welch t on ppgpp_conc, relA-KO vs wildtype, |t|>=2, effect_pct<0 i.e. lower).
falsifier.refuting_result: Either the wildtype slope 95% CI includes 0 (no growth-rate scaling at all), or BOTH causal arms fail to collapse the slope/shift ribosome_conc (ppGpp-clamped slope remains >=70% of wildtype AND relA-KO Welch t on ribosome_conc has |t|<2 with effect_pct<20%), refuting ppGpp/RelA-causality and favoring a passive flux-coupled model. If relA-KO collapses ribosome_conc/growth slope but ppgpp_conc in that KO is NOT reduced (|t|<2 on ppgpp_conc), that would instead implicate a ppGpp-independent RelA function, refuting the stringent-response-specific mechanism.

test.statistic: OLS slope of ribosome_conc on growth_rate across conditions (primary and causal-arm refits); welch_t of ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc for relA-KO vs wildtype (causal arm 2)
test.threshold: slope 95% CI excludes 0 AND R^2>=0.6 (primary); clamped/KO slope reduced >=70% vs wildtype subset slope (causal arm 1); |welch_t|>=2 on both ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc for relA-KO vs wildtype (causal arm 2)

rivals.claim: Ribosome concentration is a passive consequence of translational demand/flux (charged-tRNA availability and elongation rate), not an actively regulated ppGpp/RelA set-point: ribosomes simply accumulate to match whatever translation flux the medium supports.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, neither the ppgpp_conc clamp nor the relA knockout would flatten the growth_rate vs ribosome_conc slope (both clamped and KO slopes remain statistically indistinguishable from wildtype subset slope, reduction <30%, |t|<2 on ribosome_conc), because ribosome output still tracks flux via fraction_trna_charged independent of ppGpp/RelA status.

rivals.claim: Ribosome allocation is primarily set by RelA-dependent amino-acid starvation signaling specifically via a ppGpp-independent RelA function (e.g. ribosome-stalling-triggered RelA action on translation itself), not via the ppGpp molecule per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA knockout collapses the ribosome_conc/growth_rate slope (confirming RelA matters) but ppgpp_conc in that same KO arm is NOT reduced relative to wildtype (|welch_t|<2 on ppgpp_conc), indicating the knockout's effect on ribosomes is not mediated through ppGpp level, decoupling RelA's role from the ppGpp-centered mechanism claimed in H1.

auxiliary_assumptions: Steady-state charging/ppGpp readout mode is active (not kinetic RelA/SpoT module) so ribosome_conc, ppgpp_conc, and rela_conc channels are all written and directly comparable across conditions.

The relA gene_knockout is mechanistically simulated to reduce/abolish RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis in this model (checked post hoc via the rela_conc/ppgpp_conc readout in that arm); if the model lacks a RelA synthesis mechanism, this is logged as a scope caveat, not chased further.

The four media conditions (basal, acetate, succinate, amino_acid-supplemented via timeline) span a sufficient range of achievable growth rates to detect a slope; acetate/succinate are static-only carbon sources requiring their own condition runs rather than mid-run switches.
ppgpp_conc clamp at a single multiple (1x basal) and relA knockout are sufficient to test de-repression collapse; we are not mapping a full ppGpp dose-response here.
Per-seed averages over the last generation are representative of steady state (no major transients remain by generation 3-4).
Growth differences across conditions/perturbations are not confounded by division defects; division_rate is checked only as a sanity flag, not a primary channel here.

objection_ledger.issue: The second rival (RelA-dependent signaling as proximate driver vs ppGpp concentration itself) is stated but the design includes no rela_conc readout or relA knockout arm to actually distinguish it. The candidate_designs list only wildtype/condition/timeline/ppgpp_conc perturbations — rela_conc is listed as a channel in principle but never measured in any design row, and no gene_knockout of relA is run. Without an interventional relA arm (or at minimum logging rela_conc across the existing arms), the claim that the effect is 'ppGpp-causal' rather than 'RelA-proximate' is asserted but not tested; since RelA activity and ppGpp level are mechanistically coupled (RelA synthesizes ppGpp), a pure ppGpp clamp without breaking the RelA coupling independently leaves open that any residual/non-collapse is attributable to RelA rather than ppGpp per se, and any full collapse could still be read as 'ppGpp clamp also blocks RelA output' rather than isolating the signal.

The decision rule for the primary test (wildtype slope) and the causal test (clamp vs wildtype at basal only) are logically decoupled: the primary claim requires the growth-rate/ribosome_conc coupling to exist across ALL 4 conditions, but the causal falsifier only compares clamped-vs-wildtype at a single condition (basal), plus one extra acetate clamp run not integrated into the decision_rule/threshold. A full test of 'clamp flattens the slope' requires the OLS slope to be refit across the clamped conditions (basal, acetate at minimum) and compared statistically to the wildtype slope, not just a single two-condition Welch t at basal.

The decision rule's causal arm 2 (relA-KO) only tests a Welch t at basal (single condition shift), not a refit slope across basal+acetate like causal arm 1 (ppGpp clamp), despite both acetate and basal relA-KO designs being run. This asymmetry means the relA causal test is weaker/less comparable than the ppGpp clamp test even though both datasets exist.

Whether the model's relA gene_knockout actually implements loss of RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis (rather than e.g. an unmodeled no-op) is uncertain and is already flagged as a scope caveat in auxiliary_assumptions; this is acceptable as stated rather than further litigated.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Genome-wide, single-gene protein expression noise is dominated by translational burst size, not mRNA abundance per se: across a panel of reporter designs probed via new_gene constructs with varied translation efficiency, CV^2 in reporter protein output follows CV^2 ≈ a/mean + b (b≈0.1 extrinsic floor). At matched mean AND matched global physiology (growth_rate, ribosome_conc, ppgpp_conc held approximately fixed), a reporter-intrinsic increase in translation efficiency (graded_gene_knockout applied to the reporter's own translation, e.g. a weakened RBS/initiation-rate proxy) raises CV^2 relative to a reporter design achieving the same mean via more transcripts translated less efficiently — demonstrating the burst-size effect is NOT an artifact of coupling through the shared ribosome/growth axis.
hypothesis.h1: At matched mean reporter protein level AND approximately matched global growth_rate/ribosome_conc/ppgpp_conc (verified, not engineered away), a reporter whose OWN translation efficiency is graded upward (via graded_gene_knockout targeting the reporter's translation/initiation step, reducing its effective transcript number needed for the same mean, i.e. larger burst size) shows CV^2 at least 1.5-3x higher than an isogenic reporter with lower reporter-intrinsic translation efficiency (more transcripts, smaller burst), even though the global translation machinery (ribosome_conc) and growth_rate are statistically indistinguishable between the two reporter conditions. Genome-wide, CV^2 vs mean fits CV^2 ≈ a/mean + b with b≈0.1.
hypothesis.h0: CV^2 of reporter protein output depends only on mean expression level (CV^2 ≈ a/mean) plus a fixed extrinsic floor b that tracks only global physiological variability (growth_rate CV^2, ribosome_conc CV^2); grading the reporter's own translation efficiency up or down, while holding global growth_rate/ribosome_conc/ppgpp_conc fixed, produces NO detectable difference in reporter CV^2 beyond measurement noise — any apparent burst-size effect in prior designs was an artifact of coupled global perturbation (e.g. rrna_operon_knockout) rather than a reporter-intrinsic mechanism.
