auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift perturbation (0 minimal_plus_amino_acids, 60 minimal) is implemented in the simulator as an instantaneous withdrawal of amino acid supplementation equivalent to a rich->minimal downshift.

ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc are recorded under steady-state charging for all three designs (no kinetic charging module switched on), so these channels are directly comparable across wildtype, shift, and relA-KO runs.

A relA gene_knockout in this simulator abolishes (or strongly attenuates) RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis without introducing confounding basal-growth defects large enough to swamp the shift comparison (if relA KO has a large basal growth defect independent of the shift, growth_rate slope comparisons will be interpreted qualitatively via the ppGpp channel primarily).

1 generation (~60 min) is a sufficient and appropriate window to capture the acute stringent-response spike documented in the literature (ppGpp rises within minutes); this window is kept fixed across target and reference for comparability.

Per-seed stochastic variation (6 seeds) is sufficient to detect a >=3-fold ppGpp effect via Welch's t at the stated threshold; this is treated as a replicate-power assumption, not independently re-verified via power_mde in this round.

all_rounds.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
all_rounds.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli cells trigger the stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes sharply, which in turn drives a drop in ribosome concentration/synthesis and a slowing of growth rate, as the cell reallocates resources away from translation capacity under amino-acid starvation.
all_rounds.h1: Removing amino acids mid-run (rich -> minimal media shift) causes a rapid (within ~1 generation) rise in ppgpp_conc (>=3-fold over basal) accompanied by a fall in ribosome_conc (>=25% decrease) and growth_rate (>=30% decrease), relative to a matched wildtype run that stays on amino-acid-supplemented media throughout.
all_rounds.h0: ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, and growth_rate in the amino-acid-withdrawal timeline are not significantly different from the matched wildtype/basal reference (no stringent response triggered, or effect sizes below threshold).

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: fold-change in ppgpp_conc post-shift vs pre-shift / vs reference, across seeds

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged
operational_defs.measure: drop in fraction_trna_charged (20-species average under steady-state charging) post amino-acid withdrawal

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: % decrease in ribosome_conc post-shift vs reference

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: % decrease in instantaneous growth_rate post-shift vs reference

all_rounds.predicted_effect: Within 1 generation after amino-acid withdrawal: ppgpp_conc rises >=3-fold (300%) vs reference; fraction_trna_charged drops by >=40% relative; ribosome_conc falls by >=25%; growth_rate falls by >=30%. Welch t for target vs reference on ppgpp_conc should give |t|>=2.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, target vs reference across seeds; reject H0 (accept stringent-response H1) only if two-sided |t|>=2 AND effect_pct >= 200% (>=3-fold); if |t|<2 or effect_pct<200%, H1 is refuted.
falsifier.refuting_result: ppgpp_conc in amino_acid_shift/aa_withdrawal is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal (|t|<2) or rises by <2-fold, despite tRNA charging dropping -- indicating ppGpp induction is not the operative mechanism.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=200%

rivals.claim: Growth slows via direct substrate limitation (reduced charged-tRNA pools stalling elongation) without requiring a ppGpp surge -- i.e. a passive kinetic effect, not an active regulatory stringent response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the rela_conc clamped-low or relA-knockout-like background (approximated here via ppgpp_conc clamped to basal), growth_rate and ribosome_conc still fall sharply upon amino-acid withdrawal despite ppGpp staying flat -- showing the effect is charging-driven, not ppGpp-driven.

rivals.claim: The observed slowdown is primarily a ribosome-capacity constraint (rRNA operon output) rather than a ppGpp-signaled reallocation -- i.e. ribosomes are simply mass-limited, not actively downregulated by alarmone signaling.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout background shows growth_rate and ribosome_conc already low at baseline, and amino-acid withdrawal produces little additional ppGpp-dependent change, implicating ribosome capacity rather than signaling as rate-limiting.

auxiliary_assumptions: Steady-state tRNA charging module is active (not kinetic), so fraction_trna_charged and ribosome_conc channels are valid as specified.
The 'minimal_plus_amino_acids' -> 'minimal' timeline switch is interpretable by the instrument as an amino-acid withdrawal event equivalent to the amino_acid_shift perturbation.
RelA/SpoT ppGpp module is on so ppgpp_conc and rela_conc channels are populated.
Isogenic seed-to-seed variability reflects intrinsic noise only; no genetic heterogeneity across seeds.

A single rich->minimal shift at generation ~1 (timepoint 60) is representative of 'sudden' amino acid runout; deterministic-chaos vs stochastic-noise distinctions in individual trajectories are out of scope for this test.
residual_ambiguities: [construct_ambiguity] Should 'suddenly runs out of amino acids' be operationalized as an instantaneous step-shift from rich to minimal medium (as modeled), or as a gradual depletion process, for this test?

objection_ledger.issue: For rival 2 (ribosome-capacity/rRNA-limitation explanation), the distinguishing result relies on comparing ppGpp-dependent changes in an rrna_operon_knockout background to the wildtype shift -- but this is still an observational/correlational comparison across backgrounds, not a clean interventional separation of 'ribosome capacity limited' from 'ppGpp signaling limited'. Since ppGpp and ribosome synthesis are mechanistically coupled (ppGpp acts in part via inhibiting rRNA transcription), an rrna_operon_knockout changes the very target of ppGpp action, confounding whether reduced response reflects capacity ceiling or a different coupled readout. A cleaner test would need ppGpp held artificially high in the rrna_operon_knockout background (or vice versa) to decouple signaling from capacity.

The claim and falsifier treat 'sudden' amino acid runout as a single step-shift at one timepoint (60 min) averaged over seeds, but it's unclear whether the user's question about a cell that 'suddenly runs out' intends a single discrete shift (as modeled) versus a gradual depletion/starvation curve. This is a reasonable modeling choice but worth confirming is the intended reading.

all_rounds.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
all_rounds.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli triggers the stringent response: RelA-mediated ppGpp accumulates sharply, ribosome concentration/ribosomal protein production falls, and growth rate drops — a coordinated reallocation away from translation, not a passive starvation collapse.
all_rounds.h1: Removing amino acids mid-run causes a rapid (within ~1 generation), large rise in ppgpp_conc (>=3-fold vs wildtype/basal) accompanied by a fall in ribosome_conc/ribosomal-protein output and growth_rate, and this response requires RelA (rela_conc-dependent synthesis).
all_rounds.h0: ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, and growth_rate in the amino-acid-withdrawal timeline do not differ (beyond replicate noise) from the wildtype/basal reference, i.e. the cell does not mount a distinct stringent response to acute aa starvation.

In the relA knockout, the ppGpp rise is abolished (<20% of wildtype-shift fold-change), confirming RelA-dependence.

rivals.claim: Passive dilution/starvation collapse: ribosome and growth decline occur simply from nutrient limitation and dilution of existing machinery, with no distinct ppGpp-driven regulatory surge (ppGpp rises only mildly, proportional to generic stress, not a RelA-specific switch).
rivals.distinguishing_result: ppgpp_conc rise is small (<50%) and relA knockout shows the SAME growth_rate/ribosome_conc trajectory as wildtype under starvation (no rescue/no difference), implying RelA is not driving the phenotype.

rivals.claim: Growth-rate drop is driven primarily by a different limiting resource or FBA infeasibility (e.g. carbon/energy co-limitation) rather than amino-acid/charged-tRNA sensing, so ppGpp changes are a side-effect, not the causal lever.
rivals.distinguishing_result: fba_objective shows infeasibility/large shift uncorrelated with fraction_trna_charged timing, and growth_rate decline precedes or is independent of the ppgpp_conc rise rather than following charged-tRNA depletion.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift perturbation in the timeline (minimal -> minimal lacking amino acids, or reverse) is mechanistically wired to reduce external amino-acid availability and thus charging rates in this model.
steady_state elongation/charging model is adequate to capture the charging-fraction and ppGpp coupling at this coarse timescale (we are not resolving sub-generation kinetic transients).
relA gene_knockout is simulated with a functional consequence on ppGpp synthesis (RelA catalytic function represented), not merely a label.
Replicate seeds capture intrinsic stochastic noise sufficiently for Welch's t across n=6 seeds to be meaningful.
No confounding simultaneous carbon-source switch occurs in the timeline (only amino acid shift).

objection_ledger.issue: The second rival (carbon/energy co-limitation via fba_objective) is listed but no corresponding candidate_design or decision rule is given to actually test it — none of the three designs vary carbon source or measure fba_objective timing relative to ppgpp_conc rise. As stated the distinguishing test for rival 2 is aspirational, not wired to an actual run.

The decision rule for the main falsifier only tests ppgpp_conc (target vs reference), but h1 bundles three more claims (ribosome_conc fall, growth_rate fall, RelA-dependence) that are not given their own welch_t/threshold decision rules in the falsifier block — only asserted in predicted_effect/operational_defs. Without a stated statistical test for each, 'ribosome falls 30-50%' and 'relA knockout abolishes the rise' could be eyeballed rather than falsified.

Rival 2's distinguishing_result requires comparing fba_objective in amino_acid_shift/starvation_shift vs wildtype/basal AND in relA_knockout/starvation_shift, but no candidate_design specifies measuring/reading fba_objective at all, nor is there a decision_rule/threshold for fba_objective comparable to the ppgpp_conc/ribosome_conc/growth_rate rules. As written this rival-exclusion is still just asserted prose, not an executable test with its own welch_t criterion.

fba_objective's temporal alignment relative to the ppGpp rise (needed to adjudicate whether infeasibility precedes or follows RelA action) is not read at matched timepoints within the timeline; the decision rule only compares endpoint/steady-state values across runs, which could blur a genuinely RelA-independent transient infeasibility spike.

rivals.claim: The growth-rate drop and ribosome decline are driven directly by metabolic/charging limits (falling fraction_trna_charged slowing translation elongation) independent of ppGpp signaling, i.e., a passive substrate-limitation effect rather than an active RelA-triggered regulatory response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA knockout + amino_acid_shift condition, fraction_trna_charged still falls and growth_rate still drops by a similar magnitude as wildtype (little attenuation), showing the growth arrest is charging-limited not RelA-dependent.

rivals.claim: The ppGpp rise and growth arrest are a generic stress response not specific to amino acid starvation, triggered similarly by any media perturbation (e.g., a different timeline event) rather than specifically coupled to amino acid withdrawal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A control timeline with a different non-amino-acid media shift (if available) or the reference wildtype/basal (no shift) itself already shows comparable ppgpp_conc elevation across seeds, meaning the shift-specific signal is not distinguishable from baseline seed variability.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator implements the RelA/SpoT ppGpp synthesis pathway mechanistically enough that a relA gene_knockout measurably reduces ppGpp synthesis rate (checked downstream; if RelA KO is not mechanistically wired, this falsifier cannot distinguish rivals and the result should be read as inconclusive, not as support for H0).
The amino_acid_shift timeline event ('minimal_plus_amino_acids' -> 'minimal') is accepted by the envelope as a valid timeline string distinct from a carbon-source switch.

Seed-to-seed stochastic noise in ppgpp_conc and growth_rate under constant wildtype/basal is small enough that a true >=3-fold shift-induced spike is statistically detectable with 6 seeds (if not, this is a power/seeds limitation, not evidence against H1).

ribosome_conc is only recorded under steady-state charging; this design therefore does not invoke kinetic/coarse_kinetic elongation models, so ribosomal-protein mass is read from ribosome_conc directly rather than from kinetic ribosomal-protein counts.
The post-shift timepoint for measurement is taken at the end of generation 1 after the shift (within ~1 generation, per H1), consistently across target/reference/control designs.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: Upon sudden amino-acid starvation (removal of amino acids from the medium mid-run), E. coli triggers the stringent response: RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis spikes, which in turn drives a rapid, coordinated shutdown of ribosome synthesis/activity and growth rate, rather than growth slowing passively just because translation substrate is limiting.
hypothesis.h1: Following an amino-acid withdrawal shift, ppgpp_conc rises sharply (>=3x basal) within the shift window and this rise causally precedes/accompanies a large drop in ribosome_conc (or ribosomal-protein proxy) and growth_rate; the ppGpp rise is RelA-dependent (abolished by relA knockout), and fraction_trna_charged drops concurrently as the trigger.
hypothesis.h0: ppGpp does not rise disproportionately (<1.5x basal) upon amino-acid withdrawal relative to wildtype basal media, and/or growth_rate and ribosome_conc declines are statistically indistinguishable between wildtype and relA-knockout backgrounds, i.e. the stringent-response alarmone is not driving the shutdown.

In relA-knockout background under the same shift, ppgpp_conc rise is abolished (<1.5x, |t|<2 vs wildtype basal) and growth_rate/ribosome_conc decline is blunted/delayed relative to wildtype-shift (smaller fold-change, distinguishing causal ppGpp role from passive substrate limitation).

rivals.claim: Passive substrate-limitation: growth and ribosome activity slow simply because charged tRNA/aa substrate is scarce, with no special causal role for ppGpp signaling (ppGpp rises only as an epiphenomenal correlate).

rivals.claim: Ribosome-capacity ceiling: the shutdown is actually paced by rRNA/ribosome synthesis capacity constraints (pre-existing ribosome pool depletion via dilution), not by signaling at all — testable by comparing to an rrna_operon_knockout background which independently caps ribosome capacity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal (no aa shift) alone reproduces a similarly large growth_rate and ribosome_conc drop vs wildtype/basal even WITHOUT any ppGpp spike or aa withdrawal, showing ribosome-capacity limitation alone (independent of ppGpp signaling) can explain comparable phenotypic magnitude.

Growth_rate and ribosome_conc are read from the steady_state elongation model (no kinetic module requested) since ribosome_conc is undefined under kinetic charging; this restricts resolution of very fast (sub-generation) transients but the gen-scale fold-changes predicted are expected to still be well above replicate noise.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli triggers the stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes sharply (~5-10x basal), which in turn drives a rapid drop in ribosome concentration/ribosomal protein synthesis and growth rate, as the cell reallocates resources away from translation machinery toward amino acid biosynthesis. This response (ppGpp spike and its downstream growth/translation effects) is causally dependent on RelA.
hypothesis.h1: Following an amino-acid withdrawal shift (minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal), in wildtype: (i) ppgpp_conc rises >=5-fold over the reference within the shift window; (ii) growth_rate falls by >=50% vs reference; (iii) fraction_trna_charged drops by >=30 percentage points vs reference. In a relA-knockout background under the identical shift, the ppgpp_conc fold-change is abolished (<1.5-fold vs its own reference, and significantly smaller than the wildtype shift response).
hypothesis.h0: None of the three wildtype shift responses (ppgpp_conc, growth_rate, fraction_trna_charged) differ from the wildtype/basal reference beyond replicate noise (Welch |t|<2 and effect size below the stated threshold for each channel), and/or the relA-knockout ppgpp_conc response under the same shift is not significantly smaller than the wildtype shift response (i.e. RelA-independence of the ppGpp spike).

In relA-KO under the same shift, ppgpp_conc fold-change vs reference is <50% (i.e. <1.5x, 'abolished') and significantly smaller (Welch |t|>=2) than the wildtype shift/reference ppgpp_conc effect.

rivals.claim: Growth arrest upon amino acid withdrawal is primarily a passive consequence of substrate limitation (no active ppGpp-mediated regulatory shutdown) — ribosomes stall simply because charged tRNA runs out, not because of an active RelA-driven program.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA gene_knockout background under the same withdrawal timeline, growth_rate still collapses by >=50% (matching WT) even though ppgpp_conc stays flat (<1.5-fold), showing growth arrest is ppGpp-independent (passive substrate limitation) — i.e. the growth_rate Welch test vs reference still passes in the KO despite the ppgpp_conc RelA-dependence test confirming the spike is abolished.

rivals.claim: The dominant response is ribosome-capacity downregulation via rRNA operon control (a ribosome-synthesis throttling mechanism) rather than a ppGpp-first signal; ppGpp rise is a secondary correlate, not the driver.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout background shows the same growth_rate and fraction_trna_charged trajectory as wildtype under amino acid withdrawal, with ppgpp_conc still rising >=5-fold — implying ribosome gene dosage, not ppGpp signaling, sets the response magnitude (ppGpp rise alone is insufficient/non-causal for the growth/charging phenotype).

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline shift event at t=180 (minutes) is placed such that the recorded sampling window spans at least 2 full generations post-shift, so that both the ppGpp spike (expected within ~1 generation) and the growth-rate/charging collapse (expected within 1-2 generations) are fully captured rather than truncated by the simulation's generation count; generations=3 is chosen to satisfy this.

Seed-to-seed stochastic variation in ppgpp_conc, growth_rate, and fraction_trna_charged under the reference (wildtype/basal) condition is assumed to be unimodal and well-characterized by Welch's t (i.e. no reference-condition bimodality that would inflate variance estimates).

The relA gene_knockout is assumed to be mechanistically simulated (RelA removed from the ppGpp synthesis pathway) rather than a no-op; this is checked downstream during testing per platform note, and if relA-KO shows no phenotype at all on any channel it is treated as inconclusive for RelA-dependence rather than confirming or refuting it.

fraction_trna_charged is read as the steady-state broadcast value (20 per-amino-acid values over 86 columns) since this run does not enable kinetic charging; no claim is made about per-species (86-independent) divergence.

objection_ledger.issue: The decisive falsifier test only specifies the decision rule for ppgpp_conc (the h0 rejection), but the headline h1 claim bundles three sub-claims (ppGpp fold-change, growth_rate drop, fraction_trna_charged drop) plus RelA-dependence. No decision rule/threshold is given for growth_rate or fraction_trna_charged, nor for the relA-knockout comparison itself (what fold-change in ppgpp_conc in the relA-KO counts as 'abolished' vs merely attenuated, with what statistic?). As written, only one of four sub-claims in h1 is actually falsifiable.

The timeline shift at generation/time '180' assumes a fixed sampling window in which both the ppGpp spike and the growth-rate collapse are expected to be captured; if the simulator's time resolution or doubling time makes '1-2 generations post-shift' fall outside or only partially within the recorded window, the predicted magnitudes (50-80% growth drop) could fail for reasons unrelated to the biology. This should be stated as an explicit auxiliary assumption (sampling window aligned with generation time) rather than left implicit.

The second rival (rrna_operon_knockout driving the phenotype instead of ppGpp) is described with a 'distinguishing_result' narrative but the falsifier/decision_rule block never states a quantitative threshold or Welch test for the rrna_operon_knockout vs wildtype comparison analogous to the relA test. As written this rival is gestured at via an included design but not actually decided by a stated rule.

all_rounds.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
all_rounds.claim: When amino acids are suddenly withdrawn from a growing E. coli population (minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal shift), the stringent response is triggered: uncharged tRNA accumulation drives RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis, which spikes ppGpp_conc (>=3x basal within ~1 generation) and causes a coordinate drop in growth_rate and ribosome_conc, mediated by a fall in fraction_trna_charged. This is a population-level, reproducible physiological switch, not a rare stochastic event: the large majority of seeds (>=75%) should show a concordant ppGpp spike + growth-rate collapse.
all_rounds.h1: Sudden amino acid withdrawal causes a RelA-dependent ppGpp spike (>=3-fold over basal) accompanied by a sharp drop in fraction_trna_charged and growth_rate, in the majority of replicate seeds (>=75%), and this response is abolished (no ppGpp spike, blunted growth-rate drop) when RelA is knocked out.
all_rounds.h0: Removing amino acids mid-run produces no systematic change in ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged, or growth_rate relative to the wildtype/basal reference beyond replicate noise (|welch_t|<2), i.e. the cell's response is not a reproducible stringent-response switch.

In the relA-knockout background, the ppgpp_conc fold-change is reduced to <1.5x basal (effect attenuated by >=50%), confirming RelA-dependence.

rivals.claim: Rival A: growth arrest upon amino acid withdrawal is driven simply by substrate/metabolite limitation (loss of amino acid pools feeding biosynthesis and charged tRNA) independent of ppGpp signaling — a passive metabolic bottleneck, not an active RelA-mediated regulatory switch.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA gene_knockout background, if growth_rate still drops sharply and fraction_trna_charged still falls despite ppgpp_conc staying near basal, this supports Rival A (passive bottleneck) over the ppGpp-mediated H1.

rivals.claim: Rival B: the observed ppGpp rise and growth slowdown are confounded by the media-shift procedure itself (osmotic/handling stress of switching media) rather than specifically amino acid absence — i.e. any timeline media shift, not amino-acid-specific, would produce a similar transient.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a control timeline shift (e.g. basal media shift without removing amino acids, or an ion/oxygen shift) still produces a comparable ppgpp_conc spike and growth_rate drop of similar magnitude, this supports Rival B (generic shift stress) over an amino-acid-specific H1.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's timeline mechanism for 'minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal' is implemented as a valid amino-acid withdrawal event (not merely a label) and triggers the charging/RelA kinetics module.

Post-shift window for measuring fold-changes is taken as the first generation following the shift event (~60 min onward), consistent with known stringent-response kinetics (minutes-scale ppGpp spike).

Steady-state vs kinetic charging distinction: ppgpp_conc and rela_conc are assumed available under steady-state charging mode for this run (no kinetic module requested), so ribosome_conc remains a valid readout alongside ppgpp_conc.

Seed-to-seed stochastic variation reflects genuine intrinsic noise in the regulatory network, not simulator artifact; 8 seeds is treated as adequate replicate power for detecting a >=3-fold mean shift given expected effect size.

relA knockout background is assumed to abolish (or strongly attenuate) RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis in the model, isolating the causal pathway (SpoT-mediated basal synthesis/degradation may remain, explaining why we expect attenuation rather than complete abolition).
residual_ambiguities: [construct_ambiguity] Should the relA-knockout ppGpp fold-change cutoff (<1.5x) be used as the single criterion to both confirm RelA-dependence AND rule out Rival A's passive-bottleneck account, or do you want a separate threshold for the Rival-A discrimination test?

objection_ledger.issue: The decision rule times the 'post-shift window' as '~60 min onward' / 'first generation following the shift,' but growth_rate itself is expected to collapse (>=50%) in that same window, which would stretch generation time unpredictably. The window boundary for measuring fold-changes should be defined in absolute time (minutes) rather than in generations, since generation length is not constant across the shift.

The relA knockout control (Rival A test) uses only 6 seeds and the same decision rule (|welch_t|>=2, effect_pct>=200%) was built for the H1 test, but no explicit quantitative threshold is given for what counts as 'ppgpp_conc staying near basal' in the knockout to confirm Rival A vs the attenuation criterion (<1.5x) already stated in predicted_effect. Clarify whether the <1.5x attenuation threshold is the same cutoff used to decide between H1 and Rival A, or a separate one.

The post-shift measurement window is still described only in relative/generation terms ('within 1 generation', '60 min onward') even though growth_rate itself is predicted to collapse >=50% in that same window, which stretches generation time. An absolute-time window (e.g., fixed minutes post-shift) must be specified so the ppGpp fold-change and tRNA-charging drop are measured on a consistent clock across target and reference, not a biologically-variable 'generation'.

Two different numeric thresholds exist for judging the relA-knockout outcome: the predicted_effect text says ppGpp fold-change should fall to <1.5x basal (attenuated by >=50%) to confirm RelA-dependence, while the falsifier/decision_rule block only defines the H1-vs-H0 test (>=200% effect, |t|>=2) for the wildtype shift, with no stated statistical rule for distinguishing H1 from Rival A in the knockout arm. State one unambiguous decision rule (e.g., Welch t and effect_pct threshold) for the relA-knockout comparison itself, so Rival A exclusion is falsifiable the same way H0 is.

hypothesis.predicted_effect: ppgpp_conc rises ~5-10 fold within 1 generation of amino-acid withdrawal (steep positive step) in wildtype; growth_rate falls by ~40-60%, ribosome_conc falls ~30-50% over 2 generations. In relA knockout background, ppGpp fold-change is suppressed to <2x (>=60% reduction in fold-change response vs wildtype) AND the growth_rate decline is also significantly attenuated (|welch_t|<2 between relA-KO post-shift and relA-KO pre-shift, OR effect_pct at least 50% smaller than wildtype's growth decline), consistent with ppGpp being causally required rather than merely correlated. The rrna_operon_knockout control is predicted to still show a >=5-fold ppGpp rise post-shift (ppGpp signaling intact) with a growth decline statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2 vs wildtype/aa_withdrawal), confirming the decline is ppGpp-mediated rather than a ribosome-capacity artifact.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of ppgpp_conc (target vs reference) across seeds at shift+1 generation; reject H0 (confirm stringent response) if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct>=400% (i.e. >=5-fold rise). RelA-dependence is confirmed only if BOTH: (a) the relA-knockout/aa_withdrawal design shows |welch_t|<2 for ppgpp_conc vs its own pre-shift/basal reference (ppGpp rise abolished), AND (b) growth_rate decline in relA-knockout/aa_withdrawal is significantly smaller than wildtype/aa_withdrawal's growth_rate decline (|welch_t|>=2 comparing the two decline magnitudes). The ribosome-capacity rival is rejected only if rrna_operon_knockout/aa_withdrawal shows |welch_t|<2 for ppgpp_conc fold-change vs wildtype/aa_withdrawal (ppGpp rise preserved, i.e. still >=5-fold) while also showing |welch_t|<2 for growth_rate vs wildtype/aa_withdrawal (similar decline) - this pattern together confirms ppGpp, not rRNA capacity, as the operative driver.
falsifier.refuting_result: H1 is refuted if: ppgpp_conc in amino_acid_shift/aa_withdrawal shows |welch_t|<2 or effect_pct<100% relative to wildtype/basal (no real spike); OR relA-knockout still shows a >=5-fold ppGpp rise (welch_t>=2 vs its own reference) with growth_rate decline statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (passive-limitation rival confirmed); OR rrna_operon_knockout shows a blunted ppGpp rise (<2-fold, |welch_t|<2 vs wildtype/aa_withdrawal) together with a growth decline similar to wildtype (capacity rival confirmed).

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=400% for the primary ppGpp spike; |t|<2 as the non-significance criterion for each rival-exclusion comparison

rivals.claim: Growth arrest upon amino-acid withdrawal is driven primarily by direct substrate limitation (lack of charged tRNA stalling translation) rather than an active ppGpp regulatory program - a passive/mechanical effect, not a signal-driven adaptive response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA knockout (which blunts ppGpp rise to <2-fold) still shows growth_rate declining by a magnitude statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2 comparing relA-KO's decline to wildtype's decline) despite minimal ppGpp rise, this supports the passive-limitation rival over the ppGpp-driven rival.

rivals.claim: The ribosome/growth shutdown is mediated by a ribosome-capacity constraint (rRNA operon dosage) rather than ppGpp signaling per se - i.e. cells are simply assembly-limited post-shift, independent of alarmone levels.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout shows BOTH a growth_rate decline statistically indistinguishable from wildtype's decline (|welch_t|<2) AND a blunted ppGpp rise (<2-fold, unlike wildtype's >=5-fold), this supports the capacity-limitation rival since the decline occurs without requiring elevated ppGpp. Conversely, if rrna_operon_knockout still shows a full >=5-fold ppGpp rise alongside a similar growth decline, ppGpp signaling (not capacity) remains the parsimonious driver and this rival is rejected.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's steady-state tRNA charging module responds to the amino_acid_shift timeline event in a way that is detectable within 1-3 generations (sampling resolution is adequate).
relA gene_knockout is mechanistically simulated as removing ppGpp synthetase activity (not merely a label) - this is checked downstream per the platform note.
Seeds (6) capture enough stochastic replicate variance for a Welch t-test to be meaningfully powered at this effect size; if not, a power_mde follow-up would be warranted.

The amino-acid withdrawal is modeled as a step-function media timeline shift (minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal), not a gradual depletion, and this matches the intended 'sudden' framing of the question.
Ribosome_conc and growth_rate are read from steady-state charging channels (not kinetic), consistent with the channel notes; kinetic ppGpp module is not separately engaged unless needed.

The teleological phrase 'to conserve resources until amino acids return' is retained only as motivating narrative context for WHY the stringent response is adaptive; it is explicitly NOT part of the falsifiable claim or decision rule (no recovery/return-of-amino-acids timeline arm is tested here) - this scope limitation is accepted to keep the design modest and focused on onset/causality, deferring reversibility testing to a follow-up round if requested.

objection_ledger.issue: The rrna_operon_knockout design (third candidate_design) is never connected to a decision rule or threshold in the falsifier/predicted_effect section. The text says 'if rrna_operon_knockout shows similar growth_rate decline without requiring ppGpp elevation, this supports the capacity rival' but no quantitative criterion (effect size, statistical test) is given for what counts as 'similar decline' or 'low ppGpp', so this rival-exclusion is not actually falsifiable/decidable from the design as specified.

'Adaptive mechanism to conserve resources until amino acids return' in the main claim is not operationalized anywhere - none of the four candidate_designs include a recovery/return-of-amino-acids phase to test whether the response is reversible/adaptive versus simply a passive shutdown. The falsifier only tests the onset (spike + RelA dependence), not the 'conserve resources until return' teleological claim.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli cells mount a stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes sharply, which in turn drives a rapid, coordinated downshift in ribosome concentration and growth rate, rather than growth simply slowing passively from substrate limitation alone.
hypothesis.h1: Following an amino-acid withdrawal shift, ppgpp_conc rises substantially (>=3-fold vs pre-shift baseline) within ~1 generation, and this rise precedes/accompanies a drop in ribosome_conc and growth_rate; the ppGpp rise is causally necessary for the magnitude of the ribosome/growth downshift (a relA-knockout background shows a significantly blunted downshift).
hypothesis.h0: Amino-acid withdrawal changes growth_rate and ribosome_conc only via direct substrate/charging limitation (fraction_trna_charged drop), with no distinct ppGpp-dependent contribution: ppgpp_conc does not rise more than ~1.2-fold, and/or a relA knockout shows the same magnitude of growth_rate and ribosome_conc downshift as wildtype (no significant difference).

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: ppgpp_conc rises sharply and transiently (>=3-fold, e.g. basal ~ -> 3-5x within 1-2 generations); ribosome_conc falls ~30-50% and growth_rate falls ~50-70% by generation 2, tracking the ppGpp spike. In the relA-knockout background under the same shift, the ppGpp rise is blunted (<1.5-fold) and the ribosome_conc/growth_rate downshift is significantly smaller in magnitude (effect size difference >=2 Welch-t, roughly half the wildtype % drop).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc (generation 1-2 post-shift value) for amino_acid_shift/rich_to_minimal vs wildtype/basal across seeds; reject H0 (claim H1 stringent-response spike) if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates >=3-fold rise. If |welch_t|<2 or fold-change <1.2x, H0 holds (no distinct ppGpp signature).
falsifier.refuting_result: ppgpp_conc shows <1.2-fold change (|welch_t|<2) despite growth_rate and ribosome_conc clearly dropping -- i.e., the downshift occurs without a ppGpp spike, supporting pure substrate-limitation H0.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=200% (>=3-fold)

rivals.claim: Rival A: passive substrate-limitation model -- growth and ribosome decline are driven directly by falling fraction_trna_charged (uncharged tRNA stalling translation) with ppGpp playing no more than a minor/incidental role.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA-knockout control under the same amino-acid shift, growth_rate and ribosome_conc downshift magnitude is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (Welch t <2 between relA-KO/shift and wildtype/shift), even though fraction_trna_charged still drops similarly -- showing ppGpp is not necessary for the response.

rivals.claim: Rival B: the downshift is primarily a ribosome-capacity constraint (rRNA operon dosage), not an alarmone-signaled program -- i.e., any manipulation that limits ribosome synthesis capacity (independent of ppGpp) would reproduce the same growth/ribosome kinetics.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout under basal (no amino-acid shift) shows a similar-magnitude slow decline in ribosome_conc/growth_rate as the amino-acid shift produces, without requiring any ppGpp spike -- suggesting capacity limitation alone, not signaling, explains the kinetics.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's RelA/SpoT ppGpp kinetic module is active for this run (ppgpp_conc and rela_conc channels are meaningful under the chosen elongation model) -- if only steady-state charging is used, ppgpp_conc still reports a value via steady-state charging rules and is treated as the relevant proxy.
fraction_trna_charged broadcast-over-86-columns under steady state is treated as 20 true per-amino-acid values; we average across the amino acids removed by the shift for the charging measure.

The amino_acid_shift timeline (rich->minimal) is assumed to deplete intracellular free amino acid pools quickly enough (within 1 generation) to trigger uncharged-tRNA accumulation; exact shift kinetics are not independently verified here.

relA gene_knockout is assumed to abolish (or strongly reduce) RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis in the model without other confounding fitness defects large enough to swamp the comparison within 3 generations.
Division_rate is not the primary readout here but will be checked post hoc to ensure the relA-KO is not simply dying/failing to divide, which would confound interpretation of growth_rate.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli triggers the stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes (~5-10x basal), ribosome concentration/ribosomal protein synthesis is cut, and growth rate drops sharply, as a direct consequence of falling aminoacyl-tRNA charging.
hypothesis.h1: An abrupt amino-acid withdrawal (timeline shift from minimal_plus_amino_acids to minimal) causes a rapid, large rise in ppgpp_conc (>=5x basal within the shift window) and a corresponding fall in ribosome_conc/growth_rate, mediated by RelA sensing uncharged tRNA (drop in fraction_trna_charged).
hypothesis.h0: ppgpp_conc does not rise appreciably (less than 2x basal, not distinguishable from wildtype/basal noise) after amino-acid withdrawal, and growth_rate/ribosome_conc changes are no larger than those seen in unperturbed replicate noise.

rivals.claim: Growth arrest and ribosome downregulation occur via passive substrate limitation (translation simply stalls from lack of charged tRNA) without requiring RelA-mediated ppGpp signaling -- i.e. ppGpp is incidental, not causal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In a relA gene_knockout under the same starvation timeline, ppgpp_conc fails to rise (stays near basal) yet growth_rate still falls and ribosome_conc still declines comparably to wildtype -- showing the growth arrest is ppGpp-independent, driven directly by charging depletion.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?

In a relA knockout under the identical shift timeline, the ppgpp_conc fold-change (post vs pre) collapses to <1.5-fold (near-null), confirming RelA-dependence rather than generic nutrient stress.

rivals.claim: Growth slowdown is a passive consequence of substrate limitation (reduced translation flux from lack of charged tRNA) rather than an active RelA/ppGpp regulatory program; ppGpp rise is incidental/small.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In relA gene_knockout under the identical amino_acid_shift timeline, growth_rate still falls by a similar magnitude (>=40%, post vs pre window) and ribosome_conc still drops, even though ppgpp_conc fold-change (post vs pre) is <1.5x — i.e. growth arrest occurs without the alarmone spike, showing ppGpp is not causally necessary.

rivals.claim: The response is driven by general nutrient/energy stress signaling (e.g. generic down-regulation via reduced flux through biosynthetic reactions) rather than specifically by RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis, so clamping ppGpp directly (independent of any aa shift, flat minimal timeline) would reproduce the growth/ribosome phenotype just as well as the real shift, OR the relA knockout would show an unchanged (non-reduced) phenotype despite the lack of ppGpp induction.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under ppgpp_conc clamp to 4x basal on a flat minimal timeline (no amino_acid_shift), growth_rate and ribosome_conc fall by markedly less than the self-paired post/pre effect size seen in the real amino_acid_shift design, showing ppGpp elevation alone (absent the shift) is insufficient to explain the full phenotype; conversely if relA knockout under the shift shows UNCHANGED growth_rate/ribosome_conc (not the predicted drop), that would support this rival over H1's RelA-dependence claim.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift timeline's pre-shift window (0-60 min, rich medium) and post-shift window (60-120 min, minimal medium) within the SAME design/seeds are the correct basis for a matched-history comparison, eliminating the baseline-state confound raised in objection r1.1.

The always-minimal wildtype/basal design is retained only as a secondary descriptive reference (not the primary falsifier reference) to contextualize absolute ppGpp/growth levels, not to drive the decision rule.

Charging status (fraction_trna_charged) is assumed to be the proximate RelA-sensed signal; the residual gap in rival 2 (distinguishing charging loss from simultaneous precursor/FBA-flux loss) is acknowledged as a minor, simulator-unresolvable confound and not chased further, per r1.2.
Window boundaries (0-60 min pre-shift, 60-120 min post-shift) are assumed long enough to capture steady post-shift ppGpp/growth levels within the 3-generation run.
Seeds are isogenic stochastic replicates; cross-seed variance is assumed comparable between pre- and post-shift windows for valid Welch t application.

objection_ledger.issue: The decision rule compares amino_acid_shift to a 'wildtype/basal' reference that is run on a flat minimal-medium timeline (no shift), while the target has a shift at t=60. This conflates 'time since shift' with 'time since simulation start' as the alignment basis, and assumes the two designs are otherwise identical (same seeds, same pre-shift growth state) ceteris paribus. If pre-shift physiological state differs between the rich-to-minimal shifted culture and the always-minimal wildtype, the ppGpp/growth differences could partly reflect that baseline mismatch rather than the shift itself.

Rival 2's distinguishing test (ppgpp_conc clamp alone) only shows ppGpp elevation is insufficient to fully reproduce the phenotype; it doesn't establish that charging status per se (as opposed to some other correlate of the real shift, e.g. simultaneous loss of amino-acid biosynthetic precursors feeding FBA) is the active ingredient. This is a residual, minor gap since the primary H1 claim (RelA-dependence) is already well-tested by the relA knockout.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly withdrawn from the medium, E. coli mounts the stringent response: uncharged tRNA accumulation drives a rise in ppgpp_conc, ribosome/growth repression follows, and growth rate drops within ~1 generation. Under the simulator's implemented ppGpp-determination rule (whether that is an explicit kinetic RelA/SpoT module or a steady-state formula keyed to fraction_trna_charged), a relA gene_knockout attenuates this ppGpp rise and the accompanying growth decline relative to wildtype -- the model's realization of the 'relaxed' phenotype.
hypothesis.h1: An amino-acid downshift causes a rapid (within ~1 generation), large-magnitude (>=3-fold) rise in ppgpp_conc relative to wildtype/basal, accompanied by a concomitant fall in ribosome_conc/growth_rate; the relA knockout attenuates this ppGpp rise by >=50% and shows a correspondingly blunted growth_rate decline, whatever the underlying computational rule (kinetic RelA synthesis or steady-state charging-based formula) the simulator uses to realize that dependence.
hypothesis.h0: ppgpp_conc does not rise appreciably (<1.5-fold) after amino-acid withdrawal relative to wildtype/basal, and/or the relA knockout shows no significant attenuation (|welch_t|<2, <50% attenuation) of the ppGpp/growth response, i.e. the modeled response is RelA-independent regardless of mechanism.
