hypothesis.predicted_effect: Amino-acid downshift (timeline target) vs wildtype/basal (reference): ppgpp_conc rises >=3-fold (e.g., ~1-2 uM basal to >=4-6 uM) within ~1 generation post-shift; growth_rate falls by >=40% over the same window; ribosome_conc declines or plateaus (no further accumulation). In the relA knockout under the identical downshift timeline, the ppGpp fold-change is attenuated by >=50% relative to wildtype's shift response, and the growth_rate decline is correspondingly blunted (relaxed phenotype), REGARDLESS of whether the simulator implements this via an explicit kinetic RelA/SpoT module or via a steady-state ppGpp-from-charging formula that encodes the relA knockout's effect.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of ppgpp_conc (downshift vs wildtype/basal) across seeds, post-shift window; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates >=3-fold rise. For the RelA-dependence claim, Welch t-test of ppgpp_conc fold-change between relA_knockout/aa_downshift and wildtype/aa_downshift; reject the RelA-independence rival if |welch_t|>=2 and the knockout shows >=50% attenuation, interpreting this as 'model-realized' RelA-dependence rather than a claim about literal enzyme kinetics if the kinetic module is absent.
falsifier.refuting_result: ppgpp_conc shows <1.5-fold change post-shift (|welch_t|<2 vs wildtype/basal), or the relA knockout under the same downshift shows a ppGpp spike and growth_rate decline statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2), indicating the modeled response does not require RelA under either implementation.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=200% (i.e., >=3-fold) for the spike; |t|>=2 and >=50% attenuation for the relA-dependence test

rivals.claim: Growth slows due to generic nutrient/carbon limitation stress unrelated to the stringent response (ppGpp-independent passive dilution/translation slowdown from substrate scarcity).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, relA knockout under the same downshift would still show a comparably sharp growth_rate decline and ribosome repression despite a blunted or absent ppGpp spike (i.e., growth/ribosome channels move similarly in WT and relA-KO even though ppgpp_conc diverges).

rivals.claim: The ppGpp response is driven primarily by SpoT (ribosome-idling/hydrolase-synthetase switching) rather than RelA, so a relA-only knockout would show little attenuation (SpoT compensates).
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA_knockout/aa_downshift would show ppgpp_conc fold-change and growth_rate decline statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2), since SpoT alone sustains the spike.

rivals.claim: The simulator computes ppgpp_conc purely as a deterministic function of fraction_trna_charged with no distinct relA-knockout term, so any observed attenuation reflects a scripted charging-pathway artifact rather than any RelA-pathway mechanism, kinetic or otherwise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, relA_knockout/aa_downshift's fraction_trna_charged trajectory would be statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/aa_downshift's (|welch_t|<2) even while ppgpp_conc differs, revealing that the knockout acts on ppGpp through a channel other than charged-tRNA dynamics -- i.e., a formula artifact rather than a charging-coupled mechanism; this would be flagged as an auxiliary-assumption caveat, not grounds to abandon the operational claim.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's steady-state charging model computes ppgpp_conc as a deterministic function of fraction_trna_charged (per the dial note); under steady-state charging this still responds to the amino-acid downshift via charged-tRNA depletion even without an explicit kinetic RelA/SpoT module.

If the kinetic ppGpp/RelA module is not enabled, ppgpp_conc and rela_conc channels may not be written under kinetic charging; we assume steady-state charging mode is used here so these channels are populated.

The relA gene_knockout is assumed to be mechanistically represented in the model in SOME form (either as a kinetic synthesis term or as a modifier of the steady-state charging-to-ppGpp formula); we do not require the former specifically -- the claim and falsifier are framed as 'model-realized RelA-dependence' agnostic to the exact implementation, and this ambiguity is an irreducible scope caveat not resolvable by the simulator's output alone.
Pre-shift window (before timepoint 300) serves as each seed's own baseline; post-shift window is defined as generations 1-3 after the shift event.
Isogenic seeds capture only intrinsic stochastic noise, not structural/model uncertainty.

objection_ledger.issue: The auxiliary assumptions state that ppgpp_conc may be computed deterministically from fraction_trna_charged under 'steady-state charging' rather than via an explicit kinetic RelA/SpoT synthesis module. If that is how the simulator actually works, a relA gene_knockout may have no distinct mechanistic effect on ppgpp_conc beyond whatever hardcoded knockout-to-charging mapping exists, making the 'RelA-dependence' falsifier test the knockout's effect on fraction_trna_charged (or a scripted override) rather than a genuine RelA-synthesis mechanism. This could produce a result that looks confirmatory/disconfirmatory for reasons unrelated to the claimed RelA-mediated synthesis pathway.

The main spike falsifier compares 'downshift vs wildtype/basal' but wildtype/basal has no timeline event, so the post-shift window for wildtype/basal is undefined -- it's unclear whether the comparison uses wildtype's single steady-state value as a flat reference or an equivalent time-window average, which could shift the effective fold-change threshold.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly withdrawn mid-run (minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal), wild-type E. coli mounts a stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes sharply (>=3-fold), ribosome/rRNA synthesis is repressed and growth rate drops within ~1 generation. This repression is causally ppGpp-dependent, not merely a passive consequence of substrate (charged-tRNA) depletion: a relA knockout shows a similarly depleted charged-tRNA pool after the shift (ruling out differential substrate limitation) yet exhibits a blunted ppGpp spike (<1.5-fold) AND a substantially smaller/slower growth_rate and ribosome_conc decline than wildtype (the 'relaxed' phenotype).
hypothesis.h1: Amino-acid downshift causes a RelA-dependent surge in ppgpp_conc (>=3-fold over pre-shift baseline within the shift generation) accompanied by a fall in ribosome_conc (>=20%) and growth_rate (>=40%); relA knockout abolishes the ppGpp surge (<1.5-fold) and substantially blunts the growth_rate/ribosome_conc decline (post-shift drop in KO <=half the wildtype drop), DESPITE fraction_trna_charged declining similarly in WT and KO (|t|<2, ruling out the rival substrate-limitation account).
hypothesis.h0: ppgpp_conc after amino-acid withdrawal does not differ from the wildtype pre-shift baseline (fold-change <1.5x, |t|<2 by Welch t), OR relA knockout shows no difference from wildtype in ppGpp response AND no difference in growth_rate/ribosome_conc response to the same shift (|t|<2 for both), OR fraction_trna_charged diverges between WT and KO enough to explain any growth-rate difference by substrate limitation alone rather than ppGpp.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc trajectory across the amino-acid shift timeline
operational_defs.measure: fold-change of ppgpp_conc at post-shift generation vs pre-shift baseline, per seed

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc and growth_rate channels post-shift
operational_defs.measure: percent drop relative to pre-shift baseline, per seed

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and rela_conc channels in relA-knockout background under same shift
operational_defs.measure: fold-change of ppgpp_conc post-shift vs pre-shift, compared between wildtype and relA-KO

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged channel post-shift in WT vs relA-KO
operational_defs.measure: percent drop relative to pre-shift baseline, per seed, compared via Welch t between WT-shift and KO-shift

operational_defs.construct: ppGpp-dependence of growth/ribosome shutdown (vs mere substrate effect)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and ribosome_conc fold-change post-shift, WT-shift vs relA-KO-shift
operational_defs.measure: Welch t of percent-drop values between genotypes, holding fraction_trna_charged drop statistically indistinguishable

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Wildtype: ppgpp_conc rises >=3-fold (e.g. ~20uM -> >=60uM) within the shift generation; growth_rate falls ~40-60% and ribosome_conc falls ~20-40% over the same window. relA-KO: ppgpp_conc fold-change <1.5x (KO/WT ratio of fold-changes <0.5); fraction_trna_charged drop in KO is statistically indistinguishable from WT (|t|<2, same ~30-50% depletion in both), but KO growth_rate/ribosome_conc drop is <=half the WT drop (e.g. growth_rate falls only ~10-20% in KO vs ~40-60% in WT), demonstrating the repression tracks ppGpp, not tRNA charging.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (activation): Welch t of ppgpp_conc post-shift vs pre-shift within wildtype amino_acid_shift across seeds; reject H0 if |t|>=2 AND fold-change >=3x. Step 2 (RelA-dependence of ppGpp): Welch t of ppgpp_conc fold-change, relA-KO-shift vs WT-shift; H1 requires |t|>=2 with KO fold-change <1.5x. Step 3 (rule out substrate confound): Welch t of fraction_trna_charged percent-drop, relA-KO-shift vs WT-shift; H1 requires |t|<2 (charging deficits statistically indistinguishable). Step 4 (causal consequence): Welch t of growth_rate percent-drop and of ribosome_conc percent-drop, relA-KO-shift vs WT-shift; H1 requires |t|>=2 with KO drop <=50% of WT drop on both channels. All four steps must hold for H1 to survive.
falsifier.refuting_result: Either (a) wildtype ppgpp_conc does not rise >=3-fold (|t|<2 or <3x), or (b) relA-KO shows an equally strong ppGpp spike as WT (|t|<2 between KO-shift and WT-shift fold-change), or (c) fraction_trna_charged diverges substantially between WT and KO (|t|>=2), confounding the growth comparison with differential substrate limitation, or (d) KO growth_rate/ribosome_conc drop is statistically indistinguishable from WT (|t|<2) despite the blunted ppGpp spike, indicating growth repression is NOT ppGpp-dependent.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for steps 1,2,4 (plus fold-change magnitude criteria); |t|<2 for step 3 (tRNA charging equivalence)

rivals.claim: Growth/ribosome repression upon amino-acid withdrawal is driven mainly by substrate limitation (reduced charged-tRNA pools feeding translation) rather than an active ppGpp-mediated regulatory program.
rivals.distinguishing_result: fraction_trna_charged drops similarly in relA-KO and WT (|t|<2, step 3 holds) yet growth_rate/ribosome_conc decline in KO is NOT substantially blunted relative to WT (|t|<2 in step 4) — i.e. despite abolished ppGpp spike, growth repression proceeds unabated, showing charging deficit alone (not ppGpp) drives the shutdown.

rivals.claim: A SpoT-mediated (RelA-independent) basal ppGpp synthesis/hydrolysis balance accounts for the residual ppGpp changes seen even without RelA, meaning RelA knockout alone will not fully abolish the response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA_ko/amino_acid_shift still shows a partial ppGpp rise (e.g. 1.5-2x, intermediate between full WT response and null) rather than complete flatness, indicating a SpoT contribution the single-gene KO does not remove — step 2's <1.5x criterion would be marginally violated even though |t|>=2 vs WT.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's amino_acid_shift perturbation on the timeline channel mechanistically couples to ppGpp synthesis via the RelA module (steady-state or kinetic charging mode with RelA/SpoT module on) so ppgpp_conc and rela_conc are recorded.
relA gene_knockout is mechanistically simulated as loss of RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis (not merely a label) — this is checked downstream but assumed for test design.
Pre-shift baseline (first generation on minimal_plus_amino_acids) is a valid comparator for post-shift fold-change within the same seed, controlling for seed-to-seed basal variation.

fraction_trna_charged under steady-state charging is reported as 20 per-amino-acid values broadcast over 86 columns; the percent-drop measure is computed per seed as the mean across the 20 distinct amino-acid charging values to avoid pseudo-replication from the broadcast columns.
4-8 seeds and 2-3 generations are sufficient to capture the acute (within ~1 generation) stringent response without conflating with longer-term adaptation.

Residual SpoT-mediated ppGpp synthesis in the relA-KO (if present) is treated as a quantitative question for step 2's threshold, not grounds to abandon the RelA-dependence test; a partial (1.5-3x) response would be flagged as a scope caveat rather than full confirmation or full refutation.

objection_ledger.issue: The first rival (substrate-limitation via charged-tRNA) is stated and a distinguishing_result is given in prose, but it is not wired into the falsifier/decision_rule or candidate_designs. The actual test only compares ppgpp_conc fold-change WT vs relA-KO; it never operationalizes a decision rule on fraction_trna_charged trajectories matching between WT and KO. Without a concrete statistical criterion (e.g. Welch t on fraction_trna_charged WT-shift vs KO-shift showing |t|<2, i.e. similar charging deficit) paired with divergent growth_rate/ribosome_conc, the rival is not actually excluded by the pre-registered test — only gestured at in the rivals section.

The claim asserts growth_rate falls '~40-60%' and ribosome_conc '~20-40%' specifically BECAUSE of ppGpp-mediated repression, but no relA-KO comparison is specified for these two channels in the falsifier/decision_rule — only ppgpp_conc is compared across genotypes. If relA-KO still shows a similarly large growth_rate/ribosome_conc drop (just without the ppGpp spike), that would undercut the causal claim that ppGpp drives the repression, yet the current test design would not catch this since it doesn't test growth_rate/ribosome_conc in the KO vs WT comparison.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly withdrawn from a growing E. coli cell, uncharged tRNA accumulation triggers RelA to synthesize a sharp spike in ppGpp, which represses ribosome/rRNA synthesis and growth rate (the stringent response). Isolating RelA's causal role requires comparing a relA single knockout (which could be confounded by SpoT compensation in the shared alarmone pool) against a relA-spoT double knockout (the classic 'ppGpp0' relaxed strain) that should show the most complete abolition of the spike and should also test whether growth repression itself is ppGpp-dependent.
hypothesis.h1: Amino-acid downshift causes a rapid, large (>=3-fold) rise in ppgpp_conc relative to pre-shift baseline, with a 30-50% drop in ribosome_conc/growth_rate; a relA-spoT double knockout abolishes most of this rise (<1.5-fold, the classic 'relaxed'/ppGpp0 phenotype) AND substantially rescues growth_rate/ribosome_conc decline, while a relA single knockout shows an intermediate or possibly unblunted response if SpoT compensates.
hypothesis.h0: Amino-acid downshift does not change ppgpp_conc beyond replicate noise relative to wildtype/basal, or any ppGpp rise that does occur is unaffected by removing both RelA and SpoT (i.e. relA-spoT double KO still shows >=3-fold rise comparable to wildtype), or growth_rate/ribosome_conc decline persists unchanged in the double KO despite ppGpp abolition.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: fold-change of mean ppgpp_conc in a post-shift window vs pre-shift baseline window, same seeds

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged
operational_defs.measure: mean post-shift value relative to pre-shift baseline

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: post-shift mean growth_rate vs pre-shift mean, % reduction

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: post-shift mean vs pre-shift mean, % reduction

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc in relA KO and relA-spoT double KO backgrounds
operational_defs.measure: fold-change of post-shift ppgpp_conc rise in each KO background vs wildtype under identical shift

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Amino-acid downshift (timeline: minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal) produces a >=3-fold spike in mean ppgpp_conc within ~1 generation post-shift vs pre-shift baseline (Welch t vs wildtype/basal >=2), paired with a ~30-50% drop in growth_rate and ribosome_conc, and fraction_trna_charged drops below ~0.5 of baseline. In the relA-spoT double knockout under the identical shift, the ppGpp rise is abolished to <1.5-fold (ppGpp0/relaxed phenotype) and growth_rate/ribosome_conc decline is substantially blunted (e.g. <15% drop vs the 30-50% drop in wildtype), demonstrating ppGpp-causal repression. The relA single knockout is predicted to show intermediate blunting (roughly 1.5-3-fold rise) if SpoT's basal synthase activity partially compensates; matching wildtype implicates full SpoT compensation, matching the double KO confirms RelA dominance.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc (post-shift window) between amino_acid_shift/downshift and wildtype/basal across seeds; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 and effect_pct indicates >=3-fold rise. RelA/SpoT-dependence: Welch t of the ppGpp rise (post-shift minus pre-shift) between amino_acid_shift/downshift and relA_spoT_knockout/downshift; H1's causal-dependence claim is refuted if that |welch_t|<2 (double KO does not abolish spike). Secondary falsifier for the passive-dilution rival: Welch t of growth_rate (post-shift) between amino_acid_shift/downshift and relA_spoT_knockout/downshift; if |welch_t|<2 (growth still drops similarly despite abolished ppGpp), this refutes ppGpp-causal repression of growth.
falsifier.refuting_result: ppgpp_conc shows no significant rise after downshift (|welch_t|<2 vs wildtype/basal, or effect_pct <50%), OR the relA-spoT double knockout shows an equally large ppGpp spike as wildtype (|welch_t|<2 between wildtype/downshift and relA_spoT_KO/downshift), indicating the response is RelA/SpoT-independent, OR growth_rate/ribosome_conc still drop by a similar magnitude in the relA-spoT double KO despite the abolished ppGpp spike (|welch_t|<2 for growth_rate between wildtype/downshift and relA_spoT_KO/downshift), indicating growth repression is not ppGpp-mediated.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for the main ppGpp spike vs wildtype/basal; |t|<2 between wildtype/downshift and relA_spoT_KO/downshift required on ppGpp-rise to confirm dependence (its presence refutes H1); |t|<2 on growth_rate between the same two designs would refute ppGpp-causal repression of growth

rivals.claim: The growth slowdown after amino-acid downshift is driven mainly by direct metabolic/flux limitation (reduced amino-acid supply starves translation directly) rather than by an active ppGpp-mediated regulatory program.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, growth_rate and ribosome_conc would drop similarly across wildtype, relA KO, and relA-spoT double KO (no genotype-dependence), and ppgpp_conc would show little or no spike even in wildtype.

rivals.claim: ppGpp does rise, but growth arrest is driven primarily through SpoT (not RelA) as the dominant synthase under this shift, so a relA single knockout would NOT substantially blunt the spike because SpoT alone produces most of it; only removing SpoT as well abolishes the response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA_knockout/downshift shows a >=3-fold ppGpp rise comparable to wildtype (|welch_t|<2 between wildtype/downshift and relA_KO/downshift), while relA_spoT_knockout/downshift shows the abolished (<1.5-fold) response -- confirming SpoT, not RelA, is dominant.

rivals.claim: The ppGpp spike is a generic stress-response correlate rather than a causal repressor of ribosome/rRNA synthesis; growth slowdown is passive mass-balance dilution from reduced protein synthesis capacity, not active repression.
rivals.distinguishing_result: ppgpp_conc rises as predicted in wildtype, but ribosome_conc/growth_rate decline persists essentially unchanged even in the relA-spoT double knockout where ppGpp is abolished -- i.e. growth still drops ~30-50% despite no ppGpp spike, showing the repression is not ppGpp-mediated. This is the decisive secondary falsifier in the falsifier block.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift perturbation implemented as a timeline media-shift (minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal) engages the kinetic/coarse-kinetic charging and RelA/SpoT ppGpp module so that ppgpp_conc and rela_conc are actually written (per channel notes, these require the module ON); if only steady-state charging is active, the kinetic spike dynamics may not be resolvable and this is logged as a scope caveat.

relA single knockout and relA-spoT double knockout are assumed to be mechanistically simulated as a gene_knockout/multi_gene_knockout (removing RelA and/or SpoT synthase/hydrolase activity) in this model; if the double KO specifically is not mechanistically distinct from the single KO (e.g. SpoT's hydrolase/synthase split is not modeled), the compensation question cannot be resolved and this is a separate capability gap, not evidence against H1.
Pre-shift and post-shift windows are drawn from the same seeds in the timeline run, so the pre/post comparison controls for seed-level baseline variation.
Isogenic replicate noise across seeds is assumed small relative to the predicted >=3-fold effect, consistent with the 4-8 seed scale used here.

The relA-spoT double knockout is used here as the closest in-envelope interventional control for isolating causal ppGpp-dependence of ribosome/growth repression (rival 3), since the forbidden combined perturbation ppgpp_conc+gene_knockout cannot be used; growth_rate/ribosome_conc persistence despite ppGpp abolition is the decisive signature.

objection_ledger.issue: The decisive RelA-dependence test compares ppGpp fold-change between wildtype and relA-knockout under the SAME downshift. But ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged (and indirectly ribosome_conc/growth_rate) are mechanistically coupled in the stringent-response module -- a relA knockout doesn't just remove RelA synthesis, it also changes charging dynamics via feedback on growth and translation, which could itself alter ppGpp readout through SpoT's basal synthase/hydrolase activity. The design has no intervention that isolates RelA's synthase activity from these coupled downstream changes (e.g. a spoT-null background or a catalytically-dead RelA control), so a blunted spike in the relA KO could reflect either true RelA-dependence or compensatory coupling in the shared alarmone pool shared with SpoT.

Rival 3 (ppGpp rise is a correlated byproduct, not causally repressing ribosomes) is explicitly flagged by the candidate itself as something the proposed design 'may not cleanly separate' and is just logged as a scope caveat rather than given a decisive falsifier. As written, no test in the falsifier block can refute this rival -- it is conceded, not excluded.

hypothesis.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
hypothesis.claim: Across a broad panel of single-gene knockouts, a substantial minority of genes (roughly 20-30%) are individually dispensable for growth on basal minimal medium: their KO strains show division_rate not significantly reduced from wildtype and growth_rate within ~10% of wildtype, whereas the remaining majority show a significant division_rate or growth_rate deficit (candidate essential genes).
hypothesis.h1: A nonzero, substantial fraction (20-30%) of a sampled panel of E. coli genes can be knocked out individually without significantly impairing division_rate or growth_rate relative to wildtype on basal medium; the panel shows a bimodal split into 'dispensable' and 'essential' classes rather than a uniform graded cost.
hypothesis.h0: Knocking out any given gene in the panel produces, on average, a growth_rate and division_rate deficit that is statistically indistinguishable in frequency/magnitude from what would be expected if nearly all genes were essential or mildly deleterious (i.e., no distinct dispensable subpopulation emerges; deficits are uniformly graded rather than bimodal, OR the dispensable fraction is near 0%).

operational_defs.observable: division_rate and growth_rate channels of a single-gene knockout strain across seeds/generations
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of each KO's division_rate (and growth_rate) vs wildtype/basal across seeds; a KO is classified 'dispensable' if |t|<2 for both channels, else 'essential/impaired'

operational_defs.construct: fraction of genome that is dispensable
operational_defs.observable: proportion of a sampled gene panel classified dispensable
operational_defs.measure: count of dispensable KOs / total KOs tested, with BH-FDR correction across the panel to control false discovery of 'dispensable' calls

operational_defs.construct: distribution shape (bimodal essential/dispensable split vs graded cost)
operational_defs.observable: pooled per-gene effect sizes (growth_rate % deficit) across the panel
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled per-seed growth_rate effect-size values across the panel

operational_defs.construct: ribosome-capacity dependence of the dispensable/essential split (discriminating control)
operational_defs.observable: division_rate and growth_rate of an rRNA-operon-knockout strain vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of rrna_operon_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal on division_rate and growth_rate; a large, uniformly severe deficit here (vs the graded/bimodal single-gene panel) shows that capacity-limiting lesions behave differently from the single-gene essential/dispensable split, isolating ribosome-allocation confounds from the gene-panel claim

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Of a sampled panel of ~20 genes (spanning metabolic, biosynthetic, and non-essential-looking regulatory/transport categories), 20-30% (i.e., 4-6 genes) will show division_rate and growth_rate statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|Welch t|<2, effect_pct within ~10%), while the remaining 70-80% show growth_rate deficits >=20% or division_rate <1 with |t|>=2. The pooled effect-size distribution will be bimodal with BC>0.555, not a smooth unimodal graded-cost curve. The rrna_operon_knockout control is predicted to show a severe, near-uniform deficit (growth_rate drop >=40%, division_rate ~0) across seeds, confirming that capacity-limiting lesions do not reproduce the panel's graded/bimodal pattern.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (classification): for each of 20 single-gene KOs, run welch_disconfirm on division_rate and growth_rate vs wildtype/basal across 6 seeds; classify 'dispensable' if |t|<2 on both channels after BH-FDR correction (q<0.10) across the 20-gene panel. Step 2 (shape): compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (bimodality_bc) over the pooled per-seed growth_rate effect_pct values across all 20 KOs; reject unimodal/graded null if BC>0.555. Step 3 (control): confirm rrna_operon_knockout/basal shows a severe, non-bimodal uniform deficit distinct from the panel's split (|t|>=2 on both channels for all seeds), ruling out a trivial capacity-limitation confound. H1 requires: dispensable fraction in [0.15,0.40] AND BC>0.555 AND the control deficit is severe/uniform.
falsifier.refuting_result: Either (a) the dispensable fraction (|t|<2, FDR-controlled) falls outside [0.15,0.40] -- e.g. near 0% (almost all genes essential) or near 100% (almost all dispensable) -- or (b) the pooled effect-size distribution is unimodal (BC<=0.555), indicating a graded continuum of fitness costs rather than a discrete essential/dispensable split.

test.statistic: BH-FDR corrected Welch t per gene (classification) + Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled effect sizes (shape)
test.threshold: q<0.10 for classification significance; BC>0.555 for bimodality; dispensable fraction must land in [0.15,0.40]

rivals.claim: Rival A (near-universal essentiality under single, static basal minimal medium): because the simulated basal condition is minimal and unbuffered against any single pathway loss, almost all genes in a representative panel (e.g. metabolic/biosynthetic) will show significant growth_rate/division_rate deficits -- the 'dispensable' fraction is near 0%, not 20-30%.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A gene_knockout/basal panel run would show >=90% of KOs with |Welch t|>=2 on division_rate, and the dispensable fraction falls far below 0.15, refuting H1 outright.

rivals.claim: Rival B (condition-dependent dispensability masquerading as graded, not discrete): apparent 'dispensability' is really a continuum of mild-to-severe fitness costs (e.g. slower but nonzero growth) rather than a true bimodal essential/non-essential split; the panel's effect sizes would show a smooth unimodal distribution centered on a graded cost.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled growth_rate effect_pct values across the 20-gene panel would yield BC<=0.555 (unimodal/graded), even if the mean dispensable-classified fraction happens to land in [0.15,0.40] by coincidence of the threshold cut -- refuting the 'discrete essential/dispensable classes' part of H1.

rivals.claim: Rival C (apparent dispensability is a ribosome-capacity artifact, not gene-specific): the dispensable/essential split merely reflects how much spare ribosome capacity a KO leaves, not a genuine discrete biological classification -- any perturbation that trims capacity (not just gene-specific KOs) would reproduce the same bimodal-looking split.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout/basal produces a similarly bimodal (not uniformly severe) distribution of deficits across seeds/operon-removal levels, that would support Rival C; H1 predicts instead a uniformly severe, non-bimodal deficit from capacity removal, mechanistically distinct from the gene panel's split.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator mechanistically implements the metabolic/regulatory consequences of each targeted gene's knockout (not just a generic fitness penalty); genes where KO has no coded mechanistic effect would spuriously appear 'dispensable' -- this is a known scope caveat the simulator cannot fully resolve and is treated as an auxiliary assumption rather than chased further.

The 20-gene panel is treated as a representative (not exhaustive) sample of the genome; the predicted 20-30% dispensable fraction is a population-level claim about this sampled distribution, not a claim about every individual gene.

Basal minimal medium is held fixed across all KOs and wildtype; no mid-run media shifts are introduced, so dispensability is assessed under one static nutrient context (a caveat noted in Rival B/condition-dependence framing).

Welch t and BH-FDR classification thresholds (|t|<2, q<0.10) and the BC>0.555 bimodality threshold are the platform's standard decision thresholds and are assumed stable across seeds/generations at this modest scale (6 seeds, 3 generations).

The rrna_operon_knockout control is assumed to isolate a generic capacity-limitation mechanism distinct from gene-specific regulatory/metabolic loss; this is the closest in-envelope interventional control available (single perturbation, not a combined knockout).

hypothesis.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
hypothesis.claim: A substantial minority (roughly 30-40%) of a curated panel of non-essential-annotated E. coli genes can be individually deleted without abolishing growth or division, while a smaller but non-trivial fraction (~10-20%) of genes nominally annotated 'non-essential' in rich media will show a measurable growth/division defect in this simulator's minimal basal condition, revealing condition-dependent essentiality.
hypothesis.h1: Across a broad panel of single-gene knockouts in basal minimal media, the distribution of growth_rate and division_rate outcomes is bimodal: most KOs cluster near wildtype (viable, 'dispensable') while a distinct minority cluster at near-zero growth/division (essential), with the dispensable fraction being the majority (~60-70%) of the panel.
hypothesis.h0: Gene essentiality in this simulator is NOT bimodally distributed across the panel; instead growth_rate and division_rate declines form a continuous unimodal spread around wildtype with no distinct essential cluster, i.e. Sarle's bimodality coefficient does not exceed the bimodal threshold.

operational_defs.construct: viability / can live without a gene
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate channels averaged over seeds and generations for a knockout design
operational_defs.measure: KO classified 'dispensable' if growth_rate >= 0.5x wildtype mean AND division_rate >= 0.8; 'essential' if growth_rate < 0.1x wildtype mean OR division_rate < 0.2

operational_defs.observable: difference in classification of the same KO panel run under basal vs acetate condition
operational_defs.measure: fraction of KOs that flip from dispensable (basal) to essential (acetate) or vice versa

operational_defs.observable: pooled per-seed growth_rate values across the full KO panel
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled values; BC>0.555 taken as bimodal

operational_defs.construct: simulator capability to register essentiality (positive control)
operational_defs.observable: division_rate and growth_rate for rrna_operon_knockout vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: division_rate collapse (<0.2) and growth_rate <0.1x wildtype confirms the model CAN register essential-gene loss; failure to collapse flags a model-coverage limitation applying to the whole panel interpretation

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of growth_rate across a panel of ~20 KOs in basal media: ~60-70% of KOs within 20% of wildtype growth_rate (dispensable cluster), ~10-20% at <10% of wildtype (essential/lethal cluster), remainder intermediate; Sarle's BC > 0.555 over pooled per-seed growth_rate values. Condition-dependence: ~10-20% of the panel flips classification between basal and acetate.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed growth_rate values from the full KO panel (all genes x seeds); reject H1 (bimodal essentiality) if BC<=0.555, indicating a unimodal continuous spread instead of distinct dispensable/essential clusters. Validity of this test depends on the rrna_operon_knockout positive control showing division_rate<0.2 (confirming the simulator CAN register essentiality) -- if the positive control fails, the bimodality test is uninterpretable rather than disconfirming.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555, i.e. growth_rate values across the panel form a single continuous distribution around wildtype rather than two separated clusters, meaning essentiality is not well-described as binary dispensable-vs-essential in this simulator

test.statistic: bimodality_coefficient
test.threshold: BC>0.555 required to confirm bimodal (reject H0 of unimodal)

rivals.claim: Essentiality is a continuous trait (growth_rate declines gradiently with gene loss severity) rather than a binary dispensable/essential split -- i.e. there is no distinct essential cluster, just a spread.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc test returns BC<=0.555 over the pooled panel, and per-gene growth_rate values fill the range between 0 and wildtype roughly uniformly rather than clustering at two poles

rivals.claim: Apparent 'dispensability' in this simulator is an artifact of incomplete pathway annotation/coverage (genes appear non-essential only because the simulator lacks the reaction/regulatory links that would reveal their true essentiality), not a real biological signal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: the rrna_operon_knockout (known essential, ribosome capacity) positive control fails to show division_rate collapse (division_rate stays >=0.2 and growth_rate >=0.1x wildtype), indicating the model cannot register essentiality for genes whose consequences propagate through pathways it does not simulate -- which would undermine trust in any 'dispensable' classification from the panel

auxiliary_assumptions: The panel of 20 genes is a representative sample spanning metabolic, regulatory, structural, and essential housekeeping categories, sufficient to estimate dispensable/essential fractions at this scope.
growth_rate and division_rate channels are computed consistently across all KO designs under steady-state elongation (default), so cross-design comparisons are valid.
A KO 'crashing' does so within 3 generations; longer-term adaptation or compensatory mutation is out of scope for this test.

The simulator's gene-reaction/regulatory network coverage is assumed adequate for at least the panel genes chosen (mix of well-characterized central metabolism, biosynthesis, and structural genes); genes entirely absent from the model's reaction network cannot be meaningfully tested and are excluded from the panel.
Per-seed noise (isogenic stochastic variation) is small enough relative to the essential/dispensable gap that pooling seeds does not wash out bimodality.

The rrna_operon_knockout positive control is treated as a gating check on simulator capability, not as part of the bimodality statistic itself -- its outcome determines whether the main test result is interpretable, per the decision_rule caveat.

all_rounds.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
all_rounds.claim: Among the stratified panel of 16 E. coli genes sampled across four a-priori functional strata (known-essential controls, redundant-paralog metabolic enzymes, accessory/regulatory factors, and stress-response regulators) — selected by a pre-registered stratification rule rather than by expected-phenotype cherry-picking — most single-gene knockouts are tolerated (near-neutral growth) but a substantial minority show conditional or strong fitness defects, producing a right-skewed, long-tailed distribution of growth-rate fold-changes rather than a uniform 'all survive' or 'all die' outcome.
all_rounds.h1: Across the 16-gene panel, stratified a priori into 4 genes/stratum from {known-essential (pyrD, folK), redundant-paralog (treF, nagK, gatZ, aroH), accessory/regulatory (ybeD, yciI, ydcH, ygfF, proP), stress/global-regulatory (rpoS, relA, acrB)} with strata fixed BEFORE seeing any simulation output, single gene_knockout vs wildtype/basal yields a heterogeneous growth_rate fold-change (KO/WT) distribution: >=60% of the 16 genes show |fold-change-1|<0.1 (near-neutral), while 10-30% show fold-change<0.5 or division_rate<0.8 (strong/lethal), and the pooled distribution has Sarle's BC>0.555 (bimodal-or-long-tailed), with the known-essential stratum alone reproducing most of the lethal tail.
all_rounds.h0: All 16 tested gene knockouts, regardless of a-priori stratum, produce growth_rate and division_rate statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal (|welch_t|<2 for every gene, BH-FDR n_significant<10% of panel), i.e. the panel is homogeneous with no detectable essential or strongly-deleterious outliers — the stratification itself fails to predict outcome.

operational_defs.observable: division_rate and growth_rate channels under single gene_knockout vs wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: per-seed division_rate (fraction of generations completing division) and growth_rate (1/h); a gene is classified 'essential-like' if division_rate<0.8 or growth_rate fold-change<0.5 relative to wildtype mean

operational_defs.observable: fixed pre-registered gene-to-stratum assignment made before any run (known-essential / redundant-paralog / accessory-regulatory / stress-regulatory), documented in params
operational_defs.measure: stratum label used only for post-hoc stratified reporting of fold-change bins, never to re-select genes after seeing results

operational_defs.construct: fitness cost distribution across the gene panel
operational_defs.observable: pooled per-gene, per-seed growth_rate fold-change (KO/WT) values across the 16-gene panel
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled fold-change values; fraction of genes in each defect bin (neutral/moderate/strong), reported overall and per stratum

all_rounds.predicted_effect: Right-skewed/bimodal distribution across the 16-gene panel: ~60-70% near-neutral (|fold-change-1|<0.1), ~15-25% moderate defect (0.5<=fold-change<0.9), ~10-15% strong/lethal (fold-change<0.5 or division_rate<0.8) — with the lethal tail concentrated in the known-essential stratum (pyrD, folK expected near fold-change~0-0.2) rather than scattered randomly across strata. Pooled BC>0.555; panel mean fold-change ~0.82.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate fold-change values across all 16 genes; separately run Welch's t for each gene vs wildtype/basal and apply BH-FDR across the panel. Reject H1 (heterogeneity) if BC<=0.555 (unimodal/homogeneous) AND fewer than 10% of genes show BH-FDR-significant growth_rate reduction (n_significant_fdr10/n_genes < 0.10).
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled fold-change distribution is unimodal (BC<=0.555) and BH-FDR flags 0-1 of 16 genes as significantly different from wildtype, consistent with near-uniform tolerance (H0) rather than a stratum-predicted heterogeneous split.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-gene per-seed growth_rate fold-change
test.threshold: BC>0.555 to support H1 heterogeneity; also require n_significant_fdr10 (via bh_fdr_movers on per-gene welch_t) > 10% of panel

rivals.claim: Rival A: Dispensability is strictly binary — genes are either fully essential (near-zero growth, division_rate~0) or fully neutral, with no intermediate 'moderate defect' class; the apparent middle bin is just noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the histogram shows two tight clusters at fold-change~1 and fold-change~0 with almost nothing in the 0.5-0.9 moderate band; BC may still exceed 0.555 but the moderate-defect fraction would be ~0, contradicting the predicted 15-25% moderate bin, and the redundant-paralog/accessory strata would show NO intermediate phenotypes despite being distinct from the known-essential stratum.

rivals.claim: Rival B (panel-composition confound, previously raised): any observed heterogeneity is an artifact of hand-picking genes already known to span essential/non-essential, not a property of the broader non-essential-looking gene population.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Addressed by pre-registering 4 strata with fixed membership BEFORE simulation and reporting results per stratum: if heterogeneity is a real population property (not cherry-picking), the redundant-paralog and accessory-regulatory strata — selected WITHOUT prior expectation of lethality — should STILL show their own internal spread (some near-neutral, some moderate-defect) rather than being uniformly neutral; if instead only the known-essential stratum shows any defect and the other 3 strata are perfectly flat at fold-change~1, that supports the cherry-picking rival over genuine population heterogeneity.

rivals.claim: Rival C: seed-to-seed stochastic noise, not stable gene identity, drives apparent heterogeneity (within-gene variance ≈ between-gene variance).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, per-gene disconfirm calls would show high per-seed spread comparable to the panel's between-gene spread, and repeated seeds for the same gene would not cluster tightly around a gene-specific mean, undermining a stable distribution-of-genes claim even if pooled BC looks bimodal.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator mechanistically implements the metabolic/regulatory role of each knocked-out gene in the panel; genes with no simulated phenotype will trivially show fold-change~1, treated as 'neutral' rather than flagged as a model-coverage gap.
Basal minimal medium is the relevant condition for defining 'dispensable'; a gene essential only in another condition (e.g. acetate) is out of scope here and flagged as a caveat, not pursued further.
4 generations is sufficient to reveal a lethal or strong-defect phenotype (division arrest or severe growth slowdown) for genes essential under basal conditions.
6 seeds sample intrinsic stochastic noise adequately to distinguish gene-level signal from seed-level noise for rival C's variance check.

Stratum assignment (known-essential / redundant-paralog / accessory-regulatory / stress-regulatory) was fixed from prior literature/COG annotation BEFORE any simulation was run and is not altered after seeing results — this is the pre-registration safeguard against objection r1.1.

The 16-gene, 4-stratum panel is a representative, not exhaustive, sample of the dispensability landscape; conclusions are stated as fractions over this sampled panel and its strata, not the whole genome.

objection_ledger.issue: The panel of 14 genes (acrB, ybeD, yciI, nagK, gatZ, proP, treF, ygfF, ydcH, aroH, pyrD, folK, rpoS, relA) is hand-picked by the proposer with no stated selection procedure (e.g. random sample from a defined 'non-essential-looking' gene list, or stratified by known COG category). A rival explanation of any observed heterogeneity is simply 'cherry-picked panel composition' — the proposer selected genes already known to span essential/non-essential, which would manufacture the predicted distribution shape regardless of any true population-level rule. The decisive test does not distinguish 'genuine heterogeneity in the dispensability construct' from 'heterogeneity engineered by panel selection.'

The rrna_operon_knockout design row (operons_removed:3) appears in candidate_designs but is never connected to h1/h0, the falsifier, or either rival — it's an orphan perturbation. If it's meant to test a related claim about rRNA operon redundancy, that claim needs its own h1/falsifier; if not needed, it should be removed, since it currently just adds an unexplained auxiliary manipulation.

The stratification is still only 4 genes per stratum (except accessory=5), and 'known-essential' stratum has only 2 genes (pyrD, folK). With n=2 for known-essential, a single noisy seed could flip the per-stratum pattern used to adjudicate Rival B (cherry-picking vs genuine heterogeneity). This is a statistical-power concern on an already-resolved design choice, not a new construct problem.

The decision rule combines a global BC threshold with a global FDR-significant-fraction threshold, but doesn't specify what happens if the two criteria disagree (e.g., BC>0.555 but <10% FDR-significant, or vice versa) in a way that would support H1 rather than requiring both to jointly reject H0 only. It's stated clearly enough for 'reject H1' (AND condition) but the symmetric 'support H1' criterion is left implicit in predicted_effect rather than formalized in decision_rule.

hypothesis.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
hypothesis.claim: Among a broad panel of non-essential-looking E. coli genes (regulators, paralogs, stress-response genes not tied to core replication/translation/cell-wall machinery), most single-gene knockouts (~70%) are viable (division_rate>0, measurable growth_rate) on basal minimal medium, while a minority (~30%) are conditionally or fully lethal (division_rate≈0 or growth_rate collapse), and lethality fraction rises on a nutrient-poor static carbon source (acetate) because of reduced metabolic buffering capacity.
hypothesis.h1: Across a panel of >=12 candidate non-essential genes, the fraction of single-knockouts classified as viable (division_rate >= 0.5 of wildtype AND growth_rate within 50% of wildtype) is >=0.6 on basal medium, and this viable fraction drops by >=15 percentage points when the same panel is tested on acetate.
hypothesis.h0: The viable fraction on basal medium is <0.6, OR the viable fraction does not differ (within noise, |Δ|<10 points, Welch t<2 on growth_rate/division_rate) between basal and acetate conditions — i.e. gene dispensability is condition-independent in this panel.

operational_defs.observable: division_rate and growth_rate channels averaged over seeds/generations
operational_defs.measure: classify VIABLE if division_rate>=0.5*wildtype_division_rate AND growth_rate within 50% of wildtype growth_rate; else LETHAL/CONDITIONAL

operational_defs.construct: dispensability fraction across a gene panel
operational_defs.observable: proportion of knockout designs classified VIABLE out of total panel
operational_defs.measure: count_viable / n_genes_tested, per condition

operational_defs.construct: metabolic buffering capacity under poor carbon source
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and fba_objective under acetate vs basal
operational_defs.measure: compare viable fraction and mean growth_rate shift between basal and acetate conditions

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Viable fraction ~0.6-0.7 on basal medium (binomial shape across the panel, not a point estimate); fraction drops by ~15-25 percentage points (e.g. 0.65 -> 0.45) on acetate; per-gene growth_rate fold-change for lethal hits is a crash to <0.3x wildtype.

falsifier.decision_rule: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction over per-gene log2 fold-change in division_rate (knockout vs wildtype) across the panel, separately computed for basal and acetate conditions; a gene is classified LETHAL if division_rate log2FC is significant at FDR<0.10 and negative beyond 50% reduction. Reject H1 if n_significant_fdr10/n_genes < 0.6 on basal (viable fraction too low), OR if the lethal-fraction difference (acetate minus basal) is <0.10 percentage points with Welch t<2 on growth_rate between the two conditions' lethal-subset means (no condition-dependence).
falsifier.refuting_result: If fewer than 60% of the panel is classified viable on basal (i.e. dispensability is rarer than predicted), or if the lethal fraction on acetate is statistically indistinguishable from basal (Welch t<2, |delta|<10 points), H1 is refuted.

test.statistic: log2FC of division_rate per gene (knockout vs wildtype), BH-FDR corrected across the panel
test.threshold: FDR<0.10 and |log2FC|>1 (i.e. >50% drop) counts as lethal; reject H1 if n_significant_fdr10/n_genes < 0.6 on basal, or if the acetate-vs-basal lethal-fraction shift is <0.10 with Welch t<2

rivals.claim: Gene dispensability is essentially condition-independent: genes dispensable on basal remain dispensable on acetate because core metabolic bottlenecks (not peripheral gene loss) dominate acetate growth defects.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Welch t<2 and |delta viable fraction|<10 points between basal and acetate lethal-subset growth_rate means -- i.e. no significant shift in the panel's lethality profile across conditions.

rivals.claim: Lethality in this panel is driven mainly by division/cell-cycle machinery defects rather than metabolic buffering loss, so division_rate collapses independent of growth_rate or carbon source.
rivals.distinguishing_result: division_rate drops to ~0 for a subset of genes while growth_rate remains near-wildtype in both basal and acetate conditions, decoupling the two channels rather than both collapsing together under acetate stress.

rivals.claim: Any apparent acetate-specific lethality rise is actually a stringent-response (ppGpp-mediated) phenomenon triggered generically by nutrient restriction, not by loss of the specific knocked-out gene's buffering function -- i.e. the effect is a background physiological response common to all acetate-grown cells, confounded with the knockout.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA single-gene knockout background (abolishing stringent-response ppGpp induction) run on acetate shows the SAME lethality-fraction rise as the wildtype-background panel, indicating the acetate effect is independent of ppGpp induction and thus not confounded by it; if instead the relA-knockout background panel shows a BLUNTED or ABOLISHED lethality rise on acetate, this rival is supported and the acetate effect is attributable to stringent-response induction rather than per-gene buffering loss.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator mechanistically implements the metabolic/regulatory role of each panel gene (not all E. coli genes are modeled with equal fidelity); genes without a modeled mechanism will show no effect and must be excluded post hoc.

division_rate and growth_rate are read as per-generation averages across the simulated window (3 generations), which is assumed sufficient to detect a viability collapse (crashes manifest by gen 3-4 per prior calibration).
Acetate is used as the single static non-preferred carbon source representative of 'nutrient-poor' media; results are not assumed to generalize to fumarate/malate/succinate without separate testing.

Gene panel composition (12 genes spanning stress response, carbon overflow metabolism, nucleoid-associated regulators) is treated as representative of the broader 'non-essential-looking gene' population; true genome-wide essentiality fraction is not estimated from this subsample alone.

All 12 panel gene names (ackA, pta, poxB, sspA, cspD, yjgF, dps, rmf, hns, fis, nac, arcA) and the relA control are assumed to be valid single-gene_knockout targets in the simulator's gene list; any unresolvable name is substituted with the nearest validated ortholog before running.
The relA knockout is treated as a sufficient proxy for abolishing stringent-response induction; residual SpoT-mediated ppGpp synthesis is not separately controlled for and is noted as a scope caveat.

params.note: interventional control: relA knockout abolishes ppGpp stringent-response induction, isolating whether the acetate-specific lethality rise depends on stringent-response activation rather than per-gene metabolic buffering loss

all_rounds.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
all_rounds.claim: Across a broad panel of single-gene knockouts, most non-essential-annotated genes can be individually deleted without abolishing growth or division, but a substantial minority (~15-25%) of the panel will show severe growth/division defects (conditionally essential under basal media), while a small residual fraction (~5-10%) will be fully lethal (division_rate -> 0) under basal conditions — i.e., 'genes E. coli can live without' is a graded distribution, not a binary set, and its shape is bimodal (a large cluster near wildtype growth_rate and a smaller cluster near zero).
all_rounds.h1: When single genes are knocked out one at a time across a panel of candidate genes (drawn to include known-essential, known-conditionally-essential, and known-dispensable loci in basal media), the distribution of resulting growth_rate (and division_rate) across the panel is bimodal: a majority cluster retains >=70% of wildtype growth_rate (viable without the gene) and a minority cluster (~15-30% of panel) falls below 20% of wildtype growth_rate or division_rate (effectively cannot live without it), rather than all knockouts clustering near wildtype (fully dispensable) or all clustering near zero (universally essential).
all_rounds.h0: Single-gene knockouts across the panel do not produce a bimodal split in growth_rate/division_rate relative to wildtype/basal; instead the panel's growth_rate values form a unimodal distribution (Sarle's bimodality coefficient <= 0.555), consistent with either near-uniform dispensability or near-uniform essentiality rather than a distinguishable essential/non-essential split.

operational_defs.construct: viability / can live without the gene
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate channels at end of simulated generations, KO vs wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: per-seed growth_rate (1/h) and division_rate (frac) averaged over last generation; normalized as % of wildtype/basal mean

operational_defs.observable: normalized growth_rate / division_rate
operational_defs.measure: KO classified 'cannot live without' if mean normalized growth_rate <20% AND division_rate <20% of wildtype; 'can live without' if >=70% of wildtype on both

operational_defs.construct: distribution shape across the gene panel
operational_defs.observable: pooled per-seed, per-gene normalized growth_rate values
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over the pooled panel distribution

all_rounds.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution with BC > 0.555 over the panel; ~70-85% of knocked-out genes retain >=70% wildtype growth_rate (dispensable cluster, growth_rate ~0.9-1.1x wildtype), while ~15-30% fall below 20% wildtype growth_rate/division_rate (essential-under-basal cluster, growth_rate reduced >5-fold, division_rate -> <0.2). Mean effect size for the essential cluster vs wildtype: Welch |t| >= 2, effect_pct <= -50%.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed normalized growth_rate values across the full KO panel; reject unimodal-null if BC>0.555. Step 2 (confirmatory): Welch t-test of growth_rate, each KO vs wildtype/basal across seeds; a gene is classified 'essential-under-basal' only if |t|>=2 AND effect_pct<=-50%.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555 (panel growth rates are unimodal, i.e., either nearly all KOs look like wildtype or nearly all look lethal, with no distinguishable bimodal split), OR the fraction of genes meeting the essential-under-basal criterion falls outside ~5-40% (i.e., near 0% or near 100%), refuting the claim of a substantial intermediate conditionally-essential minority.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled normalized growth_rate across all KO genes/seeds
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 required to confirm bimodal (reject unimodal null)

rivals.claim: Rival A (graded continuum): essentiality is not bimodal but forms a continuous gradient of fitness costs (many genes give intermediate ~40-60% growth reduction), so the panel distribution is unimodal/broad rather than two clusters.
rivals.distinguishing_result: BC<=0.555 with a wide unimodal spread of growth_rate values (many genes at 40-60% of wildtype) rather than two separated peaks near 100% and near 0%.

rivals.claim: Rival B (media-dependence dominates): apparent 'essentiality' is mostly an artifact of basal media choice -- many genes scored essential in basal would be dispensable in a richer/alternative condition (e.g. acetate or amino-acid-supplemented media), so the KO's lethality is condition-specific rather than a fixed gene property.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Running the same KO panel under an alternative condition (acetate) rescues a large fraction of the 'essential-under-basal' cluster back to >=70% wildtype growth_rate, shifting the bimodal split or shrinking the essential cluster substantially.

auxiliary_assumptions: The KO panel is drawn broadly enough (>=20-30 genes spanning expected-essential, expected-conditionally-essential, and expected-dispensable annotations) to sample the real distribution rather than an arbitrary few genes.

The simulator mechanistically implements the deletion's metabolic/regulatory consequence for each gene in the panel (not all KOs may be mechanistically modeled; genes without modeled effect will trivially show wildtype growth_rate and are treated as 'dispensable' by the operational definition, which is a known scope limitation).

Growth_rate and division_rate averaged over the final generation are adequate proxies for long-run viability within the 1-4 generation simulation window; slower-onset lethality beyond that window is out of scope.
Seed-to-seed stochastic noise under wildtype/basal is small relative to the essential-vs-dispensable effect size, so the 20%/70% thresholds are not swamped by intrinsic noise.
residual_ambiguities: reached round cap without full convergence

objection_ledger.issue: The operational classification uses two thresholds (>=70% wildtype = 'dispensable', <20% = 'essential-under-basal') but genes landing in the 20-70% band (which the bimodality framing itself predicts should be rare/empty) are never assigned a label or counted in the falsifier's fraction checks. If a substantial fraction of the panel falls in that gap, the hypothesis as operationalized has no verdict for them, letting the bimodal claim survive by simply not classifying the counterexamples.

The gene panel in candidate_designs (30 named genes) is hand-picked by the proposer's own prior expectations of which genes are essential/conditional/dispensable (dnaA, ftsZ, rpoB etc. vs lacZ, trpA etc.). Since the claim is explicitly about the shape of the distribution across 'a broad panel', a panel curated to already contain a known essential cluster and a known dispensable cluster will mechanically produce bimodality regardless of whether the true underlying gene-essentiality distribution (e.g. a random or genome-wide sample) is bimodal. This is an unexcluded rival explanation (panel-selection artifact) for the predicted BC>0.555 result.

Whether the simulator's per-gene knockout mechanism (e.g. for biosynthetic genes like trpA, hisG) actually produces graded/continuous fitness costs under the instrument's metabolic model, versus just hard on/off essentiality flags, is not verified; this bears on whether intermediate-band genes can even be observed.

The auxiliary_assumptions and operational_defs now require an 'annotation-blind, every Nth locus tag' panel, but the actual candidate_designs target_genes list is still the identical 30 hand-picked, annotation-informed genes from the prior round. As submitted, the executable test does not implement the randomized-sampling control it claims distinguishes H1 from Rival B (panel-selection artifact), so the decisive test still can't exclude that rival.

Whether 'every Nth locus tag' sampling is actually annotation-blind depends on whether locus-tag/genome-position order itself correlates with functional category (e.g., operon clustering of essential genes), which the instrument can't verify independently of the essentiality labels being tested.

hypothesis.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
hypothesis.claim: Across a broad panel of single-gene knockouts, most non-essential-annotated genes can be individually deleted without abolishing growth or division, but a substantial minority (~15-25%) of the panel will show severe growth/division defects (conditionally essential under basal media), while a small residual fraction (~5-10%) will be fully lethal (division_rate -> 0) under basal conditions — i.e., 'genes E. coli can live without' is a graded distribution, not a binary set, and its shape is bimodal (a large cluster near wildtype growth_rate and a smaller cluster near zero).
hypothesis.h1: When single genes are knocked out one at a time across a panel of candidate genes (drawn to include known-essential, known-conditionally-essential, and known-dispensable loci in basal media), the distribution of resulting growth_rate (and division_rate) across the panel is bimodal: a majority cluster retains >=70% of wildtype growth_rate (viable without the gene) and a minority cluster (~15-30% of panel) falls below 20% of wildtype growth_rate or division_rate (effectively cannot live without it), rather than all knockouts clustering near wildtype (fully dispensable) or all clustering near zero (universally essential).
hypothesis.h0: Single-gene knockouts across the panel do not produce a bimodal split in growth_rate/division_rate relative to wildtype/basal; instead the panel's growth_rate values form a unimodal distribution (Sarle's bimodality coefficient <= 0.555), consistent with either near-uniform dispensability or near-uniform essentiality rather than a distinguishable essential/non-essential split.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed growth_rate (1/h) and division_rate (frac) averaged over last generation; normalized as % of wildtype/basal mean

operational_defs.observable: normalized growth_rate / division_rate
operational_defs.measure: KO classified 'cannot live without' if mean normalized growth_rate <20% AND division_rate <20% of wildtype; 'can live without' if >=70% of wildtype on both

operational_defs.construct: distribution shape across the gene panel
operational_defs.observable: pooled per-seed, per-gene normalized growth_rate values
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over the pooled panel distribution

Mean effect size for the essential cluster vs wildtype: Welch |t| >= 2, effect_pct <= -50%.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed normalized growth_rate values across the full KO panel; reject unimodal-null if BC>0.555. Step 2 (confirmatory): Welch t-test of growth_rate, each KO vs wildtype/basal across seeds; a gene is classified 'essential-under-basal' only if |t|>=2 AND effect_pct<=-50%.

test.threshold: BC > 0.555 required to confirm bimodal (reject unimodal null)

hypothesis.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
hypothesis.claim: Among a broad panel of individually non-essential genes (as annotated in the Keio/EcoCyc dispensability consensus), a substantial minority (~20-30%) nonetheless show a measurable fitness cost in this whole-cell model: when knocked out singly, this fraction will show reduced growth_rate and/or division_rate relative to wildtype, even though none of them are lethal (division_rate stays >0). The remaining majority will be statistically indistinguishable from wildtype on these channels, consistent with true dispensability.
hypothesis.h1: Across a panel of >=8 single-gene knockouts drawn from genes classified non-essential in vivo, the DISTRIBUTION of growth_rate effect sizes (vs wildtype/basal) is heterogeneous: a nonzero fraction (predicted ~20-30%, i.e. 2-3 of 8-10 genes tested) shows a significant growth_rate reduction (Welch |t|>=2, effect_pct <= -10%) while remaining viable (division_rate > 0 in all generations), and the rest show no significant effect.
hypothesis.h0: All tested non-essential single-gene knockouts are statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal on growth_rate and division_rate (i.e., the simulated 'non-essential' panel behaves as a uniform null with no detectable fitness cost in any member), OR all show lethality (division_rate collapses to 0), either of which would mean the panel does not show the predicted heterogeneous partial-cost distribution.

operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: fraction of simulated generations that complete division; a gene is 'live-without-able' if division_rate > 0 across all generations and seeds

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test effect_pct of mean instantaneous growth_rate, knockout vs wildtype/basal, across seeds

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate across gene panel
operational_defs.measure: fraction of panel genes (out of >=8) with significant growth_rate reduction (|t|>=2, effect_pct<=-10%) while division_rate remains >0

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Heterogeneous distribution across a panel of 8-10 non-essential single-gene KOs: ~20-30% (2-3 genes) show growth_rate reduction of -10% to -30% (Welch |t|>=2) with division_rate still >0 (no lethality); ~70-80% show |effect_pct|<10% and are statistically indistinguishable from wildtype on both channels.

falsifier.decision_rule: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (q<0.10) over the per-gene Welch t-test p-values for growth_rate (KO vs wildtype) across the 8-10 gene panel; H1 requires n_significant_fdr10 to be a nonzero minority (roughly 2-4 of the panel), not zero and not the full panel
falsifier.refuting_result: n_significant_fdr10 = 0 (panel behaves as uniform null, supporting pure dispensability with no cost) OR n_significant_fdr10 = all genes tested (panel shows uniform cost, contradicting true dispensability) OR any gene shows division_rate=0 (unexpected lethality contradicting the non-essential annotation)

test.statistic: per-gene Welch t p-value on growth_rate, BH-FDR corrected across panel
test.threshold: q<0.10; expect 2-4 of 8-10 genes significant

rivals.claim: Rival A: The model's metabolic/regulatory network is too coarse-grained to register subtle fitness costs of non-essential gene loss; ALL non-essential KOs will look statistically identical to wildtype (pure neutrality), regardless of true in vivo fitness costs.
rivals.distinguishing_result: n_significant_fdr10 = 0 across the entire panel on growth_rate; BH-FDR finds no gene surviving correction, supporting Rival A over H1.

rivals.claim: Rival B: Single-gene KO effects in this model are dominated by a few genes with large structural/stoichiometric roles (e.g. ribosomal or core biosynthesis adjacent genes), producing a BIMODAL split between 'fully compensated, no cost' and 'severe-but-nonlethal' rather than a smooth minority-fraction pattern; the magnitude of cost in the affected subset would be much larger (>50% growth reduction) than the predicted -10 to -30% range.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Sarle's bimodality coefficient on the pooled per-gene effect_pct distribution exceeds 0.555, AND the significant-gene subset shows mean effect_pct < -50%, indicating a bimodal severe/neutral split rather than the predicted moderate minority-cost pattern.

auxiliary_assumptions: The Keio/EcoCyc 'non-essential' annotation used to select the gene panel is an external ground truth not itself tested here; we assume these genes are not core-essential in the model's reaction network a priori (checked downstream).
Growth_rate and division_rate are measured under identical basal media conditions across all KOs and wildtype; no mid-run media shifts confound comparisons.
Seeds capture intrinsic stochastic noise only; any systematic fitness cost is assumed to be a property of the gene deletion, not of seed-specific initial conditions.

The rrna_operon_knockout control is included as a positive/interventional control with an EXPECTED large, significant growth_rate and ribosome-capacity cost, to confirm the panel and pipeline can detect real effects (sensitivity check) distinct from the non-essential panel's predicted partial-cost pattern.

Whole-cell model coarse-graining may underestimate costs from genes acting via mechanisms not explicitly modeled (e.g. stress survival, biofilm); this is a known scope limitation, not resolved by this test.

all_rounds.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
all_rounds.claim: A substantial minority (~5-15%) of individually knocked-out genes in a curated panel of metabolic/regulatory genes are dispensable for growth on basal minimal medium: their single-gene KOs show no significant reduction in growth_rate or division_rate relative to wildtype, whereas the remainder show clear fitness defects or lethality. Among genes classified dispensable, this neutrality is NOT explained by stringent-response compensation: a relA knockout background (which abolishes (p)ppGpp synthesis by RelA) will NOT convert dispensable-classified genes into fitness-costly ones.
all_rounds.h1: Across a broad panel of single-gene knockouts, the fraction of genes whose KO strain is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype on growth_rate and division_rate (|welch_t|<2 on both channels) is between 5% and 15%, i.e. the dispensability distribution is bimodal (robust-null cluster vs. fitness-cost cluster) rather than uniform. Furthermore, this dispensability is a genuine property of the knocked-out gene's function, not a stringent-response artifact: re-testing the dispensable-classified subset on a relA gene_knockout background (removing ppGpp-mediated compensation) still yields |welch_t|<2 vs the relA-knockout reference for growth_rate and division_rate.
all_rounds.h0: Either (a) single-gene KOs in the panel are uniformly costly (fewer than 5% show no significant growth/division defect), or (b) uniformly neutral (more than 15% show no defect) with no clear bimodal split, or (c) the dispensable-classified genes' apparent neutrality is a RelA/ppGpp-compensation artifact: removing RelA-dependent stringent response (relA gene_knockout background) reveals significant fitness defects (|welch_t|>=2) in genes previously classified dispensable, indicating the stringent response was masking a true cost.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate of the KO strain relative to wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-statistic of growth_rate (and separately division_rate) for KO vs wildtype across seeds; |t|>=2 on either channel classifies the gene as having a fitness cost, else classified dispensable

operational_defs.observable: proportion of knocked-out genes classified dispensable out of all genes screened
operational_defs.measure: count of dispensable classifications / total genes screened, with 95% CI via normal approximation

operational_defs.observable: distribution of per-gene effect sizes (growth_rate %-change from wildtype) pooled across the screened panel
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over the pooled per-seed growth_rate effect_pct values across all screened genes

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate of a double-perturbation strain (dispensable-gene KO + relA knockout) relative to a relA-knockout-only reference
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-statistic of growth_rate and division_rate for (gene-KO on relA-KO background) vs (relA-KO alone, basal); |t|<2 on both channels across the dispensable-subset genes supports true (RelA-independent) dispensability; |t|>=2 for a majority of the subset supports the compensation rival

all_rounds.predicted_effect: Dispensable fraction = 5-15% of screened genes (point estimate ~10%, 95% CI via normal approximation on n=20); pooled growth_rate effect_pct distribution across the panel is bimodal with BC>0.555, one cluster near 0% effect (dispensable) and a second cluster at >=30% growth reduction or lethal (division_rate -> 0). Critically, when the dispensable-subset genes (expected ~2-3 of 20) are re-knocked-out on a relA gene_knockout background, growth_rate and division_rate remain within |welch_t|<2 of the relA-knockout-only reference (predicted effect_pct <10%), i.e. removing stringent-response compensation does NOT unmask a fitness cost greater than ~10%.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (screen): for each of 20 genes run gene_knockout/basal (6 seeds, 3 generations) vs wildtype/basal (6 seeds, 3 generations); classify each gene dispensable if |welch_t|<2 on BOTH growth_rate and division_rate. Step 2 (shape): compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient over the pooled per-seed growth_rate effect_pct values across all 20 genes; reject unimodal if BC>0.555. Step 3 (fraction): reject H1 if dispensable fraction falls outside [5%,15%] OR if BC<=0.555. Step 4 (causal control): for each dispensable-classified gene, run multi_gene_knockout/basal combining {that gene, relA} (6 seeds, 3 generations) vs reference relA_only gene_knockout/basal (6 seeds, 3 generations, relA alone); reject the stringent-response-compensation rival only if |welch_t|<2 on growth_rate AND division_rate for ALL (or a clear majority, >=2/3) of the dispensable-subset genes tested this way; if >=1/3 show |welch_t|>=2, the compensation rival is supported instead.
falsifier.refuting_result: Either the dispensable fraction is <5% or >15%, or BC<=0.555 (no bimodal structure), or a majority of dispensable-subset genes show |welch_t|>=2 on growth_rate or division_rate when re-tested on the relA-knockout background relative to relA-knockout-alone reference (indicating stringent-response compensation was masking a true cost, supporting Rival B instead of true dispensability).

test.statistic: Welch t-statistic, per-gene and per-channel, for KO vs wildtype (screen) and for (gene-KO+relA-KO) vs relA-KO-alone (causal control); Sarle's BC for the pooled distribution shape
test.threshold: |welch_t|>=2 classifies a fitness cost; BC>0.555 for bimodality; dispensable fraction in [5%,15%]; causal control requires |welch_t|<2 on both channels for >=2/3 of tested dispensable-subset genes to support true dispensability

rivals.claim: Rival A (ribosome-capacity confound): apparent 'dispensable' genes are not truly neutral but merely have fitness costs too small to detect given current ribosome allocation slack; clamping ribosome capacity down (rrna_operon_knockout background) would reveal that these 'dispensable' genes actually matter once resource buffering is removed.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, genes classified dispensable under wildtype background show significant growth_rate or division_rate defects (|welch_t|>=2) when the SAME knockout is run on an rrna_operon_knockout background, because reduced ribosome slack exposes the latent cost.

rivals.claim: Rival B (stringent-response masking, now tested interventionally): genes appear dispensable because ppGpp induction via RelA compensates for the metabolic loss by reallocating resources, not because the gene itself is truly unneeded; removing RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis (relA knockout background) should unmask the true cost.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival B is true, combining a dispensable-classified gene's knockout with a relA knockout produces significant growth_rate/division_rate defects (|welch_t|>=2) relative to relA-knockout-alone, because the compensatory stringent response that was masking the cost is now absent.

params.note: pairs drawn from whichever subset of the 20-gene panel empirically classifies as dispensable in Step 1; placeholder names shown, actual genes substituted post-screen

objection_ledger.issue: Rival B's distinguishing test relies on comparing effect_pct/growth_rate (dispensability) against ppgpp_conc fold-change within the SAME wildtype background across the same knockouts — this is again a correlational/observational comparison across genes, not an interventional manipulation of ppGpp responsiveness. Since ppgpp_conc and growth outcomes are mechanistically coupled via the stringent response, elevated ppgpp_conc in 'dispensable' genes could simply reflect normal stress signaling rather than establishing that ppGpp induction is CAUSALLY compensating for loss of the gene. The decisive design should instead rerun a subset of dispensable-classified KOs on a background with suppressed/clamped ppGpp response (e.g. via the ppgpp_conc perturbation held low, or a relA-limited background) and check whether the previously 'dispensable' genes now show fitness defects.

The claim and falsifier assume that 3 generations and 6 seeds give adequate statistical power to detect a true fitness cost as small as the implicit threshold distinguishing 'cluster 2' (>=30% growth reduction) from noise, but no power analysis or expected effect-size-vs-noise floor is given to justify that |welch_t|<2 at this sample size won't simply be underpowered for intermediate-cost genes, artificially inflating the 'dispensable' cluster. This could confound the headline fraction with a sheer power issue rather than a genuine bimodal biological split.

Sarle's bimodality coefficient is sensitive to sample size and skew, and this is being computed over only 20 genes' pooled per-seed effect values (effectively ~120 points but only 20 independent gene-level clusters) — it's unclear whether the simulator and this panel size can actually deliver a reliable BC estimate near the 0.555 threshold, as opposed to an artifact of small-panel sampling.
