hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: When glucose (preferred sugar) is exhausted and only a secondary carbon source (e.g. acetate) is available, isogenic E. coli cells do NOT switch synchronously: instead there is population heterogeneity in the stringent-response/diauxie-transition timing, visible as a bimodal (or at least high-CV) distribution of ppGpp induction and growth-rate recovery across single-cell replicates, with a substantial minority (~20-40%) of cells lagging far behind the majority. This heterogeneity is at least partly ppGpp/RelA-mechanism-dependent: in a relA knockout, the heterogeneity should measurably shrink (not merely persist unchanged).
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate cells simulated under a glucose-to-acetate media shift, the distribution of post-shift ppGpp induction (and growth-rate recovery) timing/magnitude is heterogeneous/bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) rather than a tight unimodal response, with a lagging subpopulation fraction >= 0.2. Furthermore, this heterogeneity is partly driven by the RelA/ppGpp stringent-response trigger: deleting relA will measurably reduce growth-rate-recovery bimodality (BC drop of >= 0.1 and/or lagging fraction drop of >= 0.1 relative to the wildtype-shift arm).
hypothesis.h0: All replicate cells respond essentially simultaneously and uniformly: the per-seed distribution of ppGpp_conc (and growth_rate) at a fixed post-shift timepoint is unimodal and low-variance (BC <= 0.555), consistent with synchronous switching (reference: wildtype/basal with no shift, or the pre-shift steady state). Secondary null: if heterogeneity exists, it is ppGpp-mechanism-independent -- the relA knockout shift arm shows BC and lagging fraction statistically indistinguishable from (or higher than) the wildtype shift arm.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate sampled per-seed at fixed timepoints after the media shift event
operational_defs.measure: pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc (and growth_rate) values at a fixed post-shift timepoint; Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled distribution; lagging-cell fraction = fraction of seeds below a threshold fold-change in growth_rate recovery

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc rise and ribosome_conc/growth_rate drop-then-recovery trajectory following glucose exhaustion
operational_defs.measure: effect_pct and welch_t of ppgpp_conc, target (post-shift) vs reference (pre-shift/basal), across seeds

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate under acetate as sole carbon source
operational_defs.measure: steady-state growth_rate under acetate condition vs basal

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc, which should collapse toward near-zero/flat in the relA KO) pooled per-seed at t=60min in the relA-knockout shift arm vs the wildtype shift arm
operational_defs.measure: BC and lagging fraction computed identically in both arms; delta_BC = BC(wildtype shift) - BC(relA KO shift); delta_lag = lagfrac(wildtype shift) - lagfrac(relA KO shift)

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Primary: pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc at t=60min post-shift has BC > 0.555, with an estimated lagging fraction ~0.25-0.35 of seeds showing <50% of the median ppGpp fold-induction (vs a tight CV<0.15 null). Secondary (mechanism): in the relA-knockout shift arm, growth_rate BC drops by >=0.1 absolute (e.g. from ~0.65 to <=0.55) and lagging fraction drops by >=0.1 absolute (e.g. from ~0.3 to <=0.2) relative to the wildtype shift arm, consistent with partial (not necessarily complete) ppGpp-dependence of the heterogeneity.

falsifier.decision_rule: PRIMARY: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values sampled at t=60min post-shift across all seeds of the wildtype timeline design; reject H1 (support H0, synchrony) if BC <= 0.555. Also require lagging fraction >= 0.2 (seeds with ppGpp fold-induction < 0.5x median) to support the 'substantial subpopulation' magnitude claim. SECONDARY (mechanism, resolves Rival C / objection r1.2): compute the same BC and lagging-fraction statistics on growth_rate at t=60min in the relA-knockout timeline arm; compute delta_BC = BC(wildtype shift) - BC(relA KO shift) and delta_lag = lagfrac(wildtype shift) - lagfrac(relA KO shift). Support ppGpp-dependence if delta_BC >= 0.1 AND delta_lag >= 0.1 (heterogeneity shrinks substantially in the KO). If delta_BC < 0.1 and delta_lag < 0.1 (heterogeneity persists at similar magnitude or increases in the KO), reject the mechanistic ppGpp-dependence sub-claim even if the primary distributional claim holds.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC <= 0.555 (unimodal, tight distribution) AND/OR lagging fraction < 0.1 on the primary wildtype-shift ppgpp_conc test, indicating near-simultaneous switching across all seeds; OR (for the mechanism sub-claim) delta_BC < 0.1 and delta_lag < 0.1 between relA-KO and wildtype shift arms, indicating heterogeneity is ppGpp-independent.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc (primary) and growth_rate (secondary, both arms) at fixed post-shift timepoint, plus lagging-fraction threshold counts
test.threshold: Primary: BC > 0.555 and lagfrac >= 0.2 to support H1. Secondary: delta_BC >= 0.1 and delta_lag >= 0.1 to support ppGpp-mechanism-dependence; otherwise reject that sub-claim.

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic fast-switch): the diauxie transition is a deterministic, fast metabolic response governed by regulatory network dynamics (e.g. cAMP-CRP, ppGpp) with negligible stochastic cell-to-cell variation; apparent heterogeneity in prior literature is measurement noise, not biology.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate at t=60min post-shift will show BC <= 0.555 and CV < 0.15, i.e. all seeds converge tightly regardless of stochastic seed.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp-independent bet-hedging via persister-like state, not stringent response magnitude): heterogeneity in switching timing exists but is NOT reflected in ppGpp levels per se -- it is driven by a different axis (e.g. pre-existing ribosome_conc or rela_conc variation) that only indirectly shows up in growth_rate recovery, so ppgpp_conc itself may look unimodal while growth_rate is bimodal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, ppgpp_conc channel would show BC <= 0.555 (unimodal) while growth_rate channel independently shows BC > 0.555 (bimodal) -- a channel dissociation the current ppgpp_conc-only primary test would miss on its own, but the secondary relA-KO growth_rate arm partially covers this by tracking growth_rate bimodality directly.

rivals.claim: Rival C (relA/ppGpp machinery is the sole driver of any heterogeneity): if relA is knocked out, abolishing stringent-response ppGpp synthesis, any observed heterogeneity in switch timing should collapse because the stochastic trigger (RelA activation threshold) is removed, leaving a more uniform (growth-rate-only, metabolism-driven) transition.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Now explicitly tested with a pre-specified threshold: if delta_BC >= 0.1 and delta_lag >= 0.1 between wildtype and relA-KO shift arms, heterogeneity substantially collapses in the KO, supporting partial/strong ppGpp-dependence. If delta_BC < 0.1 and delta_lag < 0.1, heterogeneity persists despite abolished ppGpp, refuting ppGpp-mechanism-dependence of H1 even if the raw distributional (bimodal) claim still holds.

objection_ledger.issue: The core claim depends on per-seed stochastic heterogeneity within a timeline-driven simulator replicate run (e.g. 8 seeds), but whether the simulator's 'seeds' actually encode cell-to-cell intrinsic noise (bet-hedging, stochastic RelA activation thresholds) versus just numerical/initialization noise around a deterministic trajectory is unverified. If the envelope's seed variation is just solver/IC jitter rather than a model of biological stochasticity, a BC>0.555 finding would reflect simulator artifact, not population heterogeneity in switching.

Rival C is addressed by including a relA knockout timeline design, which is good practice -- but the decision_rule/falsifier only specifies comparing BC on the primary ppgpp_conc/growth_rate pooled distribution for the main H1 vs H0 test; it does not specify a quantitative decision rule for interpreting the relA-knockout comparison (e.g. what BC or lag-fraction in the relA KO would count as 'heterogeneity persists' vs 'collapses'). Without a pre-specified threshold for the relA-KO arm, Rival C's resolution is left as a qualitative/narrative judgment rather than a falsifiable test.

hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: When the preferred carbon source (glucose) is exhausted and cells face a diauxic-like media shift to an alternative carbon source, individual cells do NOT switch metabolic state synchronously — instead the population shows a transient bimodal split between 'still-glucose-physiology' and 'switched' cells, reflected as bimodal per-cell growth_rate and ppgpp_conc shortly after the shift, rather than all cells moving together as a single sharp step.
hypothesis.h1: Across a glucose-to-alternative-carbon media-shift timeline, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) immediately post-shift is bimodal (Sarle's bimodality coefficient BC>0.555), indicating asynchronous, cell-to-cell heterogeneous switching timing rather than a synchronous population-wide transition.
hypothesis.h0: The post-shift distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) across seeds/cells is unimodal (BC<=0.555), consistent with all cells switching together at approximately the same time (a synchronous, deterministic transition with only replicate noise).

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc

rivals.claim: Cells DO switch synchronously but with a smooth graded (not bimodal) deceleration-then-acceleration in growth_rate as internal metabolite pools re-equilibrate — i.e. heterogeneity is just replicate/intrinsic noise around one trajectory, not two subpopulations.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Post-shift growth_rate distribution remains unimodal (BC<=0.555) with a single mean that moves smoothly over generations, matching the pre-shift/wildtype unimodal shape merely shifted in location.

rivals.claim: Apparent bimodality is driven by stochastic ppGpp/RelA pathway noise (an artifact of the stringent-response module's bursty kinetics) rather than true divergent carbon-switching commitment, so clamping ppGpp would abolish the bimodality even though cells still differ in when they physically start consuming the new carbon source.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the ppgpp_conc clamp control design, post-shift growth_rate bimodality disappears (BC<=0.555) even though the media shift still occurs, showing the bimodal signature was downstream of ppGpp noise rather than an independent switching-commitment process.

hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: When the preferred carbon source (glucose) is exhausted and only a secondary substrate (acetate) is available, isogenic cells do NOT switch to the secondary-sugar utilization program in unison: the population shows a bimodal, asynchronous diauxic-lag distribution across single-cell replicates, with a substantial minority (~20-40%) remaining in a low-growth/non-switched state for an extended period while the rest resume growth.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds simulating the glucose-to-acetate diauxic shift, the distribution of post-shift growth_rate trajectories (or ppgpp_conc as the stringent-response proxy for 'still starved, not yet switched') is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) rather than unimodal/synchronous, reflecting cell-to-cell heterogeneity in switching time.
hypothesis.h0: All replicate seeds switch to the secondary substrate synchronously: post-shift growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) recovery trajectories across seeds are unimodal and tightly clustered (BC <= 0.555), consistent with a deterministic, population-uniform response governed only by condition/media and not by stochastic cell state.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp/stringent-response-driven, not metabolic-enzyme-driven heterogeneity): Any observed bimodality in growth_rate arises purely from stochastic RelA/ppGpp pulsing noise, not from heterogeneity in metabolic switching per se; if RelA is knocked out (removing ppGpp stringent control), the growth_rate bimodality should disappear even though cells must still induce acetate enzymes, showing the heterogeneity was a ppGpp-signaling artifact rather than a genuine bistable metabolic switch.

hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: When the preferred carbon source (glucose) is exhausted and only a secondary substrate remains available in the medium, individual cells in an isogenic population do NOT switch their physiology (growth rate, ppGpp alarmone level) in unison; instead the population shows a graded, asynchronous distribution of switching times/states across seeds, with a substantial minority (~20-40%) still showing 'glucose-like' low ppGpp / high growth-rate kinetics well after the mean population has shifted, producing a bimodal distribution of per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories at the shift timepoint rather than a synchronous step change.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds sampled at a fixed time shortly after preferred-sugar exhaustion, the distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) values is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555), reflecting asynchronous diauxic switching rather than a single synchronous transition.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc values sampled at the same fixed post-shift timepoint are unimodally distributed (BC <= 0.555) and cluster tightly around a single new steady-state mean, consistent with synchronous population-wide switching.

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic fast switch): all cells detect sugar exhaustion via a shared, fast-acting regulatory circuit (e.g. cAMP-CRP) and switch essentially simultaneously; apparent spread in growth_rate is just measurement/intrinsic noise around a single new steady state.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, pooled per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc at the post-shift timepoint will be unimodal (BC <= 0.555) with low coefficient of variation (<15%) around a single mean in both the target and a relA-knockout control, since switching is CRP-driven and ppGpp-independent for its timing.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp-driven bistable switch, confounded by stringent response machinery): bimodality in growth_rate, if seen, is actually an artifact of variable RelA/SpoT stringent-response activation rather than a genuine metabolic-switch bimodality — i.e., the bimodality is a ppGpp-pathway-specific phenomenon, not a general diauxic-switch phenomenon, and would disappear if ppGpp signaling is removed.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, a relA gene_knockout background (which abolishes (p)ppGpp synthesis induction) run through the same glucose-to-secondary-substrate timeline should COLLAPSE the growth_rate bimodality (BC drops to <=0.555) even though cells still physically run out of glucose, showing the bimodal switching pattern in growth_rate depended on the ppGpp machinery rather than being an intrinsic feature of metabolic switching itself.

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline perturbation 'glucose_to_acetate_shift' is implemented as a media-shift event (minimal -> minimal_plus_acetate-like) within the allowed timeline schema and is not treated internally as a forbidden mid-run carbon-source switch for FBA purposes; if the simulator cannot represent gradual nutrient depletion within a generation, we approximate glucose exhaustion by a scheduled timeline event at a fixed simulated time.

Per-seed sampling at a single fixed post-shift timepoint is a valid snapshot of switching heterogeneity, i.e., we are not required to resolve full single-cell switching trajectories, only the cross-seed distribution at one time.
Seeds are treated as if they were independent single cells of an isogenic population (not literally multi-cell agents), so cross-seed variance is our operational proxy for population heterogeneity.
ppgpp_conc and growth_rate are read under steady-state charging (no kinetic ppGpp module needed) since we only need the standard steady-state channels, not the kinetic RelA/SpoT module.

4-8 seeds and 1-4 generations give enough replicate power for a first-pass bimodality read; a definitive population-fraction estimate would need a larger seed screen, deferred to a follow-up if this first test is not dispositive.

objection_ledger.issue: The hypothesis requires per-cell (single-cell) heterogeneity within an isogenic population at a single timepoint, but the proposed measurement pools growth_rate across 8 'seeds' (replicate simulation runs), which are independent population-level trajectories, not single-cell measurements within one population. Bimodality across 8 seed-level population-average growth rates does not establish that individual cells within a given population are heterogeneous - it could just reflect seed-to-seed variability in population-average switch timing. The instrument/design conflates between-seed variance with within-population single-cell heterogeneity.

With only 8 seeds, achieving a statistically reliable Sarle's BC estimate (and distinguishing BC>0.555 from noise) is difficult - the decision rule treats a point estimate from n=8 as decisive without specifying a confidence interval, bootstrap, or minimum seed count needed to trust the BC threshold. This is an unstated auxiliary assumption about statistical power.

The relA knockout control (rival 2) is a good interventional design, but relA knockout does not fully eliminate ppGpp (SpoT retains basal synthesis/hydrolysis activity), so a bimodal growth_rate result in the relA KO does not cleanly rule out ppGpp-mediated bistability as a contributor - residual SpoT-driven ppGpp could still produce coupled bimodality. The falsifier as stated doesn't address this residual coupling.

hypothesis.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
hypothesis.claim: The simulator cannot directly test two-substrate catabolite repression because it has no channel for a second sugar's uptake/induction flux and no dual-carbon-source condition (carbon source is a binary/static 'condition' dial, not a mixture). Given that hard instrument limit, the best testable REMNANT of Monod's diauxie claim is the asymmetry prediction: a downshift that removes glucose (forcing induction of new catabolic machinery) should produce a LARGER and more RelA-dependent stringent-response/growth-lag signature than the reverse case of a cell already on a non-preferred static carbon source (e.g. acetate) being given continuous favorable conditions with no shift -- i.e. the lag is specific to the loss of the preferred, repressing substrate (glucose) and the need to induce new catabolic genes, not a generic, direction-symmetric response to any media change. We operationalize 'choice/preference' only indirectly via growth_rate/ppgpp_conc kinetics at the shift, and we explicitly scope the claim down from 'which sugar is chosen' to 'does removing the preferred (repressing) substrate produce an asymmetric, RelA-dependent induction-lag signature consistent with catabolite repression, rather than a direction-independent generic downshift stress.'
hypothesis.h1: At a glucose-withdrawal timeline shift (basal -> minimal), growth_rate dips by >=20% and ppgpp_conc rises by >=1.5x within the first post-shift window, and this signature is substantially RelA-dependent (relA KO blunts the ppGpp spike by >=50%); by contrast, a static acetate condition run continuously (no shift, already on a non-preferred carbon source, analogous to the 'after induction' state) shows no transient spike (drift <5%) because there is no repression-release event to trigger new induction -- demonstrating the lag/spike is specific to the LOSS of the repressing substrate, not a generic feature of being on any non-glucose medium.
hypothesis.h0: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc at the glucose-withdrawal shift are statistically indistinguishable from the continuous wildtype/basal reference AND from the continuous static-acetate reference (all |welch_t|<2), i.e. there is no shift-specific transient signature at all, consistent with smooth, direction-independent substrate transitions with no induction lag.

rivals.claim: Generic nutrient-downshift stress: any loss of a carbon source (regardless of whether it was a repressing/preferred substrate) triggers a RelA/SpoT stringent response of similar magnitude, so the signature is not specific to glucose/catabolite-repression release.
rivals.distinguishing_result: The continuous static-acetate design (already on a non-preferred, non-glucose carbon source with no shift) ALSO shows a comparable transient-like deviation vs wildtype/basal (|welch_t|>=2), OR a reverse-direction-style check is impossible to construct in-envelope so this rival remains only partially excluded by the acetate-static asymmetry control; if acetate-static shows no spike this rival is disfavored, but if it does, generic-stress wins over repression-specific lag.

auxiliary_assumptions: No channel exists for second-sugar uptake flux, operon induction, or a true two-sugar mixed-carbon condition; 'sequential vs simultaneous USE of two named sugars' per se is out of scope for direct measurement -- the claim is explicitly narrowed to the growth_rate/ppgpp_conc kinetic signature of substrate-withdrawal as an indirect proxy for induction lag, per the instrument's actual dials.

The timeline shift '0 basal, 1200 minimal' is treated as removing the preferred (glucose) substrate and forcing a metabolic transition; 'minimal' is assumed to still support growth via some alternative pathway rather than representing total carbon starvation -- this cannot be independently confirmed from channels alone and is flagged as an irreducible interpretive gap (per objection r1.3), carried forward as scope caveat rather than resolved.

Static acetate condition (continuous, no shift) is used as the closest in-envelope proxy for 'already on a non-preferred/non-glucose substrate with machinery already induced,' since a true reverse-direction (acetate-to-glucose) mid-run timeline switch is not confirmed to be within the envelope (timeline perturbation note explicitly excludes carbon-source switches); this is the best feasible asymmetry control available, not a perfect reverse-shift test.
Seeds are isogenic stochastic replicates; cross-seed variability in spike timing/magnitude reflects intrinsic noise, not confound.
Four generations suffices to capture shift, transient response, and onset of recovery.

residual_ambiguities: [rival_not_excluded] The proposer has not added a reverse-direction timeline shift (e.g., minimal/acetate -> basal/glucose) despite two rounds of this exact objection. They instead substitute a no-shift static-acetate condition and explicitly concede in auxiliary_assumptions that a true reverse-shift 'is not confirmed to be within the envelope.' But the timeline perturbation channel takes arbitrary condition labels at arbitrary times (as shown by their own glucose-withdrawal design: '0 basal, 1200 minimal'); nothing in the provided schema actually forbids '0 acetate, 1200 basal' or '0 minimal, 1200 basal' as a timeline string. Since the instrument plausibly CAN run this design, the claim that it 'cannot be constructed in-envelope' looks like an unverified assumption rather than a genuine instrument limit, and the asymmetry claim remains the untested core of H1.

The whole mechanism (catabolite repression suppressing induction of alternative-sugar enzymes) is asserted but the only operationalized channels are growth_rate and ppgpp_conc, which are generic stress/growth readouts, not direct evidence of 'sequential vs simultaneous substrate use' as such. The claim conflates a generic nutrient-downshift signature with evidence of diauxie/catabolite repression specifically.

The relA-knockout rival control is a good interventional step, but it only tests whether the stress spike is RelA-dependent generic starvation vs repression-specific. It does NOT distinguish the catabolite-repression mechanism (cAMP-CRP/PTS-mediated transcriptional suppression of alternative-sugar operons) from an alternative mechanism such as simple carbon-limitation-induced stringent response with no hierarchical regulatory choice at all -- i.e., a cell could show a transient ppGpp spike/growth dip from *any* carbon source switch (even sugar-to-sugar with no true 'preference') without this being due to glucose-specific repression of the second sugar's uptake genes. Nothing in the design rules out that the same signature would appear if the shift were, e.g., alternative-sugar-to-glucose (the reverse direction), which true catabolite repression should NOT reproduce symmetrically.

The design assumes 'minimal/glucose-withdrawn' timeline condition in the simulator actually represents arrival onto an alternative SUGAR (not just generic carbon starvation or an amino-acid/ion shift). This is stated as an auxiliary assumption, but it is doing heavy lifting: if 'minimal' in this envelope has no sugar/carbon-source semantics at all, the entire diauxie interpretation collapses into 'generic downshift causes transient stress,' which is a much weaker and already well-known claim unrelated to sugar choice.

The rival 'generic direction-independent downshift stress' predicts a spike on ANY carbon-source transition shift, not just removal-of-preferred-substrate. The static-acetate (no-shift) control cannot test this because it has no shift event at all -- it only shows that resting on a non-preferred medium is calm, not that a reverse SHIFT (e.g., acetate-to-glucose or minimal-to-basal) would fail to produce the same ppGpp/growth signature. Since the candidate explicitly admits a true reverse-direction timeline switch is 'not confirmed to be within the envelope,' the directional/asymmetry claim central to H1 remains interventionally untested against its most natural rival.

The central claim is that the ppGpp/growth signature is asymmetric -- specific to withdrawal of the preferred/repressing substrate -- yet no design includes an actual reverse-direction SHIFT (e.g., minimal/acetate -> basal/glucose, or acetate -> glucose timeline switch) to test whether a generic 'any transition' stress produces the same spike. The static-acetate-continuous design has no shift event at all, so it cannot distinguish 'spike only on repression-release' from 'spike on any shift, including the reverse direction.' Without an actual reverse-shift condition in the candidate_designs, the generic-downshift rival is still only partially addressed, and the asymmetry claim in H1 is not interventionally tested, only asserted as infeasible.

hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: When the preferred carbon source is exhausted in a diauxic-like media shift, the population does not switch to the secondary pathway in unison: isogenic cells show heterogeneous, asynchronous induction of the stress/stringent response, producing a distribution of growth-rate and ppGpp trajectories across seeds rather than a single synchronized transition — i.e. the population exhibits substantial between-seed (and implied between-cell) variance in timing/magnitude of the switch, not a step-like synchronous shift.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds subjected to the same preferred-sugar-to-minimal media shift, the post-shift trajectories of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show high dispersion (CV of growth_rate across seeds at a fixed post-shift timepoint >= 0.25, i.e. at least ~4x the pre-shift baseline CV), consistent with asynchronous, bet-hedging-like switching rather than a synchronous population-wide transition.
hypothesis.h0: All seeds switch at essentially the same time and magnitude: the post-shift CV of growth_rate across seeds is statistically indistinguishable from the pre-shift (steady-state basal) CV of growth_rate across seeds (no significant increase), i.e. the population responds as a synchronized unit.

operational_defs.observable: timeline perturbation: media switches at a fixed time from a glucose-like minimal condition to an amino-acid/ion shift timeline (carbon-source mid-run switches are not permitted in this envelope, so we instantiate 'running out of preferred substrate' as the closest in-envelope analogue: a sharp nutrient downshift via timeline amino_acid_shift removing amino acids, forcing cells onto de novo biosynthesis/stringent response, which is the canonical proxy for a preferred-to-secondary nutrient transition in this instrument)

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Post-shift growth_rate CV across seeds rises from a basal baseline CV of ~0.05-0.08 to >=0.25 (>=4-fold increase), and the pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc distribution at the post-shift timepoint is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with an estimated ~30-60% of seeds showing a fast/high-ppGpp response and the remainder a delayed/low-ppGpp response — i.e. a bimodal split rather than a single tight cluster.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of per-seed growth_rate at the post-shift timepoint (target) vs per-seed growth_rate at a matched pre-shift/basal timepoint (reference), across the same seeds; reject H1 (synchrony holds) if |welch_t| < 2 AND the post-shift CV is not >=4x the pre-shift CV. Additionally compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (bimodality_bc) over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values at the post-shift timepoint; refute bimodal/heterogeneous-switching claim if BC <= 0.555.
falsifier.refuting_result: Post-shift growth_rate CV across seeds is statistically indistinguishable from pre-shift CV (|welch_t|<2, effect_pct small) and ppgpp_conc pooled distribution is unimodal (BC<=0.555), indicating all seeds switched in near-lockstep.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc at post-shift timepoint; paired with welch_disconfirm on growth_rate CV comparison
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 for bimodal/heterogeneous switching; otherwise reject H1

rivals.claim: Switching heterogeneity is an artifact of simulator stochastic noise unrelated to any real bet-hedging biology — i.e. any isogenic population under ANY steady unperturbed condition would show similarly inflated CV simply from intrinsic simulator noise, not from the nutrient shift itself.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If the wildtype/basal (no-shift) reference design ALSO shows post-shift-timepoint growth_rate CV >=0.25 at the matched late timepoint (i.e. basal noise alone produces high CV), this rival is supported and the shift-specific heterogeneity claim is refuted.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is not from asynchronous stringent-response timing but from a deterministic, universal GRADED response: every cell slows down by the same fractional amount in a continuous (non-bimodal) way, and apparent variance is just continuous graded noise, not two subpopulations.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If bimodality_bc <= 0.555 (unimodal) despite elevated CV, this indicates a continuous graded response across all cells rather than a discrete fast/slow split, supporting this rival over the bet-hedging/bimodal-switch hypothesis.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift timeline (removing amino acids mid-run) is accepted as the closest in-envelope proxy for 'preferred sugar running out' since carbon-source mid-run switches are explicitly disallowed; results are interpreted as evidence about nutrient-downshift switching heterogeneity in general, not literally diauxie-specific glucose-to-lactose kinetics.

Per-seed trajectories are treated as a proxy for cell-to-cell heterogeneity within a population; the simulator's seeds represent independent stochastic replicates of an isogenic lineage, not literally single cells within one shared culture, so between-seed variance is interpreted as an upper-bound proxy for between-cell asynchrony.

ppgpp_conc and growth_rate are recorded under steady-state charging by default; we assume the steady_state elongation_model is used unless a kinetic/coarse_kinetic RelA/SpoT module is explicitly requested, and interpret ppgpp_conc accordingly.

The chosen post-shift timepoint (60 min) is assumed to fall within the window where differential stringent-response induction has already diverged across seeds but before the population has fully re-equilibrated; sensitivity to this exact timepoint choice is a known limitation not resolvable without additional timepoint sweeps.
residual_ambiguities: [construct_ambiguity] Do you have (or can you run) a calibration set of basal replicate seeds to empirically fix the baseline CV before committing to the 0.25/4x thresholds, or should the decision rule instead be defined relative to the measured basal CV from perturbation design #2 rather than a hardcoded prior number?

objection_ledger.issue: The claim is fundamentally about single-cell, within-population heterogeneity ('do all CELLS switch at the same time'), but the instrument only outputs per-seed (replicate-population) trajectories, not single-cell distributions. Between-seed CV is a proxy, explicitly flagged as an 'upper-bound proxy' in auxiliary_assumptions, but this means the hypothesis as stated (about cells) cannot actually be confirmed or refuted by the dial available (seeds) -- only a weaker claim about reproducibility across replicate runs can be tested.

The basal/wildtype reference design (perturbation 2) has no timeline shift at all -- it never experiences the amino_acid_shift -- but the decision rule compares its CV only implicitly via rivals, not via the primary falsifier, and more importantly it is sampled starting from the SAME minimal_plus_amino_acids condition without ever downshifting, so its 'post-shift timepoint' (60 min) measures 60 min of continuous growth in rich-like medium, not 60 min of growth in the SAME shifted medium the target condition reaches. This confounds 'no shift occurred' with 'different medium composition is being compared', an unstated assumption that basal noise in minimal_plus_amino_acids is representative of basal noise in minimal (post-shift) medium.

The CV thresholds (basal ~0.05-0.08, post-shift >=0.25, i.e. >=4x) and the BC>0.555 cutoff are stated as fixed numeric predictions but no justification or prior calibration run is referenced establishing what this simulator's baseline seed-to-seed CV actually is for growth_rate under unperturbed steady growth. If the real baseline CV is, e.g., 0.15, the '4x' threshold could trivially pass or fail regardless of biology.

hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: At the diauxic-type media shift (timeline switches from basal to a second fitted condition), replicate seeds of an isogenic E. coli population do NOT all resume growth at the same rate/timing; instead the across-seed distribution of post-shift growth_rate is bimodal, reflecting a stochastic split between a responsive/growing mode and an arrested mode, with the arrested mode co-occurring with sustained-high ppgpp_conc. Each simulator 'seed' is a single stochastic lineage trajectory rather than an explicit multi-cell population, so bimodality ACROSS a large seed ensemble is used as the operational proxy for population heterogeneity, and to guard against a borderline point-estimate call near the BC=0.555 threshold, the bimodality coefficient is now accompanied by a bootstrap confidence interval over resampled seeds so the result must be reliably on one side of the threshold, not a bare point estimate.
hypothesis.h1: Pooled post-shift growth_rate values across a LARGE seed ensemble (n=30) are bimodal: Sarle's BC point estimate > 0.555 AND the 95% bootstrap CI (resampling seeds with replacement, 2000 resamples) for BC lies entirely above 0.555. Arrested-mode fraction of lineages is ~20-50%, and arrested-classified seeds show mean ppgpp_conc elevated ~1.5-3x over responsive-classified seeds -- i.e. the shift outcome is bimodal/heterogeneous across lineages, not a single synchronous response.
hypothesis.h0: The post-shift growth_rate distribution across the same n=30 seed ensemble is unimodal: BC <= 0.555, OR the bootstrap 95% CI on BC straddles 0.555 (i.e. the point estimate is not reliably distinguishable from the unimodal boundary). Under H0, every lineage switches on a similar deterministic schedule with only ordinary unimodal replicate noise; no distinguishable low/arrested cluster exists, and division_rate/ppgpp_conc do not segregate into two co-varying groups.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel sampled at a fixed short window after the timeline media-switch event, pooled across a large seed ensemble
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) of the pooled per-seed post-shift growth_rate distribution, n=30 seeds, plus a 95% bootstrap CI over seed-resamples (2000 resamples) to confirm the point estimate is reliably above/below 0.555

operational_defs.observable: division_rate channel per seed post-shift
operational_defs.measure: classify a seed as arrested if its division_rate falls below 0.5x the pre-shift/wildtype median division_rate, responsive otherwise; report arrested fraction across the 30 seeds

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc channel per seed post-shift
operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc in arrested-classified seeds vs responsive-classified seeds (ratio)

operational_defs.observable: cross-seed distribution shape under a single timeline perturbation
operational_defs.measure: explicit auxiliary assumption: treat the ensemble of independent stochastic seed trajectories as sampling the same space of outcomes that lineages within one isogenic culture would occupy, since the simulator does not expose a single run with multiple coexisting single cells

operational_defs.construct: reliability of the bimodality call near threshold
operational_defs.observable: bootstrap-resampled BC values over the n=30 pooled seed set
operational_defs.measure: 95% CI of BC from 2000 seed-level bootstrap resamples; the call (bimodal vs unimodal) requires the CI to lie entirely on one side of 0.555

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Pooled post-shift growth_rate across 30 seeds is bimodal with BC point estimate > 0.555 and 95% bootstrap CI entirely above 0.555 (vs wildtype/basal single mode BC ~0.3-0.4, CI entirely below 0.555, at matched n), arrested-mode fraction ~20-50% of seeds, and arrested-mode mean ppgpp_conc 1.5-3x the responsive-mode mean.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled n=30 per-seed post-shift growth_rate values from timeline/diauxic_shift, with a 95% bootstrap CI from 2000 seed-resamples; reject unimodal H0 only if the point estimate BC>0.555 AND the CI lies entirely above 0.555. Require the matched wildtype/basal reference ensemble (also n=30, with its own bootstrap CI) to show BC<=0.555 with CI entirely at or below 0.555, confirming the bimodality is shift-specific and not a pooling artifact.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC <= 0.555 for timeline/diauxic_shift, or the bootstrap CI straddles 0.555 (inconclusive), and/or the classified arrested fraction is <10% or >90% (near-uniform response), and/or the wildtype/basal reference itself shows BC>0.555 with CI entirely above 0.555 (indicating pooling artifact rather than shift-driven heterogeneity)

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled n=30 per-seed post-shift growth_rate, with 95% bootstrap CI (2000 seed-resamples)
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 AND 95% CI entirely above 0.555 for timeline/diauxic_shift; BC <= 0.555 AND 95% CI entirely at or below 0.555 for wildtype/basal

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic fast switch): all lineages detect substrate exhaustion and switch metabolic machinery essentially simultaneously once an intracellular signal drops below threshold; apparent cross-seed spread is just ordinary unimodal stochastic noise, not a distinct arrested cluster.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled post-shift growth_rate BC <= 0.555 (CI entirely at or below 0.555) at n=30 and division_rate near 1.0 for nearly all 30 seeds within 1-2 generations post-shift -- no persistent low-division cluster emerges even at large n with a reliable CI.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp is a downstream passenger, not a causal driver of the split): the growing/arrested split is driven purely by stochastic differences in catabolic enzyme/transporter expression, and ppGpp changes are a secondary consequence of slow growth rather than a cause of arrest; a relA-knockout background (removing ppGpp synthesis capacity) would NOT change the bimodal split or arrested fraction.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In a relA-knockout run through the same timeline shift (n=30 seeds), growth_rate bimodality persists (BC still >0.555, CI entirely above 0.555) with a similar arrested fraction and ppgpp_conc flat/non-responsive across both modes -- showing ppGpp is correlative, not causal, for the split.

auxiliary_assumptions: Each simulator 'seed' is an independent stochastic single-lineage trajectory, not multiple coexisting cells within one run; cross-seed bimodality at large n is used as an explicit proxy for the distribution of outcomes an isogenic population's lineages would show, NOT as literal simultaneous coexistence captured within a single run -- this substitution is accepted as the best available operationalization given the instrument's structure.

n=30 seeds per arm, combined with a 2000-resample bootstrap CI on BC, is treated as adequate to make the bimodal/unimodal call robust to sampling noise near the 0.555 boundary; this is a pragmatic power choice, not a formal pre-registered power analysis, and remains a scope caveat.

The timeline perturbation's media-shift event (basal to a second fitted/static condition such as acetate) adequately proxies a preferred-to-secondary-sugar diauxic shift within the validated envelope.

Sampling growth_rate/division_rate/ppgpp_conc at a fixed short window post-shift (within 1-2 generations) captures the bifurcation before any slow re-convergence; later re-convergence of arrested lineages is out of scope.
division_rate <0.5x of the pre-shift/wildtype median is an adequate operational proxy for 'arrested' lineage classification, since no direct single-cell lag-time readout is exposed.

Whether the relA-knockout is mechanistically wired to ppgpp_conc output in this simulator is not fully knowable a priori; if ppgpp_conc becomes flat/non-responsive in that KO, this is taken as confirmation the knockout engaged the intended mechanism.

The bootstrap CI on BC is computed by resampling the n=30 seed-level growth_rate values with replacement (2000 resamples) and recomputing BC each time; this addresses sampling instability of the point estimate but does not constitute a formal dip-test or mixture-model null, which the platform does not provide.

objection_ledger.issue: Each 'seed' in this simulator is almost certainly a stochastic single-lineage (or small population) run, not an independent single cell within one shared population. Treating pooled growth_rate across seeds as a proxy for within-population bimodality (i.e., a single isogenic population splitting into two coexisting subpopulations at one timepoint) conflates 'variability across independent simulation replicates' with 'coexistence of two subpopulations within one culture.' A bimodal distribution across 6 seeds could just reflect run-to-run variability in shift timing, not a real bet-hedging split within any single population.

With only 6 seeds, Sarle's bimodality coefficient is a poor diagnostic -- BC on n=6 pooled growth_rate values is extremely noisy and can cross 0.555 from sampling artifacts alone in either direction, regardless of the true underlying mechanism. The decision rule as stated cannot reliably distinguish H1 from H0 at this sample size, making the falsifier practically non-risky in either direction.

The BC=0.555 threshold is the standard unimodal/bimodal boundary for the classic Sarle coefficient, but with n=30 (still fairly small for distributional shape inference) the sampling distribution of BC under the null is not characterized here (no permutation/bootstrap null or confidence interval on BC itself), so a single point estimate crossing 0.555 could still be a close call near the boundary.

hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: At the diauxic shift (preferred carbon source exhaustion), an isogenic E. coli population does NOT switch uniformly to the second substrate; instead it bifurcates into a responsive/growing subpopulation and an arrested subpopulation, with the split fraction shaped by catabolite repression/ppGpp state rather than all lineages re-accelerating in lockstep. Because each simulator seed represents one stochastic lineage trajectory (not an internally mixed cell population), this heterogeneity is operationalized as bimodality in the ACROSS-SEED distribution of post-shift growth_rate, using a post-shift window anchored to a fixed delay after the scheduled media-shift event (not to each lineage's own depletion time) to avoid conflating a dispersed-but-synchronous transition with true bimodality.
hypothesis.h1: Across >=8 seeds sampling isogenic replicate lineages through a timed media shift that depletes the preferred substrate, the pooled across-seed distribution of post-shift growth_rate (sampled in a fixed window anchored a fixed delay after the scheduled shift event, wide enough to exceed plausible per-lineage depletion-time jitter) is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555), with an estimated growing fraction ~40-70% and arrested fraction ~30-60%, and ppgpp_conc is elevated (~2-4x) and more variable across seeds (CV +>=50%) in that window relative to a matched single-substrate reference.
hypothesis.h0: Post-shift growth_rate across seeds is unimodal (BC <= 0.555) and centered near a single new steady-state value -- i.e. all lineages resume growth together at comparable rates (modulo ordinary replicate noise or a smooth dispersed-but-synchronous transition), matching the wildtype/basal single-substrate reference distribution shape, and ppgpp_conc shows no differential elevation/variance increase vs reference.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed instantaneous growth_rate sampled in a FIXED post-shift window anchored at a fixed delay (e.g. +10 to +120 min) after the scheduled shift event (not anchored to each lineage's own depletion time), pooled across >=8 seeds, tested for bimodality via Sarle's BC

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean and across-seed CV of ppgpp_conc in the post-shift window compared to pre-shift and to a static single-substrate reference

operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: fraction of lineages (seeds) that fail to complete a division cycle in the post-shift window, as a corroborating viability proxy for the 'arrested' subpopulation

operational_defs.construct: lineage-level (not per-seed-population) resolution of the instrument
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate per-seed spread
operational_defs.measure: explicit auxiliary check: per-seed within-run growth_rate trace variance is small relative to across-seed variance in the reference design, confirming each seed behaves as one lineage so that across-seed pooling is the correct operationalization of population heterogeneity

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Pooled across >=8 seeds, post-shift growth_rate shows bimodal shape with BC > 0.555 and an estimated arrested-seed fraction of 30-60% (vs <10% expected under a unimodal null); ppgpp_conc rises ~2-4 fold post-shift vs pre-shift baseline and its across-seed CV increases by >=50% relative to the single-substrate reference. If instead the apparent split merely tracked a dispersed-but-synchronous depletion time, widening the fixed post-shift window or shifting its anchor by +/-30 min should collapse BC toward <=0.555; robustness of BC>0.555 across two anchor choices is required to accept H1.

falsifier.decision_rule: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed post-shift growth_rate values (fixed window anchored +10 to +120 min after scheduled shift); reject unimodal H0 if BC>0.555 AND this holds under a second window anchored +40 to +150 min (robustness check against Rival C). Secondary corroboration: Welch t of ppgpp_conc (timeline/diauxic_shift post-shift window vs condition/basal) with |t|>=2.
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled post-shift growth_rate is unimodal (BC<=0.555) under either or both window anchors, with a single tight peak, and ppgpp_conc shows no significant elevation/variance increase vs basal (|t|<2) -- indicating synchronous, non-bifurcated (or merely dispersed-timing) resumption of growth.

test.statistic: sarle_bimodality_coefficient
test.threshold: BC>0.555 (robust across two window anchors)

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic synchronous switch / pure noise): all lineages share essentially identical internal state and switch together once the preferred substrate crosses a threshold; apparent across-seed variability is replicate noise, not true bifurcation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled post-shift growth_rate is unimodal (BC<=0.555) and per-seed spread is comparable to the basal reference's intrinsic noise -- no bimodal structure emerges, and this holds at both window-anchor choices.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp-independent arrest / induction-kinetics only): the lag/arrest is driven purely by metabolic enzyme-induction delay rather than ppGpp-mediated stringent response; a relA knockout (removing ppGpp surge capacity) would NOT abolish the bimodal split.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA-knockout background under the same diauxic timeline, growth_rate pooled across seeds remains bimodal (BC>0.555) with a similar arrested fraction, while ppgpp_conc fails to rise post-shift -- showing the split persists without the ppGpp surge, implicating induction kinetics rather than ppGpp as the driver.

rivals.claim: Rival C (dispersed-but-synchronous transition artifact): every lineage switches at a similar rate but the TIMING of depletion is itself variable across seeds (e.g. due to stochastic uptake-flux noise), so a fixed observation window catches some lineages mid-transition and others post-transition, producing spurious bimodality even though there is no true subpopulation split.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Bimodality (BC>0.555) is anchor-sensitive: it appears at a narrow/early-anchored window but collapses to BC<=0.555 once the window is widened or shifted later to let all lineages complete their individual transitions -- whereas true bifurcation (H1) keeps BC>0.555 under both window choices because the arrested subpopulation remains arrested rather than merely delayed.

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline perturbation's media shift (minimal -> minimal with only secondary substrate) adequately models preferred-substrate exhaustion within the validated envelope (no direct carbon-source-switch perturbation exists, so this is approximated via the timeline mechanism).

Each seed represents one deterministic-but-stochastic lineage trajectory (not an internally mixed cell population); across-seed pooling is therefore the correct operationalization of population-level heterogeneity, as checked by comparing within-seed vs across-seed growth_rate variance in the basal reference.

Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are recorded per-seed at sufficient temporal resolution to distinguish pre- vs post-shift windows and to support two distinct post-shift window anchors within a 330-minute / 3-generation run.
The relA knockout is assumed to abolish RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis in the model (a mechanistic KO-fidelity assumption not independently verifiable here).
Division_rate <1 in the post-shift window is treated as corroborating (not primary) evidence for 'arrest', since the primary claim is operationalized on growth_rate bimodality.

Whether the simulator's stochastic noise model is rich enough to generate a true bet-hedging split (vs only measurement-level jitter) is not fully resolvable within this instrument; this is recorded as an irreducible scope caveat rather than chased further.

candidate_designs.timeline: 0 minimal (preferred sugar), 180 minimal (secondary sugar only, preferred exhausted)
0 minimal (preferred sugar), 180 minimal (secondary sugar only, preferred exhausted)

objection_ledger.issue: No carbon-source-switch perturbation is listed among available perturbations; the design repurposes 'timeline' with a hand-authored media condition string ('minimal_glucose_to_minimal_plus_secondary_carbon') to stand in for diauxic shift. It is unclear the simulator engine actually implements per-cell stochastic subpopulation splitting (bet-hedging) rather than a single deterministic trajectory per seed, in which case seed-to-seed variability would just be numerical noise, not population heterogeneity within a seed.

The claim that growth_rate bimodality reflects a true 'responsive vs arrested' bet-hedging split (rather than, e.g., a smooth but fast transition that happens to straddle two sampling windows, or an artifact of pooling pre- and post-transition-window timepoints together) is not fully excluded by the stated post-shift window definition alone, since the post-shift window (190-300 min) is fixed rather than anchored to each lineage's actual depletion time, which could itself vary and produce spurious bimodality in a population that is actually switching in lockstep but at a dispersed depletion time.

all_rounds.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
all_rounds.claim: Bacterial persistence (survival of a stress/antibiotic-relevant perturbation without genetic resistance) arises from a stochastic, ppGpp-mediated stringent-response state: in an isogenic population subjected to a growth-limiting rRNA-capacity constraint, a sizable subpopulation of cells spontaneously enters a high-ppGpp, low-growth-rate 'persister-like' state even without any antibiotic-target mutation, and this bimodal split is causally dependent on ppGpp synthesis (RelA) rather than being an inevitable byproduct of slow growth per se.
all_rounds.h1: Across seeds of an isogenic population under ribosome-capacity stress (rrna_operon_knockout), the per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and corresponding ppgpp_conc) is bimodal with a low-growth/high-ppGpp subpopulation comprising roughly 10-30% of seeds, and this bimodality collapses (reverts to unimodal, low-ppGpp) when ppGpp synthesis is removed via a relA-family gene knockout -- demonstrating that the dormant/tolerant state is actively generated by stringent-response signaling, not a passive consequence of reduced ribosome number.
all_rounds.h0: The growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) distribution across seeds under rrna_operon_knockout is unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555), i.e. cells respond homogeneously to ribosome-capacity stress with no distinct high-ppGpp/low-growth subpopulation, and/or removing relA (gene_knockout) does not significantly change the bimodality or the mean ppgpp_conc relative to the rrna_operon_knockout alone.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state growth_rate value; a cell/seed is classified 'dormant-like' if growth_rate falls below the lower of a 2-cluster split from bimodality_bc

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state ppgpp_conc (uM), multiple of basal wildtype mean

operational_defs.observable: rrna_operon_knockout perturbation + ribosome_conc channel
operational_defs.measure: fold-reduction in ribosome_conc relative to wildtype/basal

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate under combined rrna_operon_knockout + relA gene_knockout
operational_defs.measure: change in bimodality_bc and mean ppgpp_conc relative to rrna_operon_knockout alone

all_rounds.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of growth_rate across seeds under rrna_operon_knockout, Sarle's BC > 0.555, with the low-growth cluster at roughly 20% (range 10-30%) of seeds and ppgpp_conc in that cluster >=3-fold the basal wildtype mean; upon relA knockout (stringent-response-null background), BC drops below 0.555 (unimodal) and mean ppgpp_conc falls by >=50% relative to rrna_operon_knockout alone (Welch t on ppgpp_conc, |t|>=2).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, (rrna_operon_knockout + relA-knockout) vs rrna_operon_knockout-alone, across seeds; reject H1's causal claim if |t|<2 (no significant drop) OR if bimodality_bc on growth_rate stays >0.555 in the relA-knockout background
falsifier.refuting_result: ppgpp_conc is not significantly reduced by relA knockout (|t|<2) and/or growth_rate remains bimodal (BC>0.555) in the double-perturbed background, showing the dormant subpopulation does not depend on ppGpp synthesis

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for significant ppgpp_conc reduction; additionally require bimodality_bc<=0.555 post-knockout to confirm collapse

rivals.claim: Rival A: Slow growth / low ribosome number alone (not ppGpp signaling) passively produces a heterogeneous, long-tailed growth-rate distribution purely from stochastic partitioning of few ribosomes at division -- ppGpp is a correlate, not a cause.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, relA knockout under rrna_operon_knockout would NOT collapse the bimodality in growth_rate (BC stays >0.555) even though ppgpp_conc drops, because the growth heterogeneity is driven by ribosome-partitioning noise independent of ppGpp.

rivals.claim: Rival B: The apparent 'persister' subpopulation is simply cells failing to divide (a division defect) rather than a distinct physiological dormant state, i.e. division_rate drives the low end of the growth_rate distribution via a floor effect rather than genuine bimodal stringent-response switching.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the low-growth cluster would coincide almost entirely with division_rate<1 (non-dividing) seeds rather than being a continuous low-but-nonzero growth subpopulation, and ppgpp_conc in that cluster would NOT be elevated above the high-growth cluster.

auxiliary_assumptions: Across 6-8 seeds the per-seed steady-state growth_rate/ppgpp_conc values are a sufficient sample to estimate Sarle's bimodality coefficient meaningfully (acknowledging this is a small-N approximation to a population-wide claim).
rrna_operon_knockout is simulated with a graded/partial reduction in rRNA operon copies sufficient to induce stress without being uniformly lethal (division_rate not collapsing to 0 for all seeds).

The platform's steady-state charging model (fraction_trna_charged, ppgpp_conc) responds to ribosome-capacity stress even without the kinetic RelA/SpoT module explicitly toggled on; if ppgpp_conc is flat across all designs because the kinetic module is off, this is recorded as a model-scope limitation, not a refutation.

Persistence-to-antibiotics proper (survival under drug challenge) is operationalized here via the growth-rate/ppGpp dormancy proxy, since the instrument has no direct antibiotic-kill channel; this stands as an explicit scope caveat on the claim's generalization to literal antibiotic survival.
residual_ambiguities: [construct_ambiguity] Should the 10-30% figure be interpreted strictly as a fraction of the 6-8 simulated seeds (so e.g. 2/8 seeds = 25% would count as confirming), or as a qualitative claim that at least one but not a majority of seeds falls in the low-growth cluster?

objection_ledger.issue: Rival A's proposed falsifier relies on comparing bimodality_bc of growth_rate between rrna_operon_knockout alone vs +relA-knockout. But relA knockout itself also reduces ribosome-partitioning stress indirectly if relA loss changes overall growth/ribosome allocation (feedback via RNA/protein mass channels), so a collapse in bimodality could occur even if the mechanism is Rival A's passive partitioning noise responding secondarily to altered ribosome allocation post-relA-KO, not because ppGpp signaling was the proximate cause of bimodality. The design does not include a control that holds ribosome_conc/partitioning stress constant while varying ppGpp (e.g., a relA-knockout-only or a ppgpp_conc perturbation on top of rrna_operon_knockout without relA) to isolate ppGpp's causal role from secondary ribosome-level changes.

The 10-30% subpopulation fraction and the >=3-fold ppgpp_conc threshold for the low-growth cluster are fairly specific quantitative predictions, but with only 8 seeds per design it's unclear whether 'cluster size as fraction of seeds' is meant to approximate a true within-population persister fraction or is just a statement about how many of the 8 stochastic seeds happen to land in the low-growth basin. This affects whether a result like 1/8 or 3/8 seeds in the low cluster counts as confirming versus refuting evidence.
