test.threshold: BC > 0.555 for bimodal rejection of H0; paired with welch_t |t|>=2 on ppgpp_conc between clusters

rivals.claim: Graded stress response: all cells uniformly slow growth proportional to stress severity (no distinct subpopulation), i.e. a continuous/unimodal dose-response rather than bet-hedging.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled growth_rate across seeds remains unimodal (BC <= 0.555) with a single shifted mean relative to wildtype/basal, and ppgpp_conc shows a uniform graded increase across all seeds rather than a bimodal split.

rivals.claim: ppGpp is a co-mover/consequence of slow growth (via charged-tRNA depletion) rather than a causal driver of the dormant state; the real cause is depletion of charged tRNA pools directly limiting translation, with ppGpp epiphenomenal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In a relA gene_knockout (stringent-response-abolished) background under the same amino_acid_shift, growth_rate still shows a bimodal low-growth subpopulation with reduced ribosome_conc despite blocked/reduced ppgpp_conc induction, showing ppGpp is not required for the bimodal split.

rivals.claim: Division-rate defect rather than growth-rate dormancy: the apparent 'low growth mode' actually reflects cells failing to divide (division arrest) while bulk growth_rate metrics are confounded by mass accumulation without division, not a true stringent dormancy.
rivals.distinguishing_result: The low-growth-rate cluster shows division_rate indistinguishable from the high-growth cluster (both ~1), indicating growth_rate split is not an artifact of division failure.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift timeline (minimal minus amino acids) is a reasonable proxy for antibiotic-induced stress in this simulator, since direct antibiotic-exposure perturbations are not in the envelope; we treat nutritional stringency as the operational stand-in for the stress that triggers persistence.

Per-seed growth_rate at the end of the timeline reflects a quasi-steady dormant vs active state rather than a transient fluctuation; generations=3 is assumed sufficient for the bimodal split to manifest if it exists.
The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variability is assumed to capture genuine cell-to-cell heterogeneity (intrinsic noise) rather than purely numerical artifact noise.

relA knockout is assumed to meaningfully suppress ppGpp induction in this model (kinetic/coarse_kinetic ppGpp module engaged or at least steady-state RelA-dependent synthesis reduced), making it a valid interventional control for the ppGpp-causality rival.

We do not attempt to resolve whether any observed low-growth state is heritable/epigenetic vs purely stochastic-per-generation; that distinction is out of scope for this simulator and is noted as a caveat rather than chased further.

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: A subpopulation of genetically wild-type E. coli survives antibiotic-relevant stress (simulated here as a sudden amino-acid downshift) not via resistance mutations but via a stochastic, growth-arrested 'persister' physiological state driven by stringent-response (ppGpp) induction: cells with high ppGpp/low ribosome activity at the moment of stress show a bimodal growth-rate distribution across isogenic replicates, and this bimodality collapses when the stringent response is disabled (relA knockout), proving the survival state is ppGpp-dependent dormancy rather than a resistance mechanism.
hypothesis.h1: Across a broad sample of isogenic seeds (n=48) subjected to an amino-acid downshift, the per-seed growth_rate distribution is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with a low-growth ('persister-like') mode comprising roughly 10-30% of seeds (i.e., ~5-14 of 48) showing elevated ppgpp_conc (>=2x the high-growth mode's mean) and reduced ribosome_conc (>=30% lower); this bimodality is abolished (BC <= 0.555, unimodal) when relA is knocked out, AND the knockout's mean growth_rate sits closer to the wildtype high-growth mode (within 20%) than to the low-growth mode -- ruling out 'uniform collapse to a different, unrelated state' as opposed to specific loss of the bistable switch.
hypothesis.h0: growth_rate after the downshift is unimodally distributed across the 48 seeds (BC <= 0.555, no distinct low-growth subpopulation), OR if a low-growth mode exists it persists equally when relA is knocked out (BC drop < 0.1 and still > 0.555), indicating no distinct stochastic ppGpp-dependent dormancy state; OR the relA knockout's mean growth_rate diverges from both wildtype modes by >20%, indicating the knockout produces a qualitatively different uniform physiology rather than specifically erasing the bistable switch.

operational_defs.observable: amino_acid_shift timeline (removal of amino acids mid-run, mimicking nutritional/translational stress analogous to antibiotic-induced translational arrest) and division_rate as viability readout
operational_defs.measure: division_rate (fraction of seeds/generations that successfully divide post-shift) and growth_rate trajectory per seed

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel, per-seed values pooled across replicate seeds after the shift
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed growth_rate across 48 seeds (6 seed-batches of 8, pooled, to give the 2-cluster split enough points per mode even at a 10% minority fraction, i.e. >=5 points in the minority cluster); fraction of seeds in the low-growth cluster from the 2-cluster split

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channels
operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc per cluster (low- vs high-growth), fold-difference between clusters

operational_defs.construct: ppGpp-dependence of dormancy (causal test, specific-switch vs whole-response)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate distribution shape (BC) AND mean growth_rate level in relA gene_knockout background under the same amino_acid_shift timeline
operational_defs.measure: BC in knockout vs wildtype (collapse of bimodality signals causal dependence); mean knockout growth_rate compared to wildtype's two modal means (closeness to high-growth mode vs a novel uniform level rules in/out the 'whole stress response removed' rival)

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Bimodal growth_rate distribution post-downshift in wildtype across 48 seeds (BC > 0.555), low mode = 10-30% of seeds (~5-14/48), with that low mode showing >=2-fold higher ppgpp_conc and >=30% lower ribosome_conc than the high-growth mode. In relA knockout (also n=48 seeds), bimodality collapses (BC drops by >=0.1 and/or falls below 0.555) and mean growth_rate lands within 20% of the wildtype high-growth mode's mean (not a novel third level), confirming specific loss of the bistable switch rather than generic uniform stress-response ablation.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values (n=48 seeds, 2-3 generations post-shift) in amino_acid_shift/basal; reject unimodal null if BC > 0.555 AND the low-growth cluster is 10-30% of seeds (with >=5 seeds in that cluster for a stable 2-cluster split). Then compare BC AND mean growth_rate in relA_knockout/amino_acid_shift (n=48) vs wildtype/amino_acid_shift (n=48): H1 requires BC to drop by >=0.1 and/or fall below 0.555 in the knockout, AND the knockout's mean growth_rate to be within 20% of the wildtype high-growth mode's mean (not a divergent third level).
falsifier.refuting_result: Either growth_rate stays unimodal (BC <= 0.555) in wildtype after the shift (no persister subpopulation to explain), or bimodality persists equally (BC stays > 0.555, drop < 0.1) in the relA knockout, or the relA knockout's mean growth_rate diverges by >20% from the wildtype high-growth mode (indicating generic uniform collapse rather than specific loss of a bistable switch) -- any of these refutes ppGpp-dependent bistable dormancy as the mechanism.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed growth_rate (n=48), plus welch_t comparison of mean growth_rate between relA_knockout and the wildtype high-growth cluster
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 for bimodal call in wildtype with minority cluster 10-30% (>=5 seeds); BC drop >= 0.1 (or below 0.555) in relA_knockout required to confirm collapse; knockout mean growth_rate within 20% of wildtype high-growth mode mean (welch |t| < 2 against that mode) required to rule out generic uniform-response rival

rivals.claim: Growth-rate heterogeneity post-downshift is just continuous metabolic slowing (unimodal, right-skewed distribution) proportional to each cell's pre-shift growth rate, with no discrete dormant state -- i.e. graded stress response, not a bistable switch.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc test returns BC <= 0.555 in wildtype amino_acid_shift/basal across the 48-seed pool; growth_rate histogram is unimodal/skewed rather than two-clustered.

rivals.claim: relA knockout removes the ENTIRE stress response (not just the bistable switch), so uniform post-knockout growth reflects a novel, ppGpp-independent physiological regime rather than specific loss of bistability -- 'no stress response at all' vs 'no bistability' are conflated.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA knockout's mean growth_rate diverges by >20% from the wildtype high-growth mode's mean (a new uniform level distinct from either wildtype mode), even though BC collapses -- implicating generic stress-response ablation, not specific bistable-switch removal.

rivals.claim: The low-growth subpopulation arises from division-machinery stochasticity (unequal partitioning of division proteins) unrelated to ppGpp/stringent response -- a FtsZ-limitation or replication-stress mechanism.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA knockout does NOT collapse bimodality (BC stays > 0.555, drop < 0.1) even though ppgpp_conc is flat across clusters in the knockout, while division_rate still shows a bimodal split -- implicating a ppGpp-independent mechanism.

rivals.claim: Observed survivors are actually resistant mutants (fixed genetic resistance) rather than stochastic phenotypic persisters -- i.e., this is really modeling emergence of resistance, not persistence.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Not directly testable in this simulator since it has no mutation/selection module; recorded as an auxiliary scope limitation -- we treat any heritable-looking survival as outside scope since the model holds genotype fixed within a run.

params.note: run 6 independent batches of 8 seeds (total pooled n=48) to stabilize the BC estimate and give >=5 points in a 10% minority cluster
pooled n=48 reference baseline, no shift
pooled n=48 to match target's statistical power for BC and mean-level comparison

objection_ledger.issue: With only 8 seeds, claiming a '10-30% low-growth cluster' and a bimodality coefficient threshold (BC>0.555) is statistically fragile — 8 samples cannot reliably populate a 2-cluster split with a 10-30% minority (that's roughly 1-2 cells), and BC itself is asymptotic/unstable at such small n. The design doesn't state how many seeds are actually needed for the BC statistic to be meaningfully estimated, or what happens if cluster membership is ambiguous with so few points.

The relA knockout removes ppGpp synthesis capability entirely, which could abolish bimodality simply because relA knockouts are known to grow differently/more uniformly under amino acid starvation for reasons unrelated to a 'persister' switch (e.g., relaxed-phenotype cells just keep translating and dying/growing uniformly rather than entering any alternative dormancy mode). The design doesn't rule out that the knockout's uniform behavior reflects loss of a stress-response-driven death/growth-arrest process in general rather than specific collapse of a bistable persister switch -- i.e., 'no stringent response at all' vs 'no bistability' are conflated.

The model has no mutation/selection module, so the 'resistant mutant' rival is explicitly acknowledged as unfalsifiable within this instrument and parked as an auxiliary/scope limitation already. This is fine as stated, but should remain a once-only minor flag rather than being re-litigated.

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: A subpopulation of genetically wild-type E. coli survives antibiotic-relevant stress (simulated here as an amino-acid starvation shift) not via resistance mutations but via a stochastic, pre-existing stringent-response state: cells with elevated basal ppGpp/low growth rate (a 'persister-like' phenotype) arise at low frequency even in unperturbed populations, and this bimodal subpopulation structure (not just mean growth rate) depends on functional RelA/ppGpp signaling — i.e. survival-without-resistance is explained by heterogeneous, reversible dormancy driven by the ppGpp alarmone system, not by altered genomes or by a uniform deterministic slowdown.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds, the distribution of single-seed growth_rate under an amino-acid downshift is bimodal (Sarle's BC>0.555) with a low-growth 'persister-like' tail (~10-20% of seeds, growth_rate <=30% of the high-growth mode); this bimodal STRUCTURE (not merely the mean) depends on RelA/ppGpp: in relA_knockout/aa_downshift the distribution becomes unimodal (BC<=0.555), i.e. the discrete tail is abolished, not just shifted in mean.
hypothesis.h0: The distribution of per-seed growth_rate under amino-acid downshift is statistically indistinguishable in bimodality structure between wildtype and relA-knockout backgrounds: both show BC>0.555 (or both show BC<=0.555), so RelA/ppGpp signaling has no detectable effect on the discrete subpopulation structure, even if mean growth_rate differs.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed growth_rate distribution during/after amino-acid downshift timeline; bimodality assessed via Sarle's BC over pooled per-seed values; a 'persister-like' seed is one in the low-growth mode identified by the 2-cluster split

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc per seed during downshift, compared across wildtype vs relA_knockout

operational_defs.construct: loss of bimodal STRUCTURE (not just mean shift)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's BC computed independently on wildtype/aa_downshift and on relA_knockout/aa_downshift pooled per-seed values; structural confirmation requires BC itself to cross threshold in relA KO, not only a mean-level Welch t

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate recovery after re-feed (not separately tested here; scope caveat)
operational_defs.measure: not directly measured; this study isolates the dormancy mechanism, not mutation acquisition, by design (genome is fixed across seeds)

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed ribosome_conc at downshift steady state, wildtype vs relA_knockout

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Under wildtype + amino-acid downshift, per-seed growth_rate distribution shows BC>0.555 with an estimated low-growth tail fraction of ~10-20% of seeds (growth_rate <=30% of the high-growth mode), mean growth_rate drops only ~20-30% vs basal; in relA_knockout + same downshift, BC drops to <=0.555 (structural loss of bimodality, not just a mean shift), and ppgpp_conc fails to rise (<1.2x basal vs ~3-5x in wildtype). Given n=8 seeds/arm is underpowered for a precise BC point estimate, the confirmatory claim is read with a bootstrap CI on BC (resampling seeds with replacement, ≥500 resamples) rather than a bare point threshold: H1 requires the bootstrap 90% CI for BC in wildtype/aa_downshift to lie entirely above 0.555 AND the bootstrap 90% CI for BC in relA_knockout/aa_downshift to lie entirely at or below 0.555 (non-overlapping CIs straddling the threshold in opposite directions).

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1: compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) with a bootstrap 90% CI (resample seeds with replacement, >=500 resamples) over pooled per-seed growth_rate in wildtype/aa_downshift; require CI entirely above 0.555 to confirm bimodal structure. Step 2: compute the same bootstrapped BC+CI in relA_knockout/aa_downshift; H1 requires this CI to lie entirely at or below 0.555 (structural collapse of bimodality), not merely a mean/variance (Welch t) difference. Secondary check: Welch t of growth_rate, relA_knockout/aa_downshift vs wildtype/aa_downshift, reported descriptively but NOT sufficient alone to confirm H1.
falsifier.refuting_result: Either (a) wildtype/aa_downshift BC bootstrap CI does not clear 0.555 (no reliable bimodal tail to begin with), or (b) relA_knockout/aa_downshift BC bootstrap CI ALSO remains above 0.555 (bimodal structure persists despite RelA loss, i.e. the tail is not RelA-dependent) — either outcome refutes H1 regardless of any mean-level Welch t difference.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) with bootstrap 90% CI over pooled per-seed growth_rate, computed separately for wildtype/aa_downshift and relA_knockout/aa_downshift
test.threshold: wildtype/aa_downshift: bootstrap 90% CI for BC entirely >0.555; relA_knockout/aa_downshift: bootstrap 90% CI for BC entirely <=0.555 (non-overlapping, structural loss of bimodality required to confirm H1)

rivals.claim: Rival A (uniform stress response, no heterogeneity): all cells respond to amino-acid downshift nearly identically by slowing growth proportionally (a deterministic, graded response), with no distinct dormant subpopulation; apparent spread is just stochastic noise around one mode.
rivals.distinguishing_result: wildtype/aa_downshift growth_rate bootstrap BC CI does not clear 0.555 (unimodal), even though mean growth_rate is reduced — i.e. Step 1 itself fails, before relA KO is even needed to refute.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ribosome-capacity limitation independent of ppGpp): growth-rate heterogeneity under downshift is driven by stochastic variation in ribosome_conc/rRNA capacity (extrinsic noise in translation machinery), not by RelA-triggered ppGpp signaling; knocking out relA would NOT abolish the bimodal structure because ribosome limitation persists.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/aa_downshift (ribosome-capacity-limited control) still shows bootstrap BC CI >0.555 (bimodal tail persists) comparable to wildtype, while relA_knockout/aa_downshift's BC CI drops to <=0.555 and ppgpp_conc stays flat only in relA_knockout — dissociating tail persistence from ppGpp and confirming the control isolates RelA (not ribosome capacity) as the causal driver.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino-acid downshift timeline event is a valid proxy for 'antibiotic-like stress' in that it triggers the stringent response pathway the way bactericidal stress is thought to engage ppGpp-mediated dormancy; the simulator does not implement antibiotic pharmacodynamics directly, so this study tests the dormancy-heterogeneity mechanism, not antibiotic killing per se (explicit scope caveat).

Per-seed growth_rate at a fixed timepoint post-downshift is a valid readout of persister-like dormancy (low growth = dormant-like state), independent of any resistance mutation, since genome is held fixed across all seeds within a design.

With only n=8 seeds/arm, a bootstrap CI on BC (not a bare point estimate) is used as the decision statistic precisely because BC is noisy at small n; if the bootstrap CI itself is too wide to resolve either threshold crossing cleanly, that is logged as an inconclusive/underpowered result (scope caveat) rather than a false confirmation or refutation — a larger seed count (n>=50) is the natural follow-up scale-up if this arm proves inconclusive.

relA knockout is assumed (pending downstream check) to be mechanistically simulated as abolishing stringent-response ppGpp synthesis in this platform; if not mechanistically implemented, this falls back to an auxiliary-assumption failure rather than refuting the biological claim.

The rrna_operon_knockout control is assumed to reduce ribosome capacity directly without altering RelA/ppGpp synthesis machinery, isolating 'ribosome limitation' from 'ppGpp signaling' as distinct causal arms.

objection_ledger.issue: The decision rule for confirming H1 only requires comparing wildtype/aa_downshift vs relA_knockout/aa_downshift growth_rate distributions (Welch t). But ppgpp_conc and growth_rate/ribosome shutdown are mechanistically coupled (RelA directly controls ppGpp, which directly throttles ribosome synthesis and growth rate) — so a shift in the growth_rate distribution upon relA knockout is expected under BOTH the 'bona fide stochastic dormancy' hypothesis and a trivial rival where relA knockout simply changes the population's single deterministic growth rate without creating/removing any genuine bimodal subpopulation structure. The test as specified (Welch t on pooled growth_rate, not a direct re-test of the bimodality coefficient itself in the relA KO) does not interventionally confirm that the TAIL (a discrete subpopulation) disappears specifically; it only shows a mean/variance difference. Demand that the falsifier explicitly require BC to drop below threshold in relA_knockout/aa_downshift (not just a t-test on means), since only a change in bimodality structure (not mean shift) distinguishes 'heterogeneous dormancy' from 'uniform graded slowdown.'

With only 8 seeds, estimating Sarle's bimodality coefficient (a known-noisy statistic even with hundreds of samples) and classifying a 10-20% tail is very likely underpowered to reliably return BC>0.555 vs <=0.555 reproducibility; the auxiliary_assumptions section acknowledges this but treats it as a 'follow-up scale-up' rather than resolving it for THIS falsifier. Since the primary confirm/refute hinges on a hard BC threshold with n=8, the test as specified risks being unfalsifiable in practice (noise alone could push BC either side of 0.555 regardless of true mechanism).

all_rounds.claim: Under amino-acid downshift (used here as the operational proxy for antibiotic-relevant stress, since the simulator lacks a lethality/killing channel), a minority of isogenic wildtype cells enter a persister-like phenotype — low growth_rate and elevated ppgpp_conc — driven by stochastic RelA/ppGpp pathway activation rather than genetic resistance. This produces a BIMODAL distribution of growth_rate across seeds/cells at the downshift, with ~10-20% of replicates falling into a low-growth (<=30% of median), high-ppGpp tail, and this bimodality requires an intact RelA/SpoT (stringent) pathway: a relA knockout should collapse the low-growth tail (unimodal, high mean growth_rate, no ppGpp spike).

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: In an isogenic wildtype E. coli population under basal conditions, individual seeds (interpreted as independent clonal-culture replicates, each potentially containing a mixture of normal-growth and switched-state cells captured by that seed's population-average trajectory) stochastically enter a low-growth, high-ppGpp 'persister-like' physiological state via noisy stringent-response (RelA/ppGpp) activation rather than any genetic change. This produces a bimodal distribution of per-seed growth_rate across replicate seeds with a stable low-growth-cluster fraction of ~1-10%, that cluster specifically (not merely overall variance) collapses when RelA is knocked out or ppGpp is clamped to basal, while the clamp does NOT simply flatten the whole distribution's mean/variance in a way unrelated to the cluster.
hypothesis.h1: Across >=8 replicate seeds x 4 generations of wildtype E. coli in basal condition, pooled per-seed growth_rate values (n>=32 pooled points) show bimodality (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with a distinct low-growth cluster comprising ~1-10% of points that have ppgpp_conc elevated >=2-fold over the main-cluster mean. This specific low-growth-cluster fraction (not overall variance) collapses toward 0 (>=5-fold reduction) under relA_knockout/basal AND under ppgpp_conc-clamp/basal, while the MEAN growth_rate of the remaining main cluster is NOT shifted by more than 20% between wildtype and the clamp (ruling out a trivial global-flattening confound).
hypothesis.h0: growth_rate across isogenic wildtype seeds is unimodally distributed (BC <= 0.555); any apparent low tail is replicate noise unrelated to ppGpp state and is NOT selectively abolished by relA knockout or ppGpp clamping relative to how it changes the overall distribution (i.e., any reduction in tail/variance under the interventions is proportional to, and statistically indistinguishable from, a general variance reduction rather than a cluster-specific effect).

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel value per seed-generation timepoint
operational_defs.measure: pooled per-seed-generation growth_rate distribution shape via bimodality_bc; low-cluster membership assigned by the bimodality test's 2-cluster split

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc channel per seed-generation timepoint
operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc of low-growth cluster vs main cluster (fold-elevation)

operational_defs.construct: phenotypic (non-genetic), cluster-specific origin of tolerance (vs trivial global variance suppression)
operational_defs.observable: comparison of wildtype/basal bimodal growth_rate distribution vs relA_knockout/basal and ppgpp_conc-clamp/basal, reporting BOTH the low-cluster fraction AND the main-cluster mean growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: low-cluster fraction drop (>=5-fold) co-occurring with main-cluster mean growth_rate staying within 20% of wildtype main-cluster mean, distinguishing cluster-specific collapse from general flattening

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Wildtype/basal: BC>0.555, low-growth cluster fraction ~1-10% of pooled points, ppgpp_conc in that cluster elevated >=2-fold vs main cluster. relA_knockout/basal and ppgpp_conc-clamp/basal: BC<=0.555 and low-growth fraction drops >=5-fold toward ~0%, while main-cluster mean growth_rate shifts by <20% relative to wildtype main-cluster mean (ruling out generic variance flattening).

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed-generation growth_rate values for wildtype/basal (n>=32 via 8 seeds x 4 generations); reject H0 (unimodal) only if BC>0.555. Then compare low-growth-cluster fraction and main-cluster mean growth_rate between wildtype/basal and relA_knockout/basal via Welch t across seeds: refute H1 if relA_knockout/basal ALSO shows BC>0.555 with |welch_t| < 2 on cluster-fraction difference, OR if the main-cluster mean growth_rate differs by >20% between conditions (indicating a confounded general shift rather than cluster-specific collapse), OR if wildtype/basal itself shows BC<=0.555.
falsifier.refuting_result: relA_knockout/basal retains BC>0.555 with a low-growth-cluster fraction statistically indistinguishable (|welch_t|<2) from wildtype/basal, OR the collapse of bimodality under relA_knockout/ppgpp-clamp is accompanied by a >20% shift in main-cluster mean growth_rate (signaling nonspecific flattening, not cluster-specific abolition), OR wildtype/basal shows BC<=0.555 to begin with.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed-generation growth_rate, plus Welch t on low-cluster fraction and on main-cluster mean growth_rate across seeds
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for wildtype/basal; BC<=0.555 AND |welch_t|>=2 on fraction-drop AND main-cluster mean shift <20% for relA_knockout/basal and ppgpp_conc-clamp/basal

rivals.claim: Growth-rate heterogeneity is explained by cell-cycle/division asynchrony (division_rate variance) rather than a distinct ppGpp-driven persister state; low-growth points are just cells mid-division-defect.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Low-growth cluster points show normal division_rate (~1, no division defect) and do NOT show elevated ppgpp_conc; bimodality in growth_rate does not co-occur with ppgpp_conc elevation, contradicting H1's required ppGpp co-localization.

rivals.claim: Clamping ppGpp or knocking out relA abolishes bimodality merely by flattening overall growth_rate variance/mean (a generic regulatory-input removal), not by specifically eliminating a persister subpopulation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under relA_knockout/basal or ppgpp_conc-clamp/basal, the main-cluster mean growth_rate shifts by >20% from wildtype while the low-cluster fraction also drops — i.e., both bulk and tail move together, indicating nonspecific flattening rather than selective cluster ablation.

rivals.claim: Any bimodality is a simulator/sampling artifact from finite seeds/generations, not a reproducible subpopulation structure tied to ppGpp.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Bimodality (BC>0.555) and the ~1-10% fraction fail to replicate consistently across the 8-seed x 4-generation pool, or fraction/ppgpp_conc correlation is near zero, independent of relA/clamp status.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed-generation growth_rate sampled at matched timepoints is treated as the simulator's best-available analog of a single-cell growth-state snapshot; we explicitly acknowledge (per r1.1) that the simulator may produce between-seed variability rather than literal within-one-culture single-cell heterogeneity, and we scope the claim to 'pooled seed x generation points show the Balaban-style bimodal signature' rather than asserting microscopy-level coexistence within one culture run — this residual interpretive gap is irreducible given the instrument and is not re-litigated further.

With 8 seeds x 4 generations = 32 pooled points we approximate the n>=~32-40 needed for a stable bimodality_bc estimate; if BC estimates are noisy at this n we would flag it as a power limitation rather than reinterpreting the claim.
ppgpp_conc per-seed mean is used as the best available proxy for stringent-response activation state, consistent with the note that it is recorded under steady-state charging always.

The ppgpp_conc-clamp-to-basal (1x) design is retained as the mechanical discriminating control isolating the stringent-response pathway from relA pleiotropy; objection r1.2 is addressed by requiring the decision rule to separately track main-cluster mean growth_rate (so a generic flattening confound is now detectable and would refute H1 rather than being silently counted as support).

We do not attempt to confirm antibiotic killing directly (no antibiotic-exposure perturbation exists in the envelope); persistence is operationalized purely via the growth-rate/ppGpp phenotypic signature, per available channels.

objection_ledger.issue: The whole-cell/whole-population simulator being invoked (seeds x generations) is not demonstrated to produce genuine single-cell stochastic subpopulations; if each seed deterministically yields one trajectory (population-averaged growth_rate per seed), then 'bimodality across seeds' only reflects seed-to-seed parameter/noise draws, not a persister subpopulation coexisting within one culture as the biological claim requires. This is already partly acknowledged in auxiliary_assumptions, so flagging once as minor.

The ppgpp_conc-clamp design clamps ppGpp to basal (1x), which could trivially eliminate ANY growth_rate variance (not just the persister-specific bimodal component) simply by removing a major regulatory input, since ppGpp also sets baseline ribosome/growth-rate partitioning. A collapse of bimodality under the clamp is therefore also consistent with the rival 'clamping ppGpp flattens growth_rate variance in general (including unimodal noise), not specifically abolishing a distinct persister cluster.' The decision rule should require that the clamp reduces specifically the low-growth-cluster FRACTION/separation, not merely overall variance, and should report whether mean growth_rate shifts (which would confound interpretation).
Restating the seed-vs-single-cell gap once more only to note it remains irreducible; not re-raised as substantive, already parked as auxiliary assumption.

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: In a clonal, antibiotic-naive E. coli population, a stochastically-arising, slow/non-growing subpopulation ("persisters") pre-exists before any antibiotic exposure, driven by stochastic stringent-response (ppGpp) pathway activation rather than genetic resistance. This subpopulation shows up as a distinct low-growth-rate / high-ppGpp mode across isogenic replicate seeds, present at a small but non-negligible fraction (~1-10%), and this fraction shrinks when the dominant ppGpp synthetase relA is deleted — while the WITHIN-SEED coupling of elevated ppgpp_conc to the low-growth mode also collapses, distinguishing stringent-response causation from generic expression noise.
hypothesis.h1: Across >=40 isogenic wildtype replicate seeds under constant basal media, the pooled per-seed distribution of growth_rate is BIMODAL (Sarle's BC>0.555): a dominant fast-growing mode plus a minority slow/dormant mode comprising ~1-10% of seeds, with that low mode showing >=3-fold lower growth_rate AND ~2-5x elevated ppgpp_conc versus the dominant mode. Deleting relA collapses this bimodality (BC<=0.555 in relA_knockout/basal) AND abolishes the negative within-seed correlation between ppgpp_conc and growth_rate that characterizes the low-growth-mode seeds in wildtype.
hypothesis.h0: growth_rate across isogenic wildtype replicate seeds is unimodal (BC<=0.555); any seed-to-seed variation is replicate/measurement noise, not a distinct persister subpopulation; relA deletion does not change distribution shape, low-mode fraction, or the ppgpp-growth_rate relationship.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed terminal/mean growth_rate values pooled across >=40 seeds; Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) of the pooled distribution; low-mode fraction via 2-cluster split

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed ppgpp_conc values; Pearson correlation of ppgpp_conc vs growth_rate across seeds within an arm (fit_relation), expected strongly negative in wildtype

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate distribution shape AND ppgpp-growth_rate coupling, relA knockout vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: BC comparison, low-growth-mode fraction, and slope/CI of ppgpp_conc~growth_rate regression, wildtype vs relA_KO

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Wildtype/basal: BC>0.555 over pooled growth_rate (n>=40 seeds), low mode ~1-10% of seeds, >=3-fold lower growth_rate and 2-5x higher ppgpp_conc than dominant mode; negative ppgpp_conc~growth_rate slope with 95% CI excluding 0 (e.g. slope <= -0.5 (uM per 1/h), driven by the low-growth seeds). relA_knockout/basal: BC drops <=0.555, low-mode fraction shrinks toward ~0-2%, and the ppgpp_conc~growth_rate slope CI includes 0 (coupling abolished).

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (existence): compute Sarle's BC over pooled per-seed growth_rate in wildtype/basal across >=40 seeds; H1 requires BC>0.555 with low mode at 1-10% of seeds. Step 2 (coupling): fit_relation of ppgpp_conc on growth_rate across the same wildtype seeds; H1 requires a negative slope with 95% CI excluding 0. Step 3 (causal/interventional): compute BC and the ppgpp_conc~growth_rate slope for relA gene_knockout/basal under identical sampling (>=40 seeds); reject H1 if BC in the knockout is NOT reduced below 0.555, OR if the ppgpp_conc~growth_rate slope CI in the knockout still excludes 0 with comparable magnitude to wildtype (coupling persists despite relA loss).
falsifier.refuting_result: wildtype/basal growth_rate is unimodal (BC<=0.555) or shows no significant negative ppgpp-growth_rate slope, OR relA_knockout/basal still shows BC>0.555 with comparable low-growth-mode fraction AND a comparably strong negative ppgpp_conc~growth_rate slope (bimodality and its ppGpp coupling persist despite relA loss), indicating the slow-growth mode is not stringent-response-dependent.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate; secondary slope_ci on ppgpp_conc~growth_rate fit_relation, wildtype vs relA_knockout
test.threshold: BC>0.555 and slope CI excludes 0 (negative) for wildtype/basal; BC<=0.555 AND slope CI includes 0 for relA_knockout/basal

rivals.claim: Rival A - Pure stochastic gene-expression noise (unrelated to ppGpp/stringent response): growth-rate heterogeneity arises from generic transcriptional/translational noise and is NOT specifically tied to the stringent pathway; relA knockout would NOT abolish the low-growth mode or the ppgpp-growth coupling because the noise source is elsewhere.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA_knockout/basal still shows BC>0.555 with a persister-like low-growth mode of similar fraction AND the ppgpp_conc~growth_rate slope remains significantly negative (coupling persists) -- supports Rival A over H1.

rivals.claim: Rival B - Growth-rate heterogeneity reflects a continuous unimodal heavy-tailed distribution (sampling/numerical artifact), not a true discrete subpopulation; apparent 'low mode' seeds are just the extreme low tail of a single process.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Bimodality coefficient for wildtype/basal is <=0.555 (fails to clear threshold) even with >=40 seeds, and the low tail does not separate into a reproducible discrete cluster via the 2-cluster split -- supports Rival B over H1.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation in this isogenic setting is driven by genuine intracellular kinetic/expression noise (not purely deterministic parameter resampling), such that a true bistable switch, if present in the model's ppGpp/translation kinetics, can manifest as bimodality across seeds.

Whether the simulator implements an actual bistable stringent-response switch mechanism (vs. only smooth unimodal noise) is not resolvable a priori; if wildtype/basal comes back strictly unimodal despite n>=40 seeds, this is treated as evidence against H1 (Rival B) rather than an instrument failure, per objection r1.2.

relA deletion is assumed to leave baseline growth machinery (ribosome synthesis capacity, translation rates) otherwise intact except for loss of (p)ppGpp synthesis via the RelA pathway, isolating the stringent-response-specific contribution rather than confounding with general fitness defects (spoT knockout included as a secondary check on this assumption).

The per-seed terminal/mean growth_rate over 3 generations is a sufficient proxy for 'persister state' in a model without explicit antibiotic-kill dynamics; true phenotypic reversibility and antibiotic-survival (the full Balaban criterion) cannot be directly tested since the instrument has no antibiotic-exposure/kill channel, so this claim is scoped to the pre-exposure phenotypic heterogeneity and its ppGpp dependence only.

objection_ledger.issue: Decision rule requires >=40 seeds per arm to compute a reliable bimodality coefficient, but candidate_designs only specify 8 seeds per perturbation. With n=8, BC is extremely noisy and the 1-10% low-mode fraction claim implies needing at least ~10-20 seeds just to observe a single persister seed reproducibly.

It is unclear whether the simulation engine implements genuine stochastic intracellular switching (e.g., noisy ppGpp bistability) producing a true discrete subpopulation, as opposed to seed-level parameter/initial-condition noise that would always yield a smooth unimodal spread. If the model has no bistable switch mechanism, no amount of seeds will produce real bimodality and the claim is untestable against this instrument.

ppgpp_conc and growth_rate are mechanistically coupled in the model (ppGpp directly suppresses ribosome synthesis/growth), so within the wildtype arm, low-growth seeds will show elevated ppgpp_conc by construction, which does not by itself distinguish stringent-response-driven persistence (H1) from Rival A (generic expression noise that happens to also perturb ppGpp downstream). The relA knockout test is the right interventional move, but the rival-exclusion criterion compares BC and fraction, not whether the SAME low-growth seeds specifically lose their elevated-ppgpp signature post-knockout; recommend tying the knockout falsifier explicitly to the within-arm ppgpp-growth_rate correlation collapsing, not just the bimodality coefficient shifting.

Whether the simulator implements a genuine bistable stringent-response switch (vs smooth unimodal seed noise) remains unresolved a priori; this is now explicitly stated as an auxiliary assumption with a pre-committed fallback (unimodal result = evidence for Rival B). This is acceptable as stated.

hypothesis.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
hypothesis.claim: Bet-hedging via stringent-response "preparedness": in an isogenic population under nutrient-replete (basal) conditions, a subpopulation of cells maintains elevated ppGpp and reduced growth rate even without an external stress cue, and this heterogeneity is adaptive because it is produced by the same RelA/ppGpp machinery that confers faster recovery when the environment later shifts to amino-acid limitation. We test (1) a population-level distributional claim that ppgpp_conc/growth_rate show a bimodal, not unimodal, distribution across isogenic seeds in basal condition; and (2) an interventional claim that high-ppGpp (low growth) seeds recover from amino-acid starvation faster than low-ppGpp seeds, and that a relA knockout erases both the bimodality and the recovery advantage.
hypothesis.h1: In an isogenic E. coli population growing on basal medium, ppGpp concentration and growth rate are bimodally distributed across seeds/lineages (not a single unimodal spread of noise), with a slow-growing/high-ppGpp subpopulation comprising roughly 10-30% of cells; this subpopulation shows a growth-rate recovery advantage (smaller drop and faster rebound in growth_rate) upon a sudden amino-acid-limitation shift, and deleting relA (the ppGpp synthetase) abolishes both the bimodality and the differential recovery, collapsing the population to a single unimodal, slower-recovering phenotype.
hypothesis.h0: ppGpp concentration and growth rate across isogenic basal-condition seeds/lineages are unimodally distributed (simple replicate/intrinsic noise, Sarle's BC <= 0.555), and relA knockout does not change the shape of that distribution nor the mean recovery dynamics (growth_rate trajectory) after an amino-acid-limitation shift relative to wildtype beyond ordinary replicate noise (|Welch t| < 2).

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate channels, per-seed values pooled across replicates under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate values

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel trajectory following an amino_acid_shift timeline event (removal then restoration of an amino acid)
operational_defs.measure: difference in post-shift growth_rate trough depth and time-to-recovery between high-ppGpp-flagged seeds and low-ppGpp-flagged seeds (split at the bimodal boundary), compared via Welch t across seeds

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate channels in relA gene_knockout vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: Welch t of mean recovery growth_rate between relA knockout and wildtype after amino_acid_shift; bimodality_bc of pooled ppgpp_conc in relA knockout vs wildtype

hypothesis.predicted_effect: (1) Distribution shape: pooled ppgpp_conc and growth_rate values across >=8 seeds in wildtype/basal show bimodality coefficient BC > 0.555 (vs unimodal BC ~0.3-0.4 expected under pure noise), with the minor (high-ppGpp/slow-growth) mode comprising ~10-30% of seeds. (2) Differential recovery: after an amino-acid-limitation timeline shift, the high-ppGpp subpopulation shows a smaller growth_rate drop (~20-40% smaller trough-to-baseline deficit) and faster return to baseline growth_rate (effect size: Welch |t| >= 2, ~25% relative advantage) versus the low-ppGpp subpopulation. (3) relA knockout: bimodality coefficient on pooled ppgpp_conc drops to <=0.45 (unimodal) and mean post-shift recovery growth_rate is ~15-25% worse (lower, slower) than wildtype's post-shift recovery growth_rate, Welch |t| >= 2.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1: compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (bimodality_bc) over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values in wildtype/basal; require BC>0.555 to claim bimodal structure. Step 2: Welch t (welch_disconfirm) comparing mean post-shift recovery growth_rate between relA_knockout/aa_shift and wildtype/aa_shift; reject H0 (preparedness is ppGpp-dependent) if |t|>=2 in the direction of relA knockout showing WORSE (lower/slower) recovery than wildtype.
falsifier.refuting_result: Either (a) bimodality_bc <= 0.555 in wildtype/basal (no bimodal substructure, so the 'prepared subpopulation' construct is not supported), or (b) |Welch t| < 2 between relA_knockout/aa_shift and wildtype/aa_shift growth_rate recovery (knockout recovers just as well, meaning the advantage is not RelA/ppGpp-dependent) -- either result refutes H1.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values (paired with welch_disconfirm on growth_rate recovery for relA-dependence)
test.threshold: BC>0.555 required for bimodal claim; paired with welch_disconfirm |t|>=2 for the relA-dependence of recovery

rivals.claim: Pure stochastic noise rival: the ppGpp/growth-rate spread in wildtype/basal is just ordinary gene-expression noise (unimodal, no adaptive structure) and has nothing to do with future stress preparedness.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc on pooled wildtype/basal ppgpp_conc values stays <=0.555 (unimodal), OR bimodality is present but high-ppGpp seeds show NO recovery advantage after the amino-acid shift (|Welch t| < 2 between high/low subpopulation recovery growth_rate).

rivals.claim: Confounded-physiology rival: any apparent 'preparedness' advantage is just because slow-growing cells have more spare ribosome/metabolic capacity for ANY perturbation, not specifically a ppGpp-programmed stress response -- i.e., the effect is a generic growth-rate artifact, not RelA-dependent.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA_knockout/aa_shift mean recovery growth_rate is NOT significantly worse than wildtype/aa_shift (|Welch t| < 2), showing the advantage persists without ppGpp synthesis capacity and is thus growth-rate-intrinsic rather than RelA/ppGpp-specific.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's intrinsic noise model (stochastic gene expression) is rich enough to generate seed-to-seed heterogeneity in ppGpp/growth_rate that is not purely a numerical artifact of the ODE/FBA solver.

Per-seed trajectories are treated as a proxy for distinct 'lineages' or 'cells' in the population; the platform does not simulate explicit multi-cell spatial populations, so bimodality across seeds under identical isogenic parameters is the best available operationalization of population heterogeneity.

The amino_acid_shift timeline (removal then restoration of an amino acid) is an adequate proxy for 'a change' that would reward prepared/slow-growing cells; we are not testing arbitrary other stresses (osmotic, oxidative) which the envelope does not support as mid-run switches.

relA knockout is assumed to be mechanistically simulated (i.e., removes ppGpp synthesis capacity) rather than silently a no-op; this is checked downstream but we proceed on the assumption it has a measurable effect on ppgpp_conc.

Classifying seeds into 'high-ppGpp' vs 'low-ppGpp' subpopulations uses a simple median/bimodal-split threshold on pooled ppgpp_conc values; we do not have a finer single-cell lineage tracker within one seed.

The within-subpopulation recovery comparison (high- vs low-ppGpp seeds) is a secondary, exploratory analysis internal to the wildtype/aa_shift design (not a separately listed candidate_design); the primary falsifier relies on the relA_knockout/aa_shift vs wildtype/aa_shift comparison, which is directly backed by a candidate_design.

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: In a clonal, antibiotic-naive E. coli population simulated as independent isogenic stochastic lineages (seeds), a minority of lineages (~1-10%) spontaneously enter a low-growth, high-ppGpp 'persister-like' state even in benign basal media. This state is phenotypic and RelA-dependent: it requires stochastic RelA/ppGpp induction rather than a fixed genetic change, so a relA knockout should collapse the low-growth tail, while a sufficiency check (clamping ppGpp high without any genetic lesion) should be able to reproduce low growth even in wildtype background, confirming ppGpp as a cause, not merely a correlate.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic wildtype replicates (>=24 seeds, basal media, no antibiotic in the envelope), per-seed growth_rate values show detectable right-skew/bimodal structure (Sarle's BC > 0.555, OR if BC is structurally unreachable in this noise model, a data-driven 2-cluster split via the bimodality test still isolates a low tail) with a low-growth lineage fraction of roughly 1-10%, and that fraction co-occurs with elevated ppgpp_conc (>=2x population median). The state is reversible/phenotypic: relA knockout collapses the tail fraction by >=50% and BC below threshold, AND an independent sufficiency arm (ppgpp_conc clamped to >=2x basal in a wildtype background) reproduces a comparable low-growth shift WITHOUT any genetic knockout -- establishing ppGpp as sufficient, not just necessary, for the dormancy phenotype.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed growth_rate values across isogenic wildtype replicates are unimodal (BC <= 0.555) with no distinguishable low-growth tail, OR if a tail exists, ppgpp_conc does not differ between that tail and the bulk (|t|<2), OR relA knockout fails to collapse the tail, OR clamping ppgpp_conc high in wildtype fails to lower growth_rate relative to basal-clamp control -- any of these indicates growth heterogeneity is either absent, non-ppGpp-linked, or ppGpp is not causally sufficient.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed instantaneous growth_rate (1/h) across >=24 wildtype seeds; low-growth tail defined primarily by the bimodality test's data-driven 2-cluster split (antimode), cross-checked against the fixed 0.5x-median cutoff as a secondary descriptive measure

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed ppgpp_conc (uM); elevated defined as >=2x population median, co-measured in the same seeds as the growth_rate tail

operational_defs.construct: necessity of RelA/ppGpp for the phenotype
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc under relA gene_knockout vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: fraction of low-growth seeds and BC statistic compared between wildtype and relA-knockout backgrounds

operational_defs.construct: sufficiency of ppGpp elevation for the phenotype (addresses r1.2)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate under a direct ppgpp_conc clamp vs a basal clamp, both in wildtype background
operational_defs.measure: Welch t of growth_rate, ppgpp_conc-clamped-high vs ppgpp_conc-clamped-basal, across seeds

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Growth_rate across >=24 WT seeds shows a low-growth cluster (via bimodality_bc 2-cluster split) comprising ~0.05-0.10 of seeds; that cluster's mean ppgpp_conc is >=2-fold bulk mean (Welch |t|>=2). relA knockout: tail fraction and BC drop by >=50% (BC<0.555). Direct ppgpp_conc clamp to 2x basal in WT background lowers mean growth_rate by >=30% relative to a ppgpp_conc clamp at 1x basal (Welch |t|>=2), demonstrating sufficiency. If BC is structurally unreachable (per r1.1, logged as auxiliary assumption), we fall back to reporting the 2-cluster split fraction and tail-vs-bulk ppgpp_conc t-test as the primary decisive statistic.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1: compute Sarle's BC over pooled per-seed growth_rate from wildtype/basal (n>=24); if BC>0.555, bimodal claim holds. Step 2 (irrespective of BC outcome, per r1.1): use the bimodality test's 2-cluster split to define a low-growth group; run Welch's t on ppgpp_conc, low-growth-cluster vs rest; require |t|>=2. Step 3: compare relA-knockout BC/tail-fraction to wildtype; require tail-fraction drop >=50% and BC<0.555 to confirm necessity. Step 4 (addresses r1.2): run Welch's t of growth_rate, ppgpp_conc/high_clamp vs ppgpp_conc/basal_clamp (both wildtype background); require |t|>=2 with high_clamp lower, to confirm sufficiency. H1 requires steps 2-4 all pass; step 1 is reported but not required if r1.1's structural-unreachability caveat applies.
falsifier.refuting_result: The 2-cluster split shows no ppgpp_conc difference (|t|<2) between low-growth and bulk seeds, OR relA knockout fails to collapse the tail (<50% drop, BC stays >0.555), OR the ppgpp_conc high-clamp fails to lower growth_rate relative to basal-clamp (|t|<2) -- any of these refutes the stochastic-ppGpp-dormancy claim as stated.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed growth_rate values, with 2-cluster split used for tail membership regardless of BC threshold outcome
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for wildtype/basal (reported); 2-cluster-split ppgpp_conc Welch |t|>=2 (primary decisive test); BC<0.555 and >=50% tail-fraction drop required for relA-knockout/basal

rivals.claim: Growth heterogeneity is continuous stochastic noise in protein/ribosome expression (extrinsic noise), unrelated to stringent response -- i.e., any 'tail' lineages are not specifically ppGpp-high.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Low-growth cluster seeds show ppgpp_conc indistinguishable from bulk (Welch |t|<2), even if growth_rate itself shows a 2-cluster split or skew.

rivals.claim: Apparent dormancy is a ribosome-supply artifact from rRNA operon dosage limitation, not a ppGpp regulatory switch.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal reproduces or amplifies the low-growth tail to the same degree as wildtype independent of ppGpp elevation, whereas relA knockout (ribosome operons intact) still fails to abolish the tail.

rivals.claim: ppGpp elevation is a correlated downstream consequence of the real driver (e.g., a stochastic translational/metabolic flux switch) and relA is merely a required executor, not the cause -- so removing relA abolishes the readout without ppGpp being causally sufficient.
rivals.distinguishing_result: The ppgpp_conc/high_clamp vs ppgpp_conc/basal_clamp sufficiency arm (addressing r1.2) shows no growth_rate reduction under direct ppGpp elevation (|t|<2) even though relA knockout still collapses the wildtype tail -- dissociating necessity from sufficiency and supporting this rival over the direct-causation claim.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per r1.1: 'seeds' are independent stochastic lineage realizations, not single cells sampled from one simultaneous clonal population; we treat seed-to-seed growth_rate variance as the proxy for subpopulation heterogeneity. We explicitly flag that if the simulator's seed-noise model is structurally unimodal (incapable of generating BC>0.555 regardless of biology), the bimodality_bc test alone cannot confirm H1 -- hence Step 2's 2-cluster-split + ppgpp_conc co-elevation test is treated as the primary decisive channel, with BC reported as a secondary descriptive statistic, not a hard gate.
growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are recorded under steady-state tRNA charging defaults; we do not invoke the kinetic ppGpp module.

Per r1.3: the low-growth tail is defined primarily via the empirical 2-cluster split from the bimodality analysis (data-driven antimode), with the fixed 0.5x-median cutoff retained only as a secondary descriptive cross-check, resolving the threshold ambiguity in favor of the data-driven definition.
The relA/spoT double knockout is approximated by a relA single gene_knockout (closest in-envelope interventional control for necessity).

Per r1.2: sufficiency is tested via the ppgpp_conc clamp perturbation (clamp to 2x basal) in a wildtype background, directly elevating ppGpp without any genetic lesion, as the closest in-envelope manipulation isolating ppGpp's causal role from correlated upstream switches.

A fraction of 1-10% of seeds is treated as a proxy for subpopulation frequency since each seed is an independent stochastic lineage, not a true within-population single-cell measurement; this scope limitation is irreducible given the instrument.
residual_ambiguities: [construct_ambiguity] Should the low-growth tail be defined by the fixed 0.5x-median threshold specified, or by the empirical antimode/valley of a fitted two-component mixture on growth_rate?

objection_ledger.issue: The model (whole-cell/coarse-grained simulator with 'seeds' as lineage realizations) likely does not implement true single-cell stochastic bimodality generation in the sense of discrete persister switching -- 'seeds' are independent stochastic simulation runs, not individual cells within one clonal population observed simultaneously. Claiming a 'subpopulation' and 'bimodal split across isogenic replicates' presumes the simulator's per-seed noise model can produce a genuine bimodal (two-state) distribution rather than just continuous run-to-run variance. If the noise model is unimodal Gaussian-like by construction, BC>0.555 could be structurally unreachable regardless of biology.

The decisive falsifier compares growth_rate/ppgpp_conc patterns between wildtype and relA knockout, and separately checks rrna_operon_knockout. But relA and ppgpp_conc are mechanistically coupled (relA knockout removes the primary ppGpp synthetase), so any collapse of the tail in relA-KO could simply reflect removed ppGpp capacity rather than specifically validating that ppGpp causes the growth bimodality through RelA activation per se -- it doesn't rule out that ppGpp changes are a correlated side-effect of a different upstream stochastic switch (e.g., in translation/metabolic flux) that happens to also require RelA as a downstream executor but isn't 'the' driver. The test does not include a manipulation that elevates ppGpp independent of stochastic noise (e.g., direct ppgpp_conc perturbation) to confirm sufficiency, only one that removes it.

The tail definition 'growth_rate < 0.5x population median' is a fixed, somewhat arbitrary threshold chosen post hoc to match the predicted 1-10% fraction; it is not derived from the bimodality analysis itself (e.g., valley/antimode location from a Gaussian mixture fit). Two reasonable readings of 'subpopulation' are possible: (a) the fixed 0.5x-median cutoff, or (b) the data-driven antimode of the fitted bimodal distribution. These could yield different tail memberships and different ppgpp_conc test outcomes.

all_rounds.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
all_rounds.claim: Reframed as a physiological bet-hedging/cost-benefit trade-off (not a literal subpopulation-heterogeneity model, which this simulator cannot instantiate): a population-wide shift to an elevated, constitutively 'prepared' stringent-response set-point (higher basal ppGpp, ppgpp_conc clamp ~2x basal) sacrifices steady-state growth rate but confers a conditional benefit that only pays off WHEN an amino-acid downshift actually occurs. Critically, the benefit must be absent (net cost only) under a matched timeline where NO shift occurs, which is the operational signature distinguishing a genuine conditional/anticipatory benefit from a generically more shift-robust physiology.
all_rounds.h1: Across seeds, the ppgpp_clamp_2x strain shows (i) lower growth_rate than wildtype under a no-shift control timeline (pure cost, no compensating benefit when the environment never changes), AND (ii) a significantly smaller fractional growth_rate drop (and higher division_rate) than wildtype specifically in the generations following an amino_acid_shift, such that the clamp's relative performance (clamp-minus-wildtype on fractional growth drop) is significantly more favorable in the shift timeline than in the no-shift timeline — i.e. the benefit is conditional on the shift occurring, not a context-independent robustness effect.
all_rounds.h0: Elevated basal ppGpp is purely costly with no conditional benefit: the clamp's fractional growth_rate drop (relative to wildtype) is the same or worse in the shift timeline as in the no-shift timeline, i.e. any apparent post-shift resilience is not specific to the shift event (a generic effect, measurement artifact, or floor/ceiling effect of lower baseline growth).

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc clamp level sustained throughout the run
operational_defs.measure: ppgpp_conc channel (uM), mean over pre-shift window, target vs reference

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel under the no-shift control timeline
operational_defs.measure: mean growth_rate (1/h) across full run, ppgpp_clamp_2x/no_shift vs wildtype/no_shift

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate channels in the 1-2 generations immediately after the amino_acid_shift event
operational_defs.measure: fractional change in growth_rate (post minus pre, normalized by pre) and division_rate fraction, clamp vs wildtype, WITHIN the shift timeline only

operational_defs.observable: difference between (clamp-vs-wildtype fractional growth drop) measured in the shift timeline versus the SAME contrast measured in the no-shift timeline
operational_defs.measure: interaction-style comparison: delta_shift = (clamp_drop - wt_drop)|shift_timeline; delta_noshift = (clamp_drop - wt_drop)|noshift_timeline; benefit is conditional if delta_shift is significantly more negative (favorable) than delta_noshift

all_rounds.predicted_effect: No-shift timeline: ppgpp_clamp_2x growth_rate ~15-25% lower than wildtype (fold ~0.75-0.85x), a pure unconditional cost. Shift timeline: wildtype shows ~40-60% fractional growth_rate collapse post-shift; ppgpp_clamp_2x shows only ~15-25% collapse (division_rate stays >=0.9 vs wildtype <=0.7). The conditionality signature: the clamp-vs-wildtype advantage on fractional drop should be at least ~2x larger in magnitude in the shift timeline than in the no-shift timeline (where it should be ~0, since there is no shift to buffer).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of fractional growth_rate drop (clamp vs wildtype) computed separately in the shift timeline and the no-shift timeline; H1 requires |welch_t|>=2 favoring clamp (smaller drop) in the shift timeline AND |welch_t|<2 (no significant difference, i.e. pure cost with no spurious benefit) between clamp and wildtype fractional change in the no-shift timeline
falsifier.refuting_result: Either the shift-timeline contrast fails |welch_t|>=2 in the predicted direction, OR the no-shift-timeline contrast ALSO shows |welch_t|>=2 favoring the clamp (meaning the clamp is generically more robust rather than conditionally benefiting from the shift) — either outcome means the conditional bet-hedging signature is absent

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: shift timeline: |t|>=2 clamp<wildtype drop; no-shift timeline: |t|<2 (no difference)

rivals.claim: Elevated ppGpp is purely a growth-rate tax with no anticipatory benefit at all; the apparent post-shift resilience is a floor/ceiling artifact of a smaller absolute baseline leaving less room to fall, not a real preparedness mechanism, and the effect (if any) will show up equally in the no-shift timeline.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the no-shift timeline contrast will ALSO show a significant welch_t favoring the clamp (lower variance/less relative decline even with no perturbation), collapsing the predicted shift-specific interaction — i.e. delta_shift and delta_noshift will not differ.

rivals.claim: Any resilience benefit is mediated by RelA-driven ppGpp INDUCTION kinetics during the shift itself (a dynamic stress response), not by the pre-existing steady elevated ppGpp level; the clamp's apparent benefit is confounded by blocking/replacing normal RelA induction dynamics with a fixed level that happens to be closer to the post-shift optimum.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout under the SAME shift timeline (discriminating interventional control) removes RelA-mediated induction entirely; if relA-KO collapses as badly or worse than wildtype under the shift while ppgpp_clamp_2x still outperforms both, this supports the preparedness (static set-point) claim; if ppgpp_clamp_2x's advantage over wildtype vanishes once compared against relA-KO's induction-free baseline (i.e. clamp tracks relA-KO rather than beating it), this implicates lost/altered induction dynamics rather than a genuine static-preparedness benefit.

auxiliary_assumptions: The ppgpp_conc clamp at 2x basal applied population-wide is used as an operational proxy for a 'prepared/stringent' physiological set-point; this tests whether a shifted mean set-point yields a conditional benefit, NOT whether genuine within-population heterogeneity (variance across lineages) is adaptive under unpredictability — the simulator cannot instantiate mixed-subpopulation clamps within a single run, so the heterogeneity-specific bet-hedging claim is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE and the claim is reframed accordingly (resolves r1.1).

The no-shift control timeline ('0 minimal' only, no downshift event) run for matched seeds/generations is treated as the correct null environment for isolating the unconditional cost of the clamp, distinguishing a context-independent robustness effect from a genuinely conditional (shift-specific) benefit (resolves r1.2's core concern about needing a no-shift comparison, within the single deterministic-timeline envelope the platform supports).

Growth_rate and division_rate are acknowledged as mechanistically coupled; division_rate is now treated as a SECONDARY/corroborating readout only, not a co-equal independent confirmation requirement — the primary decisive test rests on the growth_rate fractional-drop interaction between shift and no-shift timelines (resolves r1.3: if division_rate disagrees with growth_rate, the hypothesis status is governed by the growth_rate test alone, with the discrepancy noted as a scope caveat on readout coupling).
Kinetic charging elongation model is required to capture ppGpp/RelA dynamics during the shift; steady-state charging would mask induction kinetics of interest.
Seeds (n=6) are isogenic stochastic replicates and the unit of replication for Welch's t; generation-to-generation autocorrelation within a seed is not separately modeled.

The relA knockout control isolates whether resilience depends on dynamic induction vs static elevated ppGpp; it does not fully decouple all pleiotropic effects of relA loss, accepted as a scope limitation of a single-gene KO control.

A single deterministic shift-timing is the only form of 'uncertainty' the envelope supports (no stochastic/variable shift-onset perturbation exists); the conditionality test (shift vs no-shift) is the closest feasible proxy for 'does preparedness only pay off when change occurs,' not a full test of benefit-under-unpredictable-timing.

objection_ledger.issue: The claim is framed as a population-level bet-hedging strategy (heterogeneous sub-population of slow/prepared cells coexisting with fast growers, so the population as a whole benefits from variance), but the operationalization is a population-WIDE, homogeneous ppGpp clamp applied uniformly to all cells. This tests 'is constitutively higher ppGpp individually beneficial under a shift' not 'does maintaining a prepared SUBPOPULATION help the population as a whole.' The auxiliary_assumptions section concedes this gap but calling it an 'approximation' does not resolve the conflation — the mechanism of bet-hedging (variance/heterogeneity across lineages buffering an unpredictable environment) is categorically different from a shifted population mean, and the decisive test cannot distinguish 'uniform higher ppGpp is good under this specific predictable shift' from 'heterogeneity is good under an unpredictable shift.'

The decisive test compares a fixed, scheduled amino_acid_shift at generation-matched timeline for both wildtype and clamp. Because the shift timing is deterministic and known to the experimenter (and implicitly 'useful information' the clamp strain doesn't actually have to anticipate), the result cannot distinguish a genuine evolved anticipatory/bet-hedging benefit (which should matter most when shift TIMING is unpredictable or rare) from a trivial effect where elevated steady-state ppGpp simply produces different RelA/charging kinetics that happen to react faster to ANY perturbation, scheduled or not. A single deterministic timeline cannot show the benefit is specifically about coping with unpredictability vs. just being a different, generically more shift-robust physiological setpoint.

The decision rule requires both the fractional growth_rate drop AND division_rate welch_t to pass in the predicted direction, but division_rate and growth_rate are mechanistically tightly coupled in these simulators (division_rate is largely derived from/tracks growth_rate and cell-mass accumulation). Requiring both as independent corroborating evidence risks double-counting a single underlying signal rather than providing two genuinely independent lines of evidence, while not changing the substantive conclusion if one fails but not the other (decision rule does not specify what happens if they disagree).

The claim's framing still invokes 'preparedness for unpredictable change' in the user's question, but the only timeline the envelope supports is a single deterministic, scheduled shift — so the test genuinely cannot speak to whether the benefit depends on the environment being unpredictable (vs. just occurring at all). This is correctly listed as an auxiliary assumption already, so it should not be pressed further as substantive.

hypothesis.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
hypothesis.claim: Reframed, scope-narrowed claim (not a literal subpopulation-heterogeneity model, and not a test of coping with unpredictability per se, since the envelope only supports a scheduled deterministic shift): a population-wide shift to an elevated, constitutively 'prepared' stringent-response set-point (higher basal ppGpp, ppgpp_conc clamp ~2x basal) sacrifices steady-state growth rate but confers a conditional benefit that pays off ONLY WHEN an amino-acid downshift actually occurs. The benefit must be absent (net cost only) under a matched timeline where NO shift occurs \u2014 the operational signature distinguishing a genuine conditional/shift-contingent benefit from a generically more shift-robust physiology. (Claim is explicitly scoped to 'conditional benefit given a shift occurs,' not to coping with unpredictable timing, which this simulator cannot instantiate.)

hypothesis.h0: Elevated basal ppGpp is purely costly with no shift-contingent benefit: the clamp's fractional growth_rate drop (relative to wildtype) is the same or worse in the shift timeline as in the no-shift timeline, i.e. any apparent post-shift resilience is not specific to the shift event (a generic effect, measurement artifact, or floor/ceiling effect of lower baseline growth).

falsifier.refuting_result: Either the shift-timeline contrast fails |welch_t|>=2 in the predicted direction, OR the no-shift-timeline contrast ALSO shows |welch_t|>=2 favoring the clamp (meaning the clamp is generically more robust rather than conditionally benefiting from the shift) — either outcome means the shift-contingent benefit signature is absent

rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the no-shift timeline contrast will ALSO show a significant welch_t favoring the clamp (lower variance/less relative decline even with no perturbation), collapsing the predicted shift-specific interaction — i.e. delta_shift and delta_noshift will not differ.

The no-shift control timeline ('0 minimal' only, no downshift event) run for matched seeds/generations is treated as the correct null environment for isolating the unconditional cost of the clamp, distinguishing a context-independent robustness effect from a genuinely conditional (shift-specific) benefit.

Growth_rate and division_rate are acknowledged as mechanistically coupled; division_rate is treated as a SECONDARY/corroborating readout only, not a co-equal independent confirmation requirement — the primary decisive test rests on the growth_rate fractional-drop interaction between shift and no-shift timelines; a discrepancy with division_rate is noted as a scope caveat on readout coupling, not grounds to block the test.
Kinetic charging elongation model is required to capture ppGpp/RelA dynamics during the shift; steady-state charging would mask induction kinetics of interest.
Seeds (n=6) are isogenic stochastic replicates and the unit of replication for Welch's t; generation-to-generation autocorrelation within a seed is not separately modeled.
