operational_defs.measure: ppgpp_conc channel clamped value vs WT time-averaged ppgpp_conc; near-zero cross-seed CV by construction

hypothesis.predicted_effect: WT heterogeneous population: time-averaged growth_rate >=15% higher and division_rate higher (e.g. 0.95 vs <=0.80) than BOTH clamp arms across 4 amino-acid shift cycles; WT per-seed CV of ppgpp_conc/growth_rate ~0.2-0.4 vs near-zero (<0.05) in clamped arms; the clamped-mean and clamped-low arms should show similar growth deficits to each other (within ~5 percentage points), i.e. mean-matching does NOT rescue fitness, isolating variance as the causal factor.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of time-averaged growth_rate (per-seed values) for ppgpp_conc/clamp_mean vs wildtype/basal, across seeds; reject H1 (variance matters) if |t|<2 (not significantly different) AND effect_pct within +/-5% — i.e. clamp_mean performs as well as WT despite zero variance
falsifier.refuting_result: clamp_mean arm's time-averaged growth_rate and division_rate are statistically indistinguishable from WT (|t|<2, effect_pct<5%), showing mean ppGpp level alone reproduces WT fitness and heterogeneity/variance contributes nothing beyond the mean

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for WT vs clamp_mean to support H1 (variance matters); |t|<2 refutes H1

rivals.claim: Mean-level hypothesis: higher average ppGpp (not variance) drives the downshift-survival advantage; any cell constitutively at WT's mean ppGpp does equally well as heterogeneous WT.
rivals.distinguishing_result: clamp_mean arm matches WT's time-averaged growth_rate and division_rate (|t|<2 vs WT on growth_rate), refuting the variance-specific claim even though clamp_low still underperforms.

rivals.claim: Loss-of-regulon hypothesis: clamping ppGpp (at any fixed level, low or mean) breaks RelA-dependent downstream regulatory programs (not just variance or mean amplitude), so any clamp arm underperforms WT regardless of matched mean — the deficit is an artifact of the clamp perturbation mechanism, not evidence for bet-hedging.
rivals.distinguishing_result: a relA gene_knockout control (which abolishes the ppGpp synthesis burst capacity but is NOT a forced clamp) shows a similarly large growth deficit under amino-acid shifts as clamp_low, suggesting the deficit tracks with loss of inducible stringent response machinery generally, not specifically with removal of variance; this would be reported alongside the clamp comparisons as a mechanism-isolating check.

residual_ambiguities: [construct_ambiguity] Does the simulation environment report single-cell-resolved ppgpp_conc/growth_rate within one population (enabling a true cell-to-cell CV), or only one value per replicate/seed — and if the latter, do you intend CV-across-seeds as the heterogeneity proxy instead?
[proposer_unreadable] round 4

objection_ledger.issue: The claim that 'clamping ppGpp to a single low level' suppresses heterogeneity while leaving everything else (growth capacity, stress resistance, gene regulation downstream of ppGpp) unchanged is a strong ceteris paribus assumption. ppGpp is a master regulator; forcing it low could itself impair the population's ability to survive downshifts for reasons unrelated to bet-hedging (e.g. loss of RelA-independent protective regulon expression), which would produce the predicted result (clamped population does worse) even if stochastic heterogeneity itself contributes nothing to fitness. The design needs to specify how the ppgpp_conc perturbation is held low (constitutive low expression vs relA knockout vs other) and argue why that manipulation selectively removes cell-to-cell variance rather than also removing average 'preparedness' capacity.

A population with uniformly intermediate ppGpp (same mean as the heterogeneous population but zero variance) could in principle show the same time-averaged growth advantage over the fast-clamped population simply because higher mean ppGpp per cell improves downshift survival — with no role for bet-hedging/heterogeneity at all. The current two-arm comparison (heterogeneous WT vs clamped-low) cannot distinguish 'variance helps' from 'mean level helps'; you need a third arm matched on mean ppgpp_conc but with suppressed variance (e.g. via a different knockout/perturbation that homogenizes cells at the WT mean) to isolate the heterogeneity effect.

The channels list a single scalar ppgpp_conc and growth_rate per simulated condition/seed; it is unclear whether 'cell-to-cell CV' is read from single-cell trajectories across many seeds, from an explicit population substructure in the model, or just across replicate runs (which would conflate stochastic noise with heterogeneity). This affects whether the proposed 'per-seed CV' operationalization is actually available on the dial.

It is not fully established that clamping the ppgpp_conc perturbation channel actually forces near-zero cross-seed CV in downstream growth_rate (as opposed to just fixing input ppGpp while stochastic noise elsewhere still produces growth_rate variance). The design asserts this as a predicted outcome rather than a guaranteed instrument behavior.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells growing in the same medium show substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output, operationalized here as ribosome concentration and ppGpp concentration (proxies for expression/translation-capacity state), such that the population displays coefficient of variation (CV) across isogenic replicate seeds well above measurement/numerical noise (~15-30% CV), rather than all cells converging to a single shared value.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic seeds simulated under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and ppgpp_conc) measured at a FIXED matched generation (generation 3, end-of-generation snapshot, no detrending needed since each seed contributes exactly one value at that matched timepoint) shows CV >= 15%, i.e. genetically identical cells do NOT express the same level deterministically -- intrinsic/extrinsic noise produces substantial heterogeneity.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed ribosome_conc (and ppgpp_conc) values under wildtype/basal, sampled at the same fixed matched generation-3 snapshot, are tightly clustered (CV < 5%), consistent with deterministic, noise-free convergence to a single expression level across isogenic cells.

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc values recorded per seed at a FIXED matched generation-3 snapshot (end-of-generation value, identical sampling rule for every seed) under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) across the 8 seeds' generation-3 snapshot values; also pooled-seed bimodality coefficient (BC) on the same snapshot values to check for discrete subpopulations

operational_defs.observable: wildtype perturbation, basal condition, varying only seed (stochastic replicate)
operational_defs.measure: design label wildtype/basal with seeds=8

operational_defs.construct: noise source isolation (rules out deterministic bias from growth-phase drift)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel at the SAME fixed generation-3 snapshot across the same seeds
operational_defs.measure: CV of growth_rate as a covariate check at the identical timepoint; low growth_rate CV with high ribosome_conc CV argues for expression-specific noise rather than trivial physiological/trajectory desynchronization (this removes the need for detrending across the full 3-generation trajectory -- by fixing the sampling point, cell-cycle-phase drift cannot masquerade as noise)

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Ribosome_conc CV across 8 isogenic seeds at the fixed generation-3 snapshot is >= 15% (point estimate ~20-25%), and ppgpp_conc CV >= 20% (alarmone pulses are noisier), both well above a 5% noise floor (growth_rate CV at the same snapshot expected < 10%); pooled distribution is expected unimodal (not bimodal, BC < 0.555) -- heterogeneity is continuous noise, not discrete subpopulations.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of ribosome_conc across all 8 seeds using ONLY the fixed generation-3 end-of-generation snapshot value per seed (one value per seed, no averaging across generations, no detrending needed). Run power_mde to confirm n=8 is powered to detect a 15% CV effect above a 5% noise floor (i.e. MDE at n=8 is below 15%). If powered, reject H1 (accept H0) if observed snapshot CV < 5%; H1 holds if CV >= 15%. Values between 5-15% are inconclusive and reported as such (not claimed as support for either H1 or H0).
falsifier.refuting_result: CV of ribosome_conc at the fixed generation-3 snapshot across seeds < 5% (cells are near-identical, indistinguishable from the noise floor), refuting substantial heterogeneity.

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation_and_min_detectable_effect
test.threshold: CV >= 15% with MDE at n=8 below 15% (design powered to detect the claimed effect); reject H1 if observed CV < 5%

rivals.claim: Observed spread is purely numerical/integration noise from the ODE/FBA solver, not biological stochasticity -- a 'noise floor' artifact.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If an rrna_operon_knockout control (which removes ribosome-capacity buffering) shows the SAME CV at the matched generation-3 snapshot as wildtype, that supports a floor-noise artifact; if KO sharply increases CV or shifts the mean, it supports biological amplification of noise through the translation/ribosome allocation network rather than solver artifact.

rivals.claim: Variability is not intrinsic expression noise but reflects a few cells being in a qualitatively different metabolic/growth state (discrete subpopulation, e.g. persister-like), not continuous single-population noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Bimodality coefficient (BC) on the pooled generation-3 snapshot ribosome_conc values > 0.555 would indicate two discrete subpopulations rather than continuous noise around one mean.

objection_ledger.issue: The primary slope_ci test regresses log(CV) on log(mean) with only n=4 condition-level points (one per design), which gives very low statistical power to get a CI that excludes zero even if the true relationship is negative -- making 'fail to exclude zero' a weak/ambiguous falsifier rather than a crisp one.

The CV computation requires a stated time-window/detrending procedure to separate real expression noise from deterministic cell-cycle or growth-phase trends across the 3 generations; without specifying that the per-seed CV is computed after removing such trends (or at a fixed matched time point), differences in CV could reflect trajectory-shape differences rather than stochastic noise.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing under identical (basal) conditions exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variation in gene expression output — operationalized as ribosome concentration and ppGpp concentration — rather than expressing genes at a uniform level; this intrinsic noise produces a coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds of roughly 15-30% in ribosome_conc, far exceeding the ~2-5% CV expected from pure replicate/measurement noise alone.
hypothesis.h1: Across >=8 isogenic replicate seeds under the same static condition (basal), the per-seed distribution of steady-state ribosome_conc (and separately ppgpp_conc) has CV >= 15%, i.e. genetically identical cells do NOT express these gene products at the same level — expression is heterogeneous rather than uniform.
hypothesis.h0: The per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and ppgpp_conc) under wildtype/basal is tight, with CV <= 5%, consistent with cells expressing the gene product at essentially the same level (seed-to-seed spread attributable only to simulator/numerical noise, not biological heterogeneity).

operational_defs.construct: gene expression level (single-cell readout of translation-capacity / stringent-response gene products)
operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc channels recorded per seed at steady state
operational_defs.measure: per-seed terminal (or late-window-averaged) value of ribosome_conc (uM) and ppgpp_conc (uM) pooled across >=8 seeds

operational_defs.observable: spread of per-seed ribosome_conc / ppgpp_conc values within one condition
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) computed across seeds; also checked for bimodality via Sarle's BC on pooled values

operational_defs.construct: whether the heterogeneity is gene-intrinsic (stringent-response/RelA-driven) versus merely a byproduct of shared growth-rate fluctuations (extrinsic/collinear noise)
operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc / ppgpp_conc spread in wildtype/basal versus in relA gene_knockout/basal, where RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis is abolished
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of mean ppgpp_conc (and ribosome_conc) between wildtype/basal and relA gene_knockout/basal across seeds, plus CV comparison between the two designs

operational_defs.construct: whether residual ppGpp heterogeneity after RelA removal reflects a feedback/clamped-abundance rival rather than true stochastic synthesis noise
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc spread in wildtype/basal versus in a ppgpp_conc clamp design (ppGpp held at 1x basal, removing any feedback-driven fluctuation around a set point) across seeds
operational_defs.measure: CV(ppgpp_conc) in the clamp design compared against CV in wildtype/basal and in relA knockout/basal; welch_t of clamp vs wildtype as a secondary check

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: isogenic replicate seeds show substantial dispersion, not uniformity. Magnitude: CV(ribosome_conc) across >=8 seeds in wildtype/basal is predicted to be ~15-30% (vs an assumed ~2-5% baseline numerical/replicate noise floor, e.g. seen in dry_mass), and CV(ppgpp_conc) is predicted to be even larger, ~25-40%, reflecting the alarmone's pulsatile stringent-response dynamics. The distribution is predicted to remain unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555) at this modest seed count. relA knockout is predicted to COLLAPSE ppgpp_conc CV toward the noise floor (<=8%), supporting gene-intrinsic (RelA-synthesis) noise over a pure extrinsic/growth-coupled rival. The ppgpp_conc clamp design (held at 1x basal, which removes any feedback loop around a regulatory set-point without deleting RelA) is predicted to ALSO collapse ppgpp_conc CV to <=8%, similar to the relA knockout; if instead the clamp design still shows CV>=15%, that would indicate the measured 'ppgpp_conc' spread is not being driven by synthesis/feedback dynamics at all (e.g. it is a downstream readout artifact), refuting the feedback-noise rival's alternative account and reinforcing that RelA-driven synthesis (not clamp-breakable feedback) is the dominant noise source.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1: compute CV(ppgpp_conc) across seeds for wildtype/basal; H1 requires CV>=15%; refute if CV<=5%. Step 2 (interventional control vs extrinsic-noise rival): Welch t of ppgpp_conc, target=wildtype/basal vs reference=relA gene_knockout/basal, across seeds; reject H0 (support gene-intrinsic/RelA-driven heterogeneity) if |welch_t|>=2 AND CV(ppgpp_conc) in the relA knockout drops below 8%. Step 3 (feedback-rival control): compare CV(ppgpp_conc) in ppgpp_conc-clamp/basal (clamped at 1x) against wildtype/basal; if the clamp ALSO collapses CV to <=8%, this corroborates the RelA-synthesis account over a feedback-loop rival; if clamp CV remains >=15% despite the fixed set-point, the feedback rival is supported instead and the RelA-specific mechanistic claim is weakened. The primary falsifying test remains Step 1+2 on ppgpp_conc; Step 3 is the discriminator for the newly-wired feedback rival.
falsifier.refuting_result: If CV(ppgpp_conc) in wildtype/basal is <=5%, isogenic cells express ppGpp essentially identically, refuting H1 in favor of H0. Separately, if relA knockout fails to narrow the spread (CV remains >=15%) or |welch_t|<2, the RelA-dependent mechanism is refuted even though generic heterogeneity may persist. If the ppgpp_conc clamp fails to collapse CV (stays >=15%) while relA KO does collapse it, the feedback rival is excluded in favor of synthesis-noise; if BOTH relA KO and clamp fail to collapse CV, neither RelA synthesis nor feedback explains the spread, undermining the gene-intrinsic mechanistic claim entirely.

test.statistic: welch_t (ppgpp_conc, wildtype/basal vs relA gene_knockout/basal) and per-seed CV (SD/mean) in wildtype/basal, relA gene_knockout/basal, and ppgpp_conc-clamp/basal
test.threshold: CV(wildtype/basal)>=15% supports H1; CV<=5% refutes H1; |welch_t|>=2 AND CV(relA KO)<=8% supports RelA-driven mechanism; CV(clamp)<=8% corroborates synthesis-driven (non-feedback) noise, while CV(clamp)>=15% supports the feedback rival instead

rivals.claim: Apparent variation is purely numerical/integration noise from the stochastic simulator, not biologically meaningful expression heterogeneity (the model converges to a near-deterministic attractor and any spread is an artifact).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(ribosome_conc) and CV(ppgpp_conc) in wildtype/basal are both <=5% (matching a near-deterministic noise floor like dry_mass), this rival is supported and the heterogeneity claim fails.

rivals.claim: Variation is growth-rate-extrinsic: seed-to-seed fluctuations in growth_rate (not gene-intrinsic expression noise) drive correlated spread in ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc, since both are physiologically coupled to growth rate.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA gene_knockout/basal (which removes RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis without directly fixing growth_rate) STILL shows ppgpp_conc CV >=15% despite RelA being gone, that implicates a shared extrinsic driver rather than RelA-specific intrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity reflects a ppGpp regulatory feedback loop (set-point fluctuation via RelA/SpoT cross-talk) rather than raw stochastic synthesis/degradation noise -- i.e. the spread is a property of the feedback dynamics, not of RelA abundance noise per se, so deleting RelA (which also breaks the feedback) is not a clean test.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If the ppgpp_conc clamp/basal design (which fixes the set-point directly, independent of deleting RelA) STILL shows CV(ppgpp_conc)>=15%, that means clamping the mean does not remove the spread -- implicating a mechanism downstream of or parallel to the feedback loop, supporting this rival over the simple RelA-synthesis-noise account.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is bimodal/switch-like (a bistable stringent-response ON/OFF state) rather than continuous unimodal variation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Sarle's BC > 0.555 on pooled ppgpp_conc or ribosome_conc values across wildtype/basal seeds, the population is better described as two discrete expression states, refuting the continuous-heterogeneity framing of H1 as stated.

objection_ledger.issue: The falsifier's decision_rule is self-contradictory: it first says a Welch t-test comparing per-seed rela_conc to per-seed ribosome_conc is 'not the right pairing,' then specifies that exact test as the threshold condition (|t|>=2 on 'rela_conc vs ribosome_conc (z-scored/CV-normalized)'). As written, there is no single well-defined statistic that would actually falsify H1versus H0 is never crisply computed from the two actual CV estimates (no CV confidence intervals, no bootstrap, no sample-size justification for seeds=8 to distinguish a 1.5x vs 3-5x CV ratio).

Rival 1 (growth-rate-driven extrinsic noise) is correctly identified, but the design does not include an interventional control that breaks the coupling between growth_rate and rela_conc/ribosome_conc. rrna_operon_knockout perturbs ribosome capacity and will itself shift growth_rate, so comparing CVs there still leaves growth-rate and ribosome/RelA concentrations collinear — it doesn't isolate gene-intrinsic noise from growth-rate-extrinsic noise. A cleaner interventional control (e.g., a condition/perturbation that fixes or clamps growth_rate while varying ppGpp/RelA, or vice versa) is needed to attribute noise differences to regulatory class rather than shared growth-rate fluctuations.

The ppGpp-feedback rival (relA's own regulatory loop suppressing/amplifying its noise independent of abundance) is described with a clamp design (ppgpp_conc perturbation, row 5), but that design and its distinguishing_result are never incorporated into the actual decision_rule/falsifier -- only the extrinsic-noise rival's off-axis control (pykA) is wired into the primary slope_ci test. As written, the feedback rival is asserted to be excluded by argument but has no corresponding statistic in the falsifier.

The CV computation requires a stated time-window/detrending procedure to separate real expression noise from deterministic cell-cycle or growth-phase trends across the 3 generations; without specifying that the per-seed CV is computed after removing such trends (or at a fixed matched time point), differences in CV could reflect trajectory-shape differences rather than stochastic noise.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: In an isogenic E. coli population growing in identical (basal) medium, gene expression is intrinsically noisy: ribosome/tRNA-charging machinery varies substantially across individual cells (seeds) even though every cell carries the same genotype, producing a per-seed distribution with CV well above the power-based noise floor rather than a single sharp value. This noise is not a RelA/ppGpp-coupling artifact.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and separately fraction_trna_charged) shows substantial cell-to-cell variability: CV >= 15% across 8 seeds, exceeding the power_mde-estimated minimum-detectable-effect floor for that channel/n, consistent with genuine intrinsic noise rather than sampling artifact. This spread persists (mean is NOT significantly shifted, |welch_t|<2) when the RelA-ppGpp global-coupling driver is removed by relA knockout, i.e. the knockout does not simply reduce variance by crashing the mean to a degenerate low value.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed values of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) under wildtype/basal are effectively constant across isogenic replicates: CV < 15%, i.e. observed spread is within the power_mde noise floor and not biologically meaningful heterogeneity. Separately/alternatively: relA knockout produces a significant mean shift in ribosome_conc relative to wildtype (|welch_t| >= 2), indicating that the wildtype spread (if any) was entangled with RelA/ppGpp-driven mean physiology rather than reflecting intrinsic noise isolable from the coupling driver.

operational_defs.construct: gene expression level of an identical gene across isogenic cells
operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc (uM) and fraction_trna_charged (frac) recorded per seed at steady state under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: per-seed terminal-generation value; compute mean, SD, and CV = SD/mean across the 8-seed set

operational_defs.observable: spread of per-seed channel values relative to the power_mde minimum detectable effect at n=8
operational_defs.measure: CV across seeds compared against min-detectable-CV from power_mde; heterogeneity is 'real' if observed CV clearly exceeds (>~2x) the MDE floor

operational_defs.construct: intrinsic stochastic noise vs shared global physiological driver (growth-rate/ppGpp coupling)
operational_defs.observable: mean ribosome_conc under wildtype/basal vs under relA gene_knockout/basal -- a background perturbation that abolishes RelA-driven ppGpp synthesis, breaking the shared regulatory driver, WITHOUT changing which gene/channel is measured
operational_defs.measure: Welch's t-test (single executable test_id welch_disconfirm) on per-seed ribosome_conc, relA-KO vs wildtype, across matched 8 seeds; heterogeneity is attributed to intrinsic noise (surviving as H1) if |welch_t| < 2, i.e. the KO does not shift the MEAN significantly -- meaning any residual spread in the KO cannot be dismissed as a side-effect of a collapsed/shifted mean

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: per-seed ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged values scatter around a common mean rather than collapsing to a point estimate. Magnitude: CV(ribosome_conc) across 8 wildtype/basal seeds >= 15% (vs an MDE floor ~5-8% at n=8), CV(fraction_trna_charged) >= 10%. Single executable attribution test: Welch's t comparing per-seed ribosome_conc means, relA-knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal, with |welch_t| < 2 expected (no significant mean shift) -- this is the ONE test_id (welch_disconfirm) that adjudicates the hypothesis; no bootstrap or secondary CI test is invoked.

falsifier.decision_rule: Single executable test: Welch's t-test (welch_disconfirm) comparing per-seed ribosome_conc values, relA-knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal, across the matched 8 seeds. Reject H1 (i.e. the wildtype spread is RelA/ppGpp-coupling-driven, not intrinsic) if |welch_t| >= 2, since that indicates relA knockout significantly shifts the mean ribosome_conc -- meaning the wildtype distribution was entangled with the RelA-driven mean/coupling rather than reflecting a mean-independent intrinsic noise source. H1 survives only if |welch_t| < 2.
falsifier.refuting_result: Welch's t-test on ribosome_conc, relA-knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal, yields |welch_t| >= 2 (e.g. t=3.1, p<0.05), demonstrating relA knockout significantly shifts mean ribosome_conc relative to wildtype -- i.e. the RelA/ppGpp axis is a mean-level driver entangled with the measured channel, undermining the claim that the observed wildtype cell-to-cell spread is attributable to a RelA-independent intrinsic noise source.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed ribosome_conc (relA-knockout vs wildtype)
test.threshold: |welch_t| < 2 required to retain H1 (no significant mean shift); |welch_t| >= 2 refutes H1

rivals.claim: Rival A (global regulatory coupling, not intrinsic noise): Apparent cell-to-cell variability in ribosome_conc is driven by shared stochastic fluctuations propagating through the RelA/ppGpp-ribosome regulatory axis (a single coupled global driver), not independent per-gene intrinsic stochasticity -- so removing RelA-driven ppGpp synthesis should shift the mean ribosome_conc significantly, since the WT distribution's center itself depended on the coupling.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under relA gene_knockout/basal (same seeds/generations as wildtype), Welch's t on ribosome_conc (KO vs wildtype) gives |welch_t| >= 2 -- this is the refuting_result above and directly supports Rival A over intrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Rival B (non-equilibration artifact): Variability is an artifact of too few generations (transient/non-equilibrated runs) rather than a steady-state population property; running longer should shrink CV toward zero as cells converge to the same attractor.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If increasing generations from 3 to 4 under wildtype/basal substantially shrinks CV(ribosome_conc) toward the MDE floor (rather than CV staying roughly flat across the two generation counts), this supports Rival B (non-equilibration) over genuine steady-state heterogeneity.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seeds in this simulator instantiate independent stochastic trajectories that are the intended proxy for isogenic single-cell replicates; cross-seed spread at matched generation is interpretable as cell-to-cell variability.

ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged are valid proxies for 'gene expression level' at steady-state charging; under kinetic charging this would need ribosomal-protein counts instead, but this study uses steady-state charging throughout.

The simulator's intrinsic noise model (if any) is the mechanism of interest; the platform cannot distinguish deterministic chaos from true stochastic noise, so this distinction is left as an acknowledged scope caveat rather than something the test resolves.
Terminal-generation value per seed is a reasonable summary of that seed's expression level; we are not modeling within-seed temporal fluctuation here.

relA gene_knockout is assumed to meaningfully reduce/abolish RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis in this simulator's gene-knockout implementation (whether this specific KO is mechanistically simulated in sufficient depth is checked downstream), making it the best available single-perturbation interventional control within the validated envelope.

The adjudicating test is deliberately a single Welch's t-test on the MEAN (not a CV-ratio or bootstrap test), because the platform's five named executable test_ids do not include a bootstrap-CI-on-CV-ratio procedure; CV magnitude (existence of heterogeneity) is reported descriptively against the power_mde floor but is not part of the falsifier's pass/fail gate, avoiding any outruns_instrument risk.

A non-significant mean shift (|welch_t|<2) under relA knockout is treated as sufficient evidence that the wildtype spread is not an artifact of RelA-driven mean-level coupling; this does not itself prove the spread is 'intrinsic' in a deeper biophysical sense, only that it is not explained by the specific RelA-mediated mean shift this design can detect -- a scope limitation we accept.

objection_ledger.issue: The falsifier's decision rule has two conjunctive/disjunctive conditions (Welch t on CV comparison AND/OR a 3-point log-log slope regression) but with only 3 x-values (wildtype, gene_knockout, rrna_operon_knockout) the 'slope CI' is fit on essentially 3 condition-level means (even with 6-8 seeds each, the independent x-points for the regression are only 3), making a stable, well-powered slope CI estimate questionable. It's unclear whether the slope test is meant to be decisive on its own or merely supplementary to the pairwise CV comparison.

The extrinsic-noise rival's distinguishing result is framed as 'CV(rela_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc) highly correlated across seeds' vs 'abundance-dependent divergence' -- but relA and ribosomal proteins are both coupled via growth_rate/ppGpp physiology (relA governs ppGpp which governs ribosome synthesis), so these two channels are mechanistically coupled, not independent. A correlation/divergence contest between two coupled channels cannot cleanly attribute the result to abundance-scaling vs shared global driver; you need an intervention that decouples them (e.g., compare CV scaling using a gene unrelated to the ppGpp/ribosome regulon, or hold growth_rate fixed via condition while varying only gene identity) to exclude the extrinsic/global-noise rival.

The design compares CV(rela_conc) vs CV(ribosome_conc) directly, but these are two different genes with potentially different intrinsic bursting kinetics, mRNA half-lives, and regulatory architectures -- the 'burstiness/architecture' rival is listed but the proposed falsifier (a plain CV comparison between the two channels) cannot distinguish 'low abundance causes noise' from 'relA-specific feedback/bursting causes noise' because abundance and architecture are confounded in this single pair. The relA knockout control described in the rival section is not actually included in candidate_designs' decision rule -- it's mentioned narratively but the falsifier/decision_rule only uses the wildtype CV comparison. An interventional design (e.g., comparing CV before/after perturbing only copy number, holding architecture fixed, or vice versa) is needed to attribute the noise difference to abundance per se rather than gene identity.

The decision_rule and refuting_result still conflate two different tests without specifying which one is authoritative: the primary bootstrap CI test on the CV ratio, and a secondary Welch t-test on z-scored ribosome_conc/growth_rate between wildtype and relA_knockout. The refuting_result says EITHER condition refutes, but the test block only names one test_id (welch_disconfirm) with one threshold field that bundles both conditions as text, not as an executable rule. It's not specified how the bootstrap (seeds=8, 1000 resamples) will actually be computed/reported given the five named test_ids in the envelope -- the auxiliary_assumptions admits bootstrap 'is not one of the five named test_ids' and must be hoped for as available. This is edging toward outruns_instrument.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing under identical (wildtype/basal) conditions exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output, operationalized as the per-seed (replicate) spread of a representative expression-linked channel (fraction_trna_charged, as a proxy for translational/expression state) and ribosome_conc (active ribosome concentration, a bulk proxy for expression capacity), such that the coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds is substantial (CV >= 15%) rather than near-zero, i.e. cells do NOT express genes at identical levels despite identical genotype and environment.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate simulations (same genotype, same wildtype/basal condition, differing only in stochastic seed), per-seed values of ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged show a coefficient of variation (CV) >= 15%, i.e. non-trivial intrinsic expression noise exists even without any genetic or environmental perturbation.
drafts.h0: Per-seed CV of ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged across isogenic wildtype/basal replicates is small (CV < 15%, near measurement/numerical noise floor), i.e. gene expression level is effectively deterministic/identical across genetically identical cells in the same environment.

Distribution shape: unimodal but right- or left-skewed, not perfectly symmetric; bimodality coefficient (BC) expected < 0.555 (no discrete subpopulations under plain wildtype, ruling out bistable switching as the noise source).

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV = SD/mean of per-seed ribosome_conc values across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal (self-comparison across the seed ensemble, since H1 concerns within-design spread, not a between-design mean shift); treat CV>=15% as support for H1 and CV<5% as support for H0. rivals.claim: Apparent variability is mostly extrinsic/environmental microheterogeneity (e.g. slight differences in nutrient draw or division timing across seeds) rather than intrinsic stochastic gene expression noise — a bursty transcription/translation process is not actually the driver.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If variability were purely extrinsic (environment-driven), clamping a key regulatory input (e.g. ppgpp_conc clamped to a fixed multiple of basal, removing stringent-response feedback noise) should NOT reduce the CV of ribosome_conc/fraction_trna_charged much, since the extrinsic driver is unrelated to ppGpp; if instead CV collapses substantially under the ppgpp_conc clamp, that supports ppGpp-mediated (regulatory/intrinsic) noise amplification rather than pure extrinsic microheterogeneity.

rivals.claim: Any observed spread across seeds is a numerical/simulator artifact (solver stochasticity, discretization noise) rather than biologically meaningful cell-to-cell variability, and would appear identically even for a channel with no real biological stochastic process.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Compare CV of ribosome_conc (expected biologically noisy) against CV of a channel expected to be tightly constrained by FBA/metabolic stoichiometry such as dry_mass or fba_objective in the same wildtype/basal seed ensemble; if dry_mass/fba_objective show comparably large CV, that points to generic numerical noise rather than expression-specific stochasticity (this comparison is descriptive context, not the primary falsifier).

auxiliary_assumptions: Within-design seed-to-seed spread in this simulator is intended to represent biologically meaningful stochastic variability (intrinsic + modeled extrinsic noise sources), not pure solver artifact — the rival about numerical artifact is addressed only descriptively (dry_mass/fba_objective comparison), since the simulator's noise-generation mechanism cannot be fully decomposed into intrinsic vs extrinsic vs numerical sources from summary channels alone.

fraction_trna_charged under steady-state charging is broadcast from 20 per-amino-acid values over 86 columns; we average the per-seed values rather than treating all 86 as independent to avoid pseudo-replication inflating apparent variance.
3 generations is sufficient for the ribosome/charging state to reach a representative steady-state-like distribution per seed without confounding early-transient effects with steady noise.
The relA knockout is used as an interventional control to test whether ppGpp-synthesis-dependent stringent response contributes to baseline noise, not to claim relA KO eliminates all intrinsic noise.

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: positive, nonzero biological variability. Magnitude: between-seed CV of ppgpp_conc >= 0.20 (20%) at generation 3-4 under wildtype/basal with seeds=8; fraction_trna_charged CV >= 0.10 (tighter due to homeostatic buffering); ribosome_conc CV >= 0.10, corroborating broad-based noise rather than a single-channel artifact.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed CV of ppgpp_conc across seeds=8 at generation 4 under wildtype/basal (self-reference, single condition, no target/reference contrast needed for a distributional claim); treat the population as homogeneous (H0) if CV < 0.20. Secondarily, run power_mde to confirm n=8 seeds can detect a CV effect of this size against sampling noise before accepting H0.
falsifier.refuting_result: Per-seed CV of ppgpp_conc < 0.20 (e.g., CV ~0.05) with power_mde confirming n=8 is adequately powered to detect a 0.20 CV effect -- indicating isogenic cells express this gene product at essentially the same level, refuting H1.

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation + min_detectable_effect
test.threshold: CV >= 0.20 to accept H1; if CV < 0.20 AND MDE at n=8 is <= 0.20 (i.e. adequately powered), accept H0

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic homeostasis): ppGpp and tRNA charging are tightly homeostatically controlled by negative feedback (RelA/SpoT regulation), so apparent seed-to-seed spread is mostly measurement/numerical noise, not genuine expression stochasticity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A rela gene_knockout (relA_KO/basal) that removes the stringent-response feedback loop would be predicted by Rival A to REDUCE CV further (less regulatory machinery that could itself be a noise source) or leave CV unchanged if homeostasis was never the source; if instead CV of ppgpp_conc INCREASES or stays similarly high in relA_KO vs wildtype, that undermines a pure feedback-control explanation and supports genuine upstream stochastic noise propagating through other synthesis routes (e.g., SpoT).

rivals.claim: Rival B (extrinsic/environmental noise only): apparent variability arises purely from residual environmental/initialization differences between seeds (e.g., slightly different initial metabolite pools), not from intrinsic stochastic gene expression per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV scales similarly across multiple unrelated channels (ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged, ribosome_conc) in a correlated way driven by a shared initial-condition artifact, variability would track a single upstream variable; intrinsic noise predicts partially independent (decorrelated) fluctuations across these channels seed-by-seed, which the bimodality/CV comparison across channels can help distinguish qualitatively, though full decorrelation testing is a scope caveat (see auxiliary assumptions).

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed endpoint values at matched generation (gen 4) are a valid snapshot of steady-state-ish expression level, not transient startup artifacts.

Seeds encode independent stochastic realizations of the same genotype/environment (isogenic by construction in the simulator), so between-seed spread is attributable to intrinsic + simulator stochastic noise, not genotype differences.

The simulator's numerical/integration noise floor is well below 20% CV, so a CV>=0.20 reading is not an artifact of solver tolerance; this is a scope caveat the simulator itself cannot fully adjudicate (deterministic chaos vs genuine stochastic noise) and is noted rather than resolved here.

ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged are adequate proxies for 'gene expression level' broadly, since the instrument does not expose single-gene mRNA/protein copy-number noise directly in this run; this is an operationalization choice, not a claim that ppGpp IS 'the gene'.

relA knockout removes RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis but leaves SpoT-mediated synthesis/hydrolysis intact, so relA_KO is an imperfect but feasible single-gene interventional control within the envelope.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: In an isogenic E. coli population under constant basal conditions, cell-to-cell stochastic variation in gene expression produces substantial heterogeneity in protein/mRNA-linked readouts across seeds, even though all cells share identical genotype and environment — i.e. expression noise is intrinsic to the gene-expression process, not just extrinsic environmental variation.
drafts.h1: Across independent stochastic seeds (genetically identical cells, same wildtype/basal condition), the coefficient of variation (CV) of ribosome_conc (and correlated fraction_trna_charged) across seeds is substantial (CV >= 15%), reflecting intrinsic noise in gene expression rather than measurement replicate noise alone.
drafts.h0: Cell-to-cell variation across seeds is negligible/noise-floor only: CV of ribosome_conc across seeds in wildtype/basal is < 5%, i.e. isogenic cells under identical conditions express genes at effectively the same level (no meaningful intrinsic heterogeneity).

operational_defs.measure: per-seed CV across seeds, used as a correlated secondary channel

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: positive — isogenic cells show non-trivial dispersion. Magnitude: CV(ribosome_conc) across seeds >= 15% in wildtype/basal (vs an assumed instrument/measurement noise floor of ~3-5% from technical replication alone), and the pooled per-seed distribution is approximately unimodal (bimodality coefficient <= 0.555) rather than bimodal — i.e. noise is continuous/graded, not a discrete bistable switch, under basal conditions.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV (SD/mean) of ribosome_conc across seeds for wildtype/basal at generation 3. If CV < 5%, treat variation as noise-floor only and reject H1 (cells are effectively homogeneous). Separately, run bimodality_bc on pooled per-seed ribosome_conc values; if BC > 0.555 report a discrete subpopulation structure (refutes the 'graded unimodal noise' sub-claim) rather than continuous noise.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(ribosome_conc) across 8 seeds < 5% (isogenic cells converge to essentially the same expression level) OR bimodality_bc > 0.555 indicating a discrete bistable split rather than continuous graded noise.

test.statistic: sarle_bimodality_coefficient over pooled per-seed ribosome_conc (plus CV computed directly from per-seed spread)
test.threshold: BC>0.555 flags bimodal; CV<5% (from per-seed spread) flags noise-floor/homogeneous, both would refute H1 as stated

rivals.claim: Rival A (extrinsic-only noise): apparent heterogeneity is driven entirely by extrinsic factors (e.g. slightly different growth-rate trajectories or metabolic state per seed), not by intrinsic stochasticity of the gene-expression machinery itself.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, ribosome_conc CV across seeds should track tightly with growth_rate CV across the same seeds (near-perfect co-variation, high shared variance) and should collapse to near the noise floor if growth_rate is held essentially constant (e.g. via rrna_operon_knockout clamping ribosome capacity, which removes one source of extrinsic growth coupling) — i.e. the CV would NOT be intrinsic to the expression process per se but a downstream reflection of growth-rate fluctuations.

rivals.claim: Rival B (bistable/discrete subpopulations, not continuous noise): the population is not continuously variable but instead splits into 2+ discrete phenotypic states (e.g. a stringent vs relaxed subpopulation), driven by a switch-like regulatory mechanism (e.g. ppGpp-RelA feedback) rather than simple additive stochastic noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival B is true, bimodality_bc on pooled ribosome_conc (and ppgpp_conc) would exceed 0.555, revealing two separated clusters rather than one continuous spread; a relA gene_knockout control would abolish this bimodality if ppGpp-driven switching is the cause, collapsing the distribution to unimodal.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seeds in this simulator encode independent stochastic realizations of the same genotype/condition, so seed-to-seed spread is a valid proxy for cell-to-cell (isogenic population) heterogeneity.
ribosome_conc at generation 3 approximates a quasi-steady-state readout comparable across seeds (not dominated by transient startup dynamics).

The instrument's technical/measurement noise floor for ribosome_conc across replicate seeds of an otherwise-deterministic process is roughly 3-5% CV (assumed baseline, not separately measured here) — used only as a qualitative anchor for 'noise-floor only' vs 'substantial heterogeneity'.

fraction_trna_charged under steady-state charging mode is reported as 20 per-amino-acid values broadcast over 86 columns; we treat the per-seed aggregate pattern as a secondary corroborating channel, not the primary test channel.

Distinguishing extrinsic vs intrinsic noise sources in the strict Elowitz two-reporter sense is beyond this simulator's instrumentation; we approximate via growth_rate co-variation and the rrna_operon_knockout control as the closest feasible interventional proxy, per auxiliary scope caveat.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: In an isogenic E. coli population growing under identical (basal) conditions, individual cells show substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output due to intrinsic stochastic noise in transcription/translation, rather than being uniform/deterministic — operationalized as the per-seed distribution of fraction_trna_charged (and ribosome_conc as a bulk-expression-capacity proxy) across many independent stochastic replicates (seeds) of the wildtype/basal design showing a coefficient of variation well above the noise floor expected from measurement/sampling alone.
drafts.h1: Across seeds (isogenic replicates) of wildtype/basal, the per-seed steady-state values of ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged show substantial dispersion (CV >= 15%) that is NOT explained by a trivial constant/noise-floor model, reflecting genuine intrinsic expression noise among genetically identical cells.
drafts.h0: Per-seed values of ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged across wildtype/basal replicates are tightly clustered (CV < 5%), i.e. genetically identical cells under identical conditions express genes at essentially the same level, with only negligible numerical/integration noise distinguishing seeds.

drafts.predicted_effect: Positive, moderate-magnitude: CV of ribosome_conc across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal ~15-25% (vs an assumed instrument/integration noise floor of ~3-5%), and CV of fraction_trna_charged ~8-15%. The distribution across seeds is expected to be unimodal (BC <= 0.555) — i.e., continuous noise, not discrete subpopulations — consistent with intrinsic stochastic gene-expression noise rather than bistability.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of per-seed ribosome_conc across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal; treat CV>=15% as evidence of real biological noise beyond a numerical floor. Separately run power_mde to confirm 8 seeds can detect a 15% CV against an assumed ~5% null floor at the observed per-seed spread.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) across seeds falls below 5%, indistinguishable from the floor, OR power_mde shows 8 seeds are underpowered to distinguish 15% from 5% CV (i.e., MDE > 10 percentage points), meaning the data cannot support the noise claim.

test.statistic: CV (SD/mean) across seeds; minimum detectable effect in CV units
test.threshold: observed CV >= 15% AND MDE <= 10 percentage points at n=8 seeds

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is mostly integration/numerical artifact (solver tolerance, timestep discretization) rather than biological stochasticity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If artifact-driven, CV should NOT scale with known biological noise drivers (e.g., should be similar in a condition with slower transcription/translation rates); also bimodality_bc would be irrelevant since noise would be symmetric and tiny (<5%) regardless of condition.

rivals.claim: Variability reflects a bona fide bistable switch (e.g., two discrete ppGpp/growth states) rather than continuous intrinsic noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc over pooled per-seed ribosome_conc/fraction_trna_charged would exceed 0.555, showing two clusters, rather than a single continuous unimodal spread.

rivals.claim: Variability is driven by extrinsic condition differences (e.g., subtle drift in media condition across seeds) rather than intrinsic stochasticity, since the simulator reuses the same condition label but seeds could diverge via extrinsic fluctuators like RelA/ppGpp machinery levels.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout background (removing the stringent-response extrinsic fluctuator) should NOT collapse the CV to the floor if the noise is truly intrinsic (e.g., ribosome partitioning noise); if CV collapses toward 5% under relA KO, that implicates the extrinsic ppGpp-coupled fluctuator rather than pure intrinsic noise.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed stochastic variation in the simulator's random number seeding reflects genuine intrinsic expression noise (transcription/translation bursting, partitioning at division) rather than purely numerical integration artifacts; we cannot fully separate deterministic chaos from stochastic noise within this simulator, so this is treated as a scope caveat.

ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged are adequate proxies for 'gene expression level' at the whole-cell scale; single-gene mRNA/protein copy-number noise (which is the classical Elowitz/Ozbudak-style readout) is not directly exposed as a channel here, so we use the closest aggregate dials available.

Basal and acetate conditions are assumed to differ in overall expression/metabolic flux rate such that acetate serves as a reasonable (if imperfect) comparator for noise-floor magnitude, not a perfect noise-free control.
8 seeds x 3 generations is assumed sufficient compute to reach steady-state per-seed averages without transient startup effects dominating the CV.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: In an isogenic population growing in constant basal medium, intrinsic stochasticity in gene expression biochemistry (transcription/translation bursting) produces substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene-product levels even though all cells share identical genotype and environment. This noise will manifest as a non-trivial coefficient of variation (CV) in a representative expression-linked channel (ribosome_conc, a proxy for the translational output of the genome) across isogenic replicate seeds of the wildtype/basal condition, not as a tight, near-deterministic value.
drafts.h1: Across independent, isogenic seeds of wildtype cells in constant basal medium, the per-seed steady-state distribution of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged as a second expression-linked readout) shows CV >= 15%, reflecting real intrinsic noise rather than measurement/replicate artifact.
drafts.h0: Isogenic wildtype cells in basal medium express ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) at essentially the same level across seeds: CV < 15%, i.e. variability is negligible/consistent with sampling noise only, and gene expression is effectively deterministic given genotype+environment.

drafts.predicted_effect: Positive, non-trivial dispersion: predict CV(ribosome_conc) across seeds approx. 15-30% (point estimate ~20%) in wildtype/basal, and predict the pooled per-seed distribution is UNIMODAL (Sarle's BC <= 0.555) rather than bimodal, consistent with continuous intrinsic noise rather than a bistable switch. A rrna_operon_knockout background (reduced ribosome capacity) is predicted to compress CV toward <=10% (a floor/ceiling effect) by removing capacity-driven variance, serving as the discriminating control.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV = sd/mean of per-seed terminal ribosome_conc across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal. Reject H1 (accept H0) if CV < 15%. Separately, test welch_disconfirm between wildtype/basal (seeds 1-4) vs wildtype/basal (seeds 5-8) as an internal noise-floor check: |welch_t| < 2 together with CV < 15% confirms H0.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(ribosome_conc) across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds is < 15% (e.g. 5%), indicating isogenic cells express ribosome_conc at essentially the same level and intrinsic noise is negligible at this scope.

test.statistic: welch_t on ribosome_conc between two seed-halves of wildtype/basal, plus CV computed from per-seed spread
test.threshold: CV >= 15% required to support H1; |welch_t| < 2 between seed-halves expected under true isogenic noise (no systematic drift, only noise)

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is not intrinsic biochemical noise but an artifact of insufficient equilibration/transient dynamics (cells simulated too few generations have not reached steady state, inflating apparent spread).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(ribosome_conc) shrinks substantially (e.g. from ~20% to <10%) when generations is increased from 2 to 4 while seeds stay fixed, this supports the transient-artifact rival rather than genuine steady-state intrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Variability is dominated by extrinsic/global noise (e.g. fluctuations in overall ribosome capacity or growth rate) rather than gene-intrinsic stochasticity, so a ribosome-capacity-limiting perturbation (rrna_operon_knockout) should proportionally SCALE the CV rather than compress it toward a floor.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout/basal shows CV(ribosome_conc) across seeds that is similar to or HIGHER than wildtype/basal (rather than compressed to <=10%), this supports the extrinsic-noise/capacity-scaling rival over the intrinsic-noise claim.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed terminal ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) values at matched simulated time are a valid proxy for 'gene expression level at steady state' in a single cell lineage.

Seed-to-seed variation under identical params/condition/perturbation reflects the simulator's modeled intrinsic stochasticity (not solver/numerical artifact); any such artifact is a known scope caveat the simulator cannot fully disambiguate from biological noise.
CV computed from 8 seeds is a reasonable (if noisy) point estimate of the population CV; no claim is made about the exact sampling distribution of CV itself.

fraction_trna_charged is used as a secondary corroborating channel, not the primary falsifier channel, since under steady-state charging it is a broadcast of 20 per-amino-acid values over 86 columns (redundant structure), which could bias a naive variance estimate if used alone.
Bimodality (BC) is checked on pooled values purely to rule out a discrete-subpopulation (bistable switch) interpretation, not to establish unimodality as part of H1 itself.

select_score.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
select_score.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing under identical (wildtype/basal) conditions exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output, operationalized as the per-seed (replicate) spread of a representative expression-linked channel (fraction_trna_charged, as a proxy for translational/expression state) and ribosome_conc (active ribosome concentration, a bulk proxy for expression capacity), such that the coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds is substantial (CV >= 15%) rather than near-zero, i.e. cells do NOT express genes at identical levels despite identical genotype and environment.
select_score.h1: Across isogenic replicate simulations (same genotype, same wildtype/basal condition, differing only in stochastic seed), per-seed values of ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged show a coefficient of variation (CV) >= 15%, i.e. non-trivial intrinsic expression noise exists even without any genetic or environmental perturbation.
select_score.h0: Per-seed CV of ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged across isogenic wildtype/basal replicates is small (CV < 15%, near measurement/numerical noise floor), i.e. gene expression level is effectively deterministic/identical across genetically identical cells in the same environment.

select_score.predicted_effect: Positive, substantial intrinsic noise: CV across seeds >= 15% for ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged in wildtype/basal (versus a near-zero CV < 5% expected under strict determinism). Distribution shape: unimodal but right- or left-skewed, not perfectly symmetric; bimodality coefficient (BC) expected < 0.555 (no discrete subpopulations under plain wildtype, ruling out bistable switching as the noise source).

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV = SD/mean of per-seed ribosome_conc values across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal (self-comparison across the seed ensemble, since H1 concerns within-design spread, not a between-design mean shift); treat CV>=15% as support for H1 and CV<5% as support for H0. Additionally run power_mde to confirm 8 seeds can detect a 15% CV effect above noise floor at the observed per-seed spread (using the platform's power_mde check tied to this channel's seed-to-seed variance).
falsifier.refuting_result: Observed CV of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds is < 5%, and power_mde confirms the design has power to detect 15% CV if present (MDE well below 15%) — i.e. the near-zero spread is not just a false negative; this would refute H1 and support near-deterministic expression.

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation + min_detectable_effect
test.threshold: CV>=15% supports H1; MDE must be <15% for the null (CV<5%) to count as a genuine disconfirmation rather than underpowering

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is mostly extrinsic/environmental microheterogeneity (e.g. slight differences in nutrient draw or division timing across seeds) rather than intrinsic stochastic gene expression noise — a bursty transcription/translation process is not actually the driver.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If variability were purely extrinsic (environment-driven), clamping a key regulatory input (e.g. ppgpp_conc clamped to a fixed multiple of basal, removing stringent-response feedback noise) should NOT reduce the CV of ribosome_conc/fraction_trna_charged much, since the extrinsic driver is unrelated to ppGpp; if instead CV collapses substantially under the ppgpp_conc clamp, that supports ppGpp-mediated (regulatory/intrinsic) noise amplification rather than pure extrinsic microheterogeneity.

rivals.claim: Any observed spread across seeds is a numerical/simulator artifact (solver stochasticity, discretization noise) rather than biologically meaningful cell-to-cell variability, and would appear identically even for a channel with no real biological stochastic process.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Compare CV of ribosome_conc (expected biologically noisy) against CV of a channel expected to be tightly constrained by FBA/metabolic stoichiometry such as dry_mass or fba_objective in the same wildtype/basal seed ensemble; if dry_mass/fba_objective show comparably large CV, that points to generic numerical noise rather than expression-specific stochasticity (this comparison is descriptive context, not the primary falsifier).

auxiliary_assumptions: Within-design seed-to-seed spread in this simulator is intended to represent biologically meaningful stochastic variability (intrinsic + modeled extrinsic noise sources), not pure solver artifact — the rival about numerical artifact is addressed only descriptively (dry_mass/fba_objective comparison), since the simulator's noise-generation mechanism cannot be fully decomposed into intrinsic vs extrinsic vs numerical sources from summary channels alone.

fraction_trna_charged under steady-state charging is broadcast from 20 per-amino-acid values over 86 columns; we average the per-seed values rather than treating all 86 as independent to avoid pseudo-replication inflating apparent variance.
3 generations is sufficient for the ribosome/charging state to reach a representative steady-state-like distribution per seed without confounding early-transient effects with steady noise.
The relA knockout is used as an interventional control to test whether ppGpp-synthesis-dependent stringent response contributes to baseline noise, not to claim relA KO eliminates all intrinsic noise.
