drafts.predicted_effect: Positive, moderate-magnitude noise: CV(ribosome_conc) across 8 isogenic seeds >= 15% (predict ~20-25%) under wildtype/basal, and pooled per-seed distribution is non-degenerate (not a spike); bimodality coefficient BC is between 0.35 and 0.6 (i.e. unimodal-but-dispersed, not literally bimodal) — the key claim is the CV magnitude, not bimodality per se.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed CV of ribosome_conc across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal (single condition, no perturbation). Treat H1 as refuted if CV < 5% (power_mde check: is 5% above the minimum detectable effect at n=8?) OR if welch_disconfirm of a held-out seed-split (first 4 seeds vs last 4 seeds, same design) gives |welch_t| < 2, indicating the apparent spread is within replicate noise / not a real dispersed distribution worth claiming.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(ribosome_conc) across the 8 seeds is < 5% (near-deterministic) and/or the two seed-halves split via welch_disconfirm shows |t|<2 with effect_pct comparable to numerical noise floor, meaning isogenic cells behave essentially identically and the simulator shows no meaningful expression noise.

test.statistic: CV of ribosome_conc across seeds; MDE check at n=8
test.threshold: refute H1 if observed CV < 5% (below min-detectable-effect floor) or equivalently welch_t on seed-halves |t|<2

rivals.claim: Rival A (numerical-artifact noise): any observed variability across seeds is purely simulator/solver stochasticity (RNG seeding of FBA or integrator jitter) rather than biologically meaningful expression noise, and would appear identically for ANY channel including non-biological diagnostics.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(ribosome_conc) across seeds is statistically indistinguishable from CV(fba_objective) across the same seeds (both near the numerical noise floor), that supports Rival A; a real biological-noise claim predicts CV(ribosome_conc) is substantially larger than CV(fba_objective).

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp/stringent-response-driven deterministic bistability, not true cell-to-cell noise): apparent dispersion in ribosome_conc actually reflects cells sorting into two discrete regulatory states (e.g. high/low ppGpp attractors) driven by a near-deterministic switch, not continuous intrinsic noise — predicting strong bimodality (BC>0.555) rather than a smoothly dispersed unimodal distribution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If bimodality_bc on pooled ribosome_conc values across seeds exceeds 0.555, that favors discrete bistable sorting (Rival B) over continuous noise (H1, which predicts BC in 0.35-0.6, i.e. unimodal-but-dispersed).

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed stochasticity (RNG draws for partitioning, kinetic reactions, division timing) is intended to model genuine biological intrinsic noise, not merely numerical artifact — we cannot fully adjudicate this distinction with the simulator alone, so Rival A is used as a bounding check via fba_objective rather than a ground-truth arbiter.

ribosome_conc under steady-state charging is an adequate representative proxy for 'gene expression level' at the whole-cell coarse-grained scale; we are not resolving single-gene mRNA/protein noise (e.g. a specific lacZ reporter) because the instrument does not expose a single-gene fluorescent-reporter channel.
3 generations is sufficient for seeds to reach a comparable quasi-steady growth phase so that CV reflects steady-state variability rather than transient initial-condition differences.
Isogenicity is operationalized as identical perturbation/condition/params across seeds; seed value itself is the only varied input.

params.note: control channel fba_objective pulled from same run to test Rival A numerical-noise-floor comparison

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in identical (basal) media exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output, operationalized as the per-seed (replicate) spread in protein-level readouts (ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged as proxies for expression state) under a wildtype/basal design: the across-seed coefficient of variation (CV) of these channels is large (CV >= 15%) rather than near-zero, reflecting intrinsic stochastic noise rather than deterministic uniform expression.

drafts.h0: Isogenic cells express genes at effectively the same level under constant conditions: the across-seed CV of expression-proxy channels is small (<5%), consistent with deterministic/homogeneous expression with only measurement-level noise.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed value of ribosome_conc at end of simulated generations, pooled across seeds to compute across-seed CV and spread

drafts.predicted_effect: Across isogenic wildtype/basal seeds, ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged show substantial dispersion: predicted across-seed CV ~15-30% (not <5%), and the pooled per-seed distribution is unimodal but broad (bimodality_bc < 0.555, ruling out discrete subpopulations) — i.e. continuous stochastic variability, not a bimodal switch, with effect size (CV) at least 3x the null expectation of <5%.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute across-seed CV of ribosome_conc for wildtype/basal (seeds=8). Also run power_mde to establish the minimum detectable CV difference at n=8 seeds. Reject H1 (fail to find variability beyond noise) if observed CV < 5% AND power analysis shows the design has power to detect a 15% CV effect (i.e. the null result is not just underpowered).
falsifier.refuting_result: Observed across-seed CV of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) is <5%, essentially flat across all 8 seeds, AND power_mde confirms the design could detect a 15% CV if present — showing isogenic cells express the gene at indistinguishable levels (uniform expression, no meaningful intrinsic noise).

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic homogeneity): any apparent variability across seeds is purely numerical/integration noise from the solver, not biological stochasticity — cells are truly homogeneous in expression.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, CV of ribosome_conc across seeds would be indistinguishable from CV of a single-seed replicate run multiple times with identical RNG seed (not testable directly here, but CV would be near the simulator's numerical-noise floor, typically <2-3%), and bimodality_bc would show no structure at all (BC near 0.33, perfectly unimodal/symmetric).

rivals.claim: Rival B (bimodal switching, not continuous noise): cells partition into two discrete expression states (e.g. high/low ribosome content) due to a bistable regulatory switch, rather than showing continuous unimodal spread.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc computed on pooled per-seed ribosome_conc values would exceed 0.555, indicating two separable subpopulations rather than one broad continuous distribution — this would refute the 'continuous noise, unimodal' form of H1 even though it would still show cells are not identical.

rivals.claim: Rival C (environment-driven, not intrinsic, variability): apparent cell-to-cell differences are driven by subtle differences in simulated nutrient microenvironment/media condition fluctuations rather than intrinsic stochastic gene expression machinery (transcription/translation bursting).
rivals.distinguishing_result: A discriminating control run under rrna_operon_knockout (reducing ribosome capacity, altering the translational noise source) would be expected to CHANGE the CV substantially if intrinsic ribosome-synthesis stochasticity drives the variability; if CV stays the same as wildtype despite reduced ribosome capacity, that supports environment-driven variability instead.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in identical (basal) media exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output, operationalized here as the charged-tRNA fraction and ribosome concentration (proxies for translational/expression state), rather than converging on a single shared value — i.e. gene expression is intrinsically noisy across the population, not deterministic given genotype+environment.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of fraction_trna_charged (and ribosome_conc) shows substantial dispersion (CV >= 0.15) and/or a detectable bimodal split (Sarle's BC > 0.555), indicating that genetically identical cells do NOT express the same gene at the same level even in a constant environment.
drafts.h0: Per-seed values of fraction_trna_charged and ribosome_conc under wildtype/basal are tightly clustered (CV < 0.15) and unimodal (BC <= 0.555), consistent with deterministic, noise-free expression given genotype and environment.

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged (per-amino-acid charged-tRNA fraction) and ribosome_conc as a global translational-output proxy
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state value of fraction_trna_charged (one representative amino-acid channel, e.g. aggregate) and ribosome_conc, pooled across seeds at matched generation/timepoint

operational_defs.observable: spread of per-seed channel values at a fixed generation under identical wildtype/basal condition
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) across seeds; Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed values

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and rela_conc dispersion under a relA-pathway perturbation vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: CV and welch_t of ppgpp_conc between rela knockout and wildtype

drafts.predicted_effect: Dispersion: CV(fraction_trna_charged) >= 0.15 and CV(ribosome_conc) >= 0.15 across seeds at generation 3-4 under wildtype/basal (vs an idealized noise-free CV ~0.02-0.05 expected under H0); additionally expect BC > 0.555 for at least one channel if a bimodal/bistable subpopulation emerges (predicted fraction of 'low' subpopulation ~10-30% if bimodal).

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV across seeds (n=8) at generation 4 for fraction_trna_charged and ribosome_conc; also compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed values. Reject H1 (fail to find noise) if CV < 0.15 for BOTH channels AND BC <= 0.555 for both. Additionally use power_mde to confirm n=8 seeds has sufficient power to detect CV=0.15 given the observed per-seed spread; if the MDE at n=8 exceeds 0.15, the null-CV result is inconclusive rather than confirmatory.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(fraction_trna_charged) < 0.15, CV(ribosome_conc) < 0.15, and BC <= 0.555 for both channels, with power_mde confirming adequate sensitivity at n=8 seeds — i.e. isogenic replicates converge tightly and unimodally, refuting the noisy-expression claim.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed fraction_trna_charged and ribosome_conc values; CV computed as a companion descriptive statistic
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 for at least one channel OR CV >= 0.15 for at least one channel counts as support for H1; BC <= 0.555 AND CV < 0.15 for both channels refutes H1

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is just sampling/measurement noise from too few seeds (not biological stochasticity) — with more seeds the distribution would tighten toward a single value.
rivals.distinguishing_result: power_mde on the wildtype/basal design shows the minimum detectable effect at n=8 is well below the observed CV, meaning the dispersion is robustly estimated and not an artifact of underpowering; if instead MDE > observed CV, the noise claim is unconfirmed by this design.

rivals.claim: Variability exists but is entirely driven by the stringent response / ppGpp regulatory circuit (a regulated, not intrinsic-noise, source) — removing relA would collapse the spread.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In relA gene_knockout/basal, CV(fraction_trna_charged) and CV(ribosome_conc) drop sharply toward CV<0.15 relative to wildtype/basal, and welch_t(ppgpp_conc, relA_KO vs wildtype) is large, showing the dispersion was ppGpp-circuit-dependent rather than irreducible intrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Variability is condition-dependent (e.g. only appears under nutrient-poor/acetate conditions) rather than a general intrinsic-noise property of the cell.
rivals.distinguishing_result: wildtype/acetate shows markedly higher CV than wildtype/basal (slope_ci across basal->acetate conditions excludes 0 with positive slope), indicating environment-dependent rather than universal intrinsic noise.

auxiliary_assumptions: Pooling per-amino-acid fraction_trna_charged into a single representative channel value (or treating the full 20-species vector) adequately captures 'expression level' noise without needing per-gene mRNA-level readouts, which the instrument does not expose as a noise channel.
Generation 3-4 is late enough for seeds to reach a quasi-steady distributional state but early enough to avoid confounds from population-structure drift or division-rate artifacts.

Intrinsic transcriptional/translational burst noise and extrinsic (whole-cell state) noise are not separately distinguishable by this simulator; CV and BC are read as a combined 'expression variability' signature, not partitioned into intrinsic vs extrinsic components.

Steady-state charging mode is used (not kinetic) for fraction_trna_charged and ribosome_conc per the instrument's recorded_when constraints, since no kinetic ppGpp module is being toggled on in these designs.

relA knockout is assumed mechanistically simulated (affects ppgpp_conc/rela_conc) — if it is not actually wired into the stochastic charging dynamics, the rival-2 control is inconclusive rather than confirmatory, per the instrument's caveat that KO mechanism fidelity is checked downstream.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in identical (basal) media exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output — operationalized as ribosome concentration (a proxy for translational/expression capacity) and fraction_trna_charged (a proxy for amino-acid-dependent expression flux) — such that the coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds within a single condition is large (CV >= 15%) rather than near-zero, and the distribution of per-seed values is consistent with continuous (unimodal) intrinsic noise rather than two discrete expression states.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) shows CV >= 15%, i.e. genetically identical cells do NOT express at the same level — substantial intrinsic stochastic variability exists even with no genetic or environmental perturbation.
drafts.h0: Per-seed values of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) under wildtype/basal are tightly clustered (CV < 15%, effectively deterministic given genotype+environment), i.e. seed-to-seed variation is negligible noise around a single fixed point.

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: steady-state ribosome concentration (uM) per seed, final-generation snapshot

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged
operational_defs.measure: fraction of tRNA aminoacylated (aggregate across the 20 amino acids) per seed, final-generation snapshot

operational_defs.observable: spread of per-seed channel values within one design
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) across seeds; shape assessed via Sarle's bimodality coefficient

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: positive, nonzero intrinsic variability. Magnitude: CV(ribosome_conc) >= 15% and CV(fraction_trna_charged) >= 10% across 8 seeds at wildtype/basal, with the pooled per-seed distribution unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555), i.e. noise is continuous/graded rather than bimodal (no discrete subpopulations).

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of ribosome_conc across 8 seeds at wildtype/basal (single design, no perturbation needed since H1 concerns intrinsic variance, not a mean shift); separately run bimodality_bc on the pooled per-seed ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged values across seeds. H1 fails if CV < 15% (tight clustering, effectively deterministic) OR if BC > 0.555 (distribution is bimodal/discrete rather than continuous noise as predicted).
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(ribosome_conc) < 15% across seeds (cells are near-identical) and/or BC > 0.555 (values split into two discrete clusters rather than the predicted unimodal continuous spread) would refute H1 as stated.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged; CV computed descriptively from per-seed spread
test.threshold: reject unimodal-noise claim if BC > 0.555; reject 'substantial variability' if CV < 15%

rivals.claim: Apparent seed-to-seed spread is purely simulator/integrator numerical noise, not biological stochasticity — i.e. the variance reflects solver artifacts rather than a real expression-noise phenomenon.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival were true, CV would scale with solver tolerance/seed count idiosyncratically and show no relation to any biologically meaningful channel (e.g. ppgpp_conc or growth_rate would show NO correlated co-variation with ribosome_conc across the same seeds); a slope_ci test of ribosome_conc vs growth_rate across seeds would show no significant relationship (CI includes 0), consistent with noise being uncorrelated/unstructured rather than a coupled physiological phenomenon.

rivals.claim: Variability exists but is bimodal (discrete ON/OFF expression states, e.g. a bistable switch), not continuous graded noise — cells fall into two subpopulations rather than varying continuously.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc on pooled ribosome_conc/fraction_trna_charged values would return BC > 0.555, indicating two separable clusters rather than a single continuous distribution.

auxiliary_assumptions: Final-generation (last cell cycle) snapshot values are representative of steady-state per-seed expression level, not a transient artifact of initialization.

8 seeds give adequate (if modest) power to estimate CV and run bimodality_bc; a larger screen would be needed to characterize the full population distribution shape with high confidence, but this is a feasible first-pass test at the requested scale.

ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged are adequate proxies for 'gene expression level' in this whole-cell model; the simulator does not provide single-mRNA or single-protein-copy-number noise readouts directly comparable to classic GFP-noise experiments, so this is the closest available operationalization.

The relA knockout control is used to check whether seed-to-seed variability in ribosome_conc is partly ppGpp/stringent-response-mediated (a candidate noise-generating mechanism) versus intrinsic to translation machinery independent of that pathway; it is not required for the core CV/bimodality test but helps bound mechanism.

params.note: replicate check / independent seed batch to confirm CV estimate is stable, not a one-off batch artifact

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in identical (basal) media exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression — operationalized as the per-seed distribution of charged-tRNA fraction and ribosome concentration — such that the coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds is large (>=15%) rather than near-zero, reflecting intrinsic stochastic noise rather than deterministic uniformity.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate simulations (same genotype, same static condition, differing only in stochastic seed), the distribution of a representative expression-proxy channel (fraction_trna_charged, pooled per-seed) shows a coefficient of variation >=15% and/or significant bimodality (Sarle's BC>0.555), indicating that identical genotype and environment do NOT produce identical expression levels.
drafts.h0: Isogenic replicates under identical conditions show tightly clustered expression (CV<15%, unimodal, BC<=0.555) for fraction_trna_charged, i.e. genetic identity plus environmental identity is sufficient to pin down expression level, with only negligible noise.

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged (per-seed, pooled across the 20 amino-acid species under steady-state charging)
operational_defs.measure: per-seed mean value of fraction_trna_charged; compute CV = SD/mean across seeds, and Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed values

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc as a secondary corroborating channel (active ribosome concentration, steady-state only)
operational_defs.measure: CV across seeds of per-seed mean ribosome_conc

operational_defs.observable: wildtype genotype, basal condition, identical timeline
operational_defs.measure: design label wildtype/basal with seeds varied only

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: isogenic cells will NOT express identically — predicted CV of fraction_trna_charged across seeds >=15% (vs a null of <5% expected from pure numerical/solver noise), and the pooled per-seed distribution will show mild-to-moderate bimodality (Sarle's BC target ~0.55-0.65) consistent with at least two sub-populations differing by roughly 10-20% in charged-tRNA fraction. Ribosome_conc CV predicted similarly elevated, >=10%.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed mean fraction_trna_charged values across 8 seeds; separately compute CV = SD/mean across those 8 per-seed means. Reject H1 (accept H0: effectively deterministic expression) if BC<=0.555 AND CV<15%. As a secondary corroborating test, run welch_disconfirm comparing an independent high-seed-count block vs a low-seed-count block of the SAME wildtype/basal design (a resampling split) to confirm the observed spread is not an artifact of seed count; if |welch_t|<2 for that split-half comparison alongside CV<15%, this further supports H0.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV across the 8 per-seed means <15% and BC<=0.555 (unimodal, tightly clustered) — this would mean isogenic replicates express fraction_trna_charged at essentially the same level, refuting H1.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed mean fraction_trna_charged; CV as auxiliary descriptive statistic
test.threshold: BC>0.555 (bimodal) OR CV>=15% counts as support for H1; BC<=0.555 AND CV<15% refutes H1

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic/solver-noise only): apparent cell-to-cell variability is purely numerical integration noise of the deterministic steady-state solver, not biological stochasticity — increasing seed count or using a different elongation model would collapse the spread.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, switching to the coarse_kinetic elongation_model (which introduces explicit stochastic elongation) would NOT increase CV or BC relative to steady_state; CV stays <15% and BC<=0.555 even under kinetic charging, since the spread was never biologically stochastic to begin with.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp/stringent-response-driven bistability, not generic noise): the apparent bimodality is specifically caused by stochastic triggering of the RelA/ppGpp stringent response creating two discrete physiological states (stringent vs relaxed), not generic expression noise across all genes.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout (background perturbation that abolishes ppGpp synthesis capacity) should COLLAPSE the bimodality (BC drops to <=0.555) in fraction_trna_charged while CV may still remain non-trivial from residual noise — showing the bimodal component was ppGpp-dependent, distinguishing this from a generic noise claim where relA KO would leave BC largely unchanged.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed mechanism is intended to capture genuine biological/intrinsic noise sources (partitioning at division, transcriptional bursting proxies, etc.), not merely numerical integration artifacts — this cannot be fully disentangled within the simulator and is recorded as a scope caveat.

fraction_trna_charged under steady-state charging is broadcast from 20 per-amino-acid values over 86 columns; we use the per-seed MEAN across all columns as the summary observable, which may smooth out some finer-grained heterogeneity.
8 seeds is assumed sufficient replicate power to estimate CV and BC meaningfully at this modest scale; a human may need to scale seeds up if results are borderline.
The relA knockout is assumed in-envelope and mechanistically simulated (ppGpp synthesis suppressed); whether RelA KO is fully implemented is to be confirmed downstream per the platform note.
Basal condition and 3 generations are assumed long enough for steady-state charging dynamics to equilibrate per seed before the per-seed mean is computed.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in identical (basal) media exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression — operationalized here as the charged-tRNA fraction and ppGpp concentration (proxies for translational/stringent-response output that integrate transcription+translation noise) — rather than converging on a single shared value; across an 8-seed wildtype population the per-seed coefficient of variation (CV) in ppgpp_conc is predicted to be >=15%, i.e. clearly above pure numerical/solver noise.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical (wildtype/basal) conditions, the steady-state ppgpp_conc (and correspondingly fraction_trna_charged) shows substantial inter-seed dispersion (CV >= 15%), reflecting genuine intrinsic expression noise rather than a single deterministic set-point shared by all cells.
drafts.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds under identical conditions converge on the same ppgpp_conc value up to small numerical/sampling noise: inter-seed CV < 15% (effectively a point value, not a distribution).

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged recorded per seed at steady state
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of ppgpp_conc computed across 8 independent seeds of the wildtype/basal design

operational_defs.observable: same channels, same design
operational_defs.measure: CV < 15% interpreted as seeds converging on one value within noise

drafts.predicted_effect: Distribution-shape claim at population (seed-ensemble) scope: predict inter-seed CV of ppgpp_conc >= 15% (vs a null CV < 15%), with the per-seed distribution approximately unimodal but right-skewed (not bimodal) — i.e., continuous intrinsic noise around a mean, not two discrete expression states. Expect roughly a 1.5-2x spread (ratio of 90th to 10th percentile seed value) within the 8-seed wildtype population.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute coefficient of variation of ppgpp_conc across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds; separately run power_mde to confirm 8 seeds can detect a 15% CV effect above baseline instrument noise. Reject H1 (accept H0) if observed CV < 15% AND power_mde confirms this is not simply under-powered detection.
falsifier.refuting_result: Observed inter-seed CV of ppgpp_conc < 15%, and power_mde shows 8 seeds have sufficient power (MDE < 15%) to have detected a true 15% CV effect had it existed — i.e., the low CV is not an artifact of too few seeds.

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation_with_MDE_check
test.threshold: CV >= 15% to confirm H1; reject H1 if CV < 15% and MDE < 15% (adequately powered null)

rivals.claim: Rival A (homeostatic buffering): ppGpp/charged-tRNA is tightly homeostatically controlled by RelA/SpoT feedback, so apparent variability is just measurement/solver noise, not biological noise — a relA gene_knockout should not change the inter-seed CV much because the buffering is not the dominant noise source anyway.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, removing RelA (relA gene_knockout) leaves inter-seed CV of ppgpp_conc/fraction_trna_charged essentially unchanged (within the same <15% or >=15% band as wildtype), because the observed spread was never due to RelA-mediated regulation — contradicting the expectation that stringent-response machinery shapes the noise.

rivals.claim: Rival B (growth-rate-driven variability, not intrinsic noise): apparent cell-to-cell differences in ppgpp_conc are secondary artifacts of seed-to-seed differences in growth_rate (extrinsic/environmental coupling) rather than intrinsic expression noise at a fixed growth rate.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival B is true, ppgpp_conc CV across seeds should track growth_rate CV closely (high positive correlation), and a condition with tightly clamped growth (e.g., via rrna_operon_knockout which constrains ribosome capacity and growth) should collapse ppgpp_conc CV toward the null band; if instead ppGpp CV persists at >=15% even when growth_rate is tightly constrained, intrinsic noise (H1) is favored over the extrinsic growth-coupling account.

auxiliary_assumptions: Each seed represents an independent stochastic realization of the same genetic/environmental program (isogenic, same media), so any inter-seed dispersion reflects intrinsic + extrinsic noise sources the simulator implements, not genotype differences.

The simulator's steady-state ppGpp/charging module includes enough stochastic sampling (transcription/translation bursts, partitioning noise) to be a meaningful proxy for real cell-to-cell expression variability; if the steady_state elongation model clamps ppGpp too deterministically, CV may be an underestimate — noted as a scope caveat rather than chased further.
Basal media and 2-4 generations are sufficient for seeds to reach steady state so that observed dispersion is not merely transient relaxation from identical initial conditions.

ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged are adequate operational proxies for 'gene expression level' at the scope this question asks (a population-level readout of regulatory/translational output), given the instrument does not expose a generic single-gene mRNA/protein copy-number distribution channel for a broad screen.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: In an isogenic E. coli population growing under constant conditions, gene expression noise produces substantial cell-to-cell variability in instantaneous ribosome-related expression levels: ribosome concentration (a proxy for the highly-expressed rRNA/ribosomal-protein regulon) varies across isogenic replicate cells with a coefficient of variation (CV) of roughly 10-20%, i.e. cells are NOT expressing the gene product at the same level despite identical genotype and environment.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic seeds (replicate stochastic cell lineages) under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged as a secondary corroborating channel) shows substantial dispersion: CV >= 10%, reflecting genuine intrinsic/extrinsic expression noise rather than measurement/seed artifact.
drafts.h0: Per-seed ribosome_conc values under wildtype/basal are tightly clustered (CV < 5%), i.e. isogenic cells express this gene product at effectively the same level and observed spread is negligible numerical/seed noise.

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel value recorded per seed at matched generation/timepoint
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) of ribosome_conc across seeds; also report per-seed spread from disconfirm output

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged channel per seed
operational_defs.measure: CV across seeds, compared qualitatively to ribosome_conc CV

operational_defs.observable: comparison of wildtype/basal seed spread vs a ribosome-capacity-perturbed condition (rrna_operon_knockout) that should shift the mean but not necessarily eliminate relative spread
operational_defs.measure: ratio of CVs between wildtype/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal

drafts.predicted_effect: Positive, substantial dispersion: CV(ribosome_conc) across 6-8 isogenic seeds >= 10% (point estimate ~12-18%), i.e. population is NOT a single point value; this is a difference-in-spread claim, not a mean-shift claim, so the decisive test is on per-seed spread/CV rather than a mean comparison (though welch_t vs a tightened synthetic reference can proxy significance of excess spread).

falsifier.decision_rule: power_check framing: compute CV(ribosome_conc) across the 6-8 seeds of wildtype/basal at matched generation; treat H1 as supported if CV>=10%; additionally run welch_disconfirm of wildtype/basal (seeds 1-4) vs wildtype/basal (seeds 5-8) as a split-half consistency check — if |welch_t|>=2 between arbitrary seed-halves of the SAME condition, that signals spread is driven by noise consistent with H1; if CV<5% and the split-half welch_t is indistinguishable from 0 everywhere, H1 is refuted
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(ribosome_conc) across seeds < 5% and per-seed spread reported by disconfirm is negligible, indicating isogenic cells express ribosomal machinery at effectively identical levels (H0 holds)

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation_and_min_detectable_effect
test.threshold: CV>=10% supports H1; CV<5% with MDE well below 5% refutes H1

rivals.claim: Apparent cell-to-cell variability is actually a deterministic consequence of the 'basal' condition being a mild mixture/edge condition (e.g. near a growth transition), not intrinsic stochastic noise, so a 'cleaner' steady condition would show near-zero CV.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Running the same analysis on an alternative stable static condition (e.g. acetate/minimal steady-state) would still show comparable CV>=10% if noise is intrinsic; if CV collapses toward 0% under the alternative condition, the rival (condition-artifact) is supported instead.

rivals.claim: Observed spread is dominated by ribosome-capacity differences (extrinsic, rRNA-operon-copy-number-driven) rather than general stochastic expression noise, i.e. it is a structural/genetic-dose effect mimicking noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal should show a LARGE mean shift in ribosome_conc but, if the rival is true, a disproportionately large CHANGE in CV (either collapse or large increase) rather than a comparable relative CV to wildtype; if CV stays similar in proportion (~10-20%) despite the mean shift, this rival is disfavored and generic stochastic noise is supported.

auxiliary_assumptions: Matched-generation sampling across seeds captures a quasi-steady-state snapshot, not conflated with cell-cycle-phase-driven oscillation in ribosome_conc.

The simulator's intrinsic stochastic seed mechanism is an adequate proxy for real biological intrinsic/extrinsic noise sources (transcriptional bursting, partitioning at division); we do not attempt to decompose intrinsic vs extrinsic noise components, only report aggregate CV.

fraction_trna_charged is used only as a secondary corroborating channel; under steady-state charging it is broadcast over 86 columns from 20 per-amino-acid values, so we only use it qualitatively, not as the primary decisive channel.

rRNA operon knockout is assumed to alter ribosome capacity without being lethal within 3 generations, allowing CV estimation; if division_rate collapses (<0.5) we treat that design as uninformative for the CV comparison rather than forcing an interpretation.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: In an isogenic E. coli population under constant conditions, cell-to-cell gene expression noise produces substantial variation in instantaneous expression-linked readouts across seeds, even though the population mean is conserved: specifically, the per-seed coefficient of variation (CV) of fraction_trna_charged and ribosome_conc across replicate seeds is large (CV >= 15%) rather than near-zero, reflecting intrinsic stochastic noise rather than deterministic uniformity.
drafts.h1: Genetically identical cells growing under identical (wildtype/basal) conditions show substantial intrinsic variability in gene-expression-linked readouts across replicate seeds (CV of ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged across seeds >= 15%), i.e. isogenic cells do NOT express the same gene at the same level.
drafts.h0: Isogenic cells under identical conditions express genes at essentially the same level: the across-seed CV of ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged is small (<15%), consistent with deterministic/near-uniform expression dominated by simulation numerical noise rather than biological stochasticity.

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc (active ribosome concentration, uM) and fraction_trna_charged (fraction of tRNA aminoacylated)
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state value at matched generation; summarized as across-seed mean, SD, and CV = SD/mean for wildtype/basal with seeds=8

operational_defs.observable: spread (per-seed spread / across-seed CV) of ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: CV% across 8 seeds, generations 1-3, compared against a near-zero deterministic-noise expectation

operational_defs.construct: stringent-response coupling as a rival driver of heterogeneity
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and rela_conc across seeds
operational_defs.measure: across-seed CV of ppgpp_conc under wildtype/basal vs relA-knockout background

drafts.predicted_effect: Across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal, ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged each show across-seed CV >= 15% (point estimate ~20-30%) despite a conserved mean (seed means within ~5% of each other), i.e. a 3-6x larger spread than a near-deterministic null CV of ~5%. No systematic directional shift (mean effect_pct ~0) is predicted between seeds — the signature is in the SPREAD, not the mean.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed spread (CV = SD/mean across the 8 seeds) for ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged under wildtype/basal; treat CV>=15% as supporting H1. Separately, run power_mde to confirm 8 seeds can detect a CV of 15% above a 5% deterministic-noise floor (i.e. the minimum detectable effect at n=8 is <=15%).
falsifier.refuting_result: If the observed across-seed CV for both ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged is <15% (close to the ~5% deterministic/numerical floor), and power_mde confirms 8 seeds have sufficient power to detect 15%, H1 is refuted: isogenic cells behave as near-uniform expressers under this instrument.

test.statistic: across-seed CV (SD/mean) compared to min detectable effect (MDE) at n=8 seeds
test.threshold: CV>=15% supports H1; reject H1 if CV<15% AND MDE<=15% (adequately powered null)

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic/model-artifact noise): any observed spread across seeds is purely numerical/solver noise from the steady-state FBA/ODE solver, not biological stochasticity; the simulator does not implement a stochastic gene-expression module, so CV should be tiny (<5%) and insensitive to perturbations that are known to amplify biological noise (e.g. rRNA operon dosage).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout (which changes ribosome synthesis capacity and is expected to amplify expression noise biologically) shows the SAME small CV as wildtype/basal, this supports Rival A — the spread is solver artifact, not biology.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp/stringent-response-driven heterogeneity, not generic expression noise): any heterogeneity across seeds is driven specifically by stochastic triggering of the RelA/SpoT stringent response (bursty ppGpp production) rather than being a generic property of expression across many genes; removing RelA should collapse the heterogeneity in ribosome_conc/fraction_trna_charged.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a relA gene_knockout background still shows CV>=15% in ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged (i.e. heterogeneity persists despite abolishing RelA-driven ppGpp bursts), this refutes Rival B and supports a more general intrinsic-noise explanation (H1) rather than a stringent-response-specific one.

auxiliary_assumptions: Across-seed variation under fixed condition/perturbation in this simulator is the operational stand-in for 'cell-to-cell' isogenic variability (the platform runs independent stochastic replicates rather than a literal single mixed population of individual cells).

A deterministic/numerical noise floor of ~5% CV is a reasonable baseline for 'no biological heterogeneity'; this value is a modeling assumption, not a measured corpus constant, and may need calibration against an explicit null-noise run if available.
Generations 1-3 are assumed sufficient to reach a quasi-steady-state per seed so that CV reflects standing heterogeneity rather than transient divergence from a shared initial condition.

fraction_trna_charged under steady-state charging is a broadcast of 20 per-amino-acid values over 86 columns; we treat the per-seed aggregate (mean over columns) as the single-seed readout, acknowledging this collapses finer per-tRNA heterogeneity.

rivals.claim: Rival B: Heterogeneity is driven by extrinsic noise from upstream stringent-response/ppGpp fluctuations (a shared regulatory driver) rather than being intrinsic to the ribosomal gene expression process itself.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout (abolishing ppGpp synthesis, the 'relaxed' control) should collapse much of the ribosome_conc variability if ppGpp-driven extrinsic noise dominates; if CV and BC for ribosome_conc remain similarly elevated in relA_KO/basal as in wildtype/basal, intrinsic noise independent of ppGpp signaling is implicated instead.

auxiliary_assumptions: ribosome_conc is a valid proxy for 'gene expression level' at the population/noise scope being asked about, since the question is about genes in general and the instrument does not expose a generic arbitrary single-gene mRNA/protein readout panel for a broad screen in one channel.

Steady-state charging mode is in effect for this design (ribosome_conc is only written under steady-state charging, per channel notes), so no kinetic ppGpp module is engaged for the primary wildtype/basal and relA_KO runs.

Seed-to-seed variability in the simulator is intended to represent genuine intrinsic+extrinsic biological noise sources (partitioning, transcriptional bursting proxies, stochastic kinetics) and not merely numerical/integration artifacts; this cannot be fully disentangled within the simulator and is recorded as a scope caveat.

The technical/instrument noise floor is assumed to be CV ~0.05-0.08 based on typical replicate-level numerical stochasticity; this is an assumption since no separate pure-replicate (fixed-seed) calibration run is included in this modest design.

Matching dry_mass/cell_mass across seeds at the chosen timepoint is assumed sufficient to control for gross cell-cycle stage differences without requiring explicit cell-cycle phase tagging, which the instrument does not directly expose.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in the same steady-state medium show substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output (here read out at the systems level via ppGpp concentration and ribosome concentration, which integrate transcriptional/translational state), such that the population distribution across replicate seeds is not a tight point value but has CV >= 15% and is consistent with intrinsic noise rather than measurement/seed artifact.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of ppgpp_conc (and ribosome_conc) has coefficient of variation (CV) >= 15%, i.e. genetically identical cells do NOT express the same level deterministically.
drafts.h0: Per-seed ppgpp_conc (and ribosome_conc) values under wildtype/basal are effectively constant across seeds (CV < 5%), i.e. identical genotype + identical environment yields identical expression level up to negligible numerical noise.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channel values recorded per seed at matched generation under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) computed across seeds; also per-seed spread from disconfirm()

operational_defs.observable: wildtype perturbation, basal condition, same generation count, only seed varied
operational_defs.measure: design label wildtype/basal with seeds=8

operational_defs.observable: comparison of CV at wildtype/basal vs a rrna_operon_knockout background that perturbs ribosome allocation machinery
operational_defs.measure: shift in CV and mean between wildtype/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal

drafts.predicted_effect: Positive, moderate-magnitude noise: CV of ppgpp_conc across seeds >= 15% (and CV of ribosome_conc >= 10%) at wildtype/basal, i.e. population is NOT a point mass; distribution shape expected unimodal-but-dispersed (not bimodal) under this one-gene/one-condition readout.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV (sd/mean) of ppgpp_conc across the 8 seeds at the final generation under wildtype/basal; also run bimodality_bc for distribution shape. Reject H1 (accept H0 of near-determinism) if CV < 5%. If 5%<=CV<15% the result is ambiguous/underpowered given n=8 (use power_mde to check min detectable effect).
falsifier.refuting_result: CV across seeds < 5% (values essentially identical up to simulator floating-point noise), indicating deterministic steady-state convergence rather than genuine biological noise.

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation + min_detectable_effect
test.threshold: CV < 5% refutes H1; CV >= 15% supports H1; report MDE at n=8 seeds

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is purely numerical/integration noise from the ODE/stochastic solver, not biologically meaningful expression noise (model artifact rival).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If solver-artifact rival is true, CV should be tiny (<1-2%) and insensitive to any genetic perturbation that should amplify noise (e.g. rrna_operon_knockout), i.e. CV at rrna_operon_knockout/basal is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal CV.

rivals.claim: Variability exists but is driven entirely by extrinsic/global cell-mass scaling (bigger cells simply have more of everything proportionally), not independent per-gene stochasticity in the regulatory network (extrinsic-noise-only rival).

select_score.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
select_score.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing under identical conditions show substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output rather than uniform expression: across seeds (intrinsic stochastic replicates) at wildtype/basal steady state, a representative expression-proxy channel (ribosome_conc, as a proxy for translational output tied to gene expression capacity) will show coefficient of variation (CV) >= 0.20 across seeds, and the amino-acid charging channel (fraction_trna_charged) will likewise show detectable per-seed spread rather than collapsing to a single value — i.e. gene expression in isogenic populations is heterogeneous, not deterministic given genotype.
select_score.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical (wildtype/basal) conditions, single-cell-level readouts of gene expression output (ribosome_conc as proxy, fraction_trna_charged) exhibit substantial variability (CV >= 0.20 for ribosome_conc), reflecting intrinsic stochastic gene expression noise rather than a fixed deterministic level set purely by genotype+environment.
select_score.h0: Isogenic cells under identical conditions express genes at effectively the same level: per-seed variability in ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged is small (CV < 0.20), consistent with deterministic/mean-field expression with only negligible replicate noise (sampling/numerical noise only).

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc (active ribosome concentration, a bulk proxy for translational/expression capacity) and fraction_trna_charged (charging state reflecting amino-acid supply-demand coupled to expression)
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state value of each channel at the final generation, pooled across seeds within a design

operational_defs.observable: distribution of per-seed values of ribosome_conc / fraction_trna_charged within the wildtype/basal design across independent stochastic seeds
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = std/mean) across seeds; compared against replicate/numerical noise floor via Welch t and bimodality checks

operational_defs.observable: shape and spread of the per-seed distribution; whether CV exceeds a noise-floor threshold and/or distribution is bimodal (bistable expression) vs unimodal-narrow (deterministic)
operational_defs.measure: CV threshold (>=0.20) and Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed values

select_score.predicted_effect: Isogenic wildtype/basal seeds will show CV(ribosome_conc) >= 0.20 across seeds (roughly 20-40% relative spread), i.e. a 1.2-1.4-fold typical seed-to-seed range, NOT a tight <5% numerical-noise-only spread. fraction_trna_charged will show detectable but smaller spread (CV ~0.05-0.15) since it's buffered by charging kinetics. We predict the distribution is unimodal (BC <= 0.555) but with wide spread -- i.e. continuous stochastic noise, not bistable switching, under basal unperturbed conditions.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of ribosome_conc across seeds for wildtype/basal design (n=8 seeds). This is a within-design dispersion test (not a between-design mean comparison), implemented as: resample seed values into two matched-size half-splits and apply welch_disconfirm between the half-splits to confirm no spurious mean-shift (i.e. confirm the spread is noise, not a bug), and separately use power_mde to establish that at n=8 seeds the design has power to detect CV=0.20 (i.e. MDE for a mean-shift at this n is well below the dispersion implied by CV=0.20). Reject H1 (fall back to H0) if observed CV(ribosome_conc) < 0.20 AND fraction_trna_charged CV < 0.05, i.e. per-seed spread is within numerical-noise floor rather than biological stochasticity.
falsifier.refuting_result: Observed CV(ribosome_conc) across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds is < 0.20 (e.g. 0.03-0.05), indicating seeds converge to nearly identical expression levels -- consistent with H0 (deterministic expression, negligible intrinsic noise) and refuting the claim of substantial isogenic heterogeneity.

test.statistic: CV (std/mean) across seeds; power_mde used to confirm n=8 is sufficient to resolve CV>=0.20 from noise floor
test.threshold: CV(ribosome_conc) >= 0.20 required to confirm H1; refuted if CV < 0.20 and MDE analysis confirms n=8 had power to detect that effect size

rivals.claim: Rival A (extrinsic-noise-dominant): any observed variability across seeds is NOT intrinsic gene-expression stochasticity but is driven by extrinsic fluctuations in global resource allocation (e.g. ppGpp/growth-rate coupling) that correlate across many channels together -- i.e. cells differ in overall physiological state, not independently in each gene.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, ribosome_conc variability across seeds should be strongly correlated with simultaneous growth_rate and ppgpp_conc variability within the SAME seeds (all channels move together per seed), and a rrna_operon_knockout (capacity-clamping control) that removes ribosome-synthesis flexibility should COMPRESS ribosome_conc CV toward near-zero because the extrinsic driver (ribosome allocation capacity) is removed -- if instead CV(ribosome_conc) stays >=0.20 under rrna_operon_knockout, that argues against a purely extrinsic/ribosome-capacity-driven account and favors intrinsic per-gene noise.

rivals.claim: Rival B (numerical/sampling-noise-only): the observed spread across seeds is purely an artifact of the stochastic solver/sampling scheme (pseudo-random seeding of a near-deterministic ODE/FBA integration) and does not reflect biologically meaningful cell-to-cell variability.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival B is true, increasing generations (longer integration, e.g. gen 1 vs gen 4) should NOT change CV (it would stay flat since it's just solver noise), and CV should be of similar tiny magnitude across ALL channels regardless of known noisy biological steps (e.g. fraction_trna_charged should show the same CV as ribosome_conc even though charging is a different noise-generating process) -- if CV instead DIFFERS systematically across channels and GROWS with generations, that argues for genuine accumulating biological stochasticity rather than pure numerical artifact.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seeds in this simulator are the operational analog of isogenic single cells / biological replicates under identical environment -- i.e. seed-to-seed variance at fixed condition is interpreted as a proxy for cell-to-cell variability in a real isogenic population (the simulator does not literally model a spatial population of cells dividing together).

ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged are adequate (if imperfect) proxies for 'gene expression level' in a whole-cell model that does not report individual mRNA/protein copy-number noise directly at this summary-channel level; a sharper single-gene readout (e.g. a specific mRNA/protein species trajectory) is not assumed available and is out of scope here.

The noise floor (what counts as 'numerical-noise-only' CV) is assumed to be well below 0.20 based on typical stochastic whole-cell simulator behavior; this is an assumption the power_mde check partially validates but does not independently calibrate from first principles.

We assume generations 1-3 are sufficient for the system to reach a quasi-steady distributional state at which seed-to-seed spread is meaningfully comparable; very early transients are not separately modeled out.

We treat rrna_operon_knockout as the closest in-envelope interventional control for isolating ribosome-capacity-driven (extrinsic) noise from intrinsic per-gene noise, acknowledging it is a coarse background perturbation rather than a perfect mechanistic isolator.

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in identical (basal) media exhibit substantial cell-to-cell variability in gene expression output — operationalized as ribosome concentration (a proxy for translational/expression capacity) and fraction_trna_charged (a proxy for amino-acid-dependent expression flux) — such that the coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds within a single condition is large (CV >= 15%) rather than near-zero, and the distribution of per-seed values is consistent with continuous (unimodal) intrinsic noise rather than two discrete expression states.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the per-seed distribution of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) shows CV >= 15%, i.e. genetically identical cells do NOT express at the same level — substantial intrinsic stochastic variability exists even with no genetic or environmental perturbation.
hypothesis.h0: Per-seed values of ribosome_conc (and fraction_trna_charged) under wildtype/basal are tightly clustered (CV < 15%, effectively deterministic given genotype+environment), i.e. seed-to-seed variation is negligible noise around a single fixed point.

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: steady-state ribosome concentration (uM) per seed, final-generation snapshot

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged
operational_defs.measure: fraction of tRNA aminoacylated (aggregate across the 20 amino acids) per seed, final-generation snapshot

operational_defs.observable: spread of per-seed channel values within one design
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) across seeds; shape assessed via Sarle's bimodality coefficient

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: positive, nonzero intrinsic variability. Magnitude: CV(ribosome_conc) >= 15% and CV(fraction_trna_charged) >= 10% across 8 seeds at wildtype/basal, with the pooled per-seed distribution unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555), i.e. noise is continuous/graded rather than bimodal (no discrete subpopulations).

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of ribosome_conc across 8 seeds at wildtype/basal (single design, no perturbation needed since H1 concerns intrinsic variance, not a mean shift); separately run bimodality_bc on the pooled per-seed ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged values across seeds. H1 fails if CV < 15% (tight clustering, effectively deterministic) OR if BC > 0.555 (distribution is bimodal/discrete rather than continuous noise as predicted).
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(ribosome_conc) < 15% across seeds (cells are near-identical) and/or BC > 0.555 (values split into two discrete clusters rather than the predicted unimodal continuous spread) would refute H1 as stated.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged; CV computed descriptively from per-seed spread
test.threshold: reject unimodal-noise claim if BC > 0.555; reject 'substantial variability' if CV < 15%

rivals.claim: Apparent seed-to-seed spread is purely simulator/integrator numerical noise, not biological stochasticity — i.e. the variance reflects solver artifacts rather than a real expression-noise phenomenon.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival were true, CV would scale with solver tolerance/seed count idiosyncratically and show no relation to any biologically meaningful channel (e.g. ppgpp_conc or growth_rate would show NO correlated co-variation with ribosome_conc across the same seeds); a slope_ci test of ribosome_conc vs growth_rate across seeds would show no significant relationship (CI includes 0), consistent with noise being uncorrelated/unstructured rather than a coupled physiological phenomenon.

rivals.claim: Variability exists but is bimodal (discrete ON/OFF expression states, e.g. a bistable switch), not continuous graded noise — cells fall into two subpopulations rather than varying continuously.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc on pooled ribosome_conc/fraction_trna_charged values would return BC > 0.555, indicating two separable clusters rather than a single continuous distribution.

auxiliary_assumptions: Final-generation (last cell cycle) snapshot values are representative of steady-state per-seed expression level, not a transient artifact of initialization.

8 seeds give adequate (if modest) power to estimate CV and run bimodality_bc; a larger screen would be needed to characterize the full population distribution shape with high confidence, but this is a feasible first-pass test at the requested scale.

ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged are adequate proxies for 'gene expression level' in this whole-cell model; the simulator does not provide single-mRNA or single-protein-copy-number noise readouts directly comparable to classic GFP-noise experiments, so this is the closest available operationalization.

The relA knockout control is used to check whether seed-to-seed variability in ribosome_conc is partly ppGpp/stringent-response-mediated (a candidate noise-generating mechanism) versus intrinsic to translation machinery independent of that pathway; it is not required for the core CV/bimodality test but helps bound mechanism.

Welch t comparing two independently-seeded half-cohorts of wildtype/basal should still show no systematic mean shift (|t|<2) even though within-cohort spread is large — heterogeneity is a variance phenomenon, not a mean-shift phenomenon.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of per-seed growth_rate in wildtype/basal_manyseeds (n=8 seeds) and run bimodality_bc on the pooled per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc values; reject H1 (heterogeneity claim) if CV<3% (indistinguishable from reported numerical/technical floor) OR if distribution is not just non-bimodal but essentially a point mass (near-zero variance); additionally run power_mde to confirm n=8 seeds has sufficient power to detect a CV>=10% difference from a 3% floor.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV of growth_rate across the 8 seeds is <3% (e.g. 1.2%) and ppgpp_conc CV is similarly <3%, with power_mde confirming n=8 is adequately powered to detect a 10% CV if present — i.e. isogenic cells behave essentially deterministically at this resolution, refuting substantial heterogeneity.

test.statistic: CV_across_seeds; bimodality_bc
test.threshold: CV>=10% supports H1; CV<3% with adequate MDE power refutes H1; BC<=0.555 supports unimodal-continuous-noise sub-claim

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic-convergence): any apparent spread across seeds is purely numerical/integration noise from the ODE/FBA solver, not biological stochasticity; cells are phenotypically identical once solver noise is subtracted.
rivals.distinguishing_result: CV across wildtype/basal seeds is at or below the platform's intrinsic numerical noise floor (<3%), and increasing seeds (power_mde) shows no real signal above that floor.

rivals.claim: Rival B (bistable subpopulations, not continuous noise): heterogeneity is real but reflects a discrete bimodal split (e.g. a ppGpp-high dormant/persister-like subpopulation vs a ppGpp-low growing subpopulation) rather than continuous intrinsic noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc on pooled ppgpp_conc and growth_rate values across seeds exceeds 0.555, indicating two separable clusters rather than one broad unimodal distribution.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed stochastic trajectories in the simulator are intended to model intrinsic biochemical noise (reaction stochasticity), not merely pseudorandom numerical artifacts; the platform's seed mechanism is assumed to inject biologically meaningful stochasticity (e.g. in transcription/translation events), not just solver round-off.
Generation-matched sampling (comparing seeds at the same generation count) is assumed valid for cross-seed comparison despite any asynchrony in division timing.

The relA knockout control is used as a background perturbation to test whether stringent-response (ppGpp) machinery contributes to the observed ppgpp_conc heterogeneity specifically, isolating a ppGpp-pathway-driven noise source from generic expression noise; it does not itself test the growth_rate heterogeneity claim directly, which is treated as the primary generic-noise readout.

We treat z_vs_corpus_spread as a useful descriptive sanity check but rely on CV and bimodality_bc (not z_vs_corpus_spread) for the decisive statistical test, since z_vs_corpus_spread is explicitly noted as non-significance-bearing.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in the same static medium exhibit substantial intrinsic cell-to-cell variability in growth rate and in the stringent-response/translation axis (ppGpp, charged-tRNA), such that across replicate seeds the coefficient of variation (CV) of growth_rate is at least ~15% and the distribution of per-seed ppgpp_conc departs from a single tight cluster (CV >= 20%), even though every seed shares identical genotype and medium.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show substantial dispersion (growth_rate CV >= 15%; ppgpp_conc CV >= 20%) that is not explained by simulator noise floor alone — i.e. it exceeds the dispersion seen in a near-deterministic reference with reduced stochastic sensitivity.
drafts.h0: Per-seed variability in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc under wildtype/basal is indistinguishable (statistically, and in magnitude) from the variability seen when stochastic/noise-generating machinery is damped (e.g. rrna_operon_knockout reducing ribosome-pool stochastic buffering is NOT a damping control — instead we use a tighter replicate reference), i.e. observed spread reflects numerical/sampling noise rather than genuine biological heterogeneity.

Magnitude: growth_rate CV >= 15% across 8 seeds; ppgpp_conc CV >= 20% across 8 seeds; this dispersion should be at least 1.5x the dispersion seen in a reduced-noise reference design (same condition, but with rrna_operon_knockout removing a major stochastic amplifier — fewer, larger ribosome-synthesis bursts can either increase or dampen noise, so this serves as a discriminating control rather than a strict null-damping device).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of per-seed growth_rate, wildtype/basal vs rrna_operon_knockout/basal across 8 seeds each; reject H1 (i.e. support H0 that spread is just numerical noise, not biological heterogeneity) if |welch_t| < 2 (non-significant difference in dispersion/mean) AND the wildtype/basal CV itself is < 15%.
falsifier.refuting_result: If wildtype/basal growth_rate CV across 8 seeds is < 15% (tight clustering near a single value) OR the Welch t comparing wildtype/basal to rrna_operon_knockout/basal shows |t| < 2 with both CVs similarly small, H1 is refuted: isogenic cells do NOT show meaningful intrinsic heterogeneity beyond the reduced-noise reference.

rivals.claim: Rival A: Apparent variability is just simulator/integrator numerical noise, not biologically meaningful stochasticity — i.e. the spread would shrink to near-zero if intrinsic noise sources were removed.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, a design with reduced stochastic machinery (rrna_operon_knockout, fewer independent synthesis events) would show CV statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal (Welch t non-significant), meaning noise is structural/numerical not biological.

rivals.claim: Rival B: Variability is entirely attributable to extrinsic environmental/seed-to-seed media microheterogeneity rather than intrinsic stochastic gene expression — i.e. if medium were made more uniform the spread would vanish.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival B is true, variability should be similar in magnitude across different static conditions (e.g. acetate vs basal) since medium handling, not intrinsic noise, dominates; a condition-independent CV would support Rival B over an intrinsic-noise account.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed stochastic sampling (random number seeds driving gene expression bursts, partitioning at division, etc.) is the operational proxy for 'intrinsic noise'; we cannot separate deterministic chaos from true stochastic noise within this instrument, so we treat all seed-to-seed spread as the measurable heterogeneity construct.
Sampling growth_rate and ppgpp_conc at the end of generation 3 is taken as a representative steady-state-ish snapshot; transient early-generation effects are not separately modeled.

rrna_operon_knockout is used as a mechanistic perturbation to the translation-capacity noise-generating machinery, not as a perfect 'noise-off' switch; interpreting it requires assuming ribosome operon copy number materially affects stochastic bursting of translation capacity.

CV thresholds (15% for growth_rate, 20% for ppgpp_conc) are chosen as modest, biologically plausible heterogeneity magnitudes reported in prior single-cell bacterial literature; they are not derived from this simulator's own baseline corpus.

rivals.distinguishing_result: If growth_rate CV in wildtype/acetate (a harsher static condition) is substantially larger than in wildtype/basal, this would suggest heterogeneity scales with environmental stress rather than being a constitutive baseline feature.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seed-to-seed variation in the simulator is intended to represent biologically meaningful intrinsic stochasticity (molecular partitioning, expression bursts) rather than purely numerical/solver artifacts; we cannot fully disentangle these within the simulator and treat this as a scope caveat.
Pooling per-seed final-generation growth_rate values is a valid proxy for the population snapshot distribution of an isogenic population at steady state.

relA knockout is assumed to meaningfully attenuate ppGpp-amplified noise without introducing confounding viability defects that would themselves inflate variance (checked via division_rate as a secondary sanity channel).

Generations 2 vs 3 comparison is sufficient to distinguish transient startup variance from persistent steady-state heterogeneity within the modest compute budget; longer transients outside this window are out of scope for this test.

objection_ledger.issue: The relA-knockout design is listed among candidate_designs and used to argue against rival #2, but no decision rule (threshold, statistic, comparison channel) is given for it in the falsifier block — only prose in the rival description. Without a pre-registered quantitative criterion (e.g., specific slope/effect_pct threshold for 'ribosome_conc scaling survives in relA-KO'), this comparison is not yet falsifiable and could be interpreted post hoc either way.

The claim's scope is 'how does a cell decide how many ribosomes to make in a given medium' (general, any medium), but the operationalized test only samples 3 conditions (basal, acetate, one timeline shift). This is a narrower scope than the user's question; the hypothesis should either state this as a deliberate sampling-of-a-distribution claim (e.g., 'relation holds across this representative gradient of media') or justify why 3 points suffice to support a general claim about ribosome allocation across media.

The decision rule requires R^2>=0.6 pooled across only 3 conditions (basal, acetate, amino-acid-supplemented timeline), each contributing one growth-rate point (plus seed noise). With effectively 3 distinct x-values, a high R^2 is close to guaranteed by any monotonic trend and not a strong test of a general 'growth-rate control law' that the user asked about broadly across media. This is a minor concern already partly mitigated by seed pooling, but the scope (3 media points) is thin for a claim of a general scaling law.

The decision rule's causal arm 2 (relA-KO) only tests a Welch t at basal (single condition shift), not a refit slope across basal+acetate like causal arm 1 (ppGpp clamp), despite both acetate and basal relA-KO designs being run. This asymmetry means the relA causal test is weaker/less comparable than the ppGpp clamp test even though both datasets exist.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV(growth_rate) and CV(ppgpp_conc) across the 8 seeds of wildtype/basal; separately compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on the pooled per-seed values of each channel. Reject H1 if either CV falls below 15% (negligible variability, supporting H0) OR BC>0.555 (discrete bimodal subpopulations rather than continuous noise).
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(growth_rate) and CV(ppgpp_conc) both < 15% across seeds (cells behave essentially identically), or BC>0.555 indicating a bimodal split into distinct subpopulations rather than smooth noise-driven variability.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc; CV computed directly from per-seed spread
test.threshold: BC>0.555 flags bimodal (refutes 'continuous noise' sub-claim); CV<15% refutes 'substantial variability' sub-claim

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is numerical/solver artifact, not biological: the simulator's stochastic seed only perturbs initial conditions trivially and true dynamics converge to a fixed point, so CV should be near 0 once transients decay (test at generation 4 vs generation 1).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(growth_rate) across seeds shrinks toward <5% by generation 4 relative to generation 1 in wildtype/basal, that supports the artifact/transient-decay rival over genuine sustained intrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Any observed variability is bimodal and driven by a discrete ppGpp-dependent stringent-response switch (some cells 'lock in' high ppGpp / low growth, a true bistable subpopulation), rather than smooth unimodal noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: BC>0.555 on pooled ppgpp_conc (and correlated low growth_rate in the same seeds) would indicate a true bimodal subpopulation split, refuting the 'continuous noise' framing of H1 even if overall CV exceeds 15%.

rivals.claim: Variability is driven mainly by ribosome-allocation/rRNA-operon copy-number effects rather than ppGpp-independent intrinsic noise; knocking out rRNA operons should collapse or dramatically change the variance structure if ribosome capacity, not stochastic expression noise, sets the spread.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal showing CV(growth_rate) collapsing (e.g., to <10%, since all cells are now capacity-limited and clamped to a narrow regime) or dramatically increasing (if capacity limitation itself destabilizes cells) relative to wildtype/basal would implicate ribosome-capacity structure rather than generic intrinsic noise as the main driver.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seed-to-seed variation in the simulator is intended to model genuine intrinsic biochemical/stochastic noise (reaction timing, partitioning at division, expression bursts), not merely pseudo-random-number-generator artifact — we cannot fully distinguish deterministic chaos from true stochastic noise within this simulator, so this is logged as a scope caveat rather than chased further.

Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are recorded under steady-state charging (per channel notes), so ppGpp/ribosome kinetics reflect the steady-state charging approximation unless a kinetic module is separately engaged; we are not engaging kinetic ppGpp dynamics in this test.

8 seeds is sufficient replicate depth to estimate CV and a 2-cluster bimodality coefficient without being a full population screen; this is treated as a modest pilot, not a claim about the exact population fraction in distinct subpopulations.
Basal condition and generations 1-4 avoid confounds from nutrient shifts or long-run divergence/adaptation; results are scoped to this single media condition and early generations.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing under identical fixed media conditions exhibit substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity driven by intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism — specifically, a population of wildtype cells run across many independent stochastic seeds shows a growth_rate coefficient of variation (CV) of at least ~15%, and the per-seed distribution of ppgpp_conc is not perfectly uniform/deterministic (CV >= 10%).
drafts.h1: Across independent stochastic seeds under identical (wildtype/basal) conditions, growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show substantial inter-seed variance (CV_growth_rate >= 15%, CV_ppgpp >= 10%), i.e. genetically identical cells behave heterogeneously due to intrinsic noise.
drafts.h0: Seeds are effectively deterministic replicates: inter-seed variance in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc is indistinguishable from numerical/sampling noise (CV_growth_rate < 5%, CV_ppgpp < 5%), i.e. identical genotype + identical environment yields near-identical phenotype.

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: positive, non-trivial dispersion. Magnitude: CV(growth_rate) >= 15% across seeds (vs <5% expected under a purely deterministic/numerical-noise null), and CV(ppgpp_conc) >= 10%. This is a distribution-shape claim (unimodal but dispersed, not point-mass), not a mean-shift claim — reference and target share the same mean but target shows >=3x the dispersion.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed growth_rate across n=8 seeds (wildtype/basal) and treat the pooled per-seed spread as the test population; use power_mde to establish the minimum detectable CV at n=8, then compare observed CV(growth_rate) against a null CV<5% baseline derived from a tight-seed reference design; reject H0 (heterogeneity real, not noise floor) if observed CV >= 15% and exceeds 3x the MDE-calibrated noise floor. Secondarily, Welch t of growth_rate CV-proxy (per-seed abs deviation from mean) between wildtype/basal (n=8 seeds) and wildtype/basal_lowseed (n=8 seeds, truncated generation=1 to minimize divergence time) must give |t|>=2.
falsifier.refuting_result: Observed CV(growth_rate) < 5% and indistinguishable (|t|<2) from the low-divergence-time reference, i.e. seeds converge to near-identical trajectories, meaning apparent heterogeneity is just numerical noise, not biological stochasticity.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed growth_rate (treating each seed as one observation) comparing wildtype/basal (gen=4, full divergence time) vs wildtype/basal_lowseed (gen=1, minimal divergence time)
test.threshold: |t| >= 2 AND observed CV(growth_rate) at gen=4 >= 3x CV at gen=1

rivals.claim: Rival A (extrinsic/environmental noise only): any observed variance is driven entirely by residual differences in initial conditions or solver/discretization artifacts, not intrinsic stochastic gene expression — a deterministic model re-seeded would show the same spread.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, CV(growth_rate) would NOT grow with generations (seeds would not diverge further from gen 1 to gen 4); the wildtype/basal_lowseed (gen=1) vs wildtype/basal (gen=4) comparison would show equal CV and |t|<2.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp/stringent-response is the sole driver of heterogeneity, growth noise is purely downstream): heterogeneity originates specifically in the RelA/SpoT ppGpp synthesis pathway and growth_rate variance is just a passive readout; removing ppGpp regulation should collapse growth variance to near the noise floor.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA knockout control design, if CV(growth_rate) collapses to <5% while wildtype retains >=15%, this supports ppGpp-centrality (rival B); if CV(growth_rate) remains >=15% in the relA knockout too, heterogeneity is NOT solely ppGpp-mediated and a broader intrinsic-noise mechanism (H1 as stated) is favored.

auxiliary_assumptions: Each stochastic seed represents an independent realization of intrinsic biochemical noise (reaction firing order, partitioning at division) rather than a distinct deterministic trajectory; the simulator's seed mechanism is assumed to actually inject stochastic variation into reaction/molecule-count sampling.

Generations 1-4 is sufficient time for noise to accumulate and manifest as measurable growth_rate divergence; shorter runs (gen=1) are used as a low-divergence-time proxy for a 'tight' null, not a true deterministic control (the envelope has no explicit noise-off switch).
Population size of 8 seeds gives adequate power to detect CV differences of this magnitude (to be checked via power_mde); if underpowered, result is inconclusive rather than confirming H0.
ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channels are recorded under steady-state charging in this design (no kinetic ppGpp module invoked), consistent with the instrument's default recording mode.
Dry_mass/protein_mass partitioning at division is a major noise source the simulator does implement; this is not independently verified here and is taken as a scope caveat.

rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled growth_rate or ppgpp_conc values would show BC > 0.555 (clear bimodal split into two subpopulations) rather than a single unimodal spread.
