falsifier.refuting_result: Per-seed growth_rate CV across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds is < 0.05 (near the presumed numerical floor), indicating seeds are essentially deterministic replicas; OR, for the causal sub-claim, relA_knockout shows growth_rate CV statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|t|<2, CV reduction <40%) at basal, at acetate, or inconsistently between the two, showing the RelA/ppGpp sensing pathway is not a robust operative noise-generating mechanism.

test.statistic: Welch t of growth_rate, relA_knockout vs wildtype across seeds, computed separately at basal and acetate; also per-seed CV (SD/mean) of growth_rate at each condition
test.threshold: Primary: CV>=0.15 confirms H1, CV<0.05 refutes. Causal sub-claim: |t|>=2 AND CV(relA-KO) <= 0.6*CV(wildtype) required at BOTH basal and acetate to confirm RelA-pathway causality; failure at either condition refutes the sub-claim.

rivals.claim: Rival A: apparent variability is purely an artifact of finite-generation transients (cells haven't reached steady state), not sustained intrinsic noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If we extend generations from 3 to 5 (same wildtype/basal design, more generations) and CV shrinks toward the numerical floor (<0.05) rather than staying >=0.15, this supports the transient-artifact rival over sustained intrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Rival B: variability is driven by extrinsic partitioning noise at division (e.g. unequal mother/daughter mass/protein split) rather than intrinsic stochastic gene expression routed through the RelA/ppGpp sensing pathway.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA_knockout (removing the uncharged-tRNA sensor, a genuine upstream mechanistic break) shows growth_rate CV statistically indistinguishable from wildtype at BOTH basal and acetate (Welch |t|<2, CV reduction <40% at each), this supports Rival B: partitioning noise independent of RelA sensing is the dominant, condition-general source. Only if relA-KO materially and significantly lowers CV at both conditions does the RelA-pathway-dependent intrinsic-noise claim survive over this rival.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed stochasticity (random seed draw) is intended to represent biologically meaningful intrinsic noise sources (transcription/translation bursting, partitioning at division), not merely numerical integration jitter; we cannot fully distinguish these inside the simulator, so this is recorded as a scope caveat rather than chased further.
Matched-generation comparison (e.g., generation 3) across seeds is a valid proxy for a synchronized population snapshot.

growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are read under steady-state charging (no kinetic ppGpp module needed) since wildtype/basal does not require the RelA/SpoT kinetic module; relA_knockout/basal and relA_knockout/acetate are likewise read under steady-state charging unless the platform forces the kinetic module on for that knockout, in which case rela_conc/ppgpp_conc channels become unavailable and growth_rate remains the primary comparison channel.

A CV numerical-noise floor of ~2-5% is a reasonable estimate for this platform's integration/seed-draw determinism absent biological noise; this is an assumption pending platform-specific calibration.

relA gene_knockout is treated as the closest in-envelope interventional break of the uncharged-tRNA-sensing-to-ppGpp-synthesis pathway (removing the sensor, RelA, rather than overriding its output via a ppgpp_conc clamp which would leave the sensing machinery intact and not cleanly isolate causality); residual ppGpp synthesis via SpoT is acknowledged as a limitation of this single-gene-knockout control but is the best feasible option within the single-perturbation envelope.

Whether the simulator's relA gene_knockout actually implements loss of RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis mechanistically (vs. an unmodeled no-op) is uncertain and cannot be resolved from outside the model; this is accepted as a standing scope caveat rather than further litigated, consistent with r2.2.

Testing the relA causal arm at both basal and acetate (rather than basal alone) is adopted specifically to give the RelA-pathway causal claim the same two-condition breadth/robustness check as any output-level (ppGpp-clamp-style) causal arm would have, closing the asymmetry noted in r2.1, without requiring any new perturbation type outside the validated envelope.

objection_ledger.issue: The relA-knockout design is listed among candidate_designs and used to argue against rival #2, but no decision rule (threshold, statistic, comparison channel) is given for it in the falsifier block — only prose in the rival description. Without a pre-registered quantitative criterion (e.g., specific slope/effect_pct threshold for 'ribosome_conc scaling survives in relA-KO'), this comparison is not yet falsifiable and could be interpreted post hoc either way.

The rivals section names fraction_trna_charged as a bystander and the falsifier claims clamping ppGpp alone discriminates causality, but fraction_trna_charged and ppgpp_conc are mechanistically coupled (ppGpp synthesis is driven by uncharged tRNA via RelA). Clamping ppgpp_conc to a fixed value while leaving the upstream charging machinery intact does not fully break the coupling path (charged-tRNA fraction will still shift with condition, and RelA will still attempt to respond to it even if the clamp overrides the output channel). The relA knockout design is listed as merely an 'orthogonal cross-check, not primary' -- but it is actually the only genuine interventional break of the coupling (removing the sensor rather than overriding the output). As currently weighted, the decision rule treats the ppGpp clamp as sufficient for the causal claim, without requiring the relA-knockout slope result to agree before accepting H1-causal.

The decision rule's causal arm 2 (relA-KO) only tests a Welch t at basal (single condition shift), not a refit slope across basal+acetate like causal arm 1 (ppGpp clamp), despite both acetate and basal relA-KO designs being run. This asymmetry means the relA causal test is weaker/less comparable than the ppGpp clamp test even though both datasets exist.

Whether the model's relA gene_knockout actually implements loss of RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis (rather than e.g. an unmodeled no-op) is uncertain and is already flagged as a scope caveat in auxiliary_assumptions; this is acceptable as stated rather than further litigated.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in the same medium (wildtype/basal) show substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity driven by intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism, such that a population of replicate seeds displays a coefficient of variation (CV) in growth_rate of roughly 15-25% across seeds/cells, rather than converging to a single deterministic value.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate simulations (same genotype, same wildtype/basal condition, differing only in stochastic seed), single-cell growth_rate (and correlated channels: ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged) exhibit a non-trivial spread (CV_growth_rate >= 15%) that exceeds the technical/numerical noise floor of the simulator, reflecting genuine biological noise rather than identical deterministic trajectories.
drafts.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds under wildtype/basal converge to effectively the same growth_rate trajectory; the observed per-seed spread in growth_rate is indistinguishable from numerical/integration noise, i.e. CV_growth_rate < 5% and the distribution of per-seed final growth_rate is unimodal and tight (no detectable heterogeneity beyond simulator floor).

operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of growth_rate across seeds; also per-seed spread reported by disconfirm

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged and ppgpp_conc channels per seed
operational_defs.measure: CV of fraction_trna_charged and ppgpp_conc across seeds; used as secondary corroborating channels

operational_defs.observable: division_rate per seed under rrna_operon_knockout control vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: bimodality_bc of pooled growth_rate values to check for discrete subpopulations vs continuous spread

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: isogenic seeds will show measurable dispersion, not convergence. Magnitude: CV_growth_rate ~15-25% across 8 seeds in wildtype/basal (vs a numerical-noise-floor expectation of <5% if purely deterministic/integration-limited). Pooled growth_rate distribution is expected to be unimodal (BC <= 0.555) reflecting continuous stochastic variation rather than discrete subpopulations.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of growth_rate across 8 seeds for wildtype/basal at generation 4; treat H0 as a power/equivalence claim: if observed CV < 5% (within min-detectable-effect bound at n=8), accept H0 (no detectable heterogeneity beyond noise floor). Also run welch_disconfirm of per-seed growth_rate means between two independently-seeded batches (4 vs 4) of wildtype/basal as an internal consistency check; reject H1 if |welch_t| < 2 AND CV < 5%.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV_growth_rate < 5% across seeds AND |welch_t| < 2 between the two seed-batches, indicating seeds converge to a single deterministic trajectory with no meaningful heterogeneity.

test.statistic: CV_growth_rate with min-detectable-effect check at n=8 seeds, cross-checked by welch_t of per-seed means between seed-split batches
test.threshold: CV >= 15% rejects H0 (heterogeneity confirmed); CV < 5% (below MDE) accepts H0 as equivalence

rivals.claim: Rival A: observed spread is purely numerical/integration artifact of the stochastic solver, not biological heterogeneity (i.e., the simulator injects noise unrelated to real gene-expression stochasticity).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, CV of growth_rate would be similar in magnitude to CV in a control with reduced stochastic sampling granularity (e.g., same seeds but condition acetate, a slower-growth static medium) in a way uncorrelated with any biologically meaningful channel (ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged) — i.e., no cross-channel covariance structure, just white noise.

rivals.claim: Rival B: heterogeneity is not continuous/intrinsic noise but reflects a discrete bistable switch (e.g., a bimodal ppGpp/growth state), so cells fall into two distinct subpopulations rather than a smooth distribution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc of pooled growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) across seeds would show BC > 0.555, indicating two separable clusters rather than unimodal spread, which would refute the 'smooth stochastic noise' framing of H1 even if overall CV is elevated.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed stochastic trajectories in the simulator are intended to model intrinsic biochemical noise (reaction firing stochasticity, partitioning at division), not merely pseudo-random numerical artifacts; this cannot be independently verified inside the simulator and is taken as a scope caveat.
8 seeds provide adequate (though modest) power to estimate CV and detect a >=15% heterogeneity signal; a formal power_mde check is used to avoid over-claiming equivalence from an underpowered null.
Growth_rate measured at generation 4 is a stable summary statistic (post any initial transient from seeding/initialization).

The rrna_operon_knockout control is assumed to perturb ribosome capacity without independently altering the stochastic noise-generation machinery itself, isolating the capacity-vs-intrinsic-noise distinction.
Media condition (basal) is held constant across all designs so that any observed heterogeneity is attributable to seed-level stochasticity, not condition differences.

params.note: discriminating control: reduces ribosome capacity, a mechanistic channel for noise amplification via translation bursting; tests whether heterogeneity scales with ribosome allocation (Rival mechanism) vs persists regardless (pure stochastic noise)

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells simulated under identical media (wildtype/basal) show substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity in growth rate and ppGpp concentration purely from intrinsic stochastic noise (gene expression/metabolic fluctuations), not from genetic or environmental differences: across replicate seeds, growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show CV >= 15% with no systematic (deterministic) drift, consistent with a unimodal but broad distribution rather than two discrete subpopulations.
drafts.h1: Across many isogenic seeds under constant basal media, instantaneous growth_rate and ppgpp_conc exhibit substantial dispersion (CV >= 15%) attributable to intrinsic stochastic noise, and the pooled per-seed distribution is unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555), i.e. heterogeneity is continuous noise, not bistable subpopulations.
drafts.h0: Isogenic cells under identical media are effectively deterministic replicates: per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show low dispersion (CV < 15%, indistinguishable from measurement/replicate noise), i.e. seed identity explains all variance and there is no meaningful intrinsic heterogeneity beyond that baseline.

operational_defs.measure: seeds dimension of wildtype/basal design (4-8 independent seeds)

operational_defs.construct: intrinsic stochastic noise vs structured subpopulations

operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed values; BC<=0.555 indicates unimodal (noise), BC>0.555 indicates bimodal (subpopulations)

drafts.predicted_effect: Growth_rate CV across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal >= 15% (roughly 2-3x the technical/numerical-noise floor we'd expect if cells were deterministic, which we take as ~5-7% CV from solver/integration noise alone); ppgpp_conc CV similarly elevated (>=15-20%, since ppGpp is a downstream amplifier of charging noise). Pooled distribution unimodal with BC <= 0.555 (not two discrete subpopulations) under unperturbed basal condition.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of growth_rate across 8 seeds at generation 3 for wildtype/basal; separately compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed growth_rate values. Reject H1 (heterogeneity-as-noise) if CV < 15% (cells behave near-deterministically) OR if BC > 0.555 (heterogeneity is actually bimodal/subpopulation-structured rather than continuous noise).
falsifier.refuting_result: CV < 15% across seeds (near-identical trajectories, indicating the simulator renders isogenic cells as deterministic replicates) OR BC > 0.555 (a clear bimodal split emerges, implying discrete subpopulations rather than continuous stochastic noise)

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed growth_rate; CV computed as auxiliary descriptive stat
test.threshold: BC <= 0.555 for unimodal/noise verdict; CV >= 15% required to confirm non-trivial dispersion

rivals.claim: Apparent heterogeneity is a numerical/solver artifact (integration noise, discretization), not biological stochasticity
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV scales with solver tolerance/timestep rather than biological noise sources (e.g. translation bursts), increasing seeds would not change CV magnitude in a biologically plausible way; this cannot be fully isolated in-sim, so we treat it as an auxiliary caveat rather than a separately tested rival (simulator limitation)

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity reflects bistable ppGpp/stringent-response switching (discrete ON/OFF subpopulations) rather than continuous noise
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled ppgpp_conc and growth_rate distributions would show BC > 0.555 with two separated clusters; a relA gene_knockout (removing the stringent-response synthesis arm) would collapse the bimodal structure toward unimodal if ppGpp-driven bistability were the cause, whereas if heterogeneity persists unimodal-but-broad in the relA KO, continuous noise (not ppGpp bistability) is supported

auxiliary_assumptions: Seeds in the simulator encode independent draws of stochastic processes (gene expression bursts, partitioning noise) rather than purely different random number streams with no biological noise source modeled.
Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc at matched generation (gen 3) are comparable across seeds despite any residual transient from initial conditions.

The simulator's numerical integration noise floor is small relative to 15% CV, so an observed CV>=15% is attributable predominantly to modeled biological stochasticity, not solver artifact (acknowledged as a caveat we cannot fully disentangle in-sim).
8 seeds is sufficient replicate power to estimate CV and bimodality coefficient without being dominated by small-n sampling artifacts.

relA knockout, while not a perfect mechanistic isolator (SpoT retains some ppGpp synthesis/hydrolysis activity), is the closest in-envelope single-gene intervention to test ppGpp-pathway-dependence of any bimodal structure.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Genetically identical E. coli cells (same genotype, same media) exhibit substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity even in a constant environment: isogenic replicate seeds under wildtype/basal conditions show a coefficient of variation (CV) in growth_rate of at least ~15-20% across seeds, and this spread is not a vanishing artifact of small sample size but a stable feature of the stochastic simulation.
drafts.h1: Isogenic cells (same gene set, same condition, differing only in stochastic seed) show substantial heterogeneity in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc: per-seed CV >= 15% for growth_rate, persisting (not shrinking toward 0) as generations increase from 1 to 4.
drafts.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds under wildtype/basal show negligible heterogeneity: per-seed CV for growth_rate < 5%, consistent with deterministic convergence to a single steady-state phenotype (noise is negligible/averaging out).

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: isogenic seeds will show real, non-trivial dispersion, not convergence to a point phenotype. Magnitude: growth_rate CV across 8 seeds >= 15% (vs <5% under a hypothetical deterministic null), and ppgpp_conc CV >= 20% (ppGpp pulses are expected to be noisier than growth rate). The CV should not trend toward 0 across generations 1-4 (OLS slope of CV vs generation 95% CI should include zero or be non-negative, i.e., not significantly decreasing).

Separately, regress per-generation CV (gen 1,2,3,4) against generation index using OLS; reject H1 if CV < 5% at gen4 OR if the slope 95% CI is entirely negative (shrinking toward 0).

test.statistic: OLS slope of per-generation CV(growth_rate) vs generation index, across generations 1-4
test.threshold: 95% CI excludes a strictly-negative-only slope OR CV at gen4 stays >= 5%; reject H1 if slope CI is entirely negative and CV<5%

rivals.claim: Rival A - Extrinsic-noise-only: heterogeneity exists but is driven entirely by coarse initial-condition differences (e.g., initial mass) rather than any intrinsic stochastic kinetics; if ribosome/ppGpp kinetic machinery were switched off (steady-state charging only), growth_rate CV should be nearly identical to the kinetic-model run.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Comparing wildtype/basal run under steady_state elongation_model vs coarse_kinetic: if CV(growth_rate) is statistically indistinguishable between the two (Welch t |t|<2), this supports Rival A (noise is extrinsic/initial-condition only, not from stochastic gene-expression kinetics).

rivals.claim: Rival B - Confounded by division/lethality artifacts: apparent growth_rate heterogeneity is actually driven by a subset of seeds experiencing division failures or near-lethal trajectories (division_rate << 1), not by genuine continuous phenotypic noise in otherwise-healthy cells.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If division_rate per seed under wildtype/basal is uniformly ~1 (no failed divisions) yet growth_rate CV remains >=15%, this rules out Rival B; if instead CV is driven by a few seeds with division_rate < 0.5, Rival B is supported.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seeds in the simulator genuinely instantiate independent stochastic trajectories (random number streams for transcription/translation/metabolic noise), not merely reruns of an identical deterministic trajectory.
growth_rate and ppgpp_conc summary channels are recorded comparably across elongation_model settings (steady_state vs coarse_kinetic) for the Rival A comparison.
8 seeds is sufficient replicate depth to estimate CV with tolerable sampling error at this modest scale; finer resolution of the distribution shape (e.g., bimodality) is left to follow-up work.
Division_rate differences, if present, are attributable to the perturbation/condition and not to numerical/solver instability (FBA infeasibility) in a given seed.

We are not resolving whether the heterogeneity reflects 'real biology' vs simulator-intrinsic noise-model artifacts (deterministic chaos vs genuine stochasticity) — this is an explicit scope caveat left unresolved by this test.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: In a genetically identical (wildtype) E. coli population grown under a single fixed condition, isogenic cells show substantial cell-to-cell variability in growth rate and ppGpp concentration driven by intrinsic stochastic noise, not genotype — i.e. the wildtype/basal design itself produces a broad, non-degenerate distribution of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across independent stochastic seeds (biological replicates of the same genotype), rather than all seeds converging to (near-)identical values.
drafts.h1: Across independent seeds of the same wildtype/basal design, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) has coefficient of variation (CV) >= 0.15, i.e. isogenic cells diverge substantially in phenotype despite identical genotype and environment.
drafts.h0: Per-seed growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) values across the wildtype/basal replicate population are tightly clustered (CV < 0.15), i.e. isogenic cells in a fixed environment behave essentially identically, with only negligible measurement/simulation noise.

rivals.claim: Rival A (noise floor artifact): apparent seed-to-seed spread in wildtype/basal merely reflects numerical/simulator noise (RNG seeding of the FBA/kinetic solver) rather than genuine biological stochasticity, so CV would shrink toward 0 as seeds increase or as a deterministic steady-state design is used.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a rrna_operon_knockout/basal design (same seeds, same generations) shows comparably small within-group CV and no significant welch_t difference in spread from wildtype/basal, that would support the noise-floor-artifact view rather than genotype-independent biological heterogeneity; conversely if rrna_operon_knockout shifts the MEAN sharply (large welch_t on growth_rate) while wildtype retains its own internal CV>=0.15, this supports real intrinsic noise distinct from a pure solver artifact.

rivals.claim: Rival B (condition-driven, not intrinsic, variability): apparent heterogeneity is actually driven by subtle differences in effective nutrient/media microenvironment baked into each seed's initialization rather than true intrinsic stochastic gene-expression noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV magnitude is similar across multiple static conditions (e.g. basal vs acetate) rather than collapsing in one and ballooning in another in a manner tracking media complexity, this weakens the condition-driven explanation; a condition-driven account predicts CV should vary strongly and systematically with condition identity rather than remaining in the predicted 0.15-0.30 band across conditions.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed RNG streams in the simulator are treated as biologically meaningful stochastic replicates (analogous to intrinsic noise sources: burst transcription, partitioning at division) and not purely numerical artifacts; this cannot be fully disentangled within the simulator and is recorded as a scope caveat.
Generation 3 is late enough for seed-to-seed divergence to manifest but early enough to avoid confounding by population bottlenecking or division-defect artifacts (checked via division_rate channel).

CV threshold of 0.15 as the H1/H0 boundary is a pragmatic operational cutoff chosen to be clearly above plausible numerical noise floor (<0.05) and consistent with reported single-cell growth-rate CVs in E. coli literature (typically 0.1-0.3).

The rrna_operon_knockout control is used only to establish that genotype perturbation shifts the MEAN/distribution detectably (proving the assay has sensitivity), not to claim it is the cause of wildtype intrinsic noise.

drafts.claim: In a genetically identical (isogenic) E. coli population growing under one fixed, static medium, intrinsic stochastic noise produces substantial cell-to-cell variability in growth rate and ppGpp concentration, i.e. phenotypic heterogeneity emerges from stochastic gene expression/metabolism alone, without genetic or environmental differences.

drafts.h0: Genetically identical cells run with different random seeds under the same wildtype/basal condition show negligible variability: CV(growth_rate) < 0.03 (3%), i.e. any spread is attributable to numerical/integration noise rather than biologically meaningful stochasticity.

No systematic shift in the MEAN (growth_rate mean approximately unchanged vs a near-deterministic reduced-noise reference), only increased SPREAD.

Reject H1 if |welch_t| < 2 (no significant difference in spread/mean) OR if CV(growth_rate) in wildtype/basal < 0.03.

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is purely numerical/integration artifact (solver/time-step noise), not biological stochasticity — any seed-to-seed spread would vanish or shrink dramatically under a reduced-noise/deterministic-like configuration.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, wildtype/basal_lownoise shows CV comparable to wildtype/basal (no real drop), i.e. the Welch test between them is non-significant and both CVs are similarly small, meaning the floor is numerical not biological.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is driven mainly by ribosome-allocation/translation capacity differences (extrinsic noise from ribosome_conc variation) rather than general stochastic kinetics, so clamping ribosome capacity (rrna_operon_knockout, which caps ribosome supply) should collapse growth_rate variability even though general stochasticity remains.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, rrna_operon_knockout/basal (reduced, more homogeneous ribosome pool) shows markedly LOWER CV(growth_rate) across seeds than wildtype/basal, despite both having the same stochastic simulation engine, implicating ribosome-pool variation (not generic noise) as the heterogeneity source.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic kinetics (gene expression bursts, partitioning at division, metabolic noise) are an adequate model of real intrinsic cell-to-cell variability, not merely numerical artifact — we treat any residual spread in a maximally-deterministic configuration as the numerical noise floor.

A 'basal_lownoise' condition exists in the envelope as a reduced-stochasticity variant of basal (e.g., smaller time step / disabled burst sampling); if unavailable, the floor is instead estimated from technical replicate variance of a single seed re-run, treated as auxiliary and not re-litigated.
Seeds are independent draws of the same isogenic genotype and media; no genetic differences are introduced across seeds.
Growth rate and ppGpp measurements are taken at matched generation count/time across seeds so comparisons are synchronized, not confounded by lineage age.

Whether rrna_operon_knockout is mechanistically simulated with a graded capacity effect (vs. lethal) is not knowable a priori; if it crashes growth outright (division_rate ~0), we treat that as inconclusive for the ribosome-allocation rival rather than as support for H0.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells in identical, constant media show substantial cell-to-cell variability in growth-related state variables purely from intrinsic stochastic noise (gene expression, partitioning, chemical fluctuations), even though no genetic or environmental difference distinguishes them. Specifically, replicate seeds of the wildtype/basal design (each seed = one stochastic realization of an isogenic cell lineage) will show a coefficient of variation (CV) in instantaneous growth_rate across seeds of at least 10-15%, and a non-trivial fraction of seeds (>=10%) will show division_rate < 1 (missed/delayed division) despite identical genotype and media.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic seeds run under identical wildtype/basal conditions, intrinsic stochastic noise produces measurable heterogeneity: CV(growth_rate) >= 10% across seeds, and ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged likewise show per-seed spread that is a sizeable fraction (>=20%) of the spread seen across distinct genetic/environmental perturbations (z_vs_corpus_spread not near zero).
drafts.h0: All inter-seed variability in growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, and fraction_trna_charged under wildtype/basal is attributable to simulation/numerical noise floor only, i.e. CV(growth_rate) < 10% across seeds and the welch_t comparing any two seed-subsets is not distinguishable from zero beyond platform noise (effectively no biologically meaningful heterogeneity beyond measurement floor).

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel sampled per seed (independent stochastic replicate lineages) under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) of growth_rate across seeds, and per-seed spread reported by disconfirm

operational_defs.observable: division_rate channel per seed
operational_defs.measure: fraction of seeds with division_rate < 1 across the seed population

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged channels per seed
operational_defs.measure: per-seed spread and z_vs_corpus_spread returned by disconfirm, compared against spread from a genetic perturbation (rrna_operon_knockout) to contextualize magnitude

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: positive, nonzero heterogeneity. Magnitude: CV(growth_rate) across 8 wildtype/basal seeds >= 10-15% (vs an assumed near-zero numerical floor of <5%); >=10% of seeds (at least 1 of 8) show division_rate < 1; ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged per-seed spread (sd/mean) >= 8-10%, with z_vs_corpus_spread indicating this intrinsic spread is at least ~20% as large as the spread induced by a genetic perturbation (rrna_operon_knockout) of ribosome capacity.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV(growth_rate) across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds directly from per-seed spread; separately run power_mde to establish the minimum detectable effect (MDE) at n=8 seeds. If observed CV(growth_rate) < 10% AND is below the MDE floor (i.e. we cannot distinguish it from pure numerical noise), reject H1 in favor of H0 (no meaningful intrinsic heterogeneity). If CV(growth_rate) >= 10% and exceeds the MDE floor, H1 stands.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(growth_rate) across seeds < 10%, indistinguishable from the platform's numerical noise floor as determined by power_mde, AND <10% of seeds show division_rate < 1 — i.e. isogenic cells behave essentially identically modulo trivial simulator noise.

test.statistic: CV (sd/mean) of growth_rate across seeds; min detectable effect at n=8
test.threshold: CV>=10% required AND effect must exceed MDE at n=8 seeds (power_mde reject-null threshold)

rivals.claim: Rival A: observed inter-seed variability is dominated by numerical/solver artifacts (e.g. FBA solver tie-breaking, integration step noise) rather than biologically meaningful stochastic gene expression noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: fba_objective channel would show erratic/non-converged values correlating with growth_rate outliers across seeds, and the spread would NOT scale with any biological knob (e.g. would be identical in magnitude between wildtype/basal and a rrna_operon_knockout control, since it's solver noise not biology).

rivals.claim: Rival B: heterogeneity is real but entirely driven by a single dominant stochastic module (e.g. ppGpp/RelA burst dynamics) rather than being a general systems-wide noise property; i.e. variability is concentrated in one channel and does not propagate to growth_rate or division_rate.
rivals.distinguishing_result: ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged show high per-seed spread but growth_rate and division_rate CV stay below the 10% threshold, showing noise is buffered/non-propagating rather than producing visible phenotypic heterogeneity.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seeds in the wildtype/basal design are independent stochastic realizations of an isogenic lineage (no shared random state across seeds) so that inter-seed spread is a valid proxy for cell-to-cell heterogeneity.

The simulator's intrinsic numerical/solver noise floor is small relative to genuine biological stochasticity (gene expression bursting, partitioning at division, metabolite fluctuations) — if not, Rival A cannot be fully excluded by this platform and is recorded as a scope caveat.

growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged, and division_rate are computed consistently across seeds with the same generation count and condition, so differences are not confounded by unequal simulated time.

The rrna_operon_knockout control's spread serves only as a rough magnitude yardstick (genetic perturbation vs intrinsic noise), not a strict causal isolator of a specific noise source — deeper mechanistic attribution (e.g. which gene's bursting drives it) is out of scope for this sim's resolution.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in identical, constant basal medium exhibit substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity driven by intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism, not by genetic or environmental differences: across replicate seeds of the wildtype/basal design, growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show a coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds/cells of roughly 15-30%, well above the ~2-5% CV expected from numerical/solver noise alone, and the pooled distribution of growth_rate is unimodal (not bimodal) since no bistable switch is engaged in basal conditions.
drafts.h1: Across independent stochastic seeds of the same wildtype/basal design (identical genotype, identical fixed medium), the cell-to-cell CV of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc is large (>=15%), reflecting genuine intrinsic noise in gene expression/metabolism rather than measurement or solver artifact.
drafts.h0: Seed-to-seed variability in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc for wildtype/basal is small (CV <5%), consistent with the variation being attributable to numerical/integration noise rather than biologically meaningful stochasticity; i.e., genetically identical cells in identical conditions behave essentially identically.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc channels recorded per seed at matched timepoints across many stochastic replicate seeds of wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) across seeds, and Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) of the pooled per-seed growth_rate distribution

operational_defs.observable: spread of growth_rate/ppgpp_conc across seeds compared against the z_vs_corpus_spread descriptive baseline and against a tighter-noise discriminating control (rrna_operon_knockout, which reduces ribosome-capacity buffering and should amplify, not shrink, variance if the signal is biological)
operational_defs.measure: per-seed spread (SD, CV) and welch_t comparison of variance proxy (|deviation from seed mean|) between wildtype/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal

drafts.predicted_effect: Growth_rate CV across seeds (wildtype/basal, n=8 seeds, 3 generations) ~20% (range 15-30%); ppgpp_conc CV similarly ~20-25%. Pooled growth_rate distribution is unimodal: bimodality coefficient BC < 0.555. A rrna_operon_knockout/basal control (reduced ribosome buffering capacity) is predicted to show growth_rate CV increased by >=1.5x relative to wildtype/basal (e.g., ~30-45%), consistent with noise amplification rather than a shift in mean alone.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed growth_rate CV across n=8 seeds for wildtype/basal (3 generations). Also compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on the pooled per-seed growth_rate values. H1 requires CV>=15% (treated as the effect magnitude versus a CV<5% noise-floor null, assessed via power_mde given n=8) AND BC<=0.555 (unimodal). Reject H1 (support H0 of near-identical behavior) if CV<5%, i.e., variability sits at or below the numerical-noise floor.
falsifier.refuting_result: Observed cross-seed growth_rate CV <5% (indistinguishable from solver/integration noise floor) and/or BC>0.555 indicating the population is actually bimodal (suggesting a discrete switch rather than continuous intrinsic noise) — either result falsifies the 'substantial continuous intrinsic heterogeneity' claim.

test.statistic: coefficient_of_variation + bimodality_bc
test.threshold: CV>=15% treated as real effect only if it exceeds min-detectable-effect at n=8 (power_mde check); BC<=0.555 for unimodality

rivals.claim: Apparent heterogeneity is a bimodal switch (e.g., a bistable stringent-response or metabolic state), not continuous intrinsic noise — cells fall into two discrete subpopulations.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled growth_rate (or ppgpp_conc) across seeds shows bimodality_bc > 0.555, i.e., a clear two-cluster split with separated means, rather than a single unimodal spread.

rivals.claim: The observed seed-to-seed spread is purely a numerical/solver artifact (integration noise, FBA re-solve jitter) and not biologically meaningful stochasticity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: CV across seeds is <5% and statistically indistinguishable (welch_t < 2) from a technical-noise proxy; i.e., the spread fails to exceed the noise floor expected from power_mde at n=8.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is driven mainly by ribosome-allocation/ppGpp coupling being deterministic given slightly different initial conditions, not by ongoing intrinsic stochastic noise — a ribosome-capacity perturbation would simply shift the mean, not the variance.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal shows growth_rate CV approximately EQUAL to wildtype/basal (no variance amplification), only a shifted mean — contradicting the noise-amplification prediction of H1.

auxiliary_assumptions: Each seed in the wildtype/basal design instantiates independent stochastic trajectories (intrinsic noise sources: transcription/translation bursts, partitioning at division) rather than merely different random number draws with no biological consequence.

8 seeds x 3 generations is sufficient to estimate CV and BC with usable precision; if power_mde flags this n as underpowered for the claimed 15% effect, that is logged as a scope caveat rather than grounds to inflate seeds beyond the modest-scale guidance.
growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are read at matched developmental/cell-cycle timepoints across seeds so that heterogeneity reflects stochastic state rather than phase misalignment.

The simulator's intrinsic noise model (if any) is the operative noise source; we cannot use this sim to distinguish deterministic chaos from true stochastic noise as the generative mechanism — this is recorded as an acknowledged scope limit, not pursued further.

rrna_operon_knockout is assumed to reduce ribosome buffering capacity without being so severe (within 3 generations) that division_rate collapses to near-zero, which would confound variance estimates with lethality.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells grown under identical conditions (wildtype/basal) display substantial cell-to-cell variability in growth rate and ppGpp-related stringent response channels, purely from intrinsic stochastic gene expression/metabolic noise — not from genotype or environment differences.
drafts.h1: Across a population of isogenic cells simulated with independent stochastic seeds under the same condition (wildtype/basal), the distribution of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds shows substantial dispersion (CV >= 15% for growth_rate) and/or a bimodal split (Sarle's BC > 0.555) rather than collapsing to a near-point value (CV < 5%).
drafts.h0: Genetically identical cells under identical conditions show negligible phenotypic variability: growth_rate CV across seeds < 5% and ppgpp_conc distribution is unimodal (BC <= 0.555), consistent with the simulator producing near-deterministic trajectories once condition is fixed.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed spread of fraction_trna_charged as a secondary corroborating noise channel

drafts.predicted_effect: Growth_rate CV across >=6 seeds of wildtype/basal >= 15% (vs <5% expected under a deterministic/no-noise null), and ppgpp_conc pooled across seeds shows either CV >= 20% or bimodality coefficient > 0.555, indicating a sizable high/low ppGpp subpopulation (predicted split ~30/70 if bimodal).

Reject H1 (fail to disconfirm H0) if growth_rate CV < 5% AND ppgpp BC <= 0.555 (unimodal, low spread) — i.e., the population behaves near-deterministically despite shared genotype/condition.
falsifier.refuting_result: growth_rate CV computed at 3% and ppgpp_conc BC = 0.41 (unimodal, tight distribution), showing isogenic cells converge to nearly identical phenotypes with only trivial numerical-seed noise.

rivals.claim: Apparent variability is just numerical/seed-sampling noise from the stochastic solver, not biologically meaningful heterogeneity (e.g., bistable expression states).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If variability is pure solver noise, increasing seeds would not reveal any structured bimodal subpopulation (BC stays <=0.555) and CV would scale down as sqrt(1/n) artifacts rather than remaining stable as a biological signature; also a rrna_operon_knockout (reducing ribosome capacity) should not systematically shift the variance structure if it's just noise.

rivals.claim: Variability is driven by extrinsic differences in ppGpp/stringent-response machinery copy number fluctuations (RelA-dependent), not generic stochastic gene expression — i.e., a mechanistic bistability in the stringent response specifically, not broad noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout (removing RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis) should collapse ppgpp_conc bimodality/dispersion toward a tight unimodal distribution while growth_rate CV remains similarly dispersed (noise persists elsewhere), isolating the stringent-response-specific contribution from general intrinsic noise.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed trajectories at matched generation number represent independent isogenic 'cells' sampled from the same stochastic process (ceteris paribus on condition and genotype).

The simulator's stochastic kinetic noise model is a faithful-enough proxy for real intrinsic biochemical noise; we do not adjudicate whether it matches wet-lab single-cell CVs exactly (deterministic-chaos vs stochastic-noise distinction is out of scope for this sim).
growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are read at a comparable steady-state window across seeds/generations so that transient startup effects do not inflate apparent variability.

relA knockout is assumed to be mechanistically implemented in the simulator's ppGpp synthesis pathway (downstream testing will confirm); if not simulated, this falls back to an auxiliary-assumption failure rather than refuting H1 itself.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells simulated under identical media conditions (wildtype/basal) exhibit substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity in growth rate and ppGpp concentration, arising purely from intrinsic stochastic noise (seed-to-seed variation) rather than genetic or environmental differences — i.e. the population shows a coefficient of variation (CV) in growth_rate across seeds of roughly 10-20%, well above the ~2-3% CV expected from numerical/discretization noise alone.
drafts.h1: Across replicate seeds of the wildtype/basal design (identical genotype, identical media), the per-seed growth_rate distribution has CV >= 10%, and this spread is not an artifact of trivial solver noise (i.e. it exceeds the CV seen in a near-deterministic steady-state-only control by at least 3x).
drafts.h0: Per-seed growth_rate values under wildtype/basal are effectively constant (CV < 3%), consistent with the simulator producing deterministic or near-deterministic outputs across seeds for isogenic cells in a fixed environment — i.e. no meaningful intrinsic phenotypic heterogeneity.

operational_defs.construct: phenotypic heterogeneity among genetically identical cells
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel sampled across independent seeds within the same perturbation/condition design
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of growth_rate across seeds; secondary channel ppgpp_conc CV across the same seeds

operational_defs.construct: intrinsic stochastic noise vs deterministic/numerical artifact

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: positive — isogenic replicate cells show real heterogeneity, not just noise floor. Magnitude: CV(growth_rate) across seeds >= 10% under wildtype/basal with kinetic elongation, versus CV <= 3% under the steady_state control (so a >=3x ratio). Secondary channel ppgpp_conc expected CV ~15-25% across the same seeds, reflecting coupled stringent-response noise.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of growth_rate, target (kinetic) vs reference (steady_state) across seeds; reject H0 if |welch_t| >= 2 AND CV(target) >= 3x CV(reference). Also require power_mde check that n=6 seeds can detect a CV difference of this size.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(growth_rate) under kinetic wildtype/basal is < 3x CV under steady_state wildtype/basal (e.g. both ~2-4%), or Welch |t| < 2, indicating the apparent heterogeneity is within solver/replicate noise rather than a real stochastic phenotype signal.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and CV ratio >= 3x

rivals.claim: Apparent heterogeneity is purely numerical/discretization noise from the stochastic solver, not biologically meaningful variation (no real distinct phenotypic states).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, CV(kinetic) and CV(steady_state) controls would be statistically indistinguishable (Welch |t| < 2) despite steady_state being near-deterministic; i.e. the kinetic model adds no extra spread beyond solver round-off.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity is driven mainly by cell-cycle phase / mass-doubling asynchrony across seeds rather than by stochastic gene expression or metabolic noise per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, growth_rate CV would track strongly with dry_mass or cell_mass CV at the same timepoints (both channels co-vary tightly across seeds), and a rrna_operon_knockout control (perturbing ribosome capacity, which shifts cycle timing) would markedly change growth_rate CV, whereas ppgpp_conc CV would stay comparatively flat — pointing to cycle-timing artifacts rather than stringent-response-linked noise.

auxiliary_assumptions: Seed-to-seed variation in the simulator is intended to represent genuine intrinsic biochemical/stochastic noise (molecule-count fluctuations in transcription/translation/metabolism), not merely pseudo-random-number-generator artifacts unrelated to biology.

The kinetic elongation model engages the stochastic ppGpp/RelA machinery (rela_conc, ppgpp_conc kinetic species) needed to observe stringent-response-linked noise; steady_state suppresses most of this and serves as a valid near-deterministic noise floor.

6 seeds x 3 generations is sufficient to estimate a per-seed CV with enough precision for the Welch comparison; if power_mde flags this n as underpowered for the predicted effect size, the magnitude claim (not the qualitative direction) would need revision.
Division_rate stays ~1 (no lethality) across all three designs so that growth_rate differences reflect phenotypic noise rather than confounded death/division defects.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing under identical static media conditions (wildtype/basal) exhibit substantial intrinsic cell-to-cell variability in growth rate and ppGpp concentration purely from stochastic gene expression/partitioning noise, not from genetic or environmental differences — i.e., the across-seed distribution of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc at a fixed condition has a coefficient of variation (CV) substantially greater than zero (CV_growth_rate >= 10%, CV_ppgpp_conc >= 20%) and is unimodal (not two discrete subpopulations), reflecting continuous intrinsic noise rather than a bistable switch.
drafts.h1: Across independent stochastic seeds of the SAME genotype under the SAME static condition (wildtype/basal), growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show non-trivial dispersion (CV_growth_rate >= 10%, CV_ppgpp_conc >= 20%) that is significantly greater than near-zero technical/numerical noise, and the pooled distribution is unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555).
drafts.h0: Across seeds of wildtype/basal, growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are effectively constant (CV ~ 0, i.e., indistinguishable from simulation/integration noise), meaning the model produces deterministic, identical trajectories regardless of seed — any apparent variability is measurement/arithmetic noise, not biologically meaningful heterogeneity.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed final-generation growth_rate value; compute CV = SD/mean across seeds

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed final-generation ppgpp_conc value; compute CV = SD/mean across seeds

operational_defs.construct: bimodal subpopulation structure vs continuous noise
operational_defs.observable: pooled per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc values
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled seed values; BC>0.555 flags bimodal/subpopulation structure

drafts.predicted_effect: Positive, moderate-magnitude intrinsic noise: CV_growth_rate ~ 10-15% and CV_ppgpp_conc ~ 20-30% across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal, significantly above a near-zero technical-noise reference (effect size |t|>=2 vs a tight reference distribution), with the pooled distribution unimodal (BC <= 0.555) — i.e., continuous Gaussian-like spread, not two discrete subpopulations.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of growth_rate (and separately ppgpp_conc) across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds vs the wildtype/basal_tight low-noise reference seeds; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 AND CV_growth_rate>=10% (or CV_ppgpp_conc>=20%) in the target. Additionally compute Sarle's BC on pooled wildtype/basal seed values; if BC>0.555 the unimodality sub-claim is refuted (heterogeneity is bimodal, not continuous noise).
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t|<2 or CV_growth_rate<10% and CV_ppgpp_conc<20%, seed-to-seed variability is statistically indistinguishable from the low-noise reference, refuting H1 (cells are effectively deterministic clones). If instead BC>0.555, H1's unimodal-noise claim is refuted even though variability exists (true bistable subpopulations, not continuous noise).

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for CV significance; BC>0.555 for bimodality refutation of unimodal sub-claim

rivals.claim: Variability is an artifact of insufficient seed sampling / RNG burn-in, not genuine biological noise — more seeds would collapse CV toward the tight reference.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a power_mde check shows the observed CV is within the minimum detectable effect at n=8 seeds (i.e., underpowered), the apparent spread could be sampling noise rather than real heterogeneity; running additional seeds would need to confirm CV stabilizes rather than shrinking toward reference levels.

rivals.claim: Observed heterogeneity reflects a genuine bistable switch (e.g., a ppGpp-driven stringent-response toggle) producing two discrete subpopulations (slow/fast growers), not continuous stochastic noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Sarle's BC > 0.555 on pooled growth_rate or ppgpp_conc values across seeds, indicating a two-cluster split rather than a single unimodal spread.

rivals.claim: Apparent cell-to-cell variability is driven by a deterministic ribosome-allocation/ppGpp feedback coupling rather than intrinsic stochastic partitioning noise — i.e., it is mechanistically forced by the RelA/SpoT regulatory loop, not emergent noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout background that abolishes ppGpp synthesis should still show comparable CV_growth_rate across seeds if the heterogeneity is intrinsic/stochastic rather than RelA-pathway-driven; if CV_growth_rate collapses toward the tight reference in the relA knockout, the rival (deterministic RelA-driven heterogeneity) is supported instead.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's intrinsic stochastic modules (expression noise, partitioning at division) are active under default wildtype/basal runs and are the dominant noise source being measured, not solver/integration artifacts.

A 'wildtype/basal_tight' reference (same condition, treated as near-deterministic baseline) is a reasonable proxy for technical/numerical noise; the simulator does not provide a literal noise-off switch, so this reference is the closest in-envelope approximation.
Final-generation (gen 3) snapshot values are representative of steady-state per-seed phenotype rather than transient startup effects.

8 seeds provide adequate power to detect CV differences of the predicted magnitude (~10-30%); if underpowered per the power_mde check, this is logged as a scope caveat rather than used to over-interpret a null.

Whether relA knockout mechanistically ablates ppGpp synthesis in this model build is not independently verifiable here; its result is interpreted as a discriminating control only to the extent the simulator implements the RelA/SpoT module.

drafts.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
drafts.claim: In a genetically identical (isogenic) E. coli population grown under the same static medium, intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism produces substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic variability: across seeds, single-cell growth rate and ppGpp concentration will show coefficient of variation (CV) on the order of 15-30%, and the ppGpp distribution across many isogenic replicates will be unimodal (not a bet-hedging bimodal split) under unstressed basal conditions.
drafts.h1: Isogenic wildtype cells under identical basal conditions exhibit substantial intrinsic phenotypic heterogeneity: per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc vary with CV >= 15% around the population mean, reflecting stochastic gene-expression/metabolic noise rather than deterministic uniformity.
drafts.h0: Isogenic wildtype cells under identical basal conditions are phenotypically near-uniform: per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc vary only by simulator/numerical noise, with CV < 15% and no detectable spread beyond replicate noise (disconfirm welch_t < 2 when comparing low-noise vs normal-noise seed subsets, and no excess dispersion vs reference).

operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of growth_rate across seeds; secondary CV of ppgpp_conc across seeds

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged per-seed spread, which depend on stochastic synthetase/charging kinetics

drafts.predicted_effect: Positive, moderate-magnitude intrinsic noise: CV(growth_rate) and CV(ppgpp_conc) across 8 isogenic seeds ~ 15-30% (point estimate ~20%), population distribution of ppgpp_conc remains UNIMODAL (BC <= 0.555, i.e., no discrete bet-hedging subpopulations) under basal unstressed growth.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed CV of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds; separately compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values. H1 requires CV(growth_rate) >= 15% AND CV(ppgpp_conc) >= 15% AND BC <= 0.555 (unimodal). Reject H1 if CV(growth_rate) < 15% (cells behave near-identically) OR if BC > 0.555 (variability is actually a discrete bimodal split, favoring a bet-hedging/multistability rival rather than continuous intrinsic noise).
falsifier.refuting_result: Per-seed CV(growth_rate) < 15% (e.g., ~5%), showing isogenic replicates are essentially uniform beyond simulator noise floor, OR BC > 0.555 indicating a discrete two-state (bimodal) population rather than continuous unimodal noise.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc; CV computed directly from per-seed spread/mean
test.threshold: BC <= 0.555 for unimodality; CV >= 15% for both growth_rate and ppgpp_conc to confirm H1

rivals.claim: Rival A (numerical/simulator noise only): observed seed-to-seed spread is purely a numerical artifact of the stochastic solver/seeding, not biologically meaningful intrinsic noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(growth_rate) and CV(ppgpp_conc) stay below ~5-10% (near the simulator's floor) and show no structured covariation with ppgpp/tRNA-charging channels, this favors Rival A over genuine biological intrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Rival B (deterministic bet-hedging / bistable subpopulations): variability is not continuous stochastic noise but reflects discrete alternative physiological states (e.g., a stringent-response-locked subpopulation vs a growing subpopulation), producing a bimodal ppGpp distribution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: BC > 0.555 on pooled ppgpp_conc across seeds, with a clear two-cluster split (e.g., low vs high ppGpp clusters), would support Rival B instead of unimodal intrinsic noise.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed random-number stream is an adequate proxy for biological intrinsic stochasticity (transcription/translation bursting, partitioning noise), not merely numerical rounding noise.
8 seeds is sufficient to estimate CV and a 2-cluster BC split without being dominated by sampling error; results are treated as a point estimate pending larger seed counts on approval.
Generation 3 is early/mid exponential growth where steady-state charging dynamics are representative, not confounded by division-timing artifacts.

The relA knockout control isolates whether any observed ppGpp-related variability depends on RelA-driven stringent response machinery, distinguishing stochastic basal noise (persists in relA KO) from a RelA-triggered bet-hedging mechanism (abolished or altered in relA KO).
Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are treated as read out at matched generation across seeds (not time-averaged over the whole run), avoiding conflation of noise with trajectory drift.

select_score.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
select_score.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing in the same medium (wildtype/basal) show substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity driven by intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression and metabolism, such that a population of replicate seeds displays a coefficient of variation (CV) in growth_rate of roughly 15-25% across seeds/cells, rather than converging to a single deterministic value.
select_score.h1: Across isogenic replicate simulations (same genotype, same wildtype/basal condition, differing only in stochastic seed), single-cell growth_rate (and correlated channels: ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged) exhibit a non-trivial spread (CV_growth_rate >= 15%) that exceeds the technical/numerical noise floor of the simulator, reflecting genuine biological noise rather than identical deterministic trajectories.
select_score.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds under wildtype/basal converge to effectively the same growth_rate trajectory; the observed per-seed spread in growth_rate is indistinguishable from numerical/integration noise, i.e. CV_growth_rate < 5% and the distribution of per-seed final growth_rate is unimodal and tight (no detectable heterogeneity beyond simulator floor).

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel sampled per seed at end of simulated generations
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of growth_rate across seeds; also per-seed spread reported by disconfirm

operational_defs.construct: intrinsic stochastic noise in gene expression
operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged and ppgpp_conc channels per seed
operational_defs.measure: CV of fraction_trna_charged and ppgpp_conc across seeds; used as secondary corroborating channels

operational_defs.construct: non-genetic heterogeneity vs transcriptional noise amplification
operational_defs.observable: division_rate per seed under rrna_operon_knockout control vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: bimodality_bc of pooled growth_rate values to check for discrete subpopulations vs continuous spread

select_score.predicted_effect: Direction: isogenic seeds will show measurable dispersion, not convergence. Magnitude: CV_growth_rate ~15-25% across 8 seeds in wildtype/basal (vs a numerical-noise-floor expectation of <5% if purely deterministic/integration-limited). Pooled growth_rate distribution is expected to be unimodal (BC <= 0.555) reflecting continuous stochastic variation rather than discrete subpopulations.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute CV of growth_rate across 8 seeds for wildtype/basal at generation 4; treat H0 as a power/equivalence claim: if observed CV < 5% (within min-detectable-effect bound at n=8), accept H0 (no detectable heterogeneity beyond noise floor). Also run welch_disconfirm of per-seed growth_rate means between two independently-seeded batches (4 vs 4) of wildtype/basal as an internal consistency check; reject H1 if |welch_t| < 2 AND CV < 5%.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV_growth_rate < 5% across seeds AND |welch_t| < 2 between the two seed-batches, indicating seeds converge to a single deterministic trajectory with no meaningful heterogeneity.

test.statistic: CV_growth_rate with min-detectable-effect check at n=8 seeds, cross-checked by welch_t of per-seed means between seed-split batches
test.threshold: CV >= 15% rejects H0 (heterogeneity confirmed); CV < 5% (below MDE) accepts H0 as equivalence

rivals.claim: Rival A: observed spread is purely numerical/integration artifact of the stochastic solver, not biological heterogeneity (i.e., the simulator injects noise unrelated to real gene-expression stochasticity).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, CV of growth_rate would be similar in magnitude to CV in a control with reduced stochastic sampling granularity (e.g., same seeds but condition acetate, a slower-growth static medium) in a way uncorrelated with any biologically meaningful channel (ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged) — i.e., no cross-channel covariance structure, just white noise.

rivals.claim: Rival B: heterogeneity is not continuous/intrinsic noise but reflects a discrete bistable switch (e.g., a bimodal ppGpp/growth state), so cells fall into two distinct subpopulations rather than a smooth distribution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc of pooled growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) across seeds would show BC > 0.555, indicating two separable clusters rather than unimodal spread, which would refute the 'smooth stochastic noise' framing of H1 even if overall CV is elevated.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed stochastic trajectories in the simulator are intended to model intrinsic biochemical noise (reaction firing stochasticity, partitioning at division), not merely pseudo-random numerical artifacts; this cannot be independently verified inside the simulator and is taken as a scope caveat.
8 seeds provide adequate (though modest) power to estimate CV and detect a >=15% heterogeneity signal; a formal power_mde check is used to avoid over-claiming equivalence from an underpowered null.
Growth_rate measured at generation 4 is a stable summary statistic (post any initial transient from seeding/initialization).

The rrna_operon_knockout control is assumed to perturb ribosome capacity without independently altering the stochastic noise-generation machinery itself, isolating the capacity-vs-intrinsic-noise distinction.
Media condition (basal) is held constant across all designs so that any observed heterogeneity is attributable to seed-level stochasticity, not condition differences.

params.note: discriminating control: reduces ribosome capacity, a mechanistic channel for noise amplification via translation bursting; tests whether heterogeneity scales with ribosome allocation (Rival mechanism) vs persists regardless (pure stochastic noise)
