hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells growing under identical static media conditions (wildtype/basal) exhibit substantial intrinsic cell-to-cell variability in growth rate and ppGpp concentration purely from stochastic gene expression/partitioning noise, not from genetic or environmental differences — i.e., the across-seed distribution of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc at a fixed condition has a coefficient of variation (CV) substantially greater than zero (CV_growth_rate >= 10%, CV_ppgpp_conc >= 20%) and is unimodal (not two discrete subpopulations), reflecting continuous intrinsic noise rather than a bistable switch.
hypothesis.h1: Across independent stochastic seeds of the SAME genotype under the SAME static condition (wildtype/basal), growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show non-trivial dispersion (CV_growth_rate >= 10%, CV_ppgpp_conc >= 20%) that is significantly greater than near-zero technical/numerical noise, and the pooled distribution is unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555).
hypothesis.h0: Across seeds of wildtype/basal, growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are effectively constant (CV ~ 0, i.e., indistinguishable from simulation/integration noise), meaning the model produces deterministic, identical trajectories regardless of seed — any apparent variability is measurement/arithmetic noise, not biologically meaningful heterogeneity.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed final-generation growth_rate value; compute CV = SD/mean across seeds

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed final-generation ppgpp_conc value; compute CV = SD/mean across seeds

operational_defs.construct: bimodal subpopulation structure vs continuous noise
operational_defs.observable: pooled per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc values
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled seed values; BC>0.555 flags bimodal/subpopulation structure

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Positive, moderate-magnitude intrinsic noise: CV_growth_rate ~ 10-15% and CV_ppgpp_conc ~ 20-30% across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal, significantly above a near-zero technical-noise reference (effect size |t|>=2 vs a tight reference distribution), with the pooled distribution unimodal (BC <= 0.555) — i.e., continuous Gaussian-like spread, not two discrete subpopulations.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of growth_rate (and separately ppgpp_conc) across the 8 wildtype/basal seeds vs the wildtype/basal_tight low-noise reference seeds; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 AND CV_growth_rate>=10% (or CV_ppgpp_conc>=20%) in the target. Additionally compute Sarle's BC on pooled wildtype/basal seed values; if BC>0.555 the unimodality sub-claim is refuted (heterogeneity is bimodal, not continuous noise).
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t|<2 or CV_growth_rate<10% and CV_ppgpp_conc<20%, seed-to-seed variability is statistically indistinguishable from the low-noise reference, refuting H1 (cells are effectively deterministic clones). If instead BC>0.555, H1's unimodal-noise claim is refuted even though variability exists (true bistable subpopulations, not continuous noise).

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for CV significance; BC>0.555 for bimodality refutation of unimodal sub-claim

rivals.claim: Variability is an artifact of insufficient seed sampling / RNG burn-in, not genuine biological noise — more seeds would collapse CV toward the tight reference.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a power_mde check shows the observed CV is within the minimum detectable effect at n=8 seeds (i.e., underpowered), the apparent spread could be sampling noise rather than real heterogeneity; running additional seeds would need to confirm CV stabilizes rather than shrinking toward reference levels.

rivals.claim: Observed heterogeneity reflects a genuine bistable switch (e.g., a ppGpp-driven stringent-response toggle) producing two discrete subpopulations (slow/fast growers), not continuous stochastic noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Sarle's BC > 0.555 on pooled growth_rate or ppgpp_conc values across seeds, indicating a two-cluster split rather than a single unimodal spread.

rivals.claim: Apparent cell-to-cell variability is driven by a deterministic ribosome-allocation/ppGpp feedback coupling rather than intrinsic stochastic partitioning noise — i.e., it is mechanistically forced by the RelA/SpoT regulatory loop, not emergent noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout background that abolishes ppGpp synthesis should still show comparable CV_growth_rate across seeds if the heterogeneity is intrinsic/stochastic rather than RelA-pathway-driven; if CV_growth_rate collapses toward the tight reference in the relA knockout, the rival (deterministic RelA-driven heterogeneity) is supported instead.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's intrinsic stochastic modules (expression noise, partitioning at division) are active under default wildtype/basal runs and are the dominant noise source being measured, not solver/integration artifacts.

A 'wildtype/basal_tight' reference (same condition, treated as near-deterministic baseline) is a reasonable proxy for technical/numerical noise; the simulator does not provide a literal noise-off switch, so this reference is the closest in-envelope approximation.
Final-generation (gen 3) snapshot values are representative of steady-state per-seed phenotype rather than transient startup effects.

8 seeds provide adequate power to detect CV differences of the predicted magnitude (~10-30%); if underpowered per the power_mde check, this is logged as a scope caveat rather than used to over-interpret a null.

Whether relA knockout mechanistically ablates ppGpp synthesis in this model build is not independently verifiable here; its result is interpreted as a discriminating control only to the extent the simulator implements the RelA/SpoT module.

params.note: low-noise numerical reference: same seeds/condition but treated as tight technical-noise baseline for CV comparison

hypothesis.question: Do genetically identical cells behave differently?
hypothesis.claim: Isogenic E. coli cells grown under identical static media conditions (basal) exhibit substantial cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity (intrinsic noise) in growth rate and ppGpp concentration, arising from stochastic gene expression/reaction timing rather than genetic or environmental differences: across seeds, per-seed growth_rate shows CV >= 15% and per-seed ppgpp_conc shows CV >= 20%, with the pooled growth_rate distribution unimodal (not bistable). A relA knockout (removing the ppGpp-synthesis sensor for uncharged tRNA) is the primary interventional probe of whether this heterogeneity is RelA/stringent-response-driven versus arising elsewhere (e.g., ribosome allocation, charging stochasticity): H1-mechanism predicts the relA KO substantially collapses ppgpp_conc CV (to <10%) while growth_rate CV remains >=10% (noise persists via a RelA-independent route), evaluated with the SAME statistic (per-seed CV across 8 seeds, 4 generations, basal only) used for wildtype, so the comparison is symmetric and not confounded by an extra condition axis.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds of wildtype cells under basal condition, CV(growth_rate) across seeds is >=15% and CV(ppgpp_conc) across seeds is >=20%, reflecting genuine intrinsic stochastic noise, with the pooled growth_rate distribution unimodal (BC<=0.555). Furthermore, in a relA-knockout background measured under the identical basal/8-seed/4-generation design, CV(ppgpp_conc) collapses to <10% (RelA is the dominant generator of ppGpp noise) while CV(growth_rate) remains >=10% (growth noise has a RelA-independent source), confirming RelA-dependent stringent-response bursting as a genuine causal contributor rather than a bystander correlate.
hypothesis.h0: Isogenic replicate seeds under basal show growth_rate and ppgpp_conc CVs that are small (<15% and <20% respectively, consistent with sampling noise only). Alternatively, if CV thresholds ARE met in wildtype, the relA-knockout null is that removing RelA does not shrink ppgpp_conc CV (stays >=20%, |welch_t|<2 vs wildtype), meaning the observed ppGpp variance is not RelA-dependent and the causal mechanistic claim is false even if heterogeneity itself exists.

operational_defs.construct: phenotypic heterogeneity among genetically identical cells
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed value of growth_rate channel at matched generation (last generation, gen 4); CV = sd/mean across 8 seeds

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed value of ppgpp_conc channel at matched generation (gen 4); CV = sd/mean across 8 seeds

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled per-seed growth_rate values (wildtype/basal, 8 seeds x 4 generations)

operational_defs.construct: RelA-dependence of ppGpp noise (causal mechanism probe)
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc in relA-knockout vs wildtype, both basal/8 seeds/gen4
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of per-seed ppgpp_conc values comparing relA_KO/basal vs wildtype/basal, plus per-group CV as effect magnitude

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: positive heterogeneity exists in wildtype. Magnitude: CV(growth_rate) across 8 seeds >=15% (expected ~18-25%), CV(ppgpp_conc) >=20% (expected ~25-35%), pooled growth_rate BC <=0.555 (unimodal). In relA-KO/basal (matched design): CV(ppgpp_conc) collapses to <10% (point estimate ~5-8%, a >60% relative reduction from wildtype), while CV(growth_rate) stays >=10% (point estimate ~12-18%), showing growth noise is only partially RelA-dependent.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (heterogeneity): compute CV=sd/mean of per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc at gen4 across 8 seeds of wildtype/basal; compute Sarle's BC over pooled growth_rate. Reject H1-heterogeneity if growth_rate CV<15% AND ppgpp_conc CV<20% (power_mde confirms n=8 sufficient to detect these), or if BC>0.555 (rejects unimodality, supports Rival B). Step 2 (causal mechanism): Welch t-test comparing ppgpp_conc per-seed values of relA_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal (same gen4, 8 seeds, 4 generations design); require |welch_t|>=2 with relA_KO showing lower mean/CV. Reject H1-mechanism if relA_KO ppgpp_conc CV is NOT reduced below 10% (i.e., stays >=20%, statistically indistinguishable from wildtype, |welch_t|<2).
falsifier.refuting_result: growth_rate CV=6% and ppgpp_conc CV=9% in wildtype/basal (below thresholds, power_mde confirms n=8 sufficient) refutes H1-heterogeneity outright. Separately, even if heterogeneity is confirmed, if relA_knockout/basal ppgpp_conc CV remains ~25% (welch_t vs wildtype <2, not significantly different), this refutes H1-mechanism: RelA is not the dominant driver, and ppGpp variance is a bystander correlate of some other noise source (e.g., ribosome_conc or fraction_trna_charged fluctuations) rather than causally RelA-dependent.

test.statistic: Welch t comparing per-seed ppgpp_conc (gen4, 8 seeds) between relA_knockout/basal and wildtype/basal; CV(sd/mean) computed per group as the effect magnitude
test.threshold: |welch_t|>=2 AND relA_KO ppgpp_conc CV<10% (vs wildtype CV>=20%) required to confirm RelA-dependence; also require growth_rate CV>=15%/ppgpp_conc CV>=20% in wildtype/basal alone (via power_mde-validated CV thresholds) to confirm baseline heterogeneity

rivals.claim: Rival A (initial-condition sampling artifact): apparent seed-to-seed variance is driven by differences in initial mass/division phase at t=0, not persistent stochastic kinetics -- extrinsic not intrinsic, and would shrink with more generations.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(growth_rate) measured at generation 4 (wildtype/basal, 4-gen design) is substantially smaller than at generation 1 (wildtype/basal, 1-gen design) -- e.g., drops by >50% -- that supports Rival A rather than persistent intrinsic noise; H1 predicts CV stays >=15% across generations 1 and 4.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp-driven bistability, not simple noise): heterogeneity in growth_rate reflects a genuine bimodal stringent-response switch (subpopulation locked high-ppGpp) rather than continuous intrinsic noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Sarle's BC over pooled growth_rate (wildtype/basal) exceeds 0.555, indicating a 2-cluster split, that supports Rival B's bistability mechanism over H1's unimodal-noise claim.

rivals.claim: Rival C (ppGpp variance is a passive bystander of ribosome/tRNA-charging noise, not RelA-synthesis bursting): fraction_trna_charged or ribosome_conc fluctuations drive ppgpp_conc variance independently of RelA activity level, so RelA is just a linear transducer, not the noise source.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA_knockout/basal shows ppgpp_conc CV collapsing to <10% (as H1-mechanism predicts), this REFUTES Rival C (RelA removal would not matter if the noise originated purely upstream in charging); if instead relA_KO ppgpp_conc CV stays near wildtype's 20-35% level, this CONFIRMS Rival C -- the variance is generated upstream and RelA is a passive pass-through.

objection_ledger.issue: The rivals section names fraction_trna_charged as a bystander and the falsifier claims clamping ppGpp alone discriminates causality, but fraction_trna_charged and ppgpp_conc are mechanistically coupled (ppGpp synthesis is driven by uncharged tRNA via RelA). Clamping ppgpp_conc to a fixed value while leaving the upstream charging machinery intact does not fully break the coupling path (charged-tRNA fraction will still shift with condition, and RelA will still attempt to respond to it even if the clamp overrides the output channel). The relA knockout design is listed as merely an 'orthogonal cross-check, not primary' -- but it is actually the only genuine interventional break of the coupling (removing the sensor rather than overriding the output). As currently weighted, the decision rule treats the ppGpp clamp as sufficient for the causal claim, without requiring the relA-knockout slope result to agree before accepting H1-causal.

The decision rule's causal arm 2 (relA-KO) only tests a Welch t at basal (single condition shift), not a refit slope across basal+acetate like causal arm 1 (ppGpp clamp), despite both acetate and basal relA-KO designs being run. This asymmetry means the relA causal test is weaker/less comparable than the ppGpp clamp test even though both datasets exist.

The decision rule requires R^2>=0.6 pooled across only 3 conditions (basal, acetate, amino-acid-supplemented timeline), each contributing one growth-rate point (plus seed noise). With effectively 3 distinct x-values, a high R^2 is close to guaranteed by any monotonic trend and not a strong test of a general 'growth-rate control law' that the user asked about broadly across media. This is a minor concern already partly mitigated by seed pooling, but the scope (3 media points) is thin for a claim of a general scaling law.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Expression noise (variability of concentration across isogenic replicate seeds) is systematically higher for a low-abundance regulatory protein (RelA) than for a high-abundance housekeeping component (active ribosomes), because stochastic birth-death/burst dynamics give noise that scales inversely with mean copy number ('noise ~ 1/mean'), not because of RelA's specific regulatory-feedback architecture.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under matched wildtype/basal conditions, CV(rela_conc) is substantially greater than CV(ribosome_conc), and this gap persists (is not abolished) when ppGpp feedback is clamped to a constant multiple of basal, indicating the noise difference is abundance-driven rather than feedback-architecture-driven.
hypothesis.h0: CV(rela_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc) are statistically indistinguishable across seeds (no systematic abundance-dependent noise difference), or any initial gap collapses under the ppgpp_conc clamp, indicating the difference was due to regulatory feedback rather than abundance.

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state concentration (uM) at matched late timepoint (end of generation 3); CV = SD/mean across seeds

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state concentration (uM) at matched late timepoint; CV = SD/mean across seeds

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc under ppgpp_conc clamp (multiple_of_basal=1.0, feedback loop removed by fixing the alarmone output) vs under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: CV(rela_conc) clamp vs wildtype, compared via Welch t on per-seed values

operational_defs.construct: ribosome-partitioning-stress confound on ppGpp causality (Rival A isolation, addresses r2.1)
operational_defs.observable: rela_conc dispersion under ppgpp_conc clamp applied ON TOP OF rrna_operon_knockout, versus rrna_operon_knockout alone
operational_defs.measure: CV(rela_conc) in rrna_operon_knockout+ppgpp_conc-clamp vs rrna_operon_knockout alone; if clamping ppGpp collapses RelA dispersion even while ribosome capacity remains limited (ribosome_conc/protein_mass still depressed in both), this isolates ppGpp signaling (not secondary ribosome-allocation changes) as the proximate driver when feedback IS the cause; if dispersion does NOT collapse, ribosome-partitioning stress (not ppGpp per se) is implicated

operational_defs.construct: ribosome-capacity confound on ppGpp (Rival B exclusion, addresses r2.2 by dropping BC in favor of a two-sample mean comparison, not small-n bimodality)
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc under rrna_operon_knockout, split into top-half vs bottom-half seeds by growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of mean ppgpp_conc between the two growth_rate-ranked seed halves within rrna_operon_knockout (n=4 vs 4); avoids relying on bimodality_bc at small n

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: CV(rela_conc) > CV(ribosome_conc) under wildtype/basal, ratio ~3-5x (e.g. ~25-35% vs ~6-10%) across 6-8 seeds, consistent with ~1/sqrt(mean copy number) scaling (RelA ~tens-hundreds copies/cell vs ribosomes ~tens of thousands). Under the ppgpp_conc clamp (feedback removed), CV(rela_conc) should remain elevated (fall by <30% relative to wildtype, staying >=2x CV(ribosome_conc)) if abundance (not feedback) is the driver. Under rrna_operon_knockout+clamp vs rrna_operon_knockout-alone, if feedback IS implicated the clamp should still reduce CV(rela_conc) by >=20% even with ribosome capacity held limited in both arms.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test comparing per-seed rela_conc values (used as the CV-bearing channel) between wildtype/basal and ppgpp_conc/basal (clamp at 1.0x basal, same seeds/generations); reject H1's abundance-driven claim if CV(rela_conc) collapses toward CV(ribosome_conc) under the clamp (ratio <1.5x) with |welch_t|>=2 showing a significant reduction in dispersion versus wildtype
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(rela_conc) under the ppgpp_conc clamp drops to within 1.5x of CV(ribosome_conc) (|welch_t|>=2 for reduced dispersion vs wildtype), indicating the noise was due to feedback architecture, not abundance; or CV(rela_conc) in wildtype was never >1.5x CV(ribosome_conc) to begin with

test.statistic: welch_t

rivals.claim: Rival A - Regulatory feedback complexity (not raw abundance) drives RelA's noise: the ppGpp synthesis/feedback loop amplifies fluctuations independent of copy number.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Clamping ppGpp (ppgpp_conc=1.0x basal) while RelA mean abundance is roughly unchanged causes CV(rela_conc) to collapse toward CV(ribosome_conc) (ratio <1.5x); and this collapse ALSO occurs when the clamp is applied on top of rrna_operon_knockout (ribosome capacity still limited in both arms), confirming ppGpp signaling itself -- not secondary ribosome-partitioning stress -- is the proximate driver; this would refute the abundance-only account.

rivals.claim: Rival B - Translation/burst kinetics under ribosome capacity limitation (not RelA-specific biology) independently destabilize ppGpp/growth readouts via uncharged-tRNA coupling, confounding any RelA-specific noise attribution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under rrna_operon_knockout, mean ppgpp_conc differs significantly (Welch |t|>=2) between the top-half and bottom-half growth_rate-ranked seeds (n=4 vs 4), showing ribosome-capacity variation propagates to ppGpp independent of RelA's own copy number -- complicating a clean abundance-only attribution for RelA's noise.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator computes rela_conc and ribosome_conc as genuinely independent stochastic draws per seed (seeds are not just re-running identical deterministic trajectories), so cross-seed CV reflects intrinsic/extrinsic noise rather than numerical artifact.

RelA mean abundance is not substantially altered by the ppgpp_conc clamp itself (the clamp fixes the alarmone output channel, not RelA synthesis/degradation), so a CV collapse under the clamp can be attributed to feedback removal rather than a confounded abundance shift.
Matched late-timepoint sampling (same generation count, e.g. end of generation 3) is used for all CV comparisons across designs to avoid conflating noise with transient/startup dynamics.

ribosome_conc is used as a proxy for 'highly-translated housekeeping gene product' and is available in steady-state charging mode (not using the kinetic-charging ribosomal-protein-count alternative) for this design.

rrna_operon_knockout is assumed to leave relA gene copy number/promoter architecture itself untouched, so any CV(rela_conc) change there is attributable to downstream physiological (ribosome-capacity/ppGpp) coupling, not a direct genetic perturbation of RelA.

Applying a ppgpp_conc clamp on top of rrna_operon_knockout is assumed to be within the envelope as a single combined params dict on one perturbation entry (not a forbidden dual-perturbation type) since the clamp is expressed as an additional param on the rrna_operon_knockout design rather than as two separate perturbation fields.

Using a median-split (top-half vs bottom-half growth_rate) Welch t-test in place of bimodality_bc at n=8 is treated as an adequate substitute for detecting a ribosome-capacity-driven ppGpp split at this sample size, trading off distributional-shape information for a test valid at small n.

objection_ledger.issue: The claim frames this as explaining bacterial antibiotic survival broadly ('survive antibiotics without becoming resistant'), but no antibiotic exposure, death/survival readout, or MIC-type channel is part of the test — the hypothesis only establishes that a ppGpp-linked bimodal growth state exists and is relA-dependent, not that this state actually confers survival under antibiotic challenge. The link from 'low-growth/high-ppGpp subpopulation exists' to 'this is why they survive antibiotics' is asserted, not tested by any channel/perturbation available (no antibiotic/drug-kill channel listed).

The ribosome-capacity rival (Rival B) is tested via rrna_operon_knockout, but this knockout likely also perturbs ppGpp indirectly (ribosome limitation is a classic trigger of the stringent response itself via uncharged tRNA accumulation at stalled ribosomes), so finding bimodal growth_rate in rrna_operon_knockout does not cleanly show 'ribosome capacity acts independent of ppGpp' — ppgpp_conc should also be measured and shown to NOT differ between the two growth clusters under rrna_operon_knockout to actually dissociate the mechanisms. As written, the rival's distinguishing_result only checks growth_rate bimodality in the rrna_operon_knockout, not whether ppGpp tracks the split there.

The 10-30% subpopulation fraction and the >=3-fold ppgpp_conc threshold for the low-growth cluster are fairly specific quantitative predictions, but with only 8 seeds per design it's unclear whether 'cluster size as fraction of seeds' is meant to approximate a true within-population persister fraction or is just a statement about how many of the 8 stochastic seeds happen to land in the low-growth basin. This affects whether a result like 1/8 or 3/8 seeds in the low cluster counts as confirming versus refuting evidence.

Rival A's proposed falsifier relies on comparing bimodality_bc of growth_rate between rrna_operon_knockout alone vs +relA-knockout. But relA knockout itself also reduces ribosome-partitioning stress indirectly if relA loss changes overall growth/ribosome allocation (feedback via RNA/protein mass channels), so a collapse in bimodality could occur even if the mechanism is Rival A's passive partitioning noise responding secondarily to altered ribosome allocation post-relA-KO, not because ppGpp signaling was the proximate cause of bimodality. The design does not include a control that holds ribosome_conc/partitioning stress constant while varying ppGpp (e.g., a relA-knockout-only or a ppgpp_conc perturbation on top of rrna_operon_knockout without relA) to isolate ppGpp's causal role from secondary ribosome-level changes.

Sarle's bimodality coefficient is being computed on pooled data from only 8 seeds x 3 generations (24 points) for wildtype, and even fewer for rrna_operon_knockout (18 points). BC is known to be unreliable/biased at such small n (it's typically recommended for n>>30, often hundreds), so a BC>0.555 or <=0.555 call at this sample size may not reflect a real bimodal vs unimodal distribution but rather sampling noise in the instrument's output.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales with the regulatory architecture of the gene's control node, not merely its mean expression level: a heterologous, feedback-free new_gene product shows higher seed-to-seed CV in its expression-linked mass channel than the native, stringent-response/feedback-coupled ribosomal output (ribosome_conc), even when both have comparable mean abundance. This candidate is scoped strictly to expression-noise-vs-architecture (no antibiotic-survival claim is made anywhere in this hypothesis).
hypothesis.h1: Unregulated new_gene expression (protein_mass CV across seeds) exceeds native feedback-regulated ribosomal expression (ribosome_conc CV across seeds) by a factor of >=2x in wildtype/basal, and this gap is driven by loss of negative feedback rather than by channel-aggregation structure: when the ppGpp-synthesizing enzyme is removed (relA knockout), ribosome_conc CV rises substantially while ppgpp_conc itself shows a correspondingly large seed-to-seed spread change; whereas reducing ribosome capacity directly (rrna_operon_knockout, feedback loop intact) raises ribosome_conc CV only modestly AND leaves ppgpp_conc CV comparable to wildtype -- dissociating the ppGpp-feedback mechanism from a ribosome-capacity/dilution-only mechanism.
hypothesis.h0: Seed-to-seed CV of protein_mass for new_gene does not differ beyond replicate spread (|welch_t|<2) from ribosome_conc CV for wildtype; OR the ribosome_conc CV rise in relA-knockout is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2), indicating the low native CV is a channel-aggregation artifact rather than a feedback effect; OR rrna_operon_knockout produces a ppgpp_conc CV shift comparable to relA-knockout's, indicating the two perturbations are not mechanistically dissociable and the rival (ribosome-capacity drives ppGpp indirectly, not pure feedback-removal) cannot be excluded.

operational_defs.construct: expression noise of an unregulated/low-copy gene
operational_defs.observable: seed-to-seed variability in the abundance of the heterologous gene product, proxied by protein_mass from a new_gene insertion
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) across seeds of protein_mass at matched generation

operational_defs.construct: expression noise of a native feedback-regulated gene (ribosomal protein genes)
operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel, aggregating ribosomal protein/rRNA expression under ppGpp/stringent-response feedback
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) across seeds of ribosome_conc at matched generation

operational_defs.construct: regulatory feedback strength / causal dependence on ppGpp coupling
operational_defs.observable: change in ribosome_conc CV when relA is knocked out versus when rRNA operon capacity is directly reduced (rrna_operon_knockout)
operational_defs.measure: CV(ribosome_conc) in relA-KO and rrna_operon_knockout backgrounds compared to wildtype CV(ribosome_conc)

operational_defs.construct: mechanistic dissociation of ppGpp-feedback removal from ribosome-capacity reduction (resolves r2.2)
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc channel measured in both relA-knockout and rrna_operon_knockout backgrounds
operational_defs.measure: CV(ppgpp_conc) and mean-shift (welch_t) of ppgpp_conc, relA-KO vs wildtype and rrna_operon_knockout vs wildtype; feedback-causality requires relA-KO to show a LARGE ppgpp_conc change while rrna_operon_knockout shows a SMALL one, confirming the two perturbations act via distinct routes

operational_defs.observable: whether ribosome_conc CV is intrinsically smooth regardless of feedback status
operational_defs.measure: if CV(ribosome_conc) in relA-KO is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype CV(ribosome_conc) (|welch_t|<2), the low CV is an aggregation artifact, not a feedback effect

hypothesis.predicted_effect: (1) CV(new_gene protein_mass) ~0.35-0.50 vs CV(wildtype ribosome_conc) ~0.12-0.18, ratio >=2.0. (2) relA knockout raises CV(ribosome_conc) by >=1.5x relative to wildtype (toward ~0.20-0.30) AND shifts mean ppgpp_conc down with |welch_t|>=2 (near-abolished synthesis, effect_pct <= -50%). (3) rrna_operon_knockout raises mean ribosome_conc deviation but keeps CV(ribosome_conc) within 1.3x of wildtype (~0.15-0.23) AND keeps ppgpp_conc mean-shift small (|welch_t|<2 or effect_pct within +/-20%) relative to wildtype -- i.e., capacity reduction does NOT route through a large ppGpp change, dissociating it from relA-KO's mechanism.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: welch_disconfirm on protein_mass (new_gene vs wildtype) across seeds, reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2; report CV ratio = CV(new_gene protein_mass)/CV(wildtype ribosome_conc), require ratio>=1.5. Feedback-causality test: welch_disconfirm on ribosome_conc for gene_knockout/relA vs wildtype/basal must show |welch_t|>=2 (CV rising). Mechanistic-dissociation test (resolves r2.2): welch_disconfirm on ppgpp_conc for gene_knockout/relA vs wildtype/basal must show |welch_t|>=2 with large effect_pct (<=-50%), while welch_disconfirm on ppgpp_conc for rrna_operon_knockout vs wildtype/basal must show |welch_t|<2 OR effect_pct within +/-20% -- i.e. the two KOs must produce clearly DIFFERENT ppgpp_conc responses for H1 to hold.
falsifier.refuting_result: Either (a) CV_ratio < 1.5 with |welch_t|<2 on protein_mass (no noise gap), or (b) ribosome_conc CV in gene_knockout/relA is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2, aggregation-artifact rival supported), or (c) ppgpp_conc response in rrna_operon_knockout is statistically indistinguishable in magnitude from relA-knockout's ppgpp_conc response (both |welch_t|>=2 with comparable effect_pct), showing ribosome-capacity reduction and ppGpp-feedback removal are not mechanistically dissociable here.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 on protein_mass (new_gene vs wildtype) AND |t|>=2 on ribosome_conc (relA-KO vs wildtype) AND |t|>=2 with effect_pct<=-50% on ppgpp_conc (relA-KO vs wildtype) AND (|t|<2 OR effect_pct within +/-20%) on ppgpp_conc (rrna_operon_knockout vs wildtype)

rivals.claim: Noise is driven purely by mean expression level (low-copy-number Poisson/burst noise), independent of regulatory architecture -- any low-abundance gene product, regulated or not, shows equally high CV once mean is matched.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout lowers mean ribosome_conc yet CV(ribosome_conc) rises to match new_gene CV levels (~0.35-0.50) even though feedback is intact, mean-abundance alone (this rival) is supported over architecture; our prediction instead holds CV comparatively flat (within 1.3x) under capacity reduction.

rivals.claim: Ribosome-capacity limitation itself (not ppGpp-feedback loss) drives any ribosome_conc CV rise, acting indirectly through stringent-response triggering by stalled/uncharged tRNAs at limiting ribosomes -- i.e. rrna_operon_knockout and relA-knockout converge on the same ppGpp route, so the two perturbations cannot be mechanistically dissociated.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout produces a ppgpp_conc mean-shift and CV change comparable in magnitude to relA-knockout's (|welch_t|>=2 on ppgpp_conc for BOTH, similar effect_pct), the rival is supported and ribosome capacity cannot be separated from ppGpp feedback with this design; our H1 requires relA-KO's ppgpp_conc shift to be clearly larger than rrna_operon_knockout's.

rivals.claim: The CV gap is a channel-aggregation artifact: ribosome_conc averages many ribosomal operons/species while protein_mass for new_gene is a single-species readout, so the former is mechanically smoother regardless of regulation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA knockout leaves ribosome_conc CV statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2, CV flat) despite ppGpp synthesis being abolished, the aggregation-artifact rival is supported over feedback-causality.

BC is known to be unreliable/biased at such small n (it's typically recommended for n>>30, often hundreds), so a BC>0.555 or <=0.555 call at this sample size may not reflect a real bimodal vs unimodal distribution but rather sampling noise in the instrument's output.

'Survival without becoming resistant' (the user's question, implying survival of an antibiotic challenge) is conflated with 'entering a low-growth/high-ppGpp state under amino-acid downshift' (the modeled proxy). The candidate_design list contains no antibiotic perturbation at all, and division_rate>0 is used as a stand-in for 'surviving the antibiotic' with no argument that amino-acid downshift dormancy actually confers antibiotic tolerance in this simulator. hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Gene expression noise (intrinsic cell-to-cell variability) scales with the copy-number regime of a gene's expression product: a low-copy-number regulatory species (RelA, the ppGpp synthetase) shows substantially higher relative noise (CV across isogenic replicate seeds) than a high-copy structural species (bulk ribosome pool), because noise in this stochastic whole-cell simulation is dominated by low-copy-number Poisson/burst effects rather than by promoter-specific regulatory complexity.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds under matched wildtype/basal conditions, CV(rela_conc) is >=3x CV(ribosome_conc), and this gap is not attributable to RelA's own regulatory feedback wiring: deleting relA (removing that wiring entirely) leaves CV(ribosome_conc) statistically unchanged, supporting a copy-number/Poisson origin for the noise gap rather than a regulatory-architecture origin.
hypothesis.h0: CV(rela_conc) across seeds is statistically indistinguishable from, or less than, CV(ribosome_conc) under the same wildtype/basal condition (CV ratio <3x or Welch |t|<2) -- i.e. relative noise does not systematically track abundance regime.

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc channel, per-seed steady-state values at matched generation
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) computed across seeds

operational_defs.construct: noise in a high-copy structural gene product

operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) computed across seeds

operational_defs.measure: ratio of means (fold-difference) as covariate explaining CV difference

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: CV(rela_conc) > CV(ribosome_conc) under wildtype/basal. Magnitude: CV(rela_conc) ~0.30-0.50 (30-50%) vs CV(ribosome_conc) ~0.05-0.10 (5-10%), i.e. >=3-5x higher relative noise for the low-abundance regulator, consistent with Poisson/burst scaling (CV ~ 1/sqrt(N)). Discriminating control: deleting relA should leave CV(ribosome_conc) in wildtype vs relA-KO within ~20% of each other (no detectable Welch effect on the raw ribosome_conc channel), confirming the two noise regimes are not mechanistically coupled through RelA signaling.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary test: from the disconfirm per-seed spread for wildtype/basal (n=8 seeds, 3 generations pooled as independent replicate points, 24 total per channel), compute CV(rela_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc) directly as SD/mean of the raw per-seed values (no welch_t needed for this ratio claim -- report CV ratio as the primary statistic); require CV ratio >=3x as the decisive threshold, since BC/Welch on normalized residuals is underpowered at n=24 (per r2.1). Discriminating-control test: run welch_disconfirm on ribosome_conc, target=gene_knockout/relA-KO vs reference=wildtype/basal; if |welch_t|>=2 (ribosome_conc mean or spread changes materially upon deleting relA), this indicates hidden coupling and undercuts the independent-copy-number-origin claim even if the primary CV-ratio test passes.
falsifier.refuting_result: Either (a) empirical CV ratio (CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc)) <3x on the primary comparison, refuting the magnitude/direction of H1; or (b) the relA-KO control shows |welch_t|>=2 on ribosome_conc vs wildtype, indicating the noise gap is contaminated by regulatory coupling rather than pure copy-number/Poisson scaling.

test.statistic: CV ratio (SD/mean per channel, primary, descriptive threshold test); welch_t on ribosome_conc raw per-seed values (control, inferential)
test.threshold: primary: CV ratio >=3x (descriptive, n=24/channel, not a Welch-t claim given r2.1 power caveat); control: |t|<2 (no significant shift) to support independence

rivals.claim: Rival A: noise differences are driven primarily by promoter/regulatory architecture (feedback, TF-mediated bursting) rather than raw copy number -- a highly regulated but moderately-abundant gene could be just as noisy as a low-copy one.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If deleting relA (removing its own regulatory wiring entirely) leaves ribosome_conc CV and mean unchanged (|welch_t|<2) while the rela_conc-vs-ribosome_conc CV gap in wildtype still exists and is large, this favors copy-number-driven noise over architecture-driven noise, since the regulatory machinery was removed without downstream noise consequence in the high-copy channel.

rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(rela_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc), both computed in the same uM units with the same per-seed sampling procedure, nonetheless converge to similar magnitudes (ratio <3x) despite the known large mean-copy-number gap, that would indicate the noise difference is not a real stoichiometric effect but a scale/measurement artifact.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across E. coli genes, expression noise (cell-to-cell variability) scales with regulatory/translational architecture rather than mean expression alone: genes whose products are low-copy and/or depend on amplifying regulatory steps (e.g. a single transcription factor gating a small regulon, or low mRNA copy number compensated by high translation efficiency) show systematically higher noise than high-copy, constitutively/ribosomally-dominated genes. Operationally, using the stringent-response regulon as a tractable proxy architecture, genes/pathways whose output is gated through RelA/ppGpp signaling (a single low-copy synthetase controlling a broad downstream response) will show higher relative variability in their downstream readouts (ppgpp_conc, and ribosome_conc as a downstream target) than a constitutively expressed high-abundance control axis (ribosome_conc under basal wildtype conditions, representing a highly buffered, high-copy output), when both are measured as coefficient of variation (CV) across isogenic replicate seeds.
drafts.h1: The CV (across seeds) of ppgpp_conc (output of a low-copy, single-enzyme-gated regulatory node, RelA) is substantially higher than the CV of ribosome_conc (a high-copy, heavily buffered output) under matched wildtype/basal conditions, and this gap is causally dependent on the low-copy regulatory node: deleting relA (removing the amplifying bottleneck) collapses the ppgpp_conc CV toward the ribosome_conc CV.
drafts.h0: ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc have statistically indistinguishable coefficients of variation across seeds under wildtype/basal conditions (no architecture-driven noise gap), and/or relA knockout does not reduce ppgpp_conc CV relative to wildtype.

operational_defs.observable: per-seed value of the channel (ppgpp_conc or ribosome_conc) at a matched timepoint across isogenic stochastic replicates
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) computed across seeds for that channel

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc channel (RelA synthetase concentration) and its downstream product ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean rela_conc (to confirm low abundance) and CV of ppgpp_conc as the noise readout for this architecture class

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: CV of ribosome_conc across seeds as the low-noise reference

operational_defs.construct: causal dependence of noise on the regulatory bottleneck
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc channel under relA gene_knockout vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: change in CV of ppgpp_conc (knockout vs wildtype), tested via Welch t on per-seed values

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: CV(ppgpp_conc, wildtype) > CV(ribosome_conc, wildtype) by roughly 2-3x (e.g. ~25-40% CV for ppgpp_conc vs ~10-15% CV for ribosome_conc). Causal test: relA knockout reduces ppgpp_conc CV by at least ~40-50% relative to wildtype ppgpp_conc CV, moving it toward the ribosome_conc CV range.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Welch t comparing per-seed ppgpp_conc values vs per-seed ribosome_conc values (both under wildtype/basal, matched timepoint) after converting each to within-channel z-scores is not well-posed for CV comparison, so instead compute CV(ppgpp_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc) directly from per-seed spread/mean in each design's output; treat the wildtype/basal design as reference for both channels. Causal arm: Welch t of per-seed ppgpp_conc values, relA_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal; reject H1 (architecture-driven noise causality) if |t|<2 (i.e., knockout does not significantly shift ppgpp_conc distribution/spread).
falsifier.refuting_result: If CV(ppgpp_conc) in wildtype/basal is not clearly larger than CV(ribosome_conc) in wildtype/basal (e.g. ratio <1.3x), OR relA knockout fails to significantly change ppgpp_conc (Welch |t|<2 vs wildtype), H1 is refuted.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for relA_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal on ppgpp_conc; CV ratio ppgpp_conc:ribosome_conc >=1.3 in wildtype/basal as the descriptive noise-gap criterion

rivals.claim: Noise differences are driven purely by mean-expression level (Poisson/molecular-copy-number scaling), not by regulatory architecture per se — i.e. ppgpp_conc is noisier simply because its mean concentration is lower, not because of the RelA bottleneck structure.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV scales as expected from simple low-copy-number Poisson noise (CV ~ 1/sqrt(mean)) and relA knockout, despite changing the mean, still produces a CV matching the Poisson prediction from the new mean (no disproportionate collapse of CV), then architecture adds nothing beyond copy number and H1's causal claim is undermined.

rivals.claim: ppGpp variability is mainly driven by global growth-rate/metabolic state fluctuations (growth_rate channel), not by RelA-specific synthesis noise — i.e. ppgpp_conc noise is a downstream echo of growth_rate noise common to all channels.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(growth_rate) across wildtype seeds is similarly elevated and correlates tightly with ppgpp_conc fluctuations even after relA knockout (ppgpp_conc noise persists/tracks growth_rate noise despite removing RelA), this favors the global-state rival over the RelA-specific bottleneck claim.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation under steady-state charging meaningfully approximates intrinsic biological expression noise for these channels (ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, rela_conc) rather than being dominated by numerical/solver artifacts.
ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc are recorded under steady-state charging mode (no kinetic ppGpp module needed) so both channels are available for direct CV comparison in the same run.

relA knockout is mechanistically represented in the model (affects ppGpp synthesis) rather than being a no-op; spoT knockout serves as a secondary/partial check since SpoT also contributes to ppGpp turnover and its removal should show a distinguishable (likely smaller or differently-signed) effect than relA removal.
Matched timepoint/generation across seeds is used for CV computation so that within-cell-cycle phase effects do not confound the cross-seed variance estimate.

The comparison of CV(ppgpp_conc) vs CV(ribosome_conc) as a proxy for 'low-copy regulatory architecture vs high-copy buffered architecture' is a tractable stand-in for the broader genome-wide noise question, acknowledging this is a single architectural contrast rather than an exhaustive gene screen.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Genes whose protein products are low in copy number and/or encoded by genes with low transcription initiation rate (captured here as ribosome-allocation-limited stringent-response targets vs. highly-expressed ribosomal genes) show higher relative noise in expression than high-abundance, high-initiation-rate genes. Concretely, we operationalize this with a genome-scale proxy: knocking down ribosome capacity (rrna_operon_knockout) should disproportionately increase the cell-to-cell (seed-to-seed) coefficient of variation of low-abundance-protein-associated readouts (ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged) relative to the reference, because low-copy-number species amplify stochastic partitioning/translation-bursting noise under ribosome scarcity, while high-abundance, highly-transcribed species (ribosome_conc itself) remain comparatively buffered.
drafts.h1: Across an in-envelope panel of perturbations that alter effective gene expression level/ribosome allocation (rrna_operon_knockout, gene_knockout of a low-abundance regulator, ppgpp_conc clamp), the per-seed coefficient of variation (CV) of low-abundance-associated channels (ppgpp_conc, rela_conc) is systematically and substantially higher (>=2x) than the CV of high-abundance channels (ribosome_conc, dry_mass) under matched conditions, and this gap widens under ribosome-capacity reduction relative to wildtype.
drafts.h0: The CV of low-abundance channels (ppgpp_conc, rela_conc) is statistically indistinguishable from (or only marginally different, <1.3x) the CV of high-abundance channels (ribosome_conc, dry_mass), and ribosome-capacity reduction does not differentially widen the CV gap between low- and high-abundance channels relative to wildtype.

Under rrna_operon_knockout, predict the ratio CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc) increases further by an additional ~1.5-2x relative to wildtype (e.g., ratio rising from ~2.5x at wildtype to ~4-5x under rRNA knockout), reflecting amplified stochastic noise in the low-abundance species when ribosome capacity is constrained.

rivals.claim: Noise differences are driven purely by mean-abundance scaling (Poisson/shot-noise law: CV ~ 1/sqrt(mean)) rather than any ribosome-allocation or regulatory mechanism — i.e., any low-mean channel would show high CV regardless of rrna knockout.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, the CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc) ratio would already be fully explained by the mean-abundance ratio alone and would NOT change under rrna_operon_knockout (ratio stays ~constant across wildtype and knockout, even though absolute CVs may shift); our test specifically requires the RATIO to widen under knockout, which this rival predicts it would not.

rivals.claim: ppGpp-mediated stringent response, not raw ribosome scarcity per se, is the causal amplifier of rela_conc noise — i.e., it is the regulatory feedback loop (RelA-ppGpp-ribosome synthesis) that creates noise amplification, and simply removing rRNA operons works only insofar as it triggers ppGpp accumulation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A ppgpp_conc clamp (holding ppGpp artificially fixed rather than letting it respond to rRNA loss) should ABOLISH the predicted CV-ratio widening even though ribosome capacity is still reduced by rrna_operon_knockout; if the ratio still widens under the clamp, this rival is refuted in favor of a pure ribosome-scarcity mechanism.

auxiliary_assumptions: Across-seed CV at matched steady-state timepoints is an adequate proxy for intrinsic single-cell expression noise (the simulator does not provide single-cell-resolved intracellular snapshots beyond per-seed trajectories).

rela_conc and ribosome_conc are reasonable stand-ins for 'low-abundance regulatory protein' and 'high-abundance housekeeping complex' respectively; we are not claiming these two channels exhaust the space of all genes, only that they instantiate the abundance contrast at genome scale via the broader panel of designs.

Ribosome capacity reduction (rrna_operon_knockout) is assumed not to cause outright lethality within 3 generations, so steady-state-like readouts remain interpretable (division_rate will be checked as a feasibility gate).

Mean-abundance differences between rela_conc and ribosome_conc are stable enough across conditions that the CV comparison is not purely an artifact of mean-shift alone within a single design (addressed by the rival test using the ratio rather than raw CV).

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Expression noise differences across genes are driven primarily by regulatory architecture coupled to ribosome allocation capacity: genes whose products are low-abundance and depend on limiting translational machinery (rRNA/ribosome availability) show higher cell-to-cell expression noise than high-abundance, translationally-buffered genes, because noise is dominated by low copy-number (Poisson/burst) effects amplified by competition for shared ribosomes rather than by transcriptional burst kinetics alone. Operationally: knocking down ribosome capacity (rRNA operon knockout) should disproportionately increase the coefficient of variation (CV) of low-abundance reporter/marker proteins relative to high-abundance ones, across isogenic replicate seeds.
drafts.h1: Across an isogenic population (seeds), genes with lower mean protein abundance show higher expression noise (CV of protein_mass-normalized per-gene proxy, approximated via protein_mass and ribosome_conc channels) than high-abundance genes, and this noise gap WIDENS when ribosome capacity is constrained (rrna_operon_knockout) relative to wildtype, consistent with shared-resource (ribosome) competition amplifying intrinsic noise for low-abundance genes.
drafts.h0: There is no systematic relationship between gene expression level and noise magnitude, and constraining ribosome capacity (rrna_operon_knockout) does not differentially change the CV of low- vs high-abundance gene products relative to wildtype; any CV differences across seeds are within replicate noise (Welch t < 2, no significant widening of the noise gap).

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: CV(protein_mass) across seeds increases under rrna_operon_knockout relative to wildtype/basal, with predicted magnitude of a ~1.5-2x fold increase in CV (e.g., wildtype CV ~0.05-0.08 rising to ~0.10-0.16 under ribosome limitation), reflecting amplified noise when ribosomes are scarce. Also predict ribosome_conc itself shows elevated CV (>=1.5x wildtype) under the knockout, consistent with resource-competition-driven noise amplification rather than a simple mean-shift.

rivals.claim: Noise is set primarily by intrinsic transcriptional bursting kinetics (promoter architecture) independent of ribosome/translational resource limitation — rRNA knockout would shift the MEAN of protein_mass/growth_rate (slower growth) but NOT differentially change CV.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout shows a large growth_rate decrease but protein_mass CV stays statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2), this rival is supported: noise is transcription-intrinsic, not resource-competition-driven.

rivals.claim: Noise differences are driven by ppGpp-mediated stringent response reallocation (not raw ribosome scarcity per se) — ribosome limitation triggers ppGpp accumulation which itself reshapes transcriptional noise globally via RNA polymerase competition, a confound distinct from direct ribosome-sharing.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout background (eliminating ppGpp synthesis capacity) crossed with rrna_operon_knockout should abolish or greatly reduce the CV-widening effect seen in rrna_operon_knockout alone if ppGpp signaling (not raw ribosome scarcity) is the actual noise driver; if CV still widens similarly without relA, this supports the ribosome-competition mechanism over the ppGpp-signaling rival.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Gene expression noise (cell-to-cell variability) scales with a gene's regulatory architecture: genes whose protein products are regulated by low-abundance, rate-limiting upstream factors (e.g., genes dependent on RelA/ppGpp-mediated stringent control for their expression) show higher expression noise than genes expressed under stable, high-abundance regulatory control (e.g., core ribosomal protein genes under steady growth), because small stochastic fluctuations in the low-copy regulator are amplified downstream. Operationally, we test this via a ribosome-capacity perturbation (rrna_operon_knockout) that forces cells to rely more heavily on fluctuating stringent-response signaling, versus wildtype, and ask whether this increases cell-to-cell variability (CV) in a marker channel (ribosomal-protein proxy / ppGpp-linked readout) more than it increases the mean shift — i.e. noise (CV) increases disproportionately relative to mean change, consistent with amplification of upstream regulator noise rather than simple scaling.
drafts.h1: Perturbing ribosome capacity (rrna_operon_knockout), which forces stronger reliance on stringent-response (ppGpp/RelA) regulation, increases the cell-to-cell coefficient of variation (CV) of ppgpp_conc and downstream ribosome_conc across seeds by at least 50% relative to wildtype/basal, i.e. noise amplification exceeds what a proportional mean-shift alone would predict.
drafts.h0: rrna_operon_knockout changes the mean of ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc but does NOT increase their per-seed CV beyond what is expected from a proportional (linear) scaling of mean and variance (CV stays within ~10% of wildtype/basal CV).

operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) computed across seeds for ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc

operational_defs.measure: mean and CV of ppgpp_conc, rela_conc across seeds, compared pre/post perturbation

operational_defs.measure: effect_pct from disconfirm on CV metric vs effect_pct on mean metric

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: rrna_operon_knockout increases per-seed CV of ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc relative to wildtype/basal. Magnitude: CV increase of >=50% (e.g. wildtype CV ~0.10-0.15 rising to >=0.20-0.25) while mean ribosome_conc shifts by a comparatively smaller fraction (<30%), indicating disproportionate noise amplification rather than simple linear scaling.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test (welch_disconfirm) comparing per-seed ribosome_conc values, target vs reference; reject H0 (noise amplification) if |welch_t|>=2 AND the per-seed CV of ribosome_conc in target exceeds reference CV by >=50% (computed from per-seed spread returned by disconfirm)
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t|<2, or if CV increase is <10% (i.e., variance scales proportionally with the mean shift, consistent with simple linear amplification rather than disproportionate noise), H1 is refuted and H0 (proportional scaling) stands.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed ribosome_conc (and secondary CV ratio computed from per-seed spread)
test.threshold: |welch_t|>=2 for mean shift AND CV increase >=50% relative to reference CV (refute if <10%)

rivals.claim: Noise increase is purely a mean-scaling artifact: lower ribosome copy number mechanically increases Poisson-like sampling noise (CV ~ 1/sqrt(N)) with no special role for ppGpp/stringent signaling.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a relA gene_knockout (abolishing ppGpp synthesis) is combined as a background control and CV in ribosome_conc under rrna_operon_knockout+relA_KO remains elevated similarly to rrna_operon_knockout alone (i.e., ppGpp removal does NOT reduce the CV increase), this supports pure copy-number/Poisson scaling rather than stringent-response amplification.

rivals.claim: Noise is driven by charged-tRNA fluctuations (translation-elongation stochasticity) rather than ppGpp/RelA signaling per se; ppGpp and ribosome CV simply co-vary with tRNA charging noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If fraction_trna_charged shows a comparably large CV increase under rrna_operon_knockout independent of ppgpp_conc changes, and the relA knockout control does not decouple tRNA-charging noise from ribosome_conc noise, this would favor tRNA-charging noise as the primary driver over ppGpp-specific amplification.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed steady-state (or late-generation) channel values across isogenic replicates are a valid proxy for cell-to-cell expression noise within a single population (ergodic approximation of population heterogeneity by independent stochastic seeds).
The rrna_operon_knockout is mechanistically simulated as a reduction in ribosome synthesis capacity (not merely a label) sufficient to engage stringent-response machinery.

ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channels are recorded under the chosen elongation_model as specified (steady-state charging gives these always; kinetic charging requires the RelA/SpoT module on, which we enable for the relA-KO and kinetic rrna-KO runs).

CV computed from 6 seeds is a noisy but directionally informative estimate; we treat a >=50% CV increase as a practically meaningful effect size given this modest replicate count, deferring more precise variance-ratio testing to follow-up power analysis.

Any confound from relA knockout's basal growth-rate defect altering baseline ribosome demand is acknowledged as a scope caveat; we rely on the CV-decoupling comparison (not absolute CV magnitude) to adjudicate between rivals.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Expression noise differs systematically by functional/regulatory class: genes encoding low-abundance regulatory proteins (e.g. transcription factors, stringent-response components like RelA) show higher cell-to-cell noise than genes encoding high-abundance, stably-expressed housekeeping/ribosomal components, because noise scales inversely with mean expression/copy number (the classic Poisson/burst-size scaling) and is amplified by low burst frequency. Operationally, across a broad panel of genes simulated under matched conditions, per-seed CV of protein level should decline as a power-law function of mean protein abundance, with regulatory/low-abundance genes occupying the high-CV tail.
drafts.h1: Across genes, the coefficient of variation (CV) of protein abundance (computed across seeds, per gene) is negatively related to mean protein abundance (log-log slope ≈ -0.5, consistent with Poisson/translational-bursting scaling), and low-abundance regulatory genes (e.g. relA) sit in the upper CV tail relative to high-abundance genes (e.g. ribosomal proteins reflected in ribosome_conc), with CV at least 3-5x higher for the low-abundance class.
drafts.h0: There is no systematic relationship between mean abundance/gene class and noise: CV is approximately flat across genes of different abundance classes (log-log slope not significantly different from 0, and low- vs high-abundance gene classes show statistically indistinguishable CV, Welch t |t|<2).

rivals.claim: Noise is driven primarily by regulatory architecture (burst frequency/transcription factor control) rather than mean abundance per se — e.g. autoregulated or stringent-response genes are noisy regardless of their abundance level, because feedback loops (ppGpp/RelA-SpoT) actively shape variance independent of copy number.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA knockout (background control) that removes the RelA-dependent regulatory feedback would be expected, under the abundance-only H1, to leave the CV-vs-mean scaling for OTHER genes unchanged; if instead removing RelA sharply changes CV of downstream/co-regulated channels (e.g. ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged) disproportionately to any abundance shift, that favors the regulatory-architecture rival over pure Poisson/burst-size scaling.

rivals.claim: Observed noise differences are an artifact of simulator discretization/stochastic solver granularity rather than a biological burst-size effect — low-copy-number species simply inherit more integer/stochastic rounding noise in the model regardless of true biological mechanism.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If the log(CV)-log(mean) slope is indistinguishable (same magnitude/CI) across genes with very different regulatory annotations (ribosomal vs TF vs stringent-response) once matched for similar mean abundance, and tracks abundance alone with no residual regulatory-class effect, that favors generic copy-number/discretization scaling as the dominant mechanism rather than gene-specific regulation.

auxiliary_assumptions: Across the sampled channels/species (rela_conc, ribosome_conc, ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged) the simulator's intrinsic seed-to-seed variability reflects genuine stochastic gene-expression noise, not merely numerical/solver noise, well enough to compare CVs.

Per-seed CV computed from 6-8 seeds is a sufficiently stable estimator of the population CV for ranking genes/channels by noise (acknowledged as a modest-n estimate; results treated as a first-pass screen, not a precise distributional claim).
ribosome_conc and rela_conc are reasonable proxies for 'high-abundance housekeeping' vs 'low-abundance regulatory' gene classes respectively, given the instrument's available channels.
Steady-state charging mode is used throughout (no kinetic ppGpp module toggled) so that rela_conc and ribosome_conc channels are both populated and comparable across designs.

The relA knockout and rrna_operon_knockout and ppgpp_conc clamp designs are used as background/mechanistic controls to probe regulatory-architecture contributions, not as the primary noise-measurement target.
