rivals.distinguishing_result: If growth_rate CV across the same seeds is comparably large and correlates strongly with rela_conc CV (i.e., rela_conc noise tracks growth_rate noise 1:1), that would indicate extrinsic/global noise dominates rather than intrinsic low-copy-number stochasticity.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales inversely with the gene product's abundance/synthesis rate: low-abundance, low-translation-efficiency ribosomal-regulon-adjacent or regulatory genes show much higher relative noise (CV of per-seed protein counts) than high-abundance, high-synthesis housekeeping/ribosomal genes, because low copy number amplifies stochastic birth-death fluctuations (Poisson-like intrinsic noise) while high-flux genes average over many synthesis events. This is tested at a SCREEN scope across many genes/seeds, not one or two instances.
drafts.h1: Across a broad panel of genes simulated as single-gene knockout/wildtype controls under identical media, the per-seed CV of protein_mass-normalized abundance proxies (via growth_rate and protein_mass channels tied to each gene's dosage, and rna_mass as a proxy for transcriptional output) is negatively and monotonically related to mean expression level: genes with low mean abundance/synthesis exhibit CV >= 2x that of high-abundance genes, with the population of genes showing a continuous, non-bimodal distribution of CV skewed toward a long right tail for low-expressers (the high-noise fraction of low-abundance genes is >=50% of that subpopulation showing CV>0.3, versus <15% for high-abundance genes).
drafts.h0: There is no systematic (monotonic, negative) relationship between mean gene-product abundance/synthesis rate and expression noise (CV) across the gene panel; any apparent differences across genes are within replicate (seed) noise and do not scale with abundance (i.e., slope of CV vs log(mean abundance) across genes is not significantly different from 0, and the high- vs low-abundance subgroup CVs are statistically indistinguishable).

operational_defs.observable: cell-to-cell (seed-to-seed) variability in a gene's protein product abundance across isogenic replicates
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) of protein_mass (or dry_mass-normalized proxy) across seeds, computed per gene-knockout/wildtype-matched condition at matched generation

operational_defs.observable: steady-state level of the gene's product and its transcriptional/translational output
operational_defs.measure: mean protein_mass and mean rna_mass across seeds for that gene's condition, used as the abundance proxy on the x-axis

operational_defs.observable: genes partitioned by rank of mean protein_mass into bottom and top terciles across the screened panel
operational_defs.measure: binary classification threshold at 33rd/67th percentile of mean protein_mass across the gene panel

drafts.predicted_effect: Negative monotonic relation: log(CV) vs log(mean protein_mass) slope approx -0.5 (R^2>=0.3) across the gene panel; low-abundance tercile median CV >= 2x high-abundance tercile median CV (e.g., CV_low ~0.35-0.5 vs CV_high ~0.1-0.15); distribution of CV across genes is unimodal-skewed (not bimodal), long right tail dominated by low-abundance genes.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of per-seed CV(protein_mass) for the low-abundance gene subgroup vs the high-abundance gene subgroup, pooled across the screened gene panel; reject H0 if |welch_t| >= 2 (two-sided) AND additionally fit OLS slope of log(CV) on log(mean protein_mass) across all screened genes, reject H0 if 95% CI on slope excludes 0 and is negative
falsifier.refuting_result: welch_t < 2 in magnitude between low- and high-abundance CV subgroups, and/or the slope_ci of log(CV) vs log(mean abundance) includes 0 or is non-negative, indicating no systematic abundance-noise coupling

test.statistic: OLS slope of log(CV) on log(mean protein_mass) across genes; cross-validated with welch_disconfirm on tercile subgroup means
test.threshold: slope 95% CI excludes 0 and is negative; |welch_t|>=2 for low vs high tercile CV comparison

rivals.claim: Noise is driven mainly by promoter/regulatory architecture (burst size/frequency from transcription factor activity) rather than raw abundance — i.e., genes under tight negative-feedback TF control are low-noise regardless of abundance, while genes lacking feedback are high-noise regardless of abundance.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under a tf_activity clamp on a regulator feeding several low-abundance genes, if CV drops sharply toward high-abundance-like levels despite unchanged mean abundance, this shows regulatory architecture (not abundance per se) sets noise — contradicting the abundance-only H1.

rivals.claim: Noise differences reflect ribosome-allocation/growth-rate coupling (global extrinsic noise from growth-rate fluctuations) rather than gene-intrinsic stochastic birth-death — i.e., genes whose expression is more tightly coupled to growth_rate inherit more noise because growth_rate itself fluctuates across seeds, independent of the gene's own abundance.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If an rrna_operon_knockout (which perturbs ribosome capacity and growth_rate variance globally) changes the CV of both low- and high-abundance genes by a similar multiplicative factor (not preferentially the low-abundance class), this indicates a shared global extrinsic-noise source dominates over gene-intrinsic Poisson noise, contradicting the abundance-driven H1.

auxiliary_assumptions: Protein_mass channel, even though aggregate, tracks per-gene-knockout conditions closely enough that comparing protein_mass CV across different single-gene-knockout backgrounds approximates each gene's own product noise (since each KO run isolates that gene's contribution/absence).

Seeds (isogenic stochastic replicates) are the correct unit for capturing intrinsic expression noise in this simulator; deterministic vs stochastic chaos distinctions are out of scope and are not resolvable here.

Mean protein_mass across seeds in a gene's own knockout-vs-wildtype paired design is a valid abundance proxy even though it is a whole-cell aggregate, not a single-protein count; this is an acknowledged simulator-resolution limitation.
Media condition (basal) and generation number are held fixed across all screened genes so that cross-gene comparisons are not confounded by media-driven differences in growth phase.
The gene panel screened is assumed representative of the genome-wide distribution of abundance classes (sampling across annotated functional categories), not cherry-picked for the expected result.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes, expression noise (cell-to-cell variability) scales with the gene's regulatory/translational amplification: genes expressed from low mRNA copy number but high translational efficiency (high protein-per-mRNA burst size) show higher noise than genes with comparable mean expression achieved via high mRNA copy number and lower per-transcript translation. Operationally, in this whole-cell model, knocking down ribosome availability (rrna_operon_knockout, a global translational capacity cut) will disproportionately reduce the relative noise (CV) of protein output for genes whose expression depends on high per-mRNA translation bursts, compared to wildtype, revealing that noise is driven by burst-like translation rather than by mean mRNA level alone.
drafts.h1: Protein-level expression noise (CV of protein copy number across isogenic seeds) is driven predominantly by translational burst size (protein molecules per mRNA lifetime), such that reducing global ribosome/translation capacity (rrna_operon_knockout) measurably lowers CV of protein_mass-associated reporter proteins relative to wildtype, and this reduction is larger than any accompanying change in mean expression would predict from Poisson scaling alone.
drafts.h0: Expression noise (CV across seeds) is unaffected by translational capacity perturbation beyond what is explained by the corresponding change in mean (i.e., CV scales purely as 1/sqrt(mean), consistent with simple Poisson/mRNA-copy-number driven noise with no distinct translational-burst contribution). rrna_operon_knockout changes mean protein_mass but leaves the mean-normalized noise structure statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal.

operational_defs.observable: protein_mass channel, per-seed distribution across isogenic replicate seeds at a fixed generation
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of protein_mass across seeds, compared between conditions

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel (steady-state) reflecting active ribosome availability, manipulated via rrna_operon_knockout
operational_defs.measure: fold-change in ribosome_conc relative to wildtype/basal, and resulting change in protein_mass CV

operational_defs.observable: protein_mass mean and CV pairs across conditions
operational_defs.measure: whether CV change tracks 1/sqrt(mean) (Poisson null) or deviates systematically, assessed via slope_ci of log(CV) vs log(mean) across conditions

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: rrna_operon_knockout reduces ribosome_conc (~40-60% cut) and correspondingly reduces protein_mass CV by more than the Poisson-null prediction — i.e., observed CV drop > predicted drop from mean reduction alone by at least 1.5-fold in excess noise reduction (e.g., if mean protein_mass falls 2-fold, Poisson null predicts CV rises ~41%, but we predict CV instead falls or stays flat, a qualitative sign reversal vs the null, indicating burst-size suppression dominates over simple copy-number dilution).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of per-seed protein_mass CV, rrna_operon_knockout vs wildtype, both at basal condition, matched generation; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 AND the sign of CV change is a DECREASE (or no increase) despite mean protein_mass decreasing, contradicting the Poisson-null prediction of a CV increase
falsifier.refuting_result: CV of protein_mass in rrna_operon_knockout is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2) or increases in the direction and magnitude predicted by simple 1/sqrt(mean) Poisson scaling, meaning translational burst suppression has no detectable excess effect on noise beyond mean dilution

test.statistic: welch_t

rivals.claim: Noise is driven purely by transcriptional bursting (promoter on/off switching), not translational burst size — ribosome capacity cuts would proportionally scale mean and variance together, leaving CV structure explained by mRNA-level Poisson statistics with no excess translational contribution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, rrna_operon_knockout changes protein_mass CV in exact proportion to the mean shift (slope_ci of log CV vs log mean ~ -0.5, consistent with Poisson), with no systematic deviation or sign flip.

rivals.claim: Noise differences across genes are dominated by growth-rate-coupled extrinsic noise (global physiological state, e.g. division timing, ppGpp level) rather than any gene-intrinsic translational property; rrna_operon_knockout would change noise only insofar as it changes growth_rate/ppgpp_conc, a confound unrelated to burst size per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout control (removing stringent-response/ppGpp coupling) that still shows the same CV suppression pattern under rrna_operon_knockout would argue against pure ppGpp/growth-rate mediation; if instead the CV effect disappears or reverses in the relA knockout background, extrinsic ppGpp-coupled noise is the better explanation.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's protein_mass channel aggregates proteome mass rather than single-gene reporter counts; we treat protein_mass CV across seeds as a proxy for aggregate expression noise, assuming the rrna_operon_knockout effect on global translation propagates detectably to this aggregate channel over 3 generations.
Stochastic seed-to-seed variation in this whole-cell model is assumed to meaningfully sample intrinsic + extrinsic noise sources (not purely deterministic trajectories diverging only numerically).

rrna_operon_knockout is assumed to reduce active ribosome concentration enough (measurable via ribosome_conc) to constitute a genuine translational-capacity perturbation rather than being buffered away by compensatory regulation within 3 generations.

We do not attempt to resolve single-gene (reporter-level) burst-size noise because the instrument does not expose per-gene protein copy-number distributions; this is a scope caveat — the claim is tested at the whole-proteome aggregate level as the best available operationalization.

select_score.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
select_score.claim: Across E. coli genes, expression noise (cell-to-cell variability) scales with regulatory/translational architecture rather than mean expression alone: genes whose products are low-copy and/or depend on amplifying regulatory steps (e.g. a single transcription factor gating a small regulon, or low mRNA copy number compensated by high translation efficiency) show systematically higher noise than high-copy, constitutively/ribosomally-dominated genes. Operationally, using the stringent-response regulon as a tractable proxy architecture, genes/pathways whose output is gated through RelA/ppGpp signaling (a single low-copy synthetase controlling a broad downstream response) will show higher relative variability in their downstream readouts (ppgpp_conc, and ribosome_conc as a downstream target) than a constitutively expressed high-abundance control axis (ribosome_conc under basal wildtype conditions, representing a highly buffered, high-copy output), when both are measured as coefficient of variation (CV) across isogenic replicate seeds.
select_score.h1: The CV (across seeds) of ppgpp_conc (output of a low-copy, single-enzyme-gated regulatory node, RelA) is substantially higher than the CV of ribosome_conc (a high-copy, heavily buffered output) under matched wildtype/basal conditions, and this gap is causally dependent on the low-copy regulatory node: deleting relA (removing the amplifying bottleneck) collapses the ppgpp_conc CV toward the ribosome_conc CV.
select_score.h0: ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc have statistically indistinguishable coefficients of variation across seeds under wildtype/basal conditions (no architecture-driven noise gap), and/or relA knockout does not reduce ppgpp_conc CV relative to wildtype.

operational_defs.construct: expression noise / cell-to-cell variability for a given gene product
operational_defs.observable: per-seed value of the channel (ppgpp_conc or ribosome_conc) at a matched timepoint across isogenic stochastic replicates
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) computed across seeds for that channel

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc channel (RelA synthetase concentration) and its downstream product ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean rela_conc (to confirm low abundance) and CV of ppgpp_conc as the noise readout for this architecture class

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel under wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: CV of ribosome_conc across seeds as the low-noise reference

operational_defs.construct: causal dependence of noise on the regulatory bottleneck
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc channel under relA gene_knockout vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: change in CV of ppgpp_conc (knockout vs wildtype), tested via Welch t on per-seed values

select_score.predicted_effect: Direction: CV(ppgpp_conc, wildtype) > CV(ribosome_conc, wildtype) by roughly 2-3x (e.g. ~25-40% CV for ppgpp_conc vs ~10-15% CV for ribosome_conc). Causal test: relA knockout reduces ppgpp_conc CV by at least ~40-50% relative to wildtype ppgpp_conc CV, moving it toward the ribosome_conc CV range.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Welch t comparing per-seed ppgpp_conc values vs per-seed ribosome_conc values (both under wildtype/basal, matched timepoint) after converting each to within-channel z-scores is not well-posed for CV comparison, so instead compute CV(ppgpp_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc) directly from per-seed spread/mean in each design's output; treat the wildtype/basal design as reference for both channels. Causal arm: Welch t of per-seed ppgpp_conc values, relA_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal; reject H1 (architecture-driven noise causality) if |t|<2 (i.e., knockout does not significantly shift ppgpp_conc distribution/spread).
falsifier.refuting_result: If CV(ppgpp_conc) in wildtype/basal is not clearly larger than CV(ribosome_conc) in wildtype/basal (e.g. ratio <1.3x), OR relA knockout fails to significantly change ppgpp_conc (Welch |t|<2 vs wildtype), H1 is refuted.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for relA_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal on ppgpp_conc; CV ratio ppgpp_conc:ribosome_conc >=1.3 in wildtype/basal as the descriptive noise-gap criterion

rivals.claim: Noise differences are driven purely by mean-expression level (Poisson/molecular-copy-number scaling), not by regulatory architecture per se — i.e. ppgpp_conc is noisier simply because its mean concentration is lower, not because of the RelA bottleneck structure.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV scales as expected from simple low-copy-number Poisson noise (CV ~ 1/sqrt(mean)) and relA knockout, despite changing the mean, still produces a CV matching the Poisson prediction from the new mean (no disproportionate collapse of CV), then architecture adds nothing beyond copy number and H1's causal claim is undermined.

rivals.claim: ppGpp variability is mainly driven by global growth-rate/metabolic state fluctuations (growth_rate channel), not by RelA-specific synthesis noise — i.e. ppgpp_conc noise is a downstream echo of growth_rate noise common to all channels.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(growth_rate) across wildtype seeds is similarly elevated and correlates tightly with ppgpp_conc fluctuations even after relA knockout (ppgpp_conc noise persists/tracks growth_rate noise despite removing RelA), this favors the global-state rival over the RelA-specific bottleneck claim.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation under steady-state charging meaningfully approximates intrinsic biological expression noise for these channels (ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, rela_conc) rather than being dominated by numerical/solver artifacts.
ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc are recorded under steady-state charging mode (no kinetic ppGpp module needed) so both channels are available for direct CV comparison in the same run.

relA knockout is mechanistically represented in the model (affects ppGpp synthesis) rather than being a no-op; spoT knockout serves as a secondary/partial check since SpoT also contributes to ppGpp turnover and its removal should show a distinguishable (likely smaller or differently-signed) effect than relA removal.
Matched timepoint/generation across seeds is used for CV computation so that within-cell-cycle phase effects do not confound the cross-seed variance estimate.

The comparison of CV(ppgpp_conc) vs CV(ribosome_conc) as a proxy for 'low-copy regulatory architecture vs high-copy buffered architecture' is a tractable stand-in for the broader genome-wide noise question, acknowledging this is a single architectural contrast rather than an exhaustive gene screen.

hypothesis.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
hypothesis.claim: Expression noise differences across genes are driven primarily by regulatory architecture coupled to ribosome allocation capacity: genes whose products are low-abundance and depend on limiting translational machinery (rRNA/ribosome availability) show higher cell-to-cell expression noise than high-abundance, translationally-buffered genes, because noise is dominated by low copy-number (Poisson/burst) effects amplified by competition for shared ribosomes rather than by transcriptional burst kinetics alone. Operationally: knocking down ribosome capacity (rRNA operon knockout) should disproportionately increase the coefficient of variation (CV) of low-abundance reporter/marker proteins relative to high-abundance ones, across isogenic replicate seeds.
hypothesis.h1: Across an isogenic population (seeds), genes with lower mean protein abundance show higher expression noise (CV of protein_mass-normalized per-gene proxy, approximated via protein_mass and ribosome_conc channels) than high-abundance genes, and this noise gap WIDENS when ribosome capacity is constrained (rrna_operon_knockout) relative to wildtype, consistent with shared-resource (ribosome) competition amplifying intrinsic noise for low-abundance genes.
hypothesis.h0: There is no systematic relationship between gene expression level and noise magnitude, and constraining ribosome capacity (rrna_operon_knockout) does not differentially change the CV of low- vs high-abundance gene products relative to wildtype; any CV differences across seeds are within replicate noise (Welch t < 2, no significant widening of the noise gap).

operational_defs.observable: per-seed variability of protein_mass (as proxy for total proteome output) and ribosome_conc across isogenic replicate seeds at matched generation
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) computed across seeds for each channel, within a condition

operational_defs.construct: ribosome allocation capacity / shared resource competition
operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel level and its perturbation via rrna_operon_knockout
operational_defs.measure: mean ribosome_conc across seeds, compared wildtype vs rrna_operon_knockout

operational_defs.construct: low- vs high-abundance gene expression regime
operational_defs.observable: protein_mass and rna_mass channels as proxies for overall translational output magnitude (used as a population-level stand-in since no single-gene reporter channel exists)
operational_defs.measure: CV of protein_mass across seeds, stratified by condition (wildtype vs ribosome-limited)

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: CV(protein_mass) across seeds increases under rrna_operon_knockout relative to wildtype/basal, with predicted magnitude of a ~1.5-2x fold increase in CV (e.g., wildtype CV ~0.05-0.08 rising to ~0.10-0.16 under ribosome limitation), reflecting amplified noise when ribosomes are scarce. Also predict ribosome_conc itself shows elevated CV (>=1.5x wildtype) under the knockout, consistent with resource-competition-driven noise amplification rather than a simple mean-shift.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test comparing per-seed protein_mass CV (computed by dispersion across the 6 seeds in each design) between rrna_operon_knockout/basal and wildtype/basal; reject H0 if |welch_t| >= 2 (two-sided, Welch df) indicating the CV shift is beyond replicate noise, AND effect_pct shows >=50% increase in CV under knockout
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t| < 2 or the CV increase is <20%, this refutes the claim that ribosome-capacity limitation amplifies expression noise beyond replicate-level variability

test.statistic: welch_t

rivals.claim: Noise is set primarily by intrinsic transcriptional bursting kinetics (promoter architecture) independent of ribosome/translational resource limitation — rRNA knockout would shift the MEAN of protein_mass/growth_rate (slower growth) but NOT differentially change CV.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout shows a large growth_rate decrease but protein_mass CV stays statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2), this rival is supported: noise is transcription-intrinsic, not resource-competition-driven.

rivals.claim: Noise differences are driven by ppGpp-mediated stringent response reallocation (not raw ribosome scarcity per se) — ribosome limitation triggers ppGpp accumulation which itself reshapes transcriptional noise globally via RNA polymerase competition, a confound distinct from direct ribosome-sharing.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout background (eliminating ppGpp synthesis capacity) crossed with rrna_operon_knockout should abolish or greatly reduce the CV-widening effect seen in rrna_operon_knockout alone if ppGpp signaling (not raw ribosome scarcity) is the actual noise driver; if CV still widens similarly without relA, this supports the ribosome-competition mechanism over the ppGpp-signaling rival.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes/operons, expression noise (cell-to-cell variability) scales inversely with the gene's expression/regulatory load: low-abundance, tightly-regulated genes under stringent-response control (e.g. ribosomal/translation-machinery genes whose transcription is gated by ppGpp) show higher relative noise than high-abundance constitutively expressed genes, and this noise is causally coupled to ppGpp-mediated regulatory fluctuation rather than being an intrinsic Poisson/copy-number effect alone.
drafts.h1: Genes/operons whose expression is gated by a strong regulatory input (ppGpp-dependent stringent control of ribosomal protein/rRNA-linked machinery) exhibit higher cell-to-cell noise (CV) in their proxy readout than genes/operons that are constitutively expressed at similar mean abundance, and this excess noise collapses when the regulatory input (ppGpp fluctuation) is clamped/removed.
drafts.h0: There is no systematic difference in noise (CV) between regulatorily-gated and constitutively-expressed genes/operons at matched mean abundance; apparent differences are within replicate (seed) sampling noise, and clamping ppGpp does not reduce the CV of the regulated gene's proxy readout.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed CV of ppgpp_conc, and its clamped value under the ppgpp_conc perturbation (used as the causal lever)

operational_defs.construct: expression noise of a constitutive/high-abundance comparator gene class
operational_defs.observable: protein_mass (bulk proxy for a broadly-expressed, less tightly gated class) measured per-seed across isogenic replicates
operational_defs.measure: CV of protein_mass across seeds, same condition/window

operational_defs.observable: division_rate and growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: fraction of seeds dividing on schedule; mean growth_rate, to confirm perturbations are not simply lethal (which would confound noise estimates)

drafts.predicted_effect: Regulated/ribosome-linked readout (ribosome_conc) CV across seeds in wildtype/basal is predicted to be ~2-3x higher than the constitutive comparator (protein_mass) CV (e.g. CV_ribo ~0.15-0.25 vs CV_protein ~0.05-0.08). Clamping ppGpp to a fixed multiple of basal (ppgpp_conc perturbation) is predicted to reduce ribosome_conc CV by >=40% relative to wildtype/basal, collapsing most of the gap to the constitutive comparator; growth_rate mean should shift by <20% so the CV reduction is not merely a lethality artifact.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of per-seed ribosome_conc CV (computed per seed as rolling SD/mean across the generation window, then compared target vs reference) using welch_disconfirm across seeds; reject H0 (i.e. support ppGpp-causal noise claim) if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates CV reduction >=40% in the clamp condition relative to wildtype/basal
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t|<2 or the clamp condition's ribosome_conc CV is NOT reduced by >=40% (or increases), this refutes the claim that ppGpp fluctuation causally drives the excess noise in the regulated gene class.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed CV of ribosome_conc
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct <= -40% (CV reduction)

rivals.claim: Noise differences are purely intrinsic/stochastic (low-copy-number Poisson noise): the regulated class (ribosome machinery) is simply expressed at lower absolute molecule counts than the constitutive comparator, and this copy-number effect alone explains the CV gap -- ppGpp has no causal role.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If clamping ppgpp_conc does NOT reduce ribosome_conc CV (effect_pct near 0, |welch_t|<2) despite ribosome_conc mean abundance staying similar, this supports the intrinsic-noise rival over the ppGpp-causal claim.

rivals.claim: Noise is driven by ribosome-capacity/translational bursting (rRNA operon dosage) rather than by ppGpp signaling per se -- ppGpp clamp only indirectly changes noise by changing growth rate, not by removing a genuine regulatory-noise source.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout (reduced ribosome capacity, independent of ppGpp clamping) ALSO reduces ribosome_conc CV by a comparable magnitude (>=40%) while growth_rate changes substantially (>20%), this would support the rRNA-dosage/growth-rate-confound rival rather than a specific ppGpp-noise mechanism.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales inversely with the gene's effective expression level (mRNA/protein abundance), because low-copy genes are more sensitive to stochastic birth-death fluctuations in transcription/translation. Operationally, genes whose regulatory architecture forces low steady-state ribosomal-protein or RNA abundance (e.g. rRNA-operon-limited ribosome synthesis) will show higher coefficient of variation (CV) in their proxy channels (ribosome_conc / rna_mass per-seed) than genes/conditions maintaining high abundance, with CV scaling roughly as abundance^-0.5 (the classic Poisson/intrinsic-noise relation), i.e. a 2-4x CV increase when mean abundance drops ~10-fold.
drafts.h1: Across a panel of perturbations that lower the mean abundance of a gene product's proxy channel (ribosome_conc, rna_mass), the across-seed CV of that channel increases monotonically as mean abundance decreases, consistent with an inverse square-root (Poisson-like) scaling; the population-level relationship has a negative slope with R^2 >= 0.4 when CV is regressed on log(mean abundance).
drafts.h0: Across-seed CV of the proxy channel is uncorrelated with mean abundance (slope 95% CI includes 0, or |slope| negligible), i.e. noise is NOT primarily set by copy number/abundance under these perturbations.

operational_defs.observable: across-seed variability of a channel reporting abundance of the gene product class (ribosome_conc for ribosomal proteins, rna_mass for RNA-level noise)
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) computed across seeds within a condition/generation

operational_defs.observable: mean value of the same channel (ribosome_conc or rna_mass) across seeds within a condition
operational_defs.measure: per-seed mean, then condition-level mean used as the abundance covariate

operational_defs.observable: rrna_operon_knockout (reduces ribosome/rRNA synthesis capacity) vs wildtype/basal and vs ppgpp_conc clamps that further modulate ribosome abundance
operational_defs.measure: categorical perturbation level used to generate a gradient of mean abundances for the slope regression

drafts.predicted_effect: Negative, roughly square-root-law relationship: OLS slope of log(CV) on log(mean ribosome_conc) across conditions approx -0.5 (i.e., a 10-fold drop in mean abundance -> ~3.2x rise in CV), with R^2 >= 0.4; equivalently CV in rrna_operon_knockout should be 2-4x higher than in wildtype/basal.

falsifier.decision_rule: OLS slope of log(per-seed CV of ribosome_conc) on log(mean ribosome_conc) across the 4 conditions (wildtype/basal, rrna_operon_knockout/basal, ppgpp_conc=2x/basal, ppgpp_conc=4x/basal); reject H0 if slope 95% CI excludes 0 and is negative; additionally require Welch t of CV(rrna_operon_knockout) vs CV(wildtype) with |t|>=2
falsifier.refuting_result: slope 95% CI includes 0 (or is positive), OR Welch t of CV(rrna_operon_knockout/basal) vs CV(wildtype/basal) has |t|<2 despite a >=3x drop in mean ribosome_conc -- indicating abundance is not driving noise

test.statistic: OLS slope of log(CV) on log(mean abundance) across conditions
test.threshold: 95% CI excludes 0 and slope < 0

rivals.claim: Noise is set primarily by promoter/regulatory architecture (burst size/frequency) rather than mean abundance per se -- e.g. ppGpp-mediated transcriptional bursting of rRNA/ribosomal genes could inflate CV even when mean abundance is matched.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, ppgpp_conc clamps that hold mean ribosome_conc roughly constant (e.g. 2x clamp vs wildtype with similar mean) would still show elevated CV relative to wildtype -- i.e., CV would NOT line up on the same log(CV)-log(mean) regression line, producing a poor fit (R^2 < 0.4) or an outlier condition with high leverage/residual.

rivals.claim: Noise differences mainly reflect growth-rate-dependent extrinsic/global fluctuations (e.g. variation in growth_rate or dry_mass propagating into all channels) rather than intrinsic copy-number stochasticity of the specific gene product.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, CV of ribosome_conc would correlate more strongly with CV of growth_rate or dry_mass across seeds/conditions than with mean ribosome_conc itself; a rrna_operon_knockout that lowers mean ribosome_conc but leaves growth_rate CV unchanged would still show elevated ribosome_conc CV tracking growth_rate CV, not abundance.

auxiliary_assumptions: ribosome_conc and rna_mass are adequate proxies for 'gene product abundance' noise under steady-state charging (the simulator's recorded_when constraints are respected -- no kinetic-charging run is used here).

Across-seed CV at matched generation/condition is a valid estimator of intrinsic+extrinsic expression noise given 8 seeds (acknowledged as a modest sample; CI will be wide, but slope_ci test accounts for this).

The relA knockout control is included to probe whether ppGpp-synthesis capacity itself (rather than just the abundance level it produces) is the operative noise driver -- if relA KO collapses the ppgpp_conc clamp's effect on CV, that supports abundance-mediated noise over a bursting-architecture explanation tied to RelA dynamics specifically.

We assume condition-level (not per-cell/per-mRNA) channels are an acceptable operationalization of 'this gene's expression noise' given the instrument does not expose single-gene mRNA count distributions directly; this is a scope caveat the simulator cannot fully resolve at finer resolution.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Genes whose products are low-abundance and regulated by stringent-response-sensitive machinery (ribosomal/translation-linked genes under ppGpp control) show higher cell-to-cell expression noise than high-abundance, constitutively expressed housekeeping genes, because noise scales inversely with mean copy number (Poisson/burst scaling) and is amplified by upstream regulatory fluctuations (ppGpp, charged-tRNA) that ribosomal genes are sensitive to but housekeeping genes are not.
drafts.h1: Across a panel of genes spanning low-to-high mean expression and regulatory classes, per-seed (cell-to-cell) coefficient of variation (CV) of protein/mRNA-linked readouts is a decreasing function of mean abundance (CV^2 ~ a/mean + b), AND for a fixed mean-abundance band, ribosome/translation-machinery-linked genes (sensitive to ppGpp/charged-tRNA fluctuations) show systematically higher residual CV than housekeeping genes of matched abundance.
drafts.h0: CV of expression is independent of mean abundance (flat slope, CI includes 0) and does not differ between ribosome-linked and housekeeping gene classes at matched abundance (Welch t on residual CV, |t|<2).

operational_defs.observable: per-seed distribution of a proxy readout across isogenic replicates
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = std/mean) computed across seeds of ribosome_conc (proxy for ribosomal-protein-linked genes) and protein_mass/rna_mass (proxy for bulk/housekeeping expression) per condition

operational_defs.observable: per-seed mean of the same channel used for CV
operational_defs.measure: across-seed mean of ribosome_conc or protein_mass/rna_mass at steady state

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged channels
operational_defs.measure: comparison of CV in wildtype vs ppGpp-clamped and relA-knockout backgrounds to isolate ppGpp's contribution to noise

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc (ribosomal protein proxy) vs protein_mass/rna_mass bulk channels, and rrna_operon_knockout as a ribosome-capacity perturbation
operational_defs.measure: between-class comparison of residual CV after regressing out mean abundance

drafts.predicted_effect: Negative power-law relation between CV and mean abundance across conditions/seeds: CV^2 ≈ a/mean, with fitted slope (on log-log CV vs mean) significantly negative, target R^2>=0.4 across >=4 abundance-varying conditions. At matched mean abundance, ribosome-linked channel (ribosome_conc) shows ~1.5-2x higher CV than bulk housekeeping proxy (protein_mass) in wildtype; this gap collapses to <20% difference when ppGpp is clamped at basal (removing stringent-response fluctuation) or in a relA knockout.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of per-seed CV(ribosome_conc) [computed from per-seed spread across seeds within each design], wildtype vs ppGpp-clamped; reject H1's ppGpp-dependence if |t|<2 (no significant CV reduction when ppGpp fluctuation is removed). Separately, OLS slope of log(CV) on log(mean abundance) pooled across conditions (basal, acetate, succinate, amino_acid_shift) via fit_relation; reject the inverse-scaling claim if the slope 95% CI includes 0 or is positive.
falsifier.refuting_result: CV(ribosome_conc) in wildtype vs ppgpp-clamped does not differ (|t|<2), AND/OR the CV-vs-mean slope across conditions has CI including zero, indicating noise is not governed by abundance or by ppGpp/stringent-response fluctuations as predicted.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed CV(ribosome_conc), wildtype vs ppgpp_conc-clamped
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for ppGpp-dependence; slope_ci excludes 0 (negative) for abundance-scaling (secondary test via slope_ci)

rivals.claim: Noise is driven purely by transcriptional/translational burst size (intrinsic Poisson/burst noise from promoter kinetics), independent of any stringent-response (ppGpp) signaling — ribosomal genes are just low-copy, not specially ppGpp-sensitive.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, clamping ppGpp or knocking out relA will NOT reduce ribosome_conc CV relative to wildtype (|t|<2 in the falsifier test), even though the abundance-vs-CV slope remains negative — the CV gap would persist unchanged across the ppGpp-clamp intervention, showing abundance alone (not ppGpp) explains the noise difference.

rivals.claim: Noise differences are dominated by gene-specific regulatory architecture (e.g. feedback loops, operon co-regulation) rather than by mean abundance or ppGpp at all — i.e. extrinsic regulatory topology, not a universal abundance/ppGpp scaling law.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, the pooled CV-vs-mean regression across conditions will show poor fit (R^2<0.2) or an inconsistent/non-monotonic relationship, since noise would instead cluster by gene identity/regulatory class rather than following a smooth abundance-dependent curve.

auxiliary_assumptions: ribosome_conc and protein_mass/rna_mass are adequate proxies for 'ribosomal/translation-linked gene expression' vs 'bulk housekeeping expression' in the absence of single-gene mRNA/protein noise channels for arbitrary genes.

CV computed across 6 seeds is a sufficiently stable estimator of cell-to-cell noise at this replicate count (acknowledged as noisy; power_mde could be invoked downstream if effect sizes are borderline).
Steady-state charging mode is used (not kinetic), so ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channels are valid and simultaneously available.

The relA knockout is treated as abolishing the (p)ppGpp synthesis burst that the stringent response relies on, serving as the interventional control isolating ppGpp's causal contribution from mere co-variation.

Deterministic vs stochastic contributions to simulated noise are not separately decomposed by this simulator; CV is treated as the operational measure of 'noise' regardless of its generative source (explicit scope caveat).

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes, expression noise is systematically higher for genes expressed from low-copy-number/low-flux regulatory contexts (small effective burst size), such that genes whose protein product sits at low steady-state concentration (and is regulated by a single upstream synthetase/TF rather than a high-flux constitutive pathway) show higher relative noise than high-abundance, high-flux genes — operationalized here using RelA (rela_conc), a low-abundance regulatory protein, versus ribosome-associated bulk protein (ribosome_conc as a proxy for high-abundance housekeeping expression), under isogenic replicate seeds.
drafts.h1: The coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds of a low-abundance regulatory channel (rela_conc) is substantially higher (>=3x) than the CV across seeds of a high-abundance bulk channel (ribosome_conc) under matched wildtype/basal conditions, reflecting intrinsic noise scaling with inverse mean copy number (Poisson/bursting expectation).
drafts.h0: The per-seed CV of rela_conc and ribosome_conc are statistically indistinguishable (within noise of replicate seeds), i.e. expression noise does not differ systematically between low- and high-abundance channels.

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) of rela_conc across seeds at matched generation/timepoint

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) of ribosome_conc across seeds at matched generation/timepoint

operational_defs.measure: per-seed mean concentration, used to confirm the abundance ordering assumed by the mechanism

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: CV(rela_conc) > CV(ribosome_conc). Magnitude: CV(rela_conc) ~ 25-40% vs CV(ribosome_conc) ~ 5-10% (i.e. >=3x higher relative noise for the low-abundance channel), consistent with intrinsic noise scaling as ~1/sqrt(copy number) under a bursty-transcription model.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed CV of rela_conc and of ribosome_conc across the same 6-8 seeds (wildtype/basal, generations 3). Welch t-test comparing the two per-seed CV distributions (treating each seed's CV contribution via bootstrap-resampled CV estimates, or equivalently comparing the two channels' seed-to-seed variance via the disconfirm z_vs_corpus_spread / welch_t on raw values as a proxy); reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 with CV(rela_conc) at least 3x CV(ribosome_conc).
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t|<2, or CV(rela_conc) is <1.5x CV(ribosome_conc), or CV(rela_conc) is actually LOWER than CV(ribosome_conc), H1 is refuted: low mean abundance does not predict higher relative noise in this simulator.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed values of rela_conc vs ribosome_conc (variance/CV comparison)
test.threshold: |welch_t|>=2 AND CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc)>=3

rivals.claim: Noise differences are driven by regulatory architecture (feedback/TF control) rather than raw abundance — a low-abundance gene under strong negative feedback could be LESS noisy than an unregulated high-abundance gene.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Clamping ppGpp (ppgpp_conc perturbation) or RelA's own regulatory loop via a relA knockout background and re-measuring downstream fraction_trna_charged variance would show noise suppression if feedback (not abundance) is the controlling factor; if CV ordering is preserved despite breaking the feedback loop, abundance is the better explanation.

rivals.claim: Differences in CV between rela_conc and ribosome_conc reflect measurement/aggregation artifacts (ribosome_conc is a model-aggregated steady-state quantity summed over many ribosomal proteins, mechanically damping its variance), not a biological noise difference tied to abundance per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If an independent single-protein high-abundance channel (not available here) is needed to fully rule this out, the simulator cannot resolve it directly; we flag this as an auxiliary assumption/scope caveat rather than chase it, but note that ribosome_conc's aggregation would bias toward confirming H1 for a trivial reason, which the control below partially addresses.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed snapshots of rela_conc and ribosome_conc at matched generation count are comparable across seeds despite stochastic timing of division (we use generation-matched sampling, not wall-clock time).

The simulator's steady-state charging module computes rela_conc and ribosome_conc via mechanistically distinct noise-generating processes (not merely rescaled copies of the same underlying noise source), so a CV comparison is biologically meaningful and not purely numerical.

Seed-to-seed variability in this whole-cell model is intended to capture genuine intrinsic/extrinsic expression noise (not solely integration/numerical noise); we treat this as a modeling assumption the simulator is built to support.
Wildtype/basal condition is the appropriate shared background for both channels; we are not attempting to generalize beyond this single condition in this round.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales with a gene's regulatory/translational architecture: genes whose protein output depends on low-copy-number regulatory synthesis (e.g. RelA-mediated ppGpp control, a low-abundance transcription factor) show higher relative noise (CV of steady-state concentration across isogenic replicates) than genes controlled by high-copy, constitutively-expressed machinery (e.g. ribosomal proteins), because small-number fluctuations in the upstream regulator propagate multiplicatively to the target.
drafts.h1: Low-copy-regulated gene products (operationalized as rela_conc, a RelA/ppGpp-pathway readout) exhibit higher cross-seed coefficient of variation than high-copy, growth-coupled gene products (operationalized as ribosome_conc), with CV(rela_conc) at least 2x CV(ribosome_conc) under matched wildtype conditions.
drafts.h0: CV(rela_conc) and CV(ribosome_conc) across seeds are not meaningfully different (ratio near 1, i.e. within 1.5x), i.e. noise is not systematically higher for the low-copy regulatory species.

drafts.predicted_effect: Positive, large effect: CV(rela_conc) ~ 0.35-0.5 across seeds in wildtype/basal vs CV(ribosome_conc) ~ 0.05-0.15, i.e. a ratio of CVs >= 2x (roughly 3-5x expected). In the relA knockout, CV(rela_conc)/ppgpp_conc noise signal should collapse toward the low-noise regime (ratio drops below 1.5x), consistent with the low-copy-synthesis mechanism driving the excess noise rather than generic measurement/replicate variance.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed CV of rela_conc and of ribosome_conc under wildtype/basal (n=6 seeds); compare the two CV distributions with Welch's t-test on the per-seed deviation-from-mean (normalized) values as a proxy disconfirm(target=wildtype/basal rela_conc-normalized, reference=wildtype/basal ribosome_conc-normalized, channel=rela_conc); reject H0 (noise difference is real) if |welch_t| >= 2. Separately, for the relA_knockout/basal design, reject H1's causal claim if disconfirm(relA_knockout/basal, wildtype/basal, channel=rela_conc) gives |welch_t| < 2 (i.e. knockout does not reduce the noise signal).

test.statistic: welch_t

rivals.claim: Noise is driven purely by mRNA/protein copy number (molecular shot noise), independent of any specific regulatory pathway identity — any low-abundance protein would be equally noisy regardless of whether it's RelA or something else unrelated to stringent response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a different low-abundance but non-regulatory channel (not available directly, so we substitute: comparing rela_conc noise pattern persists even after relA deletion removes the RelA protein's specific autoregulatory feedback) shows the same CV without dependence on the RelA pathway specifically, i.e. CV(rela_conc)/ppgpp_conc noise does NOT drop in the relA_knockout relative to what a generic copy-number argument would predict, this would support pure shot-noise over pathway-specific propagation.

rivals.claim: Growth-rate-mediated extrinsic noise (global fluctuations in growth_rate shared by all genes) dominates and swamps any gene-specific architecture effect, so CV differences between rela_conc and ribosome_conc mainly track differences in how tightly each channel couples to growth_rate rather than copy number per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(growth_rate) across seeds is itself large and strongly correlated with both rela_conc and ribosome_conc fluctuations (extrinsic noise dominates both equally), then the CV ratio between the two channels should shrink toward 1 once growth_rate variation is accounted for; observing a persistently large CV ratio despite similar growth_rate coupling would argue against this rival.

auxiliary_assumptions: CV computed across 6 isogenic seeds at a matched generation (gen 3) is a valid proxy for intrinsic+extrinsic expression noise in this simulator.
ribosome_conc is only available under steady-state charging (not kinetic), so all designs here use default steady_state elongation_model to keep channels comparable.
rela_conc and ppgpp_conc readouts assume the RelA/SpoT module is active in the relevant designs (steady-state charging always provides them).

Deleting relA is assumed to reduce RelA-pathway-specific propagated noise without introducing a confounding growth defect large enough to independently alter ribosome_conc CV (division_rate will be checked as a viability sanity check, not a primary readout).

Gene-identity generalization: we treat rela_conc vs ribosome_conc as a stand-in for the broader claim 'low-copy regulatory genes are noisier than high-copy growth genes' since only a finite set of named channels are instrumented; we do not claim this exhausts the genome-wide distribution, only that it is a representative, falsifiable instance of the architecture-noise relationship.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes, expression noise (cell-to-cell variability) scales inversely with the gene's expression/regulatory 'load': genes whose products are low-abundance and subject to tight feedback/regulatory control (e.g. RelA, a regulatory synthetase present at very low copy number) show much higher relative noise than high-abundance, constitutively-expressed 'housekeeping-like' structural genes (e.g. ribosomal protein pool reflected in ribosome_conc). Operationally, we test this via the two channels the instrument already exposes at single-cell resolution across seeds: rela_conc (proxy for a low-abundance regulatory protein) vs ribosome_conc (proxy for a high-abundance structural/translational pool). We predict the coefficient of variation (CV) of rela_conc across seeds is several-fold higher than the CV of ribosome_conc under matched wildtype/basal conditions, consistent with the classical intrinsic-noise scaling CV^2 ~ 1/(mean copy number) (small-number Poisson-like fluctuations dominate for low-abundance regulators).
drafts.h1: Under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the across-seed CV of rela_conc is at least 3x the across-seed CV of ribosome_conc (noise scales inversely with abundance/regulatory tightness).
drafts.h0: The across-seed CV of rela_conc is not meaningfully different from (within 1.5x of) the across-seed CV of ribosome_conc; any difference seen is replicate noise, not a systematic abundance-driven effect.

rivals.claim: Rival A: Noise is driven primarily by regulatory circuit architecture (feedback/autoregulation), not raw abundance -- a low-abundance gene under strong negative feedback could be LESS noisy than a high-abundance unregulated gene.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Clamping ppGpp (ppgpp_conc perturbation) to fixed multiples of basal, which removes RelA's own feedback dynamics, would NOT change CV(rela_conc) substantially if abundance alone drove the noise; if architecture dominates, the ppgpp_conc clamp should collapse rela_conc variance far more than abundance-scaling alone predicts.

rivals.claim: Rival B: Growth-rate-coupled global noise (extrinsic noise from cell-to-cell differences in growth rate, mass, or ribosome allocation) dominates both channels equally, so the apparent CV difference is really a measurement artifact of normalization, not gene-specific intrinsic noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If growth_rate CV correlates as strongly with rela_conc CV as with ribosome_conc CV (i.e., both channels move together with growth_rate fluctuations), that would indicate extrinsic/global noise dominates rather than gene-specific intrinsic (abundance-driven) noise; distinguishing requires rela_conc noise to remain high even after regressing out growth_rate fluctuations.

operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) computed across seeds within a condition, at matched generation

operational_defs.observable: dependence of rela_conc on upstream ppGpp feedback loop vs ribosome_conc's dependence on bulk translational mass action

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: CV(rela_conc) > CV(ribosome_conc) in wildtype/basal, with ratio >=1.5 (e.g. CV_rela ~0.30-0.45 vs CV_ribosome ~0.15-0.20). Under ppgpp_conc clamp (fixed at 1x basal), CV(rela_conc) drops by >=40% relative to wildtype/basal, approaching the housekeeping-gene CV range, consistent with a slope-like dependence of noise on upstream signal fluctuation rather than on mean abundance alone.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test comparing per-seed rela_conc values vs per-seed ribosome_conc values (both z-normalized by their own means to compare CV-equivalent spread) across the same seeds/condition; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 AND CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc) >= 1.5. Separately, for the clamp control: Welch t of rela_conc (ppgpp_conc-clamp/basal) vs rela_conc (wildtype/basal); reject H0 (noise is ppGpp-driven) if |welch_t|>=2 with clamp showing lower CV.
falsifier.refuting_result: If CV(rela_conc) is not >=1.5x CV(ribosome_conc) in wildtype/basal (ratio near 1, |welch_t|<2), or if clamping ppGpp does NOT reduce CV(rela_conc) by >=40% (clamp CV stays within 10% of wildtype CV), H1 is refuted and noise is better explained by abundance alone or by an intrinsic transcriptional/translational burst mechanism independent of ppGpp.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed CV-normalized concentration values
test.threshold: |welch_t| >= 2 for both the rela-vs-ribosome comparison and the clamp-vs-wildtype comparison

rivals.claim: Noise is driven primarily by mean abundance (low-copy-number genes are noisier purely from Poisson/molecular counting statistics), independent of regulatory architecture.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a low-abundance but NON-regulatory-coupled gene (matched low mean concentration, e.g. a low-expression housekeeping-like channel) shows the same high CV as rela_conc, and the ppGpp clamp does NOT reduce rela_conc CV, this supports the abundance-only rival over the regulatory-coupling claim.

rivals.claim: Noise is driven by translational/transcriptional bursting kinetics intrinsic to the gene's promoter/RBS strength, not by upstream signaling fluctuations.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout (which perturbs ribosome capacity/bursting dynamics broadly but does not touch the ppGpp feedback loop directly) changes CV(ribosome_conc) or CV(rela_conc) as much as the ppgpp_conc clamp does, this favors a general burst-kinetics explanation over a ppGpp-specific coupling explanation.

auxiliary_assumptions: rela_conc and ribosome_conc are both recorded under steady-state charging (the default elongation model here), so both channels are available without enabling kinetic charging.

CV computed across 8 seeds at matched generation (gen 3) is a reasonable proxy for intrinsic noise, assuming seed-to-seed variability captures stochastic/intrinsic noise rather than systematic drift across generations.

The ppgpp_conc clamp perturbation is implemented as a hard clamp to a fixed multiple of basal ppGpp, removing feedback fluctuation; we assume this clamp mechanistically silences the stochastic component of RelA's regulatory input rather than merely rescaling its mean.

Ribosome_conc is treated as a proxy for a 'high-abundance, constitutively-expressed' comparator; we assume its noise is dominated by bulk mass-action kinetics rather than its own regulatory feedback (acknowledging ribosome synthesis is itself growth-rate coupled, a scope caveat the simulator cannot fully disentangle).

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales with regulatory/translational architecture: genes whose products are low-abundance and subject to tight upstream regulatory control (here operationalized via genes that act as key regulators of the ppGpp/stringent-response and translation-capacity axis, e.g. relA and rRNA-operon-linked ribosomal genes) show HIGHER cell-to-cell noise in their associated pathway readouts than a constitutively-expressed, high-abundance housekeeping-like reference axis (ribosome_conc / growth_rate under wildtype), because small-number synthesis events and feedback amplify stochastic fluctuations when copy number is low and regulation is tight.
drafts.h1: Perturbing or removing the low-abundance regulatory node (RelA, driving ppGpp) increases the coefficient of variation (CV) of its pathway's readout (ppgpp_conc, rela_conc) across seeds substantially more than the CV of a high-abundance constitutive readout (ribosome_conc, growth_rate) changes under the same perturbation — i.e. noise is inversely related to abundance/regulatory buffering, with low-copy regulators showing >=2x higher relative CV than high-abundance structural/metabolic channels in wildtype, and knocking out the regulator (relA) further increases downstream pathway CV (ppgpp_conc) by >=50% relative to wildtype while ribosome_conc CV changes by <15%.
drafts.h0: Gene/pathway identity (low-abundance regulatory vs high-abundance constitutive) does not predict relative noise: CV(ppgpp_conc) in wildtype is statistically indistinguishable from (within 2x of) CV(ribosome_conc) or CV(growth_rate), and relA knockout does not differentially inflate ppgpp_conc CV relative to ribosome_conc CV beyond replicate-level (seed) noise.

operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) computed across seeds, per channel, per design

operational_defs.measure: fold-change in CV(ppgpp_conc), Welch t on per-seed ppgpp_conc means/variances

drafts.predicted_effect: In wildtype/basal, CV(rela_conc) and CV(ppgpp_conc) will each be >=2x the CV(ribosome_conc) and CV(growth_rate) (e.g. ~25-40% CV for the regulatory channels vs ~10-15% CV for the constitutive channels). Under relA gene_knockout, CV(ppgpp_conc) [measuring residual/basal SpoT-driven ppGpp synthesis] increases by >=50% relative to wildtype CV(ppgpp_conc), while CV(ribosome_conc) and CV(growth_rate) change by <15% relative to wildtype — i.e. the perturbation selectively destabilizes the regulatory-pathway channel, not the constitutive one.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t test of per-seed ppgpp_conc values, relA-knockout vs wildtype across seeds; reject H0 (i.e. support H1's claim of destabilization) if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates CV(ppgpp_conc) increased by >=50% relative to wildtype; additionally require CV(ribosome_conc) change <15% (computed the same way) as the discriminating condition
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t|<2 for ppgpp_conc (relA KO vs wildtype), OR CV(ppgpp_conc) increases by <50%, OR CV(ribosome_conc)/CV(growth_rate) also increase by >=50% (i.e. the destabilization is NOT selective to the regulatory channel), H1 is refuted

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 on ppgpp_conc, relA KO vs wildtype, plus effect_pct corresponding to >=50% CV increase

rivals.claim: Noise differences are driven purely by mean-abundance scaling (Poisson-like: CV ~ 1/sqrt(abundance)) regardless of regulatory architecture — i.e. any low-copy channel would be noisy, not specifically regulatory ones.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV scales simply with 1/sqrt(mean concentration) across ALL measured channels (including non-regulatory low-abundance ones) with no excess noise specific to rela_conc/ppgpp_conc beyond what their abundance alone predicts, this rival is supported — tested by comparing CV-vs-mean across the measured channel set rather than architecture category.

rivals.claim: Ribosome capacity itself (not RelA/ppGpp regulation per se) sets the global noise floor: removing rRNA operons (rrna_operon_knockout) would increase noise in ALL channels nonspecifically via reduced translational buffering, rather than noise being specific to the regulatory ppGpp axis.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under rrna_operon_knockout, if CV increases broadly across ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, AND growth_rate roughly equally (not selectively in the regulatory channel), this rival is supported and H1's selective-destabilization claim is refuted.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed values are drawn at a matched generation/timepoint across all designs so CV comparisons are not confounded by growth-phase drift.
CV computed across 6 seeds is a noisy estimator but adequate for a first-pass screen at this modest scale; a larger seed count would be requested if this candidate is approved for scale-up.
The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation is taken as a proxy for intrinsic biological expression noise (deterministic-chaos vs true stochastic-noise distinction is out of scope here).
relA knockout does not eliminate ppGpp entirely (SpoT retains basal synthesis/hydrolysis activity), so residual ppgpp_conc signal is expected and measurable, not simply zero/undefined.
rrna_operon_knockout and relA knockout are each single, in-envelope background perturbations (not combined), consistent with the platform's disallowance of combined perturbations.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes/regulons, expression noise scales inversely with the gene's expression/regulatory architecture: genes whose protein products are low-abundance AND regulated through a ppGpp/stringent-response-coupled stress pathway (e.g. rRNA/ribosome-capacity-linked genes under stress) show systematically higher cell-to-cell noise (CV of protein/mRNA-proxy channels across seeds) than high-abundance, constitutively expressed 'housekeeping' genes, because low copy number amplifies stochastic birth-death noise and upstream regulatory coupling (ppGpp, charged-tRNA) adds extrinsic noise on top of intrinsic noise.
drafts.h1: Genes with low basal expression and regulatory coupling to the stringent response (ribosome-synthesis-linked genes, read out via ribosome_conc / rna_mass under perturbations that vary ppGpp) exhibit higher across-seed CV in their expression-proxy channel than high-abundance, decoupled housekeeping-like genes (read out via protein_mass / dry_mass as composite proxies), with a predicted CV ratio of at least 2x.
drafts.h0: There is no systematic difference in across-seed CV between the low-abundance/stringent-coupled gene class and the high-abundance/housekeeping gene class; any apparent difference is within replicate noise (CV ratio ~1, Welch |t|<2 on log-CV).

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc (active ribosome concentration, a proxy for ribosomal-protein/rRNA-operon expression, which is tightly ppGpp-regulated and low-copy relative to bulk protein) measured per-seed
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) of ribosome_conc across seeds within a condition

operational_defs.observable: protein_mass (bulk, largely constitutive protein synthesis dominated by abundant housekeeping gene products) per-seed
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = sd/mean) of protein_mass across seeds within a condition

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc per-seed, used to confirm the stress/ppGpp pathway is engaged in the perturbation condition
operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc and its across-seed CV, reported alongside the noise comparison

operational_defs.observable: ratio of CV(ribosome_conc) to CV(protein_mass) within the same design
operational_defs.measure: ratio of the two CVs, log-transformed for the statistical test

drafts.predicted_effect: Across seeds under basal condition, CV(ribosome_conc) is predicted to exceed CV(protein_mass) by a ratio of >=2x (e.g. ~15-20% CV for ribosome_conc vs ~6-8% CV for protein_mass), and this ratio should INCREASE further (toward 3-4x) when ppGpp is clamped high (ppgpp_conc perturbation at 2x-4x basal), reflecting added extrinsic regulatory noise from stringent coupling on top of low-copy-number intrinsic noise.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test comparing log(CV) of ribosome_conc vs log(CV) of protein_mass, both computed across the same 6 seeds under wildtype/basal; reject H0 (noise difference is real) if |welch_t| >= 2. A discriminating causal test uses relA_knockout/basal: if the CV(ribosome_conc) vs CV(protein_mass) gap collapses (welch_t drops below 2, or ratio falls below 1.3x) when ppGpp synthesis is abolished, this supports stringent-response coupling as the noise source rather than copy number alone.
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t| < 2 comparing log(CV) of ribosome_conc vs protein_mass under wildtype/basal, OR if the CV ratio stays >=2x even after relA knockout (i.e. ppGpp removal does not shrink the gap), H1 is refuted: either there is no detectable noise difference, or the difference is driven by copy number alone, not stringent-response coupling.

test.statistic: welch_t

rivals.claim: Rival A (pure copy-number / intrinsic noise): noise is set ENTIRELY by mean copy number (Poisson birth-death noise, CV ~ 1/sqrt(N)) regardless of regulatory pathway; ppGpp coupling is irrelevant once you control for abundance.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA_knockout/basal (ppGpp removed) does NOT shrink the CV(ribosome_conc)/CV(protein_mass) ratio relative to wildtype/basal (ratio stays >=2x), this supports Rival A: the gap is purely abundance-driven, not pathway-driven.

rivals.claim: Rival B (growth-rate/extrinsic global noise dominates): most of the observed CV difference reflects global extrinsic fluctuations correlated with growth_rate (e.g. division timing variability) that affect all channels proportionally, not a gene-specific or pathway-specific noise source.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If CV(growth_rate) across seeds is itself large and highly correlated with CV(ribosome_conc) and CV(protein_mass) in the SAME proportion (i.e. the ratio of the two CVs collapses to ~1 once growth_rate variance is accounted for), this would support Rival B over a pathway-specific stringent-response noise source.

drafts.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
drafts.claim: Across genes, expression noise scales with the regulatory architecture and translational amplification of the gene rather than its mean expression level: genes that are low-copy, translationally amplified regulators (e.g. stringent-response machinery like RelA, acting through few mRNA copies with high burst translation) show higher relative noise in their protein concentration than high-copy, stably-transcribed 'housekeeping' structural genes (e.g. ribosomal protein pool reflected in ribosome_conc), even when both are run under identical isogenic conditions. The key driver we can dial here is COPY NUMBER / PATHWAY POSITION: a low-abundance regulatory node (RelA) will show higher coefficient of variation (CV) across seeds than a high-abundance structural pool (ribosome_conc) under the same wildtype condition.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions, the across-seed CV of rela_conc (low-copy regulatory protein) is substantially higher (at least 2-fold) than the across-seed CV of ribosome_conc (high-copy structural protein pool).
drafts.h0: The across-seed CV of rela_conc is not meaningfully different from (within ~1.2-fold of, or lower than) the across-seed CV of ribosome_conc; both channels show comparable relative noise under wildtype/basal.

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) of rela_conc across seeds, wildtype/basal, steady_state elongation

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (SD/mean) of ribosome_conc across seeds, wildtype/basal, steady_state elongation

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc under rrna_operon_knockout (reduced ribosome gene dosage)
operational_defs.measure: CV of ribosome_conc across seeds compared to wildtype, to test whether lowering copy number alone raises noise independent of regulatory identity

drafts.predicted_effect: rela_conc CV across seeds >= 0.30 (30%) at wildtype/basal, versus ribosome_conc CV <= 0.12 (12%) at wildtype/basal -- i.e. at least a 2-2.5-fold higher relative noise for the low-copy regulator than the high-copy structural pool.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test comparing per-seed rela_conc values against per-seed ribosome_conc values (both z-normalized by their own condition mean to compare CV-equivalent dispersion), computed via welch_disconfirm across seeds within the same wildtype/basal design; reject H1 if |welch_t| < 2 (i.e. the dispersion difference is not beyond replicate noise), OR if direct CV(rela_conc)/CV(ribosome_conc) ratio < 1.5.
falsifier.refuting_result: welch_t comparing dispersion between the two channels has |t| < 2 and the CV ratio rela_conc/ribosome_conc is < 1.5, indicating the low-copy regulator is NOT reliably noisier than the high-copy structural pool.

test.statistic: welch_t on per-seed channel values (dispersion proxy) comparing rela_conc vs ribosome_conc within wildtype/basal
test.threshold: |welch_t| >= 2 AND CV ratio >= 1.5

rivals.claim: Noise is driven primarily by mean expression level (copy number) alone, following a generic Poisson/shot-noise scaling (CV ~ 1/sqrt(mean)), with no special role for regulatory identity or translational amplification -- i.e. ANY low-abundance gene would be noisy, not specifically regulatory ones.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, reducing ribosome gene dosage via rrna_operon_knockout should raise ribosome_conc CV to match rela_conc CV purely because mean abundance drops, with no need to invoke translational bursting or regulatory architecture; the rrna_operon_knockout/basal design's ribosome_conc CV should converge toward rela_conc wildtype CV even though rRNA genes are structural, not regulatory.

rivals.claim: Noise differences are an artifact of differential growth-rate sensitivity: genes whose expression is more tightly coupled to growth_rate (e.g. ribosomal protein pools scale with growth rate) appear less noisy simply because growth_rate itself is tightly controlled, not because of intrinsic transcriptional/translational burst kinetics.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, clamping or normalizing against growth_rate variance across seeds should erase most of the CV(ribosome_conc) vs CV(rela_conc) gap; i.e. residual CV after regressing out growth_rate would be similar between channels.

auxiliary_assumptions: Across-seed variance in a single-cell-equivalent whole-cell sim is an adequate proxy for intrinsic single-gene expression noise (the simulator does not report single-cell mRNA/protein burst statistics directly, only per-seed summary channel values).
rela_conc and ribosome_conc are each stationary (steady-state charging) over the simulated generations window so that across-seed CV reflects steady-state noise rather than transient dynamics.

The relA gene_knockout control isolates whether RelA's specific regulatory role (not just its low copy number) contributes to ribosome_conc dynamics/noise; it is the closest in-envelope interventional control since a direct ppgpp_conc+gene_knockout combination is disallowed.

Comparing CV of two different channels (rela_conc vs ribosome_conc) assumes both are measured in the same units (uM) and comparably sampled across seeds, making the dispersion comparison meaningful despite different absolute scales.

Deterministic solver chaos vs genuine stochastic noise cannot be distinguished by this platform; we treat all seed-to-seed variance as the noise construct of interest and do not attempt to decompose its source further.

select_score.question: What makes one gene's expression noisier than another's?
select_score.claim: Across genes/operons, expression noise (cell-to-cell variability) scales inversely with the gene's expression/regulatory load: low-abundance, tightly-regulated genes under stringent-response control (e.g. ribosomal/translation-machinery genes whose transcription is gated by ppGpp) show higher relative noise than high-abundance constitutively expressed genes, and this noise is causally coupled to ppGpp-mediated regulatory fluctuation rather than being an intrinsic Poisson/copy-number effect alone.
select_score.h1: Genes/operons whose expression is gated by a strong regulatory input (ppGpp-dependent stringent control of ribosomal protein/rRNA-linked machinery) exhibit higher cell-to-cell noise (CV) in their proxy readout than genes/operons that are constitutively expressed at similar mean abundance, and this excess noise collapses when the regulatory input (ppGpp fluctuation) is clamped/removed.
select_score.h0: There is no systematic difference in noise (CV) between regulatorily-gated and constitutively-expressed genes/operons at matched mean abundance; apparent differences are within replicate (seed) sampling noise, and clamping ppGpp does not reduce the CV of the regulated gene's proxy readout.

select_score.predicted_effect: Regulated/ribosome-linked readout (ribosome_conc) CV across seeds in wildtype/basal is predicted to be ~2-3x higher than the constitutive comparator (protein_mass) CV (e.g. CV_ribo ~0.15-0.25 vs CV_protein ~0.05-0.08). Clamping ppGpp to a fixed multiple of basal (ppgpp_conc perturbation) is predicted to reduce ribosome_conc CV by >=40% relative to wildtype/basal, collapsing most of the gap to the constitutive comparator; growth_rate mean should shift by <20% so the CV reduction is not merely a lethality artifact.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of per-seed ribosome_conc CV (computed per seed as rolling SD/mean across the generation window, then compared target vs reference) using welch_disconfirm across seeds; reject H0 (i.e. support ppGpp-causal noise claim) if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates CV reduction >=40% in the clamp condition relative to wildtype/basal
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t|<2 or the clamp condition's ribosome_conc CV is NOT reduced by >=40% (or increases), this refutes the claim that ppGpp fluctuation causally drives the excess noise in the regulated gene class.

test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct <= -40% (CV reduction)

rivals.claim: Noise differences are purely intrinsic/stochastic (low-copy-number Poisson noise): the regulated class (ribosome machinery) is simply expressed at lower absolute molecule counts than the constitutive comparator, and this copy-number effect alone explains the CV gap -- ppGpp has no causal role.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If clamping ppgpp_conc does NOT reduce ribosome_conc CV (effect_pct near 0, |welch_t|<2) despite ribosome_conc mean abundance staying similar, this supports the intrinsic-noise rival over the ppGpp-causal claim.

rivals.claim: Noise is driven by ribosome-capacity/translational bursting (rRNA operon dosage) rather than by ppGpp signaling per se -- ppGpp clamp only indirectly changes noise by changing growth rate, not by removing a genuine regulatory-noise source.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout (reduced ribosome capacity, independent of ppGpp clamping) ALSO reduces ribosome_conc CV by a comparable magnitude (>=40%) while growth_rate changes substantially (>20%), this would support the rRNA-dosage/growth-rate-confound rival rather than a specific ppGpp-noise mechanism.
