hypothesis.predicted_effect: Positive linear relation: ribosome_conc vs growth_rate slope ~ +1.5 to +3 uM per (1/h) across basal/rich/poor conditions (R^2>=0.5, pooled seeds). ppgpp_conc vs growth_rate slope negative, ~ -2 to -5 uM ppGpp per (1/h). Under ppgpp_conc clamp (1x basal across all conditions), ribosome_conc vs growth_rate slope collapses >=70% in magnitude vs wildtype (near-flat). Under rrna_operon_knockout, ribosome_conc drops ~30-50% at EVERY condition (a parallel downward shift, Welch |t|>=2 vs wildtype at each matched growth_rate) while the wildtype-vs-knockout slope difference is NOT significant (|welch_t|<2 on slope estimates) — distinguishing capacity-limitation (level shift) from signaling-abolition (slope flattening).

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1: Fit OLS slope of ribosome_conc on growth_rate pooled across seeds for wildtype across >=3 conditions (basal, acetate, amino_acid-supplemented timeline); reject H0 if slope 95% CI excludes 0 AND R^2>=0.5. Step 2: Compute the same slope under the ppgpp_conc clamp (1x basal) across the same 3 conditions; reject the ppGpp-dependence claim (favor H0) if the clamped slope's 95% CI does NOT exclude the wildtype slope point estimate, OR if Welch |t|<2 for clamped-vs-wildtype ribosome_conc at matched growth_rate bins (i.e., clamp fails to flatten). Step 3 (rival exclusion): Welch t of ribosome_conc, rrna_operon_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal, at matched growth_rate bin; if |welch_t|>=2 (level shift present) AND the knockout-vs-wildtype slope difference (computed the same way as Step 2) has |welch_t|<2 (slope preserved), this confirms the capacity rival is distinguishable from (not a confound for) the ppGpp mechanism.
falsifier.refuting_result: Either the wildtype slope CI includes 0 (no growth-rate coupling to falsify in the first place), or the ppgpp_conc clamp fails to flatten ribosome_conc relative to wildtype (|welch_t|<2 clamped-vs-wildtype AND clamped slope CI overlaps wildtype slope), showing ribosome output is set independent of ppGpp signaling.

test.statistic: OLS slope of ribosome_conc vs growth_rate, pooled seeds, wildtype vs ppgpp_conc-clamped across >=3 conditions; secondary welch_t of ribosome_conc at matched growth_rate bins for clamped-vs-wildtype and knockout-vs-wildtype
test.threshold: wildtype slope 95% CI excludes 0 and R^2>=0.5; clamp falsifies H1 if clamped slope CI overlaps wildtype point estimate OR |welch_t|<2; knockout supports rival-exclusion if |welch_t|>=2 at matched growth_rate (level shift) but slope-difference |welch_t|<2 (slope preserved)

rivals.claim: Ribosome concentration is set passively by translational flux demand (supply-demand matching via charged-tRNA pools) without ppGpp acting as the control signal — ppGpp is merely a correlated downstream reporter of charged-tRNA levels, not the allocator.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival holds, clamping ppgpp_conc while fraction_trna_charged still varies by condition would STILL show ribosome_conc tracking growth_rate/condition (clamped slope CI would NOT overlap zero and would resemble wildtype, |welch_t|<2 clamped-vs-wildtype at matched growth_rate), because the real driver (charged-tRNA-coupled flux) is untouched by the clamp — contradicting H1's flattening prediction.

rivals.claim: Ribosome allocation is primarily set by rRNA operon copy number/transcriptional capacity (a hard-wired structural limit), not by a regulatory ppGpp dial that responds to medium richness.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout depresses ribosome_conc at ALL growth rates in parallel (Welch |t|>=2 at each matched growth_rate, a level shift) while the knockout-vs-wildtype SLOPE difference stays non-significant (|welch_t|<2), AND the ppgpp_conc clamp still produces a wildtype-like (non-flattened) slope versus growth_rate — jointly showing capacity, not ppGpp signaling, sets the dial, directly refuting H1's clamp-flattening prediction.

auxiliary_assumptions: Steady-state charging mode is used (not kinetic) so ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc are both recorded as defined channels.
Across the chosen conditions (basal, acetate, amino_acid-supplemented via timeline) the model implements differential growth rates reflecting nutrient richness.
Per-seed steady-state averages over the final generation are a valid proxy for the 'decided' ribosome level, ignoring within-generation transients.
The ppgpp_conc clamp perturbation mechanistically suppresses RelA/SpoT-driven ppGpp synthesis in the model rather than only overriding the reported channel value.
Seed-to-seed intrinsic noise is small relative to between-condition differences, justifying pooling seeds for the slope fit.

'Matched growth_rate bins' for the rrna_operon_knockout comparison are feasible because the knockout, though slower overall, still spans a growth-rate range overlapping wildtype across the 3 conditions tested; if ranges do not overlap, the level-shift test uses the nearest-neighbor growth_rate bin per condition as a documented approximation.

drafts.question: How does a cell decide how many ribosomes to make in a given medium?
drafts.claim: The cell sets ribosome content via the ppGpp-mediated stringent response acting as a growth-rate control: in richer media (more amino acids available, higher charged-tRNA fraction), ppGpp is kept low, which derepresses rRNA/r-protein synthesis so that ribosome concentration scales positively with growth rate; conversely, a condition that forces low charged-tRNA (nutrient downshift) raises ppGpp and lowers ribosome concentration even though it is the SAME genotype, establishing ppGpp as the causal dial rather than growth rate being 'read' directly by the ribosome-synthesis machinery.
drafts.h1: Across media conditions that differ in amino-acid richness, ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc are negatively coupled: shifting from basal (minimal) to an amino-acid-supplemented timeline raises fraction_trna_charged, lowers ppgpp_conc (>=30% drop), and raises ribosome_conc (>=25% increase) and growth_rate, relative to basal; a ppgpp_conc clamp at high multiple-of-basal in amino-acid-rich media blocks the ribosome_conc increase despite high charged-tRNA, showing ppGpp is causally necessary, not merely a correlated passenger.
drafts.h0: ribosome_conc does not differ (beyond replicate noise) between basal and amino-acid-supplemented timelines, OR ppgpp_conc clamp does not block the ribosome_conc increase (i.e., ribosome content tracks growth rate/media directly, independent of ppGpp level).

drafts.h0: ribosome_conc does not covary with growth_rate across conditions (OLS slope 95% CI includes 0), or the slope in the ppGpp-clamped background is statistically indistinguishable from the wildtype slope (ppGpp clamp does not break the coupling).

drafts.predicted_effect: Wildtype across conditions (basal, acetate, succinate, malate, fumarate as a 5-point growth-rate gradient): OLS fit ribosome_conc ~ growth_rate gives slope > 0 with R^2 >= 0.7 (an ~2-3 fold range in ribosome_conc across the ~0.3-1.5 /h growth-rate range, consistent with the empirical growth law). In the ppgpp_conc-clamped background run across the same condition panel, predicted slope magnitude drops by >=70% (CI includes 0), i.e. the clamp abolishes the coupling.

falsifier.decision_rule: Fit OLS slope of ribosome_conc on growth_rate across the 5-condition panel (wildtype/basal, wildtype/acetate, wildtype/succinate, wildtype/malate, wildtype/fumarate) via slope_ci; reject H0 if slope>0 and 95% CI excludes 0 with R^2>=0.7. Then fit the same OLS across the matched ppgpp_conc-clamped panel; H1 requires that slope's CI to include 0 (or magnitude <=30% of wildtype slope). test.threshold: wildtype slope CI excludes 0 & R^2>=0.7; clamped slope CI includes 0 or |slope_clamped| <= 0.3*|slope_wt|

rivals.claim: Ribosome concentration is set directly by nutrient/carbon flux sensing (e.g. via cAMP-CRP or other catabolite signaling) independent of ppGpp, with ppGpp merely a downstream correlate, not a causal mediator.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, clamping ppgpp_conc will NOT flatten the ribosome_conc vs growth_rate slope -- the slope stays significant and similar in magnitude to wildtype (refuting_result above), because the real driver (catabolite flux) still varies normally across conditions.

rivals.claim: Ribosome number is passively determined by translational demand / protein synthesis flux (supply-demand matching via mRNA/ribosome queuing) rather than an active regulatory set-point, so ppGpp clamp changes absolute ribosome levels but not the condition-to-condition SCALING relationship.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Under this rival, clamping ppGpp shifts the intercept of the ribosome_conc vs growth_rate line (uniform up/down shift across all conditions) but the slope itself remains positive and significant -- distinguishable from H1's prediction of slope flattening toward zero.

auxiliary_assumptions: The five static media conditions (basal, acetate, succinate, malate, fumarate) produce a sufficiently broad spread of steady-state growth rates (roughly 0.3-1.5 /h) to support a meaningful slope fit with only 5 points per arm.
ribosome_conc as recorded under steady-state charging is a faithful proxy for 'number of ribosomes made' (active ribosome pool), not a transient or compartmentalized measure.

The ppgpp_conc clamp perturbation holds ppGpp fixed across all five conditions at the same multiple of basal, successfully decoupling ppGpp from its normal nutrient-responsive dynamics without otherwise crashing growth (division_rate not catastrophically <1).

relA knockout (discriminating control) is included to corroborate that ppGpp synthesis machinery itself (not just its clamped level) is mechanistically required; this is a complementary but not load-bearing part of the primary falsifier.
Per-seed averaging over the last generation adequately captures steady-state behavior despite stochastic noise; we are not modeling non-steady-state transitions within a condition.

hypothesis.claim: E. coli sets ribosome concentration via the ppGpp-mediated stringent response acting as a growth-rate sensor: richer media (higher achievable growth rate) drive lower ppGpp, which de-represses rRNA/r-protein synthesis, so ribosome_conc scales positively with growth_rate and negatively with ppgpp_conc across media conditions, and this coupling is causally dependent on ppGpp (not an epiphenomenon of charged-tRNA levels alone).
hypothesis.h1: Across media conditions of differing nutrient quality, steady-state ribosome_conc increases monotonically with growth_rate (approx linear, slope > 0, R^2 >= 0.6) and decreases with ppgpp_conc; clamping ppgpp_conc at a fixed multiple of basal collapses this relationship (growth-rate dependence of ribosome_conc is abolished or strongly attenuated, >=50% slope reduction) relative to the unclamped condition-matched baseline.
hypothesis.h0: ribosome_conc does not vary systematically with growth_rate across conditions (OLS slope 95% CI includes 0, or R^2 < 0.2), and/or clamping ppgpp_conc produces no significant change in the growth-rate vs ribosome_conc slope relative to the unclamped baseline (i.e., ppGpp is not causally required for the relationship).

drafts.predicted_effect: Negative, approximately log-linear relationship: log(ribosome_conc) ~ -slope * ppgpp_conc, with slope such that a 2-4x drop in ppgpp_conc (rich vs poor) corresponds to a 2-4x rise in ribosome_conc; target R^2 >= 0.6 across the condition panel (basal, acetate, succinate, fumarate, malate). In the relA-knockout background, this slope should collapse toward ~0 (ppGpp no longer tracks richness), breaking the correlation.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ribosome_conc, acetate vs basal, across seeds; reject H0 if |welch_t| >= 2 AND the directional sign matches predicted (basal higher). Also require the complementary OLS slope of log(ribosome_conc) on ppgpp_conc pooled across the 5-condition panel to have 95% CI excluding 0 (negative slope).
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t| < 2 for ribosome_conc (acetate vs basal), or if the slope_ci for log(ribosome_conc) vs ppgpp_conc across conditions includes 0 or is positive, H1 is refuted: ribosome content does not track the ppGpp set-point as predicted.

rivals.claim: Direct translational-demand sensing: ribosome allocation tracks charged-tRNA fraction / translation elongation rate directly, with ppGpp merely a correlated byproduct, not the causal lever.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA is knocked out (abolishing ppGpp synthesis) and ribosome_conc STILL rises in rich media tracking fraction_trna_charged with similar magnitude to wildtype, this shows ppGpp is not required — ribosome control is ppGpp-independent, refuting the alarmone-set-point model.

rivals.claim: Ribosome concentration is set passively by dilution/growth-rate feedback (faster growth dilutes repressors, derepressing rrn operons) rather than by an active ppGpp sensing mechanism — ppGpp and ribosome_conc co-vary only because both are downstream consequences of growth rate.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If clamping ppgpp_conc directly (via the ppgpp_conc perturbation) to a fixed low value across different media conditions FAILS to raise ribosome_conc to the predicted level (i.e., ribosome_conc still tracks growth_rate/condition rather than the clamped ppGpp value), this supports growth-rate-driven dilution over a direct ppGpp causal lever.

auxiliary_assumptions: Steady-state charging module is active for these runs (ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc are only jointly recorded under steady-state charging, not kinetic), so elongation_model is left at steady_state default.

The five static media conditions (basal, acetate, succinate, fumarate, malate) span a sufficient richness gradient to detect a monotonic ppGpp-ribosome relationship; acetate/succinate/fumarate/malate are treated as 'poor' and basal as 'rich'.
relA knockout is assumed to substantially reduce/abolish RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis in this model (downstream SpoT basal synthesis may remain, but the stringent spike is removed).
Per-seed steady-state averages over the last generation are representative of the condition's physiological set-point (avoiding transient startup effects).

Division_rate is assumed near 1 for all conditions tested here (no gross lethality), so growth_rate/ribosome_conc comparisons are not confounded by differential viability; this is not separately modeled as a rival.

select_score.question: How does a cell decide how many ribosomes to make in a given medium?
select_score.claim: E. coli sets ribosome concentration via the ppGpp-mediated stringent-response feedback that tracks charged-tRNA availability: richer media (lower amino-acid limitation) yield higher fraction_trna_charged, which lowers ppgpp_conc, which in turn permits higher ribosome_conc — i.e., ribosome allocation is a ppGpp-dependent setpoint rather than a fixed, media-independent constant.
select_score.h1: Across media conditions that differ in amino-acid richness, ribosome_conc negatively covaries with ppgpp_conc (steady-state growth law), and this coupling is causally mediated by ppGpp: directly clamping ppgpp_conc to a low multiple of basal in poor medium raises ribosome_conc toward rich-medium levels, while clamping it high in rich medium suppresses ribosome_conc toward poor-medium levels.
select_score.h0: Ribosome_conc does not track ppgpp_conc causally across conditions: artificially clamping ppgpp_conc produces no significant shift in ribosome_conc relative to the matched unclamped condition (ribosome level is set by some ppGpp-independent mechanism, e.g. direct nutrient-flux sensing of translation capacity).

rivals.claim: Ribosome concentration is set directly by charged-tRNA/translation-flux sensing without requiring ppGpp as the causal intermediate (ppGpp is merely a correlated co-mover of growth rate, not the lever).
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA knockout background (which abolishes amino-acid-starvation-induced ppGpp synthesis), ribosome_conc still shifts with condition richness (basal vs rich) by a similar magnitude to wildtype, showing ppGpp is dispensable for the ribosome-richness relationship.

auxiliary_assumptions: Steady-state charging model is used (not kinetic), so ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc channels are both recorded and comparable across all designs.
fraction_trna_charged under steady-state is a broadcast of 20 per-amino-acid values; averaging across them is an acceptable scalar summary for this test.
The ppgpp_conc clamp perturbation holds the alarmone at a fixed multiple of basal for the whole run (no mid-run switching), consistent with the envelope.
basal_plus_amino_acids is treated as a static fitted media condition (not a mid-run timeline shift), avoiding the disallowed carbon-source-switch restriction.
Cell-to-cell seed variability (intrinsic noise) is small relative to the condition/clamp effect size we predict (>=30%), so 6 seeds give adequate power; this will be checked post hoc.

We are not claiming the model mechanistically simulates every real regulatory detail of RelA/SpoT; the test only asks whether the simulator's built-in ppGpp module behaves as a causal lever on ribosome_conc.

hypothesis.question: How does a cell decide how many ribosomes to make in a given medium?
hypothesis.claim: E. coli sets ribosome concentration via the ppGpp-mediated stringent-response feedback that couples ribosome synthesis rate to charged-tRNA availability (amino-acid supply): in richer media (higher charged-tRNA fraction), ppGpp is lower, derepressing rRNA/r-protein synthesis and producing a higher steady-state ribosome concentration, following the classical growth-rate-dependent ribosome allocation (Scott/Hwa-type) relation across media.
hypothesis.h1: Across media conditions that differ in amino-acid richness, ribosome_conc scales positively with growth_rate and negatively with ppgpp_conc, with ppgpp_conc tracking (inversely) fraction_trna_charged; a background knockout of ppGpp synthesis (relA-type, approximated here by rrna_operon_knockout as the closest in-envelope lever on ribosome capacity, and more directly by clamping ppgpp_conc) causally shifts ribosome_conc independent of nutrient richness, confirming ppGpp as the causal setpoint rather than a mere correlate.
hypothesis.h0: Ribosome_conc does not depend on ppGpp level or media richness in a systematic, feedback-driven way: across conditions and across ppgpp_conc clamps, ribosome_conc and growth_rate show no reliable (CI-excluding-zero) relationship with ppgpp_conc or fraction_trna_charged, i.e. any apparent correlation across wildtype media is noise or is not altered by direct ppGpp manipulation.

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Positive linear relation of ribosome_conc on growth_rate across 3 media conditions (basal, acetate, and a richer amino-acid-supplemented timeline) with slope >0 and R^2>=0.6 (Scott-Hwa-like line); ppgpp_conc negatively correlated with fraction_trna_charged (slope<0, CI excludes 0) and with ribosome_conc (~2-3 fold higher ppgpp_conc in acetate/basal vs amino-acid-rich, paired with ~1.5-2x lower ribosome_conc). Clamping ppgpp_conc to 4x basal is predicted to cut ribosome_conc by >=30% relative to wildtype/basal regardless of media richness (Welch t>=2, effect_pct<=-30%).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ribosome_conc, 4x ppGpp clamp vs wildtype/basal, across seeds; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct<=-30% (directionally consistent with ppGpp suppressing ribosome synthesis)
falsifier.refuting_result: 4x ppGpp clamp shows |welch_t|<2 or effect_pct within +/-10% of wildtype/basal ribosome_conc, indicating ribosome level is insensitive to directly elevated ppGpp and the correlational media-dependence is not causal

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |welch_t|>=2 and effect_pct<=-30%

rivals.claim: Ribosome concentration is set primarily by translation elongation/demand (passive dilution and mass-action with ongoing protein synthesis) rather than by ppGpp signaling per se — ppGpp and ribosome level are both downstream co-movers of growth rate, not cause and effect.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, clamping ppgpp_conc at 4x basal would leave ribosome_conc close to wildtype (|effect_pct|<10%) because ribosome allocation is actually driven by growth-rate-coupled demand, not by the alarmone directly — i.e., the falsifier's refuting_result is observed.

rivals.claim: Ribosome capacity itself (rRNA operon dosage) is the primary determinant, and ppGpp merely reports/modulates around a capacity set by operon copy number; media richness changes demand but the cell cannot exceed capacity set elsewhere.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal (reduced rRNA gene dosage) would show a strong reduction in ribosome_conc (large effect, e.g. >=40%, |welch_t|>=2) even without any ppGpp clamp, and would blunt or override the ppGpp clamp's effect when combined conceptually (though combined perturbations are out of envelope here, the standalone knockout's large effect size relative to the ppGpp clamp's effect size would indicate capacity, not signaling, is primary).

auxiliary_assumptions: Steady-state charging mode is used (not kinetic), so ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc channels are populated and directly comparable across conditions.

fraction_trna_charged broadcast columns are averaged across the 20 amino acids to obtain a single per-seed scalar proxy for nutrient richness; no attempt is made to resolve per-amino-acid heterogeneity.
The amino-acid-supplemented timeline condition is assumed to raise mean fraction_trna_charged relative to basal/acetate, serving as the 'rich medium' endpoint of the Scott-Hwa-type line.

ppgpp_conc clamp is assumed to act upstream of rRNA/r-protein transcription in the model's regulatory network (i.e., the simulator implements ppGpp-dependent transcriptional control of rRNA), which is checked downstream; if the clamp has no wiring to ribosome synthesis in the model, this is logged as a capability gap rather than re-litigated.

Division_rate is not the primary readout here but will be monitored as a sanity check that rrna_operon_knockout and extreme ppGpp clamps do not simply kill the cell before steady-state ribosome_conc can be assessed.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli triggers the stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes sharply, which in turn suppresses ribosome synthesis/activity and collapses growth rate, rather than the cell simply growing slower due to generic substrate limitation without an alarmone surge.
hypothesis.h1: Amino-acid starvation causes a rapid (within ~1 generation), large-magnitude rise in ppgpp_conc (>=3-fold vs basal) driven by RelA, accompanied by a fall in ribosome_conc/ribosomal-protein levels and growth_rate, and this response requires RelA (relA knockout abolishes the ppGpp spike and blunts the growth-rate response).
hypothesis.h0: Removing amino acids changes growth_rate and ribosome_conc only via mass-action substrate limitation (reduced charged-tRNA availability slowing translation), with no significant ppGpp spike above basal/replicate noise, and a relA knockout shows the same growth-rate trajectory as wildtype under starvation.

hypothesis.predicted_effect: ppgpp_conc rises >=3-fold (e.g. from ~20uM basal to >=60uM) within 1 generation of amino-acid removal; growth_rate falls by >=50% over the same window; ribosome_conc declines by >=20-30%; in relA_knockout under the same shift, ppgpp_conc fold-change is <1.5x (abolished spike) and growth_rate decline is attenuated to <25%. A power_mde check confirms n=6 seeds/3 generations can detect effects >=100% fold-change on ppgpp_conc and growth_rate, well below the predicted >=200% effect, so the headline test is not underpowered.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (power check): power_mde on ppgpp_conc at seeds=6, generations=3 must show min-detectable-effect <=100% fold-change; if not, increase seeds before interpreting a null. Step 2: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, amino_acid_shift/aa_removal vs wildtype/basal, across seeds at the post-shift timepoint; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct>=200% (i.e. >=3-fold rise)
falsifier.refuting_result: Either the power_mde check shows the design IS adequately powered (MDE<=100%) and yet ppgpp_conc shows |welch_t|<2 or effect_pct<100% (less than 2-fold change) -- indicating no meaningful stringent-response alarmone surge despite adequate power to detect one

test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=200%, confirmed powered via power_mde MDE<=100% at n=6

rivals.claim: Growth arrest is driven purely by substrate-level translation slowdown (charged-tRNA depletion reducing elongation rate) without a necessary ppGpp regulatory surge — ppGpp rises only marginally as a passive correlate, not a causal driver.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In relA_knockout under the same amino_acid_shift, growth_rate still collapses by >=50% (same magnitude as wildtype) because the mechanism is substrate-level, not RelA-ppGpp dependent; fraction_trna_charged still drops similarly in both genotypes.

rivals.claim: The response is mediated primarily by ribosome-capacity limitation (fewer ribosomes made available) rather than an active ppGpp alarmone signal — i.e. a structural/capacity constraint, not a regulatory stringent response. This rival predicts that capacity limitation ALONE (no starvation) reproduces the growth/ribosome phenotype without any ppGpp involvement, which the rrna_operon_knockout/basal design below directly tests as a discriminating control.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout under basal (non-starved) condition alone reproduces a similar growth_rate decline and ribosome_conc drop WITHOUT any ppGpp spike (disconfirm(rrna_operon_knockout/basal, wildtype/basal, ppgpp_conc) shows |welch_t|<2), showing capacity limitation alone suffices and ppGpp is not necessary for the growth phenotype. If instead rrna_operon_knockout/basal shows a significant ppGpp rise too, that would suggest ppGpp responds generically to any ribosome-translation imbalance, weakening the specific amino-acid-starvation-trigger claim.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's RelA/SpoT ppGpp kinetic module is active for this run (required for rela_conc and kinetic ppGpp dynamics to be meaningful); if only steady-state charging is available, ppgpp_conc reflects a quasi-equilibrium approximation rather than a true kinetic spike, which is a scope caveat on timing claims.

The amino_acid_shift timeline event ('minimal_plus_amino_acids' -> 'minimal') is interpreted by the simulator as a genuine withdrawal of exogenous amino acid supply, not merely a carbon-source change (disallowed).
Replicate seeds capture intrinsic stochastic noise only; deterministic vs stochastic contributions to any residual ppGpp variability are not separable by this instrument and are not pursued further.

relA_knockout removes the (p)ppGpp synthetase activity sufficiently to be treated as a clean mechanistic ablation of the stringent-response synthesis arm, ceteris paribus for other regulatory network components.

The rrna_operon_knockout/basal design is included specifically and ONLY as the discriminating control for the ribosome-capacity rival (r1.2 resolved): it isolates whether ribosome-capacity limitation alone, absent starvation, can mimic the phenotype without a ppGpp surge; it is not used to test any additional independent claim about operon redundancy.

power_mde is computed on the same channel/design pair used for the headline falsifier (ppgpp_conc, amino_acid_shift/aa_removal vs wildtype/basal) at the proposed n=6 seeds, so a non-significant Welch result cannot be dismissed as mere underpowering (r1.1 resolved).

objection_ledger.issue: The claim and falsifier assume that 3 generations and 6 seeds give adequate statistical power to detect a true fitness cost as small as the implicit threshold distinguishing 'cluster 2' (>=30% growth reduction) from noise, but no power analysis or expected effect-size-vs-noise floor is given to justify that |welch_t|<2 at this sample size won't simply be underpowered for intermediate-cost genes, artificially inflating the 'dispensable' cluster. This could confound the headline fraction with a sheer power issue rather than a genuine bimodal biological split.

The rrna_operon_knockout design row (operons_removed:3) appears in candidate_designs but is never connected to h1/h0, the falsifier, or either rival — it's an orphan perturbation. If it's meant to test a related claim about rRNA operon redundancy, that claim needs its own h1/falsifier; if not needed, it should be removed, since it currently just adds an unexplained auxiliary manipulation.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli triggers the stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes sharply (>=5-fold basal), which in turn drives rapid downshift of ribosome synthesis/activity and growth rate, rather than growth declining passively from substrate limitation alone.
hypothesis.h1: Removal of amino acids causes a fast (within ~1 generation), large (>=5-fold) rise in ppgpp_conc relative to the wildtype/basal reference, accompanied by a drop in ribosome_conc/growth_rate, and this ppGpp rise is causally necessary for the ribosome/growth downshift (abolished when RelA is knocked out).
hypothesis.h0: ppgpp_conc does not rise appreciably (less than 2-fold, not Welch-significant) after amino-acid removal, and/or the growth-rate and ribosome_conc decline is unaffected by relA knockout — i.e., the downshift is driven purely by substrate (charged-tRNA) limitation on translation, not by an active regulatory ppGpp surge.

hypothesis.predicted_effect: ppgpp_conc rises >=5-fold (e.g., basal ~20-50 uM -> >=100-250 uM) within 1 generation of amino-acid removal in wildtype; growth_rate drops by >=50% and ribosome_conc drops by >=30% over the same window. In the relA knockout background, the ppGpp rise is blunted to <2-fold and the growth-rate/ribosome_conc decline is significantly attenuated (at least 40% smaller relative decline than wildtype under the SAME aa-removal shift), demonstrating causal dependence on RelA-driven ppGpp rather than passive substrate exhaustion. Both the ppGpp-induction criterion and the causal-attenuation criterion must hold jointly to confirm H1; either one failing supports H0 (see decision_rule).

falsifier.decision_rule: Two-part AND test, both must pass to confirm H1: (1) induction test -- Welch t of ppgpp_conc, target (amino_acid_shift/wildtype_aa_removed) vs reference (wildtype/basal) across seeds at the post-shift timepoint; pass if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct>=400 (>=5-fold rise). (2) causal-necessity test -- Welch t of growth_rate DECLINE MAGNITUDE (pre- vs post-shift delta) comparing relA-KO-under-shift (gene_knockout/relA_aa_removed) vs wildtype-under-shift (amino_acid_shift/wildtype_aa_removed); pass (supports causality) if |welch_t|>=2 AND the KO's decline magnitude is >=40% smaller (attenuated) than wildtype's. H1 is confirmed only if BOTH (1) and (2) pass. If (1) fails (induction test: |t|<2 or effect_pct<400) OR (2) fails (|t|<2, i.e., KO decline statistically indistinguishable from WT decline, OR attenuation <40%), H0 is supported -- a single failing leg is sufficient to refute H1, no further criterion is needed to adjudicate disagreement.
falsifier.refuting_result: welch_t for ppgpp_conc target vs reference is <2 (not significant) or effect_pct<400 (less than ~5-fold rise), OR the relA knockout shows growth_rate decline statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (|welch_t|<2 for the knockout-vs-wildtype decline-magnitude comparison) or attenuation <40% -- either failing leg alone refutes H1's causal claim.

test.threshold: leg1: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=400 for ppgpp induction (target vs reference); leg2: |t|>=2 and >=40% smaller decline magnitude for relA-KO-vs-WT growth_rate decline under shift; BOTH legs must pass to confirm H1, either failing refutes H1

rivals.claim: Passive-limitation rival: growth and ribosome decline are explained entirely by charged-tRNA/substrate depletion slowing translation elongation directly, with ppGpp playing no causal regulatory role (it may rise as an epiphenomenal byproduct of the same depleted tRNA pools).
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA knockout, fraction_trna_charged still drops sharply (confirming substrate depletion occurs) but growth_rate/ribosome_conc decline tracks the SAME magnitude/timecourse as wildtype despite blunted ppGpp -- i.e., no significant attenuation (leg 2 fails: |welch_t|<2 or <40% attenuation) of the growth/ribosome drop in relA KO vs wildtype.

rivals.claim: Ribosome-capacity-limited rival: the growth defect is primarily a consequence of pre-existing ribosome capacity (rRNA operon dosage) rather than an acute ppGpp-driven regulatory downshift -- i.e., cells with fewer ribosome operons would show a comparable growth defect regardless of amino acid shift, implicating constitutive capacity over an acute signaling response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout under basal (no aa shift) condition already shows comparably depressed growth_rate close to the amino-acid-shifted wildtype magnitude, suggesting capacity alone (not the acute aa-removal signal) explains most of the effect; this would appear as a small growth_rate gap between rrna_operon_knockout/basal and amino_acid_shift/wildtype_aa_removed even though no acute signal was given to the rRNA-KO strain.

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline shift from 'minimal_plus_amino_acids' to 'minimal' is interpreted by the simulator as a sharp, complete removal of all supplemented amino acids at the 60-min mark (not a gradual depletion), matching the intended 'sudden' perturbation.
steady-state charging mode is in effect (ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc channels are populated), not kinetic-charging-only mode where these channels go silent.
relA knockout in this model does not also eliminate SpoT basal ppGpp synthesis entirely; residual SpoT activity is treated as part of the 'blunted but not necessarily zero' ppGpp response in the KO.

The r1.1 objection (n=2 stratum power) pertains to a different, now-superseded multi-gene screen candidate and is out of scope for this single-shift causal hypothesis; it is not applicable here and is not re-addressed.
Per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories are sampled finely enough post-shift to identify a clear 'post-shift timepoint' within 1 generation for the fold-change comparison.

objection_ledger.issue: The stratification is still only 4 genes per stratum (except accessory=5), and 'known-essential' stratum has only 2 genes (pyrD, folK). With n=2 for known-essential, a single noisy seed could flip the per-stratum pattern used to adjudicate Rival B (cherry-picking vs genuine heterogeneity). This is a statistical-power concern on an already-resolved design choice, not a new construct problem.

The decision rule combines a global BC threshold with a global FDR-significant-fraction threshold, but doesn't specify what happens if the two criteria disagree (e.g., BC>0.555 but <10% FDR-significant, or vice versa) in a way that would support H1 rather than requiring both to jointly reject H0 only. It's stated clearly enough for 'reject H1' (AND condition) but the symmetric 'support H1' criterion is left implicit in predicted_effect rather than formalized in decision_rule.

Sarle's bimodality coefficient is sensitive to sample size and skew, and this is being computed over only 20 genes' pooled per-seed effect values (effectively ~120 points but only 20 independent gene-level clusters) — it's unclear whether the simulator and this panel size can actually deliver a reliable BC estimate near the 0.555 threshold, as opposed to an artifact of small-panel sampling.

The claim and falsifier assume that 3 generations and 6 seeds give adequate statistical power to detect a true fitness cost as small as the implicit threshold distinguishing 'cluster 2' (>=30% growth reduction) from noise, but no power analysis or expected effect-size-vs-noise floor is given to justify that |welch_t|<2 at this sample size won't simply be underpowered for intermediate-cost genes, artificially inflating the 'dispensable' cluster. This could confound the headline fraction with a sheer power issue rather than a genuine bimodal biological split.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli triggers the stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes sharply, ribosome concentration falls, and growth rate drops, with the ppGpp spike being RelA-dependent (abolished in a relA knockout).
hypothesis.h1: An abrupt amino-acid withdrawal causes a rapid (within ~1 generation) rise in ppgpp_conc (>=3-fold over basal) accompanied by a fall in fraction_trna_charged and ribosome_conc, and a drop in growth_rate, in a RelA-dependent manner (the spike collapses in a relA knockout under the same starvation timeline).
hypothesis.h0: ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, and growth_rate in the amino-acid-withdrawal timeline do not differ from the wildtype/basal reference beyond replicate noise (|welch_t|<2), i.e. no stringent response is triggered; equivalently, the relA knockout shows the same ppGpp fold-change as wildtype under starvation (no RelA-dependence).

In the relA knockout under the same starvation timeline, the ppGpp fold-change collapses to <1.5x basal (i.e. |welch_t|<2 vs wildtype/basal reference), demonstrating RelA-dependence.

rivals.claim: Growth arrest upon amino-acid withdrawal is driven primarily by direct metabolic/charging limitation (reduced translation elongation due to uncharged tRNA stalling ribosomes) rather than by the RelA/ppGpp regulatory stringent response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA gene_knockout background under the same starvation timeline, growth_rate still drops comparably to wildtype (no rescue), while ppgpp_conc shows no spike — indicating the growth defect is ppGpp-independent and purely due to charging/elongation limitation.

rivals.claim: The ribosome_conc decrease is a passive consequence of slower growth (dilution/synthesis balance) rather than an active ppGpp-mediated downregulation of rRNA/ribosome synthesis.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout control (reduced ribosome capacity) under basal (non-starved) conditions reproduces a similar growth_rate reduction without requiring any ppgpp_conc spike, showing ribosome depletion alone (independent of ppGpp signaling) can explain slowed growth.

auxiliary_assumptions: The steady-state charging module is active for this run, so ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc are valid readouts (not kinetic-only mode).
The amino_acid_shift timeline removes all 20 amino acids simultaneously (a full withdrawal) rather than a single amino acid, matching the 'suddenly runs out of amino acids' framing.
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation under isogenic conditions reflects genuine intrinsic noise, not a confound from deterministic solver artifacts.

The relA gene_knockout is assumed to disable ppGpp synthesis induction in the simulator without altering basal growth physiology substantially (a scope caveat: basal physiology of the knockout may be confounded, which the simulator cannot fully resolve).

This hypothesis concerns the core stringent-response mechanism in a single genetic background (wildtype vs relA KO vs rRNA-operon KO); it does NOT claim a genome-wide/population-level distributional result and so does not require a broad multi-gene screen — the prior objection about an annotation-blind gene panel applied to a different (now superseded) screening sub-claim, not to this three-arm mechanistic comparison.

Whether the simulator implements graded (dose-dependent) versus binary on/off fitness costs for individual biosynthetic-gene knockouts is an open implementation detail that this mechanistic hypothesis does NOT depend on: the relA and rrna-operon knockouts used here are tested only for their qualitative (present/absent) effect on ppgpp_conc and growth_rate, not for a graded dose-response, so this candidate is insensitive to r3.1's concern. Any graded-knockout dose-response question is left as a separate, future sub-hypothesis outside this scope.

objection_ledger.issue: The rrna_operon_knockout design row (operons_removed:3) appears in candidate_designs but is never connected to h1/h0, the falsifier, or either rival — it's an orphan perturbation. If it's meant to test a related claim about rRNA operon redundancy, that claim needs its own h1/falsifier; if not needed, it should be removed, since it currently just adds an unexplained auxiliary manipulation.

The decision rule combines a global BC threshold with a global FDR-significant-fraction threshold, but doesn't specify what happens if the two criteria disagree (e.g., BC>0.555 but <10% FDR-significant, or vice versa) in a way that would support H1 rather than requiring both to jointly reject H0 only. It's stated clearly enough for 'reject H1' (AND condition) but the symmetric 'support H1' criterion is left implicit in predicted_effect rather than formalized in decision_rule.

The auxiliary_assumptions and operational_defs now require an 'annotation-blind, every Nth locus tag' panel, but the actual candidate_designs target_genes list is still the identical 30 hand-picked, annotation-informed genes from the prior round. As submitted, the executable test does not implement the randomized-sampling control it claims distinguishes H1 from Rival B (panel-selection artifact), so the decisive test still can't exclude that rival.

Whether the simulator's per-gene knockout mechanism (e.g. for biosynthetic genes like trpA, hisG) actually produces graded/continuous fitness costs under the instrument's metabolic model, versus just hard on/off essentiality flags, is not verified; this bears on whether intermediate-band genes can even be observed.

rivals.claim: The growth slowdown and ribosome reduction are a generic nutrient-limitation/dilution effect independent of ppGpp signaling (e.g. passive substrate depletion slowing flux), not an active RelA-mediated stringent response.

rivals.claim: Ribosome concentration falls simply because rRNA/ribosomal protein synthesis is diluted by continued cell growth without new ribosome synthesis (passive dilution), not because of active stringent-response downregulation of ribosome synthesis.
rivals.distinguishing_result: ribosome_conc decline in wildtype tracks dry_mass/protein_mass growth dilution kinetics with similar magnitude even when ppGpp is clamped low (ppgpp_conc perturbation at basal level) under the same timeline, i.e. the ribosome drop persists without a ppGpp spike.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's amino_acid_shift timeline (media switch to minimal lacking amino acids) adequately models an abrupt amino-acid starvation event comparable to in vivo shift experiments.
Steady-state charging model is used (ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc channels are populated); if kinetic charging module is engaged, ribosomal-protein counts substitute for ribosome_conc.
RelA is the dominant ppGpp synthetase simulated for this starvation signal (SpoT's hydrolase/synthetase dual role is treated as background and not separately isolated here).
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation under isogenic conditions reflects genuine intrinsic noise, not a modeling artifact, for the purposes of Welch's t comparisons.
A single post-shift window (within generations 1-3) is sufficient to capture the acute stringent-response induction; slower adaptive remodeling beyond gen 3 is out of scope for this test.

select_score.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
select_score.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli cells trigger the stringent response: ppGpp rapidly accumulates (driven by RelA sensing uncharged tRNA), ribosome concentration/synthesis is cut, and growth rate drops sharply — a coordinated reallocation away from translation capacity rather than a passive starvation collapse.

rivals.claim: Growth arrest upon amino-acid withdrawal is a passive consequence of substrate limitation (reduced charged-tRNA pools stalling ribosomes mechanically) and does NOT require an active RelA/ppGpp regulatory signal — ribosome concentration and growth fall the same with or without RelA.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA gene_knockout under the same amino_acid_shift timeline, growth_rate and ribosome_conc decline by a similar magnitude as wildtype (Welch t vs wildtype/amino_acid_shift |t|<2), even though ppgpp_conc fails to rise.

rivals.claim: The dominant response is ribosome-capacity limited reallocation (rRNA operon output throttling) independent of ppGpp, i.e. ribosome synthesis capacity itself is the rate-limiting node, not the alarmone.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout run (reduced ribosome capacity at baseline, no amino acid shift) reproduces a comparable growth_rate drop and ribosome_conc decrease WITHOUT any ppGpp change, suggesting the ribosome-capacity channel alone (not ppGpp signaling) can explain the growth phenotype, decoupling the two mechanisms.

auxiliary_assumptions: The instrument's steady-state charging model computes fraction_trna_charged and ppgpp_conc consistently across the shift window even though these are nominally steady-state-fitted values; we treat the post-shift window mean as a valid proxy for the dynamic response.
The amino_acid_shift perturbation as specified (minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal) is interpretable by the simulator as a genuine withdrawal of all/most amino acids, not a single amino acid.

RelA knockout is assumed to be mechanistically simulated (ppGpp synthesis pathway present in model) — if not simulated, this falls back to an auxiliary scope caveat rather than refuting the biological claim.
Growth_rate and ribosome_conc are read at matched post-shift time windows across conditions so comparisons are not confounded by different sampling times.
Seeds (n=6) are treated as the sole source of replicate variance for the Welch t-test; no additional technical noise source is modeled.

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline-based amino_acid_shift (media switch from amino-acid-supplemented to minimal) is simulated as an acute total withdrawal event comparable to 'running out of amino acids suddenly'.
Post-shift window (last 20% of simulated timeline) is long enough to capture steady induction rather than transient noise.

fraction_trna_charged under steady-state charging mode (20 per-amino-acid values broadcast) is an adequate proxy for aggregate charging status; kinetic charging granularity is not required for this claim.
relA gene_knockout is assumed to abolish (not merely reduce) ppGpp synthesis in response to uncharged tRNA, consistent with known RelA mechanism, for use as the discriminating control.
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation under isogenic conditions is the appropriate noise model for Welch's t; no deterministic chaos vs noise distinction is attempted here.
ppgpp_conc clamp perturbation holds ppGpp at basal multiple throughout the shift, isolating its causal role on ribosome_conc independent of nutrient stress magnitude.

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli triggers the stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes sharply, ribosome concentration falls, and growth rate drops, with the magnitude of ppGpp induction scaling with the severity of charged-tRNA depletion.
hypothesis.h1: An abrupt amino-acid withdrawal (minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal) causes a rapid (within ~1 generation) rise in ppgpp_conc (>=3-fold over the pre-shift baseline), a concomitant fall in fraction_trna_charged, and a drop in ribosome_conc and growth_rate relative to a continuously-fed wildtype control.
hypothesis.h0: ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, and growth_rate in the amino-acid withdrawal timeline do not differ (Welch |t|<2) from the wildtype/basal reference across seeds; any apparent change is within replicate noise.

rivals.claim: The growth slowdown is driven by generic nutrient/energy limitation (carbon/ATP shortfall) rather than a specific ppGpp-mediated stringent response; ppGpp rise is incidental, not causal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA gene_knockout background (RelA is the primary ppGpp synthetase under amino acid starvation), ppgpp_conc fails to spike (stays within <2-fold of basal) under the same amino_acid_shift timeline, yet growth_rate still drops similarly — showing growth arrest is ppGpp-independent.

rivals.claim: Ribosome downregulation is passive dilution from reduced protein synthesis capacity (a consequence of slowed translation elongation), not an active ppGpp-driven transcriptional shutdown of rRNA/r-protein genes.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Clamping ppgpp_conc at basal (via the ppgpp_conc perturbation) during the same amino acid withdrawal still shows ribosome_conc held near pre-shift levels despite reduced charged-tRNA, demonstrating ribosome loss requires elevated ppGpp rather than being a passive consequence of starvation.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift timeline event ('minimal_plus_amino_acids' -> 'minimal') is interpreted by the simulator as an abrupt withdrawal of exogenous amino acids, not a gradual depletion.

steady-state charging model is used (default), so fraction_trna_charged reflects the broadcast 20-value per-amino-acid readout rather than kinetic per-species charging; this is sufficient to detect a bulk charging drop.
ribosome_conc channel is valid under steady-state charging (per channel notes) and is not required to use ribosomal-protein-count proxies since we are not invoking the kinetic module.

Seed-to-seed intrinsic noise is assumed small enough that 6 seeds give adequate power to detect a >=3-fold ppGpp change and >=50% growth_rate change (large effect sizes expected for the stringent response).

The relA knockout is assumed to abolish the dominant RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis pathway in this model (SpoT basal synthesis/hydrolysis still present but not starvation-inducible to the same degree).

rivals.claim: Growth slowdown is driven purely by passive metabolic/biosynthetic limitation (lack of amino acid substrate for translation) without a dedicated regulatory ppGpp surge — i.e., translation simply stalls mechanically, not via RelA signaling.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In a relA gene_knockout background subjected to the same aa_withdrawal timeline, growth_rate still drops sharply and ribosome_conc still falls, with NO corresponding ppgpp_conc rise (since RelA is absent) — if growth defect magnitude is similar to wildtype, this supports passive substrate limitation rather than active ppGpp-mediated regulation.

rivals.claim: The ribosome/growth response is mainly a consequence of general nutrient stress signaling (e.g., via ppGpp from SpoT alone or other global stress pathways) rather than acute aminoacyl-tRNA sensing by RelA specifically, so the response kinetics would be slow/graded rather than an acute spike.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If ppgpp_conc rises only gradually across generations 2-4 (not within generation 1) in wildtype, this is inconsistent with RelA's known acute ribosome-stalling sensing mechanism and instead suggests a slower SpoT-basal or general stress pathway.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's amino_acid_shift timeline produces a genuine step-change in extracellular amino acid availability that propagates to intracellular aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase kinetics within the modeled charging reactions.

RelA knockout in this model abolishes (or strongly attenuates) ppGpp synthesis in response to uncharged tRNA, consistent with known biology (RelA is the primary stringent-response synthetase triggered by ribosome-stalling).
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation in ppgpp_conc and growth_rate under matched conditions is small enough that a true >=2-fold ppGpp change is detectable with 6 seeds (not swamped by intrinsic noise).

The post-shift timepoint chosen (within generation 1, i.e., by ~60 min) is early enough to capture the acute ppGpp spike before potential homeostatic recovery, based on known E. coli stringent response timescales (minutes).

Division_rate is not expected to drop to zero (lethal) under aa_withdrawal within 3 generations — this is a growth slowdown/stress response, not a lethal perturbation; if division_rate collapses to 0, this would need separate handling as a viability failure rather than a graded response.

rivals.claim: Passive starvation decay: growth and ribosome decline are simply due to substrate exhaustion (no amino acids to build protein), independent of any regulatory ppGpp signaling spike.

rivals.claim: Ribosome-capacity-limited response: the growth shutdown is primarily driven by rRNA/ribosome operon capacity limits (a ribosome-autonomous program) rather than ppGpp signaling, so an rrna_operon_knockout (reduced ribosome capacity control) would show a similar shutdown trajectory regardless of ppGpp level.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout under basal (no aa withdrawal) alone reproduces a comparable growth_rate drop and ribosome_conc drop to the aa_withdrawal condition, this suggests ribosome capacity constraints, not ppGpp stringent signaling, are the dominant driver.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's RelA/SpoT ppGpp kinetic module is active for this run (steady-state or kinetic charging mode both record ppgpp_conc/rela_conc per the instrument note) so causal knockout comparisons are meaningful.
The amino-acid withdrawal timeline event (switching media from minimal_plus_amino_acids to minimal) is interpretable by the simulator as a genuine substrate removal, not merely a label change.

Ribosome_conc is read under steady-state charging; if the run uses kinetic charging, ribosomal-protein counts would need to substitute (not needed here since default steady-state charging is assumed).

Seed-to-seed stochastic variation in the isogenic population is small enough (CV comparable to baseline wildtype replicate spread) that a >=3-fold ppGpp shift is detectable as a significant Welch t beyond noise.

A single relA knockout approximates 'loss of stringent response' even though SpoT retains basal synthetic/hydrolase activity; this is treated as the best feasible interventional control within the envelope (a relA+spoT double knockout is not assumed available).

hypothesis.question: What does a cell do when it suddenly runs out of amino acids?
hypothesis.claim: When amino acids are suddenly removed from the medium, E. coli triggers the stringent response: RelA-driven ppGpp spikes sharply, which in turn triggers a drop in ribosome synthesis/active ribosome concentration and a collapse in growth rate, all contingent on uncharged tRNA accumulation.
hypothesis.h1: Removal of amino acids (minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal timeline shift) causes a rapid (within ~1 generation) rise in ppgpp_conc (>=3-fold over basal), a fall in ribosome_conc (>=25% reduction), and a fall in growth_rate (>=40% reduction), and this response is abolished (ppGpp rise <1.5-fold, growth drop <15%) when RelA is removed via gene_knockout of relA.
hypothesis.h0: Removing amino acids produces no significant change in ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, or growth_rate relative to the wildtype/basal reference beyond replicate noise (welch_t < 2), i.e. the cell's response is not mediated by a RelA-dependent stringent mechanism distinguishable from baseline fluctuation.

rivals.claim: The growth/ribosome collapse is driven primarily by generic metabolic/energetic stress (e.g. ATP or charged-tRNA depletion feeding directly into translation elongation slowdown) rather than an active RelA-mediated ppGpp regulatory program.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA knockout, growth_rate and ribosome_conc would STILL drop substantially (similar magnitude to wildtype) despite blunted ppGpp, because the passive mechanism does not require ppGpp signaling.

rivals.claim: The ribosome_conc decline is a passive consequence of dilution by growth-rate slowdown (less new ribosomal protein synthesis) rather than an active ppGpp-mediated transcriptional downregulation of rRNA/r-protein operons.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Ribosome_conc decline would track growth_rate decline proportionally across both WT and relA-KO (same ratio), rather than showing an amplified/disproportionate ribosome-specific drop that depends on ppGpp level.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift perturbation in the instrument faithfully represents sudden complete amino-acid withdrawal (minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal) without confounding carbon-source changes.

fraction_trna_charged aggregated over 20 amino acids under steady-state charging is a sufficient proxy for 'uncharged tRNA accumulation' even though per-species kinetic resolution is unavailable in steady-state mode.

relA gene_knockout is mechanistically simulated as abolishing RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis (the (p)ppGpp synthetase I activity) in this model; SpoT basal synthesis/hydrolysis still operates as background.

Generation-level granularity (2-3 generations) is sufficient temporal resolution to capture the onset dynamics of the stringent response; faster sub-generation kinetics are not resolved at steady_state elongation.
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation under isogenic conditions represents genuine biological replicate noise, not a numerical artifact.

hypothesis.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
hypothesis.claim: Among a broad panel of genes classically annotated non-essential in E. coli, the majority (>60%) can be individually knocked out in minimal (basal) medium without abolishing growth or division, but an identifiable minority (~10-20%) of these "non-essential" genes nonetheless shows a substantial fitness cost (growth_rate reduced by >=20% and/or division_rate <1), revealing a graded rather than purely binary essentiality landscape.
hypothesis.h1: Across a panel of single-gene knockouts drawn from genes classically annotated non-essential, the distribution of growth_rate/division_rate outcomes on basal medium is heterogeneous/bimodal: most KOs cluster near wildtype, but a distinguishable subset (~10-20%) shows a large growth defect (>=20% growth_rate reduction) or incomplete division (division_rate < 1) -- i.e. "can live without" is graded, not all-or-none.
hypothesis.h0: All individually tested non-essential-gene knockouts are statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal on both growth_rate and division_rate (|welch_t| < 2 for every KO vs wildtype, and no KO's division_rate falls below 1 beyond replicate noise) -- i.e. essentiality in this panel is uniformly absent/binary rather than graded.

operational_defs.measure: mean instantaneous specific growth rate (1/h) per KO across seeds vs wildtype/basal, expressed as percent reduction

operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed growth_rate effect values; BC>0.555 indicates a bimodal (graded, two-population) structure rather than a single unimodal cluster

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Across a panel of 20 genes (single knockouts, basal medium): (1) pooled growth_rate effect-size distribution is bimodal, BC>0.555; (2) ~60-80% of KOs fall within +/-10% of wildtype growth_rate with division_rate=1; (3) ~10-20% (roughly 2-4 of 20) show >=20% growth_rate reduction and/or division_rate<1, forming a distinguishable low-fitness cluster rather than isolated outliers in an otherwise flat/unimodal scatter.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled per-seed growth_rate percent-effect values from the full 20-gene KO panel; reject H1's graded/bimodal claim if BC<=0.555 (unimodal). Secondary per-gene check: Welch t of growth_rate, each KO vs wildtype/basal across seeds; a KO counts as a member of the low-fitness minority only if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct<=-20%, or division_rate<1 beyond seed spread. Rival B check: if BC<=0.555, additionally inspect the ranked per-gene effect-size sequence (from per-seed spread output); a smooth ramp (no adjacent-rank gap >1.5x median gap) confirms Rival B (continuum) rather than Rival A (pure noise/no effect at all). Discriminating control: repeat the same 20-gene KO panel in the relA/spoT double-knockout (stringent-response-incapable) background; if the low-fitness cluster's defects are abolished there (effect sizes shift toward 0, division_rate restored to 1), the apparent gene-specific graded essentiality is instead a shared stringent-response artifact (Rival C).
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555 (unimodal) and/or fewer than ~2 of 20 KOs (<10%) reach |welch_t|>=2 with >=20% growth reduction or division_rate<1 in the gene_knockout/basal panel -- indicating essentiality in this panel is effectively uniform/binary or an unstructured continuum, not a graded two-population structure.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate effect-size values across the KO panel
test.threshold: BC>0.555 required to support bimodal/graded H1; BC<=0.555 refutes it (and triggers the Rival B ranked-gap descriptive check using per-seed spread output to distinguish continuum-noise from no-effect)

rivals.claim: Rival A (uniform tolerance / pure noise): all tested non-essential genes are truly redundant/dispensable with no meaningful fitness cost -- any observed variation is replicate noise, not a real low-fitness subpopulation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: BC<=0.555 (unimodal) and no KO reaches |welch_t|>=2 with >=20% growth reduction; all per-gene effect sizes fall within the wildtype/basal seed-noise band.

rivals.claim: Rival B (continuous/linear cost, not two clusters): fitness costs of non-essential KOs form a smooth continuous gradient rather than two discrete populations -- essentiality is a continuum, not graded-into-two-groups. Operationally: when per-gene mean growth_rate effect sizes are ranked, the increments between adjacent ranks are approximately uniform (no step), and BC computed on the pooled distribution stays <=0.555 despite nonzero spread -- i.e. variance without structure.
rivals.distinguishing_result: BC<=0.555 AND the ranked effect-size plot shows no gap exceeding 1.5x the median adjacent-rank increment between any consecutive genes (checked descriptively from per-seed spread output) -- a smooth ramp, not a step, confirming a continuum rather than two discrete clusters.

rivals.claim: Rival C (stringent-response masking): any apparent low-fitness KOs are not failing because of their own gene's direct function, but because KO-induced starvation triggers ppGpp-mediated growth arrest common to many unrelated gene losses -- i.e. the low-fitness cluster is a single shared stringent-response phenotype, not evidence of graded, gene-specific essentiality.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA/spoT (stringent-response-incapable) background, the same KO panel shows the low-fitness cluster members LOSE their growth defect (effect sizes shift toward wildtype, division_rate restored to 1) -- i.e. the defect was ppGpp-dependent/stringent-response-driven, not specific to each knocked-out gene's direct metabolic role.

auxiliary_assumptions: The 20-gene panel, chosen from classically non-essential/dispensable-annotated loci, is representative enough of the broader non-essential gene set that its effect-size distribution generalizes qualitatively (shape, not exact fraction) to the full genome.
division_rate and growth_rate as simulated reflect the same construct of 'viability' the question intends (no confounds from solver/integration artifacts at 3 generations).

Seed-to-seed stochastic variation (intrinsic noise) is small enough relative to true KO effect sizes that |welch_t|>=2 with 6 seeds has adequate power to detect a true 20% growth defect; underpowering at n=6 seeds is accepted as a scope limitation of this screen, not grounds to abandon the test.

The relA/spoT double knockout is an adequate (if imperfect) way to silence the stringent response as a confound; any residual ppGpp-independent effects of this background are treated as a scope caveat, not pursued further here.
KO strains that fail to complete generation 1 are scored as division_rate=0/severe growth defect rather than treated as missing data.

The ranked adjacent-gap heuristic used to distinguish Rival B (continuum) from a true two-cluster structure is a descriptive, not inferential, check -- it supplements but does not replace the primary BC threshold decision.

objection_ledger.issue: The mechanism named in the claim (CRP-cAMP-mediated transcriptional repression of the alternative-sugar operon) is never operationalized: no channel measures operon/promoter activity, uptake flux allocation, or pathway-specific gene expression. growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are generic bulk physiology consistent with many non-regulatory explanations (e.g. simple carbon-source quality differences), so confirming the falsifier cannot actually support the CCR-specific mechanistic claim as worded.

The user's question is about choice between two sugars present simultaneously in the same flask (active catabolite repression/diauxie). The design still only compares two separate single-carbon runs (acetate-only vs basal/glucose-only) plus a succinate-only arm. This answers 'which single carbon source yields faster growth/less stringency' but never presents both sugars together, so it cannot distinguish genuine repression/choice behavior from simply 'acetate supports slower growth than glucose on its own' -- a mixed-substrate co-utilization rival is still never excluded because no condition in candidate_designs has both substrates present.

The clamp multiplier '2x basal' is explicitly flagged by the author as potentially needing recalibration to match true acetate-level ppGpp, and no actual acetate ppgpp_conc value is reported/compared against the clamp target before running the causal test. Without first confirming (from the wildtype/acetate run) what the actual acetate/basal ppGpp ratio is, the clamp may not target the right operating point, making the causal test under- or over-powered.

The second rival (media-fitting artifact vs genuine hierarchy signal) is described only narratively ('if differences are highly variable/inconsistent that would suggest noise') with no concrete statistic or threshold tied to it in the decision_rule or falsifier block, unlike the first rival which has the relA KO test wired into the design. As stated, no specific test result would count as confirming or refuting this rival.

The rrna_operon_knockout rival-test is reasonable in isolation, but neither rival design actually touches the central scope question (choice between two co-present sugars). Both rivals (generic nutrient stress vs ribosome-limitation) are about explaining the single-substrate acetate-vs-basal gap, which is a secondary question once the main hypothesis about dual-sugar choice is admitted to be untestable by this instrument. The rivals do not compete to explain any dual-substrate selection signature because none exists in the design.

hypothesis.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
hypothesis.claim: Among a broad panel of non-essential-looking E. coli genes (transporters, paralogs, stress-response regulators not required for core biosynthesis), the majority can be individually deleted without abolishing growth, but a substantial minority (~15-25%) of single-gene knockouts in this panel cause a severe growth/division defect (>50% drop in growth_rate or division_rate <0.8) under basal minimal media, consistent with the known genome-wide distribution of essential vs non-essential genes in E. coli (~90% dispensable singly, ~10% essential/severely detrimental in rich media; we predict a somewhat higher detrimental fraction ~15-25% under minimal basal media where auxiliary pathways become load-bearing).
hypothesis.h1: Across a panel of >=15 individually knocked-out genes, the fraction of knockouts showing a severe growth/division defect (growth_rate drop >50% vs wildtype OR division_rate <0.8) under basal minimal media is between 0.15 and 0.25, i.e. most genes are individually dispensable but a non-trivial minority are not.
hypothesis.h0: The knockout panel shows either (a) uniformly mild effects (severe-defect fraction <0.05, i.e. nearly all genes are freely dispensable) or (b) uniformly severe effects (severe-defect fraction >0.5, i.e. the panel was not actually enriched for non-essential-looking genes) -- in either case the data would not support a 15-25% severe-defect fraction.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate channels over the simulated generations
operational_defs.measure: per-seed mean growth_rate (1/h) and division_rate (frac) in knockout vs wildtype/basal reference; a gene is classified 'severe-defect' if mean growth_rate drop >50% vs wildtype OR division_rate <0.8

operational_defs.observable: proportion of genes in the panel classified severe-defect out of total panel size
operational_defs.measure: count(severe-defect genes)/count(panel genes), with 95% CI via binomial proportion across the panel

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate of the same panel under an amino-acid-supplemented timeline vs basal
operational_defs.measure: severe-defect fraction recomputed under the supplemented timeline; a large drop (toward <0.05) vs basal (~0.20) indicates media-dependent rather than intrinsic essentiality

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc under rrna_operon_knockout alone vs the gene-specific knockout panel
operational_defs.measure: compare the magnitude/pattern of growth_rate drop and ppgpp_conc elevation in the ribosome-capacity-limited background to the panel's severe-defect cases; convergence onto the same signature favors the rival, a distinct smaller phenotype disfavors it

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Distribution-level claim: panel severe-defect fraction f ~ 0.15-0.25 (point estimate ~0.20), i.e. roughly 1 in 5 genes in this non-essential-looking panel shows growth_rate reduction >50% or division_rate <0.8, while ~75-85% of genes show growth_rate within 20% of wildtype and division_rate >=0.8. This is a claim about growth/division-defect severity and its genome-wide distribution; it does not assert or require any pathway-specific transcriptional/regulatory mechanism for why a given gene is essential.

falsifier.decision_rule: For each of the >=15 panel genes, run welch_disconfirm (gene_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal) on growth_rate across seeds; classify severe-defect if welch_t>=2 AND effect_pct indicates >50% drop, OR division_rate<0.8. Compute panel fraction severe-defect with binomial 95% CI. Reject H1 if the CI excludes the [0.15,0.25] band (i.e. CI entirely below 0.05 or entirely above 0.5).
falsifier.refuting_result: Binomial 95% CI on severe-defect fraction falls entirely outside [0.15,0.25] (e.g. 0/15 genes severe, CI upper bound <0.05; or >10/15 genes severe, CI lower bound >0.5)

test.statistic: welch_t per gene on growth_rate, then panel-level binomial proportion with CI
test.threshold: per-gene |welch_t|>=2 for classification; panel fraction 95% CI must overlap [0.15,0.25] to support H1

rivals.claim: Essentiality is highly media-dependent rather than reflecting an intrinsic ~20% hard-core minority: on amino-acid-supplemented media nearly ALL of these genes become dispensable (severe-defect fraction collapses toward 0), so the 'minority is essential' pattern is an artifact of minimal basal media stress rather than a general genome property.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Running the identical panel under a timeline with amino-acid supplementation shows severe-defect fraction drops to <0.05 while basal stays at ~0.20, confirming media-dependence rather than a stable intrinsic essentiality fraction; if the supplemented-media fraction remains near 0.15-0.25 (statistically indistinguishable from basal), this rival is disfavored and the ~20% figure is supported as a more general property.

rivals.claim: Severe growth defects in the panel are driven predominantly by a shared ribosome/translation-capacity bottleneck (convergent stringent-response stress) rather than by diverse gene-specific loss-of-function mechanisms, so the panel's apparent 20% 'essential minority' is really just genes that happen to tip the same shared capacity limit.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout background run shows growth_rate drop and ppgpp_conc elevation of similar magnitude/pattern to the severe-defect genes in the panel, indicating convergence on one shared bottleneck rather than gene-specific essentiality; if instead rrna_operon_knockout produces a distinct, smaller, or differently-shaped phenotype (e.g. different ppgpp_conc/growth_rate ratio) than the panel's severe-defect cases, this rival is disfavored and gene-specific mechanisms are supported.

auxiliary_assumptions: The panel of 15 genes is a representative sample of 'non-essential-looking' genes (transporters, paralog-redundant metabolic enzymes, stress regulators), not cherry-picked known-essential genes, so the predicted fraction generalizes to the broader non-core-biosynthesis gene set.

The simulator mechanistically implements each knocked-out gene's reaction/regulatory role; genes whose KO has no coded mechanistic consequence will trivially show no defect, which is a simulator-coverage limitation noted here rather than chased further.
Per-seed stochastic noise in growth_rate across 6 seeds is small enough that a true >50% mean effect is detectable by Welch's t at this replicate count (checked post hoc via power_mde if needed).
division_rate <0.8 threshold is treated as capturing lethality/division-defect phenotypes that growth_rate alone might average over or mask.

Basal minimal media is the appropriate default condition for testing 'can live without' in the classical sense (cf. Keio collection scored on rich LB); results may not generalize to all media without the discriminating timeline control.

This hypothesis is scoped strictly to growth-rate/division-rate severity and its distribution across genes; it makes no claim about any pathway-specific transcriptional or regulatory mechanism (e.g. CRP-cAMP catabolite repression), since no channel here measures operon/promoter state or substrate-uptake allocation -- any such mechanistic question is explicitly out of scope for this instrument and this hypothesis.

objection_ledger.issue: The claim's mechanism is explicitly CRP-cAMP-mediated operon repression of the alternative pathway, but no channel here measures operon/promoter state, uptake flux allocation, or pathway-specific gene expression; growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are generic physiology, consistent with many mechanisms besides selective transcriptional repression of the acetate pathway. The candidate should either rename the hypothesis to 'single-substrate acetate produces lower growth/higher ppGpp than glucose' (a claim the design actually tests) or add an observable tied to pathway-specific regulation (e.g., fba_objective flux allocation across competing uptake routes) to speak to the CCR mechanism itself.

The rrna_operon_knockout rival-test is reasonable in isolation, but neither rival design actually touches the central scope question (choice between two co-present sugars). Both rivals (generic nutrient stress vs ribosome-limitation) are about explaining the single-substrate acetate-vs-basal gap, which is a secondary question once the main hypothesis about dual-sugar choice is admitted to be untestable by this instrument. The rivals do not compete to explain any dual-substrate selection signature because none exists in the design.

The clamp multiplier '2x basal' is explicitly flagged by the author as potentially needing recalibration to match true acetate-level ppGpp, and no actual acetate ppgpp_conc value is reported/compared against the clamp target before running the causal test. Without first confirming (from the wildtype/acetate run) what the actual acetate/basal ppGpp ratio is, the clamp may not target the right operating point, making the causal test under- or over-powered.

drafts.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
drafts.claim: Among a broad panel of individually non-essential genes (as annotated in the Keio-type dispensability sense), the large majority (~70-80%) can be deleted singly without abolishing growth or division in this simulator, but a reproducible minority (~15-25%) show a severe, detectable fitness defect (division_rate drop or growth_rate collapse) even though they are not formally 'essential' in rich media — i.e. single-gene dispensability is itself a graded distribution rather than a strict binary, and the fraction of genes whose KO is tolerated depends on which cellular process they serve (metabolic vs ribosomal/translation-machinery genes being more fragile in this model).
drafts.h1: Across a panel of >=15 single-gene knockouts spanning multiple functional categories (central metabolism, amino-acid biosynthesis, ribosomal/translation accessory, regulatory), the distribution of division_rate outcomes across genes is bimodal: most genes (~70-80%) cluster near wildtype division_rate (no significant defect) while a minority (~15-25%) cluster at low/zero division_rate, and this low-division cluster is enriched for translation-machinery genes relative to metabolic genes.
drafts.h0: Single-gene KO effects on division_rate are NOT bimodal across the panel (Sarle's BC <= 0.555, i.e. a unimodal/continuous distribution of fitness effects), and/or there is no enrichment difference between translation-machinery and metabolic gene categories (the two category subsets do not differ by Welch's t on division_rate at |t|>=2).

operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: fraction of simulated generations that complete division, per seed, averaged across seeds, for each single-gene knockout design

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: instantaneous specific growth rate (1/h) per seed, compared to wildtype/basal reference

operational_defs.measure: a priori categorical label attached to each knockout design based on annotated gene function (metabolic enzyme vs ribosomal protein/translation factor)

drafts.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of division_rate across the ~15-20 gene panel with Sarle's BC > 0.555; low-fitness cluster centered near division_rate ~0.0-0.3 comprising ~15-25% of genes, high-fitness cluster centered near division_rate ~0.9-1.0 (wildtype-like) comprising ~70-80%; translation-machinery KOs show mean division_rate at least 2-fold lower than metabolic KOs (Welch |t|>=2).

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (shape): compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient over the pooled per-seed division_rate values across all panel KO designs; reject unimodal H0 if BC>0.555. Step 2 (category difference): Welch's t of division_rate, translation-machinery-gene-KO designs vs metabolic-gene-KO designs, across seeds; reject H0 of no category difference if |t|>=2 (two-sided p<0.05 at Welch df). Both must pass for H1 to survive.
