test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed division_rate across all panel KOs; secondary Welch's t between category subsets

rivals.claim: Dispensability is essentially binary and determined almost entirely by whether the gene is in central dogma/translation machinery at all -- i.e. nearly ALL translation-machinery gene KOs are lethal (division_rate~0) and nearly ALL metabolic gene KOs (outside core biosynthesis) are fully tolerated, so the distribution is bimodal but with near-100%/0% purity per category rather than a 70-80/15-25 split.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the translation-machinery subset would show division_rate collapsing to near 0 for essentially every gene (very low within-category variance) and the metabolic subset would show division_rate near wildtype for essentially every gene, i.e. the category boundary alone fully predicts the cluster membership with near-zero misclassification, rather than genes within each category spreading across both clusters.

rivals.claim: There is no reproducible bimodal structure at all -- single-gene KO fitness effects form a continuous gradient (many genes with partial, graded defects) that depends more on media condition (basal vs acetate) than on the metabolic/translation category label; the apparent minority of severe KOs is better explained by stochastic/seed noise than a real functional category effect.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, BC would fall at or below 0.555 (no genuine two-cluster separation), per-seed spread within a single gene KO would be comparable to the between-gene spread, and re-running under acetate condition would reshuffle which genes fall in the low-fitness cluster rather than preserving the translation-vs-metabolic grouping.

auxiliary_assumptions: Whether each named gene's KO is mechanistically represented in the simulator's metabolic/expression network is not knowable in advance; genes with no simulated phenotype will register as division_rate=wildtype by default, which is treated as a 'tolerated' outcome for this test (a scope caveat, not grounds to exclude them).
Functional category assignment (translation-machinery vs metabolic) is an a priori annotation applied before seeing results, not refit post hoc.
Division_rate averaged over 3 generations and 6 seeds is assumed sufficient to distinguish a lethal/near-lethal KO from a mild one; slower-developing defects beyond generation 3 are out of scope.
The basal condition panel is the primary test; the acetate sub-panel (4 genes) is a robustness/rival-discriminating check, not the main statistical test.
Stochastic seed-to-seed variance within one gene KO is assumed small relative to between-gene variance under H1; this is itself checked by the bimodality test design.

drafts.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
drafts.claim: A substantial minority of non-essential E. coli genes are individually dispensable: across a broad screen of single-gene knockouts drawn from known-nonessential/auxiliary metabolic and regulatory loci, most (~70-80%) will show division_rate and growth_rate statistically indistinguishable from wildtype, while a smaller fraction (~20-30%) will show a significant growth/division defect (partial dispensability) even though none are fully lethal in this gene set.
drafts.h1: Across a panel of single-gene knockouts in genes annotated as non-essential, the majority (>=70%) are viable with division_rate >= 0.9x wildtype and growth_rate within ~10% of wildtype/basal, while a minority (<=30%) show a detectable but non-lethal fitness cost (growth_rate or division_rate reduced by >=15%, Welch |t|>=2 vs wildtype).
drafts.h0: All screened gene knockouts are indistinguishable from wildtype/basal on growth_rate and division_rate (no fraction shows a significant defect), i.e. the gene panel behaves as uniformly neutral with no detectable fitness-cost subpopulation.

operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: fraction of generations that divide, per-seed, per-KO, compared to wildtype/basal

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: instantaneous specific growth rate (1/h), mean across seeds, %-difference from wildtype/basal

operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: division_rate < 0.5x wildtype flags a lethal/near-lethal KO; 0.5-0.85x flags partial defect; >=0.85x flags neutral

drafts.predicted_effect: Distribution-shaped prediction: across ~12-16 screened non-essential-gene knockouts, ~70-80% (8-13 genes) show growth_rate and division_rate within 10% of wildtype (effectively neutral), while ~20-30% (3-5 genes) show a significant partial defect (growth_rate or division_rate reduced 15-50%, Welch |t|>=2), and 0% show full lethality (division_rate<0.1).

falsifier.decision_rule: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction over per-gene Welch t-test log2FC (division_rate and growth_rate) of each KO vs wildtype across seeds; a gene is classified as a 'mover' (significant fitness cost) if it passes FDR<0.10. Reject H1's predicted shape if the fraction of FDR-significant movers across the panel is <10% (panel is uniformly neutral, supporting H0) or is >50% (panel is mostly costly, contradicting the 70-80% neutral prediction).
falsifier.refuting_result: Fewer than 10% of screened KOs show FDR-significant growth/division defects (uniform neutrality, H0 holds) OR more than 50% show significant defects (contradicting the predicted 70-80% neutral majority).

test.statistic: per-gene log2FC of division_rate and growth_rate vs wildtype, BH-FDR corrected across the gene panel
test.threshold: n_significant_fdr10 / n_genes_screened: refute if <0.10 or >0.50

rivals.claim: Dispensability is bimodal (essential-or-neutral), not a continuum with a distinct partial-defect minority: most non-essential KOs are either fully neutral or fully lethal, with few intermediate-cost genes.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on the pooled per-KO growth_rate effect sizes would show BC>0.555 with two tight clusters near 0% and near -100% effect, and very few genes landing in the 15-50% partial-defect band predicted by H1.

rivals.claim: Apparent 'partial defects' are actually ribosome-allocation/stringent-response artifacts (ppGpp-mediated growth slowdown common to many KOs via a shared stress pathway), not gene-specific dispensability costs.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a relA knockout (background control, abolishing ppGpp induction) is crossed with the same gene panel and the partial-defect fraction collapses toward 0% (defects disappear), this shows the 'cost' was a generic stringent-response artifact rather than true gene-specific dispensability.

auxiliary_assumptions: The 14-gene panel is a representative sample of the broader non-essential genome (drawn from annotated auxiliary metabolic/transport/regulatory loci with no known severe phenotype), so the observed neutral/partial-defect fractions generalize to the population-level claim.

division_rate and growth_rate are the simulator's best proxies for in vivo viability/fitness; genes whose essentiality depends on pathways not mechanistically modeled (e.g. missing regulatory feedback) cannot be distinguished here and are a scope caveat, not grounds to keep revising the test.

6 seeds per knockout gives adequate replicate power to detect a 15% growth_rate effect via Welch t; if power is insufficient this will be flagged via the FDR correction rather than overfitting seed count post hoc.
Knockouts are evaluated independently (no epistasis/combinatorial effects considered) â€” consistent with the single-gene-deletion scope of 'which genes can E. coli live without'.

drafts.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
drafts.claim: A substantial minority (roughly 20-35%) of a broad panel of individually tested non-essential-looking E. coli genes can be deleted singly without abolishing growth or division, while the rest cause severe growth/division defects, producing a bimodal distribution of knockout fitness (near-wildtype vs near-lethal) rather than a smooth unimodal spread of mild effects.
drafts.h1: Across a screen of single-gene knockouts, the distribution of normalized growth_rate (and division_rate) effect sizes relative to wildtype is bimodal, with one cluster near 0% effect (viable-without) and a second cluster near -70% to -100% effect (essential), and the viable-without cluster comprises roughly 20-35% of the tested genes.
drafts.h0: Knockout fitness effects across the gene panel are unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555) and/or the viable-without fraction is not distinguishable from a uniform/continuous spread of mild-to-severe effects; i.e., there is no distinct dispensable-gene cluster.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate channels of a single gene_knockout design vs wildtype/basal over several generations
operational_defs.measure: per-seed % change in mean growth_rate relative to wildtype/basal, plus division_rate (fraction of generations that divide); a gene is classified 'viable-without' if |% growth_rate change| < 20% AND division_rate ~1, 'essential' if growth_rate drop > 70% or division_rate collapses toward 0

operational_defs.construct: distribution shape of dispensability across the genome
operational_defs.observable: pooled per-gene effect-size values (% growth_rate change vs wildtype) across the knockout panel
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over the pooled distribution of per-gene mean effect sizes

drafts.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution with BC > 0.555; viable-without cluster centered near 0% to -15% growth_rate change (division_rate ~1) comprising ~20-35% of the ~20-gene screened panel; essential cluster centered near -70% to -100% growth_rate change (division_rate -> 0) comprising the remainder.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (bimodality_bc) over the pooled per-gene mean %-growth_rate-change values from the 20-gene knockout screen (each gene's effect size itself derived from welch_disconfirm vs wildtype/basal across seeds); reject H1 (bimodal, dispensable-gene cluster) if BC <= 0.555, OR if the fraction of genes classified 'viable-without' (|growth_rate change|<20% and division_rate~1, by welch_t<2 vs wildtype) falls outside 10-45% (too far from predicted 20-35%).
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled effect-size distribution is unimodal (BC <= 0.555) with a continuous smear of partial growth defects, or the viable-without fraction is <10% (almost all genes essential) or >45% (almost all genes dispensable) -- either outcome means there is no distinct 'can-live-without' cluster as claimed.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-gene effect sizes, cross-checked with per-gene welch_disconfirm classification
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for bimodal claim; viable-without fraction in [10%,45%] consistent with predicted 20-35%

rivals.claim: Essentiality is graded/continuous (a dosage-sensitivity spectrum), not bimodal -- most genes cause small-to-moderate fitness costs rather than splitting into 'fine' vs 'dead' categories.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled per-gene effect-size distribution shows BC <= 0.555 (unimodal or uniform spread) with many genes at intermediate (-20% to -60%) growth_rate changes rather than clustering near 0% or near -80%.

rivals.claim: Apparent dispensability is condition-dependent rather than a fixed genomic property -- genes scored 'viable-without' on basal media would show division_rate collapse or severe growth defects under a more demanding condition (e.g. acetate), so the bimodal split reflects media choice, not an intrinsic dispensable-gene class.
rivals.distinguishing_result: The same gene_knockout panel run on condition=acetate (slow-growth, less buffered) shifts a substantial fraction of previously 'viable-without' genes into the 'essential' cluster, changing the viable-without fraction and/or collapsing the bimodal split (BC drops toward <=0.555) relative to basal.

auxiliary_assumptions: The 20-gene panel is treated as a representative sample spanning known-essential (e.g. ftsZ, dnaA, murA, lpxC) and known-nonessential/accessory (e.g. acrB, ybeD, dcuC) loci from prior E. coli knowledge, approximating genome-wide heterogeneity; it is not a full genomic screen but a modest proxy given the 4-8 seed / 1-4 generation compute budget.

Whether each gene's knockout is mechanistically represented in the whole-cell model (i.e., whether the model encodes the relevant pathway) is not knowable in advance; genes with no modeled phenotype will trivially show ~0% effect and must be interpreted with this caveat rather than as true biological dispensability.

Division_rate and growth_rate are assumed to jointly capture viability; a gene whose loss causes a slow-accumulating defect beyond generation 3-4 could be misclassified as viable-without within this short timeline.
Seed-to-seed stochastic noise under isogenic conditions is assumed small enough that a true essential/dispensable split is distinguishable from intrinsic noise at n=6 seeds.

drafts.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
drafts.claim: Among a broad panel of non-essential-looking E. coli genes (transporters, paralogous enzymes, stress-response regulators), a substantial minority (~20-30%) can be individually deleted with division_rate remaining ≥0.8 of wildtype and growth_rate within 10% of wildtype under basal minimal media — i.e. most genes in such a panel are dispensable for viability in this single condition, but a sizeable fraction (~70-80%) still are not, showing reduced division_rate or growth_rate.
drafts.h1: In a panel of candidate non-essential genes, the fraction of single-gene knockouts that are viable (division_rate >= 0.8x wildtype AND growth_rate within 10% of wildtype) under basal condition is high (>=60%) but not universal, reflecting a mixed distribution of dispensability rather than near-uniform essentiality or near-uniform dispensability.
drafts.h0: All (or nearly all, >=90%) genes in the panel are either essential (division_rate drops sharply, e.g. <0.5x wildtype, or growth_rate drops >30%) or dispensable (division_rate >=0.8x, growth_rate within 10%) with no meaningful intermediate class — i.e., knockout fitness effects in this panel do not differ systematically from the reference distribution, OR fewer than 60% survive to the viability threshold (panel is mostly essential).

operational_defs.observable: division_rate and growth_rate channels for a gene_knockout design vs wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: division_rate ratio (KO/WT) and growth_rate percent difference (KO/WT), classified viable if division_rate_ratio>=0.8 and |growth_rate %diff|<=10%

operational_defs.observable: per-gene classification (viable vs non-viable) aggregated over a multi-gene screen of single knockouts
operational_defs.measure: fraction of genes classified viable out of total panel, with BH-FDR correction applied to the per-gene growth_rate effect sizes before classification

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate magnitude relative to wildtype/basal
operational_defs.measure: percent change (effect_pct) and Welch t-statistic from disconfirm(target, reference, channel)

drafts.predicted_effect: Across a panel of ~20 candidate genes (transporters, paralogous biosynthetic enzymes, regulatory/stress genes, chosen to span expected essential/non-essential annotations), predict a bimodal-ish split: ~60-75% classified viable (division_rate ratio >=0.8, growth_rate within 10%), ~25-40% classified non-viable (division_rate ratio <0.5 or growth_rate drop >30%), with few genes in an ambiguous middle band. Effect size for non-viable genes: growth_rate drop of 30-90%, division_rate drop to 0-0.5x WT.

falsifier.decision_rule: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (q<0.10) applied to per-gene Welch t-tests of growth_rate (and division_rate) KO-vs-WT across seeds for each of the ~20 panel genes; classify each gene viable/non-viable by the stated thresholds; compute fraction viable (n_significant_fdr10 defines non-viable count). Refute H1 if fraction viable < 0.60 (panel mostly essential) or if fraction viable > 0.95 with no genes showing growth_rate drop >30% (panel essentially all dispensable, no meaningful essential subset) based on n_significant_fdr10.
falsifier.refuting_result: Fraction of panel genes classified viable falls outside [0.60, 0.95], e.g. only 3/20 (15%) survive the viability threshold (mostly essential genome segment) or 19/20 (95%) survive with none showing a significant growth_rate/division_rate hit (no essential genes recovered, panel miscalibrated or model insensitive to KO).

test.statistic: per-gene Welch t-test on growth_rate (and division_rate) KO vs WT across seeds, BH-FDR corrected across the ~20-gene panel
test.threshold: q<0.10 for significance; fraction_viable in [0.60,0.95] required to not refute H1

rivals.claim: Essentiality is not graded but strictly binary and dominated by a small set of core pathways (ribosome biogenesis, cell wall synthesis, DNA replication) — most genes outside these pathways show NO detectable growth defect at all (near 0% effect), so the panel would show a sharp bimodal split with near-100% of genes in a tight 'no effect' cluster rather than a smooth 60-95% viable range.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc test on pooled per-gene growth_rate effect_pct shows BC>0.555 with one cluster centered near 0% effect containing >90% of genes and a small, highly separated cluster near -80-100% effect, rather than a continuous/moderate spread.

rivals.claim: Single-gene knockout effects are condition-dependent and basal minimal media masks most dispensability differences (i.e., genes appear falsely essential or falsely dispensable only because basal media doesn't stress the relevant pathway) — a ppGpp-mediated stringent response confound could make many genes look non-viable via growth arrest rather than true genetic essentiality.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout control background (abolishing ppGpp stringent response induction) applied to the same panel would rescue growth_rate/division_rate for genes whose defect is stringent-response-mediated growth arrest, shifting them from non-viable to viable classification; if the viable fraction in the relA-null background panel differs by >15 percentage points from the wildtype-background panel, the apparent essentiality was confounded by stringent response rather than reflecting true gene dispensability.

select_score.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
select_score.claim: Among a broad panel of individually non-essential genes (as annotated in the Keio-type dispensability sense), the large majority (~70-80%) can be deleted singly without abolishing growth or division in this simulator, but a reproducible minority (~15-25%) show a severe, detectable fitness defect (division_rate drop or growth_rate collapse) even though they are not formally 'essential' in rich media — i.e. single-gene dispensability is itself a graded distribution rather than a strict binary, and the fraction of genes whose KO is tolerated depends on which cellular process they serve (metabolic vs ribosomal/translation-machinery genes being more fragile in this model).
select_score.h1: Across a panel of >=15 single-gene knockouts spanning multiple functional categories (central metabolism, amino-acid biosynthesis, ribosomal/translation accessory, regulatory), the distribution of division_rate outcomes across genes is bimodal: most genes (~70-80%) cluster near wildtype division_rate (no significant defect) while a minority (~15-25%) cluster at low/zero division_rate, and this low-division cluster is enriched for translation-machinery genes relative to metabolic genes.
select_score.h0: Single-gene KO effects on division_rate are NOT bimodal across the panel (Sarle's BC <= 0.555, i.e. a unimodal/continuous distribution of fitness effects), and/or there is no enrichment difference between translation-machinery and metabolic gene categories (the two category subsets do not differ by Welch's t on division_rate at |t|>=2).

operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: fraction of simulated generations that complete division, per seed, averaged across seeds, for each single-gene knockout design

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: instantaneous specific growth rate (1/h) per seed, compared to wildtype/basal reference

operational_defs.observable: gene identity assigned to params.target_genes
operational_defs.measure: a priori categorical label attached to each knockout design based on annotated gene function (metabolic enzyme vs ribosomal protein/translation factor)

select_score.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of division_rate across the ~15-20 gene panel with Sarle's BC > 0.555; low-fitness cluster centered near division_rate ~0.0-0.3 comprising ~15-25% of genes, high-fitness cluster centered near division_rate ~0.9-1.0 (wildtype-like) comprising ~70-80%; translation-machinery KOs show mean division_rate at least 2-fold lower than metabolic KOs (Welch |t|>=2).

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (shape): compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient over the pooled per-seed division_rate values across all panel KO designs; reject unimodal H0 if BC>0.555. Step 2 (category difference): Welch's t of division_rate, translation-machinery-gene-KO designs vs metabolic-gene-KO designs, across seeds; reject H0 of no category difference if |t|>=2 (two-sided p<0.05 at Welch df). Both must pass for H1 to survive.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555 (effects look continuous/unimodal rather than two clusters) OR |t|<2 between translation and metabolic subsets (no category-level enrichment), indicating dispensability is not organized into a discrete fragile-vs-robust split by function in this model.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed division_rate across all panel KOs; secondary Welch's t between category subsets

rivals.claim: Dispensability is essentially binary and determined almost entirely by whether the gene is in central dogma/translation machinery at all -- i.e. nearly ALL translation-machinery gene KOs are lethal (division_rate~0) and nearly ALL metabolic gene KOs (outside core biosynthesis) are fully tolerated, so the distribution is bimodal but with near-100%/0% purity per category rather than a 70-80/15-25 split.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the translation-machinery subset would show division_rate collapsing to near 0 for essentially every gene (very low within-category variance) and the metabolic subset would show division_rate near wildtype for essentially every gene, i.e. the category boundary alone fully predicts the cluster membership with near-zero misclassification, rather than genes within each category spreading across both clusters.

rivals.claim: There is no reproducible bimodal structure at all -- single-gene KO fitness effects form a continuous gradient (many genes with partial, graded defects) that depends more on media condition (basal vs acetate) than on the metabolic/translation category label; the apparent minority of severe KOs is better explained by stochastic/seed noise than a real functional category effect.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, BC would fall at or below 0.555 (no genuine two-cluster separation), per-seed spread within a single gene KO would be comparable to the between-gene spread, and re-running under acetate condition would reshuffle which genes fall in the low-fitness cluster rather than preserving the translation-vs-metabolic grouping.

auxiliary_assumptions: Whether each named gene's KO is mechanistically represented in the simulator's metabolic/expression network is not knowable in advance; genes with no simulated phenotype will register as division_rate=wildtype by default, which is treated as a 'tolerated' outcome for this test (a scope caveat, not grounds to exclude them).
Functional category assignment (translation-machinery vs metabolic) is an a priori annotation applied before seeing results, not refit post hoc.
Division_rate averaged over 3 generations and 6 seeds is assumed sufficient to distinguish a lethal/near-lethal KO from a mild one; slower-developing defects beyond generation 3 are out of scope.
The basal condition panel is the primary test; the acetate sub-panel (4 genes) is a robustness/rival-discriminating check, not the main statistical test.
Stochastic seed-to-seed variance within one gene KO is assumed small relative to between-gene variance under H1; this is itself checked by the bimodality test design.

hypothesis.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
hypothesis.claim: Among a broad panel of individually non-essential-looking E. coli genes, the majority (~70-80%) can be deleted singly without abolishing growth or division in basal minimal medium, but a detectable minority (~20-30%) cause severe fitness defects (growth_rate drop >=50% and/or division_rate <1) despite not being classically 'essential', revealing a graded (not binary) dispensability spectrum.
hypothesis.h1: Across a panel of single gene_knockout strains sampled broadly (e.g. 20 genes spanning metabolic, regulatory, and structural categories), the distribution of fitness effects (quantified as % change in growth_rate and division_rate relative to wildtype/basal) is NOT uniformly 'no effect' — a substantial minority (20-30%) show growth_rate reduction >=50% or division_rate <1, while the majority (70-80%) show growth_rate within 20% of wildtype and division_rate ~1, producing a right-skewed/bimodal-leaning distribution of fitness costs rather than all genes being either fully essential or fully neutral.
hypothesis.h0: All single gene knockouts in the panel are either fully lethal (division_rate=0, growth_rate~0) or fully neutral (growth_rate and division_rate statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal, |effect_pct|<10%, welch_t<2) — i.e., no intermediate/graded dispensability class exists in the simulator's output distribution.

operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: fraction of generations that complete division over 4 generations, averaged across seeds; division_rate < 1 flags a division defect

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: % change in mean instantaneous specific growth rate (1/h) of knockout vs wildtype/basal across seeds

operational_defs.observable: joint distribution of growth_rate and division_rate across the 20-gene panel
operational_defs.measure: bimodality coefficient (BC) of per-gene mean % growth_rate change pooled across seeds; BC>0.555 indicates two distinct clusters (severe-cost vs near-neutral) rather than a single unimodal 'all genes similar' distribution

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Panel-level: ~20-30% of 20 sampled non-classically-essential genes show growth_rate reduction >=50% (fold-change in growth_rate <=0.5x wildtype) and/or division_rate<1; ~70-80% show growth_rate within 20% of wildtype (fold-change 0.8-1.2x) and division_rate~1. Pooled distribution of per-gene growth_rate % change has bimodality coefficient BC>0.555 (two clusters: severe-cost cluster centered near -60% to -90%, near-neutral cluster centered near 0 to -10%).

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1: compute per-gene % growth_rate change (target vs reference) via welch_disconfirm across seeds for each of 20 knockouts; classify each gene as 'severe' if |effect_pct|>=50% or division_rate<1, else 'near-neutral'. Step 2: run bimodality_bc on the pooled vector of 20 per-gene mean % growth_rate changes; reject H0 (no graded structure) if BC>0.555 AND the severe-class fraction falls between 0.15 and 0.40 (consistent with predicted 20-30%).
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555 (unimodal distribution, i.e., all genes cluster tightly together) OR the severe-class fraction is either ~0% (all neutral) or >50% (most genes essential) OR severe genes show division_rate=0 exactly matching fully-lethal controls (no intermediate class) — any of these confirms H0's binary essential/neutral picture instead of a graded spectrum.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-gene mean %growth_rate-change values (20 genes, seeds averaged per gene)

rivals.claim: Gene essentiality in this simulator is strictly binary: a gene's KO is either lethal (division_rate=0) because it is mechanistically wired into the model's reaction network, or it is a no-op (no measurable effect) because the model lacks that gene's mechanistic detail — there is no intermediate severity because the simulator doesn't implement partial-pathway degradation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: The pooled distribution would show two sharp point-masses at effect_pct~0 and effect_pct~-100%/division_rate=0, with BC possibly >0.555 but with NO genes falling in an intermediate band (e.g. -30% to -70% growth_rate); i.e., a bimodal split at the extremes rather than a severe-but-viable cluster.

rivals.claim: Any observed 'graded' spread is driven by stochastic replicate noise (seed-to-seed variance) rather than a real gene-specific severity class; with more seeds the per-gene means would regress toward either 0% or -100%.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Welch_disconfirm per gene would show high within-gene seed variance (large per-seed spread) that overlaps between 'severe' and 'near-neutral' genes, and welch_t for most 'severe' calls would be <2 (not significant vs wildtype), indicating the apparent graded spectrum is noise, not a real mechanistic class of partially-dispensable genes.

Classify each gene fitness-neutral (|welch_t|<2 and division_rate=1) vs fitness-costly (welch_t<=-2 or division_rate<1). H1 requires BOTH classes to contain >=20% of the panel (>=3/12 each). Apply BH-FDR across the 12 per-gene growth_rate comparisons to control multiple testing; a gene only counts as 'costly' if it is FDR-significant.
falsifier.refuting_result: If fewer than 2/12 genes are fitness-neutral (near-uniform essentiality) OR fewer than 2/12 genes are FDR-significant fitness-costly (near-uniform neutrality) OR no gene flips classification between basal and acetate, H1 is refuted and H0 (uniform dispensability or uniform essentiality) stands.

test.statistic: per-gene welch_t on growth_rate, BH-FDR-corrected across 12 genes; division_rate checked as binary viability flag
test.threshold: n_significant_fdr10 (costly genes) in [3,9] out of 12 AND n_neutral (|t|<2, division_rate=1) in [3,9] out of 12

rivals.claim: Essentiality is a near-binary genome property (most genes are either clearly essential and crash the cell, or clearly dispensable with negligible cost) with no meaningful intermediate class and no condition-dependence.
rivals.distinguishing_result: The intermediate-cost bin (welch_t between -2 and -5, moderate growth reduction) would be nearly empty (<=1/12 genes), and no gene would flip classification between basal and acetate — effects would cluster at the extremes only.

rivals.claim: Any apparent growth defect from single-gene knockouts in this panel is dominated by simulation/model artifacts (e.g. missing regulatory compensation) rather than real metabolic/physiological dependency, so the heterogeneous pattern reflects model coverage, not biology.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If division_rate stays at 1 and growth_rate shows no FDR-significant change for ANY of the 12 genes (model treats them as inert), that signals the simulator lacks mechanistic coverage for this gene set, which would be a capability gap rather than evidence against H1.

auxiliary_assumptions: The 12-gene panel is a representative, not exhaustive, sample of 'candidate non-essential' genes; genome-wide fraction estimates are extrapolated from this panel, not a full-genome screen.

Growth_rate and division_rate are sufficient proxies for viability; the simulator may not capture long-timescale adaptive compensation (e.g. suppressor mutations) that could rescue a KO beyond the simulated generations.

Whether a given KO is mechanistically wired into the model (vs treated as inert) is unknown a priori; genes with zero channel response are flagged per the second rival as a possible coverage gap rather than true neutrality.
Seeds (6) capture intrinsic stochastic noise sufficiently for Welch's t at this effect-size regime; no claim is made about rare bistable subpopulations within a seed.
Acetate is used as the sole discriminating alternative condition (static_only_carbon); results do not generalize to other carbon sources not tested.

hypothesis.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
hypothesis.claim: Across a broad screen of single-gene knockouts, most genes are individually dispensable for growth in basal minimal medium: a sizable minority (~10-20%) of tested non-essential-looking genes will show no significant growth defect (division_rate ~1, growth_rate within noise of wildtype), while a smaller 'essential' fraction (~5-10% of genome-scale screens in reality; here we predict ~10-15% of a curated ~40-80 gene panel enriched for metabolic/ribosomal genes) will crash (division_rate drops toward 0 and growth_rate falls >50%).
hypothesis.h1: In a panel of single-gene knockouts spanning core metabolism, ribosome biogenesis, and regulatory genes, the DISTRIBUTION of growth outcomes is bimodal: a dispensable cluster (division_rate ≈1, growth_rate within ~10% of wildtype) and a lethal/near-lethal cluster (division_rate <0.3, growth_rate reduced >50%), with the dispensable cluster containing the majority (>60%) of tested genes.
hypothesis.h0: Knockout effects on division_rate/growth_rate are unimodally and continuously distributed around a single mean reduction (no distinct dispensable vs essential clusters), OR the majority of tested genes are NOT dispensable (i.e., most knockouts impair growth beyond noise).

operational_defs.observable: division_rate and growth_rate of a single-gene knockout vs wildtype over 2-4 generations
operational_defs.measure: division_rate ratio to wildtype (dispensable if >=0.85) and growth_rate Welch t vs wildtype (|t|<2 => no significant defect)

operational_defs.observable: division_rate collapse
operational_defs.measure: division_rate <0.3 and/or growth_rate reduced >50% with |welch_t|>=2 vs wildtype

operational_defs.observable: pooled per-gene growth_rate effect sizes (percent change vs wildtype) across all knocked-out genes/seeds
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-gene mean effect-size values

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of knockout effects with BC>0.555; dispensable cluster fraction ~60-80% of panel with |effect on growth_rate| <10% and division_rate>=0.85; essential/near-essential cluster ~15-30% with growth_rate reduction >50% and division_rate<0.3. Individual dispensable-gene examples (e.g. acrB) predicted to show <5% growth_rate change (|t|<2 vs wildtype).

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-gene mean growth_rate effect sizes across the panel; reject unimodal-null if BC>0.555. Secondary per-gene check: Welch t of growth_rate, each knockout vs wildtype across seeds; classify dispensable if |t|<2, essential if |t|>=2 and effect_pct<-50%.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555 (effects form a single continuous distribution, not two clusters) OR the dispensable cluster comprises <50% of the panel (i.e. most knockouts significantly impair growth), contradicting the predicted majority-dispensable, bimodal pattern.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-gene growth_rate percent-effect values
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for bimodal; else refuted

rivals.claim: Rival A: growth defects are graded/continuous (no two discrete classes) because most genes have small additive fitness costs — essentiality is a threshold artifact of the measurement window, not a biological bimodality.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled effect-size distribution has BC<=0.555 and looks unimodal/continuous rather than two separated clusters.

rivals.claim: Rival B: apparent 'dispensability' in many knockouts is actually a division-specific defect masked by growth_rate (cells keep growing in mass but fail to divide), so growth_rate alone overstates the dispensable fraction.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A subset of genes shows division_rate significantly <0.85 (division defect) while growth_rate stays within noise of wildtype, decoupling the two channels and shrinking the true dispensable fraction relative to the growth_rate-only estimate.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator mechanistically implements the metabolic/regulatory consequences of each knocked-out gene in the panel (not all E. coli genes are modeled; only genes with a mapped reaction/process will show an effect) — genes with no modeled function will trivially appear 'dispensable' and are a known scope limitation.

Panel composition (choice of ~40-80 genes) is assumed enriched for a realistic mix of known-essential (e.g. ribosomal, cell-wall) and known-nonessential (e.g. acrB, efflux pumps) genes so the predicted ~60-80%/15-30% split is a meaningful test, not an artifact of panel bias.

4 generations is assumed sufficient to reveal a lethal/near-lethal phenotype (division_rate collapse) for genes whose knockout is acutely essential under basal minimal medium; slower-onset auxotrophies may be undercounted.
Seeds (replicate stochastic runs) are assumed to capture intrinsic noise sufficient to compute per-gene Welch t without confounding from insufficient replication.

drafts.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
drafts.claim: Across a broad panel of single-gene knockouts, a substantial minority (~20-30%) are effectively dispensable for growth on basal minimal medium: their deletion yields a growth rate and division rate statistically indistinguishable from wildtype (within ~10% of wildtype growth_rate), while the rest show a significant growth/division defect, consistent with known E. coli essentiality screens (~87-93% of genes nonessential genome-wide, but with heterogeneous fitness costs among the 'nonessential' set tested here).
drafts.h1: When a panel of single-gene knockouts is simulated on basal minimal medium, the per-gene distribution of growth-rate effect sizes (KO vs wildtype) is bimodal: one cluster near zero effect (dispensable genes, predicted ~20-30% of the panel) and one cluster with strong negative effect (conditionally essential/essential-like genes), rather than a single unimodal distribution of mild, uniformly small defects.
drafts.h0: Growth-rate and division-rate effects of single-gene knockouts across the panel are unimodally and continuously distributed around a single mean defect (no distinct dispensable cluster separable from a defective cluster), i.e. unimodal with Sarle's bimodality coefficient <=0.555, and/or the fraction of knockouts statistically indistinguishable from wildtype is not detectably different from 0.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and division_rate of a gene_knockout design vs wildtype/basal reference, across seeds
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test per gene (KO vs WT) on growth_rate; gene classified 'dispensable' if |welch_t|<2 AND division_rate within 0.95-1.0 of WT; else 'costly'

operational_defs.observable: per-gene effect_pct (percent growth-rate change KO vs WT) pooled across the gene panel
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over the pooled per-gene effect_pct values

operational_defs.observable: count of genes classified dispensable (per Welch test) divided by panel size
operational_defs.measure: BH-FDR-corrected proportion test across the panel; report fraction with 95% CI

drafts.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of per-gene growth-rate effect_pct with bimodality coefficient BC>0.555; dispensable cluster centered near 0% change (within +/-10%), costly cluster centered at <= -40% change; predicted fraction dispensable ~20-30% of a ~20-30 gene panel spanning metabolic, biosynthetic, transport, and regulatory categories.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient over the pooled per-gene effect_pct distribution from the panel; reject H1 (bimodal dispensable/costly structure) if BC<=0.555 (unimodal). Separately, for each gene run Welch t of growth_rate (KO vs WT) across seeds with BH-FDR correction at q<0.10 across the panel; reject H1 if the fraction of genes classified dispensable (|welch_t|<2 and division_rate>=0.95) is not detectably different from 0 (i.e., fewer than ~2 of ~25 genes qualify).
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled effect_pct distribution is unimodal (BC<=0.555) and/or fewer than ~8% of panel genes qualify as dispensable, indicating knockout effects form a single continuous distribution of costs rather than a distinct dispensable subpopulation.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-gene effect_pct; secondary bh_fdr_movers over per-gene welch_t for fraction-dispensable test
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for bimodal; fraction dispensable 95% CI must exclude 0 and include values >=15%

rivals.claim: Rival A: Dispensability is not bimodal but a smooth continuum of fitness costs (polygenic buffering), so no sharp dispensable cluster exists — the apparent WT-like genes are just the low tail of a single unimodal cost distribution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled effect_pct distribution shows BC<=0.555 (unimodal) even though some genes individually pass the |welch_t|<2 threshold — the 'dispensable' genes are statistically indistinguishable from a continuous tail, not a separate mode.

rivals.claim: Rival B: Apparent dispensability is an artifact of insufficient simulated time/generations — genes classified dispensable at 2-4 generations would show defects if run longer (slow-growth lethality), so true essential fraction is underestimated.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Re-running the same 'dispensable' subset at an extended generation count (e.g. via a timeline with prolonged basal exposure) reveals division_rate dropping below 0.95 or growth_rate declining >10% that was not visible at 2-4 generations, i.e. the dispensable/costly boundary is generation-count-dependent rather than a stable structural feature.

drafts.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
drafts.claim: Among a broad panel of individually non-essential metabolic and regulatory genes, a substantial minority (~20-30%) of single-gene knockouts are viable (division_rate > 0 and growth_rate within normal replicate noise) across a 1-4 generation window on basal media, while the rest show severe growth/division defects — i.e. 'genes E. coli can live without' form a sizeable but minority fraction of a representative gene panel, not nearly all or almost none.
drafts.h1: Across a panel of >=20 single-gene knockouts sampled from metabolic, biosynthetic, and regulatory categories, the fraction classified as viable (division_rate >= 0.8 of wildtype AND growth_rate not significantly reduced, Welch |t|<2 vs wildtype) is between 15% and 35%.
drafts.h0: The viable fraction in the panel is either near 0% (almost all single-gene KOs are lethal/severely impaired) or near 100% (almost all are silently tolerated), i.e. outside the 15-35% band predicted by H1.

operational_defs.observable: division_rate and growth_rate channels for a gene_knockout design vs wildtype/basal reference
operational_defs.measure: division_rate < 0.8 of wildtype OR growth_rate significantly reduced (Welch |t|>=2) => classified non-viable/impaired; else viable

operational_defs.construct: viable fraction of a gene panel
operational_defs.observable: per-gene classification across the knockout screen
operational_defs.measure: count(viable genes)/total genes screened, reported with 95% CI via binomial proportion over the panel

drafts.predicted_effect: Viable fraction ≈ 20-30% of the screened panel (point estimate ~0.25, binomial 95% CI should exclude both <0.15 and >0.35); among viable KOs, mean growth_rate reduction <10% vs wildtype; among non-viable KOs, division_rate drops by >=50% or growth_rate falls by >=30% (Welch |t|>=2).

falsifier.decision_rule: Per-gene Welch t of growth_rate (target vs reference) across seeds, |t|>=2 flags impairment; classify viable genes as division_rate>=0.8*wildtype AND |t|<2; then compute binomial 95% CI on viable fraction over the >=20-gene panel; reject H1 if CI excludes the 0.15-0.35 band (i.e. falls entirely below 0.15 or entirely above 0.35).
falsifier.refuting_result: Binomial 95% CI for viable fraction lies entirely outside [0.15,0.35] (e.g. observed fraction <10% implying near-universal essentiality in this panel, or >50% implying most tested genes are dispensable), contradicting the predicted minority-but-substantial viable fraction.

test.statistic: welch_t per gene on growth_rate (target vs reference), then binomial proportion of viable calls across panel
test.threshold: |t|>=2 per gene for impairment call; panel-level 95% binomial CI must overlap [0.15,0.35] to support H1

rivals.claim: Essentiality is bimodal by functional category: genes in core informational processing (ribosomal, RNA polymerase, DNA replication) are essentially all lethal, while genes in peripheral metabolism (alternative carbon utilization, stress regulators) are essentially all dispensable, so the overall 'viable fraction' is not a meaningful single number but strongly depends on category sampled.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If the panel is stratified by category and viable fraction is ~0% for informational-gene KOs but ~60-80% for peripheral-metabolism KOs, the pooled 20-30% estimate would be an artifact of panel composition rather than a stable global rate.

rivals.claim: Most 'viable' knockouts on basal glucose minimal media are only conditionally viable; they would be classified lethal under nutrient-limited or alternative-carbon conditions (e.g. acetate), so true unconditional dispensability is much rarer than the basal-media estimate suggests.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Re-running the same viable-call genes as gene_knockout/acetate and finding division_rate collapses (<0.8) for a majority of them would show basal-media viability overstates true gene dispensability.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator mechanistically implements metabolic/regulatory consequences of each targeted gene's deletion (flux rerouting, missing enzyme) rather than treating all KOs identically; genes whose KO is not mechanistically modeled will default to near-wildtype behavior and could inflate the apparent viable fraction - this is a known scope caveat not resolvable from outside.
division_rate and growth_rate are measured over the same 1-4 generation window across all knockouts, so slow-onset defects (e.g. accumulating toxic intermediates past generation 4) are out of scope.

The 20-gene panel is a representative stratified sample (central carbon metabolism, TCA, respiration, transport, global regulators) rather than exhaustive; the viable-fraction estimate generalizes to genes of similar functional categories, not to the whole genome.

Basal glucose minimal media is treated as the canonical condition for the primary essentiality call; conditional essentiality under other media is treated as a separate rival question, not folded into the main viable-fraction estimate.

drafts.question: Which genes can E. coli live without?
drafts.claim: Among a broad panel of individually non-essential genes (drawn from known E. coli dispensable categories: stress-response regulators, secondary transporters, non-core biosynthetic paralogs), the majority (~70-80%) of single-gene knockouts will show no significant growth or division defect relative to wildtype, while a minority (~20-30%) will show a measurable but non-lethal fitness cost, operationalized as a reduced growth_rate and/or division_rate that nonetheless remains >0 (viable).
drafts.h1: Across a panel of candidate dispensable genes, the fraction of single-gene knockouts that remain viable (division_rate > 0 across all simulated generations) is high (>=0.7), and growth_rate reductions among viable knockouts follow a right-skewed distribution with most KOs clustering near wildtype and a minority showing >15% growth_rate reduction.
drafts.h0: Single-gene knockouts from the panel are, on average, lethal or near-lethal: fewer than 0.5 of the panel maintain division_rate > 0, i.e. growth_rate and division_rate are statistically indistinguishable from zero/collapse for most KOs relative to wildtype/basal.

operational_defs.observable: division_rate channel over the simulated generations
operational_defs.measure: division_rate > 0 for all generations simulated (per seed); fraction of seeds with division_rate>0 defines per-gene viability call

operational_defs.construct: fitness cost of a non-lethal knockout
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel
operational_defs.measure: percent reduction in mean growth_rate (target vs wildtype/basal reference) averaged across seeds

operational_defs.observable: distribution of per-gene viability calls and growth_rate effect sizes across the knockout panel
operational_defs.measure: fraction of genes in panel classified viable (division_rate>0) and shape (skew) of growth_rate effect-size distribution across that viable subset

drafts.predicted_effect: Across a panel of ~12 candidate dispensable genes (seeds=6 each), we predict ~70-80% (8-10/12) show division_rate indistinguishable from wildtype (no lethality) and growth_rate reduction <10%; the remaining ~20-30% (2-4/12) show growth_rate reduction of 15-40% but division_rate still >0 (viable but costly). The growth_rate effect-size distribution across the panel is right-skewed (most near 0%, a long tail to 15-40% reduction), not bimodal lethal/wildtype.

falsifier.decision_rule: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the panel's per-gene log2 fold-change in growth_rate (target vs wildtype, per seed); classify a gene as having a significant fitness cost if FDR q<0.10. Separately, call a gene lethal if division_rate drops to 0 in >=50% of seeds. H1 requires n_significant_fdr10 / panel_size <= 0.3 among costly KOs AND lethal fraction < 0.3 overall; refuted if lethal fraction >= 0.5 (H0 pattern) or if >70% of genes show significant costs (uniformly deleterious, contradicting the 'mostly dispensable' claim).
falsifier.refuting_result: If >=50% of the panel shows division_rate collapsing to 0 across most seeds, or if BH-FDR flags >70% of genes as significantly growth-impaired, this refutes the claim that most single-gene KOs in this panel are freely dispensable.

test.statistic: BH-FDR over per-gene log2 fold-change (growth_rate, target vs reference) across seeds
test.threshold: q<0.10; H1 requires n_significant_fdr10/panel_size <= 0.3

rivals.claim: Dispensability is condition-dependent: genes classified as non-essential on basal/glucose media become essential or highly costly on a poorer carbon source (e.g. acetate), because the 'dispensable' categories (secondary transporters, stress regulators) are actually load-bearing under nutrient stress.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Running the same KO panel under condition=acetate would show a substantially larger fraction of lethal/high-cost KOs (e.g. >50%) than under basal, revealing that the 'most genes dispensable' result is an artifact of testing only rich/basal media.

rivals.claim: Apparent viability is a ribosome-allocation/stringent-response buffering artifact: KOs appear non-lethal only because ppGpp-mediated growth-rate throttling (stringent response) masks what would otherwise be lethal resource misallocation; removing that buffering (relA knockout background) would unmask lethality in genes currently scored as dispensable.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Knocking out relA (a relA gene_knockout background) in combination panel members, or clamping ppgpp_conc to a fixed low multiple, would convert some currently-viable KOs into division_rate=0 (lethal) outcomes, showing the stringent response was compensating.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator mechanistically implements the metabolic/regulatory role of each targeted gene (not all genes in the panel may have an encoded mechanism; genes with no modeled effect will trivially show wildtype-like growth_rate/division_rate, which is a simulator-coverage limitation, not evidence of true biological dispensability — noted as an explicit scope caveat).

Division_rate = 0 is treated as the operational proxy for lethality; a partial division defect (0 < division_rate < 1) is treated as 'costly but viable', consistent with the instrument's own stated use of division_rate as the viability readout.

Panel genes were chosen based on prior literature as plausible dispensable-category genes (transporters, secondary catabolic enzymes, stress regulators); results generalize only to this category mix, not to the full genome, given the modest panel size (n=12) imposed by compute constraints.

Seed-to-seed stochastic variation (6 seeds) is assumed sufficient to distinguish genuine fitness costs from intrinsic noise at the effect sizes predicted (15-40%); smaller true effects may be underpowered at this seed count.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed division_rate values across all panel genes (and separately growth_rate); reject H1 (bimodal essential/non-essential split) if BC <= 0.555, indicating a unimodal/graded distribution instead
