operational_defs.measure: compare acetate-vs-basal growth_rate and ppgpp_conc gap in relA-knockout background vs wildtype background

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: acetate (poorer substrate) shows lower growth_rate, lower ribosome_conc, higher ppgpp_conc than glucose/basal. Magnitude: growth_rate fold-change ~0.5-0.6x (40-50% reduction), ribosome_conc fold-change ~0.7-0.75x (25-30% reduction), ppgpp_conc fold-change ~1.5-2x (50-100% increase), each with |Welch t| >= 2 across seeds.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, acetate vs basal across seeds; reject H0 if two-sided |t|>=2. Also require growth_rate shows |t|>=2 in the predicted direction (lower under acetate) and effect_pct <= -40%.
falsifier.refuting_result: If ppgpp_conc Welch |t| < 2 (no significant elevation) OR growth_rate does not drop by at least ~40% with |t|>=2, the data refute the hierarchical-preference/catabolite-repression signature and support the interchangeable-substrate null.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t| >= 2 on ppgpp_conc AND on growth_rate, with growth_rate effect_pct <= -40%

rivals.claim: Rival A (pure growth-capacity rival): Acetate simply supports slower growth due to lower ATP yield per carbon, with NO distinct stringent-response/ppGpp signature — growth_rate drops but ppgpp_conc stays statistically unchanged from basal, i.e., it's a bioenergetic limitation, not a regulatory 'choice' hierarchy.
rivals.distinguishing_result: growth_rate Welch |t|>=2 showing reduction, but ppgpp_conc Welch |t| < 2 (no significant ppGpp elevation) in condition/acetate vs wildtype/basal.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ribosome-allocation-independent rival): Any apparent ppGpp/ribosome covariation under acetate is driven by a RelA-independent pathway (e.g., SpoT basal turnover or general slow-growth scaling) rather than a stringent-response 'preference' mechanism; knocking out relA would NOT abolish the ppGpp elevation or close the growth-rate gap.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In gene_knockout/relA (acetate condition), ppgpp_conc elevation vs basal persists (Welch |t|>=2, similar effect_pct to wildtype), showing the signal is RelA-independent.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's static 'acetate' fitted condition is a valid stand-in for the physiological state a cell would adopt on the non-preferred/second sugar in a real two-sugar mixture, even though no true simultaneous mixed-sugar condition exists in the envelope.

ppGpp and ribosome concentration readouts are recorded under steady-state charging for both conditions (no kinetic-charging-only artifacts), so basal and acetate are measured on the same channel semantics.

Growth-rate and ppGpp differences across conditions are attributable to media-fitting physiology rather than numerical/solver artifacts (fba_objective used only as a diagnostic sanity check, not as evidence).

Seed-to-seed stochastic variation under isogenic replicates is small enough that 4-8 seeds give adequate power to detect the predicted fold-changes (checked post hoc via power_mde if initial test is ambiguous).

RelA knockout removes the dominant RelA-dependent synthesis arm of ppGpp induction in this model; residual SpoT-mediated synthesis/hydrolysis is treated as a separate, not confounding, mechanism for this test's purposes.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: Diauxic-shift-like carbon hierarchy in this model is implemented via catabolite repression acting through the stringent response: when a second, less-preferred carbon/amino-acid source is available alongside a preferred one, cells do not co-utilize both at full rate; instead a stringent-response-like signature (elevated ppGpp, reduced ribosome concentration, reduced charged-tRNA fraction) appears that suppresses growth-rate gains from the second substrate until the first is exhausted. Because this simulator's glucose uptake is a binary on/off switch (not graded), I operationalize 'choosing between two sugars' as a timeline media-shift (minimal -> minimal_plus_amino_acids), using amino-acid addition as the tractable analog of a second nutrient becoming available, and ask whether the cell shows a repression/hierarchy signature (a transient ppGpp spike and sub-additive growth-rate response) rather than an immediate, additive growth benefit.
drafts.h1: Upon mid-run addition of a second nutrient (amino acids) to cells growing on minimal medium, the cell exhibits a transient hierarchical/repressive response: ppgpp_conc rises transiently (>=1.5-fold over pre-shift baseline) and growth_rate shows a sub-additive (damped, not step-additive) increase, consistent with regulatory gating of simultaneous substrate use rather than immediate full co-utilization.
drafts.h0: The growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories after the amino-acid addition are indistinguishable (Welch t, |t|<2) from a step/additive null in which the added nutrient is used immediately and fully alongside the first, with no transient ppGpp elevation beyond wildtype/basal seed-to-seed noise.

operational_defs.measure: fold-change in ppgpp_conc at first 1-2 post-shift timepoints relative to pre-shift mean, per seed

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate trajectory post-shift vs pre-shift
operational_defs.measure: slope/step-size of growth_rate increase in the 2 generations after shift, compared across timeline/shift vs wildtype/basal (no shift) reference

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc and fraction_trna_charged
operational_defs.measure: mean level in post-shift window vs pre-shift window, per seed

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: ppgpp_conc rises transiently post-shift (predicted +50-100%, i.e. 1.5-2x baseline) before relaxing; growth_rate increase after the shift is damped/sub-additive, reaching <70% of the naive additive-step prediction within the first post-shift generation, then converging upward over 2-3 generations. Effect size target: Welch t on ppgpp_conc (shift vs no-shift reference) |t|>=2; growth_rate step-size reduced by >=30% relative to an additive-null expectation.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc (timeline target, post-shift window) vs reference (wildtype/basal, matched timepoints) across seeds; reject H1 if |t|<2, i.e. no detectable transient ppGpp elevation beyond basal seed noise
falsifier.refuting_result: ppgpp_conc in the timeline/shift condition is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal (|t|<2) and growth_rate rises step-wise/additively immediately after the amino-acid addition with no damping, indicating free simultaneous co-utilization rather than a repression/gating mechanism

test.statistic: welch_t

rivals.claim: No regulatory hierarchy exists in this model at all — the amino-acid shift simply adds biosynthetic capacity and growth_rate increases immediately and additively, with ppgpp_conc staying flat or even decreasing (since amino acid biosynthesis costs drop), because the model does not implement catabolite-repression-like coupling of ppGpp to nutrient richness.
rivals.distinguishing_result: ppgpp_conc shows no transient rise (or decreases) post-shift, and growth_rate step change at shift time matches/exceeds a naive additive prediction (no damping).

rivals.claim: The response is a generic nutrient-upshift/overflow signature, not a repression/hierarchy mechanism per se — ppGpp changes reflect transient translational supply-demand mismatch (ribosome synthesis lag) rather than active substrate-choice gating, and would appear identically regardless of which second nutrient is added or even for an amino-acid REMOVAL in the opposite direction.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A matched amino_acid_shift in the opposite direction (removal) or a relA-knockout background still shows a similar transient ppGpp/growth perturbation, i.e. the signature is symmetric/mechanism-agnostic rather than specific to nutrient hierarchy gating.

auxiliary_assumptions: Because glucose uptake in this simulator is a strict binary on/off switch, true two-sugar (e.g. glucose/lactose) preferential uptake cannot be graded or titrated here; amino-acid addition via the timeline perturbation is used as the closest in-envelope analog of a second-nutrient-availability event that can trigger regulatory gating.

ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channels are read under steady-state tRNA charging in this design (no kinetic ppGpp module requested), so dynamics reflect the steady-state charging approximation, not explicit RelA/SpoT kinetics, except in the relA-knockout control which still uses steady-state charging logic for its baseline.

Seed-to-seed intrinsic noise is assumed small enough relative to the predicted >=50% ppGpp fold-change and >=30% growth-rate damping that 6 seeds give adequate power; if not, this is a scope limitation flagged for a follow-up power_mde check rather than an infinite regress on noise sources.

The relA-knockout control is treated as the interventional discriminator: if ppGpp fails to rise in relA-knockout yet growth-rate damping persists, that would indicate damping is ppGpp-independent (supporting the generic-overflow rival); if both ppGpp rise and damping disappear together in relA-knockout, that supports ppGpp-dependence of the gating mechanism.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: E. coli's choice between two sugars is implemented as catabolite-repression-mediated carbon hierarchy: when a preferred carbon source is available, the stringent/ppGpp and growth-rate state settles to a 'glucose-like' high-growth, low-ppGpp regime, and this regime is causally imposed by the stringent response machinery rather than being a passive byproduct of flux — knocking out the alarmone synthetase (relA) should blunt the growth-rate/ppGpp divergence normally seen between a preferred (glucose-like, basal) and a non-preferred (acetate) static carbon condition.
drafts.h1: Across static carbon conditions that stand in for preferred vs non-preferred sugars (basal vs acetate), wildtype cells show a large, reproducible divergence in growth_rate (>=2-fold higher on basal) and ppgpp_conc (>=1.5-fold higher on acetate), and this divergence is substantially attenuated (effect size shrinks by >=50%) when relA is knocked out, because ppGpp signaling causally mediates the hierarchical response rather than merely correlating with flux state.
drafts.h0: There is no reproducible growth_rate/ppgpp_conc divergence between basal and acetate conditions beyond replicate noise, OR the divergence is unchanged (shrinks by <50%, i.e. the Welch t vs reference stays |t|>=2) in the relA knockout, indicating ppGpp is not causally necessary for the carbon-source-dependent phenotype.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel under condition=basal
operational_defs.measure: mean growth_rate (1/h) across seeds, generations 1-4

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc channels under condition=acetate
operational_defs.measure: mean growth_rate and mean ppgpp_conc (uM) across seeds

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate channels under gene_knockout(relA) crossed with condition
operational_defs.measure: difference in (acetate-basal) effect size for growth_rate and ppgpp_conc between wildtype and relA-knockout backgrounds

drafts.predicted_effect: Wildtype basal vs acetate: growth_rate fold-change >=2x (basal higher), ppgpp_conc fold-change >=1.5x (acetate higher). In relA-knockout background, the basal-vs-acetate growth_rate and ppgpp_conc differences shrink by >=50% in effect_pct relative to wildtype's basal-vs-acetate effect_pct (interaction/attenuation effect, not full abolition expected since SpoT remains).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, relA-knockout/acetate vs wildtype/acetate across seeds; also compute the wildtype basal-vs-acetate effect_pct and the relA-KO basal-vs-acetate effect_pct separately via disconfirm calls, then compare attenuation; reject H1 if |t|<2 for the KO-vs-WT-at-acetate comparison AND the KO's basal-vs-acetate effect_pct is not reduced by >=50% relative to WT's
falsifier.refuting_result: relA knockout shows the same basal-vs-acetate ppgpp_conc and growth_rate divergence as wildtype (effect_pct shrinks by <50%, |t|<2 for KO-vs-WT contrast), implying ppGpp induction is not the causal lever and the carbon hierarchy is driven by another mechanism (e.g. direct flux/PTS-mediated catabolite repression independent of the stringent response)

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for significance; attenuation claim requires >=50% effect_pct reduction in KO vs WT

rivals.claim: The growth-rate/ppGpp divergence between basal and acetate is driven purely by flux/FBA-level metabolic constraints (e.g. differential ATP yield, PTS-independent catabolite repression via cAMP-CRP-like flux sensing) and is independent of ppGpp signaling.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA knockout shows NO attenuation of the basal-vs-acetate growth_rate or ppgpp_conc divergence (effect_pct unchanged, |t|<2 for KO-vs-WT contrast) — ppGpp rises/falls but is a non-causal correlate of flux state.

rivals.claim: The divergence reflects ribosome-allocation limits (rRNA operon capacity) rather than alarmone signaling per se — i.e. growth rate differences are explained by ribosome_conc/rrna capacity directly, with ppGpp as a downstream readout rather than driver.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout control shows a growth-rate divergence between basal and acetate comparable to wildtype (ribosome capacity, not ppGpp, sets the phenotype), while relA knockout alone fails to shrink the divergence much, confirming ribosome allocation as the primary lever.

auxiliary_assumptions: Static media conditions 'basal' (glucose-like/minimal) and 'acetate' are valid proxies for 'preferred vs non-preferred sugar' since the instrument cannot do a mid-run carbon-source switch or simultaneous two-sugar mixture; true simultaneous two-sugar diauxie dynamics are out of scope for this envelope and are treated as a caveat.

relA knockout is assumed to meaningfully reduce ppGpp synthesis capacity in the simulated stringent-response module even though SpoT-mediated synthesis may remain, so full abolition of the ppGpp signal is not expected, only attenuation.

Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are read under steady-state charging (since ppgpp_conc/rela_conc are only recorded under steady-state or kinetic-with-ppGpp-module); we assume the default steady-state charging mode is active for both conditions and knockout runs so channels are comparable.

Seed-to-seed stochastic variation (4-8 seeds) is assumed sufficient to distinguish a >=50% attenuation effect from replicate noise over 1-4 generations; if not, this is a power limitation to flag via power_mde in a follow-up rather than over-interpreting a null here.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: E. coli's choice between two sugars in the same flask is implemented as catabolite-repression-driven sequential use (diauxie): when a preferred carbon source is present together with a second one, the cell's physiology converges on the fitted single-substrate state rather than a blended intermediate, because cAMP-CRP/PTS-mediated repression suppresses the second substrate's utilization pathway until the first is exhausted. Since this simulator only exposes static fitted media conditions (no mid-run carbon switch), the operational proxy is: growth on a mixed/alternative-carbon condition should resemble growth on the preferred-sugar-only condition far more than a naive average of the two single-sugar conditions, and should NOT show an intermediate/blended growth-rate phenotype.
drafts.h1: Across static media conditions representing single vs. alternative carbon sources, the cell's growth_rate and ribosome_conc under an alternative (non-preferred) carbon condition (e.g. acetate) are substantially lower (>=30% reduction) and more stress-like (elevated ppgpp_conc) than under the preferred basal (glucose) condition, consistent with a hierarchical/repressive rather than a smoothly blended resource-allocation strategy; this gap should NOT shrink when ppGpp signaling is removed (relA knockout), indicating the hierarchy is not merely a ppGpp-dose artifact but reflects condition-specific pathway engagement.
drafts.h0: growth_rate, ribosome_conc, and ppgpp_conc under the alternative-carbon condition do not differ significantly (Welch |t|<2) from the basal (preferred-carbon) condition, i.e., the cell treats both carbon conditions equivalently (no hierarchical preference signature).

operational_defs.measure: instantaneous specific growth rate (1/h) under condition=basal (glucose)

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate, ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: growth rate and alarmone concentration under condition=acetate (a static fitted alternative-carbon condition)

operational_defs.measure: active ribosome concentration (uM) compared across basal vs acetate conditions

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc, growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: same comparison repeated in a relA gene_knockout background to test whether the gap persists without stringent-response signaling

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: acetate (alternative, non-preferred carbon) condition shows LOWER growth_rate and ribosome_conc and HIGHER ppgpp_conc than basal (glucose). Magnitude: growth_rate fold-change ~0.4-0.6x of basal (>=30-40% reduction), ribosome_conc reduced ~20-40%, ppgpp_conc elevated ~1.5-3x basal. This gap should persist (not disappear) in the relA-knockout background, with growth_rate fold-change still <=0.7x, showing the hierarchy is not solely a ppGpp-magnitude effect.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of growth_rate, condition/acetate vs wildtype/basal, across seeds; reject H0 (i.e., support hierarchical-preference H1) if |t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates >=30% reduction in acetate growth_rate relative to basal
falsifier.refuting_result: growth_rate under acetate is statistically indistinguishable from basal (|t|<2) or reduced by <10%, indicating no strong hierarchical penalty for the non-preferred carbon source

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=30% reduction

rivals.claim: Rival A (graded/blended allocation): the cell allocates resources proportionally/continuously based on substrate quality rather than a sharp hierarchical switch, so growth_rate and ribosome_conc under acetate would show only a MILD (<15%) reduction relative to basal, scaling smoothly with substrate 'quality' rather than reflecting a repression-like step change.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, disconfirm(condition/acetate, wildtype/basal, growth_rate) would show |t|<2 or effect_pct<15%, i.e., a small graded difference rather than the predicted >=30% drop.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp-magnitude-only explanation): the apparent 'hierarchy' between basal and acetate growth is entirely mediated by ppGpp dosage (i.e., acetate simply triggers more stringent response, and clamping/removing ppGpp signaling eliminates the growth-rate gap), rather than reflecting substrate-specific pathway engagement.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival B is true, in the relA gene_knockout background the growth_rate gap between acetate and basal should COLLAPSE (effect_pct<10%, |t|<2), unlike H1 which predicts the gap persists (effect_pct>=? i.e. fold-change still <=0.7x) even without RelA-driven ppGpp synthesis.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's static fitted media conditions (basal=glucose-like, acetate) are valid proxies for 'preferred vs alternative carbon source' since no mid-run carbon-source switch is available in the envelope (uptake is a binary per-condition fit, not a continuous titration).

Catabolite repression / diauxie mechanisms (cAMP-CRP, PTS-mediated inducer exclusion) are assumed to be reflected indirectly through the fitted condition-specific kinetic/flux parameters even if not explicitly molecularly simulated gene-by-gene.

Cross-condition comparisons (basal vs acetate) are treated as a proxy for the preference hierarchy a single cell would show if offered both sugars simultaneously; we cannot simulate true simultaneous dual-sugar presence or a mid-run switch, so this is a between-condition (not within-run sequential) test.

relA knockout is used as the feasible interventional control for ppGpp-dependence; we assume RelA is the dominant ppGpp synthetase under amino-acid/carbon stringency in this model so its removal meaningfully perturbs stringent signaling.

Growth differences across conditions are assumed not to be dominated by simulation artifacts (e.g., FBA solver objective infeasibility) distinct from genuine biological substrate-quality effects; fba_objective will be checked as a sanity diagnostic but is not itself a claimed biological channel.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: Catabolite repression (diauxie) is implemented in this simulator as a ppGpp/stringent-response-mediated prioritization: when a preferred carbon source is available, cells entering a mixed/alternative-substrate condition show elevated ppGpp and reduced ribosome concentration relative to growth on the preferred substrate alone, reflecting a stringent-like reallocation away from growth machinery; this signature should be abolished when ppGpp synthesis is blocked (relA knockout), establishing that the model's substrate-prioritization behavior routes through the stringent response rather than being a pure enzyme-induction effect invisible to these channels.
drafts.h1: Shifting cells from a preferred static carbon condition (basal/glucose-like) to a non-preferred static carbon condition (acetate) produces a ppGpp increase (>=1.5-fold vs basal) and a ribosome_conc decrease (>=20%) consistent with stringent-response-mediated catabolite control, and this signature requires RelA (abolished or strongly attenuated in a relA gene_knockout on the same acetate condition).
drafts.h0: ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc on acetate are not significantly different from basal (Welch |t|<2), i.e. the model shows no stringent-response signature distinguishing preferred from non-preferred carbon conditions, or the signature persists unchanged in the relA knockout (indicating it is not RelA-dependent).

drafts.predicted_effect: Acetate vs basal: ppgpp_conc +50-100% (fold-change ~1.5-2.0x), ribosome_conc -20 to -35%, growth_rate reduced ~40-60% (consistent with slower acetate growth). In relA_knockout/acetate, the ppgpp_conc fold-change relative to relA_knockout/basal should collapse to <1.2x (near-null), i.e. effect attenuated by >=60% relative to the wildtype acetate-vs-basal effect.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, condition/acetate vs wildtype/basal, across seeds; reject H0 if two-sided |t|>=2 AND effect_pct >= 50%. Separately, Welch t of ppgpp_conc, gene_knockout(relA)/acetate vs condition/acetate; H1 requires this second comparison to show |t|>=2 in the direction of attenuation (knockout lower than wildtype-acetate), confirming RelA-dependence.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=50% for main effect; |t|>=2 for attenuation in knockout comparison

rivals.claim: Catabolite repression is implemented purely via enzyme/transporter induction logic (e.g. uptake flux switching) with no stringent-response involvement; ppGpp and ribosome_conc are unaffected by carbon source identity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: disconfirm(condition/acetate, wildtype/basal, ppgpp_conc) returns |t|<2 and small effect_pct, while growth_rate still differs strongly between conditions (showing the metabolic switch happens without a ppGpp signature).

rivals.claim: ppGpp/ribosome changes on acetate are a generic slow-growth artifact (growth-rate law coupling, independent of RelA or substrate-preference signaling) — any slow-growth condition would show the same shift regardless of RelA status.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA gene_knockout on acetate shows UNCHANGED ppgpp_conc elevation and ribosome_conc depression relative to wildtype/acetate (|t|<2 between knockout and wildtype on acetate), i.e. the effect persists without RelA, indicating it is growth-rate-law-driven rather than RelA-dependent signaling.

auxiliary_assumptions: The instrument's 'condition' perturbation with acetate as a static media setting is a valid proxy for the 'non-preferred/alternative sugar' arm, since mid-run carbon-source switching is not permitted in the envelope.
steady_state elongation model is used for all arms so that ppgpp_conc, ribosome_conc, and rela_conc channels are populated (these channels require steady-state charging per the instrument notes).

relA gene_knockout is assumed to abolish or strongly reduce RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis in the simulator's biochemical network (SpoT-mediated basal synthesis/degradation may remain, so full abolition is not expected — attenuation is the criterion, not zero).

Growth rate differences between acetate and basal are treated as an expected confound (acetate is a slower carbon source) rather than a construct to control for; the claim is about ppGpp/ribosome signature, not growth rate per se.
Seeds are isogenic stochastic replicates; cross-seed variance is assumed to reflect intrinsic noise, not condition-specific bias.

drafts.claim: Diauxie / carbon-source choice in this model is implemented as a binary glucose-uptake switch governed by catabolite repression, such that cells in a glucose-containing medium show glucose-dominant physiology (high growth rate, low ppGpp, high charged-tRNA) regardless of the presence of a second, poorer carbon source, because the simulator does not implement a graded preference but a static fitted-media condition per run. drafts.h0: ppGpp concentration and growth rate do not differ beyond replicate noise between basal and acetate conditions (Welch |t| < 2 on ppgpp_conc and on growth_rate across seeds).

drafts.claim: E. coli exposed to a mixed-sugar environment implements carbon catabolite repression: the presence of a preferred carbon state (modeled here via amino-acid/media richness as a proxy for a second substrate) suppresses stringent-response alarmone signaling and reallocates ribosome synthesis, so growth is dictated by a hierarchical 'choose-one-source-at-a-time' program rather than a blend of both. Operationally, this predicts that adding a second, richer nutrient input (an amino-acid shift that mimics a preferred co-substrate entering the medium) during growth on a single defined carbon source triggers a FAST, step-like rise in growth_rate and ribosome_conc and a step-like FALL in ppgpp_conc, consistent with a regulatory switch rather than a gradual additive blend of two independent growth programs.
drafts.h1: Introducing a preferred-substrate signal (amino_acid_shift onto minimal medium) causes a discrete, rapid (within 1 generation) upward shift in growth_rate and ribosome_conc and downward shift in ppgpp_conc, of magnitude >=25% change in growth_rate and >=30% drop in ppgpp_conc relative to the unshifted wildtype/basal reference — consistent with a hierarchical catabolite-repression-like switch.
drafts.h0: The shift produces no discrete step: growth_rate, ribosome_conc, and ppgpp_conc in the amino_acid_shift timeline do not differ from the wildtype/basal reference beyond replicate noise (|welch_t| < 2), i.e. the cell blends resources additively/gradually rather than switching.

Predict NOT a smooth/gradual blend but a discrete jump, reflected as bimodality coefficient BC>0.555 in the pooled pre/post growth_rate distribution across seeds.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, target (post-shift window) vs reference across seeds; reject H0 if two-sided |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates >=30% drop. Additionally require bimodality_bc (Sarle's BC) on pooled growth_rate values across the pre/post shift boundary to exceed 0.555 to support a discrete-switch interpretation rather than a continuous drift.
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t| < 2 for ppgpp_conc (no significant drop) OR the drop is <10%, OR growth_rate/ribosome_conc show no corresponding step (|welch_t|<2), OR bimodality_bc <= 0.555 (indicating a smooth gradual change, not a switch), H1 is refuted and the cell is better described as blending resources continuously.

test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=30% drop in ppgpp_conc

select_score.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
select_score.claim: E. coli's choice between two sugars is implemented as catabolite-repression-driven sequential use, and in this whole-cell model that mechanism is readable as a ppGpp/stringent-response-mediated growth-rate penalty when the preferred carbon source's uptake pathway is removed, forcing reliance on the alternative (lower-quality) substrate: knocking out the gene(s) needed for the preferred sugar's uptake (modeled here via a static media condition contrast, since the simulator does not support a true mixed-sugar switch) will drop growth rate and raise ppGpp relative to growth on the preferred substrate, mimicking the diauxic hierarchy.
select_score.h1: Loss of the preferred-sugar utilization gene (forcing metabolism onto the inferior static carbon condition) causes a substantial growth-rate decrease (>=25% drop) accompanied by a significant rise in ppgpp_conc (>=30% increase) relative to wildtype growth on the preferred (basal/glucose-like) condition, consistent with the stringent-response signature of a forced shift down the catabolite-repression hierarchy.
select_score.h0: Growth rate and ppgpp_conc on the inferior static carbon condition (with the uptake gene intact) do not differ significantly from wildtype on the preferred basal condition beyond replicate noise (|welch_t| < 2 for both channels).

hypothesis.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
hypothesis.claim: Carbon catabolite repression via the stringent/ppGpp-coupled regulatory axis causes E. coli to prioritize one sugar over a second, alternative carbon source by suppressing growth-rate contribution and shifting physiology toward a single-substrate-like state even when a second sugar is nominally available — i.e., the simulated 'choice' manifests as the mixed condition behaving statistically like the preferred-sugar-only condition rather than an intermediate/blended state. Since this simulator exposes only static fitted media conditions (no true simultaneous two-sugar mixed condition), we operationalize 'choice between two sugars' as comparing a glucose-only basal condition against an alternative static carbon condition (acetate) and testing whether physiological state under acetate shows hallmarks of catabolite-repression-like deprioritization (elevated ppGpp, reduced growth rate, reduced ribosome concentration) relative to glucose — consistent with glucose being the preferred/chosen substrate when both would be present.
hypothesis.h1: Growth rate, ribosome concentration, and ppGpp concentration under the non-preferred static carbon condition (acetate) differ from glucose/basal in the direction predicted by a hierarchical-preference (catabolite repression) model: acetate condition shows lower growth_rate (>=40% reduction), lower ribosome_conc (>=25% reduction), and higher ppgpp_conc (>=50% increase) relative to basal, reflecting that cells deprioritize the poorer substrate in a manner consistent with a chosen hierarchy rather than symmetric substrate use.
hypothesis.h0: There is no systematic difference in growth_rate, ribosome_conc, or ppgpp_conc between basal (glucose) and acetate conditions beyond replicate noise — i.e., the simulator's static media-fitting treats alternative carbon sources as physiologically interchangeable rather than reflecting a preference hierarchy.

Magnitude: growth_rate fold-change ~0.5-0.6x (40-50% reduction), ribosome_conc fold-change ~0.7-0.75x (25-30% reduction), ppgpp_conc fold-change ~1.5-2x (50-100% increase), each with |Welch t| >= 2 across seeds.

falsifier.refuting_result: If ppgpp_conc Welch |t| < 2 (no significant elevation) OR growth_rate does not drop by at least ~40% with |t|>=2, the data refute the hierarchical-preference/catabolite-repression signature and support the interchangeable-substrate null.

rivals.claim: Rival A (pure growth-capacity rival): Acetate simply supports slower growth due to lower ATP yield per carbon, with NO distinct stringent-response/ppGpp signature — growth_rate drops but ppgpp_conc stays statistically unchanged from basal, i.e., it's a bioenergetic limitation, not a regulatory 'choice' hierarchy.
rivals.distinguishing_result: growth_rate Welch |t|>=2 showing reduction, but ppgpp_conc Welch |t| < 2 (no significant ppGpp elevation) in condition/acetate vs wildtype/basal.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ribosome-allocation-independent rival): Any apparent ppGpp/ribosome covariation under acetate is driven by a RelA-independent pathway (e.g., SpoT basal turnover or general slow-growth scaling) rather than a stringent-response 'preference' mechanism; knocking out relA would NOT abolish the ppGpp elevation or close the growth-rate gap.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In gene_knockout/relA (acetate condition), ppgpp_conc elevation vs basal persists (Welch |t|>=2, similar effect_pct to wildtype), showing the signal is RelA-independent.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's static 'acetate' fitted condition is a valid stand-in for the physiological state a cell would adopt on the non-preferred/second sugar in a real two-sugar mixture, even though no true simultaneous mixed-sugar condition exists in the envelope.

ppGpp and ribosome concentration readouts are recorded under steady-state charging for both conditions (no kinetic-charging-only artifacts), so basal and acetate are measured on the same channel semantics.

Growth-rate and ppGpp differences across conditions are attributable to media-fitting physiology rather than numerical/solver artifacts (fba_objective used only as a diagnostic sanity check, not as evidence).

Seed-to-seed stochastic variation under isogenic replicates is small enough that 4-8 seeds give adequate power to detect the predicted fold-changes (checked post hoc via power_mde if initial test is ambiguous).

RelA knockout removes the dominant RelA-dependent synthesis arm of ppGpp induction in this model; residual SpoT-mediated synthesis/hydrolysis is treated as a separate, not confounding, mechanism for this test's purposes.

hypothesis.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
hypothesis.claim: Carbon catabolite repression via the stringent/ppGpp-coupled regulatory axis causes E. coli to prioritize one carbon source over a less-preferred one by suppressing the growth-rate and translational-machinery signature that would otherwise be used on the non-preferred substrate. Because the instrument cannot represent two substrates present simultaneously (uptake is a binary condition switch, not a mixture), 'choice' is operationalized as the reproducible, mean-level physiological divergence (growth_rate, ribosome_conc, ppgpp_conc) between the preferred (basal) and non-preferred (acetate) static conditions, and the claim is restricted to population-mean differences ACROSS independent seeds (biological/parametric replicates of the same condition), NOT to within-population single-cell asynchrony, which this instrument's seed mechanism cannot resolve (per r1.1).
hypothesis.h1: Across seeds, the mean growth_rate, ribosome_conc, and ppgpp_conc differ reproducibly between basal and acetate static conditions, with acetate showing growth_rate reduced by >=40%, ppgpp_conc elevated by >=50%, and ribosome_conc reduced by >=25% relative to basal, and this mean-level shift is causally dependent on ppGpp signaling (collapses under relA knockout and under direct ppGpp clamp), consistent with stringent-response-mediated carbon-source prioritization rather than a passive metabolic-bottleneck artifact.
hypothesis.h0: There is no reproducible mean difference in growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, and ribosome_conc between basal and acetate conditions beyond replicate noise (Welch |t|<2 on growth_rate), OR the observed mean difference persists unchanged under relA knockout and ppGpp clamp (i.e., is not ppGpp-dependent), indicating the simulator does not encode an active ppGpp-mediated substrate-preference mechanism at this level.

Magnitude: growth_rate fold-change ~0.5-0.6x (>=40% reduction), ppgpp_conc fold-change ~1.5-2x (>=50% elevation), ribosome_conc fold-change ~0.70-0.75x (>=25% reduction), each Welch |t|>=2 across 6 seeds. The relA-knockout and ppGpp-clamp controls are predicted to shrink the growth_rate/ribosome_conc gap vs basal by >=50% (i.e., |t|<2 or effect_pct within 20% of basal), evidencing causal ppGpp-dependence.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of per-seed mean growth_rate across seeds, acetate vs basal; reject H0 (support H1) if |t|>=2 AND effect_pct <= -40% (acetate lower); require ppgpp_conc |t|>=2 with effect_pct>=+50% and ribosome_conc |t|>=2 with effect_pct<=-25% as corroborating mean-level channels; additionally require the relA_knockout/acetate vs wildtype/basal comparison on growth_rate to show |t|<2 (gap collapses) to support ppGpp-causal dependence over a pure metabolic-bottleneck account
falsifier.refuting_result: If growth_rate |t|<2, or effect_pct does not reach -40%, or ppgpp_conc/ribosome_conc show no concordant significant shift, the mean-level preference signature is not supported and H0 stands; separately, if relA_knockout/acetate vs wildtype/basal on growth_rate remains |t|>=2 with a gap similar to wildtype/acetate vs wildtype/basal (i.e., removing relA does not shrink the gap), ppGpp-dependence is refuted even if the basal-vs-acetate difference itself holds

rivals.claim: The growth_rate/ppGpp/ribosome differences between basal and acetate are driven purely by generic metabolic/FBA flux limitations of acetate catabolism (a stoichiometric/kinetic bottleneck), not by an active ppGpp-signaling regulatory decision.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA_knockout on acetate still shows growth_rate and ppgpp_conc shifted from basal by a similar magnitude as wildtype/acetate (|t|>=2, comparable effect_pct), i.e. removing RelA does not collapse the gap, the effect is metabolic-bottleneck-driven, not ppGpp-signaling-driven.

rivals.claim: The ribosome_conc/growth_rate shift is a passive consequence of reduced carbon flux (slower growth mechanically yields fewer ribosomes via growth-rate-dependent synthesis scaling) rather than active ppGpp-mediated prioritization -- i.e., epiphenomenal co-variation with no causal ppGpp mediation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If clamping ppgpp_conc to basal-like levels on acetate fails to restore ribosome_conc/growth_rate toward basal (acetate/ppgpp_clamp vs wildtype/basal remains |t|>=2, large effect_pct), passive co-variation is supported over active ppGpp causation.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's 'condition' perturbation (basal vs acetate) is an adequate proxy for 'two sugars in the same flask' since the envelope disallows a true simultaneous two-substrate or mid-run carbon-source switch (uptake is binary); we treat the preferred/non-preferred static conditions as representing the two ends of a catabolite-repression choice rather than literal co-presence.

Seeds are independent stochastic/parametric replicates of the SAME condition (population-level simulation runs), not individual cells within one shared population; the hypothesis and all statistics are about cross-seed MEAN differences, not within-population single-cell dispersion/asynchrony, which this instrument cannot resolve (explicit scope limitation, not pursued further).

relA knockout is assumed to meaningfully attenuate ppGpp synthesis in the charging model used; if relA is not mechanistically wired to ppgpp_conc in this build, the discriminating control will be uninformative and should be logged as a capability gap rather than taken as evidence for either rival.

n=6 seeds is assumed sufficient to detect a >=40% growth_rate mean effect via Welch t given expected inter-seed CV in this simulator; if replicate noise is much larger than expected, power may be insufficient (a scope limitation, not pursued further here).

We are NOT modeling an explicit decision circuit (e.g., a PTS/cAMP-CRP two-gene switch) because no such 'choice' channel exists in the instrument; the claim is restricted to the downstream physiological signature (growth/ribosome/ppGpp triad), the operationalizable proxy for 'preference' in this simulator.

objection_ledger.issue: The model's 'seeds' most likely instantiate independent whole-population (bulk) simulation runs with randomized initial/parameter draws, not individual cells within one shared population. The claim is about per-cell asynchrony WITHIN a population, but the operationalization pools across seeds (separate simulation replicates), which conflates population-replicate variance with single-cell heterogeneity.

The decision_rule combines a Welch t-test (designed to detect a difference in MEANS) with a claim about DISPERSION (CV, variance). A Welch t-test on 'growth_rate at a fixed post-shift timepoint' tests whether shift and basal groups have different average growth_rate, not whether the shift group is more dispersed. As written it's unclear whether |welch_t|>=2 on means is being used as a proxy for a variance claim, which could pass or fail independently of whether CV truly differs. The test for the core asynchrony claim should be a variance-comparison statistic (e.g., Levene's test or F-test on variances, or a direct CV ratio with a bootstrap CI) rather than a t-test on means.

The user's question is about whether individual CELLS within a population switch synchronously. The design operationalizes this via dispersion ACROSS INDEPENDENT SEEDS (separate simulator runs), which is a proxy for run-to-run stochastic variability, not within-population cell-to-cell heterogeneity. A simulator seed likely represents a single lineage trajectory per run, so high across-seed CV shows that replicate population-average trajectories differ from each other, which is a distinct claim from 'not all cells switch at the same time within one population.' The hypothesis should either justify why across-seed dispersion is a valid stand-in for within-population asynchrony, or reframe the claim/falsifier explicitly as being about population-average switch timing variability (not single-cell synchrony).

The decision rule mixes 'Primary: BC>0.555' with a separate 'Secondary/confirmatory' welch test, but the falsifier/refuting_result section requires BOTH BC<=0.555 AND welch_t<2 to refute H1. This leaves an ambiguous middle zone (e.g., BC>0.555 but welch_t<2, or BC<=0.555 but welch_t>=2) where neither H1 nor H0 is clearly declared, weakening the risky prohibition.

Rival B's discriminator relies on comparing dispersion/BC of growth_rate between wildtype and relA-knockout under the same shift — but growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are mechanistically coupled in the stringent response, so if relA knockout simply dampens ppGpp induction globally (shifting the mean), it could also mechanically reduce growth_rate variance for reasons other than 'turning off the asynchrony-generating mechanism' (e.g. simply flattening the whole dynamic range so there's less to be variable about). The design doesn't separate 'reduced dispersion because synchrony restored' from 'reduced dispersion because the whole response is suppressed/flattened.'

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: Carbon catabolite repression via the stringent/ppGpp-coupled regulatory axis causes E. coli to prioritize one sugar over a second by suppressing growth-rate contribution from the non-preferred pathway until the preferred substrate is scarce; operationally, this manifests as a growth-rate and ppGpp signature that differs between a glucose-containing medium and an alternative-carbon medium, with the glucose condition showing higher growth rate and lower ppGpp (less stringent signaling) than a poorer, non-preferred carbon source, because the cell is NOT co-limited by both substrates simultaneously but rather runs a sequential, hierarchical program keyed to ppGpp/stringent-response state.

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc / ppgpp_conc under relA knockout
operational_defs.measure: ppGpp concentration and growth rate in a relA gene_knockout under acetate vs basal, to test whether the ppGpp gap collapses when RelA is removed

drafts.predicted_effect: Growth rate on basal (glucose) is predicted to exceed growth rate on acetate by >=2-fold (e.g., ~1.0-1.2 /h basal vs ~0.3-0.5 /h acetate). Concomitantly, ppgpp_conc on acetate is predicted to exceed ppgpp_conc on basal by >=1.5-fold, reflecting stronger stringent-response engagement on the poorer carbon source. In a relA knockout, this ppGpp gap between acetate and basal should shrink toward near-equivalence (<1.2-fold), while the growth-rate gap persists (since RelA removal does not restore acetate's intrinsic metabolic ceiling), isolating the ppGpp signal as RelA-dependent rather than a secondary consequence of growth rate alone.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, acetate vs basal across seeds; reject H0 (support hierarchical/stringent signature) if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates acetate higher by >=50%. Refute H1 if |welch_t|<2 or effect_pct <50% (no meaningful stringent-response differential).
falsifier.refuting_result: ppgpp_conc on acetate is statistically indistinguishable from basal (|welch_t|<2) or the fold-difference is <1.5x, showing no stringent-response-based hierarchy signature between the two carbon conditions.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=50%

rivals.claim: The growth-rate/ppGpp difference is purely a generic poor-carbon-source stress response unrelated to any sugar-sugar choice mechanism — i.e., any nutrient-poor static condition (not just acetate vs glucose specifically) would show the same ppGpp elevation, so this is not evidence of hierarchical PRIORITIZATION between two sugars but just a single-substrate quality effect.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the relA knockout control would show the SAME growth-rate gap AND the ppGpp gap would not be particularly RelA-dependent (i.e., removing RelA would not collapse the ppGpp differential), because the effect would stem from generic metabolic flux limitation rather than stringent-response signaling specifically keyed to substrate hierarchy.

rivals.claim: tRNA charging (fraction_trna_charged) directly sets growth rate via translation efficiency, with ppGpp merely a passive co-mover/readout of charging state rather than a causal enforcer of the hierarchy — i.e., ppGpp and growth rate are collinear because both depend on charged-tRNA pools, not because ppGpp enforces repression.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, fraction_trna_charged would track ppgpp_conc tightly across conditions (both moving together), and the relA knockout would NOT decouple ppGpp from charging — but critically, since relA knockout removes ppGpp SYNTHESIS (not charging-dependent regulation), if the growth-rate/ppGpp relationship were purely charging-driven, deleting relA would leave the growth-rate gap between acetate and basal UNCHANGED while still abolishing the ppGpp differential, which would actually be consistent with this rival too — the key distinguishing test is whether ppGpp given unprodu directly causes feedback onto growth (not observable here) vs is epiphenomenal; we treat the relA-knockout growth-rate persistence as the operational signature of this rival being correct about ppGpp's non-causal role in growth-rate determination specifically.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: E. coli's choice between two sugars in a mixed-substrate flask is mediated by catabolite repression / stringent-response coupling: the model's available 'condition' media (which encode carbon-source identity rather than true simultaneous mixtures) will show that a preferred, high-growth-rate carbon source (basal/glucose-equivalent) drives LOW ppGpp and HIGH growth rate, while a poorer, alternative carbon source (acetate) drives HIGH ppGpp and LOW growth rate — the ppGpp/growth-rate axis is the operational proxy for 'which sugar wins', since the simulator cannot run a true simultaneous two-sugar mixture (no mid-run carbon-source switch; uptake is a binary per-condition switch). Because the instrument cannot literally mix two sugars in one run, the diauxie-like preference hierarchy is operationalized as a STATIC cross-condition comparison across the available static-only carbon conditions, predicting a graded, monotonic ordering of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across conditions that mirrors the known preference hierarchy (glucose/basal > succinate/malate/fumarate > acetate), with a fold-change in growth_rate of >=2x and in ppgpp_conc of >=1.5x between the best (basal) and worst (acetate) condition.
drafts.h1: Across the static media conditions available (basal, acetate, fumarate, malate, succinate), growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are inversely and monotonically related to carbon-source quality, reproducing the known catabolite-repression preference hierarchy: basal (glucose-like) yields highest growth_rate/lowest ppgpp_conc, acetate yields lowest growth_rate/highest ppgpp_conc, with TCA-cycle intermediates (succinate, malate, fumarate) intermediate.
drafts.h0: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc do not differ systematically across these static carbon conditions (no monotonic ordering); any differences are within replicate noise (|welch_t| < 2 for basal vs acetate) and show no significant slope when regressed against an a priori quality ranking of the conditions.

operational_defs.construct: carbon source preference / catabolite repression hierarchy
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel across static conditions
operational_defs.measure: mean growth_rate (1/h) per condition, averaged over seeds/generations

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc channel across static conditions
operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc (uM) per condition, averaged over seeds/generations

operational_defs.observable: ordinal quality score assigned to each condition (basal=4 (best), succinate/malate/fumarate=2, acetate=1 (worst))
operational_defs.measure: OLS slope of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) vs this ordinal score across the 5 conditions

drafts.predicted_effect: Monotonic decreasing relationship: growth_rate drops from basal to acetate by >=2-fold (e.g. ~0.8-1.0 /h on basal to <=0.4/h on acetate), while ppgpp_conc rises by >=1.5-fold over the same ordering (e.g. ~20uM basal to >=30uM acetate); OLS slope of growth_rate on the ordinal quality score should be positive with R^2>=0.6, and slope of ppgpp_conc on the same score should be negative with R^2>=0.6.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of growth_rate, acetate vs basal, across seeds; reject H0 if |t|>=2 AND effect direction matches prediction (acetate lower). Separately, OLS slope of growth_rate on the ordinal quality score across all 5 conditions; reject H0 if slope 95% CI excludes 0 and is positive.
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t| < 2 for acetate vs basal growth_rate, OR the OLS slope CI includes 0 (no monotonic trend across the 5 conditions), H1 is refuted: the simulator shows no catabolite-repression-like preference hierarchy at the growth_rate/ppgpp level.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for acetate vs basal on growth_rate; direction acetate<basal

rivals.claim: Rival A: differences across conditions are driven purely by generic metabolic/FBA flux limitations (poorer carbon sources simply have lower max flux), NOT by a ppGpp-mediated regulatory 'choice' mechanism — i.e. it's a passive capacity effect, not an active stringent-response signal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If ppgpp_conc does NOT rise significantly on acetate relative to basal (|welch_t|<2) even though growth_rate clearly drops, that supports Rival A: growth differs but the alarmone signal that would indicate active regulatory sensing of carbon quality is flat.

rivals.claim: Rival B: any growth_rate/ppgpp_conc differences across conditions are an artifact of RelA/SpoT module parameterization per condition rather than a real carbon-quality signal — knocking out relA (via a relA gene_knockout background) should abolish the ppGpp rise on acetate if ppGpp synthesis genuinely depends on the stringent pathway responding to nutrient quality, but if growth_rate differences persist unchanged, the effect is ppGpp-independent.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA knockout on acetate still shows the same growth_rate deficit vs basal (no rescue) but ppgpp_conc is flattened/abolished, this confirms ppGpp is a consequence not a driver of the growth choice — supporting Rival B over a causal stringent-response-driven preference mechanism.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's binary per-condition carbon-source identity is an adequate proxy for 'which sugar a cell would choose' since true simultaneous dual-sugar mixtures / mid-run carbon switches are outside the validated envelope.
The ordinal quality ranking (basal > succinate/malate/fumarate > acetate) reflects accepted empirical catabolite-repression hierarchies and is assigned a priori, not fit post hoc.

ppGpp and growth_rate channels are read under steady-state charging (since kinetic charging requires the RelA/SpoT module explicitly on); if the module is off, ppgpp_conc/rela_conc reflect the steady-state approximation, not dynamic stringent-response kinetics.

Seed-to-seed stochastic noise within a condition is small relative to between-condition differences; 6 seeds/3 generations is sufficient replicate power for the Welch test at the predicted effect sizes.
relA knockout is assumed to abolish/attenuate RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis in this model background; downstream SpoT-mediated basal synthesis may still produce residual ppGpp.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: E. coli in a mixed-sugar flask enforces diauxie-like carbon prioritization via the stringent/ppGpp-ribosome allocation axis: when glucose uptake is active, the simulated regulatory state suppresses alternative-sugar catabolic commitment by keeping ppGpp low and ribosome synthesis high (glucose-favoring physiology), and this allocation state is causally dependent on ppGpp signaling rather than being a passive byproduct of growth rate alone.
drafts.h1: Across static media conditions representing glucose-replete vs glucose-poor/alternative-carbon states, ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc shift in a coordinated, condition-dependent manner consistent with hierarchical carbon prioritization (low ppGpp + high ribosome_conc on glucose/basal; higher ppGpp + lower ribosome_conc on the non-preferred static carbon source such as acetate), and this shift requires an intact ppGpp synthesis pathway (relA-dependent), not just the growth-rate difference between conditions.
drafts.h0: ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc do not differ beyond replicate noise between basal (glucose) and acetate conditions, OR any difference that does appear persists unchanged when relA is knocked out (i.e., the shift is relA-independent and thus not evidence of an active stringent-response-mediated prioritization mechanism).

operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc (uM) and mean ribosome_conc (uM) per seed, compared across the two static conditions

operational_defs.construct: stringent-response dependence of the prioritization signal
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channels under gene_knockout(relA)/acetate vs wildtype/acetate

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: ppgpp_conc is higher on acetate than on basal glucose (predicted +40% to +100% fold-change), ribosome_conc is lower on acetate (predicted -20% to -40%), and growth_rate is lower on acetate (~-30% to -50%), consistent with reallocation away from ribosome synthesis under the less-preferred carbon source. This basal-vs-acetate ppGpp shift should be substantially attenuated (relative effect_pct shrinks by at least half, or welch_t drops below 2) in the relA knockout background, demonstrating causal dependence on the stringent pathway rather than being a pure growth-rate artifact.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of ppgpp_conc, condition/acetate vs wildtype/basal, across seeds; reject H0 if two-sided |welch_t|>=2. Then run the same disconfirm on gene_knockout(relA)/acetate vs gene_knockout(relA)/basal; H1 requires this second |welch_t| to be clearly smaller (or <2) than the first, showing relA-dependence.
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t|<2 for basal vs acetate ppgpp_conc (no detectable shift), OR if the relA-knockout basal-vs-acetate contrast shows an equally large or larger |welch_t| than wildtype (shift persists without relA), H1 is refuted.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for the wildtype contrast; relA-knockout contrast must show |t|<2 or a markedly reduced effect_pct to support relA-dependence

rivals.claim: Rival A (passive growth-rate coupling): ppGpp and ribosome_conc differences between basal and acetate are simply a passive consequence of the slower growth rate on acetate (growth-rate-dependent ribosome scaling, the classic Scott/Hwa law), with no distinguishable causal role for active relA-driven stringent signaling in enforcing the shift.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If the relA knockout leaves the ppgpp_conc/ribosome_conc basal-vs-acetate contrast essentially unchanged in magnitude (|welch_t| still >=2, effect_pct similar to wildtype) while growth_rate differences persist, this supports Rival A: the correlation is growth-rate-driven, not relA-dependent.

rivals.claim: Rival B (no regulatory differentiation in this simulator): the model's metabolic/regulatory network does not implement meaningful condition-dependent ppGpp or ribosome regulation at all — any apparent basal-vs-acetate difference is noise or an artifact of FBA objective switching rather than biological signaling.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If |welch_t|<2 for ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc between basal and acetate in wildtype (no detectable difference beyond replicate noise), this supports Rival B regardless of the relA knockout result.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's static 'acetate' condition is a valid proxy for a non-preferred/slow-growth carbon source relative to basal glucose, even though a live mid-run glucose-to-acetate switch is not permitted (static_only_carbon).

Replicate-to-replicate (seed) variability in ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc is small enough relative to the condition effect that 6 seeds over 3 generations gives adequate power; this is checked qualitatively via per-seed spread rather than a formal pre-registered power analysis.

relA deletion is mechanistically simulated in this platform's gene_knockout pathway (i.e., it actually removes ppGpp synthesis capacity) rather than being a no-op; this is treated as an assumption to be confirmed by inspecting whether ppgpp_conc drops substantially in the relA knockout vs wildtype at baseline.

The question 'how bacteria choose between two sugars' is operationalized here as a regulatory-state proxy (ppGpp/ribosome allocation under glucose vs a non-preferred static carbon source) rather than a literal two-sugar-in-one-flask competition, since the instrument only supports single static media conditions, not simultaneous dual-sugar provisioning.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: Carbon catabolite repression (CCR) via the stringent/cAMP-CRP-coupled regulatory axis causes E. coli to prioritize a preferred carbon source over a secondary one, and this mechanistic commitment is reflected in a stringent-response signature (ppGpp/RelA elevation) that differs between a preferred-substrate condition and an alternative-substrate condition even though the cell never runs both simultaneously in this simulator. Since the instrument does not expose a two-sugar mixed-carbon condition or diauxic switch directly, the operational proxy for 'choice' is: growth-rate and stringent-response channels differ systematically and reproducibly across single-carbon static conditions (basal/glucose-like vs acetate), consistent with the known asymmetry in catabolic efficiency that underlies CCR-driven sequential use. H1: the acetate (non-preferred, slow, more gluconeogenic) condition shows significantly lower growth_rate and significantly higher ppgpp_conc than basal, reflecting the same regulatory logic (ppGpp-mediated resource reallocation away from growth) that in vivo produces diauxie and sugar preference.
drafts.h1: Growth on acetate (a slower, non-preferred carbon source) induces a stringent-response state (elevated ppgpp_conc, reduced ribosome_conc, reduced growth_rate) relative to basal, by a magnitude consistent with regulatory deprioritization rather than mere stoichiometric slowdown: growth_rate drops by >=40% and ppgpp_conc rises by >=50% vs basal.
drafts.h0: Acetate and basal conditions produce statistically indistinguishable ppgpp_conc and growth_rate (within replicate noise), i.e. the simulator shows no regulatory/stringent-response signature distinguishing a poor vs preferred carbon source — any growth difference is not accompanied by the predicted stringent-response shift.

rivals.claim: Pure stoichiometric/metabolic-flux limitation: acetate growth is slower simply because of lower ATP/carbon yield via the glyoxylate/TCA route, with no distinct ppGpp-mediated regulatory signature -- the ribosome/ppGpp changes are passive consequences of slower flux, not an active 'choice' mechanism.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, a relA gene_knockout under acetate would show the SAME growth_rate reduction vs basal as wildtype (ppGpp machinery is irrelevant to the slowdown), i.e. growth_rate in relA_KO/acetate is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/acetate (Welch |t|<2).

rivals.claim: Ribosome-allocation economics alone (growth-rate-dependent ribosome concentration per Scott/Hwa scaling) explains the ppGpp/ribosome shift without any CCR-specific 'preference' logic -- i.e. any slow-growth condition (not just acetate specifically) would show the same signature, so this is a generic growth-law effect, not carbon-source choice.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the ppgpp_conc vs growth_rate relationship across MULTIPLE static conditions (basal, acetate, plus other available conditions) would fall on a single monotonic curve (slope_ci excludes 0, good fit) with acetate being just one point on that curve -- no acetate-specific discontinuity beyond what growth rate predicts.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's 'condition' perturbation (basal vs acetate) is a valid proxy for preferred-vs-non-preferred carbon source quality, since the instrument cannot run a true mixed two-sugar diauxic-shift experiment (glucose uptake is a binary switch and carbon-source mid-run switching is disallowed).

ppgpp_conc and growth_rate are recorded under steady-state charging for both conditions (no kinetic ppGpp module needed), so values are comparable across conditions without switching elongation_model.
relA gene_knockout is assumed to meaningfully attenuate ppGpp synthesis in the model (mechanistic KO effect is checked downstream, not assumed to be guaranteed).
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation within a condition is small enough that 6 seeds give adequate power to detect a >=40-50% effect (to be confirmed via power_mde if the initial test is ambiguous).

We are NOT claiming the simulator reproduces an explicit sequential diauxic switch in one run; the claim is restricted to the regulatory-signature asymmetry between single-carbon conditions as a proxy for the choice mechanism.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: Carbon catabolite repression via the stringent/ppGpp-coupled regulatory axis means that when glucose is present alongside a second, less-preferred carbon source, cells suppress alternative-sugar catabolism until glucose is exhausted — operationally, growth rate and ppGpp dynamics under a glucose+acetate mixed condition will closely track the glucose-only (basal) condition rather than an intermediate blend, because acetate utilization genes stay repressed while glucose lasts. This is a population-level claim: across replicate seeds, the mixed condition's growth-rate trajectory should be statistically indistinguishable from glucose-only until a late shift, not an averaged intermediate rate.
drafts.h1: Under mixed glucose+acetate media, instantaneous growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories resemble the glucose-only (basal) condition (within noise) rather than an intermediate between basal and acetate-only, reflecting diauxic repression of acetate catabolism while glucose is present.
drafts.h0: Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc under mixed glucose+acetate media are statistically indistinguishable from a simple intermediate/blend of the basal and acetate-only reference conditions (no preferential suppression), consistent with co-utilization rather than hierarchical choice.

falsifier.refuting_result: Welch t >=2 with mixed-condition growth_rate landing near the basal/acetate_only average (effect_pct ~40-60% below basal) rather than within ~10% of basal, indicating co-utilization/blending rather than repression-driven preference
