rivals.claim: Co-utilization: cells simultaneously metabolize glucose and acetate at reduced individual rates, producing a true intermediate growth rate and ppGpp level (no hierarchical repression).
rivals.distinguishing_result: Mixed-condition growth_rate and ppgpp_conc sit near the arithmetic mean of basal and acetate_only values across all generations, with no late-generation inflection in growth_rate.

rivals.claim: ppGpp-independent catabolite repression: the preference for glucose is enforced by a transcription-factor-level mechanism (e.g. CRP/cAMP-like regulation) rather than the stringent/ppGpp pathway, so clamping ppGpp should NOT abolish the glucose-preference signature in growth_rate.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the ppgpp_conc clamp control (ppGpp held at basal multiple), mixed-condition growth_rate still resembles basal glucose-only behavior rather than shifting toward the blend, showing the preference is ppGpp-independent.

auxiliary_assumptions: The instrument's 'condition' perturbation supports a fitted mixed glucose+acetate media condition (static, not a mid-run switch) distinct from the two static_only_carbon pure conditions; if not available in the validated envelope, the mixed condition is approximated as the closest available static mixed-media fit.
Acetate uptake/catabolism genes are mechanistically represented in the model such that an acetate-only condition yields slower growth than glucose-only, consistent with known E. coli physiology.
Within-generation stochastic noise across seeds is small enough (CV<15%) that a 10% deviation from basal is detectable at n=6 seeds.

The diauxic shift timing (glucose exhaustion then acetate uptake) is not required to be dynamically resolved within 3 generations under a static 'condition' fit; this design tests the steady preference signature, not the shift kinetics (a true shift would require a timeline perturbation, treated as future work).

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: E. coli cells facing two sugars prioritize one via the stringent response/ppGpp-linked regulatory axis: the simulator's only available carbon-source axis is the static per-condition media (glucose vs. an alternative like acetate), so 'choosing' is operationalized as the growth-rate and ppGpp signature differing sharply and predictably between a glucose-basal condition and an alternative-carbon condition, reflecting the known hierarchy (glucose preferred, acetate/alternative only used when glucose is absent). H1: growth on the preferred (glucose/basal) condition is faster and ppGpp lower than on the non-preferred (acetate) condition, by a large, reproducible margin consistent with catabolite-hierarchy physiology, not just noise.
drafts.h1: Across seeds, wildtype cells in basal (glucose) condition show significantly higher growth_rate and significantly lower ppgpp_conc than wildtype cells in the acetate condition, with effect sizes exceeding replicate noise (|welch_t|>=2 on both channels).
drafts.h0: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc distributions in basal vs acetate conditions are statistically indistinguishable (|welch_t|<2 on both channels), i.e. the simulated 'choice' between carbon conditions produces no detectable physiological signature.

operational_defs.construct: preference for glucose over acetate (catabolite hierarchy)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel compared between basal and acetate static conditions
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of per-seed growth_rate, basal vs acetate

operational_defs.construct: stringent/stress signature when forced onto the non-preferred, poorer carbon source
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc channel compared between basal and acetate
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of per-seed ppgpp_conc, basal vs acetate

operational_defs.construct: ribosome allocation consistent with growth-rate difference (rules out ppGpp clamp artifact)
operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel under a ppgpp_conc clamp vs wildtype basal
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of ribosome_conc, ppgpp clamp vs wildtype basal

drafts.predicted_effect: Growth rate on basal (glucose) is ~2-3x higher than on acetate (e.g. ~0.9 /h vs ~0.3 /h, fold-change ~3); ppgpp_conc on acetate is ~1.5-2x higher than on basal (consistent with stringent-response activation on the poorer carbon source). Both differences should give |welch_t|>=2 across 6 seeds.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of per-seed growth_rate, acetate vs basal wildtype across 6 seeds; reject H0 (support H1) if |welch_t|>=2 with acetate growth_rate lower; additionally require |welch_t|>=2 on ppgpp_conc (acetate higher) as a co-confirmation
falsifier.refuting_result: growth_rate and/or ppgpp_conc differences between acetate and basal are not significant (|welch_t|<2), indicating the simulator does not encode a detectable catabolite-hierarchy / stringent-response signature distinguishing the two static carbon conditions

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |welch_t|>=2 on growth_rate AND on ppgpp_conc

rivals.claim: Any growth-rate difference between basal and acetate is purely a generic 'poor carbon source' slow-growth effect unrelated to a ppGpp-mediated regulatory 'choice' mechanism — i.e. growth is slower on acetate simply because less ATP/precursor flux is available (a stoichiometric/FBA constraint), not because of an active stringent-response hierarchy signal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If ppgpp_conc does NOT rise on acetate relative to basal (|welch_t|<2 on ppgpp_conc) despite growth_rate being significantly lower, this favors the purely-metabolic-constraint rival over the stringent-response-hierarchy claim.

rivals.claim: The apparent 'ppGpp signature' is actually a side effect of ribosome under-allocation/division stress on acetate rather than a cause of the slow growth — i.e. ppGpp is a downstream readout, not a regulatory driver of the carbon preference.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Clamping ppgpp_conc to the basal (low) multiple while running the cell on acetate (ppgpp_conc perturbation/acetate) and checking whether growth_rate still drops to the same low acetate level: if growth_rate recovers toward basal levels despite the clamp, ppGpp is causal; if growth_rate stays low regardless of the clamp, ppGpp is merely a correlate and the metabolic-constraint rival is favored.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-condition static media fitting (basal vs acetate) is the best available proxy for 'two sugars in the same flask' since a mid-run carbon-source switch and glucose dosing are not supported in the envelope; we treat condition-level comparison as the operationalization of sugar preference/hierarchy rather than a true diauxic time-course.
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation (intrinsic noise) is assumed small relative to the condition effect; if not, the welch_disconfirm test will show this directly via per-seed spread.
ppGpp and ribosome channels are read under steady-state charging (kinetic module off) for this design, consistent with channel availability notes.
We assume 4 generations is sufficient for growth_rate and ppgpp_conc to reach a stable per-seed average without requiring lethality/division-rate tracking.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: E. coli given simultaneous access to glucose and a second, less-preferred carbon source (acetate) exhibits catabolite-repression-mediated carbon hierarchy: growth, ribosome allocation, and the stringent response are set by glucose signaling, not by the secondary substrate, so acetate media produces a markedly different physiological operating point (slower growth, higher ppGpp, lower ribosome concentration) than glucose/basal, and this hierarchy is causally linked to the stringent-response (ppGpp) machinery rather than being a passive side-effect of slow growth.
drafts.h1: Across seeds, the acetate-only condition produces a stable, reproducible physiological state that differs from basal (glucose) on growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, and ribosome_conc in the direction predicted by hierarchical catabolite control (lower growth_rate, higher ppgpp_conc, lower ribosome_conc), and this hierarchy state is causally dependent on an intact ppGpp/RelA stringent-response pathway: removing relA (rela gene_knockout) collapses or strongly attenuates the ppGpp difference between acetate and basal, decoupling the two channels.
drafts.h0: Acetate vs basal media produce no reliable difference in growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, and ribosome_conc beyond replicate noise (|welch_t|<2 on each channel), OR any observed difference persists unchanged after relA knockout (i.e., the hierarchy signal is relA-independent, consistent with growth-rate-driven passive coupling rather than an active stringent-response mechanism).

operational_defs.construct: carbon source preference / catabolite repression state
operational_defs.observable: condition channel: basal (glucose) vs acetate (static media condition)
operational_defs.measure: categorical condition label driving steady-state physiology

operational_defs.construct: growth output under each carbon regime
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel (1/h)
operational_defs.measure: mean instantaneous specific growth rate per seed, averaged over generations

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc channel (uM)
operational_defs.measure: mean ppGpp concentration per seed

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc channel (uM)
operational_defs.measure: mean active ribosome concentration per seed

operational_defs.construct: causal dependence of hierarchy on stringent response machinery
operational_defs.observable: rela gene_knockout perturbation crossed with condition (basal vs acetate)
operational_defs.measure: difference-in-differences: (acetate - basal) ppgpp_conc in wildtype vs in relA knockout background

drafts.predicted_effect: Acetate vs basal: growth_rate lower by ~40-60% (e.g. 0.6/h basal vs 0.25-0.35/h acetate), ppgpp_conc higher by ~1.5-2.5-fold, ribosome_conc lower by ~30-50%. In the relA knockout background, the acetate-vs-basal ppGpp fold-change should shrink to <1.3-fold (i.e. the interaction/difference-in-differences effect size drops by at least 50%), indicating the hierarchy signal is substantially relA-dependent.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of ppgpp_conc, acetate vs basal across seeds; reject H0 if |welch_t|>=2 (two-sided). For causal dependence: compute the same disconfirm(acetate, basal, ppgpp_conc) within the relA-knockout background; H1 requires the welch_t magnitude there to drop by >=50% relative to the wildtype-background welch_t (decision rule for the DiD claim).
falsifier.refuting_result: If |welch_t|<2 for ppgpp_conc (acetate vs basal) in wildtype, there is no reliable hierarchy signal to begin with (refutes H1 outright). If the welch_t magnitude in the relA-knockout background is NOT reduced by >=50% relative to wildtype (i.e. the acetate-vs-basal ppGpp difference persists essentially unchanged after relA removal), this refutes the causal/stringent-response-dependence claim and supports H0's passive-coupling alternative.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |welch_t|>=2 for main effect; >=50% reduction in |welch_t| magnitude from wildtype to relA-KO background for the causal claim

rivals.claim: Passive growth-rate coupling: the ppGpp/ribosome differences between acetate and basal are simply a generic consequence of slower growth (via reduced translational demand / charged-tRNA pool), with no specific causal role for the RelA-driven stringent response per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA knockout background, acetate vs basal still shows a |welch_t|>=2 difference in ppgpp_conc (or ribosome_conc) of similar magnitude to wildtype -- i.e., the DiD reduction criterion (>=50% drop) is NOT met, showing growth-rate/charged-tRNA coupling alone reproduces the signal without RelA.

rivals.claim: Acetate media simply fails to sustain growth at all (a lethality/division-defect confound) rather than inducing a genuine alternative hierarchical physiological state, so any ppGpp/growth differences reflect a dying population rather than regulated catabolite hierarchy.
rivals.distinguishing_result: division_rate on condition/acetate drops well below 1 (e.g. <0.5) indicating a viability crash rather than a stable alternate growth state; this would undermine interpreting the ppGpp/growth differences as a genuine regulated hierarchy response.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's acetate condition is a validated static fitted media condition that engages a qualitatively distinct metabolic/regulatory operating point from basal glucose, not merely a scaled-down version of the same program.

relA gene_knockout is mechanistically simulated to measurably reduce/attenuate ppGpp synthesis in this model (checked downstream); if relA KO is not mechanistically wired to ppgpp_conc in the simulator, the causal/DiD arm of the test is not decisive and should be treated as an auxiliary-assumption failure rather than a refutation of the biology.
Per-seed generation-averaged channel means are an adequate summary of steady-state physiological state for Welch's t comparison (ignoring within-generation transients).
Division_rate differences are used only as a confound check (rival 2), not as the primary falsifier channel.

Two static conditions (basal, acetate) stand in for the 'two sugars in one flask' framing since the instrument does not support a true mixed-substrate / diauxic timeline perturbation; this is the closest in-envelope operationalization of carbon hierarchy and is recorded as a scope caveat.

select_score.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
select_score.claim: Carbon catabolite repression via the stringent/ppGpp-coupled regulatory axis causes E. coli to prioritize one sugar over a second by suppressing growth-rate contribution from the non-preferred pathway until the preferred substrate is scarce; operationally, this manifests as a growth-rate and ppGpp signature that differs between a glucose-containing medium and an alternative-carbon medium, with the glucose condition showing higher growth rate and lower ppGpp (less stringent signaling) than a poorer, non-preferred carbon source, because the cell is NOT co-limited by both substrates simultaneously but rather runs a sequential, hierarchical program keyed to ppGpp/stringent-response state.
select_score.h1: Growth rate is higher and ppGpp concentration is lower under a preferred-carbon (glucose/basal) condition than under a poor alternative-carbon condition (e.g., acetate), consistent with a hierarchical, ppGpp-gated catabolite-repression-like prioritization rather than co-utilization; the gap in growth rate is large (>=2-fold) and the ppGpp gap is substantial (>=1.5-fold higher on the poor source).
select_score.h0: Growth rate and ppGpp concentration do not differ (beyond replicate noise) between the preferred-carbon (basal/glucose) condition and the poor alternative-carbon (acetate) condition — i.e., the simulated cell treats both carbon regimes as physiologically equivalent, with no hierarchical/stringent-response signature distinguishing them.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: instantaneous specific growth rate (1/h), averaged over seeds, compared between basal (glucose) and acetate conditions

operational_defs.construct: stringent-response engagement as the hierarchy-enforcing signal
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: steady-state ppGpp concentration (uM), averaged over seeds, compared between basal and acetate conditions

operational_defs.construct: charging status feeding the stringent response
operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged
operational_defs.measure: mean fraction of aminoacylated tRNA across the 20 amino-acid species, compared between conditions

operational_defs.construct: causal dependence of the growth/ppGpp hierarchy signature on the RelA/SpoT stringent pathway
operational_defs.observable: rela_conc / ppgpp_conc under relA knockout
operational_defs.measure: ppGpp concentration and growth rate in a relA gene_knockout under acetate vs basal, to test whether the ppGpp gap collapses when RelA is removed

select_score.predicted_effect: Growth rate on basal (glucose) is predicted to exceed growth rate on acetate by >=2-fold (e.g., ~1.0-1.2 /h basal vs ~0.3-0.5 /h acetate). Concomitantly, ppgpp_conc on acetate is predicted to exceed ppgpp_conc on basal by >=1.5-fold, reflecting stronger stringent-response engagement on the poorer carbon source. In a relA knockout, this ppGpp gap between acetate and basal should shrink toward near-equivalence (<1.2-fold), while the growth-rate gap persists (since RelA removal does not restore acetate's intrinsic metabolic ceiling), isolating the ppGpp signal as RelA-dependent rather than a secondary consequence of growth rate alone.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, acetate vs basal across seeds; reject H0 (support hierarchical/stringent signature) if |welch_t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates acetate higher by >=50%. Refute H1 if |welch_t|<2 or effect_pct <50% (no meaningful stringent-response differential).
falsifier.refuting_result: ppgpp_conc on acetate is statistically indistinguishable from basal (|welch_t|<2) or the fold-difference is <1.5x, showing no stringent-response-based hierarchy signature between the two carbon conditions.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=50%

rivals.claim: The growth-rate/ppGpp difference is purely a generic poor-carbon-source stress response unrelated to any sugar-sugar choice mechanism — i.e., any nutrient-poor static condition (not just acetate vs glucose specifically) would show the same ppGpp elevation, so this is not evidence of hierarchical PRIORITIZATION between two sugars but just a single-substrate quality effect.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the relA knockout control would show the SAME growth-rate gap AND the ppGpp gap would not be particularly RelA-dependent (i.e., removing RelA would not collapse the ppGpp differential), because the effect would stem from generic metabolic flux limitation rather than stringent-response signaling specifically keyed to substrate hierarchy.

rivals.claim: tRNA charging (fraction_trna_charged) directly sets growth rate via translation efficiency, with ppGpp merely a passive co-mover/readout of charging state rather than a causal enforcer of the hierarchy — i.e., ppGpp and growth rate are collinear because both depend on charged-tRNA pools, not because ppGpp enforces repression.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, fraction_trna_charged would track ppgpp_conc tightly across conditions (both moving together), and the relA knockout would NOT decouple ppGpp from charging — but critically, since relA knockout removes ppGpp SYNTHESIS (not charging-dependent regulation), if the growth-rate/ppGpp relationship were purely charging-driven, deleting relA would leave the growth-rate gap between acetate and basal UNCHANGED while still abolishing the ppGpp differential, which would actually be consistent with this rival too — the key distinguishing test is whether ppGpp given unprodu directly causes feedback onto growth (not observable here) vs is epiphenomenal; we treat the relA-knockout growth-rate persistence as the operational signature of this rival being correct about ppGpp's non-causal role in growth-rate determination specifically.

hypothesis.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
hypothesis.claim: Carbon catabolite repression (CCR) via the stringent/cAMP-CRP-coupled regulatory axis causes E. coli to prioritize a preferred carbon source over a secondary one, and this mechanistic commitment is reflected in a stringent-response signature (ppGpp/RelA elevation) that differs between a preferred-substrate condition and an alternative-substrate condition even though the cell never runs both simultaneously in this simulator. Since the instrument does not expose a two-sugar mixed-carbon condition or diauxic switch directly, the operational proxy for 'choice' is: growth-rate and stringent-response channels differ systematically and reproducibly across single-carbon static conditions (basal/glucose-like vs acetate), consistent with the known asymmetry in catabolic efficiency that underlies CCR-driven sequential use. H1: the acetate (non-preferred, slow, more gluconeogenic) condition shows significantly lower growth_rate and significantly higher ppgpp_conc than basal, reflecting the same regulatory logic (ppGpp-mediated resource reallocation away from growth) that in vivo produces diauxie and sugar preference.
hypothesis.h1: Growth on acetate (a slower, non-preferred carbon source) induces a stringent-response state (elevated ppgpp_conc, reduced ribosome_conc, reduced growth_rate) relative to basal, by a magnitude consistent with regulatory deprioritization rather than mere stoichiometric slowdown: growth_rate drops by >=40% and ppgpp_conc rises by >=50% vs basal.
hypothesis.h0: Acetate and basal conditions produce statistically indistinguishable ppgpp_conc and growth_rate (within replicate noise), i.e. the simulator shows no regulatory/stringent-response signature distinguishing a poor vs preferred carbon source — any growth difference is not accompanied by the predicted stringent-response shift.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean ppGpp concentration (uM) across seeds, basal vs acetate condition

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean active ribosome concentration (uM) across seeds, basal vs acetate condition

operational_defs.construct: causal dependence of the slowdown on ppGpp signaling (vs pure metabolic throughput limitation)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate under relA-pathway disruption
operational_defs.measure: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc in a relA gene_knockout under acetate vs basal, to test whether the stringent signature is abolished

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Acetate vs basal: growth_rate fold-change <= 0.6x (>=40% reduction), ppgpp_conc fold-change >=1.5x (>=50% increase), ribosome_conc reduced by >=20%. Expect Welch |t|>=2 on both growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of ppgpp_conc, acetate vs basal, across >=6 seeds per condition; reject H0 (accept H1) if two-sided |t|>=2 AND effect_pct indicates >=50% increase in acetate. Also require growth_rate Welch |t|>=2 with >=40% decrease.
falsifier.refuting_result: Welch |t|<2 for ppgpp_conc (or effect_pct <50%) despite a significant growth_rate drop -- showing the slowdown is not accompanied by a stringent-response signature, refuting the regulatory-commitment framing of H1.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 on ppgpp_conc and growth_rate; effect_pct>=50% (ppgpp_conc) and <=-40% (growth_rate)

rivals.claim: Pure stoichiometric/metabolic-flux limitation: acetate growth is slower simply because of lower ATP/carbon yield via the glyoxylate/TCA route, with no distinct ppGpp-mediated regulatory signature -- the ribosome/ppGpp changes are passive consequences of slower flux, not an active 'choice' mechanism.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, a relA gene_knockout under acetate would show the SAME growth_rate reduction vs basal as wildtype (ppGpp machinery is irrelevant to the slowdown), i.e. growth_rate in relA_KO/acetate is statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/acetate (Welch |t|<2).

rivals.claim: Ribosome-allocation economics alone (growth-rate-dependent ribosome concentration per Scott/Hwa scaling) explains the ppGpp/ribosome shift without any CCR-specific 'preference' logic -- i.e. any slow-growth condition (not just acetate specifically) would show the same signature, so this is a generic growth-law effect, not carbon-source choice.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the ppgpp_conc vs growth_rate relationship across MULTIPLE static conditions (basal, acetate, plus other available conditions) would fall on a single monotonic curve (slope_ci excludes 0, good fit) with acetate being just one point on that curve -- no acetate-specific discontinuity beyond what growth rate predicts.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's 'condition' perturbation (basal vs acetate) is a valid proxy for preferred-vs-non-preferred carbon source quality, since the instrument cannot run a true mixed two-sugar diauxic-shift experiment (glucose uptake is a binary switch and carbon-source mid-run switching is disallowed).

ppgpp_conc and growth_rate are recorded under steady-state charging for both conditions (no kinetic ppGpp module needed), so values are comparable across conditions without switching elongation_model.
relA gene_knockout is assumed to meaningfully attenuate ppGpp synthesis in the model (mechanistic KO effect is checked downstream, not assumed to be guaranteed).
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation within a condition is small enough that 6 seeds give adequate power to detect a >=40-50% effect (to be confirmed via power_mde if the initial test is ambiguous).

We are NOT claiming the simulator reproduces an explicit sequential diauxic switch in one run; the claim is restricted to the regulatory-signature asymmetry between single-carbon conditions as a proxy for the choice mechanism.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: E. coli's choice between two sugars in one flask is implemented as catabolite-repression-driven diauxie: the stringent/cAMP-CRP regulatory axis (proxied here by ppGpp dynamics since no direct cAMP-CRP channel exists) forces sequential, not simultaneous, substrate use, which the simulator should show as the ppGpp/growth-rate trajectory under a glucose-to-alternative-carbon media timeline reproducing a diauxic-like growth-rate dip and ppGpp spike, rather than smooth monotonic growth.
drafts.h1: When cells experience a timeline that removes glucose and leaves only an alternative static carbon source (e.g. acetate) available, growth_rate will show a transient drop (>=40% reduction from pre-shift baseline) coincident with a transient ppgpp_conc spike (>=1.5-fold over basal) within the first generation after the shift, consistent with a regulatory lag/choice mechanism rather than smooth co-utilization.
drafts.h0: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show no significant transient change across the media-shift timeline relative to a matched wildtype/basal run with no shift (i.e., the shift is seamlessly absorbed, consistent with simultaneous/unregulated substrate use).

operational_defs.measure: percent drop in growth_rate in the generation immediately following the shift vs the pre-shift generation, same seeds

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc trajectory across the same timeline
operational_defs.measure: fold-change in ppgpp_conc peak value post-shift vs pre-shift baseline, same seeds

rivals.claim: The growth dip is purely a stoichiometric/metabolic-flux artifact of the new carbon source's lower ATP yield (FBA objective constraint), not a ppGpp-mediated regulatory choice.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If ppgpp_conc is clamped to basal (ppgpp_conc perturbation, clamp=1x) during the same timeline and the growth_rate dip persists at similar magnitude (>=40% drop, not abolished), this supports the metabolic-flux-only rival over the ppGpp-regulatory-choice hypothesis.

rivals.claim: The dip is driven by ribosome reallocation lag (translation capacity mismatch) independent of ppGpp signaling, i.e., a passive consequence of ribosome pool size rather than active stringent signaling.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout (reduced ribosome capacity) under the same timeline shows a growth dip of similar relative magnitude to wildtype (not exaggerated), while ppGpp clamp abolishes it, this favors ribosome-lag over active ppGpp signaling as the proximate cause.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's 'timeline' media-shift mechanism for an aa/ion/oxygen-type shift can be repurposed to represent a glucose-removal event leaving only a static_only_carbon source (acetate) present, since direct mid-run carbon-source switches are disallowed; we approximate via a timeline event description '0 minimal, T acetate-only' and treat this as the closest in-envelope analog.

ppgpp_conc as captured is a reasonable proxy for cAMP-CRP-mediated catabolite repression signaling even though the two pathways are not identical in real biology; the simulator does not expose a cAMP-CRP channel directly.
Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories are read out at per-generation resolution; 'post-shift generation' means the first full generation after the timeline event.
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation is assumed small enough that 4-8 seeds give adequate power for the Welch test at the stated effect sizes (checked via power_mde if needed).

The static_only_carbon acetate condition is assumed to be a valid steady-state endpoint reachable by the timeline mechanism without requiring a forbidden mid-run carbon-source switch perturbation type.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: The classic "glucose first" catabolite-repression choice is implemented in this cell model as a stringent-response/ribosome-allocation effect: because the simulator treats glucose uptake as a binary switch (no graded two-sugar co-utilization channel exists), the closest testable proxy for sugar choice is how a cell on a single, non-preferred static carbon source (acetate) reallocates ribosomal/stringent machinery relative to the preferred basal (glucose-like) condition. H1: growth on acetate forces a stringent-response state (higher ppGpp, lower active ribosome concentration) that mimics the physiological state imposed during catabolite repression of a second sugar's operon, i.e. acetate acts as the 'repressed/non-preferred' condition analogous to never inducing the second sugar's pathway while glucose is present.
drafts.h1: Relative to basal (glucose-like) condition, cells fitted to acetate show a stringent-response shift: ppgpp_conc increases by >=50% and ribosome_conc decreases by >=20%, consistent with the allocation logic that underlies preferential-substrate (catabolite-repression-like) utilization.
drafts.h0: ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc on acetate are statistically indistinguishable from basal (within replicate noise), i.e. the model shows no stringent-response-like reallocation distinguishing a preferred vs non-preferred carbon source.

rivals.claim: Rival A: the ppGpp/ribosome shift on acetate is purely a slow-growth/nutrient-poverty effect common to ANY poor carbon source, not specifically a 'repression/choice' signal — i.e. it reflects growth-rate-dependent ribosome economy (Scott/Hwa scaling) rather than anything resembling substrate hierarchy or choice.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, a relA gene_knockout on acetate should still show the growth_rate drop (poor carbon source) but the ppgpp_conc rise should be abolished or strongly blunted (RelA is the main ppGpp synthetase under starvation), while ribosome_conc tracks growth_rate rather than ppgpp_conc directly -- showing the alarmone response is mechanistically separable from the raw growth slowdown.

rivals.claim: Rival B: the simulator's static per-condition fitting means basal and acetate parameter sets are simply independently calibrated steady states with different global expression profiles, and any ppgpp_conc/ribosome_conc difference is an artifact of the two conditions being fit from different proteomics/flux datasets rather than evidence of a real regulatory 'choice' mechanism.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the magnitude and direction of ppgpp_conc/ribosome_conc differences would NOT track the expected physiological ordering (richer->less ppGpp, poorer->more ppGpp) in a dose-like manner across multiple static conditions, and relA knockout would have no coherent effect on the cross-condition pattern (noise-like rather than systematically abolished).

auxiliary_assumptions: The instrument has no true two-sugar co-utilization or graded glucose-dose channel (uptake is binary and carbon-source mid-run switching is disallowed), so 'sugar choice' is operationalized indirectly via the stringent-response proxy on a single poor static carbon source (acetate) vs basal, rather than via direct simultaneous dual-substrate kinetics.

acetate/succinate/fumarate/malate are the only static-only non-glucose carbon conditions available; acetate is treated as representative of a 'non-preferred, repressing' substrate state analogous to what would be repressed when glucose is present.
ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc are read from the steady-state charging branch (kinetic ppGpp module assumed off unless stated), consistent with the always-on steady-state recording note.
Isogenic replicate noise across seeds is assumed small relative to the predicted condition effect; if not, the welch_disconfirm test will show this directly via per-seed spread.

relA gene_knockout is used as the closest in-envelope interventional control to break the ppGpp-synthesis mechanism without combining forbidden perturbation types (ppgpp_conc clamp + gene_knockout together is out of envelope).

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: Carbon catabolite repression via the stringent/ppGpp-coupled regulatory axis causes E. coli to prioritize one sugar over a second by actively suppressing the alternative pathway's flux, rather than the two sugars being co-utilized at matched rates. Because the instrument's uptake is a binary per-carbon-source switch (no mixed-sugar co-feed, no graded glucose), the operational proxy for 'choosing glucose over a second sugar' is: growth on the preferred (glucose/basal) condition shows higher growth_rate and distinct ppGpp/charged-tRNA physiology than growth on the alternative static carbon condition, AND a stringent-response-incapacitated background (relA/spoT-pathway knockout, approximated here as a gene_knockout of relA) collapses much of that growth-rate gap and the associated ppGpp difference — indicating the choice/prioritization machinery is ppGpp-mediated rather than purely stoichiometric.
drafts.h1: Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc differ substantially between basal (glucose-preferred) and an alternative static carbon condition (e.g. acetate), and this gap is causally dependent on the stringent response: knocking out relA markedly attenuates (by >=50%) the growth_rate and ppgpp_conc differences between the two conditions.
drafts.h0: Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc differences between basal and the alternative carbon condition are statistically indistinguishable from zero, OR if present, they persist essentially unchanged (attenuation <20%) in the relA knockout background, implying the gap reflects fixed metabolic stoichiometry rather than an active regulatory choice.

drafts.predicted_effect: Wildtype basal vs acetate: growth_rate higher on basal by >=40% (e.g. ~0.9 1/h vs ~0.5 1/h) and ppgpp_conc higher on acetate by >=50% (stringent response engaged under the poorer carbon source). In the relA-knockout background, this growth_rate gap shrinks by >=50% (attenuation) and the ppgpp_conc gap shrinks by >=50%, consistent with ppGpp-mediated active prioritization rather than pure stoichiometry.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test comparing growth_rate across seeds between wildtype/acetate vs wildtype/basal (test A), and separately between gene_knockout(relA)/acetate vs gene_knockout(relA)/basal (test B); compute percent attenuation of the mean difference from test A to test B. Reject H1 if |welch_t|<2 for test A (no baseline gap to explain) OR if attenuation <20% (gap persists despite relA knockout).
falsifier.refuting_result: The basal-vs-acetate growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) gap in the relA-knockout background is statistically indistinguishable from the wildtype gap (attenuation <20%, |welch_t| for the knockout contrast still >=2 and of similar magnitude), showing the differential is fixed metabolic stoichiometry, not ppGpp-mediated active choice.

test.threshold: |t|>=2 for presence of gap; attenuation>=50% required to confirm H1, <20% refutes H1

rivals.claim: The growth-rate and ppGpp differences between basal and acetate are explained purely by fixed enzymatic/stoichiometric differences in central metabolism (acetate requires glyoxylate shunt, lower ATP yield) with no active regulatory 'choice' signal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA knockout shows negligible attenuation (<20%) of the basal-vs-acetate growth_rate and ppgpp_conc gaps, i.e. the gap is relA-independent.

rivals.claim: Ribosome allocation/capacity (not ppGpp signaling per se) is the limiting causal factor: cells on acetate simply cannot afford as many ribosomes, and ppGpp changes are a downstream correlate, not a cause.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout (ribosome capacity reduction) under basal condition reproduces a similarly large growth_rate drop and ppgpp_conc rise WITHOUT needing the acetate condition itself, suggesting ribosome capacity, not carbon-source identity, drives the signal, and that the relA-knockout attenuation in the main test is confounded by general fitness loss rather than specific ppGpp mechanism.

auxiliary_assumptions: The instrument's binary per-carbon-source uptake switch means true simultaneous mixed-sugar co-feed cannot be simulated; acetate/basal condition contrast is used as the closest in-envelope proxy for a 'preferred vs non-preferred sugar' choice scenario, not a literal two-sugar-in-one-flask co-culture.

relA knockout is treated as a reasonable approximation of 'stringent response incapacitated'; it does not fully null ppGpp (SpoT remains), so residual ppGpp signal is expected and only a >=50% attenuation threshold is used to claim causal dependence.

Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are both read under steady-state charging mode (kinetic charging module assumed off) so ribosome_conc/rela_conc channels are valid comparators without extra kinetic-module caveats.

Seeds (6) and generations (3) are assumed sufficient to detect a fold-scale growth_rate/ppgpp_conc difference given typical replicate noise in this simulator; if underpowered this will surface as |welch_t|<2 and should be read as inconclusive rather than confirming H0 outright.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: Diauxie / catabolite repression in this whole-cell model is implemented as a ppGpp-and-stringent-response-coupled growth-rate decision: when the simulated cell is challenged with a nutrient-limitation signal that mimics a shift from a preferred to a less-preferred carbon source, the resulting growth-rate/physiology response is driven by a rise in ppGpp (stringent response) rather than growth rate changing independently of ppGpp. Because the instrument cannot switch carbon source mid-run, I operationalize the 'choice' as the amino-acid downshift timeline (a nutrient-quality shift that is known to trigger the same ppGpp-mediated stringent machinery used in carbon hierarchy decisions), and ask whether the ppGpp/ribosome axis mediates the growth response across STATIC carbon conditions (basal/glucose-like vs acetate) that differ in substrate quality.
drafts.h1: Across static carbon conditions that differ in preferred-vs-nonpreferred substrate quality (basal vs acetate) and across an amino-acid downshift timeline, ppgpp_conc rises substantially (>=2-fold vs reference) and ribosome_conc/growth_rate fall concomitantly, consistent with a ppGpp-mediated stringent-response mechanism gating growth on the poorer substrate; knocking out relA (the main ppGpp synthetase under amino-acid limitation) will blunt this ppGpp rise and partially rescue growth rate, demonstrating causal mediation.
drafts.h0: ppGpp is not causally mediating the growth-rate difference between substrate-quality conditions: growth_rate differs between basal and acetate (or across the amino-acid downshift) to the same degree with or without relA knocked out, i.e. ppgpp_conc changes are an epiphenomenal correlate, not a driver, of the growth response.

operational_defs.measure: growth_rate (1/h) and division_rate across conditions

drafts.predicted_effect: Acetate (poor substrate) vs basal: growth_rate drops by ~50-70% and ppgpp_conc rises >=2-fold (target fold-change ~2-4x basal). Under relA knockout in acetate, the ppgpp_conc rise is blunted to <1.3-fold vs wildtype-acetate and growth_rate is rescued by >=30% relative to wildtype-acetate, i.e. the genotype x condition interaction on growth_rate has a Welch |t|>=2 between (wildtype:acetate vs basal) and (relA-KO:acetate vs basal) deltas.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of ppgpp_conc (relA-KO/acetate vs wildtype/acetate) across seeds; reject H0 (support ppGpp-mediation, H1) if |t|>=2 AND the relA-KO growth_rate on acetate is higher than wildtype/acetate growth_rate by >=30% (checked via a second disconfirm call on growth_rate, gene_knockout/acetate vs wildtype/acetate)
falsifier.refuting_result: If relA-KO/acetate shows ppgpp_conc indistinguishable from wildtype/acetate (|t|<2) OR growth_rate remains as low as wildtype/acetate (no rescue), H1 is refuted and the growth deficit is attributed to ppGpp-independent mechanisms (Rival A or B).

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 on ppgpp_conc AND >=30% growth_rate rescue

rivals.claim: Rival A (metabolic/flux-limitation only): growth-rate differences across substrate quality are explained purely by FBA flux capacity differences (ATP/carbon yield) and do not require ppGpp signaling at all; ppGpp changes are a passive byproduct of slower growth, not a mediator.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, relA knockout would show the SAME growth_rate deficit on acetate as wildtype (no rescue) despite a blunted ppgpp_conc response -- i.e. ppgpp_conc and growth_rate dissociate without a corresponding growth rescue.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ribosome-allocation only, ppGpp-independent): the growth effect is mediated purely by ribosome_conc/translational capacity reallocation (e.g. via rRNA operon dosage) and ppGpp is merely a correlated marker, not the control variable; knocking down ribosome capacity directly (rrna_operon_knockout) would reproduce the growth defect independent of ppGpp level.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, an rrna_operon_knockout under basal conditions (ppGpp untouched) would show a comparable growth_rate drop to the acetate condition, showing ribosome capacity alone -- not ppGpp -- sets growth rate.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's 'acetate' static condition is a reasonable proxy for a non-preferred/low-quality carbon source relative to 'basal' (glucose-like), even though the instrument cannot do a true mid-run diauxic carbon switch.

The amino-acid downshift timeline engages the same RelA/ppGpp stringent-response module that would be engaged by carbon-source quality shifts, so it is an admissible auxiliary probe of the same mechanism, not a literal model of diauxie.

relA knockout is assumed to be mechanistically simulated in this model (i.e., it measurably reduces ppGpp synthesis under limitation) -- if the KO has no effect on ppgpp_conc even in a positive-control sense, this is logged as a simulator-capability gap, not evidence against H1.

Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are read under steady-state charging (ppGpp/ribosome channels are only reliably recorded in that regime per the instrument notes); kinetic-charging runs are out of scope for this test.
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation is treated as intrinsic noise; 6 seeds is assumed sufficient replicate power for a Welch t at the predicted >=2-fold effect size.

drafts.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
drafts.claim: Carbon catabolite repression via the stringent/ppGpp-linked regulatory axis causes cells confronted with glucose plus a second sugar to suppress alternative-sugar catabolic flux while growth remains glucose-like; this is a regulatory choice (diauxie-like repression), not a simple additive co-utilization, and is read out indirectly through altered growth rate, ppGpp level, and ribosome allocation relative to a glucose-only reference, since the simulator exposes uptake as a binary per-condition switch rather than a true mixed-sugar flask.
drafts.h1: When the model is run on a glucose-containing condition versus an alternative-carbon-only condition, cells show a growth-rate and ribosome/ppGpp signature consistent with glucose being prioritized (higher growth_rate, lower ppgpp_conc, higher ribosome_conc on glucose-like basal than on the static-only alternative carbon source such as acetate), reflecting the regulatory hierarchy that underlies catabolite repression; this difference should be large (growth_rate fold-change >= 1.5x, ppgpp_conc fold-change <= 0.7x) and consistent across seeds.
drafts.h0: There is no systematic difference in growth_rate, ppgpp_conc, or ribosome_conc between the glucose/basal condition and the alternative-carbon (acetate) condition beyond replicate noise (Welch |t| < 2 on growth_rate), i.e. the model treats both carbon sources as physiologically equivalent at the level of these channels.

rivals.claim: The growth-rate/ribosome difference between basal and acetate is purely a metabolic/stoichiometric (FBA flux) consequence of acetate's lower ATP yield, with no distinct ppGpp-mediated regulatory 'choice' involved.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA-knockout background, the basal-vs-acetate growth_rate and ribosome_conc gap persists essentially unchanged (ppgpp_conc also fails to rise on acetate in relA KO, confirming ppGpp synthesis is disabled, yet the growth/ribosome gap remains), showing the effect is downstream of ppGpp and driven by raw metabolic capacity rather than stringent signaling.

rivals.claim: Any apparent 'choice' signature is a seed-noise artifact or condition-labeling artifact, not a reproducible regulatory distinction, because the simulator cannot actually mix two sugars (uptake is a binary switch per static condition).
rivals.distinguishing_result: Across seeds the basal vs acetate differences in growth_rate/ppgpp_conc/ribosome_conc show high per-seed spread with Welch |t|<2 on at least one of the three channels, i.e. the signature does not replicate robustly.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-condition binary uptake switch (glucose vs acetate as separate static conditions) is treated as a proxy for carbon-source preference ordering, since a true simultaneous two-sugar mixed flask is outside the validated envelope.

Growth-rate, ppGpp, and ribosome-concentration differences between basal and acetate conditions are assumed to reflect the same regulatory hierarchy (catabolite repression / stringent response) that governs real diauxic preference, even though the model does not simulate a mid-run sugar switch for this comparison.

relA knockout is assumed to meaningfully disable ppGpp synthesis in this model (reducing/abolishing the stringent response) so that a persisting growth/ribosome gap in the relA KO can be interpreted as evidence against ppGpp-dependence.
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation under isogenic conditions is an adequate proxy for 'replicate noise' against which the condition effect is judged.

We are not attempting to resolve which specific sugar is 'chosen' in a mixed flask (outside scope); we restrict the claim to the growth/regulatory signature consistent with a preference hierarchy across two static single-carbon conditions.

first_draft.predicted_effect: Directional: growth_rate drops by >=40% (transient trough) and ppgpp_conc rises by >=1.5-fold within 1 generation post-shift in the timeline design, relative to pre-shift baseline and relative to the no-shift wildtype/basal reference; effect should decay back within 2-3 generations as the cell adapts to the new static carbon source.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of growth_rate at the post-shift generation, target vs reference, across seeds; reject H0 if two-sided p<0.05 (|t|>=2) AND effect_pct indicates >=40% drop. If |t|<2 or effect_pct<40%, H1 is refuted.
falsifier.refuting_result: growth_rate in the shift timeline does not differ significantly (|t|<2) from the no-shift wildtype/basal reference at the equivalent generation, or the drop is <40%, indicating seamless/simultaneous substrate use rather than a regulatory choice lag.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct>=40%

rivals.claim: The growth dip is purely a stoichiometric/metabolic-flux artifact of the new carbon source's lower ATP yield (FBA objective constraint), not a ppGpp-mediated regulatory choice.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If ppgpp_conc is clamped to basal (ppgpp_conc perturbation, clamp=1x) during the same timeline and the growth_rate dip persists at similar magnitude (>=40% drop, not abolished), this supports the metabolic-flux-only rival over the ppGpp-regulatory-choice hypothesis.

rivals.claim: The dip is driven by ribosome reallocation lag (translation capacity mismatch) independent of ppGpp signaling, i.e., a passive consequence of ribosome pool size rather than active stringent signaling.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout (reduced ribosome capacity) under the same timeline shows a growth dip of similar relative magnitude to wildtype (not exaggerated), while ppGpp clamp abolishes it, this favors ribosome-lag over active ppGpp signaling as the proximate cause.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's 'timeline' media-shift mechanism for an aa/ion/oxygen-type shift can be repurposed to represent a glucose-removal event leaving only a static_only_carbon source (acetate) present, since direct mid-run carbon-source switches are disallowed; we approximate via a timeline event description '0 minimal, T acetate-only' and treat this as the closest in-envelope analog.

ppgpp_conc as captured is a reasonable proxy for cAMP-CRP-mediated catabolite repression signaling even though the two pathways are not identical in real biology; the simulator does not expose a cAMP-CRP channel directly.
Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories are read out at per-generation resolution; 'post-shift generation' means the first full generation after the timeline event.
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation is assumed small enough that 4-8 seeds give adequate power for the Welch test at the stated effect sizes (checked via power_mde if needed).

The static_only_carbon acetate condition is assumed to be a valid steady-state endpoint reachable by the timeline mechanism without requiring a forbidden mid-run carbon-source switch perturbation type.

hypothesis.question: How do bacteria choose between two sugars in the same flask?
hypothesis.claim: Classic diauxie / catabolite repression logic is implemented in this whole-cell model: when a second, less-preferred carbon source is nominally available alongside glucose, the model's physiology still behaves as if glucose dominates — but because this simulator exposes carbon source only as a single static 'condition' (uptake is a binary switch, not a mixture), the operational test is reframed as a comparison ACROSS static conditions that stand in for the two sugars and their joint/alternative regime. Specifically, I claim that growth physiology (growth_rate, ribosome_conc, ppgpp_conc) on a preferred-sugar condition (basal/glucose-like) is substantially more 'repressed-stringent-response-off, high-growth' than on a non-preferred static carbon condition (e.g. acetate), and that this gap reflects the same regulatory logic (stringent response / ribosome allocation) that underlies diauxic sugar choice — i.e. the model encodes a graded hierarchy of carbon-source quality via ppGpp/ribosome allocation rather than two sugars being used identically.
hypothesis.h1: Across static carbon conditions that proxy preferred vs non-preferred sugars, growth_rate and ribosome_conc are substantially higher and ppgpp_conc substantially lower on the preferred condition (basal) than on the non-preferred condition (acetate), consistent with the same stringent-response/ribosome-allocation logic that drives real diauxic catabolite repression.
hypothesis.h0: There is no substantial difference in growth_rate, ribosome_conc, or ppgpp_conc between the basal and acetate static conditions beyond replicate noise — i.e. the model treats all static carbon conditions as physiologically equivalent and encodes no carbon-quality hierarchy.

operational_defs.construct: preference for the better sugar / catabolite repression strength
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: mean instantaneous specific growth rate (1/h) over simulated generations, basal vs acetate

operational_defs.construct: stringent response activation (signal that a sugar is 'bad')
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean ppGpp concentration (uM) over the run, basal vs acetate

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean active ribosome concentration (uM), basal vs acetate

operational_defs.construct: causal dependence of the growth/ppGpp coupling on the RelA/SpoT stringent pathway
operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate under rela gene_knockout
operational_defs.measure: compare the basal-vs-acetate gap in ppgpp_conc/growth_rate with and without relA deleted

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Direction: basal (preferred-sugar proxy) > acetate (non-preferred proxy) for growth_rate and ribosome_conc; ppgpp_conc is basal < acetate. Magnitude: growth_rate fold-change ~1.8-3x higher on basal than acetate; ppgpp_conc ~1.5-2.5x higher on acetate than basal; ribosome_conc ~1.3-2x higher on basal. These are the same order-of-magnitude shifts reported for E. coli glucose-vs-acetate physiology.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of growth_rate, acetate vs basal, across seeds; reject H0 (i.e. claim holds) if |welch_t|>=2 and effect_pct indicates basal higher; refute H1 if |welch_t|<2 or acetate growth_rate is not substantially lower
falsifier.refuting_result: Welch t between acetate and basal growth_rate has |t|<2, or acetate growth_rate is statistically indistinguishable from (or higher than) basal, indicating no carbon-quality hierarchy encoded by the model

test.statistic: welch_t

rivals.claim: Any growth_rate/ppgpp_conc difference between basal and acetate reflects generic media richness (more total nutrient flux) rather than any catabolite-repression-like regulatory hierarchy specific to sugar preference.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a relA gene_knockout abolishes or sharply attenuates the ppgpp_conc gap between basal and acetate while the growth_rate gap persists at similar magnitude, this supports the rival: the signal channel (ppGpp) is decoupled from the growth effect, meaning growth differences are not mediated by the stringent-response hierarchy the claim invokes.

rivals.claim: The model does not implement any meaningful carbon-source-dependent regulatory tuning at all; any observed growth_rate differences are an artifact of generic flux-balance differences between static media parameterizations (condition presets), not a RelA/ppGpp-mediated response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If ppgpp_conc shows no significant difference between basal and acetate (Welch |t|<2) even though growth_rate differs significantly, this shows the model encodes condition-specific growth via metabolic flux alone, without any stringent-response signaling difference.

auxiliary_assumptions: The static 'condition' presets (basal vs acetate) are an acceptable proxy for 'preferred vs non-preferred sugar' since the simulator cannot run a true two-sugar mixture or mid-run carbon-source switch (uptake is a binary switch).
Ribosome_conc and ppgpp_conc are read under steady-state charging (not kinetic), consistent with how these channels are recorded by default.
Seed-to-seed stochastic variation under isogenic conditions is small enough that a 4-8 seed Welch t-test has reasonable power to detect the predicted >=1.3x effect sizes.

RelA is the dominant ppGpp synthetase represented in the model such that its knockout meaningfully perturbs the ppgpp_conc channel; if RelA is not mechanistically simulated for this condition, that is logged as a capability gap rather than taken as disconfirming the broader claim.

Diauxic choice in vivo is a dynamic, mixed-sugar phenomenon; this design necessarily tests the STATIC endpoint physiology associated with each sugar's regulatory regime as the best available proxy, not the transition dynamics themselves.

hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: When glucose is exhausted and cells must shift to a less-preferred carbon source (diauxic-like shift), individual isogenic cells do NOT switch metabolic/stringent-response state synchronously: across replicate seeds, the timing and magnitude of the ppGpp/growth-rate transition shows substantial cell-to-cell (seed-to-seed) heterogeneity rather than a single sharp, uniform switch, consistent with population bimodality in the transition dynamics rather than a synchronous all-cells-at-once switch.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds subjected to a nutrient downshift timeline (preferred-sugar-equivalent condition shift from a nutrient-rich/basal state to a poorer static condition such as acetate), the distribution of per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate values at the shift timepoint is heterogeneous/bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) rather than tightly clustered, indicating cells do not all switch at the same time.
hypothesis.h0: All replicate seeds switch together: per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate values at the post-shift timepoint are unimodal and tightly clustered (BC <= 0.555), consistent with a synchronous, deterministic population-wide switch with only ordinary replicate noise.

operational_defs.observable: timeline media-shift event from basal (glucose-rich) condition to a poorer static carbon condition (acetate)
operational_defs.measure: timeline perturbation: '0 basal, 180 acetate' (minutes)

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate channels sampled per seed shortly after the shift
operational_defs.measure: per-seed ppgpp_conc (uM) and growth_rate (1/h) at timepoint ~post-shift generation 2

operational_defs.construct: synchrony vs heterogeneity of switching across cells
operational_defs.observable: dispersion/shape of the per-seed distribution of ppgpp_conc and growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled per-seed values; BC>0.555 indicates heterogeneous/bimodal switching

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Post-shift, per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate values form a bimodal or widely dispersed distribution: predicted BC ~0.65-0.75 (vs reference condition BC~0.4-0.5), with a >=2-fold spread in ppgpp_conc across seeds and a >=1.5-fold spread in growth_rate, rather than all seeds converging to within ~10% of each other.

falsifier.decision_rule: Sarle's bimodality coefficient computed over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values at post-shift timepoint (shift design) vs at matched timepoint in steady basal reference; reject H1 (switch is synchronous) if BC<=0.555 for the shift design, i.e. per-seed values are unimodal/tightly clustered
falsifier.refuting_result: BC for the shift design is <=0.555 and per-seed ppgpp_conc values cluster within ~10% of each other, indicating a single near-simultaneous switch across all seeds

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc
test.threshold: BC>0.555 required to support H1 (heterogeneous switching); BC<=0.555 refutes

rivals.claim: Deterministic-synchronous rival: the shift is governed by a shared, essentially deterministic metabolic threshold (e.g., glucose exhaustion kinetics identical across seeds), so all cells switch within a narrow time/magnitude window; observed spread is just ordinary replicate/measurement noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: BC<=0.555 and per-seed spread in ppgpp_conc/growth_rate is comparable to the spread seen in the steady basal reference (no shift), showing no excess heterogeneity attributable to the shift itself.

rivals.claim: RelA/ppGpp-independent rival: any apparent heterogeneity in growth_rate during the shift is driven by generic growth-rate noise unrelated to the stringent response (ppGpp), not by stochastic timing of stringent-response activation; knocking out relA (abolishing ppGpp synthesis) should leave growth_rate heterogeneity largely unchanged if ppGpp is not the driver.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA knockout control under the same shift timeline, growth_rate heterogeneity (BC) remains similarly elevated/bimodal despite loss of ppGpp signaling, indicating the observed heterogeneity is not mediated by stringent-response (ppGpp) switching timing.

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline perturbation '0 basal, 180 acetate' is interpretable by the simulator as a nutrient downshift analogous to glucose exhaustion forcing a shift to a secondary carbon source (acetate is listed as a static_only_carbon condition reachable via condition, and we assume the timeline mechanism can enact a media-shift event onto it since timeline explicitly supports aa/ion/oxygen-like shifts).

Per-seed values at a single post-shift timepoint (generation 2-3) adequately capture 'switch timing/state' even though the instrument does not give a continuous single-cell trajectory; we treat each seed as one stochastic replicate cell lineage.
Replicate noise under the unshifted basal reference establishes the baseline BC/spread against which the shift condition's heterogeneity is judged as 'excess'.

ppgpp_conc and growth_rate are treated as valid proxies for 'metabolic switch state'; we do not have a direct single-cell lineage-tracking channel, so bimodality in these pooled per-seed readouts is our best operational stand-in for population asynchrony.

We do not attempt to resolve whether any observed bimodality reflects deterministic chaos vs genuine stochastic gene-expression noise in the switch circuit — this is recorded as an explicit scope limitation of the simulator.
residual_ambiguities: reached round cap without full convergence

objection_ledger.issue: The entire hypothesis rests on 'seeds' in the whole-cell/whole-population simulator corresponding to independent single CELLS with stochastic initialization, so that per-seed CV reflects cell-to-cell variability. If the simulator's 'seed' instead perturbs a population-average or lineage-level trajectory (common in many whole-cell models), per-seed CV measures run-to-run numerical/initialization variability, not single-cell heterogeneity, and the claim 'genetically identical cells' would not be operationalized by the instrument at all.

The gen2-vs-gen4 welch_disconfirm check is framed as validating 'steady-state stability,' but generations is a perturbation-level dial that changes population age-structure/lineage depth, not just averaging window. A pass (|t|<2) could occur even if the per-seed CV itself is driven by transient early-generation dynamics that happen to look similar at both checkpoints by coincidence, and a fail could reflect genuine population-structure change rather than 'CV estimate instability.' This conflates two different things (noise-floor stability vs generation-structure effects) under one test; the decision rule should be stated as a coarse sanity check only, not proof of steady-state, or it should be dropped from the primary falsifier chain.

drafts.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
drafts.claim: When the preferred carbon source (glucose) is exhausted and cells must shift to a secondary substrate, the diauxic switch is population-heterogeneous rather than synchronous: individual-cell timing and magnitude of the shift (captured in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories across seeds) show substantial spread, with a sizeable minority of seeds lagging far behind the population mean — i.e. the switch is NOT a single synchronous event but a distribution of switch times with CV > 0.3 across seeds.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds subjected to the same glucose-to-secondary-carbon media timeline, the post-shift growth_rate recovery time and ppgpp_conc peak timing are heterogeneous: the coefficient of variation (CV) of time-to-half-recovery of growth_rate across seeds exceeds 0.3, and/or the pooled per-seed switch-time distribution is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555), reflecting a 'bet-hedging'-like split between fast- and slow-switching subpopulations.
drafts.h0: All seeds switch at effectively the same time: the CV of time-to-half-recovery of growth_rate across seeds is <=0.3 and the distribution of switch times is unimodal (BC <=0.555), consistent with a deterministic, synchronous population-wide response governed only by shared kinetic/regulatory parameters with no meaningful cell-to-cell heterogeneity.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate trajectory following the glucose-exhaustion timeline event
operational_defs.measure: time from media-shift event to the point growth_rate first reaches 50% of its new (post-shift) steady-state value, computed per seed

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc trajectory following the shift
operational_defs.measure: time-to-peak ppgpp_conc post-shift, per seed, and peak magnitude relative to pre-shift baseline

operational_defs.observable: distribution of per-seed time-to-half-recovery values pooled across seeds
operational_defs.measure: coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of time-to-half-recovery across seeds; Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) of the pooled distribution

drafts.predicted_effect: Asynchronous switching: CV of time-to-half-recovery of growth_rate across 6-8 seeds > 0.3 (vs <0.15 expected if purely synchronous/deterministic), and/or pooled switch-time distribution bimodal with BC > 0.555, reflecting a fast-switching subpopulation (~60-70% of seeds) recovering within ~1 generation and a slow subpopulation (~30-40%) taking >=2 generations to reach half-recovery.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute per-seed time-to-half-recovery of growth_rate after the media-shift event across 8 seeds; test for asynchrony using Sarle's bimodality coefficient on the pooled per-seed switch-time values. Reject H0 (synchronous) if BC > 0.555; additionally report CV across seeds as supporting evidence (expect >0.3 under H1).
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled switch-time distribution is unimodal (BC <= 0.555) AND CV of time-to-half-recovery <= 0.3, indicating all seeds switch at essentially the same time (synchronous, low-noise transition) — refutes H1.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed time-to-half-recovery values
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 rejects unimodal/synchronous null

rivals.claim: The population IS synchronous: apparent per-seed spread in timing is just measurement/simulation noise around a single deterministic switch time set by shared enzyme-level kinetics (e.g. cAMP-CRP/PTS dynamics common to all cells), not true bistable heterogeneity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, pooled switch-time distribution is unimodal with BC <= 0.555 and CV <= 0.3; per-seed ppgpp_conc peak times cluster tightly (narrow spread) rather than splitting into fast/slow clusters.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity exists but is driven entirely by stringent-response (ppGpp) bistability rather than carbon-sensing bistability per se — i.e. the spread in growth_rate recovery is a downstream consequence of variable RelA/SpoT activation, not an independent carbon-switch mechanism.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout (removing ppGpp induction capacity) should COLLAPSE the bimodality/CV in growth_rate recovery time even though cells still must physically switch carbon sources; if BC drops below 0.555 and CV drops below 0.3 in the relA KO timeline run while the wildtype timeline remains bimodal/high-CV, this supports ppGpp-driven heterogeneity rather than an independent carbon-sensing switch mechanism.

rivals.claim: Rival A: The apparent spread in post-shift growth rates is just ordinary stochastic noise around a single synchronous mean switching time, not a true bimodal subpopulation split.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, BC stays <=0.555 and the pooled distribution is well-described as unimodal with wide variance rather than two separable clusters; bimodality_bc would show a single dominant cluster.

rivals.claim: Rival B: Any asynchrony is driven by ppGpp/stringent-response heterogeneity (RelA-dependent), not by intrinsic metabolic-switch bistability — i.e., the bimodality is downstream of variable stringent response rather than a cause of differential switching.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout background should abolish or strongly dampen the ppGpp-linked bimodality (ppgpp_conc becomes flat/low and unimodal across seeds) while growth_rate bimodality, if still present, would indicate the switch heterogeneity is independent of ppGpp — if growth_rate bimodality ALSO collapses in the relA KO, that supports Rival B (ppGpp-driven) over an intrinsic bistable-switch mechanism.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's timeline perturbation can encode a glucose-to-acetate (or other static_only_carbon) media shift event mid-run and that uptake switching is modeled as a discrete/binary event per cell-seed, consistent with the instrument note that uptake is binary.

8 seeds is sufficient replicate depth to estimate a bimodality coefficient meaningfully; we treat each seed as one independent cell-lineage sample of the post-shift distribution (not literally thousands of single cells), so BC is a coarse proxy for population heterogeneity.

Sampling growth_rate and ppgpp_conc at a single fixed post-shift generation (gen 3) is an adequate operationalization of 'switch timing'; we are not resolving continuous-time single-cell trajectories, only a cross-seed snapshot.

The relA knockout control is assumed to still produce viable, dividing cells over the simulated generations (division_rate used as a sanity check) so that growth_rate/ppgpp_conc readouts remain interpretable.

Seed-to-seed variability under isogenic conditions is an adequate proxy for cell-to-cell heterogeneity in a single population, given the simulator's per-seed stochastic replicate framework.

Per-seed trajectories are treated as independent isogenic single-cell lineages, so pooling ppgpp_conc across seeds at a fixed generation approximates a population snapshot (cross-sectional distribution) even though the simulator runs seeds as separate lineage replicates rather than a true single mixed population.

Stochastic (kinetic) charging / ppGpp module is assumed to be switched on for this run so that ppgpp_conc reflects dynamic per-seed noise rather than a deterministic steady-state value common to all seeds; if only steady-state charging is available, bimodality could be structurally suppressed regardless of biology — this is flagged as a simulator-resolution caveat, not chased further.

Generation-to-generation cluster persistence (laggard fraction) is a descriptive secondary readout, not itself subject to a formal significance test in this round; the primary falsifying test is the single-timepoint BC check at generation 2.
