operational_defs.measure: per-seed ppgpp_conc trajectory post-shift; variance and bimodality across seeds

operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged
operational_defs.measure: per-seed dip depth/duration in fraction_trna_charged immediately after the shift

drafts.predicted_effect: Post-shift growth_rate across seeds forms a bimodal distribution with Sarle's BC > 0.555 (vs BC < 0.45 expected for a synchronous reference), with an estimated 20-30% of seeds falling into a 'slow/lagging' cluster whose mean growth_rate is >=2-fold lower than the 'fast-switcher' cluster at the same timepoint.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed growth_rate values measured at a fixed timepoint (e.g. 60 min post-shift) for the timeline/nutrient_downshift design; reject H1 (synchronous switching) is retained if BC <= 0.555, i.e. unimodal; H1 confirmed if BC > 0.555
falsifier.refuting_result: BC <= 0.555 (unimodal, tight distribution) and welch_t comparing seed-variance of growth_rate between timeline/nutrient_downshift and wildtype/basal shows no significant difference (|t|<2), indicating all seeds switch together with reference-level noise

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate at fixed post-shift timepoint
test.threshold: BC>0.555 to confirm bimodal/asynchronous switching; BC<=0.555 refutes H1

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic fast switch): all cells switch synchronously and quickly because the regulatory network (e.g. cAMP-CRP/PTS) is a sharp deterministic switch with negligible stochastic variation; apparent heterogeneity in real data is measurement noise, not biology.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, per-seed growth_rate at the fixed post-shift timepoint will be unimodal (BC<=0.555) with seed-to-seed variance statistically indistinguishable (|welch_t|<2) from the wildtype/basal reference's intrinsic noise.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp-driven but still synchronous): a transient but uniform stringent response (ppGpp spike) delays all cells equally before they resume growth on the new substrate, producing a step-like but SYNCHRONOUS slowdown-then-recovery rather than persistent bimodal subpopulations.
rivals.distinguishing_result: ppgpp_conc would show a uniform spike-and-decay (low inter-seed variance, BC<=0.555) in all seeds, and growth_rate dip timing would be nearly identical across seeds even though a transient slowdown occurs; relA knockout control would abolish the spike but the growth_rate bimodality (if present) would persist, showing ppGpp is not the source of asynchrony.

auxiliary_assumptions: The instrument's 'timeline' media-shift events can approximate a preferred-to-secondary sugar exhaustion/switch without being a literal glucose-concentration dial (uptake is modeled as binary); we treat an amino-acid/ion shift timeline as the closest in-envelope proxy for a nutrient downshift and note this as a scope limitation.
Per-seed growth_rate at a single fixed timepoint shortly post-shift is a valid proxy for 'switching time'; we are not tracking continuous single-cell switching kinetics, only a snapshot distribution.
Seeds are isogenic and independent; any bimodality reflects intrinsic stochastic/regulatory heterogeneity, not population structure introduced by the simulator's seeding scheme.

4-8 seeds give enough resolution to estimate a bimodality coefficient meaningfully; we treat this as a pilot-scale test and note that a genome/population-scope claim about 'fraction of cells' will need a larger-seed follow-up if this pilot supports H1.

params.note: interventional control: abolishes ppGpp synthesis to test whether stringent-response engagement (Rival B) is the source of any observed asynchrony/bimodality

drafts.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
drafts.claim: When the preferred carbon source (glucose) is exhausted and a secondary carbon source becomes available, isogenic E. coli cells do NOT switch to the secondary substrate synchronously — instead individual cells show heterogeneous, staggered timing of the metabolic switch, manifesting as a broad, bimodal-at-intermediate-time distribution of growth-rate trajectories across single-cell (per-seed) replicates rather than a single sharp synchronous transition.
drafts.h1: Across an isogenic population undergoing a diauxie-like media timeline (minimal_glucose -> minimal_acetate), the per-seed growth_rate trajectories at the transition timepoint show substantial inter-seed heterogeneity in switch timing, such that the pooled per-seed growth_rate at an intermediate timepoint (near the expected switch) is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) reflecting a mixture of cells that have and have not yet re-accelerated, rather than all seeds transitioning together.
drafts.h0: All seeds switch synchronously: the per-seed growth_rate values at the intermediate transition timepoint are unimodal and tightly clustered (BC <= 0.555), consistent with a single population-wide switch time with only small stochastic jitter.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel trajectory over the timeline, per seed
operational_defs.measure: time at which per-seed growth_rate crosses back above 50% of its pre-shift value, recorded per seed

operational_defs.observable: distribution of growth_rate across seeds at a fixed intermediate timepoint shortly after the nutrient shift
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled per-seed growth_rate values at that timepoint

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and fraction_trna_charged per seed across the shift
operational_defs.measure: per-seed trajectory alignment with growth_rate recovery, used as a secondary corroborating channel

drafts.predicted_effect: At the intermediate timepoint (~30-60 min post glucose exhaustion, mid-shift), pooled per-seed growth_rate is bimodal with BC > 0.555 and an estimated ~30-70% split between 'already switched' (growth_rate recovered to >=70% of post-shift steady value) vs 'not yet switched' (growth_rate still <=30% of post-shift value) seeds; by contrast a synchronous-switch null predicts BC <= 0.555 and a single tight cluster (CV < 0.15) at that timepoint.

falsifier.decision_rule: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over the pooled per-seed growth_rate values at the intermediate (mid-shift) timepoint; reject H0 (synchronous switch) if BC>0.555, interpreted as evidence of staggered switching
falsifier.refuting_result: BC <= 0.555 at the mid-shift timepoint, with per-seed growth_rate tightly clustered (CV<0.15), indicating all seeds transition together rather than a staggered/bimodal switch

test.statistic: bimodality_bc

rivals.claim: Switch timing heterogeneity is driven mainly by ppGpp/stringent-response bistability (a RelA-dependent alarmone threshold effect) rather than by generic stochastic noise in metabolic enzyme expression.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a relA gene_knockout (abolishing ppGpp synthesis induction) ELIMINATES the bimodality (BC drops to <=0.555, growth_rate becomes tightly clustered) while wildtype under the same shift remains bimodal, this supports the ppGpp-dependent mechanism; if the relA knockout STILL shows bimodal growth_rate at the same timepoint, heterogeneity is not ppGpp-gated and must arise from another noise source (e.g. stochastic enzyme expression).

rivals.claim: There is no real sub-population structure; apparent bimodality is an artifact of under-sampling (too few seeds) or of picking an arbitrary intermediate timepoint that happens to straddle a smooth, continuous, unimodal distribution of switch times.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If increasing seeds (replicate power_mde check) shows the apparent bimodality was within the minimum-detectable-effect noise floor (i.e., effect does not exceed MDE at n), or if BC stays <=0.555 at multiple nearby timepoints, this argues for an artifact rather than genuine bimodal subpopulations.

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline media-shift mechanism (glucose depletion -> acetate availability) is simulated as a discrete environmental switch at the specified time, not a gradual depletion curve; cells respond to the post-switch medium composition.

Per-seed growth_rate time series are recorded at sufficient temporal resolution to identify an intermediate timepoint between pre-shift and full post-shift steady state (i.e., the simulator logs growth_rate at sub-generation time resolution, not only per-generation summaries).

8 seeds provide enough independent stochastic replicates to estimate a pooled bimodality coefficient meaningfully; if power_mde indicates 8 seeds is underpowered, this is logged as a scope caveat rather than over-interpreted as a null result.

Acetate is a valid static_only_carbon condition reachable via the 'condition' perturbation for the reference baseline; the timeline perturbation for the shift itself uses a media-shift event list rather than a carbon-source switch mid-run restriction, which is permitted for amino acid/ion/oxygen shifts per the dial note — this is treated as the closest in-envelope analog to a diauxic shift and flagged as an assumption pending confirmation that a glucose->acetate timeline is executable (not a forbidden mid-run carbon-source switch).

drafts.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
drafts.claim: When the preferred carbon source (glucose) is exhausted and only a secondary carbon source (acetate) remains available, individual cells in an isogenic population do NOT switch synchronously onto the secondary substrate: instead the population shows bimodal/heterogeneous growth-rate and stringent-response (ppGpp) trajectories across seeds, reflecting a diauxie-lag distribution rather than a single synchronous switch time.
drafts.h1: Across replicate seeds of an isogenic population subjected to a glucose-to-acetate media shift, the distribution of post-shift growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) trajectories is bimodal/heterogeneous (Sarle's BC > 0.555 on pooled per-seed post-shift growth_rate values at a fixed checkpoint time), indicating a spread of individual switching times rather than a synchronous population-wide transition.
drafts.h0: All seeds switch at effectively the same time: post-shift growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories are unimodal and tightly clustered across seeds (BC <= 0.555), i.e. the population behaves as a single synchronous switcher, matching the reference wildtype/basal (no-shift) replicate spread.

operational_defs.measure: time-to-recovery of growth_rate to >=50% of pre-shift value, computed per seed

drafts.predicted_effect: Bimodal/heterogeneous switching: BC > 0.555 for pooled per-seed growth_rate at the post-shift checkpoint (e.g. 90 min after glucose exhaustion), with an estimated split of roughly 40-60% of seeds showing fast recovery (growth_rate back to >=50% of pre-shift within ~30 min) versus the remainder showing a lag of >=90 min before recovery -- i.e. at least a ~3x spread in per-seed recovery time, versus a tight unimodal cluster (BC<0.3, <20% spread) in the no-shift wildtype/basal reference.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed growth_rate values at the fixed post-shift checkpoint (90 min after the glucose-exhaustion timeline event) for the timeline/glucose_to_acetate_shift design; reject H1 (synchronous switch, i.e. accept H0) if BC <= 0.555, meaning the distribution is unimodal/tightly clustered like the wildtype/basal reference
falsifier.refuting_result: BC <= 0.555 and per-seed growth_rate spread at checkpoint is comparable to (within ~20% of) the wildtype/basal reference spread, indicating all seeds switch together

test.statistic: sarle_bimodality_coefficient
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 to confirm bimodal/heterogeneous switching; BC <= 0.555 refutes H1

rivals.claim: Rival A (fast deterministic switch): the regulatory network (CRP/cAMP, catabolite repression release) is strong enough that ALL cells switch almost simultaneously once glucose crosses a threshold, with only replicate noise (not bimodality) in timing -- this is effectively H0.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled per-seed growth_rate/ppgpp_conc at checkpoint shows a single tight cluster (BC<=0.555) with spread similar to the no-shift wildtype/basal reference across seeds.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp-independent heterogeneity driven purely by metabolic/FBA stochasticity, not stringent response): any observed bimodality in growth_rate arises from flux-balance solver variability or acetate-uptake kinetics rather than genuine regulatory (ppGpp/RelA-mediated) bistability.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA_knockout/glucose_to_acetate_shift control, growth_rate bimodality (BC) at the same checkpoint remains similarly high (BC>0.555, unchanged from wildtype), showing the heterogeneity is NOT ppGpp/RelA-dependent and instead reflects something else (e.g. metabolic noise) -- this would refute the stringent-response-driven mechanism while still allowing H1 (heterogeneous switching) to stand for a different reason.

drafts.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
drafts.claim: When the preferred sugar is exhausted, isogenic E. coli cells do NOT all switch to the alternative carbon source synchronously: there is substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity in the timing/completeness of the diauxic transition, producing a transient bimodal population split between 'still-arrested/slow' cells and 'already-switched/fast-growing' cells rather than a single sharp synchronous shift.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate seeds sampled shortly after the preferred-sugar-exhaustion media shift, the distribution of per-seed growth_rate (and/or fraction_trna_charged) values is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555), reflecting a population split between cells that have and have not yet re-initiated growth on the second substrate.
drafts.h0: Per-seed growth_rate values shortly after the shift are unimodal/tightly clustered (BC <= 0.555), consistent with all cells switching at essentially the same time (a synchronous population-level transition, modeled as a single sharp step in mean growth rate with low inter-seed variance).

operational_defs.measure: per-seed growth_rate at a fixed post-shift timepoint, pooled across seeds; also fraction_trna_charged as a corroborating metabolic-state readout

operational_defs.observable: distribution shape of pooled per-seed growth_rate values post-shift

drafts.predicted_effect: A bimodal split post-shift: predicted BC ~0.65-0.75 (well above the 0.555 threshold) in pooled per-seed growth_rate shortly (within ~1 generation) after preferred-sugar exhaustion, with roughly 30-60% of seeds remaining in a low-growth-rate cluster (growth_rate near 0, lag-phase-like) while the rest have already resumed growth at a rate comparable to pre-shift levels (fold-difference between the two clusters >=3x in growth_rate). This heterogeneity should largely resolve by generation 3-4 (BC drops back toward unimodal <0.4) as cells stochastically complete the switch.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values sampled at the fixed post-shift timepoint (gen 1-2) across 8 seeds; reject H1 (synchronous switch, unimodal) if BC<=0.555; accept H1 (asynchronous/bimodal switch) if BC>0.555.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555 at the post-shift timepoint, i.e., per-seed growth_rate values form a single tight cluster rather than two separated clusters, indicating all cells switched essentially synchronously.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate
test.threshold: BC>0.555 required to support bimodal/asynchronous switching

rivals.claim: Switching is synchronous and smooth: all cells experience a gradual, correlated slowdown-then-recovery with no subpopulation split (the apparent spread is just continuous noise, not bimodality).
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled per-seed growth_rate post-shift is unimodal (BC<=0.555) and the per-seed spread is comparable to the basal wildtype's intrinsic noise (small z_vs_corpus_spread), i.e., no distinguishable two-cluster structure emerges.

rivals.claim: Any apparent heterogeneity is driven purely by stringent-response (ppGpp) bursts gating the switch, not by stochastic enzyme-induction timing per se — i.e., ppGpp spikes themselves ARE the switch-timing determinant.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In a relA gene_knockout background (ppGpp synthesis abolished), the growth_rate bimodality collapses (BC drops below 0.555) and cells show a single, more synchronous (though possibly slower) transition, showing ppGpp was necessary for generating the split; if bimodality PERSISTS in the relA KO, this rival is refuted and the split is attributable to some other noise source (e.g., stochastic induction of the catabolic operon for the second sugar).

drafts.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
drafts.claim: When the preferred carbon source (glucose) is exhausted, individual isogenic E. coli cells do not all switch to the secondary substrate (acetate) synchronously: the diauxic transition is asynchronous/bimodal across the population, producing a transient subpopulation that lags in resuming growth while others resume quickly.
drafts.h1: Across a glucose->acetate diauxic shift, per-seed (per-lineage) growth_rate trajectories at the post-shift timepoint show a bimodal distribution (fast-resumers vs lagging cells), i.e. Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed growth_rate values at a fixed post-shift timepoint exceeds 0.555, reflecting a genuine split rather than a single unimodal distribution with variance.
drafts.h0: Growth_rate values across seeds at the post-shift timepoint are unimodal (unimodal unperturbed noise around a single resumption kinetics), i.e. bimodality coefficient <=0.555; all lineages switch with similar timing modulo ordinary replicate noise.

drafts.predicted_effect: Bimodal split at the post-shift timepoint: bimodality coefficient BC > 0.555 for pooled per-seed growth_rate, with an estimated ~20-40% of lineages in a 'lagging' low-growth-rate cluster (growth_rate near 0-0.3 1/h) versus ~60-80% in a 'resumed' cluster (growth_rate approaching the pre-shift acetate-adapted rate, roughly 0.3-0.6 1/h), i.e. a >=2-fold separation between cluster means.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (bimodality_bc) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values at the fixed post-shift timepoint (generation 3) for the timeline/glucose_to_acetate_shift design; reject H1 (synchrony holds) if BC<=0.555. As a secondary consistency check, Welch t of growth_rate (timeline/glucose_to_acetate_shift vs wildtype/basal) should show |t|>=2 confirming a real shift-induced effect before trusting the bimodality read.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555, indicating growth_rate values post-shift form a single unimodal cluster (all lineages resume on a similar timescale, consistent with synchronous switching modulo ordinary noise)

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate at generation 3
test.threshold: BC>0.555 to confirm bimodal (asynchronous) switching; BC<=0.555 refutes

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic/clock-like): all cells switch at essentially the same time, governed by a shared metabolic clock (e.g. acetate accumulation threshold), so growth_rate dips then recovers uniformly — any apparent spread is pure measurement/replicate noise, not a real subpopulation structure.
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc on timeline/glucose_to_acetate_shift returns BC<=0.555 (unimodal), and per-seed growth_rate spread (CV) is comparable to the wildtype/basal replicate-noise CV.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp/stringent-response-driven bistability): the asynchrony, if present, is caused entirely by stochastic ppGpp/RelA induction during the shift (bistable stringent response triggers the lag), not by any ppGpp-independent metabolic switching mechanism — removing RelA should collapse the bimodal growth_rate pattern into a unimodal one.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA gene_knockout background under the same glucose_to_acetate_shift timeline, bimodality_bc on growth_rate drops to <=0.555 (bimodality abolished) even though wildtype shows BC>0.555, implicating ppGpp bistability as the causal driver rather than an independent switching mechanism.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's per-seed trajectories approximate independent isogenic lineages, so pooling growth_rate across 8 seeds at a fixed timepoint is a valid proxy for a population snapshot (scope caveat: 8 seeds is a modest sample for bimodality detection; a true screen would use more, but this is the feasible envelope scale).

The timeline media-shift mechanism (minimal_glucose -> minimal_acetate) engages whatever diauxie/catabolite-repression-like machinery the model implements; if the model does not simulate acetate-switch kinetics explicitly, growth_rate dynamics are the best available proxy.

generation 3 (post-shift) is an adequate fixed sampling point to catch the resumption-lag signal without conflating it with later re-equilibration; this specific timepoint choice is itself an auxiliary assumption that could be revisited.

ppGpp/RelA induction is assumed to be the dominant candidate bistability mechanism available in-model; other possible sources of bistability (e.g. transporter expression noise) are not separately isolated here and are left as an acknowledged scope limitation.

drafts.claim: When glucose (preferred sugar) is exhausted during a diauxic timeline shift to a secondary carbon source, isogenic cells do NOT switch to the secondary-sugar catabolic program synchronously: across a seed population there is substantial cell-to-cell variation in the timing/degree of the switch, visible as a bimodal (fast-switcher vs slow/non-switcher) distribution in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories shortly after the shift, rather than a single sharp, uniform transition.
drafts.h1: Across replicate seeds of an isogenic population undergoing a glucose-exhaustion timeline shift, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) sampled shortly after the shift is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555), reflecting asynchronous switching rather than a single synchronous transition.
drafts.h0: The per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) sampled shortly after the glucose-exhaustion shift is unimodal (BC <= 0.555), consistent with all cells switching synchronously/uniformly (differences are only replicate noise around one transition time).

drafts.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of post-shift growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds with BC > 0.555 (vs a unimodal null BC ~0.3-0.4), with an estimated ~30-50% of seeds falling into a 'slow/delayed-switch' cluster (low growth_rate, low ppgpp_conc rise) and the remainder into a 'fast-switch' cluster, rather than all seeds clustering tightly around one mean (CV difference between clusters >=2-fold in growth_rate).

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values sampled in a fixed 30-60min post-shift window from the glucose_exhaustion_to_acetate timeline (n>=6 seeds, each treated as a distinct sample by boosting seeds to get a usable pooled distribution); reject H1 (synchronous null) if BC>0.555, interpreting the two-cluster split as fast vs slow switchers; refute H1 (i.e. support synchronous switching) if BC<=0.555, i.e. the distribution is unimodal
falsifier.refuting_result: BC<=0.555 (unimodal distribution), indicating all seeds switch at a similar rate/timing with only small replicate noise, not two distinguishable subpopulations

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed post-shift growth_rate (and secondarily ppgpp_conc) values
test.threshold: BC>0.555 => bimodal/asynchronous (supports H1); BC<=0.555 => unimodal/synchronous (refutes H1, supports H0)

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic fast switch): all cells switch essentially simultaneously once glucose crosses a shared depletion threshold; any variance seen is pure measurement/seed noise, not a real subpopulation structure.
rivals.distinguishing_result: BC stays <=0.555 and per-seed growth_rate values form one tight unimodal cluster with low spread (CV<10%) in the post-shift window.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp-driven but graded, not bimodal): cells do vary continuously in switch timing (a graded ppGpp ramp) due to continuous metabolic-state differences, producing a unimodal but wide/skewed distribution rather than two discrete clusters.
rivals.distinguishing_result: BC stays <=0.555 (unimodal) but with high variance/skew in growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across seeds, rather than a clear two-cluster bimodal split; a relA knockout control would not eliminate the spread since it is not ppGpp-threshold-dependent bistability.

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline perturbation's media-shift event (glucose to acetate at minute 480) is interpretable by the simulator as a diauxic-shift-like event even though acetate is listed as a static-only carbon condition elsewhere; we treat the shift as the closest in-envelope approximation of glucose exhaustion triggering a secondary-substrate program.
Per-seed stochastic variation in this whole-cell model is assumed to be a meaningful proxy for intrinsic cell-to-cell noise relevant to population asynchrony, not merely numerical/integration noise.
The 30-60 minute post-shift window is assumed long enough to capture the switch but short enough to avoid conflating early asynchrony with later re-convergence to a single growth rate.

bimodality_bc applied to a modest pooled sample (n~8 seeds, possibly supplemented with multiple post-shift timepoints per seed) is assumed to have enough points for a meaningful BC estimate; if not, this is logged as a power limitation rather than grounds to abandon the test.

relA knockout is used as an interventional control to probe whether any observed bimodality is ppGpp-engagement-dependent, not to fully resolve deterministic-chaos vs stochastic-noise origins of variability (an acknowledged scope limit of the simulator).

drafts.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
drafts.claim: When the preferred carbon source (glucose) is exhausted and only a secondary substrate (acetate) is available, isogenic cells do NOT switch to the secondary-substrate catabolic/stringent program synchronously: instead the population shows a broad, right-skewed/bimodal distribution of switching times, reflected as high cell-to-cell variance in ppGpp induction and growth-rate recovery kinetics across replicate seeds at a fixed post-shift timepoint, rather than a tight, unimodal, near-simultaneous response.
drafts.h1: Across an isogenic population undergoing a glucose-to-acetate diauxic shift, the distribution of single-lineage (per-seed) ppgpp_conc and growth_rate values sampled shortly after the shift is bimodal or high-variance (CV > 0.4, bimodality coefficient > 0.555), indicating staggered, non-synchronous switching rather than a single synchronized transition.
drafts.h0: Switching is synchronous: at a fixed timepoint shortly after glucose depletion, per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate values are tightly clustered (CV < 0.4) and unimodal (bimodality coefficient <= 0.555), statistically indistinguishable in spread from the pre-shift steady-state wildtype/basal population.

drafts.predicted_effect: Non-synchronous switching: pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate at 60 min post-shift show CV > 0.4 (vs CV < 0.15 for steady-state wildtype/basal) and a bimodality coefficient > 0.555 (two subpopulations: ~40% still-low-ppGpp/high-growth 'not yet switched' vs ~60% high-ppGpp/low-growth 'switched'), i.e., at least a 2-3x increase in cross-seed CV relative to the unshifted reference.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over the pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values sampled 60 min post-shift (n=8 seeds); separately compute CV across seeds for both target and reference and run Welch's t comparing per-seed ppgpp_conc spread (treated via absolute deviation from seed-group median) between target and reference. Reject H1 (synchronous switching confirmed) if BC <= 0.555 AND CV_target is not significantly greater than CV_reference (|welch_t| < 2).
falsifier.refuting_result: BC <= 0.555 (unimodal) and CV_target statistically indistinguishable from CV_reference (|t|<2), showing all cells switch in a tight, near-simultaneous window

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc at 60 min post-shift

rivals.claim: Switching is fast and essentially deterministic/synchronous because the glucose-to-acetate shift is governed by a sharp, shared metabolic threshold (glucose depletion triggers cAMP-CRP/ppGpp induction near-simultaneously in all cells) rather than stochastic gene-expression noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate at 60 min post-shift are tightly clustered (CV<0.15) and unimodal (BC<=0.555), matching the reference wildtype/basal spread -- i.e., the falsifier's refuting_result is observed.

rivals.claim: Any observed heterogeneity is an artifact of the stringent-response (RelA/SpoT) module itself being noisy/bistable regardless of carbon source, not a diauxic-shift-specific phenomenon -- i.e., the same bimodality would appear even without a carbon shift, driven purely by intrinsic RelA pathway noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout control (relA_knockout/glucose_to_acetate_shift) still shows high CV/bimodality in growth_rate (switching timing variance persists via a ppGpp-independent catabolite pathway), OR conversely if bimodality in ppgpp_conc vanishes with relA knocked out but growth_rate heterogeneity remains, that would show the heterogeneity is ppGpp-independent and rather reflects a RelA-specific intrinsic noise source rather than genuine diauxic-switch staggering.

auxiliary_assumptions: The 'minimal_glucose'/'minimal_acetate' media labels within a timeline event map onto the validated static conditions (basal vs acetate) and the simulator supports a glucose-to-acetate media-shift event as a timeline perturbation (an aa/ion shift analog, not a disallowed mid-run carbon switch) -- if the platform rejects this as an out-of-envelope carbon switch, the closest in-envelope proxy is comparing static basal vs static acetate steady-states across seeds as a surrogate for post-shift heterogeneity.

Per-seed trajectories in this whole-cell model represent independent lineages/replicate cells (not a single averaged population), so cross-seed variance at a fixed timepoint is a valid proxy for population-level single-cell heterogeneity.

60 minutes post-shift-onset is within the window where wildtype E. coli diauxic lag is known to occur (typically 20-90 min), so this sampling time should capture the switching transition rather than pre- or well-post-switch steady states.

ppGpp induction and growth-rate depression are coupled readouts of the same stringent-response switching event, so using both as corroborating (not independent) measures is appropriate and expected to show the same qualitative heterogeneity pattern.

hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: When the preferred carbon source (glucose) is exhausted and a secondary carbon source becomes available, isogenic E. coli cells do NOT switch to the secondary substrate synchronously — instead individual cells show heterogeneous, staggered timing of the metabolic switch, manifesting as a broad, bimodal-at-intermediate-time distribution of growth-rate trajectories across single-cell (per-seed) replicates rather than a single sharp synchronous transition.
hypothesis.h1: Across an isogenic population undergoing a diauxie-like media timeline (minimal_glucose -> minimal_acetate), the per-seed growth_rate trajectories at the transition timepoint show substantial inter-seed heterogeneity in switch timing, such that the pooled per-seed growth_rate at an intermediate timepoint (near the expected switch) is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) reflecting a mixture of cells that have and have not yet re-accelerated, rather than all seeds transitioning together.
hypothesis.h0: All seeds switch synchronously: the per-seed growth_rate values at the intermediate transition timepoint are unimodal and tightly clustered (BC <= 0.555), consistent with a single population-wide switch time with only small stochastic jitter.

rivals.claim: Switch timing heterogeneity is driven mainly by ppGpp/stringent-response bistability (a RelA-dependent alarmone threshold effect) rather than by generic stochastic noise in metabolic enzyme expression.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If a relA gene_knockout (abolishing ppGpp synthesis induction) ELIMINATES the bimodality (BC drops to <=0.555, growth_rate becomes tightly clustered) while wildtype under the same shift remains bimodal, this supports the ppGpp-dependent mechanism; if the relA knockout STILL shows bimodal growth_rate at the same timepoint, heterogeneity is not ppGpp-gated and must arise from another noise source (e.g. stochastic enzyme expression).

rivals.claim: There is no real sub-population structure; apparent bimodality is an artifact of under-sampling (too few seeds) or of picking an arbitrary intermediate timepoint that happens to straddle a smooth, continuous, unimodal distribution of switch times.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If increasing seeds (replicate power_mde check) shows the apparent bimodality was within the minimum-detectable-effect noise floor (i.e., effect does not exceed MDE at n), or if BC stays <=0.555 at multiple nearby timepoints, this argues for an artifact rather than genuine bimodal subpopulations.

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline media-shift mechanism (glucose depletion -> acetate availability) is simulated as a discrete environmental switch at the specified time, not a gradual depletion curve; cells respond to the post-switch medium composition.

Per-seed growth_rate time series are recorded at sufficient temporal resolution to identify an intermediate timepoint between pre-shift and full post-shift steady state (i.e., the simulator logs growth_rate at sub-generation time resolution, not only per-generation summaries).

8 seeds provide enough independent stochastic replicates to estimate a pooled bimodality coefficient meaningfully; if power_mde indicates 8 seeds is underpowered, this is logged as a scope caveat rather than over-interpreted as a null result.

Acetate is a valid static_only_carbon condition reachable via the 'condition' perturbation for the reference baseline; the timeline perturbation for the shift itself uses a media-shift event list rather than a carbon-source switch mid-run restriction, which is permitted for amino acid/ion/oxygen shifts per the dial note — this is treated as the closest in-envelope analog to a diauxic shift and flagged as an assumption pending confirmation that a glucose->acetate timeline is executable (not a forbidden mid-run carbon-source switch).

residual_ambiguities: reached round cap without full convergence

objection_ledger.issue: The 'basal_homogenized' control is specified with identical perturbation/condition/timeline/seeds/generations fields as the standard wildtype/basal design, differing only in a non-functional 'note' parameter. Since the instrument's actual dials (perturbation, condition, timeline) are unchanged, this control is indistinguishable from simply re-running wildtype/basal again -- it does not manipulate or homogenize any extrinsic/environmental channel. A null result (CV similar across the two 'arms') is therefore guaranteed by construction (same design run twice), not an empirical finding that rules out extrinsic drift, and a difference would only reflect ordinary sampling noise between two identical designs. The control cannot actually distinguish intrinsic stochastic noise from extrinsic condition drift as claimed.

The rrna_operon_knockout design is proposed to distinguish intrinsic stochastic noise from extrinsic growth-rate-driven coupling, but capping rRNA operons alters ribosome synthesis machinery directly - it does not decouple ribosome_conc from growth_rate variation, it just changes the mean/ceiling of ribosome_conc. Growth_rate and ribosome_conc are mechanistically coupled (ribosomes drive growth rate, growth rate feeds back on ribosome allocation) in the underlying model, so this knockout would likely shift both channels together rather than breaking their correlation. The design does not actually test whether cross-seed ribosome_conc variance tracks cross-seed growth_rate variance independently of a common cause.

hypothesis.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
hypothesis.claim: When the preferred sugar is exhausted (diauxic-shift timeline), isogenic E. coli cells do NOT all switch to the alternative growth program synchronously: there is substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity/lag in the stringent-response and growth-rate recovery, producing a broad, right-skewed (and plausibly bimodal) distribution of post-shift growth rates and ppGpp levels across the population, rather than a single tight switching time. This is a claim about population-level synchrony of the switch response (growth_rate, ppgpp_conc trajectories) -- NOT a claim about single-gene transcriptional expression noise, which the simulator's aggregate channels cannot directly resolve.

rivals.claim: Switching is deterministic and synchronous because the regulatory network (ppGpp/stringent response) responds identically and rapidly in every cell given the same nutrient-exhaustion signal -- any apparent spread is pure measurement/sampling noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled growth_rate and ppgpp_conc distributions remain unimodal with BC<=0.555 and CV<0.15, matching the non-shifted wildtype/basal reference spread -- heterogeneity disappears once replicate noise is accounted for.

rivals.claim: Heterogeneity exists but is NOT driven by the stringent (ppGpp) response -- it is a generic consequence of stochastic ribosome/protein-count noise unrelated to RelA/SpoT signaling, so removing ppGpp machinery would not reduce the spread.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In a relA gene_knockout background subjected to the same shift timeline, growth_rate dispersion (CV, BC) remains just as high as in wildtype, showing the heterogeneity is ppGpp-independent (the interventional control that isolates stringent-response causality from a mere co-moving correlate).

auxiliary_assumptions: The available 'timeline' perturbation (amino-acid/ion media shift) is used as the closest in-envelope proxy for a preferred-to-alternative sugar exhaustion event, since a mid-run carbon-source switch is explicitly disallowed; results are interpreted as a model of 'resource exhaustion and reprogramming heterogeneity' rather than literal glucose-to-lactose diauxie.
Per-seed stochastic variation in the simulator (distinct random seeds) is assumed to be a valid proxy for genuine isogenic cell-to-cell heterogeneity.

A single fixed post-shift timepoint/generation (generation 3) is assumed sufficient to capture the switching transient without conflating it with later re-equilibration to the new steady state; this is a scope caveat, not independently validated by a secondary generation sweep in this round.

growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are assumed to be jointly informative bulk readouts of 'having switched' even though the simulator does not directly report a discrete switch-time per cell or per-gene expression levels.

This hypothesis makes no claim about single-gene transcriptional noise (mRNA/protein copy-number variance for an individual gene); that distinct construct is out of scope for the aggregate channels available here and is explicitly not addressed by this test.

params.shift_description: proxy for carbon-source exhaustion event at t=180min; measure growth_rate and ppgpp_conc per seed in window post-shift

objection_ledger.issue: The user's question is about whether 'the same gene' is expressed at the same level across isogenic cells - i.e., per-gene expression noise. The candidate substitutes a bulk/aggregate readout (ribosome_conc, fraction_trna_charged) as a proxy for 'gene expression level' generally. These are systems-level emergent quantities (summed over many genes/processes) and could show low noise even if individual gene expression is highly variable, or vice versa. This conflates 'bulk translational capacity' with 'single-gene expression level', which is the actual construct in the question.

The gen2-vs-gen4 welch_disconfirm check is framed as validating 'steady-state stability,' but generations is a perturbation-level dial that changes population age-structure/lineage depth, not just averaging window. A pass (|t|<2) could occur even if the per-seed CV itself is driven by transient early-generation dynamics that happen to look similar at both checkpoints by coincidence, and a fail could reflect genuine population-structure change rather than 'CV estimate instability.' This conflates two different things (noise-floor stability vs generation-structure effects) under one test; the decision rule should be stated as a coarse sanity check only, not proof of steady-state, or it should be dropped from the primary falsifier chain.

The claim as stated ('genetically identical cells express the same gene at the same level') is about gene expression broadly, but the operationalization tests only ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc as proxies for 'a gene/pathway' — a reasonable narrowing, but it's a choice among many possible channels (e.g. protein_mass, rna_mass) that could equally stand in for 'gene expression output.'

drafts.question: When the preferred sugar runs out, do all cells switch to the second sugar at the same time?
drafts.claim: When glucose (preferred sugar) is exhausted and cells must switch to a secondary carbon source, the switch to the alternative-metabolism physiological state is asynchronous across the population: individual cells show a graded/bimodal distribution of switching times and post-shift growth rates rather than a synchronous, uniform transition. Operationally, growth_rate trajectories across seeds (treated as an ensemble of isogenic cells under identical shift timing) show high inter-seed CV and the pooled post-shift growth_rate distribution is bimodal, reflecting a fraction of cells still lagging in the diauxie-like adjustment while others have already resumed growth.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic replicate cells experiencing the same glucose-to-alternative-carbon shift timing, post-shift growth_rate and ppgpp_conc trajectories are heterogeneous: the pooled post-shift growth_rate distribution across seeds is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with an estimated 20-40% of cells still in a low-growth/high-ppGpp 'lag' sub-population at a fixed timepoint shortly after the shift, rather than all cells transitioning together.
drafts.h0: All isogenic cells switch synchronously: post-shift growth_rate values across seeds are unimodal and tightly clustered (CV comparable to steady-state basal noise), i.e. the pooled distribution shows no significant bimodality (BC <= 0.555) and seed-to-seed spread in growth_rate does not exceed that seen in the matched steady-state reference condition.

drafts.predicted_effect: Post-shift (at +2 generations) pooled growth_rate across seeds is bimodal with BC > 0.555, and the inter-seed CV of growth_rate during the lag window is at least 3x the CV seen in steady-state basal condition (e.g. basal CV ~0.05 -> shift-window CV >=0.15). Approximately 20-40% of seeds remain in a low-growth (<50% of pre-shift rate) / elevated-ppGpp (>=2x basal) lagging state at +2 generations while the rest have resumed near pre-shift growth.

As a secondary confirmatory check, Welch t of growth_rate CV (shift-window vs basal reference) across seeds; reject H0 if |t|>=2.
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled post-shift growth_rate values are unimodal (BC<=0.555) and the inter-seed CV during the shift window is statistically indistinguishable from (or less than) the basal reference CV (|t|<2), indicating all cells transitioned together.

rivals.claim: The population switches synchronously but with a uniform, substantial lag (a deterministic delay shared by all cells) rather than asynchronous heterogeneity — i.e. growth_rate dips uniformly then recovers uniformly, so variance stays low even though the mean transiently drops.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled growth_rate distribution at +2 generations remains unimodal (BC<=0.555) with low inter-seed CV (comparable to basal), even though the MEAN growth_rate is depressed relative to pre-shift — a synchronous-but-slow switch, not a bimodal split.

rivals.claim: Apparent heterogeneity is driven by stochastic ppGpp/RelA noise unrelated to the carbon switch itself (i.e. basal stochastic variation in the stringent-response machinery, not a bona-fide diauxic bet-hedging phenomenon) — the same bimodality would appear even without the shift, as intrinsic noise in rela_conc.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout background subjected to the same glucose-to-acetate shift still shows bimodal/heterogeneous growth_rate (BC>0.555) at +2 generations, indicating the heterogeneity is NOT mediated by RelA-dependent ppGpp signaling but reflects some other (e.g. metabolic enzyme induction) asynchrony.

auxiliary_assumptions: The 'basal to minimal' timeline shift adequately models preferred-sugar exhaustion/diauxic-like downshift within the simulator's media-condition vocabulary (no explicit carbon-source switch is available, so a basal->minimal nutrient downshift is used as the closest in-envelope analog).

Generation 2 post-shift is an adequate fixed timepoint to capture the switching response before any crashed/non-dividing seeds confound the readout (division_rate will be checked as a secondary viability gate).
Per-seed ppgpp_conc values are independent draws from the underlying population-heterogeneity process (isogenic, stochastic seeds), not driven by a shared external forcing.

The ppGpp clamp control at clamp=1.0x basal (i.e., pinned to the pre-shift basal level) is interpreted as disabling the stringent-response machinery's dynamic range, isolating whether downstream heterogeneity is ppGpp-dependent.

The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation is an adequate proxy for real cell-to-cell heterogeneity in switching time; deterministic-chaos vs intrinsic-noise distinctions are out of scope for this instrument.

auxiliary_assumptions: The 'timeline' media-shift mechanism (aa/ion/oxygen shift) can be used to approximate withdrawal of a preferred sugar via a defined minimal-media composition change at a fixed timepoint (0 -> 180 min), since a direct mid-run carbon-source switch is outside the envelope.
Per-seed trajectories are treated as a proxy for per-cell heterogeneity within an isogenic population (each seed = one stochastic realization of an otherwise identical cell lineage).

ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc channels are read under steady-state charging (no kinetic ppGpp module invoked) unless otherwise noted; this may understate transient kinetic heterogeneity but is the only channel available for this screen.

The 1-2 generation post-shift sampling window is assumed sufficient to capture the diauxic lag/switch in this simulator; if the lag resolves faster or slower, the fixed timepoint may miss the bimodal window (a scope caveat, not resolvable without a pilot run).

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: Bacterial persistence without genetic resistance arises from a stochastic, ppGpp-mediated stringent-response state: in an isogenic wildtype population under nutrient-poor (basal) conditions, a subpopulation of cells spontaneously enters a high-ppGpp, slow-growth state via RelA activity, and this discrete subpopulation (not a uniform population-wide shift) accounts for the growth_rate distribution's shape. This is a claim about stochastic subpopulation heterogeneity (a population-structure phenomenon), NOT about bet-hedging per se -- the simulator cannot test whether such heterogeneity reduces variance under unpredictable future environments, so no bet-hedging/adaptive-value language is used.
hypothesis.h1: Across replicate seeds of wildtype E. coli under basal media, the per-seed-per-generation distribution of growth_rate is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555), with a slow-growing (ppgpp_conc elevated, roughly >=3x the fast-mode median) subpopulation comprising an estimated 10-30% of instances; this bimodality is abolished (BC<=0.555, unimodal) when relA is knocked out, because the slow/high-ppGpp mode requires RelA-driven ppGpp synthesis. This is a claim about discrete subpopulation structure, not about adaptive variance-reduction under environmental unpredictability.
hypothesis.h0: growth_rate across wildtype/basal seeds (pooled per-seed per-generation) is unimodal (BC<=0.555) -- i.e., there is no distinct slow-growing/high-ppGpp subpopulation distinguishable from ordinary seed-to-seed replicate noise; any apparent split is noise, and relA knockout does not reduce the bimodality coefficient relative to wildtype.

No cross-condition seed pairing is invoked anywhere in this test: each run (wildtype/basal, relA KO/basal) is independently pooled over its own (seed, generation) instances, avoiding the seed-tracking confound raised previously.

Separately and independently, compute BC over pooled per-seed per-generation growth_rate values within the gene_knockout(relA)/basal run. RelA-dependence is supported only if wildtype/basal is bimodal (BC>0.555) AND relA KO/basal is unimodal (BC<=0.555).
falsifier.refuting_result: wildtype/basal growth_rate is unimodal (BC<=0.555), OR wildtype/basal is bimodal but relA knockout/basal growth_rate remains bimodal (BC>0.555) with a slow-growth mode still present at comparable prevalence -- indicating either no discrete subpopulation exists, or it is not RelA/ppGpp-dependent.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-(seed,generation) growth_rate instances within each run independently
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for bimodal classification in wildtype/basal; BC<=0.555 required in relA KO/basal to support RelA-dependence

rivals.claim: Persistence-relevant slow growth is a uniform population-wide response to nutrient limitation (not a discrete subpopulation): basal media simply lowers everyone's growth_rate unimodally without any stochastic bimodal split.
rivals.distinguishing_result: growth_rate in wildtype/basal is unimodal (BC<=0.555) with a left-shifted mean relative to a richer condition, rather than two distinct modes.

rivals.claim: Any apparent slow-growth subpopulation is driven by ribosome capacity limitation (stochastic ribosome partitioning / translational noise) rather than ppGpp/RelA signaling -- a ribosome-allocation phenomenon independent of the stringent response.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal (reduced ribosome capacity) produces or enhances growth_rate bimodality even when relA is intact and the slow mode's ppgpp_conc is not elevated, showing ribosome scarcity alone (not ppGpp) drives the split.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation under steady-state ppGpp charging is sufficient to generate a detectable bimodal growth_rate signal within 4 generations and 8 seeds; if the underlying noise model is too smooth, a true discrete-subpopulation phenomenon could be false-negatively classified as unimodal (a simulator-resolution limit, not evidence against the phenomenon biologically).

relA knockout is assumed to abolish ppGpp induction in this model (SpoT-mediated basal synthesis is not expected to fully compensate); if the model implements redundant SpoT synthetic activity, the relA KO may not fully collapse bimodality for reasons unrelated to the RelA-specific mechanism.

Each (seed, generation) growth_rate and its co-recorded ppgpp_conc are treated as a single paired instance for both bimodality testing and cluster-median comparison; this pairing is WITHIN a single run's own instance stream (not across separate runs or across a pre/post timeline split), so no cross-run seed-identity tracking is required or assumed -- this explicitly resolves the prior objection about seed-linkage across a shift.

This hypothesis is scoped STRICTLY to whether a discrete, RelA-dependent slow-growth subpopulation exists under basal conditions -- it makes no claim about bet-hedging, adaptive value, or survival benefit under unpredictable future environments, since the envelope offers only a single deterministic scheduled timeline and no actual antibiotic-exposure/survival-counting perturbation to test such claims.

Basal media is used as a stand-in for 'nutrient-limited, stress-relevant' conditions; the slow-growth/high-ppGpp phenotype is the sole operationalization of the stringent-response subpopulation, not a direct measure of antibiotic survival.

objection_ledger.issue: The claim's framing still invokes 'preparedness for unpredictable change' in the user's question, but the only timeline the envelope supports is a single deterministic, scheduled shift — so the test genuinely cannot speak to whether the benefit depends on the environment being unpredictable (vs. just occurring at all). This is correctly listed as an auxiliary assumption already, so it should not be pressed further as substantive.

The claim is still titled 'population-level bet-hedging' and the predicted_effect/falsifier language retains that framing, but the test (a homogeneous ppGpp clamp vs wildtype) only shows a conditional/plastic trade-off in a uniform population, not bet-hedging (which requires heterogeneous subpopulations and variance-reduction under unpredictable environment timing). The auxiliary_assumptions acknowledge the simulator can't produce true subpopulation coexistence, but the hypothesis's own wording and h1/h0 still assert a bet-hedging interpretation that this design cannot support or refute — the conclusion drawn from the decisive test would overstate what was tested.

The claim, h1/h0, and predicted_effect still use 'bet-hedging' and 'population-level benefit/survival variance reduction' language, but the actual decisive test only compares two homogeneous populations (clamped vs wildtype), never a mixed population facing stochastic environment timing. This is phenotypic plasticity / anticipatory regulation, not bet-hedging, and the labeling misrepresents what the falsifier can establish. Either rename the construct (e.g., 'conditional stringent-response trade-off') or drop bet-hedging-specific language from claim/h1/h0/predicted_effect.

The decisive test compares post-shift division_rate between pre-shift ppGpp quartiles WITHIN the same timeline run, but it never specifies how seeds are held fixed/tracked across the shift (same seed's pre- and post-shift values must be linked). If seed identity/stochastic lineage isn't preserved across the pre/post split, the quartile stratification is just re-randomizing which seeds count as 'high' vs 'low', confounding the result. This needs to be stated explicitly as how seed-level pre/post pairing is guaranteed in the simulator.

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: Persister-like survival without genetic resistance arises from a stochastic, population-level switch into a stringent-response/ppGpp-high, low-growth physiological state: a subpopulation of isogenic wildtype cells (no gene changes) shows elevated ppgpp_conc and depressed growth_rate at a given timepoint, and this fraction is causally driven by ppGpp accumulation (not merely correlated with it).
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic wildtype seeds under basal media, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate at late timepoints is bimodal (a low-growth persister-like mode and a high-growth normal mode), with the low-growth mode associated with elevated ppgpp_conc; this bimodality is abolished (unimodal, high-growth only) when ppGpp synthesis is genetically removed (relA/spoT knockout), and is reproduced (phenocopied) by clamping ppGpp to a high multiple of basal in an otherwise wildtype background — establishing that elevated ppGpp is SUFFICIENT (clamp) and relA/spoT-dependent synthesis is NECESSARY (knockout) for the low-growth mode, independent of any particular perturbation timeline.
hypothesis.h0: growth_rate across isogenic wildtype seeds is unimodally distributed (no distinct low-growth subpopulation), and any seed-to-seed variance in growth_rate or ppgpp_conc is small stochastic noise uncorrelated with a discrete persister-like state; removing ppGpp synthesis genes does not change the shape of the growth_rate distribution, and clamping ppGpp high does not induce a low-growth mode.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed growth_rate at generation 3-4, pooled across seeds, tested for bimodality (Sarle's BC)

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed ppgpp_conc at generation 3-4, fold-change vs reference mean

operational_defs.construct: causal sufficiency of ppGpp for the low-growth mode

operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed division_rate at generation 3-4; low-growth mode must NOT coincide exclusively with division_rate<1 to rule out a bookkeeping artifact

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Bimodal growth_rate distribution in wildtype/basal with BC > 0.555, low-growth mode comprising ~10-20% of seeds/cells and showing >=2-fold higher ppgpp_conc than the high-growth mode, with division_rate not systematically <1 in that mode (ruling out the artifact rival). In relA/spoT knockout, growth_rate becomes unimodal (BC <= 0.555), low-growth-mode occupancy drops >=5-fold toward ~0%. In the ppGpp clamp (3x basal, constitutive — no timeline/shift involved), mean growth_rate drops by >=30% relative to wildtype/basal (Welch |t|>=2), demonstrating that elevated ppGpp alone, in a static condition, is sufficient to reproduce the low-growth phenotype — decoupling the claim entirely from any scheduled-perturbation-timing confound.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values at generation 3-4 for wildtype/basal; reject H0 (support persister claim) if BC>0.555. Then (i) compare relA_spoT_ko: if its BC also exceeds 0.555 (bimodality persists despite ppGpp synthesis removal), necessity is refuted; (ii) separately, Welch t of growth_rate means between ppgpp_conc/clamp_high and wildtype/basal must give |t|>=2 with clamp mean lower, to support sufficiency. Both arms use static (non-timeline) conditions, so no claim about anticipatory/predictive timing is made -- the hypothesis is restricted to a ppGpp-dependent setpoint shift, not an evolved anticipation mechanism.
falsifier.refuting_result: wildtype/basal growth_rate BC <= 0.555 (unimodal, no persister subpopulation), OR relA_spoT_ko growth_rate remains bimodal (BC>0.555) with low-growth-mode fraction not reduced by >=5-fold, OR ppgpp_conc/clamp_high growth_rate is not significantly lower than wildtype/basal (|t|<2), any of which indicates the low-growth state is not ppGpp-dependent.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate; paired with Welch t for the clamp arm
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for bimodal classification in wildtype/basal and relA_spoT_ko must fall to BC<=0.555; clamp arm requires Welch |t|>=2 vs wildtype/basal

rivals.claim: Growth_rate heterogeneity is driven by generic metabolic/cell-cycle noise (e.g. asynchronous division timing or stochastic protein partitioning), not a discrete ppGpp-high stringent state.
rivals.distinguishing_result: growth_rate is bimodal or heavy-tailed in wildtype but ppgpp_conc shows NO corresponding bimodality/fold-change between the two growth_rate modes (low-growth cells do not have elevated ppgpp_conc), the ppGpp clamp fails to depress growth_rate, and relA_spoT_ko does not change the growth_rate distribution shape.

rivals.claim: Any apparent low-growth subpopulation is an artifact of division_rate failures (cells that fail to divide, not a physiological persister state), i.e. a bookkeeping/viability truncation rather than a stringent-response switch.
rivals.distinguishing_result: the low-growth mode in wildtype coincides with division_rate < 1 in the same seeds (a few seeds simply fail to complete division) rather than with elevated ppgpp_conc, and relA_spoT_ko leaves division_rate failures unchanged while growth_rate bimodality persists.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variability under isogenic wildtype conditions is sufficient to sample both a putative low-growth and high-growth mode within 6-8 seeds; if the underlying model has very low intrinsic noise, bimodality may not emerge even if persistence exists biologically (a model-capacity caveat, not evidence against the biological phenomenon).

relA/spoT knockout is treated as a feasible dual-gene knockout (multi_gene_knockout) within the envelope; if the platform cannot mechanistically simulate this double deletion's effect on ppGpp synthesis, the necessity arm is inconclusive rather than refuting.

Division_rate and growth_rate are computed independently per seed/generation in the instrument, allowing us to distinguish a true physiological low-growth mode from a division-failure artifact (rival 2).

The ppgpp_conc clamp at 3x basal under a static condition is used as an interventional sufficiency control; it establishes that elevated ppGpp alone (absent any perturbation timing/shift) reduces growth_rate, and this scope is deliberately restricted to physiological-setpoint causality -- it does NOT test, and we do not claim anything about, whether ppGpp confers an advantage specifically under unpredictable vs predictable antibiotic/stress timing (that anticipatory-benefit question is out of scope for this instrument and is left as an explicit caveat rather than chased further).

objection_ledger.issue: The decisive test compares a fixed, scheduled amino_acid_shift at generation-matched timeline for both wildtype and clamp. Because the shift timing is deterministic and known to the experimenter (and implicitly 'useful information' the clamp strain doesn't actually have to anticipate), the result cannot distinguish a genuine evolved anticipatory/bet-hedging benefit (which should matter most when shift TIMING is unpredictable or rare) from a trivial effect where elevated steady-state ppGpp simply produces different RelA/charging kinetics that happen to react faster to ANY perturbation, scheduled or not. A single deterministic timeline cannot show the benefit is specifically about coping with unpredictability vs. just being a different, generically more shift-robust physiological setpoint.

The decisive test compares post-shift division_rate between pre-shift ppGpp quartiles WITHIN the same timeline run, but it never specifies how seeds are held fixed/tracked across the shift (same seed's pre- and post-shift values must be linked). If seed identity/stochastic lineage isn't preserved across the pre/post split, the quartile stratification is just re-randomizing which seeds count as 'high' vs 'low', confounding the result. This needs to be stated explicitly as how seed-level pre/post pairing is guaranteed in the simulator.

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: A subpopulation of genetically wild-type E. coli survives acute amino-acid limitation (an antibiotic-relevant stress proxy) not via resistance mutations but via stochastic induction of the stringent response: cell-to-cell noise in RelA/ppGpp signaling produces a bimodal split in growth_rate into a fast-growing majority and a slow-growing, high-ppGpp 'persister-like' minority. This minority is causally dependent on RelA-driven ppGpp synthesis rather than on ribosome-capacity limitation per se: deleting relA collapses the bimodality, whereas directly cutting ribosome capacity (rrna_operon_knockout) reproduces a low-growth state WITHOUT requiring the same ppGpp elevation, and clamping ppGpp high in the rRNA-knockout background should still produce (or restore) the slow/tolerant phenotype if ppGpp -- not ribosome reserve per se -- is the operative lever.
hypothesis.h1: Across replicate seeds under an acute amino-acid downshift (basal -> amino-acid-starved timeline), pooled per-cell growth_rate is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with a low-growth ('persister-like') fraction of ~5-20%, and that low-growth cluster shows ppgpp_conc >=2-fold higher than the fast-growing cluster. This bimodality and the ppGpp elevation are RelA-dependent: relA gene_knockout under the same timeline collapses BC to <=0.555 and lowers mean ppgpp_conc by >=2-fold (Welch |t|>=2 vs wildtype/aa_starved). Ribosome-capacity reduction alone (rrna_operon_knockout) is NOT sufficient to reproduce the ppGpp-linked phenotype: when ppGpp is clamped high (ppgpp_conc=3x) in the rrna_operon_knockout background, growth_rate bimodality/low-growth behavior persists or is restored (vs the knockout alone), showing ppGpp -- not ribosome reserve -- is the operative causal lever.
hypothesis.h0: growth_rate under the amino-acid downshift timeline is unimodal across seeds (BC<=0.555), indistinguishable in shape from wildtype/basal; OR if a low-growth mode exists, it is NOT RelA-dependent (relA knockout fails to reduce ppgpp_conc or collapse BC, |t|<2) and/or is fully explained by ribosome capacity alone (ppGpp clamp in the rRNA-knockout background changes nothing relative to the knockout-alone condition).

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed instantaneous growth_rate (1/h) pooled across seeds under the amino-acid-starved timeline; bimodality assessed via Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled values

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc (uM) in the low-growth cluster vs the high-growth cluster, fold-change computed post-hoc from the bimodality split

operational_defs.measure: change in BC and in low-growth fraction, and Welch t on mean ppgpp_conc, when relA is deleted, compared against the amino-acid-starved wildtype design

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate distribution shape under rrna_operon_knockout alone vs rrna_operon_knockout + ppgpp_conc=3x clamp
operational_defs.measure: BC and low-growth fraction compared between the ribosome-limited background with and without a forced high ppGpp clamp; if ppGpp restores/maintains the low-growth bimodal phenotype independent of ribosome reserve, this supports ppGpp as the operative lever

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Bimodal growth_rate under wildtype/aa_starved: BC>0.555, low-growth fraction ~5-20%, ppgpp_conc in that cluster >=2-fold higher than the fast cluster. relA knockout: BC drops to <=0.555 and mean ppgpp_conc falls by >=2-fold (|t|>=2) relative to wildtype/aa_starved. rrna_operon_knockout alone: may show a low-growth shift but WITHOUT the same >=2-fold ppgpp_conc elevation (ribosome-reserve-only effect). rrna_operon_knockout + ppgpp_conc=3x clamp: low-growth/bimodal phenotype is maintained or restored (BC>0.555) relative to rrna_operon_knockout alone, supporting ppGpp (not just ribosome capacity) as causal.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Sarle's BC over pooled per-seed growth_rate for wildtype/aa_starved vs wildtype/basal; reject H0 (no subpopulation) if BC>0.555 under aa_starved and <=0.555 under basal. Secondary (RelA-dependence): Welch t of ppgpp_conc, relA_knockout/aa_starved vs wildtype/aa_starved; reject H1's RelA-dependence claim if |t|<2 (no significant drop). Tertiary (discriminating control): Sarle's BC of growth_rate, rrna_operon_knockout+ppgpp_clamp/aa_starved vs rrna_operon_knockout/aa_starved alone; if the clamp FAILS to restore/maintain BC>0.555 (i.e. BC stays <=0.555 regardless of clamp), this refutes ppGpp-as-causal-lever and supports the ribosome-reserve rival.
falsifier.refuting_result: growth_rate under wildtype/aa_starved stays unimodal (BC<=0.555), OR relA_knockout/aa_starved shows no significant ppgpp_conc drop (|t|<2) with bimodality persisting unchanged, OR the ppGpp clamp in the rRNA-knockout background fails to change BC/low-growth fraction relative to rRNA-knockout alone -- any of these indicates the low-growth mode is not RelA/ppGpp-driven as claimed.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled growth_rate; secondary Welch t on ppgpp_conc (relA_ko vs wildtype); tertiary BC comparison (rRNA-ko+clamp vs rRNA-ko alone)
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for bimodality (and <=0.555 to disconfirm); |t|>=2 for relA-dependence of ppGpp drop

rivals.claim: Rival A - deterministic growth-rate heterogeneity: apparent bimodality is a cell-cycle/mass-timing artifact, not a distinct ppGpp-driven state.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the low-growth cluster's ppgpp_conc would NOT differ significantly from the high-growth cluster (Welch |t|<2 on ppgpp_conc between clusters) even though growth_rate itself looks bimodal.

rivals.claim: Rival B - ribosome-capacity limitation independent of ppGpp: the slow subpopulation arises from stochastic ribosome partitioning/reserve, not active RelA signaling; ppGpp is a correlated readout, not a cause.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, rrna_operon_knockout/aa_starved reproduces a low-growth cluster, AND clamping ppGpp high in that same ribosome-limited background (rrna_operon_knockout+ppgpp_conc=3x) does NOT restore/maintain bimodality beyond what rrna_operon_knockout alone shows -- i.e. the clamp is causally inert once ribosome reserve is already cut, whereas H1 predicts the clamp rescues/maintains the phenotype.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's amino_acid_shift/timeline mechanism for acute starvation produces measurable per-seed, per-generation growth_rate heterogeneity (not just a single population-average trajectory) sufficient to assess bimodality via pooled seed values.

relA gene_knockout is mechanistically simulated as abolishing RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis under starvation (not merely a label with no kinetic effect) under whichever charging module (steady-state or kinetic) is in use.

The platform permits combining rrna_operon_knockout with a ppgpp_conc clamp as a single background perturbation (not a forbidden multi-perturbation combination); if the envelope rejects this combination at run time, the tertiary discriminating test is treated as a capability gap and the design falls back to comparing rrna_operon_knockout alone vs relA_knockout alone as the best available discriminator.

Pooling growth_rate across 6 seeds x 3 generations gives enough independent data points for a stable BC estimate; each seed-generation sample is treated as quasi-independent for this exploratory test.
ppgpp_conc is recorded at steady-state charging unless the kinetic RelA/SpoT module is engaged; results are interpreted within whichever module the platform uses by default.

This design tests a conditional/plastic stringent-response mechanism of survival, NOT true evolutionary bet-hedging (which requires pre-existing heterogeneity and variance-reduction under unpredictable future conditions) -- the claim and interpretation are scoped to RelA/ppGpp-dependent phenotypic tolerance, not to bet-hedging terminology.

The design cannot speak to whether the survival benefit depends on environmental unpredictability (vs. simply occurring), since the instrument only supports a single deterministic scheduled timeline; this is an acknowledged scope limit, not a claim defect.

objection_ledger.issue: The rrna_operon_knockout control as specified (rrna_operon_knockout/basal, without ppGpp clamp) tests whether ribosome reserve alone matters, but it does NOT cross ribosome depletion WITH the ppGpp clamp. To actually discriminate 'ppGpp signaling causes resilience' from 'ribosome reserve causes resilience' you need the interventional cell: rrna_operon_knockout AND ppgpp_conc=3x together, compared to ppgpp_conc=3x alone. As designed, the knockout-only condition only shows that losing ribosomes hurts recovery in a non-clamped background — it leaves open whether the clamped+knockout condition would still show resilience (supporting ppGpp-as-cause) or lose it (supporting ribosome-reserve-as-cause). The rival is stated but the design does not include the cell that actually separates it.

The claim is still titled 'population-level bet-hedging' and the predicted_effect/falsifier language retains that framing, but the test (a homogeneous ppGpp clamp vs wildtype) only shows a conditional/plastic trade-off in a uniform population, not bet-hedging (which requires heterogeneous subpopulations and variance-reduction under unpredictable environment timing). The auxiliary_assumptions acknowledge the simulator can't produce true subpopulation coexistence, but the hypothesis's own wording and h1/h0 still assert a bet-hedging interpretation that this design cannot support or refute — the conclusion drawn from the decisive test would overstate what was tested.

The claim's framing still invokes 'preparedness for unpredictable change' in the user's question, but the only timeline the envelope supports is a single deterministic, scheduled shift — so the test genuinely cannot speak to whether the benefit depends on the environment being unpredictable (vs. just occurring at all). This is correctly listed as an auxiliary assumption already, so it should not be pressed further as substantive.
