operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state ppgpp_conc (uM), used to corroborate the low-growth mode as high-ppGpp

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate in relA gene_knockout background
operational_defs.measure: bimodality coefficient and mean/variance of growth_rate distribution compared to wildtype

drafts.predicted_effect: Wildtype pooled growth_rate across seeds shows bimodal shape (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with an estimated minor-mode fraction of ~10-20% of seeds at a growth_rate roughly 3-5x lower than the major mode (e.g. major mode ~1.0-1.2 /h, minor mode ~0.2-0.3 /h); ppgpp_conc in the minor mode is predicted to be elevated ~2-3 fold over the major mode. In the relA knockout, the distribution collapses to unimodal (BC <= 0.555) and ppgpp_conc dispersion (CV) drops by >=50% relative to wildtype.

falsifier.decision_rule: Compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values for wildtype/basal; reject unimodal H0 if BC>0.555. Then compare dispersion/shape of growth_rate between wildtype/basal and relA gene_knockout/basal using Welch's t on variance-stabilized (log) growth_rate across seeds; if |t|>=2 with relA-KO showing reduced spread/no minor mode, this supports relA-dependence.
falsifier.refuting_result: If wildtype/basal growth_rate BC<=0.555 (unimodal) OR if relA gene_knockout/basal shows an equally bimodal distribution (BC>0.555, |t|<2 vs wildtype), H1 is refuted — persistence shape does not depend on stringent response as claimed.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed growth_rate; secondary welch_disconfirm on growth_rate wildtype vs relA-KO
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for wildtype to confirm bimodality; |welch_t|>=2 for wildtype vs relA-KO comparison to confirm dependence

rivals.claim: Persistence is not a discrete bistable subpopulation but reflects continuous, unimodal cell-to-cell variation in growth rate (noise without bistability) — i.e., antibiotic survival is stochastic survival of a continuum, not a distinct dormant state.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled wildtype growth_rate distribution is unimodal (BC<=0.555) with a long tail rather than two separable modes; relA knockout changes mean/variance only marginally (|welch_t|<2), since there is no discrete mode to abolish.

rivals.claim: Low-growth states arise from ribosome-capacity limitation (rRNA operon dosage) rather than active ppGpp signaling — i.e., persistence is a passive consequence of ribosome scarcity, not an active stringent-response program.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal produces a similar or stronger bimodal/low-growth shift in growth_rate than wildtype, while relA knockout does NOT abolish the low-growth mode (BC remains >0.555), indicating ribosome capacity, not RelA/ppGpp, drives the minor mode.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Antibiotic survival without genetic resistance ("persistence") arises because a subpopulation of isogenic cells spontaneously enters a stringent-response-driven dormancy state (high ppGpp, low growth rate, low ribosome content) even in unperturbed, drug-free growth conditions. This pre-existing physiological heterogeneity — not mutation — is what a tolerant subpopulation would exploit to survive antibiotic exposure. The simulator cannot apply an antibiotic directly, so the operational claim is pushed to the upstream, testable mechanism: wild-type E. coli growing in steady basal conditions shows a bimodal, long-tailed distribution of ppgpp_conc / growth_rate across isogenic replicate cells (seeds), with a distinguishable low-growth/high-ppGpp subpopulation comprising roughly 5-15% of the population, and this subpopulation is abolished (collapses to unimodal) when the stringent response is genetically disabled (relA knockout).
drafts.h1: Across isogenic wild-type replicates (seeds) in basal media, the joint distribution of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with a minority low-growth/high-ppGpp mode containing ~5-15% of seeds; this minority mode depends on a functional stringent response and disappears (distribution becomes unimodal, BC <= 0.555) when relA is knocked out.
drafts.h0: The distribution of growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) across isogenic wild-type seeds in basal media is unimodal (BC <= 0.555), i.e. there is no distinguishable dormant/persister-like subpopulation; relA knockout produces no significant change in distribution shape or in mean ppgpp_conc/growth_rate relative to wild-type.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc per seed at steady state
operational_defs.measure: per-seed scalar values of growth_rate (1/h) and ppgpp_conc (uM) pooled across many seeds, then Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on each channel's pooled distribution

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate in relA knockout vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: Welch's t-test of per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate, relA_knockout vs wildtype/basal, plus BC recomputed on the relA_knockout pooled distribution

operational_defs.observable: fraction of seeds falling in the low-growth/high-ppGpp cluster identified by the bimodality split
operational_defs.measure: proportion of seeds below the trough of the fitted 2-cluster split (from bimodality_bc), reported as a %

drafts.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc across >=40 pooled wildtype seeds (BC > 0.555), with the minor low-growth/high-ppGpp cluster comprising 5-15% of seeds and showing ~2-3x higher ppgpp_conc and ~0.5x (50% lower) growth_rate than the major cluster. In relA_knockout/basal, this bimodality collapses (BC <= 0.555, unimodal) and mean ppgpp_conc drops by >=50% (Welch |t|>=2) relative to wildtype/basal.

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Sarle's bimodality coefficient on pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc (and growth_rate) values for wildtype/basal across >=40 seeds (8 seeds x 5 reps or pooled across generations); reject H0 (claim bimodality) if BC>0.555. Secondary/discriminant: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, relA_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal across seeds; reject H1-dependence-on-stringent-response if |t|<2 (i.e. relA KO fails to collapse ppGpp level/distribution).
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled wildtype ppgpp_conc and growth_rate distributions are unimodal (BC<=0.555) indicating no distinguishable dormant subpopulation, OR relA_knockout/basal shows BC>0.555 and |welch_t|<2 vs wildtype (bimodality persists independent of stringent response), refuting a stringent-response-specific mechanism.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc and growth_rate
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for bimodal claim in wildtype/basal; BC<=0.555 in relA_knockout/basal confirms dependence

rivals.claim: Persistence is driven by stochastic fluctuations in ribosome/protein content (slow-growth noise) independent of the ppGpp stringent response — i.e. generic translational noise, not a regulated alarmone switch.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, relA_knockout/basal would still show bimodal growth_rate (BC>0.555) and a low-growth subpopulation even though ppgpp_conc is flat/low and unimodal — i.e. growth_rate bimodality survives loss of ppGpp while ppGpp bimodality does not.

rivals.claim: Apparent bimodality in basal wildtype is an artifact of insufficient sampling / transient early-generation noise rather than a true stable subpopulation, and would vanish with more generations or seeds.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If this rival is true, the bimodality coefficient on wildtype/basal would trend toward unimodal (BC decreasing toward <=0.555) as seeds/generations increase from the baseline design to an expanded design with more seeds, rather than remaining stably bimodal.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variability under steady_state elongation is sufficient to produce detectable heterogeneity in ppgpp_conc/growth_rate; if the steady-state charging model enforces near-deterministic per-seed trajectories, bimodality may be undetectable regardless of biology (a simulator-resolution caveat, not evidence against H1).

relA knockout is assumed to functionally reduce/abolish ppGpp synthesis in this model (the stringent response module); if relA KO is not mechanistically wired to ppgpp_conc in the simulated metabolic network, the discriminating control is uninformative (flagged as a scope caveat).

Pooling per-seed scalar values (one value per seed, e.g. generation-4 steady-state reading) is treated as the unit of analysis for bimodality; within-seed temporal fluctuation is not separately modeled here.

No antibiotic-killing channel exists in the instrument; survival-under-drug itself is out of scope and the claim is restricted to the upstream physiological heterogeneity that the persistence literature attributes as its cause.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Persister-like survival without genetic resistance arises from a stochastic, non-genetic switch into a stringent-response (ppGpp-high) dormant state: in an isogenic wildtype population under nutrient stress, a subpopulation of cells spontaneously spikes ppGpp and collapses growth rate, producing a bimodal (not unimodal) distribution of growth_rate/ppgpp_conc across seeds even though no mutation is introduced; knocking out relA (the main stringent-response ppGpp synthetase) should abolish this bimodality and compress the population into a single fast-growing mode, confirming the dormancy switch is ppGpp-dependent rather than an artifact of generic simulation noise.
drafts.h1: Across an isogenic wildtype population under nutrient (amino-acid) stress, per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc values are bimodally distributed (Sarle's BC > 0.555), with a persister-like low-growth/high-ppGpp subpopulation comprising roughly 5-20% of seeds; this bimodality requires RelA-dependent ppGpp production and is abolished (BC drops toward unimodal, <0.555) when relA is knocked out.
drafts.h0: Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc values across isogenic seeds under nutrient stress are unimodally distributed (BC <= 0.555), i.e. survival/dormancy is not a discrete bistable switch but continuous stochastic variation around a single mode, and relA knockout does not significantly change the distribution shape or bimodality coefficient relative to wildtype.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed instantaneous growth_rate (1/h) pooled across seeds at end of timeline; low-growth mode = growth_rate < 50% of population median

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed ppGpp concentration (uM) pooled across seeds; high-ppGpp mode = ppgpp_conc > 2x basal wildtype mean

operational_defs.observable: pooled per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc distributions
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled seed values; BC>0.555 flags bimodal

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate distributions under relA knockout
operational_defs.measure: BC and mean-shift of relA_knockout vs wildtype under identical stress timeline

drafts.predicted_effect: Wildtype under amino-acid starvation: BC > 0.555 for pooled growth_rate across seeds, with an estimated 5-20% of seeds falling into a low-growth (<50% median) high-ppGpp (>2x basal) persister-like mode; relA knockout under the same stress collapses this to BC < 0.555 (unimodal) and shifts mean ppgpp_conc down by >=50% relative to wildtype-stress.

falsifier.decision_rule: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values from wildtype/amino_acid_stress (n>=24 seeds via multiple seed batches); reject H1 (treat as unimodal/no discrete switch) if BC<=0.555. Confirm RelA-dependence via Welch t of growth_rate and ppgpp_conc, relA_knockout/amino_acid_stress vs wildtype/amino_acid_stress; reject ppGpp-dependence if |welch_t|<2 or if relA_knockout/amino_acid_stress ALSO shows BC>0.555 (bimodality persists without RelA).
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled growth_rate across >=24 wildtype-stress seeds gives BC<=0.555 (single continuous mode, no discrete persister subpopulation), OR relA knockout fails to reduce BC below 0.555 and fails to show |welch_t|>=2 drop in ppgpp_conc/growth_rate shift relative to wildtype-stress, indicating the heterogeneity (if any) is RelA-independent.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed growth_rate (primary) and ppgpp_conc (secondary)
test.threshold: BC > 0.555 => bimodal (supports H1); BC <= 0.555 => unimodal (refutes H1)

rivals.claim: Rival A: survival is driven by generic stochastic gene-expression noise (e.g. variable ribosome_conc or protein_mass) unrelated to a specific ppGpp stringent-response switch -- any apparent growth_rate bimodality is a byproduct of intrinsic simulation noise, not a regulated dormancy program.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, relA knockout would NOT reduce bimodality coefficient or shift ppgpp_conc/growth_rate relative to wildtype-stress (BC stays >0.555 and welch_t on ppgpp_conc stays |t|<2), because the heterogeneity is RelA-independent and driven by other noise sources.

rivals.claim: Rival B: apparent heterogeneity is not a discrete bistable switch but continuous graded slowdown proportional to stress severity -- i.e. growth_rate scales smoothly (unimodally) with nutrient depletion across the population, with no distinct subpopulation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled growth_rate distribution across wildtype-stress seeds shows BC<=0.555 (single broad unimodal peak) rather than two separable modes, even though mean growth_rate is reduced relative to basal wildtype.

auxiliary_assumptions: Pooling growth_rate/ppgpp_conc across 24+ independent seeds (4-6 seeds x 4-6 batches) approximates a population-level distribution sufficient for a bimodality coefficient estimate.
amino_acid_shift (removal of an amino acid mid-timeline) is an adequate operationalization of 'nutrient stress' capable of triggering a stringent response in this simulator.

relA_knockout is mechanistically wired to reduce ppGpp synthesis in the model (checked downstream); if RelA/SpoT module genes are not simulated, this falsifier cannot discriminate and is logged as a capability gap.

Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are read under steady-state charging (ppGpp/ribosome channels available) rather than kinetic-only mode, since relA_conc and ppgpp_conc require steady-state or RelA/SpoT-module-on recording.
A single stress timeline/condition combination is treated as representative of 'nutrient stress' generally; broader generalization across other stressors is out of scope for this test.

params.label: ppgpp_clamp_low/amino_acid_stress
params.note: discriminating control: clamping ppGpp low during stress should also abolish bimodality if ppGpp is causally required, independent of relA's other potential pleiotropic effects

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: A subpopulation of genetically wild-type E. coli cells survives bactericidal antibiotic-like stress not via resistance mutations but via a stochastically induced, high-ppGpp 'persister' physiological state (elevated stringent response, reduced growth rate, reduced ribosome concentration) that pre-exists or is triggered by stress, and this state is a graded/bimodal population phenomenon, not a universal or absent response.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic wild-type populations under nutrient-downshift (stringent-response-inducing) stress, the distribution of per-seed/per-cell ppGpp_conc and growth_rate is bimodal: a minority fraction (predicted ~10-20%) of cells/seeds occupy a low-growth-rate, high-ppGpp 'persister-like' state, distinguishable from the bulk fast-growing state, and this fraction is abolished (collapses toward unimodal) when ppGpp induction is blocked (relA-pathway knockout), demonstrating the state is ppGpp-dependent rather than an artifact of generic growth noise.
drafts.h0: The population response to stress is unimodal: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate across seeds/cells form a single continuous distribution with no distinguishable high-ppGpp/low-growth subpopulation (Sarle's BC <= 0.555), and relA knockout does not significantly change the distribution shape or the mean ppGpp/growth_rate response to stress relative to wild-type.

operational_defs.measure: per-seed (ppgpp_conc, growth_rate) pairs across seeds pooled; bimodality coefficient on ppgpp_conc distribution

operational_defs.construct: stringent response induction under antibiotic-like stress
operational_defs.observable: amino_acid_shift perturbation (removal of an amino acid mid-run) as a stress proxy inducing ribosome stalling/charging deficit, since direct antibiotic exposure is not a listed perturbation
operational_defs.measure: fraction_trna_charged drop and ppgpp_conc rise relative to wildtype/basal

operational_defs.observable: rela gene knockout removing ppGpp synthesis capacity
operational_defs.measure: comparison of ppgpp_conc and bimodality_bc of growth_rate between wildtype-stress and relA_KO-stress conditions

operational_defs.observable: division_rate channel remaining >0 (cells persist, don't die) despite reduced growth_rate, with no genetic/resistance mechanism simulated (no efflux/target-mutation perturbation applied)
operational_defs.measure: division_rate per seed under stress vs reference

drafts.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of ppgpp_conc and growth_rate across seeds under amino-acid-downshift stress, with Sarle's BC > 0.555 and an estimated low-growth/high-ppGpp fraction of 10-20% of seeds; this high-ppGpp subpopulation shows growth_rate reduced by >=50% (fold-change <=0.5x) and ppgpp_conc elevated >=3-fold relative to the bulk/reference state. In relA_knockout/stress, the bimodality collapses (BC <= 0.555) and mean ppgpp_conc response drops by >=70% relative to wildtype/stress (Welch t < 2, non-significant difference from wildtype/basal baseline ppGpp).

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Sarle's bimodality coefficient computed on pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values under amino_acid_shift/stress; reject H0 (unimodal) if BC>0.555. Secondary/control: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, relA_knockout/stress vs amino_acid_shift/stress across seeds; if |t|<2 (no significant drop) the ppGpp-dependence claim is refuted.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC <= 0.555 for amino_acid_shift/stress (distribution is unimodal, no distinguishable persister subpopulation), OR relA_knockout/stress shows ppgpp_conc and bimodality statistically indistinguishable from amino_acid_shift/stress (|t|<2), indicating the putative persister state is not ppGpp-dependent.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values
test.threshold: BC>0.555 to reject unimodal H0; paired with welch_disconfirm |t|>=2 for the relA control comparison

rivals.claim: Rival A: The low-growth/high-ppGpp state is purely a universal, deterministic shift of ALL cells under stress (graded stringent response), not a bimodal subpopulation split — i.e., persistence is a population-wide average physiological adjustment, not heterogeneity.
rivals.distinguishing_result: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate distributions under amino_acid_shift/stress remain unimodal (BC<=0.555) with a shifted mean, rather than showing a distinct minority cluster.

rivals.claim: Rival B: Apparent 'persister' heterogeneity is simply stochastic replicate noise (seed-to-seed variability) unrelated to ppGpp/stringent response mechanism — i.e., any bimodal-looking split is an artifact of small-seed sampling, not a real ppGpp-driven state.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA_knockout/stress shows the SAME bimodal split and fraction as wildtype/stress (BC remains >0.555, ppgpp_conc control comparison |t|<2), meaning the heterogeneity persists even without ppGpp synthesis capacity, implicating generic noise rather than the stringent response.

auxiliary_assumptions: amino_acid_shift (removal of an amino acid mid-run) is an acceptable in-envelope proxy for antibiotic/nutritional stress since direct antibiotic perturbations are not in the instrument's perturbation list.
relA gene_knockout sufficiently abolishes stringent-response ppGpp induction in this simulator (spoT-mediated basal synthesis is assumed negligible for this comparison).

The simulator's per-seed stochastic variation under kinetic/coarse_kinetic elongation is a valid proxy for genuine cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity (bet-hedging), not merely numerical noise — this is a scope caveat the simulator cannot fully resolve.

division_rate <1 under stress is interpreted as surviving-but-slow-dividing (persister-like) rather than lethality, provided division_rate remains >0; division_rate=0 would indicate death, which is outside the 'survival without resistance' claim.

No resistance-conferring perturbation (e.g., efflux pump upregulation, target mutation) is applied in any condition, isolating the physiological/stochastic persistence mechanism from genetic resistance.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Antibiotic survival without genetic resistance is achieved by a stochastic, non-genetic "persister" state driven by the stringent response: in an isogenic population, a subpopulation of cells spontaneously spikes ppGpp and consequently lowers growth rate into a dormant-like regime, and this fraction is a heritable-free, seed-to-seed stochastic phenomenon rather than a uniform population shift. Clamping ppGpp high phenocopies this low-growth survival state, while removing the ppGpp synthetase (relA knockout) abolishes the high-ppGpp/low-growth subpopulation.
drafts.h1: Across an isogenic wildtype population under basal condition, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate is bimodal (a dominant fast-growing mode plus a slow/dormant-like mode comprising ~5-15% of seeds), and that slow mode co-occurs with elevated ppgpp_conc (>=2x the fast-mode median). Clamping ppgpp_conc to a high multiple of basal reproduces the slow-growth phenotype (growth_rate drops by >=40% vs wildtype/basal), and this drop requires RelA: a relA gene_knockout abolishes the ppGpp-associated slow mode / blunts the clamp's effect.
drafts.h0: growth_rate across wildtype/basal seeds is unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555, no distinguishable slow subpopulation); ppgpp_conc clamp at a high multiple produces no significant growth_rate reduction relative to wildtype/basal (Welch |t| < 2); and relA knockout does not change the clamp's effect on growth_rate.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed ppGpp concentration (uM), compared between the fast-growth and slow-growth sub-populations via co-occurrence

drafts.predicted_effect: (1) Bimodal growth_rate distribution across wildtype/basal seeds: BC > 0.555, slow mode = 5-15% of seeds, slow-mode mean growth_rate <= 0.5x fast-mode mean. (2) ppgpp_conc clamp at 4x basal: growth_rate falls by >=40% vs wildtype/basal (fold-change ~0.6x or less). (3) relA knockout blunts this: in relA-KO background, the same 4x ppGpp clamp produces <15% growth_rate reduction (i.e., the clamp effect size drops by >60% relative to relA-intact).

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Welch t of growth_rate, ppgpp_conc-clamp(4x) vs wildtype/basal, across seeds; reject H0 if |t|>=2 AND effect_pct <= -40%. Distributional claim tested separately via Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values from wildtype/basal; reject unimodal null if BC>0.555.
falsifier.refuting_result: If ppgpp_conc clamp at 4x basal shows |t|<2 or effect_pct > -40% vs wildtype/basal (no meaningful growth suppression), OR if wildtype/basal growth_rate is unimodal (BC<=0.555) with no distinguishable slow mode, H1 is refuted.

test.statistic: welch_t and effect_pct on growth_rate
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct<=-40%

rivals.claim: Survival is driven by passive phenotypic/metabolic heterogeneity (e.g., stochastic variation in ribosome_conc or dry_mass at division) unrelated to ppGpp signaling -- a 'growth-rate noise' rival with no causal stringent-response link.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA knockout does NOT blunt the ppgpp_conc-clamp growth suppression (clamp still reduces growth_rate by >=40% in relA-KO background), this indicates the growth suppression is not RelA-pathway-specific and the slow mode may instead track generic noise in ribosome_conc/dry_mass, supporting this rival.

rivals.claim: Survival is a deterministic, ribosome-capacity-limited slowdown (rRNA operon dosage sets a fixed slow growth ceiling for all cells) rather than a stochastic bimodal persister state -- an rrna_operon_knockout should produce a UNIFORM slow population, not a bimodal split.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rrna_operon_knockout/basal produces a unimodal (BC<=0.555) uniformly slow growth_rate distribution across all seeds (not a two-mode split), this supports a deterministic ribosome-capacity rival over the stochastic persister rival.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's intrinsic seed-to-seed stochasticity (molecular noise in gene expression / initial conditions) is a valid proxy for biological cell-to-cell heterogeneity within an isogenic population.

ppgpp_conc clamp at a fixed multiple is mechanistically comparable to an endogenous ppGpp spike in magnitude and downstream effect, even though the clamp is exogenously imposed rather than self-regulated.

growth_rate and division_rate jointly capture 'dormancy/persistence' well enough that we do not need a direct antibiotic-killing readout (the instrument has no explicit survival-under-drug channel, so slow growth / non-division is used as the operational proxy for persister phenotype).

relA knockout is assumed in this simulator to substantially reduce ppGpp synthesis capacity (not fully eliminate, since SpoT may remain), so 'abolish' is interpreted as a strong blunting rather than complete elimination.

20-80 seeds would be ideal to resolve a 5-15% subpopulation and bimodality robustly; the modest seeds=8 run here is a pilot and may be underpowered for the BC test -- flagged as a scope caveat for follow-up scaling.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Antibiotic survival without genetic resistance ("persistence") arises from a stochastically-triggered, reversible stringent-response state: in a subset of an isogenic wildtype population, ppGpp spikes (via RelA activation driven by stochastic amino-acid starvation / low charged-tRNA) drive growth rate toward near-zero, producing a bimodal (dormant vs growing) distribution of growth rates across cells/seeds even under constant, nutrient-replete conditions — NOT a stable resistance mutation. The fraction of cells in the dormant/high-ppGpp state is small (~5-15%) and is causally dependent on RelA/ppGpp machinery, not just general metabolic slowdown.
drafts.h1: Across an isogenic wildtype population under constant basal media, per-seed growth_rate at steady state is bimodally distributed (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with a low-growth-rate subpopulation comprising roughly 5-15% of seeds, and this low-growth mode coincides with elevated ppgpp_conc (>=2x population median) and reduced fraction_trna_charged. Deleting relA (abolishing stochastic ppGpp spiking) collapses this bimodality, shifting the distribution toward unimodal high growth.
drafts.h0: growth_rate across wildtype seeds under constant basal media is unimodal (BC <= 0.555) with no distinct low-growth subpopulation, i.e. any seed-to-seed variance is simple replicate noise unrelated to ppgpp_conc, and relA knockout does not change the distribution shape or spread of growth_rate relative to wildtype.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Antibiotic tolerance without resistance arises because a subpopulation of isogenic, genetically wild-type E. coli stochastically enters a slow-growth 'persister-like' physiological state driven by stringent-response (ppGpp) activation, rather than acquiring any mutation. This is detectable as a bimodal split in growth_rate across seeds/cells under basal conditions, with the slow-growth mode showing elevated ppgpp_conc, and this bimodality should collapse (toward unimodal fast growth) when ppGpp induction is prevented by knocking out relA.
drafts.h1: Across many isogenic replicate seeds under identical (basal) conditions, the distribution of growth_rate is bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with a low-growth-rate subpopulation (roughly 5-20% of seeds) that co-occurs with elevated ppgpp_conc (>=1.5x the fast-growth mode's level), and this bimodality is abolished (or strongly reduced) when relA is knocked out, confirming a ppGpp-dependent stochastic switch rather than genetic resistance.
drafts.h0: growth_rate across isogenic wildtype seeds under basal conditions is unimodal (BC <= 0.555), i.e. there is no distinct slow-growth/high-ppGpp subpopulation; any seed-to-seed variance in growth_rate or ppgpp_conc is continuous replicate noise, and relA knockout does not change the shape of the growth_rate distribution relative to wildtype.

Under relA knockout, BC drops below 0.555 (distribution becomes unimodal) and/or the slow-growth fraction shrinks toward 0%, consistent with loss of the ppGpp-dependent switch.

select_score.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
select_score.claim: Persister-like survival under stringent-response activation arises from ppGpp-driven growth arrest (a phenotypic, non-genetic tolerance state), not from a heritable resistance mutation: clamping ppGpp to high basal multiples in a wildtype population reproduces a drastically slowed-growth, low-ribosome physiological state in a reproducible fraction of the population, and this state is abolished when the ppGpp-synthesis machinery itself is removed (relA knockout), showing it is ppGpp-dependent dormancy rather than a fixed resistant subpopulation.
select_score.h1: Clamping ppGpp to a high multiple of basal (mimicking stringent-response induction) drives a large, reversible drop in growth_rate and ribosome_conc across the population (a shift in the population mean/distribution, not a rare bimodal resistant subclone), and this drop requires intact ppGpp-synthesis capacity: a relA knockout background blunts the growth-rate response to the same nutritional/stress cue.
select_score.h0: Growth_rate and ribosome_conc under ppgpp_conc clamp do not differ from wildtype/basal beyond replicate noise, OR the relA knockout shows the same growth-rate response as wildtype (i.e., the effect is not ppGpp-dependent).

operational_defs.measure: ppgpp_conc channel value relative to basal-condition mean

operational_defs.measure: difference in growth_rate effect size (ppgpp clamp in relA-KO background is infeasible as combined perturbation, so instead compare relA-KO's own growth_rate response to amino_acid_shift/basal vs wildtype's response to the same shift)

select_score.predicted_effect: Growth_rate falls by >=60% (e.g. from ~1.0 1/h basal to <=0.4 1/h) and ribosome_conc falls by >=40% in the ppgpp_conc=5x-basal clamp vs wildtype/basal, applied broadly across the population (seeds), not confined to a rare subclone (i.e., per-seed distribution shifts as a whole, bimodality coefficient <=0.555). In the relA knockout, the growth-rate drop in response to amino-acid downshift is attenuated by at least 50% relative to wildtype's drop under the same shift, indicating ppGpp-synthesis dependence.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of growth_rate, ppgpp_conc=5x target vs wildtype/basal reference, across seeds; reject H0 if two-sided |t|>=2 AND effect_pct <= -40% (growth_rate reduced by at least 40%). Additionally compute bimodality_bc on pooled per-seed growth_rate values for the target design; if BC>0.555 the population-wide framing is refuted (effect is a rare subclone, not a population shift).
falsifier.refuting_result: If Welch |t|<2 or effect_pct > -40% (ppGpp clamp does not substantially slow growth), OR if growth_rate is bimodal with BC>0.555 (only a small fraction of cells arrest while most grow normally), H1 is refuted as stated.

test.threshold: |t|>=2 and effect_pct<=-40%

rivals.distinguishing_result: If wildtype/basal growth_rate (or ribosome_conc) is already bimodal (BC>0.555) across seeds WITHOUT any ppGpp clamp, this supports pre-existing heterogeneity rather than an induced stringent response.

rivals.claim: Rival B: the growth-rate drop under ppGpp clamp is a generic toxicity/off-target artifact of the clamp mechanism itself, not mediated by the normal RelA/SpoT regulatory pathway, so it would persist even without endogenous ppGpp synthesis machinery.

The simulator's relA gene_knockout removes ppGpp synthesis capacity sufficiently to test pathway-dependence, even though RelA is not the sole ppGpp synthetase (SpoT also contributes) — this is a scope caveat, not resolvable by re-running.

Persistence/survival itself (e.g. antibiotic killing) is not a channel the instrument measures directly; growth-rate/ribosome arrest is used as the operational proxy for a dormancy/tolerance phenotype, per the available dials.
Seeds are isogenic stochastic replicates; distributional claims about 'population-wide vs subclone' are read from per-seed spread at a single clamp level, not a genuine single-cell lineage trace.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Antibiotic survival without resistance arises from stochastic persistence: a subpopulation of isogenic E. coli cells enters a transiently dormant, stringent-response (ppGpp-high) state that is accessible to any wildtype cell by intrinsic noise, not by mutation. Operationally, clamping ppGpp to a high multiple of basal mimics this persister-like physiological state and should phenocopy the growth-arrest / dormancy signature seen in the noisy tail of wildtype replicate populations, while a relA-pathway knockout (which prevents cells from ever reaching the high-ppGpp state) should abolish that tail.

drafts.h0: growth_rate across wildtype replicates is unimodal (bimodality coefficient <= 0.555) with no ppGpp-linked low-growth subpopulation; clamping ppgpp_conc to 5x basal does not reduce growth_rate by a Welch-significant amount relative to wildtype/basal; and relA knockout does not change the shape of the growth_rate distribution relative to wildtype.

rivals.claim: Rival B - Metabolic/charging noise independent of ppGpp: dormancy arises from stochastic drops in fraction_trna_charged (nutrient/charging noise) that only secondarily correlate with ppGpp, so ppGpp is a downstream marker, not a cause.

Pooling growth_rate across seeds and generations within a condition is a valid proxy for a population snapshot of phenotypic heterogeneity, since the simulator does not provide a true single-timepoint multi-cell population readout.

The simulator's steady-state tRNA charging module is used (not kinetic), so fraction_trna_charged reflects equilibrium charging rather than fast dynamic fluctuations.

drafts.claim: Persister-like survival under stress is explained by a stochastic, population-level bistability in the stringent response: a subpopulation of isogenic wildtype cells spontaneously enters a high-ppGpp / low-growth-rate state that is phenotypically tolerant without any genetic resistance change, and this fraction grows with ppGpp pathway activity and shrinks when the stringent response is disabled.

rivals.distinguishing_result: growth_rate distribution under wildtype/basal_stress stays unimodal (BC<=0.555) with a single shifted mean, and the ppGpp clamp merely shifts the whole population's mean rather than creating/enlarging a distinct low-growth cluster.

rivals.claim: Any observed low-growth subpopulation is driven by ribosome-capacity limitation (translation capacity bottleneck) rather than by the ppGpp/stringent-response alarmone signal itself -- i.e. rRNA operon dosage, not ppGpp, sets the bimodal split.

Bimodality assessed via Sarle's BC on 8 seeds is treated as a coarse screen consistent with the population-scope question; a larger screen (more seeds/conditions) would be needed to pin down exact fraction estimates, but 8 seeds suffices to detect gross bimodal vs unimodal shape differences.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: A subpopulation of genetically wild-type E. coli survives antibiotic-relevant stress (simulated here as a sudden severe nutrient downshift, i.e. an amino-acid-removal timeline) not via resistance mutations but via a stochastically triggered, reversible stringent-response state (ppGpp spike + growth-rate collapse) that produces a persister-like phenotype. This state arises from intrinsic noise in RelA/ppGpp/ribosome allocation across isogenic cells, not from any genetic change, and should appear as a bimodal (non-resistant) split in growth-rate/ppGpp phenotype across seeds rather than a uniform shift.

drafts.h0: The amino-acid downshift produces a single, unimodal, graded population response: all seeds shift together to a similarly elevated ppgpp_conc and reduced growth_rate (no distinct persister subpopulation), i.e. stress tolerance is a uniform physiological response rather than a bimodal, stochastically-gated one, and relA knockout only shifts the mean response rather than eliminating a distinct subpopulation.

rivals.claim: Uniform stringent response: all cells respond identically and gradedly to downshift (no distinct persister subpopulation); apparent variance is just replicate/measurement noise.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc/growth_rate distribution is unimodal (BC<=0.555) with low seed-to-seed variance, i.e. a single shifted Gaussian rather than two separable clusters.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Antibiotic survival without genetic resistance ("persistence") arises from a stochastically-induced, non-genetic stringent-response state: in a wildtype population a subpopulation of cells transiently spikes ppGpp and crashes growth_rate even in rich/basal media with no perturbation other than intrinsic noise, and this same dormancy-prone state is causally produced (not merely correlated) by the RelA/ppGpp stringent-response module — knocking out relA abolishes the low-growth subpopulation.
drafts.h1: Across an isogenic wildtype population (many seeds), ppgpp_conc and growth_rate are bimodally distributed across seeds, with a minority ( ~10-20%) of seeds occupying a high-ppGpp/low-growth ("persister-like") mode; this bimodality requires RelA, so a relA gene_knockout collapses the distribution to unimodal and shifts mean ppgpp_conc down.
drafts.h0: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate across wildtype seeds are unimodally distributed (Sarle's BC <= 0.555, consistent with ordinary seed-to-seed noise around one mode), and/or a relA knockout does not change the distribution shape or mean ppgpp_conc relative to wildtype.

select_score.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
select_score.claim: Antibiotic survival without resistance arises from stochastic persistence: a subpopulation of isogenic E. coli cells enters a transiently dormant, stringent-response (ppGpp-high) state that is accessible to any wildtype cell by intrinsic noise, not by mutation. Operationally, clamping ppGpp to a high multiple of basal mimics this persister-like physiological state and should phenocopy the growth-arrest / dormancy signature seen in the noisy tail of wildtype replicate populations, while a relA-pathway knockout (which prevents cells from ever reaching the high-ppGpp state) should abolish that tail.
select_score.h1: Across isogenic wildtype replicates, growth_rate shows a long low-growth tail driven by elevated ppgpp_conc in a minority of seeds/replicates (a bimodal-leaning distribution, bimodality coefficient > 0.555), and this low-growth/high-ppGpp state can be reproduced on-demand by clamping ppgpp_conc to ~5x basal (growth_rate drops by >=50% vs wildtype/basal), whereas deleting relA (the ppGpp synthetase) abolishes both the tail and the capacity to enter the dormant state.
select_score.h0: growth_rate across wildtype replicates is unimodal (bimodality coefficient <= 0.555) with no ppGpp-linked low-growth subpopulation; clamping ppgpp_conc to 5x basal does not reduce growth_rate by a Welch-significant amount relative to wildtype/basal; and relA knockout does not change the shape of the growth_rate distribution relative to wildtype.

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: Persister-like survival under stringent stress is a stochastic, non-genetic physiological state: a subpopulation of wildtype E. coli cells, under amino-acid starvation, spikes ppGpp and collapses growth rate into a dormancy-like regime WITHOUT any genetic change, and this occurs in a bimodal (two-state) fashion across isogenic replicate seeds rather than as a uniform population-wide slowdown.
hypothesis.h1: Under an amino-acid downshift (starvation timeline), the distribution of per-seed growth_rate across isogenic wildtype replicates becomes bimodal (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with a low-growth ('persister-like') fraction of roughly 10-30% showing growth_rate near 0 and elevated ppgpp_conc (>=3x basal), while the remaining majority continues near-normal growth — i.e. survival-without-resistance is achieved via stochastic partitioning into a dormant state driven by the stringent response, not by any fixed genetic resistance mechanism.
hypothesis.h0: Growth_rate under the same amino-acid downshift is unimodally distributed across seeds (BC <= 0.555), i.e. all isogenic wildtype cells respond with a similar, graded growth reduction proportional to the shared ppGpp rise, with no distinct dormant subpopulation.

Per-seed terminal growth_rate (end of 3 generations) is a reasonable proxy for persister-like dormancy; we are not tracking single-cell lineage re-growth upon re-feeding, only the instantaneous bimodal split under stress.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Bacterial persistence (survival without genetic resistance) is driven by stochastic entry into a dormancy-like physiological state characterized by elevated ppGpp and reduced growth rate, arising from intrinsic noise in the stringent-response network even in a genetically uniform, isogenic population under constant conditions. This predicts a BIMODAL distribution of per-cell growth rate / ppGpp across seeds (a small 'persister' subpopulation with high ppGpp and near-zero growth), not a unimodal shift, and this bimodality should collapse toward unimodal when the stringent-response trigger (RelA) is removed.
drafts.h1: Across an isogenic population (wildtype/basal, many seeds), the distribution of steady-state ppgpp_conc (and correspondingly growth_rate) is bimodal: a minority fraction (~5-15%) of seeds/cells occupy a high-ppGpp, low-growth-rate 'persister-like' state while the majority occupy a low-ppGpp, normal-growth state. This bimodality requires RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis: a relA gene_knockout collapses the distribution toward unimodal (low, uniform ppGpp).
drafts.h0: The per-seed distribution of ppgpp_conc (and growth_rate) in wildtype/basal is unimodal (single Gaussian-like mode) with only replicate noise around the mean; any apparent bimodality is sampling artifact, and a relA knockout does not change the shape (bimodality coefficient) of the distribution relative to wildtype.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate per seed
operational_defs.measure: per-seed steady-state value of ppgpp_conc (uM) and growth_rate (1/h) pooled across many seeds; bimodality assessed via Sarle's bimodality coefficient

operational_defs.observable: rela_conc and ppgpp_conc under relA knockout vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: disconfirm(relA_knockout/basal, wildtype/basal, ppgpp_conc) and change in bimodality_bc of ppgpp_conc distribution

operational_defs.observable: fraction of seeds classified as high-ppGpp / low-growth via 2-cluster split
operational_defs.measure: bimodality_bc clustering output: fraction of pooled values assigned to the minority (high) cluster

drafts.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution of ppgpp_conc and growth_rate across a broad seed sample in wildtype/basal, with Sarle's bimodality coefficient BC>0.555 and minority ('persister') cluster fraction ~5-15% showing ppGpp elevated ~3-5x basal and growth_rate reduced to <20% of the majority mode. In relA_knockout/basal, BC should drop below 0.555 (unimodal) and the minority high-ppGpp cluster should disappear (fraction ~0%), with ppgpp_conc reduced by at least 50% (Welch t vs wildtype, |t|>=2).

falsifier.decision_rule: Primary: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (bimodality_bc) over pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc values (n>=40 seeds pooled across 4-8 seeds x conditions) in wildtype/basal; reject H0 (unimodal) if BC>0.555. Secondary/discriminating: Welch t of ppgpp_conc, relA_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal across seeds; reject H1's mechanism-dependence claim if |t|<2 (i.e. knockout fails to lower ppGpp) or if BC for relA_knockout/basal remains >0.555 (bimodality persists despite knockout).
falsifier.refuting_result: Pooled wildtype/basal ppgpp_conc (and growth_rate) is unimodal (BC<=0.555) across >=40 seed-samples, indicating no distinct persister-like subpopulation; OR relA_knockout/basal retains BC>0.555 and/or |t|<2 vs wildtype, indicating the (if present) bimodality is NOT RelA-dependent.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc; paired Welch t for RelA-dependence check
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for bimodal claim in wildtype/basal; BC<=0.555 (collapse) in relA_knockout/basal; |t|>=2 for ppgpp_conc reduction in knockout

rivals.claim: Rival A (deterministic slow-growth niche, not stochastic switching): apparent 'bimodality' simply reflects a continuous unimodal spread of growth rates under basal nutrient limitation, with no distinct RelA-dependent subpopulation — i.e., persistence is a graded response to resource scarcity, not a discrete bistable switch.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, pooled ppgpp_conc/growth_rate in wildtype/basal shows BC<=0.555 (continuous unimodal spread) rather than a clear 2-cluster split, and relA knockout only shifts the mean (not the shape) of the distribution.

rivals.claim: Rival B (toxin-antitoxin / non-ppGpp persistence mechanism): dormancy entry is driven by a mechanism independent of the RelA/ppGpp stringent-response pathway (e.g. a toxin-antitoxin-like growth arrest), so bimodality in growth_rate would persist even after relA knockout, while ppgpp_conc bimodality might or might not track it.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, relA_knockout/basal still shows BC>0.555 for growth_rate distribution (persister-like low-growth subpopulation remains) even though ppgpp_conc bimodality may collapse, showing growth-rate bimodality is NOT ppGpp/RelA-dependent.

auxiliary_assumptions: Per-seed steady-state ppgpp_conc and growth_rate values at the final simulated generation are a valid proxy for 'per-cell' physiological state in a population (the simulator reports one lineage per seed; pooling many seeds approximates sampling many isogenic cells).

The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variability captures the intrinsic noise source relevant to persister formation (not deterministic chaos); we do not attempt to distinguish stochastic noise from deterministic sensitivity to initial conditions mechanistically — this is recorded as an explicit scope caveat.

relA gene_knockout is mechanistically simulated as reducing/eliminating RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis in this model (checked downstream); if the KO is not implemented with phenotypic effect, this falsifier reduces to a power/implementation check rather than a biological refutation.

Basal media condition is nutrient-limited enough to permit stringent-response activation in at least some seeds; if basal is too nutrient-rich for any stringent response to trigger, a null result could reflect condition choice rather than absence of the phenomenon.

No antibiotic-killing readout exists in the instrument; 'survival without resistance' is operationalized purely via the dormancy/stringent-response proxy (ppGpp/growth-rate bimodality), not via direct antibiotic challenge, which is outside the envelope.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Antibiotic survival without genetic resistance (persistence/tolerance) arises from a stochastic, ppGpp-mediated stringent-response subpopulation: a minority of isogenic wildtype cells spontaneously enter a high-ppGpp, low-growth-rate state that is phenotypically but not genetically distinct, and this fraction (and the depth of growth-rate depression) is reduced when the stringent response is disabled (relA knockout), showing the tolerant state is ppGpp-dependent rather than a fixed trait.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic wildtype populations, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate is bimodal (a low-growth-rate shoulder consistent with dormant/tolerant cells) and this shoulder coincides with elevated ppgpp_conc; deleting relA (removing ppGpp synthesis capacity) collapses the low-growth shoulder, shifting the population toward a single growth-rate mode and reducing ppgpp_conc variance, demonstrating the subpopulation is ppGpp-driven rather than a fixed basal distribution.
drafts.h0: Growth_rate across wildtype seeds is unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555) and relA knockout does not change the growth_rate distribution shape or mean ppgpp_conc relative to wildtype (no significant Welch t, |t|<2), i.e. any apparent low-growth subpopulation is sampling noise, not a ppGpp-dependent stringent-response state.

rivals.claim: Persistence is a fixed, deterministic subpopulation set by stochastic gene-expression noise in an unrelated pathway (e.g. toxin-antitoxin systems), independent of ppGpp/stringent response entirely.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA knockout does NOT change the low-growth-rate fraction or BC of growth_rate (BC stays >0.555 and unchanged vs wildtype), showing the subpopulation persists without ppGpp.

rivals.claim: Apparent bimodality in growth_rate is an artifact of cell-cycle/division timing (division_rate variability) rather than a distinct physiological state.
rivals.distinguishing_result: division_rate shows the same bimodal split as growth_rate but ppgpp_conc does NOT differ between the two clusters (no correlation with ppGpp), indicating the split is cycle-timing noise, not stringent-response-driven.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation in growth_rate reflects biologically meaningful intrinsic noise (not purely numerical artifact), sufficient to reveal a bimodal subpopulation across 8 seeds.

relA knockout is mechanistically simulated as removing (RelA-mediated) ppGpp synthesis capacity in this model; if relA is not wired to ppgpp_conc in the model, this falls outside what the simulator can resolve and is logged as a scope caveat rather than re-litigated.

The ppgpp_conc clamp (3x basal) design serves as a positive-control/discriminating condition to confirm that elevated ppGpp alone is sufficient to depress growth_rate, independent of relA's natural induction, helping separate ppGpp's causal role from relA-specific pleiotropy.
Four generations is enough time for a stringent-response-driven low-growth subpopulation to manifest and be distinguished from pure division-timing noise.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Antibiotic survival without genetic resistance ("persistence") arises because a subpopulation of isogenic wildtype cells stochastically enters a stringent-response-like dormancy state (high ppGpp, low growth rate) even in unperturbed basal medium; this pre-existing physiological heterogeneity — not any mutation — is what lets a minority fraction survive. We operationalize this as a bimodal, right-skewed distribution of ppgpp_conc (and correspondingly low growth_rate) across isogenic replicate seeds of the wildtype strain, with a 'high-ppGpp/low-growth' minority comprising roughly 5-15% of the population, and we test causal dependence on the stringent pathway via rela gene_knockout, which should collapse that minority tail.
drafts.h1: Across isogenic wildtype seeds in basal medium, per-seed ppgpp_conc (and growth_rate) is bimodally distributed, with a distinguishable low-growth/high-ppGpp subpopulation comprising ~5-15% of seeds; this tail depends on relA (ppGpp synthetase) activity and disappears (or is strongly reduced in magnitude) when relA is knocked out.
drafts.h0: ppgpp_conc and growth_rate across isogenic wildtype seeds are unimodally distributed (no distinguishable dormant subpopulation), and relA knockout does not significantly change the spread or mean of ppgpp_conc or growth_rate relative to wildtype.

rivals.claim: Growth-rate heterogeneity is simply unimodal stochastic noise in metabolic flux (e.g. noisy translation/protein synthesis), unrelated to the stringent response or ppGpp — i.e., 'persistence' is not a distinct state but the tail of a single continuous noise distribution.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, pooled wildtype ppgpp_conc and growth_rate would show BC<=0.555 (unimodal, not bimodal) and relA knockout would NOT significantly shift the ppgpp_conc distribution or its variance, since the heterogeneity is generated by something other than RelA/ppGpp signaling.

rivals.claim: Any observed bimodality in growth_rate/ppgpp_conc is a ribosome-capacity artifact (fewer active ribosomes transiently reduce growth) rather than an active stringent-response dormancy program.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout control would be predicted by this rival to ALSO produce a similarly bimodal, low-growth tail independent of relA status; if the bimodal fraction and magnitude in rrna_operon_knockout/basal closely matches wildtype/basal even though ppGpp signaling is intact or altered differently, this favors the ribosome-capacity rival over the ppGpp-dependent dormancy claim.

drafts.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
drafts.claim: Phenotypic persistence to antibiotics arises from a ppGpp-mediated stringent-response bet-hedging mechanism: a subpopulation of isogenic wildtype E. coli stochastically enters a high-ppGpp, low-growth-rate dormant state even in nutrient-replete (basal) conditions, without any genetic resistance mutation. This dormant subpopulation is the source of antibiotic survival, and its size/depth is causally controlled by ppGpp level, not by acquired resistance alleles.
drafts.h1: Across seeds in basal condition, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate (and correspondingly ppgpp_conc) is bimodal, with a low-growth/high-ppGpp subpopulation comprising roughly 5-15% of simulated lineages; clamping ppgpp_conc to a high multiple of basal (mimicking stringent response induction) shifts the whole population toward this slow-growth state (fraction >50%), while a relA-pathway knockout (rela gene_knockout) abolishes the low-growth shoulder, collapsing the distribution toward unimodal fast growth.
drafts.h0: growth_rate (and ppgpp_conc) across wildtype/basal seeds is unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555, no distinguishable low-growth shoulder), and relA knockout produces no significant shift in the growth_rate distribution or mean relative to wildtype/basal — i.e., persistence-like heterogeneity is not ppGpp-dependent bet-hedging but uniform/noise-only variation.

(2) Dose/causal test: ppgpp_conc clamped to 4x basal shifts population growth_rate mean down by >=40% (fold-change <=0.6x wildtype) and increases the slow-growth fraction to >50%. (3) Discriminator: rela gene_knockout abolishes the bimodal shoulder (BC drops below 0.555) and raises mean growth_rate toward wildtype fast-mode level (no significant decrease, Welch |t|<2 vs wildtype/basal fast-growth subpopulation).

Separately, Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed growth_rate values in wildtype/basal; reject unimodal-H0 if BC>0.555.

rivals.claim: Rival A (growth-rate noise without ppGpp causality): heterogeneity in growth_rate is driven by generic stochastic noise in protein/metabolite partitioning (intrinsic biochemical noise), not specifically by the ppGpp/RelA stringent pathway.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If rela gene_knockout/basal shows a growth_rate distribution (BC, mean, spread) statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/basal (Welch |t|<2, BC difference negligible), this supports Rival A: the slow-growth shoulder persists without RelA, meaning ppGpp is not the causal driver.

rivals.claim: Rival B (resistance-like adaptation, not transient dormancy): the low-growth subpopulation reflects a stable metabolic/regulatory shift (e.g., altered ribosome allocation becoming fixed across generations) rather than a transient, reversible bet-hedged state, which would behave more like partial resistance than true phenotypic persistence.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If the low-growth subpopulation fraction and division_rate remain constant and fixed across generations (no stochastic switching between fast/slow seeds across the generations window) and ribosome_conc/rna_mass tracks growth rate rigidly with no decoupling, this points to a stable adapted state rather than stochastic bet-hedging, undermining H1's bet-hedging framing.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation in wildtype/basal is an adequate proxy for isogenic cell-to-cell phenotypic heterogeneity (persister formation), even though it is not an explicit single-cell lineage-switching model.

ppgpp_conc clamp at a fixed multiple is interpreted as a static analog of stringent-response induction; the model's charging kinetics (steady-state charging mode) are assumed to map growth suppression correctly even without kinetic RelA/SpoT dynamics.

relA gene_knockout is assumed to meaningfully reduce RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis in this model (downstream check during testing); if relA KO is not mechanistically wired to ppgpp_conc in the simulator, the discriminating control is uninformative and should be flagged as a capability gap rather than taken as support for a rival.

Division_rate and growth_rate over only 3 generations are assumed sufficient to detect a slow-growth shoulder; deeper dormancy (many-generation lag) is out of scope here and is noted as a caveat, not chased further.

No explicit antibiotic-killing perturbation exists in the envelope, so 'survival' is operationalized indirectly via the existence and ppGpp-dependence of a low-growth/high-ppGpp subpopulation (the accepted mechanistic proxy for persister phenotype), not via direct death-rate measurement.
