first_draft.predicted_effect: Bimodal distribution: BC > 0.6 in wildtype/basal with an estimated minor-mode fraction of 5-15% of seeds showing growth_rate < 0.5x the major-mode mean and ppgpp_conc >= 2x the major-mode mean. In relA_knockout/basal, BC drops below 0.555 (effectively unimodal) and the minor low-growth mode's mean ppgpp_conc difference vs wildtype's minor mode is reduced by >=50% (Welch |t| >= 2 for ppgpp_conc wildtype vs relA_knockout within the low-growth-tagged subset).

falsifier.decision_rule: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled per-seed growth_rate values (n>=40 seeds) in wildtype/basal; reject unimodal H0 if BC>0.555. Separately, Welch t of ppgpp_conc between relA_knockout/basal and wildtype/basal restricted to the low-growth-tagged seed subset; reject causal-RelA-dependence if |t|<2.
falsifier.refuting_result: BC <= 0.555 (growth_rate distribution is unimodal, no distinct minor mode) OR relA_knockout/basal still shows BC>0.555 with an unchanged low-growth/high-ppGpp subpopulation (|t|<2 vs wildtype), indicating the bimodality is not RelA-dependent and the stringent-response persister story is wrong

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient over pooled per-seed growth_rate
test.threshold: BC>0.555 to reject unimodal H0; BC<=0.555 refutes bimodality claim

rivals.claim: Persistence is explained purely by deterministic slow growth under nutrient limitation (a graded, unimodal response to stress), not a discrete stochastic subpopulation — i.e. all cells slow down together proportionally rather than splitting into two phenotypic classes.
rivals.distinguishing_result: growth_rate distribution across seeds remains unimodal (BC<=0.555) with a single shifted mean rather than two modes, for both wildtype/basal and nutrient-poor timeline conditions

rivals.claim: Any observed bimodality is driven by ribosome/translation capacity variation (rrna operon dosage noise) rather than ppGpp/RelA signaling per se — i.e. stringent response is a correlate, not the cause.
rivals.distinguishing_result: rrna_operon_knockout/basal (reduced ribosome capacity) reproduces or exaggerates the bimodal growth_rate split (BC>0.555) even when ppGpp signaling is intact, showing ribosome capacity alone (not RelA) drives the split

auxiliary_assumptions: Pooling growth_rate across >=40 independent seeds under identical wildtype/basal conditions approximates sampling from the underlying population distribution of a genetically clonal culture (ergodic-like assumption).

The simulator's steady-state ppGpp/charging module (with RelA/SpoT module on where applicable) captures enough stringent-response dynamics to produce a detectable growth_rate/ppgpp_conc split if the mechanism is real; if the module is off or not stochastic enough, failure to find bimodality could reflect simulator limitation rather than biological falsification (recorded as a scope caveat, not chased further).

relA_knockout is assumed to abolish RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis while leaving SpoT-mediated basal ppGpp turnover intact, i.e. it is a clean mechanistic lesion of the stringent-response synthesis arm rather than a confounded global physiology change.

Growth_rate measured at the end of the simulated generations window (1-4 generations) is an adequate proxy for persister-like dormancy; we are not simulating actual antibiotic killing kinetics, only the pre-existing phenotypic heterogeneity that the persister hypothesis requires.

params.label: basal_highseed
params.note: same condition as reference wildtype/basal design; used as the null/reference distribution

hypothesis.question: Why do some bacteria survive antibiotics without becoming resistant?
hypothesis.claim: Antibiotic survival without genetic resistance (persistence/tolerance) arises from a stochastic, ppGpp-mediated stringent-response subpopulation: a minority of isogenic wildtype cells spontaneously enter a high-ppGpp, low-growth-rate state that is phenotypically but not genetically distinct, and this fraction (and the depth of growth-rate depression) is reduced when the stringent response is disabled (relA knockout), showing the tolerant state is ppGpp-dependent rather than a fixed trait.
hypothesis.h1: Across isogenic wildtype populations, the per-seed distribution of growth_rate is bimodal (a low-growth-rate shoulder consistent with dormant/tolerant cells) and this shoulder coincides with elevated ppgpp_conc; deleting relA (removing ppGpp synthesis capacity) collapses the low-growth shoulder, shifting the population toward a single growth-rate mode and reducing ppgpp_conc variance, demonstrating the subpopulation is ppGpp-driven rather than a fixed basal distribution.
hypothesis.h0: Growth_rate across wildtype seeds is unimodal (Sarle's BC <= 0.555) and relA knockout does not change the growth_rate distribution shape or mean ppgpp_conc relative to wildtype (no significant Welch t, |t|<2), i.e. any apparent low-growth subpopulation is sampling noise, not a ppGpp-dependent stringent-response state.

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: per-seed distribution of growth_rate across many wildtype seeds; bimodality coefficient (BC) and fraction of seeds in low-growth cluster

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean and variance of ppgpp_conc per seed; co-occurrence with low-growth cluster membership

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate, ppgpp_conc in relA gene_knockout vs wildtype
operational_defs.measure: Welch t-test of growth_rate distribution shape (via BC) and mean ppgpp_conc, knockout vs wildtype

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Wildtype growth_rate across seeds is bimodal with BC > 0.555 and an estimated low-growth subpopulation fraction of ~5-15% of seeds/timepoints, with that cluster showing >=2-fold higher ppgpp_conc than the main mode; relA knockout reduces the low-growth fraction toward <5% (BC drops below 0.555, approaching unimodal) and lowers mean ppgpp_conc by >=30% relative to wildtype.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of mean ppgpp_conc, relA-knockout vs wildtype across seeds; reject H0 (ppGpp-dependence) if |t|>=2 is NOT met (i.e. refute if |t|<2), and separately require wildtype growth_rate BC>0.555 (bimodality_bc) with relA-KO BC<=0.555 to support the subpopulation-collapse claim
falsifier.refuting_result: relA knockout shows no significant change in mean ppgpp_conc (|t|<2) and/or wildtype growth_rate distribution is NOT bimodal (BC<=0.555), indicating no ppGpp-dependent dormant subpopulation exists

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) on pooled per-seed growth_rate values; paired with welch_disconfirm on ppgpp_conc
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for wildtype (bimodal); relA-KO |t|<2 vs wildtype on ppgpp_conc refutes dependence; relA-KO BC<=0.555 supports collapse

rivals.claim: Persistence is a fixed, deterministic subpopulation set by stochastic gene-expression noise in an unrelated pathway (e.g. toxin-antitoxin systems), independent of ppGpp/stringent response entirely.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA knockout does NOT change the low-growth-rate fraction or BC of growth_rate (BC stays >0.555 and unchanged vs wildtype), showing the subpopulation persists without ppGpp.

rivals.claim: Apparent bimodality in growth_rate is an artifact of cell-cycle/division timing (division_rate variability) rather than a distinct physiological state.
rivals.distinguishing_result: division_rate shows the same bimodal split as growth_rate but ppgpp_conc does NOT differ between the two clusters (no correlation with ppGpp), indicating the split is cycle-timing noise, not stringent-response-driven.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation in growth_rate reflects biologically meaningful intrinsic noise (not purely numerical artifact), sufficient to reveal a bimodal subpopulation across 8 seeds.

relA knockout is mechanistically simulated as removing (RelA-mediated) ppGpp synthesis capacity in this model; if relA is not wired to ppgpp_conc in the model, this falls outside what the simulator can resolve and is logged as a scope caveat rather than re-litigated.

The ppgpp_conc clamp (3x basal) design serves as a positive-control/discriminating condition to confirm that elevated ppGpp alone is sufficient to depress growth_rate, independent of relA's natural induction, helping separate ppGpp's causal role from relA-specific pleiotropy.
Four generations is enough time for a stringent-response-driven low-growth subpopulation to manifest and be distinguished from pure division-timing noise.

hypothesis.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
hypothesis.claim: Bet-hedging via stringent-response "preparedness" is adaptive at the population level: wildtype populations that maintain basal ppGpp/RelA activity and slightly slower growth under steady nutrient-rich conditions pay a fitness cost in constant conditions but confer a population-level growth-recovery advantage when an abrupt amino-acid downshift occurs, relative to a population lacking this preparedness (relA-knockout).
hypothesis.h1: Across seeds (identical initial molecule counts, forward stochastic trajectories differing only by RNG seed), wildtype populations exposed to an amino-acid downshift show a smaller growth-rate penalty and faster division-rate recovery than relA-knockout populations; this advantage is reversed in constant nutrient-rich conditions, where wildtype pays a growth-rate cost relative to relA-knockout. The genotype x condition interaction (not a main effect alone) is the signature of preparedness being adaptive only conditionally.
hypothesis.h0: No preparedness benefit: wildtype and relA-knockout show statistically indistinguishable growth_rate and division_rate trajectories both in constant basal conditions and after the amino-acid downshift (no genotype x condition interaction; any main-effect difference, if present, is the same sign in both conditions).

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc, rela_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc (uM) at steady state before the shift, wildtype vs relA-knockout (knockout should be near-zero/strongly reduced, confirming the perturbation removed the preparedness mechanism, not just relabeling noise)

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: mean growth_rate (1/h) in constant basal condition, wildtype vs relA-knockout

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate, division_rate
operational_defs.measure: post-shift growth_rate trajectory and division_rate (fraction dividing) in the 2 generations following the amino-acid downshift

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Two-part, directional prediction: (1) In constant basal condition, wildtype mean growth_rate is 5-10% LOWER than relA-knockout (cost of preparedness), Welch effect ~5-10%, |t|>=2. (2) Following an amino-acid downshift, wildtype division_rate recovers to >=90% of pre-shift baseline within 2 generations while relA-knockout division_rate drops by >=25% and stays below 75% of baseline — a >=15 percentage-point gap between genotypes in post-shift division_rate. The DECISIVE signature is the SIGN FLIP: relA-KO is higher in basal (cost) but lower post-shift (no benefit) — a genotype x condition interaction, not just two separate main effects.

falsifier.decision_rule: Step 1 (cost in constant condition): Welch t of growth_rate, gene_knockout/basal vs wildtype/basal; expect |t|>=2 with relA-KO higher (confirms the cost side of the interaction). Step 2 (benefit under shift): Welch t of division_rate, gene_knockout/shift vs wildtype/shift (amino_acid_shift timeline); reject H0 only if |t|>=2 AND wildtype division_rate exceeds relA-KO by >=15 percentage points post-shift AND the sign of the genotype effect has flipped relative to Step 1 (KO advantaged in basal, disadvantaged post-shift). Any intermediate outcome (e.g. |t|>=2 in Step 2 but gap <15pp, or |t|<2 in Step 1) is scored as NOT supporting H1 (conservative: ambiguous bands count as non-confirmation, not as a third undefined outcome) — this removes any ambiguous middle-ground verdict.
falsifier.refuting_result: If gene_knockout/shift division_rate is statistically indistinguishable from (or higher than) wildtype/shift (|t|<2 or KO higher), OR if relA-knockout shows no growth-rate cost in basal condition (|t|<2 in Step 1), OR if the same genotype wins in BOTH conditions (no sign flip), OR if the post-shift gap is <15 percentage points even with |t|>=2, the preparedness-benefit (bet-hedging tradeoff) claim is refuted.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 for both the basal cost comparison and the post-shift division_rate comparison, with opposite-sign genotype effects across the two conditions, and post-shift gap >=15 percentage points (no partial-credit band)

rivals.claim: Growth-rate differences after the downshift are simply a direct, universal consequence of losing RelA-mediated ppGpp induction during starvation (an individual stress-response failure in every cell equally, no distinct 'prepared' subpopulation needed).
rivals.distinguishing_result: bimodality_bc on pooled per-seed ppgpp_conc in wildtype/basal (pre-shift) returns BC<=0.555 (unimodal) yet wildtype still outperforms relA-KO post-shift per the Step1/Step2 decision rule: this supports a uniform individual physiological-readiness mechanism rather than literal bet-hedging subpopulations, but does NOT itself refute the conditional-tradeoff claim (H1 only requires the mean mechanism to help, not bimodal structure) — it just changes the descriptive label from 'bet-hedging' to 'uniform readiness'.

rivals.claim: Any observed wildtype advantage post-shift is an artifact of relA-knockout having a GENERAL fitness defect unrelated to preparedness for downshifts specifically (relA-KO is simply sicklier under ANY condition, including constant basal).
rivals.distinguishing_result: If relA-knockout growth_rate is also significantly LOWER than wildtype in the constant basal condition (same direction deficit as post-shift, i.e. no sign flip), Step 1 fails its predicted direction and this rival is supported; the conditional-tradeoff interpretation is refuted in favor of a general knockout defect, exactly as encoded in the Step1/Step2 sign-flip requirement.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift timeline (removing amino acids mid-run) is a valid proxy for an abrupt nutrient downshift that would normally trigger the stringent response.

relA-knockout is assumed to abolish (RelA-dependent) ppGpp induction without the simulator introducing unrelated confounding basal defects beyond what SpoT alone can buffer; any residual SpoT-mediated ppGpp synthesis is treated as a scope caveat, not grounds to reject the design.

Different seeds hold initial molecule counts fixed and only randomize the forward stochastic trajectory (RNG), so per-seed dispersion in ppgpp_conc reflects intrinsic dynamical noise rather than sampling different starting populations; if the simulator instead randomizes initial conditions per seed, the heterogeneity-vs-individual-response rival distinction (bimodality_bc test) becomes less clean and is noted as a scope caveat.
Division_rate measured over 2-3 generations post-shift is sufficient to detect a recovery-trajectory difference; slower long-run adaptation beyond this window is out of scope for this test.

The sign-flip (interaction) criterion is treated as the decisive discriminator between the conditional-tradeoff hypothesis and the general-fitness-defect rival; we are not attempting to additionally prove literal bimodal subpopulation structure as a requirement for H1 to hold (that is a secondary, non-decisive characterization addressed by rival 1).

The decision rule is deliberately binary (support / not-support) with no third 'ambiguous' outcome: any run landing in an intermediate zone (e.g. significant t but sub-threshold gap) is scored as not supporting H1, trading some leniency for a clean falsifiable test.

params.note: all seeds use identical initial molecule counts; only the forward stochastic trajectory differs by RNG seed
same fixed initial state as wildtype/basal; downshift event only differs

objection_ledger.issue: Which seed is used to generate the fixed 'initial' cell state that differs only stochastically is undefined — does 'isogenic' mean identical initial molecule counts with only forward stochastic simulation differing, or do different seeds also randomize initial conditions? If initial conditions themselves are randomized per seed, the measured dispersion conflates true dynamical noise with sampling of a different starting population, which the proposer should clarify matches their intended construct of 'intrinsic noise from identical starting state'.

predicted_effect says |r|<0.3 between growth_rate and ppgpp_conc is 'NOT required' for H1 because coupling is plausible, yet the artifact rival's distinguishing_result says artifact is supported if r is 'near 0'. If true biological coupling also predicts r near 0 is uninformative either way, the correlation check as stated cannot actually discriminate the artifact rival from H1 — it should be dropped as a decisive criterion or re-specified with a threshold that does discriminate the two cases.

The rrna_operon_knockout control is meant to distinguish 'true intrinsic noise' from 'deterministic numerical/initialization artifact' (Rival A), but rrna_operon_knockout changes ribosome gene dosage deterministically AND could itself alter the mean growth rate, which can mechanically shrink CV (since CV=sd/mean) even if the per-seed noise-generating process is identical. A lower CV in the knockout doesn't cleanly show 'true biological noise amplification' was removed — it's confounded with a different operating point / different sensitivity of growth_rate to the same underlying noise source. The design does not isolate 'numerical seeding artifact' from 'biological noise' because both wildtype and knockout runs still use the SAME stochastic seeding machinery; the knockout cannot show whether variance is a numerics artifact independent of seeds.

The simulator-artifact rival's distinguishing result (CV shrinking toward zero as seed count increases; correlation with ppgpp_conc/fraction_trna_charged) is stated as a claim but not wired into any explicit decision_rule or test_id the way the bimodality and power checks are. Without a concrete threshold (e.g. correlation r >= X between per-seed growth_rate and ppgpp_conc) this rival-exclusion is asserted rather than operationalized.

The decision rule has a gap: if growth_rate CV and ppgpp_conc CV land strictly between 0.05 and 0.15 (e.g., 0.08), the rule neither rejects H1 (not <0.05) nor confirms the predicted range (0.15-0.25), and no action is specified. Since real CVs often fall in ambiguous middle ranges, this leaves a wide band where the hypothesis is neither supported nor falsified, weakening the risky-prediction character of the test.

hypothesis.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
hypothesis.claim: A bet-hedging subpopulation that grows slowly and keeps stringent-response machinery (RelA, ppGpp) elevated acts as 'insurance': under a sudden amino-acid downshift, clamping ppGpp to a constitutively high ('prepared') level pre-emptively raises division_rate (survival) relative to wildtype, even though it lowers mean growth_rate in steady nutrient-rich conditions — i.e. a fitness trade-off across environments, not a free lunch in any single one.
hypothesis.h1: Across a panel of seeds, cells/lineages with elevated basal ppgpp_conc (a 'prepared' state, clamped to ~2-4x basal) show LOWER mean growth_rate in steady basal media (>=15% reduction) but HIGHER division_rate (survival through the shift, >=10 percentage points) after an abrupt amino_acid_shift (removal) compared to wildtype, demonstrating a population-level advantage for a slow/prepared phenotype that only manifests under environmental change.
hypothesis.h0: Elevated basal ppGpp confers no survival/division_rate benefit after an amino-acid downshift relative to wildtype (division_rate difference is not distinguishable from noise), and/or it carries no steady-state growth cost (growth_rate difference is not distinguishable from noise) — i.e. there is no trade-off structure, just a uniform cost or no effect.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc clamp level relative to wildtype basal
operational_defs.measure: ppgpp_conc channel, clamped via ppgpp_conc perturbation to 2x-4x the wildtype steady-state mean

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate channel under condition=basal, no shift
operational_defs.measure: mean growth_rate across seeds/generations, Welch t vs wildtype/basal

operational_defs.observable: division_rate channel after amino_acid_shift removal event
operational_defs.measure: fraction of generations completing division post-shift, Welch t vs wildtype/same timeline

operational_defs.construct: mechanistic dependence on stringent response (not just slow growth per se)
operational_defs.observable: rela_conc / growth_rate under relA knockout background
operational_defs.measure: compare division_rate benefit of ppgpp_conc clamp in a relA-knockout background vs wildtype background

hypothesis.predicted_effect: Trade-off, two numbers: (1) steady-state basal growth_rate reduced by ~15-25% (fold-change ~0.75-0.85x wildtype) under ppgpp_conc=3x clamp vs wildtype/basal; (2) division_rate after amino_acid_shift(removal) increased by ~10-20 percentage points (e.g. wildtype division_rate ~0.6-0.7 dropping further under shift, prepared clamp staying >=0.8) in the clamped condition vs wildtype on the same shift timeline.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of growth_rate, ppgpp_conc clamp (3x) vs wildtype, both under condition=basal no shift, across seeds; reject H1's cost premise if |welch_t|<2 or effect_pct<10% (no steady-state cost) AND simultaneously test division_rate after shift: Welch t of division_rate, ppgpp_conc clamp vs wildtype on amino_acid_shift(removal) timeline; refute H1 if |welch_t|<2 (no survival benefit)
falsifier.refuting_result: Either growth_rate shows no significant reduction in basal (|t|<2, effect_pct<10%) OR division_rate after the amino-acid-removal shift shows no significant increase in the clamped condition vs wildtype (|t|<2) -- in either case the claimed trade-off collapses (uniform cost with no benefit, or benefit with no cost = not a bet-hedging trade-off)

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 on both growth_rate (basal) and division_rate (post-shift) comparisons, in the predicted directions

rivals.claim: Rival A: High ppGpp is simply globally toxic/growth-limiting (a blanket stress response), with no differential protective benefit under the shift -- i.e. division_rate is suppressed or unchanged (not increased) after the shift in the clamped condition relative to wildtype.
rivals.distinguishing_result: division_rate in ppgpp_conc/shift is NOT higher than wildtype/shift (|t|<2 or negative direction), while growth_rate cost in basal is still present -- shows pure cost, no insurance value.

rivals.claim: Rival B: Any survival benefit after the shift is not specifically ppGpp-mediated but is a generic consequence of slower growth/smaller cell size (e.g. via rrna_operon_knockout reducing ribosome capacity would give the same division_rate benefit without ppGpp signaling).
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout/basal control (slow growth without ppGpp elevation) shows comparable division_rate benefit after the same amino_acid_shift, indicating the benefit is from slow growth per se, not the stringent-response/ppGpp mechanism specifically.

auxiliary_assumptions: The ppgpp_conc perturbation (clamp to a multiple of basal) mechanistically engages the same downstream effects (RelA/SpoT regulon, translation slowdown) as naturally elevated ppGpp in bet-hedging subpopulations, even though it is an exogenous clamp rather than emergent stochastic bimodality.
division_rate measured over 2-3 generations post-shift is a valid proxy for 'surviving the shift' (short-term survival), not long-term fitness over many generations.
The amino_acid_shift(removal) perturbation is a reasonable proxy for the kind of abrupt nutrient downshift that bet-hedging is thought to protect against.
Seed-to-seed variability under isogenic wildtype conditions reflects genuine stochastic/intrinsic noise relevant to interpreting effect sizes, not simulator artifact.

We are not claiming to observe emergent bimodal subpopulations in a single run (the simulator here is operationalized at the population/mean level via a clamp), but using the clamp as an interventional stand-in for a 'prepared' phenotype -- this is a scope caveat on what 'bet-hedging' means operationally here.

hypothesis.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
hypothesis.claim: Bet-hedging via stringent-response priming: a subpopulation of cells that maintains elevated basal ppGpp and slower growth under steady nutrient-rich conditions pays an immediate growth-rate cost, but this 'preparedness' is a population-level strategy whose signature is a persistent, non-collapsing heterogeneity (bimodality) in growth rate / ppGpp across isogenic cells, rather than convergence to a single optimal growth rate. The anticipatory mechanism is RelA/SpoT-driven ppGpp synthesis, which can be clamped or removed to test whether the slow/primed subpopulation is mechanistically tied to the stringent response.
hypothesis.h1: Across an isogenic population simulated under constant rich (basal) media with IDENTICAL initial molecule-count state per seed (only the stochastic random-number stream differs across the 8 seeds -- i.e. seeds randomize forward dynamics only, NOT starting conditions), per-cell growth_rate and ppgpp_conc show a bimodal distribution (Sarle's BC > 0.555) with a substantial slow/high-ppGpp subpopulation (predicted fraction ~15-30% of cells) that is STABLE (does not collapse) from generation 2 through generation 4, and this bimodality is MECHANISTICALLY TIED to RelA/SpoT ppGpp synthesis capacity specifically: a relA knockout or low-ppGpp clamp collapses growth_rate to unimodal (BC<=0.555), whereas rrna_operon_knockout (a ribosome-dosage perturbation that leaves RelA/SpoT intact) PRESERVES a bimodal/high-BC growth_rate distribution.
hypothesis.h0: Growth_rate and ppgpp_conc are unimodally distributed across isogenic cells under constant basal media (BC <= 0.555) at generation 4 once initial-condition identity is controlled; OR, if bimodality exists, it is NOT specific to RelA/SpoT signaling -- relA_knockout fails to collapse it (BC stays >0.555, indistinguishable from wildtype) or rrna_operon_knockout ALSO collapses it (BC<=0.555), either of which shows the heterogeneity is a generic noise/ribosome-dosage artifact rather than a ppGpp-dependent bet-hedging mechanism.

operational_defs.observable: per-seed, per-generation growth_rate and ppgpp_conc values pooled across an isogenic replicate population, where all seeds share IDENTICAL initial molecule-count state (the simulator's standard fixed-initial-state, varied-random-stream seeding mode) so that dispersion reflects intrinsic stochastic dynamics, not sampled differences in starting population composition
operational_defs.measure: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) computed over pooled per-seed growth_rate values and separately over ppgpp_conc values, at generation 4

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate distribution split by bimodality test's 2-cluster assignment
operational_defs.measure: fraction of cells/seeds assigned to the low-growth-rate, high-ppgpp_conc cluster

operational_defs.construct: stability of the split (vs transient cell-cycle asynchrony)
operational_defs.observable: BC(growth_rate) computed separately at generation 2 and generation 4 within the SAME wildtype seeds (identical initial state)
operational_defs.measure: BC must remain >0.555 at BOTH generation 2 and generation 4 (pre-registered: persistence = BC_gen4 within 0.1 BC-units of BC_gen2, not a one-off peak); collapse toward BC<=0.555 by generation 4 falsifies persistence regardless of any CV calibration

operational_defs.construct: stringent-response-SPECIFIC dependence of priming (vs generic ribosome-dosage noise)
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate and ppgpp_conc channels under relA gene_knockout, ppgpp_conc clamp, and rrna_operon_knockout, each vs wildtype/basal, at generation 4
operational_defs.measure: BC(growth_rate) and mean growth_rate (welch_t) compared pairwise: wildtype vs relA_knockout, wildtype vs ppgpp clamp, wildtype vs rrna_operon_knockout -- H1 requires relA/clamp to collapse BC while rrna_operon_knockout does NOT collapse BC (BC difference from wildtype <=0.1 units)

hypothesis.predicted_effect: H1 predicts BC > 0.555 (bimodal) for growth_rate and ppgpp_conc in wildtype/basal at BOTH generation 2 and generation 4 (pre-registered persistence criterion: |BC_gen4 - BC_gen2| <= 0.1, ruling out a one-off transient peak), with ~15-30% of cells in the slow/high-ppGpp cluster showing roughly 30-50% lower instantaneous growth_rate than the fast cluster. Under relA_knockout/basal or ppgpp_conc clamped-low/basal, predicted collapse to unimodal (BC <= 0.555) with mean growth_rate shifting up by ~10-20% relative to wildtype (Welch |t| >= 2). Under rrna_operon_knockout/basal (ribosome-dosage control, RelA/SpoT intact), BC should REMAIN > 0.555 (bimodality preserved, difference from relA_knockout BC of at least 0.1 BC-units), even though mean growth_rate itself may shift due to reduced ribosome capacity -- the mechanistic specificity claim is about BC (shape), not mean level. No CV-noise-floor fallback is used; persistence across generations 2-4 (not a CV comparison to a noise floor) is the pre-registered falsifiable criterion that replaces it.

falsifier.decision_rule: All seeds use IDENTICAL initial molecule-count state with only the stochastic random-number stream varied across the 8 seeds (standard fixed-initial-state seeding). Primary persistence test: compute Sarle's bimodality coefficient (bimodality_bc) over pooled per-seed growth_rate values for wildtype/basal separately at generation 2 and generation 4. H1 requires BC>0.555 at BOTH timepoints with |BC_gen4-BC_gen2|<=0.1 (pre-registered persistence, no post-hoc fallback threshold). Mechanistic specificity test: compute BC for relA_knockout/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal at generation 4. H1 requires BC(relA_knockout)<=0.555 (collapse) AND BC(rrna_operon_knockout)>0.555 (preserved, within 0.1 of wildtype BC). Confirmatory: Welch t (welch_disconfirm) of mean growth_rate, wildtype/basal vs relA_knockout/basal across seeds at generation 4; reject H0 only if |t|>=2 AND both BC patterns above hold.
falsifier.refuting_result: Refuted if ANY of: (a) wildtype/basal growth_rate is unimodal (BC<=0.555) at generation 2 OR generation 4; (b) BC_gen4 drops by more than 0.1 units relative to BC_gen2 (favoring a transient/collapsing artifact over persistent bet-hedging); (c) relA_knockout/basal BC remains >0.555, indistinguishable from wildtype; (d) rrna_operon_knockout/basal ALSO collapses to BC<=0.555; (e) Welch |t|<2 between wildtype and relA_knockout mean growth_rate.

test.statistic: Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) over pooled per-seed growth_rate at generations 2 and 4, cross-checked against ppgpp_conc BC; compared pairwise across wildtype/basal, relA_knockout/basal, rrna_operon_knockout/basal
test.threshold: BC>0.555 for wildtype/basal and rrna_operon_knockout/basal at both gen 2 and gen 4 with |BC_gen4-BC_gen2|<=0.1; BC<=0.555 for relA_knockout/basal and ppgpp_conc-clamped/basal

rivals.claim: Rival A: apparent 'bimodality' is just sampling/seed noise around a single optimal growth rate (no real subpopulation structure), driven by stochastic fluctuation rather than a stringent-response-controlled switch.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, BC for wildtype/basal would hover near or below 0.555 at generation 2 and/or generation 4 (fail to clear the pre-registered threshold at both timepoints), and relA_knockout would show the SAME BC as wildtype (no mechanistic relA dependence) because the heterogeneity never depended on ppGpp synthesis.

rivals.claim: Rival B (INTERVENTIONAL, not observational): heterogeneity exists but is driven by generic ribosome-partitioning/dosage stochasticity (captured by rrna_operon_knockout, which perturbs ribosome capacity WITHOUT touching RelA/SpoT) rather than active RelA/ppGpp signaling -- i.e. it is a byproduct, not an adaptive 'preparedness' strategy.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, rrna_operon_knockout would COLLAPSE growth_rate bimodality (BC<=0.555) just as much as relA_knockout does, because reducing ribosome gene dosage removes the noise source regardless of ppGpp -- directly refuting the RelA-specificity claim even if wildtype bimodality itself is real.

rivals.claim: Rival C: apparent bimodality is a transient artifact of early-generation cell-cycle-phase asynchrony that washes out as the population equilibrates, rather than a stable bet-hedging subpopulation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, BC(growth_rate) measured within the SAME wildtype seeds would be high at generation 2 and collapse toward BC<=0.555 by generation 4 (|BC_gen4-BC_gen2|>0.1, decreasing) -- the opposite of H1's pre-registered persistence requirement.

objection_ledger.issue: The rrna_operon_knockout control is meant to distinguish 'true intrinsic noise' from 'deterministic numerical/initialization artifact' (Rival A), but rrna_operon_knockout changes ribosome gene dosage deterministically AND could itself alter the mean growth rate, which can mechanically shrink CV (since CV=sd/mean) even if the per-seed noise-generating process is identical. A lower CV in the knockout doesn't cleanly show 'true biological noise amplification' was removed — it's confounded with a different operating point / different sensitivity of growth_rate to the same underlying noise source. The design does not isolate 'numerical seeding artifact' from 'biological noise' because both wildtype and knockout runs still use the SAME stochastic seeding machinery; the knockout cannot show whether variance is a numerics artifact independent of seeds.

Rival A's distinguishing test relies on comparing CV of growth_rate/fraction_trna_charged against CV of dry_mass as 'proxy for pure numerical noise.' But dry_mass, growth_rate, and fraction_trna_charged are all mechanistically coupled outputs of the same integrated cellular state in this model (mass accumulation depends on charged tRNA fraction and vice versa via ribosome allocation). A difference in their CVs could reflect differential sensitivity/amplification along the coupled network rather than true distinction between 'numerical artifact' and 'biological noise' channels. This comparison does not interventionally break the coupling between the channels being contrasted.

The 'numerical noise floor of <5% CV' used to justify the CV>=10% threshold is asserted but never actually measured in the design. No candidate_design computes CV from a trivial duplicate/identical-seed run (e.g., re-running the same seed twice) to establish what the floor actually is in this instrument; the 10% cutoff is simply assumed rather than calibrated.

The cell-cycle-phase-asynchrony rival is handled only as a discursive assertion ('CV at generation 4 should be markedly lower than at generation 1'), but none of the three candidate_designs record or compare growth_rate CV at generation 1 vs generation 4 within the same seeds. As specified, the decisive test cannot actually be run.

The decision rule includes a fallback ('if CV_floor cannot be driven near zero... fall back to absolute 10% threshold') that reintroduces an uncalibrated arbitrary cutoff if the primary calibration doesn't behave as expected. This is a reasonable contingency but slightly softens falsifiability; stating explicitly in advance which outcome triggers which branch (rather than post hoc) would tighten it.

Which seed is used to generate the fixed 'initial' cell state that differs only stochastically is undefined — does 'isogenic' mean identical initial molecule counts with only forward stochastic simulation differing, or do different seeds also randomize initial conditions? If initial conditions themselves are randomized per seed, the measured dispersion conflates true dynamical noise with sampling of a different starting population, which the proposer should clarify matches their intended construct of 'intrinsic noise from identical starting state'.

drafts.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
drafts.claim: Bet-hedging via stringent-response 'preparedness': a subpopulation of isogenic E. coli cells that maintain elevated ppGpp and slower growth even in nutrient-replete (basal) conditions will show a growth-rate advantage over the bulk population specifically when challenged by a sudden nutrient downshift (amino-acid withdrawal), because their pre-activated stringent response buffers the shock. In steady favorable conditions this preparedness is a fitness cost (lower mean growth rate / bimodal growth-rate distribution), but it becomes a population-level benefit under fluctuating/shift conditions (faster recovery, less growth-rate collapse) relative to a population lacking this heterogeneity (e.g., a relA knockout that cannot mount ppGpp pre-induction).
drafts.h1: In basal (favorable, steady) conditions, isogenic wildtype populations exhibit a bimodal/heterogeneous ppGpp and growth-rate distribution (slow-growing, high-ppGpp subpopulation present), and upon an amino-acid downshift timeline, wildtype populations show a significantly smaller growth-rate drop (less collapse / faster recovery) than a relA-knockout population that lacks stringent-response heterogeneity.
drafts.h0: ppGpp/growth-rate heterogeneity in basal conditions is unimodal (no distinct 'prepared' subpopulation; bimodality_bc <= 0.555), AND/OR the relA-knockout population shows no significant difference in growth-rate drop upon amino-acid downshift compared to wildtype (|welch_t| < 2 on growth_rate effect_pct between wildtype/downshift and relA_knockout/downshift).

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: per-seed per-cell ppgpp_conc distribution in basal condition; bimodality coefficient over pooled values

operational_defs.construct: growth cost of preparedness in steady state
operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: mean growth_rate and its distribution shape (bimodality_bc) across seeds in basal condition, wildtype vs relA_knockout

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: percent drop in growth_rate (effect_pct) immediately after amino_acid downshift timeline event, compared between wildtype and relA_knockout

operational_defs.construct: bet-hedging mechanism specificity (not just slower baseline growth)
operational_defs.observable: fraction_trna_charged
operational_defs.measure: trajectory of fraction_trna_charged post-shift, wildtype vs relA_knockout, as a mechanistic correlate of the stringent response buffering charged-tRNA depletion

drafts.predicted_effect: (1) In basal/wildtype, ppgpp_conc and growth_rate pooled across seeds show a bimodal distribution with Sarle's BC > 0.6, consistent with ~10-20% of trajectories/seeds in a 'high-ppGpp, slow-growth' (prepared) regime (growth_rate roughly 30-50% lower than the fast mode). (2) Upon amino_acid_shift downshift, wildtype growth_rate drops by only ~15-25% (effect_pct) relative to its own pre-shift baseline, whereas relA_knockout growth_rate drops by ~40-60%, i.e. a >=2-fold larger collapse in the knockout, with Welch |t|>=2 between wildtype/downshift and relA_knockout/downshift on growth_rate.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of growth_rate effect_pct (post-shift drop relative to pre-shift baseline), relA_knockout/downshift vs wildtype/downshift across seeds; reject H0 (no protective benefit of preparedness) if |welch_t| >= 2 with relA_knockout showing a LARGER drop (more negative effect_pct) than wildtype
falsifier.refuting_result: relA_knockout/downshift shows growth_rate drop statistically indistinguishable from wildtype/downshift (|welch_t| < 2), or relA_knockout actually recovers BETTER than wildtype, indicating stringent-response heterogeneity confers no protective population benefit

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t| >= 2, with sign indicating relA_knockout drop > wildtype drop

rivals.claim: Rival A: observed growth-rate/ppGpp heterogeneity in basal conditions is just intrinsic stochastic noise in ribosome/metabolic flux allocation, unrelated to any adaptive 'preparedness' function, and relA deletion simply removes a constitutive growth-rate brake (uniformly slower baseline) rather than removing a bet-hedging subpopulation.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, basal ppgpp_conc/growth_rate distributions in wildtype would be UNIMODAL (bimodality_bc <= 0.555) rather than bimodal, and relA_knockout would show a uniformly shifted (not differentially protected) growth_rate trajectory post-shift — i.e. relA_knockout baseline growth_rate would be faster than wildtype in basal AND show the SAME proportional drop on downshift.

rivals.claim: Rival B: any apparent protection in wildtype after downshift is driven purely by generic ribosome-capacity reserve (more ribosomes per cell), not by ppGpp/stringent-response signaling per se — i.e. it's a ribosome_conc effect, not a regulatory bet-hedging effect.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout/downshift control (reduced ribosome capacity but intact ppGpp signaling) would show a growth_rate drop similar to wildtype (ppGpp-mediated buffering still works despite lower ribosome reserve), whereas if Rival B were true, rrna_operon_knockout would show a drop as large as relA_knockout, implicating ribosome capacity rather than ppGpp signaling as the protective factor.

auxiliary_assumptions: The simulator's stochastic seed-to-seed variation in basal condition approximates genuine isogenic cell-to-cell heterogeneity (bet-hedging subpopulations), even though each run is a single-lineage trajectory rather than an explicit multi-cell population snapshot; bimodality is assessed over pooled per-seed per-timepoint values as a proxy for population heterogeneity.

relA knockout is assumed to be mechanistically simulated (abolishing (p)ppGpp synthesis induction) in this model version; if relA KO shows no ppgpp_conc change at all vs wildtype, this would indicate the knockout is not mechanistically implemented and the test is uninformative (a scope caveat, not evidence against H1).
The amino_acid_shift timeline event (minimal minus amino acids) is assumed to be a sufficient proxy for a 'sudden nutrient downshift' stress relevant to stringent-response activation.

Growth-rate effect_pct is computed relative to each condition's own pre-shift baseline (within-seed normalization) so that comparisons across wildtype and relA_knockout are not confounded by baseline growth-rate differences alone.

drafts.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
drafts.claim: Bet-hedging via stringent-response "preparedness": a subpopulation of cells maintaining elevated basal ppGpp and reduced growth rate (a slow/prepared phenotype) pays an immediate growth-rate cost but confers a population-level advantage when an abrupt nutrient downshift occurs, because prepared cells already have ribosome/tRNA-charging states suited to the new condition and avoid the growth-rate crash that fast, unprepared cells suffer upon shift.
drafts.h1: Across an amino-acid downshift timeline, lineages/seeds with a clamped elevated basal ppGpp (mimicking a prepared subpopulation) show a smaller growth-rate drop and faster growth-rate recovery after the shift than wildtype, despite having lower pre-shift growth rate.
drafts.h0: Elevated basal ppGpp confers no growth-rate-recovery advantage after the shift; post-shift growth_rate trajectories of the ppgpp_conc-clamped condition are statistically indistinguishable from (or worse than) wildtype once pre-shift growth-rate differences are accounted for.

operational_defs.observable: ppgpp_conc
operational_defs.measure: mean ppgpp_conc (uM) during the pre-shift steady-state window, clamped to 2x basal in the perturbed condition vs 1x in wildtype

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: mean growth_rate (1/h) in the pre-shift window, expected lower in clamped condition

operational_defs.observable: growth_rate
operational_defs.measure: growth_rate trajectory in the 60 min post-shift window: magnitude of trough (min growth_rate reached) and time-to-recover to 90% of pre-shift baseline

operational_defs.observable: division_rate
operational_defs.measure: fraction of generations completing division across the shift window, compared between clamped and wildtype

drafts.predicted_effect: Pre-shift: ppgpp_conc-clamped cells grow ~15-25% slower than wildtype (growth_rate fold-change ~0.75-0.85x). Post-shift (amino acid removal): wildtype shows a deep growth_rate trough (>=40% drop from pre-shift baseline) with slow recovery (>45 min to reach 90% of baseline), while clamped cells show a shallower trough (<=20% drop) and faster recovery (<=20 min), i.e. a net reversal where clamped cells' post-shift mean growth_rate exceeds wildtype's by ~10-20% during the recovery window, and division_rate stays >=0.9 for clamped vs a measurable dip (<0.8) for wildtype during the shift.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of mean growth_rate during the post-shift recovery window (30-60 min after amino-acid removal), ppgpp_conc-clamped vs wildtype, across seeds; reject H0 if two-sided p<0.05 AND effect direction shows clamped > wildtype (|t|>=2 with positive sign for clamped advantage)
falsifier.refuting_result: Welch t shows |t|<2, or |t|>=2 but with wildtype growth_rate higher than clamped post-shift (i.e., no recovery advantage, or clamped is simply worse throughout), indicating elevated ppGpp is a pure cost with no compensating benefit

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2 and sign(clamped-wildtype)>0

rivals.claim: Rival A: growth-rate variation is purely passive/noise-driven (intrinsic stochastic variation in ribosome/tRNA pools), not an adaptive preparedness strategy; ppGpp clamping just imposes a constant tax with no shift-specific benefit.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the ppgpp_conc-clamped condition shows a growth_rate deficit of similar magnitude BOTH pre-shift and post-shift (no narrowing of the gap, no faster recovery) relative to wildtype -- i.e., clamped trails wildtype throughout, including the recovery window.

rivals.claim: Rival B: any benefit seen is not due to ppGpp's regulatory role (stringent response priming of transcription/translation machinery) but is an artifact of ribosome capacity limitation itself -- clamped cells simply have fewer ribosomes to lose, so the 'crash' looks smaller trivially.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout condition (reduced ribosome capacity, no ppGpp clamp) would show the SAME blunted-crash pattern (shallow trough, fast nominal recovery) as the ppgpp_conc clamp, meaning the effect is about ribosome number, not ppGpp-mediated readiness.

auxiliary_assumptions: The timeline event 'minimal_plus_amino_acids -> minimal' is treated as an amino_acid_shift-class downshift within the allowed timeline envelope (aa shift, not a carbon-source switch).

ppgpp_conc clamp at 2x basal is a reasonable operationalization of a 'prepared/slow' subpopulation state; the simulator's clamp mechanism is assumed to propagate into ribosome/tRNA-charging dynamics realistically.

Pre-shift growth-rate cost and post-shift recovery are measured on the same seeds' trajectories, so within-seed pairing is not required but seed-to-seed variability is assumed comparable between conditions (isogenic backgrounds).

Division_rate is used as a secondary population-fitness corroborating channel, not the primary falsifier channel, since growth_rate trajectory shape is the more direct readout of 'crash vs resilience'.

We do not attempt to resolve whether any observed effect reflects deterministic model structure vs genuine stochastic bet-hedging ecology; this is recorded as a scope caveat given the simulator's architecture.

rivals.claim: Rival B: ppGpp elevation is purely costly with no benefit — there is no variance-reduction component at all; the stringent response simply shuts down growth machinery (ribosome_conc, protein synthesis) without conferring any population-level hedging advantage.
rivals.distinguishing_result: CV of growth_rate in ppgpp_conc/elevated is statistically indistinguishable from or GREATER than wildtype/basal, meaning the mean cost exists but no variance payoff accompanies it.

rivals.claim: Rival C: RelA-independent pathway — the observed ppGpp-growth coupling is driven by SpoT/other factors unrelated to RelA, so a relA knockout would NOT abolish the phenotype, falsifying the mechanistic claim that 'preparedness' is RelA-dependent per se.
rivals.distinguishing_result: relA gene_knockout control still exhibits reduced CV equivalent to the ppgpp_conc/elevated design, showing ppGpp effects arise independent of RelA synthesis (e.g. via clamp alone), separating the 'ppGpp level' causal claim from a 'RelA pathway' causal claim.

auxiliary_assumptions: The ppgpp_conc clamp mechanistically reproduces the physiological stringent-response growth-rate reduction (slower translation/ribosome synthesis) seen in RelA-mediated stringent response, not merely an arbitrary growth penalty.

Across-seed CV of growth_rate at n=8 seeds is a valid proxy for 'population-level phenotypic variance / bet-hedging', even though the simulator does not model an actual mixed population of fast+slow subclones within one run (each seed is a separate isogenic lineage, not a coexisting mixture).

Division_rate is assumed to stay at or near 1 (no lethality) for both ppgpp_conc/elevated and rrna_operon_knockout at the chosen multiple/target so that growth_rate comparisons are not confounded by differential culling of non-dividing lineages; this will be checked but is not the primary channel.
3 generations and 8 seeds are assumed sufficient for stable per-seed growth_rate estimates and CV computation; a KO or clamp causing early crash would be visible within this window.

The relA gene_knockout is assumed to abolish RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis in the model (downstream stringent response induction) without directly manipulating ppgpp_conc itself, making it a valid interventional control for mechanism rather than a redundant clamp.

drafts.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
drafts.claim: Bet-hedging via stringent-response "preparedness": a subpopulation of cells that constitutively hold elevated ppGpp (and thereby grow slower, with lower ribosome concentration) under steady nutrient-rich conditions pays an immediate growth cost, but this same stringent-poised state confers a survival/continuity advantage when challenged by a sudden nutrient downshift — i.e., the trait is maintained because it is conditionally beneficial, not because it is uniformly optimal.
drafts.h1: Across an isogenic population simulated with the RelA/SpoT (ppGpp) module on, per-seed variance in ppgpp_conc is substantial (CV >= 0.25) under basal rich media, growth_rate anti-correlates with ppgpp_conc (Pearson r <= -0.4), and when the population is challenged with an amino-acid downshift timeline, seeds/cells with higher pre-shift ppgpp_conc show a smaller post-shift drop in growth_rate and higher division_rate than low-ppGpp seeds/cells — i.e., the slow/prepared sub-state buffers the shock.
drafts.h0: ppgpp_conc variance across isogenic seeds is noise uncorrelated with shock response: pre-shift ppgpp_conc does not predict post-shift growth_rate or division_rate (slope CI includes 0), and a ppgpp_conc clamp at basal level (removing the variance) does not change the population-level post-shift growth_rate/division_rate drop relative to the unclamped wildtype under the same timeline.

operational_defs.measure: population growth_rate/division_rate drop after shift compared to unclamped wildtype

drafts.predicted_effect: Direction: negative growth_rate-ppgpp_conc correlation pre-shift (r ~ -0.4 to -0.6, cost of preparedness) but POSITIVE relationship between pre-shift ppgpp_conc and post-shift resilience (slope of delta_growth_rate on ppgpp_conc > 0, i.e., high-ppGpp seeds lose less growth rate, roughly half the relative drop of low-ppGpp seeds, e.g. -15% vs -35% growth_rate change). Clamping ppGpp to basal (removing variance/stringent capacity) should worsen the average post-shift growth_rate drop by >=20% relative to unclamped wildtype, and reduce division_rate by a detectable margin (>=0.1 absolute).

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t-test of post-shift growth_rate (averaged over the post-shift window, per seed) comparing ppgpp_conc-clamped-to-basal/amino_acid_shift vs unclamped wildtype/amino_acid_shift across seeds; reject H0 (support bet-hedging causal role) if |welch_t| >= 2 with clamped mean LOWER than wildtype. Additionally, within wildtype/amino_acid_shift use slope_ci of delta_growth_rate regressed on pre-shift ppgpp_conc across seeds; reject H0 if the 95% CI on the slope excludes 0 and is positive.
falsifier.refuting_result: If the clamped condition shows no significant difference from wildtype (|welch_t| < 2) in post-shift growth_rate, OR the slope of delta_growth_rate on pre-shift ppgpp_conc has a CI that includes 0 (or is negative), this refutes the bet-hedging/preparedness claim — ppGpp variance would then be either irrelevant or costly-without-benefit.

test.statistic: welch_t
test.threshold: |t|>=2, clamped mean growth_rate lower than wildtype

rivals.claim: Rival A - pure neutral noise: ppGpp variance is unselected molecular noise with no fitness consequence; any apparent correlation with shock resilience is a statistical artifact of correlated upstream noise (e.g., ribosome_conc variation) rather than a causal buffering role for ppGpp itself.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the ppgpp_conc clamp (basal/amino_acid_shift) should show NO worse post-shift growth_rate/division_rate drop than unclamped wildtype/amino_acid_shift (disconfirm welch_t < 2), even though cross-seed correlation might still appear in the unclamped data.

rivals.claim: Rival B - ribosome reserve, not ppGpp per se, drives resilience: cells with lower ribosome_conc (not higher ppGpp) are simply growing slower and have spare translational/metabolic capacity to reallocate after a shift; ppGpp is just a correlated marker, and a rrna_operon_knockout (which lowers ribosome capacity directly without necessarily elevating ppGpp output) should reproduce the resilience benefit as well or better.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, rrna_operon_knockout/amino_acid_shift should show comparable or greater post-shift resilience (smaller growth_rate drop, higher division_rate) than high-ppGpp wildtype seeds, and the ppgpp_conc clamp control would NOT abolish resilience since the mechanism runs through ribosome capacity, not the alarmone.

auxiliary_assumptions: The RelA/SpoT kinetic ppGpp module, when enabled, produces genuine cell-to-cell stochastic variance in ppgpp_conc under isogenic basal conditions (not a fixed deterministic value) — if the simulator's ppGpp kinetics are deterministic given seed-level noise elsewhere, the preparedness framing reduces to a seed-noise correlation only, which is an accepted scope caveat.

An amino_acid_shift that removes an amino acid (leucine) from a minimal medium timeline is a sufficient proxy for a 'nutrient downshift challenge' that engages the stringent response; the simulator need not model natural environmental fluctuation frequency or probability of shift occurring.

Growth_rate and division_rate in the post-shift window are read over a short fixed interval (e.g., first generation after the shift event) comparable across designs; we are not modeling long-run multi-generation selection dynamics, only the immediate buffering effect.

Per-seed ppgpp_conc pre-shift is treated as a stand-in for population heterogeneity in 'preparedness' (bet-hedging across isogenic lineages), not literal multi-type population genetics; this is the best available operationalization given the instrument records per-seed trajectories rather than explicit subpopulation fractions.

The rrna_operon_knockout control's ribosome capacity reduction is assumed to leave the RelA/SpoT ppGpp synthesis pathway otherwise intact, so it isolates 'ribosome reserve' from 'ppGpp alarmone level' as the rival mechanism claims.

drafts.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
drafts.claim: Bet-hedging via stringent-response "preparedness" is adaptive at the population level: a subpopulation of cells that constitutively hold elevated ppGpp (and thus grow slower, with lower ribosome concentration) under steady nutrient-rich conditions pays an individual fitness cost but confers a population-level advantage when an amino-acid downshift occurs, because the prepared fraction maintains higher growth/division continuity through the shift than an unprepared, uniformly fast-growing population.
drafts.h1: Across replicate populations, clamping ppGpp to a moderately elevated multiple of basal (simulating a 'prepared' slow-growing phenotype) reduces mean growth_rate under steady basal conditions by >=15% but, upon an amino-acid downshift timeline, yields a smaller relative drop (and faster partial recovery) in growth_rate and division_rate than wildtype, consistent with an adaptive preparedness/bet-hedging benefit that only manifests under the perturbation, not at baseline.
drafts.h0: ppGpp-clamped ('prepared') populations show no difference, or a strictly worse outcome, in growth_rate/division_rate resilience during and after the amino-acid downshift relative to wildtype; any baseline growth reduction is a pure cost with no compensating benefit under the shift.

Resilience benefit: upon amino-acid downshift, wildtype growth_rate drops ~40-50% relative to its own pre-shift baseline while the ppGpp-clamped population drops only ~15-20% relative to its own pre-shift baseline (i.e., a >2-fold smaller relative decrement), and division_rate stays closer to 1.0 (wildtype dips below 0.9, clamped stays >=0.95) in the 1-2 generations following the shift.

If |t|<2, or the clamped population's relative drop is equal or larger, H1 is refuted.

test.threshold: |t|>=2, with sign indicating smaller relative drop in clamped condition

rivals.claim: The slow growth under ppGpp clamp is simply a resource-diversion artifact (ribosome underinvestment) with no adaptive payoff — any apparent resilience during the shift is just a smaller absolute baseline to fall from (ceiling/floor effect), not a真正 preparedness mechanism.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If division_rate and growth_rate recovery trajectories (not just relative-to-self percentages) show the clamped population's ABSOLUTE post-shift growth_rate is never higher than wildtype's at any timepoint, that supports the floor-effect rival over true preparedness.

rivals.claim: Any apparent resilience is driven by RelA/SpoT regulatory dynamics reacting appropriately to the shift, not by the pre-shift elevated ppGpp clamp itself; i.e., it is the RESPONSE capacity (functional RelA) that matters, and a relA knockout under the same clamp would abolish the benefit, showing the clamp alone (independent of regulatory machinery) is not sufficient.
rivals.distinguishing_result: In the relA_knockout/basal_then_shift control, if the resilience benefit seen in ppgpp_conc/basal_then_shift disappears or reverses (clamped-but-relA-null population now drops as much or more than wildtype), this supports the rival that intact stringent-response machinery (not merely elevated ppGpp level) is required.

auxiliary_assumptions: The ppgpp_conc clamp perturbation mechanistically suppresses ribosome synthesis/charging dynamics in the simulator similarly to natural stringent response induction (not merely a label).
An amino_acid_shift timeline (removal mid-run) is a valid proxy for a nutritional downshift that would naturally trigger stringent response in wildtype.

Growth_rate and division_rate are adequate proxies for 'population fitness through a shift'; we are not modeling multi-generation selection/competition between subpopulations directly, only comparing two homogeneous clamped vs wildtype populations as a proxy for a mixed bet-hedging population.

Seed-to-seed variation (4-8 seeds) captures the main stochastic noise relevant to detecting a >=15% effect size at Welch |t|>=2; we are not resolving deep deterministic-chaos vs intrinsic-noise questions.
The simulator's amino_acid_shift and ppgpp_conc perturbations can be combined with a basal condition timeline without being a disallowed combined/carbon-switch perturbation.

drafts.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
drafts.claim: A bet-hedging subpopulation that maintains elevated stringent-response "preparedness" (high ppGpp, slower growth) at steady state achieves higher expected fitness under an unpredictable nutrient downshift than a population that is uniformly fast-growing and unprepared, even though the prepared population grows slower on average in stable conditions — a population-level benefit of heterogeneous/slow growth, not just an individual cost.
drafts.h1: Across a broad sample of seeds, a population engineered toward chronically elevated ppGpp (via ppgpp_conc clamp at ~2-4x basal, mimicking a prepared/slow-growing subpopulation) shows a SMALLER growth-rate collapse and FASTER recovery (measured by growth_rate and division_rate trajectories) upon an abrupt amino-acid downshift timeline than the wildtype/unclamped population, despite having lower steady-state growth_rate beforehand (predicted ~15-30% lower basal growth_rate, but >=50% smaller post-shift growth_rate drop and recovery time at least 1.5x faster).
drafts.h0: The ppGpp-clamped ("prepared") population shows no significant difference from wildtype in post-shift growth_rate drop magnitude or division_rate recovery time (|welch_t| < 2 across seeds for the post-shift growth_rate and division_rate channels), i.e. preparedness confers no population-level protective advantage during the shift.

drafts.predicted_effect: Prepared (ppGpp-clamped 2-4x) population: ~15-30% lower pre-shift growth_rate than wildtype (cost), but post-shift growth_rate drop reduced by >=50% in magnitude and division_rate recovery time reduced by >=1.5-fold (fewer generations to return to >=90% baseline) relative to wildtype under the same amino_acid_shift timeline.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of post-shift growth_rate drop magnitude (and separately division_rate recovery generations), target vs reference across seeds; reject H0 (preparedness helps) only if |welch_t| >= 2 in the protective direction (smaller drop / faster recovery) for growth_rate; if |welch_t| < 2 or the effect direction is reversed (clamp shows equal or larger drop / slower recovery), H1 is refuted

test.statistic: welch_t

rivals.claim: Rival A: ppGpp clamp merely slows growth uniformly (a constitutive brake) without conferring any specific shock-anticipation benefit — any apparent 'resilience' is just regression toward a lower baseline that is trivially easier to maintain, not a real protective mechanism.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, the rrna_operon_knockout control (which also slows growth via reduced ribosome capacity but WITHOUT elevating ppGpp) would show the SAME protective effect on post-shift drop/recovery as the ppgpp_conc clamp; i.e. disconfirm(rrna_operon_knockout/basal_then_shift, wildtype/basal_then_shift, growth_rate) would ALSO show |welch_t|>=2 in the protective direction, indicating slow growth per se (not ppGpp-mediated preparedness) is sufficient.

rivals.claim: Rival B: the apparent resilience is an artifact of charged-tRNA dynamics being coupled to ppGpp (both move together during the shift), not a causal role of ppGpp preparedness — i.e. fraction_trna_charged pre-shift differences explain the recovery difference, with ppGpp just a passive co-mover.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If true, a relA gene_knockout background (relaxed control, abolishing ppGpp synthesis capacity) combined with the same amino_acid_shift would show the resilience benefit DISAPPEAR even when fraction_trna_charged still drops similarly, demonstrating ppGpp itself (not charged-tRNA state) is necessary for the protective effect; conversely if relA knockout still shows resilience, ppGpp is not causal.

auxiliary_assumptions: The ppgpp_conc clamp perturbation mechanistically reproduces the physiological consequences of stringent-response activation (reduced ribosome synthesis, altered gene expression) well enough that clamped cells behave like a 'prepared' phenotype, not merely an arbitrary parameter override.

The amino_acid_shift timeline (removal of amino acids) is a valid proxy for the 'unpredictable nutrient downshift' construct in the research question; other shock types (oxygen, ion) are out of scope for this test.
Division_rate <1 after the shift reflects a genuine division defect/delay rather than a simulation artifact of the division-rate estimator.

Population-level benefit is assessed via these engineered homogeneous clamped populations as a proxy for a genuinely heterogeneous bet-hedging mixture; we are not simulating within-population phenotypic switching directly, which is a scope limitation the simulator's current perturbation set cannot address.

drafts.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
drafts.claim: Bet-hedging via stringent-response "preparedness" is adaptive at the population level: isogenic cells that maintain elevated basal ppGpp/RelA (and correspondingly slower growth) show less growth-rate collapse upon a sudden nutrient downshift than cells with ppGpp clamped low, even though the low-ppGpp cells grow faster in steady unshifted conditions. The population-level readout is the DISTRIBUTION of post-shift growth rates and survival across seeds, not a single-cell story.
drafts.h1: Across a broad sample of isogenic replicate seeds, populations with intact/elevated stringent response (basal or high ppgpp_conc clamp) show a right-shifted, lower-variance distribution of post-shift growth_rate and higher division_rate than populations with ppGpp clamped low, specifically after an amino-acid downshift; the steady-state (pre-shift) growth_rate is LOWER for the prepared population by >=15%, but the post-shift growth_rate recovery is >=25% higher and division_rate is >=10 percentage points higher, consistent with a slow-growth/prepared strategy being adaptive under fluctuating conditions (a bet-hedging trade-off).
drafts.h0: There is no systematic trade-off: populations with ppGpp clamped low show growth_rate and division_rate after the amino-acid downshift that are statistically indistinguishable from (or better than) the basal/high-ppGpp populations, i.e. any pre-shift growth advantage of low ppGpp persists or is not reversed post-shift (Welch t on growth_rate and on division_rate, target vs reference, |t|<2, or effect in the direction opposite predicted).

drafts.predicted_effect: Pre-shift: basal/high-ppGpp population grows ~15-25% slower than low-ppGpp-clamp population (growth_rate fold-change ~0.75-0.85x). Post-shift (amino_acid_shift removing an amino acid): low-ppGpp population's growth_rate drops sharply (>=40% reduction from its own pre-shift value) and division_rate falls by >=15 percentage points, while the basal/high-ppGpp population's growth_rate recovers to within 10% of its pre-shift value within 2 generations and division_rate stays >=90%. Net population growth-rate distribution post-shift is right-shifted and less variable (lower CV, no bimodal collapse, BC<0.555) for the prepared population versus a bimodal/collapsed distribution (BC>0.555, higher CV) for the low-ppGpp population.

falsifier.decision_rule: Welch t of post-shift growth_rate (mean over 2 generations post-shift, per seed) comparing low-ppGpp-clamp target vs high/basal-ppGpp reference across >=6 seeds; reject H0 (i.e. support H1) if |t|>=2 AND effect direction shows target (low ppGpp) has LOWER post-shift growth_rate than reference. Additionally require bimodality_bc on pooled post-shift growth_rate values for the low-ppGpp target: refuting if BC<=0.555 (no collapse/bimodal signature) despite the mean difference, since H1 predicts a qualitatively different (collapsed) distribution shape, not just a mean shift.
falsifier.refuting_result: Welch |t|<2, or low-ppGpp population's post-shift growth_rate is statistically indistinguishable from or HIGHER than the basal/high-ppGpp population's, showing no adaptive cost to losing preparedness.

test.threshold: |t|>=2 with target < reference

rivals.claim: Growth rate differences post-shift are driven purely by direct ppGpp-independent nutrient limitation kinetics (amino acid uptake/synthesis capacity), not by any 'preparedness' regulatory state -- ppGpp clamp level is epiphenomenal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: A relA gene_knockout (which abolishes RelA-mediated ppGpp synthesis, the 'relaxed' control) subjected to the same amino_acid_shift would show the SAME post-shift growth collapse as the ppgpp_conc-clamp-low condition, with no further degradation from removing RelA on top of the clamp -- indicating the clamp itself (not endogenous RelA machinery) is what matters, or conversely if the relA KO differs from the clamp-low condition, that shows the clamp is not capturing the true regulatory mechanism.

rivals.claim: Any apparent benefit of basal/high ppGpp is just a passive consequence of slower ribosome accumulation (fewer ribosomes make the cell less sensitive to acute translation stress), unrelated to any population-level bet-hedging logic -- i.e. it's a single-cell biophysical buffering effect, not evidence of an evolved strategic trade-off.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout (reducing ribosome capacity directly, independent of ppGpp) subjected to the same shift would show a SIMILAR buffering benefit (less growth collapse) as the high-ppGpp condition even without elevated ppGpp, demonstrating the effect is about ribosome content per se, not the stringent-response regulatory state.

auxiliary_assumptions: The amino_acid_shift perturbation (removing an amino acid mid-run) adequately models an environmental fluctuation that a 'prepared' stringent-response state would buffer against; the simulator's minimal_minus_amino_acids timeline is mechanistically coupled to the tRNA-charging/ppGpp module.

ppgpp_conc clamp overrides endogenous RelA/SpoT dynamics cleanly enough that 'basal' vs clamped conditions are comparable in all respects except ppGpp level (no confounding off-target effects of the clamp mechanism itself).

6 seeds x 4 generations gives adequate power to detect a >=25% post-shift growth_rate effect; this is treated as a pilot-scale screen, with the understanding that a population-level claim ('can it ever help a population') is being approximated by distributional statistics (mean, CV, bimodality) over replicate seeds rather than literally thousands of sub-clones -- this is an explicit scope caveat on what 'population' means in a single-strain multi-seed simulation.

Division_rate and growth_rate jointly capture 'adaptive benefit'; the simulator does not compute explicit long-run competitive fitness, so recovery speed/magnitude over 2 generations is used as a proxy for population-level advantage under fluctuation.

Post-shift (after aa withdrawal): ppgpp_clamped(3x) mean growth_rate and division_rate are ~20-30% HIGHER than wildtype in generations 3-4 (fold-change ~1.25), i.e. a sign-reversal of the fitness differential between conditions (crossover interaction).

rivals.claim: Elevated ppGpp is simply a constitutive growth-rate tax with no conditional benefit (pure cost, no hedging payoff) — the 'stringent response is just slow growth' rival.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Post-shift disconfirm shows ppgpp_clamped(3x) growth_rate/division_rate NOT significantly higher than wildtype (|t|<2 or effect_pct<=0) even though pre-shift cost is confirmed — i.e. clamped cells are slow everywhere, no crossover.

rivals.claim: Any post-shift advantage is driven by ribosome-capacity reallocation (fewer ribosomes to maintain under starvation) rather than ppGpp signaling per se — the 'ribosome economy' rival, mechanistically confounded with ppGpp since ppGpp represses rRNA transcription.
rivals.distinguishing_result: An rrna_operon_knockout control (reduced ribosome capacity, no ppGpp clamp) shows a SIMILAR post-shift recovery advantage over wildtype, implying the benefit comes from ribosome capacity reduction itself, not ppGpp signaling — this would mean the ppgpp_conc clamp's effect is not specifically a ppGpp-mediated preparedness mechanism.

auxiliary_assumptions: The ppgpp_conc clamp perturbation mechanistically engages the same downstream growth-rate-control pathways (rRNA transcription repression, translation slowdown) as endogenous stringent-response induction, even though it bypasses RelA/SpoT kinetics.

A single amino-acid-withdrawal timeline shift is a sufficient operationalization of 'environmental change' for testing preparedness; results may not generalize to other shift types (e.g. oxygen, carbon source) which are outside this envelope or infeasible mid-run.

Population-level heterogeneity (true bet-hedging, i.e. a mixed subpopulation within one seed) is approximated here by comparing distinct clamped-vs-wildtype strains across seeds rather than simulating within-population phenotypic bimodality, since the instrument clamps ppGpp uniformly per run; this tests the fitness consequence of the phenotype but not its evolutionary stability as a mixed strategy.

Division_rate <1 in either arm would flag a viability confound; we treat it as a secondary consistency check, not the primary falsifier channel, since growth_rate is the more sensitive continuous readout for the crossover claim.

drafts.question: Can it ever help a population for some cells to grow slowly or stay 'prepared' for a change?
drafts.claim: A bet-hedging subpopulation that stays growth-slow / stringent-response-primed (high basal ppGpp, lower growth rate) under steady favorable conditions pays an immediate fitness cost but confers a population-level advantage when an abrupt nutrient downshift occurs, because primed cells retain higher charged-tRNA buffering capacity and resume growth faster after the shift than cells that were growing fast and unprepared.
drafts.h1: Clamping ppGpp to a moderately elevated level (a 'primed' population proxy) relative to wildtype reduces steady-state growth_rate under basal medium but yields a smaller post-shift growth-rate penalty / faster recovery when amino acids are removed mid-run (amino_acid_shift / timeline), compared to wildtype, i.e. there is a crossover in integrated fitness favoring the primed strain after the perturbation.
drafts.h0: The ppGpp-clamped 'primed' population shows no steady-state growth deficit and no differential recovery advantage after the nutrient downshift relative to wildtype — i.e. growth_rate trajectories (pre- and post-shift) are statistically indistinguishable from wildtype within replicate noise.
